## (2026-11-11) — Dialog fades under reduced motion instead of opening at once (#3488)

**Status:** Dialog def prose + its `test.ts` arm. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no token path moves.
No executor change: Figma shows the panel at rest, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What changed

- **Owner decision Q-M5 A (2026-11-07, on #3413), amending Q491 A:** under reduced motion every placement (centered,
  bottom sheet, full screen, end panel) and the backdrop fade only, with no slide and no scale, on
  `motion.duration-reduced.normal`, to open and to close. Before, the def said they opened and closed at once, citing
  `motion.duration-reduced.moderate` as 0ms.
- `dialog.ts`: `motion.reduceMotion` and the code-only `motion` line say the fade and the token; a new `evolution` note
  records Q-M5 A over Q491 A.
- `skills/prism3-motion/SKILL.md`: the Dialog recipe drops its "(the def still drops the fade; #3488 corrects it)" note.
- `test.ts`: the `#2877 dialog reduced motion` arm pinned Q491 A ("at once … no fade … 0ms"). It is now the
  `#3488 dialog reduced motion` arm and asserts the reverse: both lines name the fade on
  `motion.duration-reduced.normal`, and neither says "at once", "no fade", "0ms" or `duration-reduced.moderate`.
  Mutation: putting back the old `reduceMotion` sentence fails the arm by name.

### Why `normal` and not the dialog's own `moderate` twin

The decision names `normal`. The reduced ramp's `moderate` is 0ms in every tempo today, so a twin of the full
duration would be no fade at all; the ramp's order and floor are #3493 and #3484, both waiting on an owner value.

**Status:** plugin only. No engine change, so no change note; CONTRACT unchanged. `file-components.ts` is outside
the executor (`lint-executor-revision.ts` lists its files), so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What changed

  set border as the projected sets (#1714).
- `file-components.ts` gains `paintSetBorder`, called after `stackVariants` in `buildSectionHeader` and

  own border.
- **Mutations:** dropping the stroke write fails `_Section-header: the set carries…` and `_Headings: the set

## (2026-11-11) — Update file: a member still marked in progress reads to update in the dry run (#3497)

The executor writes a member's stamp, then clears its in-progress marker (`finishUpdated`, `write-components.ts`). A host that throws on the clear leaves a member with its new stamp and the marker. The dry run read that member as current, because the marker only narrowed its hand-edit read. #3492's stopped-set count, which requires no marker, left it out. So after a stop on the 10th marker clear, the verdict line said 9 members updated and the next dry run said 10 were current, and the next Update skipped the unfinished member.

### The change

`update-plan.ts` holds the marker against the stamp: a stamped member that still carries the marker is "to update", after the record and hand-edit reads, so its kept paths are still kept and reported. The next Update finishes it and clears the marker. This follows the executor's own protocol (the marker comes off last), so it is a correctness fix, not a reporting choice. The executor is unchanged, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` does not move. Plugin only: `out/` is byte-identical, and no engine change note.

### The gate

`test-update-apply.ts` `stop/count marker` takes the dry run as its second witness: 9 current, 36 to update, the marked member among them, agreeing with the line's 9. A new arm runs the update again and reads all 45 current with no marker left. Mutation: `unfinished` dropped from the member's state fails `stop/count marker dry run` and `stop/count marker finished` by name.

## (2026-11-11) — Button options' Weights readout wraps inside its card (#3338)

At 1280, Components › Button options drew the Weights readout ("subtle 300 · default 400 · emphasis 500 · strong 600 ·
max 900") on one line, 43px past the card's content edge. `.p3-readout` is `white-space: nowrap`, and the only rule that
lets it wrap (#1975) keys on the levers pane's `data-fit="snug"`. Button options is drawn in the preview's card
(`.p3-cp-optsec`), which that attribute never reaches. The fix gives a readout in that card the same wrap that snug
rule gives (`white-space: normal; text-align: right`). It adds no new look.

### Gate

`test-chrome.mjs` section `3338` (shard 2) measures the rendered card on both hosts, both themes, at 1280 and 380. Every
readout in the card has to end inside its content box. The Weights readout has to be present by name, because a check
over zero readouts would pass. Mutation: drop the new rule, and `3338 web light 1280: readout "components-weights" ends
43.4px past the card's content edge` fails, along with the other three 1280 cases.

## (2026-11-10) — Update file no longer reads a moved tinted wash as a hand edit (#3527)

Under `outlineInteraction: solid-tint`, Update file read Button's and Button.Destructive's outline hover and pressed
members as hand-edited, though nobody had edited them. With Keep, those members kept the old minimum width and failed
the footprint check: 36 parts in Button and 48 in Destructive.

**Cause.** The as-built record (`member-baseline.ts`) hashes each paint, and each paint's opacity with it. A bound
paint's opacity belongs to the host, not the designer. The executor stores the variable's alpha there, and the host
writes it again on a combine and whenever Apply Theme rewrites the variable. A `solid-tint` hover binds
`interactive.<c>.subtle-fill.<state>`, a wash whose alpha is the brand's opacity step. So a theme that moved the step
moved the opacity on every wash-bound member, and the record read that as a hand edit. The issue's two candidates
were both ruled out: the record is read off the node, never computed from the `overlay-neutral` def, and the
subtle-fill binding is the plan.

**Fix.** The node hashes are unchanged. Each node that holds a bound paint now also gets a `tint` hash, which reads
that paint's opacity as 1. `baselineDiff` compares `tint` in place of the node's hash wherever both records hold it,
the same pattern as #3474's `own`. `BASELINE_V` holds, and a record written before this has no `tint` and is compared
whole, as before. That means a file built before this fix still reads those members as edited until one Overwrite
(the issue's workaround) or Accept as baseline writes them again. `finishUpdated` keeps a kept node's prior `tint`
hash, as it does for `own`, so a kept edit is not recorded as built. That is an executor change: `EXECUTOR_REVISION`
goes 55 → 56. Its reach entry names the 50 sets `lint-executor-reach` measured. Nothing draws differently, but the
gate compares plugin data, and every set that holds a bound paint now carries `tint` in its record. So Update file
re-applies those sets once, and that re-apply writes the new hash into their records. Two tests assumed a set no revision
since 42 had redrawn, and revision 56 redraws it. `test-update-apply.ts`'s reach check moves from Tag to the accordion
indicator, which is still quiet, with that premise asserted. `test-build-completed.ts` is built around Badge. It now
asserts that Badge recorded under 42 is due for the executor, and its "current" path reads the same record with Badge
left out of every entry since 42. One limit is stated in the module header:
someone who sets a bound paint's opacity by hand is not seen.

**Verified.** In `test-update-apply.ts`, Button and Button.Destructive are built under `solid-tint`, the subtle-fill
variables are rewritten as Apply Theme does (96 members' paint opacity moves), and the update runs with Keep to a new
min-width ratio: 0 hand-edited, 864 updated, both sets verify, and the next dry run is all current. Two guards check
that nothing was loosened: a wash rebound by hand still reads as a hand edit, and when an update keeps that edit, the
next dry run still reports it. Mutations: dropping the `tint` branch from `baselineDiff` fails `tint/not
hand-edited`, `tint/updated`, `tint/converges`, `tint/binding still seen` and `tint/kept still reported`. Dropping
the `finishUpdated` keep fails `tint/kept still reported` and `#3474 kept/earlier record`.

#3522 placed Report a problem at the foot of the plugin's Activity drawer. The web studio draws no drawer (#3011), so
it had no way in. The owner suggested a place beside Help in the rail (Q151 A). The placement and any new copy are

- **One dialog, two doors.** `main.ts` lends `reportLend` on both hosts. `frame.ts` mounts the same `mountReport`
  layer, and when there is no drawer (the web), it adds a `report-open` tile to the rail's foot after Help, before

  no new string is added. The plugin is unchanged: its rail has no new tile, and the drawer keeps its button.

  with `chrome/vendor-icons.mjs` from `@tabler/icons@3.49.0`, the pinned version, so `tabler.ts` and
  `tabler-digest.json` each gain one line. The choice is DRAFT.

### Traps for whoever re-verifies

- Section 1's rail arms are authored from decisions: web order, names, icons and the icon-only tiles. Each now lists
  `report-open` with a `#3524 (DRAFT)` note. If the owner moves the tile, change those literals, never a read of
  `frame.ts`.
- The icon-only loop in section 1 used to hover each tile without checking it existed, so a missing tile stopped the
  whole run on a hover timeout. It now skips a missing tile, and the `#3083 rail …` arm fails by name, because the
  `bare` count is short.
- Section 2069's web case stubs `window.open` before the click, so the run reaches no network. It checks that the
  opened URL's body is exactly the text the dialog shows.

## (2026-11-09) — Report a problem: palette and custom mode names replaced with [brand] (#3523, Q147 A)

The #3522 review (finding 4) found that with the brand's settings off, a report still carried the brand's palette and
custom mode names, as in `hf/core/palette/tidewater/500` or `mode night-watch`. The owner decided (Q147 A) that those
names are brand input under Q116 A, so they are replaced with `[brand]` too.

### How it works

- `brandWords` (`apps/studio/src/state/report.ts`) now adds each `brandColors[].name` and `customModes[].name` after
  the `id`, `name` and `root`. A name the brand already lists as one of those three keeps that word's rule.
- **Always a whole segment.** Palette and mode names are often ordinary words, so they are returned as
  `{ whole: name }`, and `scrub` matches them only as a whole segment (the same `SEGMENT` bound as a short root), at
  any length. `tidewaters` and `overnight-watchers` stay whole. The `id`, `name` and `root` keep their rules: a
  substring match from 3 characters, a segment match under that.
- **The segment bound includes prose punctuation** (#3525 review, finding 1). `SEGMENT` was built for token paths
  (`/` `.` `-` a space, a quote), so a name next to `,` `:` `;` or a bracket leaked: the plugin writes mode lists as
  `per mode (light, dark, night-watch)` and `→ light, night-watch;`. It now also counts `,` `:` `;` `!` `?`, round,
  square and curly brackets, a backtick and curly quotes. A letter or digit never bounds, so `tidewaters` still
  stays whole. This widens the short-root rule too (`hf, …` and `hf: …` were the same leak before this PR).
- `test-report.ts` adds the reviewer's two fixtures as arms, and the review's punctuation fixtures as `#3525 R1` arms. Each mutation fails its arm by name: palette names
  dropped, mode names dropped, either matched by substring, `SEGMENT` narrowed back to the path characters, and
  letters added to `SEGMENT`.

### Traps for whoever re-verifies

- The off-state note (`REPORT_COPY.brandOff`) still says only "Its name and token prefix are replaced with [brand]."
  It is now incomplete. New wording is proposed in the PR as the owner's call and is not changed here.
- A plain string in `brandWords`' result still means "the length decides"; only `{ whole }` forces a segment match.
  The existing literal arms that compare `brandWords` output as JSON are unchanged for that reason.

## (2026-11-08) — Report a problem: a diagnostic bundle and a prefilled issue (#2069, Q116 A)

The owner decided (Q116 A) on a no-backend report for now: a diagnostic bundle the person can copy, and a link that
opens a prefilled GitHub issue, with the brand input included only if the person opts in. A backend comes later.

### How it works

- **The bundle** (`apps/studio/src/state/report.ts`, pure): the build stamp (`PRISM3_BUILD`), `ENGINE_VERSION`, the
  host, and each operation's latest result from the Activity drawer (verdict and lines, and whether an agent ran it).
  Built from those fields alone, as Markdown with a "What happened" heading first for the person's own words.
- **The brand, opt-in.** A checkbox, off every time the dialog opens. Off, the brand's settings are left out and its
  `id`, `name` and `root` are replaced with `[brand]` wherever a line carries them (every token name starts with the
  root). The product's own name is never replaced: the house brand carries it, and every result line says it.
- **No file names, no keys.** The panel never holds the Figma file's name. `scrub` removes a Figma file link (with or
  without its scheme), an absolute path (`/Users`, `/home`, `C:\`), an email address, a run of 16+ hex characters, a
  token-shaped run (20+ letters, digits, `-`, `_`, holding both a letter and a digit), and a 22-letter mixed-case file
  key. Token names, the 8-hex tree token and the short commit stay. A brand word under 3 characters (a root can be
  `g`) is replaced only as a whole segment, bounded by the start or end, `/`, `.`, `-`, a space or a quote.
- **The link.** `issueUrl` prefills `github.com/adamforrester/prism3/issues/new`, cut to 7,000 characters with a line
  saying the full report is on the clipboard; both actions copy the whole report first. The plugin posts `open-issue`;
  the main thread opens it with `figma.openExternal` only when `isIssueUrl` holds (this repo's issue form), so the
  offline plugin still makes no network call. `lint-network-reach`'s reason for `github.com` now says so.
- **Placement:** a "Report a problem" button at the foot of the Activity drawer, which only the plugin draws. The web
  has no placement yet. Placement and copy are DRAFT for the owner.

### Traps for whoever re-verifies

- The dialog shows the exact text both actions send; the box is rebuilt as the opt-in changes. A test that reads the
  textarea and the posted URL's body and finds them equal is the check that nothing extra is sent.
- `open-issue` is listed as plumbing in `lint-ecosystem.ts`, beside `open-docs`; whether Report a problem earns a
  feature entry on the ecosystem map is the owner's call. The guide citations that moved are re-cited.
- `URL_LIMIT` (7,000) is held to a literal ceiling in `test-report.ts` and `test-open-docs.ts`, under the roughly 8 KB
  at which GitHub refuses a prefilled issue URL (observed, not documented). The cut backs off a surrogate pair:
  `encodeURIComponent` throws on half an emoji.
- `copyText` (the drawer's, now exported) may select a hidden textarea in `document.body`; the dialog puts focus back
  on its button afterwards, or Escape stops reaching it.

## (2026-11-08) — A short host notice when a run ends while the plugin is minimized (#533, Q110 A)

The owner decided (Q110 A) that when a run finishes with the panel closed, the plugin shows a short completion notice
and nothing more; the detail stays in Activity. The owner's note: it should read like a snackbar.

### What "closed" means here

Closing a Figma plugin's window ends the plugin (`figma.on('close')`), so no run can finish after it. The one state in
which the panel is out of sight and a run still finishes is the link strip (#2949): the window is 480×40, the UI stays
mounted and the Activity drawer still records the run. So the notice shows while the window is minimized to the strip,
and never while the full window is up, where it would repeat what Activity shows.

### Who decides what

- **The panel knows when a run ends.** The Activity drawer reads one result per run, even for a build of several sets
  (the queue records each set before its topics fire) and for Update file's steps. So `shell/activity.ts` calls a new
  `ActivityLend.ended` with a short line once nothing else runs: the worst of what ended, in the status line's words
  without the reason (`noticeLine`). An agent's command answers the agent, so it is not reported. The ends are kept
  across readings until nothing runs (the review: a panel run that ended beside an agent's command was otherwise lost),
  and `shell/run-ended.ts` `worstEnd` picks the one the line names.
- **The main thread knows whether the window is the strip,** and only it can call `figma.notify`. The panel posts
  `run-ended`; `main.ts` asks `run-notice.ts` and shows the notice only while minimized.

### The snackbar feel

`figma.notify` already has a snackbar's shape: one line, gone on its own, at most one action button. So it is used
as it comes: a 6000 ms timeout (the host's default is 3000), Restore as the button (the strip's own word, for the same
action), and not the host's error style, so the tool's voice stays recessive on the person's canvas. The timeout, the
error style and the notice lines are listed in the PR as proposals for the owner.

### Gates

- `apps/plugin/test-agent-link.ts` `run-notice/*` drives the real `main.ts`: no notice with the full window up or after
  Restore, one notice while minimized with the panel's line, 6000 ms, not the error style, and Restore restoring the
  window.
- `test:chrome` section 10 reads every `run-ended` the panel posts: one, "Update file failed.", when the panel's Update
  file run stops; none for an agent's command.
  The review added two arms there: the panel's confirmed prune, ending while an agent's build runs, is told only once
  the build ends too, as "Prune stale finished.". `apps/studio/test-run-ended.ts` holds `worstEnd` to literals: a
  failure, else a warning, else the first.

## (2026-11-08) — Apply Theme: Skip or Rename for each collision (#1909, Q112 A)

#1906 left one outcome for an apply that collides with content Prism3 did not make: a refusal, with every collision
named. The owner decided (Q112 A) that the person chooses, per collision, **Skip** or **Rename**, with "Apply to all";
refusal stays the default and nothing is remembered in v1. This builds it.

### How it works

- **Plugin.** The panel's refused `apply-result` now carries `collisions`, each with a key (`conflictKey`: kind,
  collection for a variable, name). `apply-theme` takes an optional `collisions` map back. `runApplyTheme` runs the
  pre-flight, applies the choices to the seven plans (`resolveCollisions`, `collision-choice.ts`, pure), then runs the
  pre-flight **again over the resolved plans** before any write. A collision with no choice leaves the plans as built,
  so the refusal is exactly #1906's. A renamed name someone else already holds is a collision there, before any write.
  With a choice for it too, the plans are resolved again (at most eight passes); without one, the refusal names it and
  carries `chosen`, the choices already used, which the panel posts back with the new row's (`withEarlier`). Before the
  review of #3518 caught it, the first list came back unchosen and the two lists alternated for ever.
- **Skip** drops the item, and every reference to a skipped variable lets go (alias targets, the wash's opacity,
  `aliasByMode`, gradient stops, the glass blur radius, a text style's three bound fields), so nothing binds to the
  foreign variable. A skipped `core` or `color` collection is `null` in the color executor's new `names` argument, so it
  is neither found nor created. **Rename** writes Prism3's item under `<name> (Prism3)` and the references follow.
- **Studio.** A modal list built to Update file's dialog and its Kept edits rows (`shell/collisions.ts`,
  `state/collisions.ts`): one select per row, "Apply to all" in the foot, Apply off until every row has a choice.
  Cancel, Escape and the scrim leave the refusal standing. Layout, copy and the rename suffix are DRAFT for the owner.
- An agent's apply is unchanged: its result carries no `collisions`, and `ACTIONS.applyTheme` posts no choices.

### Traps for whoever re-verifies

- **The second pre-flight is the safety, not `resolveCollisions`.** The `Q112 rename collides` arm fails by name if it
  is dropped. The resolver only reshapes plans.
- **Stranded report.** A collection written under a new name would read as "no plan writes it"; `main.ts` now counts
  the resolved names as planned.
- **Two gates moved with it.** `lint-stranded-collections` ARM 4 now also reads the color executor's default-name
  object, where its `'color'` literal lives now (mutated to `'colour'`, it names it). `test-mcp-paste`'s slicing arm
  cuts at 30,000 rather than 29,500: the one-item color script had about 100 characters to spare and grew past it, and
  30,000 still cuts the float aliases into six scripts. The public guides now say what the choice does.
- **Not covered, stated:** later runs (component builds, updates, prune) find items by their usual names, so after a
  Rename they find the item the person kept. Q112 A asks for this apply alone; the follow-up is the owner's.
- **Skip's references, one arm each** (the review of #3518): the glass blur radius and a text style's font size, family
  and style each fail by name when Skip stops releasing them. A Rename no longer touches `fontSizeCollection`, which no
  writer reads.

## (2026-11-07) — Contrast floor follow-ups: an emission oracle for "follows", the two unreached names, accurate comments (#2228)

### What changed

- **An independent oracle for the floor's "follows" clause (#2228.1).** The #2179 sweep took "does the Auto floor follow
  `background.secondary`?" from the button's own tooltip, so a change that dropped "follows" from both the tooltip and
  the accessible name passed. For prism3 it now reads the answer off the committed emission: `EMITTED_FLOOR` gains each
  mode's `secondary`, the palette step `background.secondary`'s alias chain ends on, and the floor follows exactly when
  `foreground.brand`'s `against` is that step. The tooltip and the name are each held to it. Other brands have no
  committed emission, and the tooltip still stands in for them. A floor check requires at least one prism3 state where
  the emission says "follows", so the mutation has something to fail.
- **The two names the sweep never reached (#2228.2)**, asserted as computed names (CDP) in the #2250 block, against
  literal oracles: at Primary Black the Auto floor follows no tier ("Contrast floor, Light: Auto · neutral 950. Pick a
  step"), and a picked step ("Contrast floor, Light: neutral 050. Pick a step").
- **Shipped comments (#2228.3).** In `fills-input.ts`, `floorAutoShortLabel`'s doc comment sat above `floorAutoFollows`
  and said the full sentence was still the button's accessible name. It now sits above its own function and says the
  sentence is the tooltip, with the name built in `color-fills.ts` as option 1.
- **The record (#2228.4).** The `test-chrome.mjs` header's "(web)" for the layout check now says both hosts. The #2193
  entry is folded into the log, which is prose and isn't edited outside a fold, so its corrections are here: under
  "(2026-10-06) — Surfaces & fills: the Contrast floor row puts its picker on the right…", the block runs on **both
  hosts** (not "on the web host"), and the bullet "shows its whole label, not cut off" belongs to the list above "The
  block runs on both hosts".

### What the oracle found first, and why it isn't a fix here

The first run read the emission's own mode in HC light and HC dark, and failed there. The studio says "follows
background.secondary" in both, while the emitted `background.secondary` is white and black. The studio is consistent:
Surfaces edits Light and Dark only (`SURFACE_MODES`), and a derived mode's row shows, read-only, the surfaces of the
mode it's drawn from, so the floor row in HC light describes Light's floor. The oracle now models that (HC light reads
Light, HC dark reads Dark, restated in the test, not read from the studio). Whether an HC mode's accessible name should
say "Contrast floor, HC light: … follows background.secondary", when the previewed mode's own secondary is a different
color, is a copy call. It's raised on the PR for the owner.

### Mutations, each failing by name (from `wip:` commits; a temporary local shard ran sections 18 and 18-s4f)

- `floorAutoFollows` returning null and `floorAutoLabel` always `Auto · ‹step›` (the clause dropped from both the name
  and the tooltip): 32 failures, the first `#2179 web 1280 prism3 / light: FL1 A: the Contrast floor's tooltip is the
  full sentence (the emission: the floor is background.secondary's step) — want "Auto · follows background.secondary
  (neutral 050)", read "Auto · neutral 050"`, and its name twin.
- `floorAutoFollows` always naming the tier: 1 failure, `#2228: Primary Black: the Auto floor follows no tier, and its
  computed accessible name is "Contrast floor, Light: Auto · neutral 950. Pick a step" …`.
- The picked step given `follows` too (`color-fills.ts`): 1 failure, `#2228: floor picked at neutral 050: its computed
  accessible name is "Contrast floor, Light: neutral 050. Pick a step" …`.

## (2026-11-07) — Badge inline labels take the contained sizes (#3475 part 1, Q93 B)

The owner decided (Q93 B) that an inline Badge is a standalone status label like the others, only quieter, and not
text set in running copy. So its label now takes the contained label's rung at each size, at the regular weight:
`label.sm.default` (12px) at medium and `caption.md.default` (the corpus's 11px, 10px on the reference brand) at small,
replacing #3199's `body.md` / `body.sm` (16px / 14px). The dot cell follows the label's line box.

### What the change needed beyond the token swap

- **A caption line box.** No `type.caption.*.line-box` existed, only label and body. `tree.ts` now bakes the caption
  twin from the same loop as the label one (`lineBoxOf`), and `emit-figma-dims.ts` emits `type/caption/{rung}/line-box`
  beside the other two. Two added contract paths (`caption.md`, `caption.lg`), so CONTRACT 14.15.0.
- **`typeWeight.keys`.** Badge's `typeWeight` (#2983) repointed *every* `type.caption.*` ref to the bold caption, which
  would have turned the inline small label bold and rewritten `caption.md.line-box` to `caption.md.strong`. `keys`
  scopes it to `size.small.contained.type`; the schema checks each key is a bound `type.<group>.*` ref.

### Trap for whoever re-verifies

- **Small is taller than medium inline.** Caption's cozy leading makes `caption.md`'s line 15px against `label.sm`'s
  14px (both 14px on the reference brand). The contained sizes hide this behind padding; the inline ones show it. It is
  a consequence of the type ramp, not of this change, and is flagged to the owner in the PR.
- The `test.ts` arm "badge inline and contained share a text size at each size" compares each brand's emitted
  composite font size and line height through the projected plan's text style, not the def's keys, so it fails by size
  and brand if either style is rebound.

The description, docs and usage prose that described the inline label as matching the surrounding copy is rewritten
as a draft flagged for owner sign-off in the PR.

## (2026-11-07) — `@prism3/tokens` ships the house brand's token CSS as an installable tarball (#3408 S1)

**What changed.** `packages/tokens` was only a gate; since Q99 A it also builds what a client installs. `npm pack -w @prism3/tokens` now produces a tarball holding the house brand's CSS custom properties and the README, nothing else, and that tarball installs into a client project with no registry (Q84 A). Engine output doesn't move, so there is no change note.

- **`sd.ship.mjs`** builds `prism3` from the conforming projection the engine already emits: one stock Style Dictionary v5 run per mode, the base (the light defaults) under `:root`, each overlay under `[data-theme="<mode>"]`. It is the consumer build's shape, in its own file so the gate's config never bends to suit a deliverable. The four per-mode files are then joined into `dist/prism3.css`; joining finished files is plumbing after Style Dictionary ran, not a format, and no client runs it. No Style Dictionary bump was needed: the installed 5.5.0 does all of it.
- **Names stay `--pds3-…`** (Q98 A, now `docs/35` §9.4 with its index rows). No `prefix` option, no rename.
- **`package.json`:** `exports` (`.` and `./prism3.css` → the joined file, `./prism3/*.css` → one block each), `style`, `files: ["dist/"]`, `prepack` running the build. Still `private` at `0.0.0`: `npm pack` works on a private package, and publish refuses it. No JS is emitted, so there is no ESM entry to declare; `"type": "module"` stays.
- **The no-custom-code rule now covers both files.** `check-consumability.mjs` reads `sd.ship.mjs` as source with the same banned list as `sd.consumer.mjs`.
- **New gate, `check:package`** (CI step, `verify.ts`, CONTRIBUTING §3, CLAUDE.md §4, PR template). It packs, installs the tarball with `--offline` into a temp folder outside the repo, resolves the CSS through the installed `exports`, and checks every guaranteed name from `token-contract.json` with a DTCG type (618 of 621) under `--pds3-` in each of the four promised blocks, plus that each `[data-theme]` block changes at least one value from `:root`. The contract, the prefix and the promised blocks are the oracle; none is read off the build.
- **Mutations, each failing by name:** dropping `dark` from the build's mode list fails `[BLOCK] [data-theme="dark"] is in the installed CSS`; adding Style Dictionary's `prefix` option fails `[NAMES] … under --pds3-` and `[PREFIX]` for every block.

**A trap for whoever re-verifies this.** The three `motion.spring.*` contract names aren't in the CSS, by design: `spring` isn't a DTCG type, so it isn't in the projection the build reads (#642). The gate excludes them by its own copy of the DTCG type list and prints them on every run. If a spring ever reaches the projection, the gate's count rises rather than failing silently.

The code-surface adherence scorer (`tools/agent-adherence/`, #3440) now checks the CSS custom-property names stock
Style Dictionary emits, `--pds3-color-text-primary`, instead of stripping the `pds3` root. Owner decision Q98 A keeps the
stock names (no custom build step in `packages/tokens`), so the scorer learns the prefix.

  at `zz9` (`oracle/other-root`, `R1/other-root`, `R1/other-root-pds3`).

  invented name on a real page. The violation names the stock name so a run that dropped the prefix everywhere reads as

  pinned tree.

  change was told unprefixed names and would score every token read as R1, so it must be re-planned, not compared. The

## (2026-11-07) — Draw specs verdicts carry causes (#3404)

Every Draw specs verdict that is not ok now carries one cause, so the Activity drawer can say why. It was split out of
#3492 by the independent review's option B and held for #3404's owner questions. **This changes what the drawer
shows.** The drawer already renders `causes` (`apps/studio/src/shell/activity.ts`), so Draw specs verdicts that are not
ok gain a cause disclosure and a new status-line reason. The words are existing headlines and items. No executor code
moved.

### Owner decisions (2026-11-07)

- **#3404 Q1: yes.** Draw specs verdicts carry causes.
- **Q89 A:** each cause's kind follows `runCause`, so the cause's mark matches the headline's: ⚠ → `warn`, ✗ → `bad`.
  The first build mapped "nothing drawn" to `bad`, a ✗ cause under a ⚠ headline; that is gone.
- **Q90 A (#3404 Q2):** a run that drew every panel but has a note is not ok, so its headline reads ⚠
  (`⚠ drew 1 spec panel`), not ✓. Before this, a ✓ headline could post `ok: false`.
- The per-family causes proposal is not decided and stays out.

### The mapping

The cause is the run's own (`subject: null`): `runCause`'s kind and wording from the headline, its reasons the items
the lines already print, or the summary when no set is on the page. So: no set → ✗ / `bad`; nothing drawn or some
drawn → ⚠ / `warn`; all drawn with a note → ⚠ / `warn`; the throw → ✗ / `bad`. The status-line reason moves from the
first line (`Drew n of m`) to the first item.

### Gates

`test-build-completed.ts` pins every case literally, so the mapping cannot move without a test failing by name:
section 8a `causes/draw specs noted` (section 8's own run, every panel drawn with a note); section 8b

## (2026-11-07) — Canvas furniture names every size: `size` is labeled past the row-depth cap (#3475 part 2)

**The gap.** On the Badge page the canvas furniture labeled `type`, `style` and `emphasis` but not `size`, so the
medium and small rows had no name. The cause was general, not Badge's: `planFurniture` labels the outer
`ROW_LABEL_DEPTH` (3) row axes, and `size` always sits last among the row keys, because `planComponentName` gives it a
fixed place after the declared axes. Any set with more than three labeled outer row axes lost exactly `size`. Measured
over every def with a `size` axis: Badge, Accordion, Link and Pagination item had the gap; every other set already
named its sizes, as rows or as its grid columns.

**The fix.** `size` is labeled even when the cap cuts it, the way the Inverse bracket is already extra, and in row-key
order, so it stays the bracket nearest the set. The cap itself, held for the owner, is unchanged: raising it to 4 would
have also drawn Link's `selection` and Pagination item's `labeled` brackets, which nobody asked for. No new on-screen
words: every size value these four sets now show ("Medium", "Small", "Large", "X small") is already drawn on other
sets' furniture.

**The gate.** `test-canvas-furniture.ts` `rollout/<def> sizes`: for every def whose own axes declare `size` with two or
more values, each value is drawn as a label, row or column, in the label wording written out in the test rather than
read off `sentenceCase`. Mutation: the cap applied to `size` again fails `rollout/badge sizes`, `rollout/accordion
sizes`, `rollout/link sizes` and `rollout/pagination-item sizes`, and nothing else.

**Not in scope.** Part 1 of #3475, Badge's label sizes across styles, is an owner decision still open.

### What landed

  motion token families an agent binds, rules R1–R11, six recipes on today's tokens (dialog, accordion, tabs

  animates in (Q-M4 A); the dialog fades at `motion.duration-reduced.normal` under reduced motion (Q-M5 A).
  **The wording is held for the owner's sign-off in the PR.**
- **Discovery:** the `.claude/skills/prism3-motion` symlink (`lint-skills` check 6), the ecosystem page's
  `load-skills` members (`lint-ecosystem` MEMBERS), `llms.txt`, the README, CLAUDE.md's layer table and docs/07.
- **Pointers:** one line each from `prism3-build-ui` (beside the `motion.*` exception) and
  `prism3-build-component` (beside the ungated `motion` field, #2773).
- **`packages/engine/lint-motion-literals.ts`**, in CI after the skills gate. Three halves: no duration, curve
  or spring constant in the skill's text, and every `motion.*` name resolving in every brand's committed
  `out/<brand>.tokens.json`; and (added below) no reduced exit longer than its entrance.
- **Filed, per Q-M6 A:** G1–G6 as #3481–#3486; raw milliseconds in `tab`/`tabs`/`banner` motion prose as
  #3487; `dialog`'s reduced form dropping the fade as #3488.

  `fast` outlasts the reduced `normal`), so the accordion and the toast and banner recipes now use one reduced
  role, `motion.duration-reduced.normal`, both ways. R3, R7, checklist item 3 and the gaps table say so. The
  gate gains a third half, REDUCED EXIT LONGER: each recipe's direction-tagged reduced roles are compared in
  the emitted milliseconds of every brand, aliases followed to the primitive, with floors on the reduced
  forms and pairs it reads.

### Why the literal oracle is a shape

The obvious gate reads the emitted durations and flags any number equal to one. It's derived from the
subject's neighbor (docs/34 sub-shape 2) and passes an off-ramp `180ms`, which is the value an agent invents.
So the literal half imports nothing from `theme.ts` and reads nothing from `out/**`: the patterns are typed
in the gate. A `motion.duration-ms.*` path fails too, as a number spelled as a path. Non-motion numbers are
admitted by exact text and file, each with a reason; today one, WCAG 2.2.2's "five seconds". An unused
allowance fails as stale.

Recorded with the commands and output in the PR: a literal `200ms` in the skill (DURATION LITERAL), a
`cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` in a recipe (CURVE LITERAL), and `motion.easing-role.enter` renamed in the
skill (UNRESOLVED PATH; `lint-skills` also fails it, as a dead token path, from its own probe tree). The
accordion's or the toast's reduced form put back to `…normal` entering and `…fast` leaving fails as REDUCED
EXIT LONGER, naming all 5 brands.

P2 (the token gaps), P3 (the motion-patterns file and its gates), P4 (Figma animation styles) and P5 (the
skill teaching patterns) stay open on #3413. The gate's scope widens to the defs' `motion` prose when #3487

## (2026-11-07) — The agent's build makes `_Doc-block`, a missing one is a note, and Update file offers Set up file when setup's pieces are gone (#3467)

#3467's investigation traced why an agent's fresh file came out of `file-setup` → `apply-theme` → `build-components button` reading `ok:false`. The build was clean. The only problem was "No usage panels drawn: this file has no _Doc-block component". The owner answered Q1–Q7 A. Q6 and Q7 were docs, and shipped in their own PR. This entry covers Q1–Q5.

### What changed

- **Q1, the agent's build asks for `_Doc-block`.** The `build-components` route in `agent-dispatch.ts` passes `{ docBlock: true }`, the same ask Update file's sets step sends, to the same `ACTIONS.buildComponents`. With Documentation's usage panels on, the theme in the file and no `_Doc-block`, the agent's first build now builds Badge, Tag, List Item and Divider first, then `_Doc-block`, as the panel's first run does. A build from Studio's Components page still doesn't ask. Q1 is about the agent route only.
- **Q2, a missing `_Doc-block` is a note.**
  - `canvas-furniture.ts`: `templatesLine` and `withTemplateWarning` now cover only `_Label` and the two backdrops (`WARN_TEMPLATES`), which keep Q284.3 A's warning.
  - A missing `_Doc-block` gets its own line, `docBlockLine`. It goes in the summary, where an agent reads it, and in one run-level `note` cause (`docBlockNotes`, subject `null`). The verdict keeps its `ok` and `✓`.
  - Activity's problem list (#3309) no longer counts it.
  - This is the first writer that sends a `note`. Studio's queue run (`runCauses`, `build-queue.ts`) used to drop every cause of a clean set, which would have hidden it. It now keeps each subject's latest note.
- **Q3 + Q4, the "setup incomplete" read.**
  - `setup-incomplete.ts` lists what Set up file would build on the file now: the `↳ File Components` page, `_Section-header`/`_Headings`, `_Label`, both backdrops, the three style-guide cell sets, and `_Doc-block` once it can be built. Each is looked for where setup looks for it.
  - `fileSets` posts the list as `setupIncomplete` beside `setUp`. `isSetUp` is unchanged (P8).
  - Studio's Update file offers the Set up file step whenever the list isn't empty (`setupOfferedOf`). On a set-up file the step starts unticked, and its line names what is missing. The cover step stays a fresh file's.
- **Q5, the remedy names the real fix.** `docBlockParts` chooses the line from what the file holds (`docBlockFixOf` in `main.ts`):
  - no theme: "Apply the theme, then build again";
  - sets missing: "Build tag, list-item, then run Set up file and build again";
  - everything present: "Run Set up file, then build again". These are the old words, now true because Q3 makes the step reachable.
  
  **The wording is a DRAFT held for the owner's sign-off**, as is the Set up file line "Builds what this file lacks: …".

### Verification

Every behavior has an arm that fails by name under a mutation (16 run, each listed in the PR). The end-to-end arms are in `test-update-doc-block.ts`, against the real `main.ts` under the strict shim:

- `agent` drives the dispatcher's own `ROUTES['build-components']`;
- `#3467 note` and `#3467 label still warns` cover Q2;
- `setup incomplete/…` walks a fresh file, a set-up one, one with the four sets, one with deleted pieces, and a repaired one.

`test-update-owner-run.ts` changed meaning: the owner's nine-set run is now clean, with the note on the five sets that draw a panel. Its two old mutations, `stepDone` ignoring `warn` and `runVerdict`'s `⚠`, are held in `test-update-file.ts` and `test-component-groups.ts`, which its header now names.

### Traps

- **The usage-panel line is read before the settle probe.** `docBlockFixOf` reads the file after the build, and the build's verdict is posted inside `verdictBeforeSettle`'s synchronous callback, so the read is awaited just before it. It returns at once unless a set lacked `_Doc-block`. When one did, a document-wide set search runs before the probe starts.
- **Studio's chrome test reads the plugin's bundle.** A shell-only mutation must rebuild both `dist`s, or the `ui.html freshness` arm fails first and hides the arm you meant to test.
- **The `✗` lines go to stderr** in these suites. A mutation harness that reads only stdout reports every mutation as missed.

### Not done

- `tools/agent-adherence/selftest-figma.ts` still has fixtures where the missing `_Doc-block` made a run `ok:false`. They are recorded runs from before this change, scored by the adherence harness and not wired into CI, so they stay as they are.

## (2026-11-07) — Plugin verdicts: an over-budget set member throws, a stopped set counts what it finished (#3418, #3449)

Two correctness fixes in the plugin, one PR. No executor code moved, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` is unchanged. The line
wording is unchanged; the wording question #3449 raises is a proposal in the PR body, under "Owner sign-off needed".
The Draw specs causes (#3404) began in this PR and moved to a PR of their own, held for the owner: whether Draw specs
shows causes at all, and which mark each case gets, is #3404's first owner question, and the drawer already renders
causes, so carrying them changes what it shows.

### #3418 — a one-member chunk over its budget is a thrown error

`mcp-paste.ts`'s header says a single indivisible unit that will not fit is a thrown error. For a set, that unit is one
member in a chunk, and `planSetChunks` ships it alone and over budget rather than loop. The engine stays permissive: its
own gates pack to a budget of 1 on purpose (`test.ts` measures one member per chunk that way), so a throw there would
break them. `componentScripts` knows the real per-script budget, so it checks each chunk's measured `bytes` against it
and throws, naming the def and the member. Only a one-member chunk can be over, because `settleChunks` moves members off
any larger one.

`componentScripts` takes `chunkCeiling`, which lowers the ceiling and never raises it, as `themeScripts`' `sliceCeiling`
does, so the gate can reach the case. Arm: `test-mcp-paste.ts` `size/one member`, Badge at a 32,000 ceiling. The
ceiling is chosen so the smallest member sits between the budget and the ceiling (29,115 < 30,110 < 32,000), which is
the issue's harm: a chunk over its budget but under the ceiling. The premise asserts exactly that, with the member's
size measured off the engine's packer at budget 1, not off `componentScripts`. **Trap:** the first version used a
30,000 ceiling, where every member is over the ceiling too, so a check against the ceiling instead of the budget still
passed (the independent review found it). Mutations: the check dropped, or compared against the ceiling →
`size/one member: a member that will not fit alone throws`.

### #3449 — a stopped set's count is read off the host

`applySet` set `out.updated` only from the pass's return value, which a throw never delivers, so the count was always 0.
Now a stop reads the count off the host. A member counts as finished when it carries its planned stamp, did not carry it
before the pass, and has no in-progress marker.

**What this means in practice.** The executor writes every member's stamp after the whole pass (§7). So a stop inside the
members' writes, the usual case and #3424's reproduction, still reads 0, and 0 is correct there: no member is finished.
The count is above 0 only when the stop comes during the stamp writes. Arms in `test-update-apply.ts`: `stop/count none`
(the existing stop, 0), `stop/count finished` (the 10th stamp write throws: the line reads 9, and the dry run's own read
of the stamps gives 9 current and 36 out of date), and `stop/count marker` (the 10th marker clear, the write after the
stamp, throws: the line reads 9). Mutations: the host read dropped → `stop/count finished`; the marker clause dropped →
`stop/count marker`.

**The dry run is not a witness for the marker case.** It reads the 10th member, stamped but still marked, as current
(10), because it does not hold a marker against the stamp; the marker only narrows its hand-edit read. So the count
and the dry run disagree by one in that case. The arm's premise is read off the host instead: 10 members restamped, 1
of them still marked.

**Side effect.** A stopped set with at least one finished member now counts as changed, so it appears in the publish
description's sets (`update-apply.ts`'s `changed`). Before, a stopped set never did, because its count was 0.

The line's other clause, "the rest are unchanged", is not true after a stop inside the writes: those members were
written and are not finished. That wording is the owner's. It is a proposal in the PR body.

## (2026-11-07) — The disposition is one of four names in both schemas, and `check:ignore` checks every web input (#3451, #3407)

Two schema and gate gaps found in review, fixed in one PR.

### #3451: the four disposition names in both schemas

The `disposition` of a `syncBoundary` item was `{ type: string, minLength: 1 }` in both `schema/component-docs.schema.json` and `schema/component-defs.schema.json`, so a consumer validating an export accepted a typo. Both are now an `enum` of CARRIED, LOWERED, REFUSED and UNSUPPORTED (Q3441.1 A), written as literals in each schema and not read from `DISPOSITION_NAMES` (`docs/34` shape 1: a schema built from the constant would accept whatever the constant says). The register's header now says a rename edits the two enums too.

- **Nothing emitted moves.** The schemas are authored, not `regen.ts` artifacts, and every export already carries the four names, so `regen.ts` changes nothing. No change note: the engine's behavior did not change. `CONTRACT_VERSION` does not move (no token name moves). The schemas' `$id` does not move either: no field was added, removed or renamed, and every export that validated before still validates.
- **Mutations, each failing by name in `lint-component-docs.ts`:** `"CARIED"` written into the committed `components.ai.json` and `component-defs.json` fails `SCHEMA` and `DEFS SCHEMA` (`"CARIED" is not one of [...]`). The same mutation against main's schemas reports nothing. `DISPOSITION_NAMES.carried = 'CARIED'` fails `DEFS SCHEMA (<brand>)` for every live brand export.

**Correction to 2026-11-05 "`codeOnly` as data: a class register and a four-way disposition (#3441)".** Its totals were measured before the merge. After #3380, the export carries **547 entries on 62 defs**, not 530 on 60. By disposition: CARRIED 2, LOWERED 116, REFUSED 251, UNSUPPORTED 178 (measured from `out/components/components.ai.json`).

### #3407: every web bundle input sits under a trigger path

`vercel-ignore-check.mjs` asked one question of the bundle's inputs: is an engine file on the skip list? A web input outside `packages/engine/` and outside every `PATHS` entry passed, so a change to it alone skipped the deploy. That happened in #3389 with `apps/plugin/src/causes.ts`.

The gate now checks every input. Neither side is computed by the gate:
- **The inputs** are esbuild's metafile, plus the files the chrome CSS plugin builds the virtual `p3-chrome:chrome-css` from (the token trees, fonts and icon license), taken from the `watchFiles` it already returns to esbuild. A virtual input with no recorded file behind it fails.
- **The trigger set** is the script's own array code, run by bash, so the `:(exclude)` pathspecs arrive as `git diff` gets them. Which files they cover is answered by `git ls-files`, with git's own pathspec rules. A `node_modules/` input counts as `package-lock.json`. An input git does not track is reported as one no commit can change.
- **One declared exemption, `CHECK_ONLY = ['apps/plugin/src/']`.** The chrome plugin also watches every plugin source file, because its `[glyphs]` check reads their string literals. That check can fail the build but never changes the CSS. The entry fails as stale once the glyph check stops reading that root.
- **Represented, not counted:** the walk must contain an input under `apps/studio/`, one outside it, and one file the chrome plugin builds from.
- **The detector is held to a plant:** a bundle importing `apps/plugin/src/pace.ts`, which is under no trigger path, must be reported by that name.

A new fixture asserts that a change to `causes.ts` alone BUILDS. Mutations: dropping `apps/plugin/src/causes.ts` from `PATHS` fails with `apps/plugin/src/causes.ts` named under "sit under no trigger path". Blinding the detector fails on the plant (`does not report apps/plugin/src/pace.ts`).

Trap for whoever extends this: `watchFiles` is what a plugin asks esbuild to watch, and that can include files a check reads (as `[glyphs]` does). It is an over-approximation of what the build reads, so an exemption needs a reason and a staleness check, never a silent filter.

## (2026-11-07) — lint-guide-claims: a citation past a file's end, and one under a table, now fail; each gap is a planted fixture (#3456, #3457, #3417)

**Status:** gate and one guide only, so no engine bump, no artifact moves and `CONTRACT_VERSION` is unchanged.

### What changed

- **#3456: lines are counted as the file has them.** `split('\n')` gives a file that ends in a newline one empty
  element more than its line count, and the range check read it as a line, so `provenance.ts:1-58` passed on a
  57-line file. The cited file's lines now drop that element. The fingerprints are unchanged, because no
  citation's slice reached it.
- **#3457: a citation on its own line steps over one blank line to the block above.** A citation set under a
  table after a blank line read an empty claim, so it counted as quoting nothing, and the table's code spans were
  never held to the cited lines. It now claims the table.
- **#3417: the fixture the issue asked for.** #3458 added the FINGERPRINT arm but planted no fixture, so nothing
  showed the arm still caught a moved block. The CITE and FINGERPRINT checks now live in one function, `citeLine`.
  The guides and a new SELF-CHECK arm both run through it. The SELF-CHECK arm runs the function over a small
  in-memory tree that plants all three gaps. Each must fail by name. A control with the same three shapes cited
  correctly must pass with exactly one citation that quotes nothing, so a gate that fails everything, or that reads
  the table's claim as empty, cannot satisfy it. The fixture files and their fingerprints are written by hand
  (`printf '%s' <line> | sha256sum`), never computed by the gate (`docs/34`).

## (2026-11-07) — Update file: a change that reaches a member only through a nested instance's main is not a hand edit (#3474)

The owner's rule on #3474: a hand-edit flag must mean a person edited that member. The update check flagged the button
family's focus-visible members on the reference brand's master as "edited by hand" with nobody having touched them.

### Diagnosis, on the shim

Focus Ring, then Icon button nesting it, built into one file; the main then changed without touching the host:

- **A property added to Focus Ring's set** moves `props` in the host ring's signature. **A Focus Ring member renamed**
  moves `main`. Either flags exactly the 36 focus-visible members, at `focusRing`. A shim instance inherits nothing else
  from its main, so this is all the plain shim can show.
- **On Figma an instance reads every field it does not override from its main**: its stroke and stroke weight (and their
  bindings), paints, effects, opacity, visibility, property values. `nodeSignature` hashed all of them on the ring
  instance, so any change to Focus Ring's main moved every host's record. The host's own overrides (absolute, inset, the
  four corners, the cleared size bindings) are the only part that is the host's.
- **The other cause tried, an executor or plan change to how the ring's overrides are written, has no path today.** The
  only writer of those overrides is the executor, and the in-place update records each member after it writes
  (`finishUpdated`). A record taken before an executor change is replaced by the update that applies the change.

### The counts are not explained

The shim reproduces **one mechanism**: a change to a nested component's main flags every member that nests it. It flags
all 36 of Icon button's focus-visible members. The real distribution does not look like that, and this entry does not
claim to explain it:

- **Flush icon button flags 9 of its 12 focus-visible members** (60 members). Its Destructive and Neutral sets flag 12,
  their focus-visible count. A change to the shared ring main would flag all 12, so it is not the whole story for the
  plain set.
- **Icon button Destructive flags 48, but holds only 36 focus-visible members**, so at least 12 flagged members do not nest
  Focus Ring at all. Button's 36 of 96 does not follow from the shim either.
- **On the real file, every focus-visible ring in a set has the identical override shape** (read 2026-11-07, both
  surfaces): the corners, size, positioning, name and `boundVariables`. So the shape cannot tell Flush's 9 from its other
  3: the flagged subset must differ by value. One candidate is the two ring mains (default and inverse surface) having
  moved differently.
- **The Spinner lead is plausible but unconfirmed.** The extra 12 appear only on sets with a pending state, whose 36
  pending members each nest a Spinner instance that overrides only its name and reads its size through its main. A change
  to Spinner's main for one paint family would fit, and the rule here would cover it, but nobody has seen the flagged list.

Only the plugin's dry run (`update-components confirm:false`) produces the flagged member paths; a read of the file
cannot. That run is what would confirm or rule out this mechanism for #3474's counts.

### The rule

**A change that arrives only through a nested instance's main is not a hand edit on the host; what the host set on the
instance still is.** Each member's record holds, beside the node hashes, one hash per nested instance of what the host
itself set on it (`Baseline.own`): the instance's signature cut to the fields its own entry in `InstanceNode.overrides`
lists, plus its type, its main, its property references and its exposure. Where both records hold it, `baselineDiff`
compares it in place of the node's hash. `nodeSignature` is unchanged, so every node hash is too and `BASELINE_V` stays 3
(the header's `reactions` and `art` precedent).

- **Existing records read exactly as they did.** A record from before this holds no `own` part, so its instances are
  compared whole, and a main change still flags them. They clear as each set is next written (an update, or Overwrite,
  the workaround in use). Owner decision Q77 A (2026-11-07): records written before this PR stay as they are, and
  Option B (clearing them sooner) is not taken. No real hand edit is lost.
- **A swap is still the host's** (`main` is always in the own part). **A rename of the nested component still moves it**:
  v3 names the main by name, not by key.
- **A binding is resolved against the main.** Figma lists a binding the host set or cleared as one field,
  `boundVariables`, not by the bound field's name (read on the real file: every nested focus ring lists it, while its
  `boundVariables` also holds the stroke weights and strokes its main binds). So each field whose binding on the instance
  differs from the main's is the host's, and one the two share is the main's. A host rebind still reads as a hand edit; a
  rebind on the main does not. Where the main's bindings cannot be read, every binding is kept as the host's.
- **A kept hand edit keeps its own part as recorded** (`finishUpdated`), as it keeps its node hash, or the next dry run
  would stop reporting it. On a record from before this, which holds no own part, the update leaves the part out, so the
  ring is still compared whole. That is the executor's code, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 54 → 55, reaching no set (it draws
  nothing).

### Gates

`figmaInstances` (`component-shim.ts`) models a Figma instance through `wrapNode`, from the typings and the real-file
read, never from the record code: unset fields and bindings read through from the live main, and a binding the host sets
or clears is listed as `boundVariables`. A plain shim instance carries `overrides` reading `undefined`, a host that lists
none: without it the snapshot's read of `overrides` was a host API the shim lacked, and `lint-executor-reach.ts` read four
sets (code input and its cell, page navigation and its item) as redrawn by 55. Nothing is drawn from that read, so entry
55 names none, measured clean.

Arms: `test-update-components.ts` `#3474/…` and `test-update-apply.ts` `#3474 kept/…`. Mutations, each failing by name:
the own-part branch dropped → `#3474/main`; the own signature ignoring overrides → `#3474/host`, `#3474/host override`;
the snapshot not reading `overrides` → `#3474/main`; `finishUpdated`'s keep dropped → `#3474 kept/still reported`;
`finishUpdated`'s branch for a record with no own part removed → `#3474 kept/earlier record`; `boundVariables` dropped
unresolved → `#3474/host rebind`; every binding counted as the host's → `#3474/main`, `#3474/main rebind`; only the
instance's own binding keys walked, so a host clear of a main binding is dropped → `#3474/host clear`; the unreadable-main
fallback inverted → `#3474/host rebind, main unreadable`.

## (2026-11-06) — Agent adherence: the `↳ Buttons` capture in parts, and every command checked against the plugin (#3469)

The first adherence setup on the Mac stopped at the `inspect-buttons` capture: `figma-plan.ts` sent `inspect` with
`depth: 4, maxNodes: 5000`, and the plugin takes a depth from 0 to 3 and at most 2000 nodes. Both values were past
its limits, not only the depth the error named.

- **Depth 3 under-covers, so the page is read in parts.** In the component shim the Button set is page → set →
  576 variants → 1,272 children: 1,850 nodes three levels down, close to the cap, and in a real file an icon slot's
  instance has its own layers a level further. The plant now cuts the page into parts (`PARTS`, a JavaScript string the
  plant runs in Figma and the self-test runs in Node): each part is one `inspect` within depth 3 and 1,500 nodes, and
  together they read every node four levels down exactly once. `buttonsInspect` joins them for the golden hash and
  V6. A truncated part stops `setup` and `run` before any agent starts. The plugin's cap is unchanged.
- **Reordering stays visible (review of #3470).** `inspect` gives each id it is asked for `parentId: null`, so the
  parts joined back record what each part root holds, not where it sits: two variants swapped, or the set and its usage
  panel, read the same. The `reads` program now also returns `buttonsAt`, each part root's child-index path in the page
  worked out at capture time (no ids, so stable across plants), and the golden hash and V6 compare it with the nodes
  (`canonicalButtons`). This changes the golden hash's `buttons` input, so a `golden.json` from an earlier head misses
  its baseline: run `setup` again. Arms `buttons/reorder-variants` and `buttons/reorder-page` run the plant's cut, the
  plugin's own `inspect` and the real `reads` program over a stand-in page; `setup/part-truncated` covers the guard
  that stops `setup` on a truncated part. Mutations: positions dropped from `canonicalButtons` → both reorder arms;
  `cutShort` made `false` → `setup/part-truncated`.
- **The positions are guarded (second review of #3470).** A `reads` capture with no `buttonsAt`, or with a `-1` step,
  now voids a run (`voidReason`) and stops `setup` and `run` before any agent starts (`cutShort`), through one
  `buttonsAtFault`. Without that, a capture missing the positions on both sides hashed `at: null` and a reorder scored
  V6-clean again. The `reads` program finds a child by id (`findIndex`), not by `indexOf`, so a host that returns a new
  object per lookup still gives real positions. Arms: `void/no-positions` and `void/position-minus-one` (golden and
  baseline hashes recomputed over the edited before side), `setup/no-positions`, `setup/position-minus-one`, and
  `buttons/new-objects`. Mutations: the `voidReason` line deleted → both `void/*` arms; the setup refusal dropped →
  both `setup/*` arms; a `-1` let through → `void/position-minus-one` and `setup/position-minus-one`; `indexOf` back →
  `buttons/new-objects`.
- **The plugin is the oracle.** `selftest-figma.ts`'s new `args/*` arms send every command from `setupCommands`,
  `resetCommands` and `captureCommands` (the `reads` program among them) through the plugin's own `parseCommand`, and
  `parseRunCode` for the dev `run-code`, imported from `apps/plugin/src/`, never restated. `parseCommand` drops an arg
  it does not read rather than refusing it, so an arm also fails when the plugin's parsed args differ from what was
  sent. Mutations: the old `depth: 4` back → `args/inspect-buttons`; an unread arg on a snapshot → `args/snapshot-hero`.
- **The rest of the plan, checked.** `file-setup`, `apply-theme`, `build-components`, every `run-code` (version, plant,
  reads), `audit-frames`, the six snapshots and `component-keys` are all taken as sent. The runner's `status`, marker
  and `mark` commands are written inline in its CLI, so the arms do not see them; each is `status {}` or a `run-code`
  with a 30 s timeout.

## (2026-11-06) — Agent adherence setup accepts a build whose only misses are usage panels or members already present (#3466)

The Figma half's `setup` stopped on both kinds of scratch file, because the runner's `send()` throws on any `ok:false`.
A used file answers `build-components button` with `⚠ already built`, and a fresh one builds all 576 variants and the
three sets it nests, then answers `ok:false` because no usage panel was drawn. Test tooling only: the plugin is
unchanged.

- **The diagnosis that made it small.** Both replies are `ok:false` for one reason: the file has no `_Doc-block`, so
  the plugin's missing-template warning turns the build's verdict `⚠`. Members already present are not misses by the
  plugin's own rule (`misses.length === skipped`), so "already built" alone would have been `ok:true`.
- **Read from data, not words.** The agent link strips `causes` from the verdict (`forAgent`), so
  `setupBuildAccepts` reads `completed` from the verdict and the facts the plugin's `ok` comes from in
  `result.data.build`: the report's misses (every one `ALREADY PRESENT`), no stale member, no miss on a set built
  first, and no missing template but `_Doc-block`. Any other `ok:false` still throws, with the reason appended.
- **Setup only.** `send()` takes an `accept` predicate per command key; only `setup()`, now exported, passes one.
  Both sides of `run` stay strict.
- **Self-test.** Five literal replies drive `setup()` through a stand-in client: "already built" and "no usage
  panels" carry on and write `golden.json`; a real miss, panels plus a real miss, and a build that did not complete
  still throw. One more arm shows `send()` without the acceptance still throws on the "already built" reply. With the
  acceptance dropped, `setup/already-built` and `setup/no-usage-panels` fail by name.

## (2026-11-06) — lint-guide-claims: a range-only citation carries its block's fingerprint (#3417)

**Status:** gate and guides only, so no engine bump, no artifact moves and `CONTRACT_VERSION` is unchanged. The
citation format gains an optional `#<8 hex>` suffix, listed in the PR as an owner question with A recommended.

### What changed

- **A FINGERPRINT arm in `lint-guide-claims.ts`.** A citation whose claim quotes nothing was checked for range
  only, so code inserted above it left it pointing at other lines, and the gate stayed green. Each such citation now
  carries `<!-- src: path:a-b#1a2b3c4d -->`: the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the cited lines as the file
  holds them. The gate hashes the lines and fails by name when they differ, and names where the block now sits when
  it is found once elsewhere in the file. A range-only citation with no fingerprint fails.
- **`--stamp`** writes a fingerprint where a citation has none and never rewrites one: a gate allowed to rewrite
  what it reads has no memory. To re-cite changed code, read it, fix the numbers, delete the old fingerprint and
  stamp again.
- **Why a fingerprint, not the issue's merge-base mapping.** A mapping run in CI needs the base's history and is
  only as good as the base: main itself already carried the drift (below), so a base-relative check would have held
  every stale citation to its stale number. The fingerprint needs no history, so it runs the same locally, in CI
  and on a shallow clone.

### The migration: 23 re-points, then 140 stamps

Stamping today's numbers would have locked in the drift main already carries. For example, `agent-link.md:27`
cited `main.ts:2343`, which reads `});`, while `figma.on('close', …)` sits at 2355. So every range-only citation was
checked by content first:
- For each one, find the commit where its claim's prose first appeared, and map the cited range from there to
  `HEAD` through the cited file's line diff (the mapping #3417 proposes).
  - **102 mapped exactly to today's numbers**, with no hunk inside the block. They are unchanged since the claim
    was written.
  - **17 mapped elsewhere.** 15 were re-pointed to the mapped block after reading it. `agent-link.md:61` was already
    two lines off at authoring, and now cites the "Nothing connects while the link is off" comment. `style-guides.md:50`
    keeps its range, which a later PR widened on purpose.
  - **19 had a hunk inside the block.** They were read by hand. 7 were re-pointed: #3432 and #3433 had shifted them by
    offsets that belonged to other ranges (the tool list in `mcp.ts`, `export_theme`, `INSPECT`, the preflight in
    `apply-theme.ts`, `componentDefs` twice, and the page taxonomy). The other 12 still bound the block they were written for.
  - **2 had no origin** under that rule. Both were read and are correct.
- Then `--stamp` fingerprinted all 140. The diff adds nothing but `#<8 hex>`.
- **An independent recompute** (`sed -n a,bp | perl -pe 'chomp if eof' | sha256sum`, no code shared with the gate)
  matches all 140.
- It first disagreed on two: both cited `provenance.ts:1-58` in a 57-line file, which the gate's range check admits
  (an off-by-one, filed separately). Both were re-pointed to `1-57` and re-stamped.

### Verification

Each mutation was committed first and restored with `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>`.
- **One line inserted above `main.ts:2355`.** The gate fails `FINGERPRINT: …agent-link.md:27: …main.ts:2355#13449644 now
  hashes to #9eb0b17b … The block now sits at apps/plugin/src/main.ts:2356`. Main's gate and guides on the same
  shift pass, `140 quote nothing and are checked for range only`.
- **One line inserted above `main.ts:1904`** (the issue's file-setup case). Four range-only citations fail as
  FINGERPRINT, and the two quoting ones fail through CITE, as before.
- **A fingerprint deleted.** The gate fails `…quotes nothing, so only a fingerprint can tell when its code moves, and
  it has none`.
- **A wrong fingerprint, then `--stamp`.** `fingerprinted 0` leaves `#00000000` in place, and the gate still fails.
- **The cited line edited in place.** The gate fails and says the cited code changed.

### For whoever re-verifies this

A fingerprint proves the cited lines are unchanged since they were stamped, not that they were the right lines then.
The audit above is that check for the stamps this PR wrote. A PR that edits a range-only cited block now has to
re-read it to go green, which is the point, and also the cost.

## (2026-11-06) — Agent adherence, code surface: a grouped date entry needs three fields or a date word (#3440)

The owner's Q2 decision for the code half of #3440, A tightened (2026-11-06). In `score-code.ts`'s R5 detector, two
or more selects or numeric inputs grouped under one label, fieldset or role=group are a faked date picker only when
there are exactly three of them (day, month, year) or the group's own label or legend carries a date word, read with
`DATE_RE`. Before, any two counted, so a height fieldset (ft, in) or a split one-time code would have scored faked.

- **The group's words.** A fieldset's own legend, a role=group's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and a label's own
  text without the option text of the selects inside it, so an option such as "2000" can't lend a group a date word.
- **Exactly three, not three or more.** A split one-time code is six numeric inputs under "Code", and the owner's
  wording names it as not caught.
- **Arms, each with a literal expectation.** `R5/three-selects` (faked, 3 fields), `R5/fieldset-numbers` (faked,
  3 fields), `R5/date-word-pair` (faked, date word), `R5/height-fieldset`, `R5/one-time-code` and `R5/neutral-pair`
  (each not faked). The self-test runs 73 assertions.
- **Mutation.** `why` made true for any two or more fails `R5/height-fieldset`, `R5/one-time-code` and
  `R5/neutral-pair` by name, and `R5/date-word-pair` on its reason text.
- **A trap for the next editor.** The detector runs inside a template string, so a backtick in a comment there ends
  the page script and the transform fails before any arm runs.

## (2026-11-06) — Components: a set with kept edits shows its Kept edits tag (#3446)

`statusesOf` (`apps/studio/src/state/update-file.ts`) returns `kept` for a set the file-sets read lists as kept (#3421, Q39 A), and `UPDATE_COPY.status.kept` reads "Kept edits". So Update file listed the set under Kept edits, but its Components row showed no such tag.

### The change

`STATUS_ORDER` gains `kept`, after `due` and before `hand`: the order `statusesOf` already gives them. The tag text is the existing `UPDATE_COPY.status.kept`, "Kept edits", so no new copy. Where it sits in the order is the owner's call (the issue says so), so it is asked A-first on the PR. The guide `build-components.md` lists Kept edits among the states a set can carry.

`test:chrome` section `ia2` (figma, light and dark) plants a file-sets read where tag is `kept`, with its hand edits still posted. Tag's row must read `In file · Kept edits · Hand-edited`, compared as literal status ids and texts. Then the section's own world is posted back. Mutation: `kept` dropped from `STATUS_ORDER` (the bug put back) fails `#3446: a set with kept edits shows Kept edits among its tags on Components` by name, at both appearances.

### Escape review

#3428 added `kept` to `statusesOf` and to the copy, and gated Update file's Kept edits group. Nothing drew a kept set on Components: the `ia2` status arm's world had due, hand-edited, unrecorded and not-in-file sets, but no kept one. `STATUS_ORDER` is a hand list beside the `SetStatus` type, so a new status that is not added to it is dropped without a sound. The new arm plants a kept set.

## (2026-11-06) — The agent-adherence test, Figma half: bridge arms, a call log, a scratch-file plan and a scorer (#3440)

The owner's Q52 A: build the Figma half of #3440's single adherence test in parallel with the code half. This adds the bridge's arm switch and call log, the scratch file's plan and reset, the Mac's runner and the scorer. Nothing has run on the Mac yet; the PR body holds the JOB text for the first run (F0 against F2, 5 runs each, Q3440.3 A).

### What changed

- **`PRISM3_BRIDGE_ARM=0|1|2`** in `tools/figma-bridge/server.ts`, default 2 (today's bridge). Arm 0 sends no `instructions` or `readFirst`, has no resources capability (`resources/*` are method-not-found) and refuses `figma_run context` at the bridge with `unknown-command`, leaving `context` out of both command lists. Arm 1 adds the note. Any other value refuses to start.
- **`--record <file>`**: an `attempt` line per `figma_run` call before it runs, and an `outcome` line after, so a refused call is on record and V7 is scored from the bridge's log rather than the agent's account.
- **`tools/agent-adherence/`**: `figma-plan.ts` (the plant program, which is also the reset; the captures; the golden hash, over both plan pages, the `↳ Buttons` page, the variables with their values and `component-keys`, with ids and the plant's own keys removed), `run-figma.ts` (setup, one run, the invariants, the contamination probe), `score-figma.ts` (R1, R2, R3, R5, R6, R7 and Done), `selftest-figma.ts` and one hand-written good run.

### Verification

- `test-agent-bridge.ts` gains `arm/…` and `record/…`: arm 0's `initialize`, `server/discover`, `tools/list`, `figma_status` and `resources/list` carry none of eleven sentinels written in the test. Mutation: one sentence of the note appended to arm 0's `figma_status` description fails `arm/no-leak: arm 0's tools/list …`.
- `selftest-figma.ts`, 130 assertions after both reviews' fixes (61 at first, 113 after the first review). Mutations, each failing by name: the variant-option check dropped → `R1/bad-variant`; the primitive check dropped → `R2/bad-primitive`; the spec-field test dropped → `R3/bad-fill-override`; R5's report match accepting anything → `R5/bad-silent`; the protected-role diff dropped → `R6/bad-protected`; the version-save search dropped → `good/clean`, `R7/good-version-first`; the write search dropped → `R7/bad-no-version`.
- The self-test found three defects in the first draft, fixed before commit: R2 counted a detached copy's inherited spacing field by field; a refusal was charged to every protected role rather than the one it named; and an id match was a substring match (`2:1` inside `12:1`).

### The review's fixes (CHANGES of 2026-11-06)

- **B1:** the probe voids on a plugin or agent the host didn't ship, not on the built-in ones every host lists (a real `init` line is a fixture), and on a `Task` or `Agent` call. **B2:** its cwd check follows links on both sides (macOS `/var` → `/private/var`). **B3:** the bridge starts as `npx --yes tsx` (pinned to `tsx@4` after the delta review), and `run` starts the agent's bridge as configured, and waits for `listening` on its arm, before anything is sent.
- **S1:** a `skills/`, `CLAUDE.md` or GitHub call voids a run only when its result succeeded, since only arm 2's resources name a `skills/` path. **S2:** static arms read the source of `score-figma.ts` and every local module it reaches (#3450's walk, so a new helper with no policy fails `independence/static-modules`); the review's M5 (the scorer reading `SKILL.md`) now fails `independence/static-names` and `independence/static-reads`. **S3:** the golden hash covers the variables, `component-keys` and `↳ Buttons`, and a change there is V6. **S4:** V7 catches `figma.variables.create…` and compound assignment. **S5:** `--file-name`, a scratch-file marker that `mark` writes and every write checks, the plant's refusal to empty a page it didn't create, and a named version first. The JOB stops on a golden mismatch and runs in a fresh worktree.
- **Nits:** the leak test scans the `context` refusal and `figma_logs`; `R5/bad-swapped`; a deleted page is one V8; a run on another plugin build than setup's is void; R5's word match is a listed blind spot.
- **Q1 A and Q2 A, the owner's to confirm,** each in its own commit: a per-arm count of runs that wrote, next to Done; and a deleted rating stays faked. Reverting either commit removes A; it doesn't build B or C. Q1 B changes the task's wording and Q1 C the bridge's command list, and Q2 B needs a fourth verdict, `removed`, written into the scorer. Each is new code.

### The delta review's fixes (CHANGES of 2026-11-06, 08:39 UTC)

- **B4:** a run whose agent deleted a snapshotted layer or page used to exit before writing its run file, because `snapshot` refuses a missing node and the runner threw on any `ok:false`. The after side now keeps that envelope (`finishRun`), and the scorer reads it as a changed role; a transport error still throws, and the before side stays strict. `after/deleted-snapshot-written`, `-scored`, `after/page-deleted-written`, `after/transport-error` and `after/before-strict` drive it with a stand-in client. Mutation: the keep dropped → the first three fail.

Each fix's mutation fails its arms by name.

Restoring them by re-running `apply-theme` and `build-components` on every reset was left out, untried on a live file.
