## (2026-11-06) — Update file: a second Keep run over a kept set keeps it under Kept edits (#3436)

#3428 records a set whose kept hand edits keep out the plan's values with `held`, so the due read lists it under Kept edits. One run later the record was lost. The first Keep run stamps the set's members with today's plan, so the next dry run reads nothing moved under the edited nodes. It marks none of them `conflict` (`dryRunSet`: a hand edit conflicts only where the plan or the executor moved), `heldOf` finds nothing, and `ledgerAfter` recorded the set as current. The designer's rings still held their red, not the indicator binding.

### The change

`ledgerAfter` takes the ledger as it was before the run (`main.ts` reads it with `readLedger` and passes it in). Under `keep`, while the run still keeps hand edits on the set (`kept` is not empty), the `held` the set's entry carried stands. It is joined with any `held` this run found: members the larger count, each change once. Overwrite and Accept as baseline record no `held`, as before, and nor does a run that finds no hand edits left to keep.

**A technical call, stated:** the ledger's `held` counts members and does not name them. So a run that keeps edits on other members than the held ones still lists the set under Kept edits. That can over-report a kept set, as the dry run's own conflict test can. It never reads one current while its edits keep the plan out.

The verdict of the second run is unchanged. It names the kept edits ("60 hand edits kept (dot size)") but has no "keep out N of the plan's values" line, because that line is built from this run's `held`. Whether it should repeat the line is copy, so it is held for the owner on the PR.

### The gate

`apps/plugin/test-update-kept-main.ts` gains step 4b, through the real `main.ts` under the strict shim. After the first Keep run records radio-control `kept`, radio-control is checked and updated again under the default Keep, with no per-set choice. Premise: the check still reads 30 members edited by hand, and all 30 rings still hold the designer's red. Then the ledger must still carry `held` with 12 members and the three indicator border changes (`main/held survives a second Keep`), and `file-sets` must read radio-control `kept` (`main/kept after a second Keep`). Step 5's Overwrite then still replaces the edits, and the set reads current.

Mutations, each failing both arms by name: `ledgerAfter` ignoring the earlier `held` (the bug put back), and `main.ts` not passing the earlier ledger in.

`apps/plugin/test-update-kept-run.ts` gains `edits gone`, on `ledgerAfter` directly: a Keep run that keeps no hand edits (`kept: []`), over an entry that carries `held`, records no `held`, so a designer who reverts their edits sees the set read current. A control arm with one kept edit carries the `held`. Mutation: dropping ` && o.kept.length` fails `edits gone` by name.

### Escape review

#3428's gates ran one Keep run. The issue was found by mutation-testing that gate, not by a check: nothing ran Keep twice. The new arm is that second run.

## (2026-11-06) — Agent adherence, code surface: the scorer, the packets and the orchestrator (#3440)

The first slice of #3440's single agent-adherence test, under the owner's Q3440.1–.6 (all A). `tools/agent-adherence/`
holds the scorer, its self-test, the C0 and C1 packets and the orchestrator for the code surface. A tool, not a gate.

- **The rules.** R1 (invented name), R2 (raw value or primitive), R4 (below the contrast floor) and R5 (faked or
  silent can't-do), as the proposal specifies them. R3 is N/A until a coded library exists. R4 renders the output in
  Chromium once per mode, with the mode's token values injected as custom properties, and scores the computed colors
  with the engine's `contrast()`, never the agent's declared pairs (`docs/34` shape 1).
- **Independence.** The scorer reads only `packages/engine/out/`, at a pinned commit (`pin.json`, with each file's
  sha256), through `git show`, so a later regen can't move a score. The self-test fails by name if an oracle points at
  the skill or a scoring pass opens `skills/`.
- **The slice, measured.** The six task components' whole entries are 59.7 KB of the 521 KB `components.ai.json`;
  the 820 token names are 21.7 KB. C0 is 98 KB and C1 120 KB.
- **The trap the self-test caught.** A raw hex or `rgb()` value is also a contrast failure in the modes it doesn't
  follow, so the first R2 fixtures failed R4 too. Each bad fixture now plants its raw value where no contrast is
  measured, so every arm fails by one rule only.
- **The arms differ in two things.** C0 is an exact prefix of C1, and C1 adds the skill and the line "Follow this
  skill." that introduces it, so a difference measures the skill as framed by that line.
- **Review fixes.** Contamination now reads tool calls only, never prose, so a C1 run is no longer voided for an
  escaped packet or a mention of the `skills/prism3-rebind/…` path C0 never sees; `Grep`, `Glob`, `Agent` and `Task`
  count as reads. Static arms read the source of the scorer and of every local module it imports (`oracle.ts` today),
  each with its own allow-list, because the read probe saw only `readPinned`; a module with no allow-list fails. R5's report regex reads `dob`, `birthday` and `birth date`, and
  only an interactive node can be called faked by its id or class.
- **Owner's to confirm, built as their recommended A in revertible commits:** Q1, a substitute the report discloses
  stays faked; Q2, two or more selects or numeric inputs grouped as one entry are faked.
- **Known blind spots** are listed in the README: R2 skips negative lengths; R4 doesn't measure `div role=textbox`
  fields or button boundaries, and doesn't composite partial opacity.
- **Not in this PR:** the runs themselves, and the Figma surface.

## (2026-11-06) — An override row's step picker offers the palette the override names (#3406)

On Theme › Color › Interactive, an override row's step picker offered only the row's own ramp. When the stored override named another palette (a brand color `brand-neutral`, as #3391's case does), the picker opened on the row's family with no step current. The designer couldn't see the held step or move within its palette. A re-pick moved the override onto the row's family. The owner chose option A in the lane brief: the picker must show that palette's steps.

### Fix

- `interactive-input.ts` gains `pickerPalettesOf(mode, row)`: the row's own ramp, then the inverse fill's neutral ramp (#1384), then the palette the held override names when it's none of those. A held palette the theme no longer builds (removed, #3391) isn't offered, because it has no steps. `color-interactive.ts` builds the picker's palettes from it. The picker already opens on `current.palette` when that palette is offered, so it opens on the held step.
- A pick in the held palette writes that palette. `writeInteractiveRow` takes `‹palette›::‹step›` on an override row as it already did on the inverse fill. The row's call site sends that form when the picked palette isn't the row's own, and a bare step still writes the row's family.
- Section 3b of `test-interactive-input.ts` uses literal palette lists: `['primary', 'brand-neutral']`, the inverse fill's `['primary', 'neutral', 'brand-neutral']`, and the own ramp alone with no override, a neutral hold, or a removed palette. The move is checked through the engine's own resolved path (`pds3.core.palette.brand-neutral.400`). Section 3391 of `test-chrome.mjs` had pinned the old behavior ("marks no step current"). It now checks that the picker opens on `brand-neutral 350` with the options `[own, brand-neutral]`, and that a pick of `brand-neutral 400` persists there, under the primary family and with the action palette on neutral.
- Mutations, each failing by name: drop the offer (`#3406 offer` in 3b, and `#3406 … opens on brand-neutral` in chrome); ignore `::` in the override write (`#3406 move`); send a bare step from the call site again (`#3406 … a pick of brand-neutral 400 persists`, chrome only, since the unit arm can't see the call site).

### Trap

`stepPicker` reads `current.palette` to choose the palette it opens on, and falls back to the first offered palette without a word. A held palette that isn't offered doesn't raise an error. The picker opens on the row's family with nothing marked, which is exactly the bug.

## (2026-11-06) — Renaming a brand color carries the overrides that name it (#3405)

When a designer renamed a brand color, an override written on that color kept the old name, and the brand stopped building: `overrides[light]: unknown palette 'accent-x' (role 'interactive.primary.border.rest')`. Nothing warned about it. #3403 added a warning to the *remove* confirm, but the rename path had the same gap.

### Diagnosis

`cascadeRename` (`apps/studio/src/state/palette-input.ts`) is docs/24 #53's reference-integrity rule: every field that names the palette follows the rename. It moved the action palette, the link palette, `roleColors`, `interactivePalettes` and gradient stops. It didn't move `overrides[mode][role].palette`, the one per-mode field that stores a palette name as a value.

### Fix

- `cascadeRename` carries every override whose `palette` is the old name over to the new name, in every mode (custom modes included), and keeps its step: the ramp is the same one. It runs inside `renameBrandColor`, so the carry is part of the same state write as the rename. A refused rename (empty, unchanged, or taken) moves nothing.
- Section 10 of `test-interactive-input.ts` is the issue's repro. It uses the prism3 brand, brand color `accent-x`, the primary border overridden to `accent-x 350` in Light and `accent-x 700` in Dark, a third override on `primary` that must not move, and `accent-x 400` in a custom mode, `promo`, so the custom-mode carry is pinned (added after review). It then renames to `accent-y`. The expected overrides are literals. "Still builds" and "resolves to accent-y" come from the engine's own `resolveAllModes`. Mutation: drop the carry, and `#3405 carry` fails by name, all three checks. Restrict the carry to the built-in modes, and the custom-mode arms fail by name (72/76).
- Removal still doesn't cascade overrides. That stays the owner's call (#3403's Q-block). A rename has an answer the removal lacks: the new name is the same ramp.

### Trap

The column's other key is not covered. `interactivePalettes` follows the rename, but `modeAnchors[mode][<old name>]` doesn't, and the engine doesn't refuse it. It ignores the key, so the column's per-mode anchor goes back to its default without any warning (measured: Dark 400 → 500). An override keyed by the column's role path (`interactive.<old>.…`) is probably lost the same way. Filed as #3448, not fixed here.

## (2026-11-06) — lint-token-consumers: a def's evolution history is not a read (#3444)

**Status:** gate change only, so no engine bump, no artifact moves and `CONTRACT_VERSION` is unchanged. Option A of
#3444.

### What changed

- **`lint-token-consumers.ts`.** The `defs` reader walks each def by key path and skips `notes.evolution` (`HISTORY`,
  written in the gate by hand). That field is history: a line saying the icon once took a token kept the token read
  after its binding was gone. The other `notes` fields state live behavior and still read.
- **A floor for the skip.** If no def has a `notes.evolution` field, the gate fails: a rename in the schema would
  otherwise leave the skip matching nothing, and the gate back to counting history without a word.
- **Header.** WHAT COUNTS AS A READ names the skip, and LIMITS says history written in any other field still reads,
  so history belongs in `notes.evolution`.

### Re-measured

Nothing moves today: 621 guaranteed, 382 read (224 by defs), 239 unread, 27 entries. No token on main was read only
by a history note, because #3438 had already reworded Link's evolution line to name no token path. The run reports
58 defs' `notes.evolution` skipped.

### Verification

Each mutation was committed first and restored with `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>`.
- **The issue's case.** Drop ` and color.icon.link.visited on a standalone link's trailing icon` from Link's
  `codeOnly` visited entry and add an evolution line naming the token. The gate fails
  `unclaimed: 'color.icon.link.visited'`. Main's gate on the same tree passes.
- **The inverse.** Keep the binding and add the same evolution line, and the gate passes.
- **The floor.** Point `HISTORY` at `notes.history`, and the gate fails
  `floor: no def has a 'notes.history' field`.

### For whoever re-verifies this

#3447 (`codeOnly` as data) wraps each `codeOnly` entry as `{ class, disposition, description }`. The walk still
reaches the description string, so those reads hold. The two PRs touch different files. If #3447 lands first, run
the gate again and check that the `by defs` count stays 224.

## (2026-11-06) — Update file: a set the apply stopped inside stays due in the as-built ledger (#3424)

After an in-place update, `ledgerAfter` (`apps/plugin/src/update-apply.ts`, called from `updateComponents` in `main.ts`) recorded every set the apply acted on as built from today's def. It left out refused sets only. A set whose outcome has `stopped` (the build's pass threw partway, `applySet`) was recorded too, so `dueOf` read it `current`. Update file's checklist then never offered the update that finishes it, though the verdict says "Run the update again to finish".

### The change

`ledgerAfter` leaves `stopped` outcomes out, as it does refused ones. The set's old entry stands, and the due read keeps it due until a later run finishes it. Nothing else moves: the verdict, the member stamps and the rest of the run are as they were.

### The gate

`apps/plugin/test-update-kept-main.ts` gains step 2b, through the real `main.ts` under the strict shim. After Theme, tag alone is checked and updated, and the host throws once on the 40th `unlockAspectRatio` call among tag's nodes, inside the build's pass. The verdict reads `✗ update stopped at tag`. Then `file-sets` must read tag `due` (`main/stopped stays due`). Step 3 then checks again and runs the update, which finishes tag: the gate's later arms read it `current`, as before.

Mutation: `ledgerAfter` filtering refused outcomes only (the bug put back) fails `main/stopped stays due`, which reads tag `current`.

### Escape review

`test-update-apply.ts`'s stop section stops a run inside a set and shows the next run finishes it. It drives `applyUpdate` alone, so it never reaches the ledger. `test-update-kept-main.ts`, the one gate that reads the ledger `main.ts` writes, had no stopped run. The new arm is that run.

### Noticed, filed separately

A stopped set's verdict line always reads "0 members updated": `applySet` sets `updated` only after the build's pass returns, so a throw inside it leaves the count at 0, though some members were written. Filed as #3449.

## (2026-11-06) — `codeOnly` as data: a class register and a four-way disposition (#3441)

Owner decision #3437 Q1 A. Each def's `anatomy.codeOnly` entry was one line of prose, so nothing could count or diff what the design file leaves to code. Each entry is now `{ class, disposition, description }`:
- `class` is an id from `CODE_ONLY_CLASSES` in `packages/engine/code-only-register.ts`, a declared list of 21 classes, each with its meaning;
- `disposition` is one of four keys, `carried`, `lowered`, `refused` or `unsupported`, whose printed names (CARRIED / LOWERED / REFUSED / UNSUPPORTED, the outside reference's) sit in one constant, `DISPOSITION_NAMES`. The owner kept these names (Q3441.1 A); a later rename edits that constant and no def;
- `description` is the prose, kept whole. It still leads with the name an admission needs.

### What moved
- `component-schema.ts`: `codeOnly: CodeOnlyEntry[]`; validation requires each entry's description; `admits()` reads the description.
- All 482 source entries (530 across the 60 registered defs, templates counted per def) were migrated by a one-off AST script that wrapped each literal in place. The classification was mechanical from each entry's leading term, with a short list of hand overrides, then reviewed class by class. By class: semantics 74, not-projected 48, runtime-behavior 51, right-to-left 47, responsive-layout 36, and 16 more classes. By disposition: CARRIED 2, LOWERED 114, REFUSED 242, UNSUPPORTED 172. Whether each class fits its prose is a reading call for review.
- `components.ai.json` adds `syncBoundary` per component (class and disposition name, never the prose); its format moves `prism3-component-docs/1.0` → `1.1` (a field added: minor). The maintainer record carries all three fields.
- The component-defs export (#3433) carries the same `syncBoundary` on every def: the field sits in `project-def.ts`, which both payloads compose. `schema/component-defs.schema.json` gains it, and the format moves `prism3-component-defs/1.1` → `1.2` (a field added: minor) in the schema's `$id`, its `const`, `COMPONENT_DEFS_FORMAT` and `test.ts`. Page navigation (#3380) had already moved it `1.0` → `1.1` for `currentIndicator`.
- The plugin's maintainer-prose strip cuts `description` to its subject and keeps the class and disposition.
- Plans keep `codeOnly` as the prose list (`codeOnlyText`), so no plan digest, executor input or Figma emission moved, and `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.
- Docs: `docs/28` §4 (the sync boundary as data) and the build-component skill.

### The gate
`lint-code-only-classes.ts`: UNREGISTERED CLASS, NO DISPOSITION, NO DESCRIPTION, DEAD CLASS (a register id no entry uses), ADMISSION CLASS (an entry leading with an unprojected axis or state, by a restated `admits()`, must be `not-projected`), PAYLOAD (syncBoundary against the defs), REGISTER, and floors of 50 defs and 450 entries. Mutations, each committed first and restored with `git show HEAD:<path>`:
- `forced-colors` → `forced-colours` on a divider entry → `UNREGISTERED CLASS: divider.anatomy.codeOnly[4]`;
- a divider entry's disposition deleted → `NO DISPOSITION: divider.anatomy.codeOnly[4]`;
- a `print-styles` class added to the register → `DEAD CLASS: 'print-styles'`;
- Button's `width` admission reclassed `responsive-layout` → `ADMISSION CLASS: button.anatomy.codeOnly[5] admits 'width'`.

### Merging page navigation (#3380)
- PageNav's 10 and PageNav.Item's 7 `codeOnly` entries arrived as strings and are converted. No register class was added: each entry follows the class and disposition its nearest precedent already uses (Tabs and Tab for the semantics, keyboard, overflow and RTL entries; Link for the underline; the brand-setting and item-count entries LOWERED, as everywhere else).
- Link's `semantics` / REFUSED current-page entry takes #3380's longer sentence: the bar's width is the brand's Current page indicator.
- Both PRs moved `prism3-component-defs` `1.0` → `1.1` by the identical edit, which git merges silently and no gate notices; this PR raises it to `1.2` by hand.
- #3380's change note says 227 committed artifacts (229 on the merged tree) and omits the defs-export `1.0` → `1.1` move. `lint-emission-version` (ONE WRITER) refuses an edit to another PR's pending note, so the correction is a note of this PR's own, `changes/claude-3441-codeonly-data-2.md`. This is mechanical fallout of the merge.
- #3380's code-contract arm in `test.ts` joined `codeOnly` as strings; it reads `codeOnlyText` now.

### Traps
- Two PRs that each raise a payload format by the same identical edit merge clean: the second lander must raise it again by hand.
- An entry the schema reads as an admission must be an axis or state the def declares and does not project. Divider's `decorative` is a prop, so reclassing it does not fire ADMISSION CLASS. The mutation that proves that arm is Button's `width`.
- `lint-icon-count` walks every shipped string for the icon defs; `syncBoundary[].class` and `.disposition` are ids, listed in its `NOT_PROSE`.
- Merging #3433 conflicts in `emit-component-docs.ts` and `lint-component-docs.ts`: keep both import sides, and take main's `export { projectDef };`. `syncBoundary` belongs in `project-def.ts`; taking main's side as written drops it, and `lint-code-only-classes` then fails `PAYLOAD` on every def.

`CONTRACT_VERSION` is unchanged: no token name moves. Version classes: engine minor (`changes/claude-3441-codeonly-data.md`, and the `-2` correction); both payload formats minor (component-docs 1.0 → 1.1, component-defs 1.1 → 1.2); `EXECUTOR_REVISION` unchanged.

## (2026-11-06) — Page navigation: a navigation of links between sibling pages, and the current page's bar width as a brand setting (#3345)

### What landed
- **PageNav** (`page-nav`) and **PageNav.Item** (`page-nav-item`), built from the owner decisions of 2026-11-03 on #3345. A page-to-page switch is a `<nav>` of links with `aria-current="page"`; Tabs stays for in-place panels (Q1 A). The look is Link's, not the tab look (Q2): the item nests Link, at its standalone look: the other pages plain at rest and underlined at hover (Q7 B), and the current page plain, with Link's 2px current-page bar (`selection=selected`). There's no baseline. Two components, 6 members.
- **`currentIndicator: full | partial`**, the brand setting (Q2 A). Partial is the engine default (Q10 B): round(0.5 × the title's width), centered. Full is the title's width. It moves Link's current-page bar, because a nested instance can't differ from its main component, so every current link in a brand draws the same bar.
- **`footShare`**, a part field. Both executors draw a foot bar at a share of its parent, centered, constrained `SCALE` across so a longer label keeps the share. The readback reads the constraint off the plan's share, and `test-roundtrip.ts` builds and reads back the Partial-materialized Link (`link@partial`) so that branch is gated. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` is raised for it, to 54, which redraws `link` alone.

- **The component-defs export carries the setting.** The export (#3433) restates the plugin's lever chain, so `currentIndicator` joins its brand `settings` and its chain, and the export's format moves to `prism3-component-defs/1.1` (a field added). `test-roundtrip.ts`'s off-defaults brand sets it to `full`.

### Gates
Arms in `packages/engine/test.ts`, each with literals typed from the decision comment:
- `#3345 page-nav code contract`: `<nav`, `<a href` and `aria-current="page"` are present, and no tab role, tablist or aria-selected.
- `#3345 tabs ↔ page-nav cross-reference`: Tabs and PageNav each name the other.
- `#3345 page-nav items`: every item nests Link, the current page at standalone/selected; the other pages are plain at rest and underlined at hover (Q7 B), read off the Link member each lands on.
- `#3345 page-nav indicator: Partial is the engine default`: the lever's default and the null brand's Link bar (Q10 B).
- `#3345 page-nav indicator: 2px`: the bar binds `border-width/thick`, which is 2px in every brand.
- `#3345 page-nav indicator: Full … / Partial …`: on both executor legs, Full is the title's width at x 0, and Partial is round(0.5 × title) at x = (title − bar) / 2 with `SCALE`.

The mutations each failed by name; they're listed on the PR.

### Owner decisions (2026-11-03, on the PR)
Q1–Q5, Q8, Q9 and Q12 A as drafted. Q7 B: the other pages are plain at rest, underlined at hover. Q10 B: Partial is the engine default. Q6 A: the reference fixture sets Partial in a follow-up. Q11 A: a KB component brief is filed.

### Found while building
At Full width the 2px bar sits just below the 1px underline's position, so on the engine default brand the current page reads close to an underlined link: thicker and lower, but the same color and length. Partial reads as clearly different. This finding led to Q10 B: Partial is now the default.

### Trap
- The early renders were drawn in a browser from the projected plans, not from the plugin shim. The shim measures text as `characters × 6`, which is too crude to show a reviewer. The executors' bar arithmetic is the part the arms hold.
- `lint-rung-names` wants PageNav's prop ladder small→medium beside variants medium-first, admitted as `DEFAULT_FIRST`, the way Breadcrumbs does it. Putting the prop in variant order fails as a stale admission.

so its component surface digest, moves). `CONTRACT_VERSION` is unchanged: no token name moves.

## (2026-11-06) — Activity drawer draws a run's causes (#3326 PR 2)

**STATUS: done.** Second of the four PRs in #3326's build plan (§4). Owner decisions Q3326.1 A, Q3326.4 A to Q3326.8 A,
#3308 Q3308.1 A, and Q3390.1 A to Q3390.3 A (2026-11-05). PR 1 (causes as data, #3389) is in `main`. This branch merged
`main` and was never rebased.

### What it does

**Causes first.** A bad result's causes come first in its Activity row, one disclosure each, with the first one open
(`causesEl`, `apps/studio/src/shell/activity.ts`). Closed, a cause reads its mark, the set's name in emphasis, what
happened, then `· <first reason>` clipped to one line. Open, it shows every reason, one per line, then its why, what
stays and what to do, under the approved labels "What stays:" and "What to do:". The set is named from the panel's
catalog (`nameOf`), never by a writer. `splitLines`' positional pick is gone, so no line is "the reason" because of
its place, and `.p3-op-reason` goes with it. The status line's finish words use the first cause's first reason when
there is one.

**Update file is one row** (Q3326.4 A, Q3390.1 A). `main.ts` lends the latest run it started (`UpdateReading`): each
step's name, the operation that runs it, and, once it ended, its verdict and that operation's lines, causes and publish
description as they stood then. The drawer files a step's operation under the run instead of on its own row. It knows
which verdicts are the run's by their `ref`, kept for the whole session (`runRefs`), so a later run does not hand an
earlier run's verdict back to the operation's row. Every other writer keeps its own row: an agent's command, Check, the
boot Read-back, Clean up, Draw specs, and a build from Components. The row reads "Update file" and the status strip's
verdict ("Stopped at To add", "Theme applied"). Its body is the causes, then the notes, then "Steps". Each step has its
mark, name and verdict words, and its mono lines sit behind its own closed disclosure (Q3326.6 A). A step the run never
reached reads with a dash and "Not run" (Q3326.8 A). The panel fills each cause's `step` with the step's name. The run
counts once.

**"Update again"** (Q3390.2 A) is the run's one next step. It opens Update file again, and that checklist reads the file
afresh and checks what is due. It does not replay the run's steps, because the run's own writes moved the hashes its
update step compared, so a replay would be refused as "changed since the check". No step offers a button.

**Notes** (Q3390.3 A, Q3326.7 A). `note` is now a `Cause` kind (`apps/plugin/src/messages.ts`, accepted by
`write-adapter.ts`). It is drawn under a "Note" or "Notes" label with the info mark, its step in emphasis, then what it
says. It counts nothing, and a clean run stays clean. No writer sends one yet; PR 4's split is the first. `mergeCauses`
ranks the kinds so a note never hides a warning.

**Two fixes the run row needed.**
- A refusal that ended a step is the run's. The step already carries the host's words, so it no longer opens a lone
  operation row holding only "Refused".
- The bar row leads with the most recent row by a sequence stamp (`Rec.at`), not by the clock's minute. A run row and
  an older operation row can share one minute, and the older one used to win the tie.

### Tests

- `apps/studio/test-chrome.mjs` section `3326` (shard 3), light and dark, at 1280 and 380, each with literal
  expectations:
  - The owner's first run: causes first, no positional reason, every line kept.
  - A run stopped at To add: one "Update file" row reading "Stopped at To add", with no Set up file row. The body is
    causes, then "Steps", then next steps. Badge's cause carries its step "To add". The steps are Set up file ✓ "File
    set up", To add ✗ "Build failed", and Style guides with a dash and "Not run". There is no button in a step, the next
    steps are "Update again" and "Copy details", and the count is one failure. "Update again" opens Update file and
    posts nothing.
  - An agent's Build set after the run keeps its own row.
  - A clean run whose To add step sends a note: "Note", the info mark, "To add: <what>", no cause, "Sets added", and no
    count.
- Section 10 now reads the run row where it read a step's operation row after an Update file run: the running Theme, the
  clean Theme run, Set up file's failure and warning, its rerun and history, the #3128 refusal, and the #3308 runs. The
  agent's Set up file result keeps its own row. Section 3150 opens the run row's lines.
- `test-write-adapter.ts` accepts a note on a clean verdict; its unknown-kind arm uses `info`.

### Mutations, each failing by name at all four cells

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| A button drawn in each step | `… no step offers a button; the run offers "Update again" and "Copy details"` |
| A note counted as a warning (`counts`) | `… a note adds nothing to the count, and the run stays clean` |
| `owned` folding every operation into the run | `… an agent's Build set after the run keeps its own row, not a step of the run` |
| A never-run step drawn without "Not run" | `… a step the run never reached is listed with a dash and "Not run", and no disclosure` |
| `splitLines` put back (earlier push) | `#3326 figma … no line is set apart as the reason by its place` |

### Left for later PRs

- The row's verdict uses the strip's words alone. The renders' "· 5 sets with problems" suffix has no general form in
  the drafted copy, so it waits for PR 4 (the words).
- A `⚠` Set up file step stops the run. The run row and the count read it as a failure, as the strip does, while the
  step keeps its warning mark.
- PR 3 scopes the count to the latest run.

## (2026-11-05) — Components shows what's already in the file: a checked, disabled box and an In file tag (#3439)

Owner decisions Q-IF.1 A, Q-IF.2 A and Q-IF.3 A, superseding Q3129.6 A's empty cell for a set the file holds. On the
plugin's Components page a set already in the file drew no box, so the owner saw blank space where the checkbox would
be. Now:

- **Q-IF.1 A:** a set or family the file holds whole draws its box checked and disabled, in the chrome's existing
  checkbox pattern (`role="checkbox"`, `aria-checked="true"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, the held style #3306 already
  draws). Its accessible name is `{name} is in this file` (DRAFT, the issue's draft; the final wording is the owner's).
  A tick on it writes nothing.
- **Q-IF.2 A:** an **In file** tag sits first among a row's status tags, as in `In file · Due`.
- **Q-IF.3 A:** a family partly in the file keeps an active box; a tick adds only the missing sets, as before. Once every
  set of it is in the file, its box is checked and disabled.

### How
- `state/component-groups.ts`: `inFileOf(catalog, ids, present)`, true when the file holds a set of `ids` and could add
  none of them (`addableOf` empty). `boxOfSets` is unchanged: a box with something to add is three-state as before.
  `GROUPS_COPY.inFile` and `GROUPS_COPY.inFileName`.
- `domains/components.ts`: `boxOrCell` draws the in-file box where it drew the empty cell, when `inFileOf` holds.
  `statusTags` puts In file first when any of its sets is in the file. On a family that holds mixed statuses the
  existing `has.delete('current')` rule is kept, and In file still shows, since it says the family holds some of its
  sets (the issue's "shows when any set is in the file").
- Unchanged: the held state, the queued state, the web (no file, no boxes, no tag), private parts (no box), the tier
  actions, and a **section of several rows** (Fields, Other components, Subcomponents): it is no family, so with
  nothing to add it keeps its empty cell. A section that stands in for one family (Buttons, Tag, Radio…) draws the
  family's in-file box. Held for the owner on the PR.

### The audit learned one thing
The chrome's contrast audit holds every disabled control to its appearance's disabled roles, and read a `.p3-check`'s
mark as a ghost button's glyph (`disabled.icon`). No checked, disabled check box had been audited before, so it never
met a mark that sits inside the box, on `disabled.fill`, which the CSS draws in `disabled.on-fill`. That is the role
DB1 A already holds the fixed Light row's mark to, read from the emission. The audit now holds a mark inside
`.p3-check-box` to `disabled.on-fill` and every other glyph as before.

### Verification
`test-component-groups.ts` section 2c and `test-chrome.mjs` sections 3129 (light and dark at 1280, light at 380) and
IA2, with literal expectations. Mutations, each committed first and failing by name: the empty cell drawn again →
`3129 figma … Q-IF.1 A: a set or family the file holds draws its box checked and disabled …`; the tag dropped →
`3129 figma … Q-IF.2 A: In file sits first …` and `IA2 figma … #3439 Q-IF.2 A`; a partly-in family's box disabled →
`3129 figma … Q-IF.3 A: a family partly in the file keeps an active box …`. `inFileOf` mutations fail
`Q-IF.1 A` and `Q-IF.3 A` in the unit test. The guide `build-components.md` names the new state and its citations moved
by content.

## (2026-11-05) — The component-defs export: TypeScript stays the source, a generated JSON export maps to Specs (#3425)

**Status:** engine module + two committed artifacts + gates + CLI, MCP and Studio surfaces. ENGINE minor (change
note). CONTRACT unchanged: no token path moves. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. `regen --check` grows
by two artifacts, so `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` in `verify.ts` and the count in `ci.yml` move to 227 together.

### The decision this builds (Q45 A)

The component definitions stay one TypeScript `ComponentDef` per file, the only hand-edited form. What is new is a
**published, generated JSON export** of them: brand-neutral (token names) and per brand (settings resolved), mappable
to `@directededges/specs-schema` (`docs/13` §3: conformant-or-mappable). It closes the "final on-disk format" question
`component-schema.ts`'s header left open.

### Why a sibling of `specs.json`, not `specs.json` versioned

`specs.json` is the spec-sheet model (#2830), read by the plugin's spec panel and each page's Specs section; the
def-level fields (props, states, accessibility, `avoidWhen`, relationships) already ship as `components.ai.json`, read by
the docs. Each has its own contract and its own readers. So the export **composes** the two and re-projects nothing:
each entry is `projectDef(def)` (the `components.ai.json` entry, field for field) beside `componentSpec(def)` (the
`specs.json` entry, or the brand's materialization of it). One file a consumer takes whole; neither existing contract
moves. The cost is bytes: the two committed files are 2.0 MB and 1.7 MB.

### What changed

- **`packages/engine/component-defs-export.ts`** (new, `@prism3/engine/component-defs-export`):
  `exportComponentDefs(defs, { brand? })` and `toSpecsComponents(doc)`. A brand export resolves the brand's component
  settings (`brandMaterializer`, restating the plugin's `materializerFor`, since the engine must not import a surface)
  and puts each geometry token's px, in the brand's default mode, beside its name. `brand.settings` lists every
  component setting the Studio offers, defaults filled in: the eight that move a def's bindings, plus Radio dot size
  and the raised surface, which move a token's value (they reach the spec as px, never as a different token name).
- **`packages/engine/project-def.ts`** (new): `projectDef` moved out of `emit-component-docs.ts` (re-exported there),
  so a surface can bundle it without the emitter's I/O.
- **Emission:** `out/components/component-defs.json` and `out/components/component-defs.specs.json`, both payload in
  `payload-manifest.json`. Per-brand exports are written on demand and never committed.
- **CLI:** `cli.ts <design.md> --component-specs` writes `<id>.component-defs.json` and `<id>.component-defs.specs.json`.
- **MCP:** `export_theme` takes `include: ["componentSpecs"]`, which is opt-in, so a call that names no sections
  writes what it always wrote.
- **Studio:** Export gets a third artifact, **Component specs**, with **↓ Download component specs**, for the brand on
  screen. The web bundle carries no component definitions (an existing rule: `test-shell-imports.ts`,
  `vercel-ignore-check.mjs`), so the plugin's iframe entry provides the exporter, the same way it provides the
  component catalog (`apps/plugin/src/ui/component-specs-export.ts` → `studio/src/state/component-specs-export.ts`).
  On the web the artifact shows as off, and says why (Q3425.2 below).

### Versioning: how a consumer tells what changed

- `format` (`prism3-component-defs/1.0`, equal to the schema's `$id`) is the **shape** of the file: minor for a field
  added, major for one removed or renamed.
- `engineVersion` answers "what code produced this?" and moves with any def change, like every emitted artifact.
- `contractVersion` answers "do these token names still resolve?" Every token name in the export belongs to that
  contract, so a consumer holding a cached export compares this one first.
- `digest` per component (FNV-1a over its entry) says **which** components changed between two exports without a
  diff. That is the per-component signal the consumer change log (#3411) can read.

### The Specs mapping, field by field

Specs closes `Component`, `Element` and `AnatomyElement` (`additionalProperties: false`) and opens `$extensions` on
two things only: a prop and a token reference. So a Prism3 field either rides `$extensions["com.prism3"]` on the prop
or token it belongs to, or is omitted from the projection and kept in the Prism3 export.

| Prism3 (`component-defs.json`) | Specs (`component-defs.specs.json`) |
|---|---|
| `def.name` | `title` |
| `spec.anatomy[].part` (path) | `anatomy` key: the leaf name, or the whole path where two leaves share a name |
| `spec.anatomy[].kind` | `anatomy.<key>.type`: frame → `container`, text → `text`, glyph → `glyph`, slot → `slot`, instance and swap → `instance` |
| `spec.nesting[]` instance `component` | `anatomy.<key>.instanceOf` |
| `def.props[]` boolean | `BooleanProp` (`default`, false when unset) |
| `def.props[]` with `values` | `EnumProp` (`enum`, `default` when it is one of the values) |
| `def.props[]` number | `NumberProp` |
| `def.props[]` slot / node / `anyOf` | `SlotProp` (`anyOf`; `minItems` → `minChildren`; `maxItems` → `maxChildren`) |
| `def.props[]` other | `StringProp` (`default: null`, or the default plus `examples`, which only the string shape admits) |
| prop `description`, `required`, `deprecated`, type prose | `props.<name>.$extensions["com.prism3"]` |
| `spec.axes[]` not already a prop (incl. `state`) | `EnumProp` of the axis values; `axis` kind and `figmaName` under `com.prism3` |
| `spec.codeOnlyStates` | `props.state.$extensions["com.prism3"].codeOnlyStates` |
| the default member (each axis at its first value) | `default`: `configuration`, `layout` (the part tree), `elements.<key>.styles` |
| `spec.redlines` / `type` / `colors` rows off the default | `variants[]`: one per row coordinate (`where` → `configuration`), its parts' styles under `elements` |
| `paddingTop/Right/Bottom/Left` | `styles.padding` (`Sides`: `top`, `end`, `bottom`, `start`) |
| `gap`, `height`, `minHeight`, `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` | `itemSpacing`, `height`, `minHeight`, `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` |
| a token value | `TokenReference` (`$token`, `$type: dimension`); a brand export prefixes the brand's root |
| a literal or derived px | a number |
| `textStyle` | `styles.typography`, `TokenReference` (`$type: typography`) |
| `fill` / `stroke` / `ink` / `icon` | `backgroundColor` / `strokes` / `textColor` / `fillColor`, `TokenReference` (`$type: color`) ; `icon` lands on the element for its part, which is an `instance` element (a nested icon) far more often than a `glyph` one: see the traps |
| per-brand px | `TokenReference.$extensions["com.prism3"].px` |

**What Prism3 carries that Specs has no place for, kept in the Prism3 export and omitted from the projection:**

| Prism3 | Why it has no Specs home |
|---|---|
| Brand settings (`brand.settings`) | `Component` and `metadata` are closed; `metadata` also requires a Figma `source` node |
| Token bindings per state across brands | The projection is one brand (or none) at a time; the Prism3 export per brand is the cross-brand form |
| Nesting rules (`follows`, `exposes`, `when`, `where`, swap and slot properties) | `Element` is closed; only `instanceOf` maps |
| Code-only states | Carried on the `state` prop's extension, the one open place |
| `accessibility`, `content`, `docs`, `ai` (incl. `avoidWhen`), `motion`, `composition` (relationships) | No Specs field; `Component` is closed |
| `aliases`, `category`, `status`, `summary`, `description`, `inherits` | No Specs field |
| Figma component properties (`spec.properties`) | Specs props here are the code API; a Figma-only property has no code prop to ride |
| `rowGap`, `buildWidth`, `buildHeight`, computed (per-file) values, gradients, the provider `literal` record | No matching style, or no single value to write |

### The gates

- **Bytes:** `regen --check` byte-checks both files. Mutation: `radio-control`'s `def.ai.avoidWhen` hand-edited, and
  `regen --check` fails naming `out/components/component-defs.json`.
- **Its own schema:** `lint-component-docs.ts` arm G validates the committed export against the authored
  `schema/component-defs.schema.json` (`json-schema-lite`, closed objects), holds each `def` and `spec` to the two
  committed projections and each `digest` to an FNV-1a it recomputes, and validates a live brand export for every
  example brand and one brand with every setting off its default. Tag, Text field, Dialog, Banner and Radio must each
  draw a different spec with and without the one setting that moves them, compared brand to brand so both sides carry
  px. The same hand edit fails as `DEFS DEF` + `DEFS DIGEST`; a field added and a color moved fail as `DEFS SCHEMA` +
  `DEFS SPEC` + `DEFS DIGEST`; the exporter ignoring `tagStyle` fails `DEFS SETTINGS` on `tag`; dropping px resolution
  fails it on `radio-control`. The first draft of that check compared a brand export with the neutral one, which
  differs on px alone and so could not fail; it was rewritten before review.
- **The Specs mapping, independent of our code:** `packages/tokens/check-specs.mjs` (run by
  `check:consumability`) imports nothing from the engine. It validates every component against the published
  `@directededges/specs-schema` 0.39.0 (pinned exact, integrity in the lockfile) with stock Ajv, and checks that the
  projection carries every component, code prop, axis, part and token of the export and nothing else. Mutations: a
  free-string prop without its disambiguator fails `[VALID]` (`oneOf`); a token renamed in the projection fails
  `[REPRESENTED]`. `[REPRESENTED]` compares token *sets*, so it cannot see where a token lands; `[PLACED]` (added in
  review) reads every export binding at the Specs key a literal register in the gate names (the mapping table, typed
  out, not read from the projector), on its part's element, in the default or in the variant configured at its row's
  coordinate: 5,622 bindings. Mutations: `fill` written to `textColor` and `ink` to `backgroundColor` fails
  `[PLACED] button container … fill … belongs at styles.backgroundColor … (it sits at styles.textColor)`; padding
  left and right swapped fails `[PLACED] button container … paddingRight … belongs at styles.padding.end`; the
  coordinate fix below reverted fails `[PLACED] banner: two variants are configured …`. `[PLACED]` found one defect
  on its first run: Banner's redline and color rows name the same coordinate in different key orders, and the
  projector keyed variants on the raw object, so nine Banner coordinates were each two variants, one with the
  geometry and one with the colors. Variants are now keyed on the coordinate in axis order (1,346 → 1,337 variants;
  only Banner moves).
- **The materializer restatement:** `apps/plugin/test-roundtrip.ts` holds `brandMaterializer` to the plugin's
  `materializerFor` on every def, for no brand, each example brand and one brand with every setting off its default.
  Mutation: the tag-style lever dropped from `brandMaterializer` fails `… for every setting off its default … differs on tag`.

### Traps for whoever re-verifies

- Specs' `AnyProp` is a `oneOf`, and its string and enum shapes overlap: `{type: "string"}`, with or without a string
  `default`, matches both. The projection writes `default: null` or adds `examples`, which only the string shape
  admits. Drop that and seven components fail.
- The Specs package exports its schemas, not its `package.json`; `check-specs.mjs` resolves a schema to find it.
- **`icon` → `fillColor` lands on `instance` elements.** The published schema describes `fillColor` as "Glyph fill
  color. Present on GLYPH element type only" (and `textColor` as TEXT only). That is description text, not a
  constraint, so the projection validates; but in the committed projection 981 of the 1,039 `fillColor` styles sit on
  `instance` elements (a nested icon, e.g. `button.leadingVisual`) and 58 on `glyph` ones. A Specs reader that keys on
  element type may drop them. Kept as is, on purpose: the icon color is a binding of the part that holds the nested
  icon, and Specs has no other color key for an instance; omitting it would lose the binding, and moving it under
  `$extensions` is not open on `Element` styles. Recorded here and in the mapping table rather than changed.
- A coordinate written in two key orders (`{tone, width}` and `{width, tone}`) is one coordinate: the projector keys
  variants on it in axis order. `[PLACED]` fails on two variants with the same configuration.
- `cli.ts --component-specs` without `--out` writes into `packages/engine/out/`, where the files are untracked and make
  `regen --check` count two more. Pass `--out`.

### Owner questions (option A is the recommendation)

**Q3425.1 — the Studio copy.** A: as drafted. The artifact is labeled **Component specs**, described as "Every
component's props, states, parts and the tokens each part binds, built with this brand's component settings. As Prism3
JSON and in the Specs format."; the button reads **↓ Download component specs**; the settings column reads "Nothing to
set — the specs follow this brand's component settings."; after a failed restore: "Off after a failed restore: these
specs would be the demo brand's, not this file's." B: other wording.

**Q3425.2 — the web Studio.** The web bundle carries no component definitions, by an existing rule, and the export is
built from them. A: on the web the artifact shows as off, with "In the Figma plugin: the specs are built from the
component definitions, which the web Studio leaves out." (as built). B: hide the artifact on the web. C: load the
definitions on demand on the web (a separate chunk, about 1.9 MB, 566 KB gzipped, measured when they were bundled
whole); filed as #3429 rather than built here.

## (2026-11-05) — Update file ticks Theme only when the file differs from the brand (#3422, Q44 A)

**What.** Update file's checklist always opened with Theme ticked (Q2909.2 A). The badge counted Theme only when the
file's variables differed from the brand (`badgeParts`, the live recount's `theme`). So a run with nothing to change
still re-applied the whole brand, and the checklist looked as if something was due. In real Figma the owner saw
"1 update" for a real Theme change, then wondered whether Theme is ever unticked. Q44 A (the owner, 2026-11-04): Theme
opens ticked only when the file differs from the brand. When it matches, the row stays, unticked, tagged "Up to date",
and can still be ticked to apply the brand again. This supersedes the always-ticked part of Q2909.2 A. Theme is still
always an item.

- `themeDueOf(live)` (`apps/studio/src/state/update-file.ts`) is the one signal: the live recount answered, could read
  the file, and says it differs. `badgeParts` counts Theme on it, and `defaultTicks` (a new `live` argument) ticks
  Theme on it, so the badge and the ticks agree. A file that is not set up holds no brand, so its Theme is always
  ticked; this keeps its cover step (#3308).
- `shell/update-file.ts` keeps the recount it opened with (`liveAtOpen`). The default tick and the tag read it, and the
  first due read asks against the brand that tick picks (#3023 Q701 B). So a recount landing while the checklist is open
  moves neither the ticks nor the counts.
- "Up to date" is the sets' existing status word (`UPDATE_COPY.themeCurrent`, held equal to `status.current` by the test).
- Before the first recount answers, and on the plugin's demo brand, where the panel shows no recount (`liveShown`), the
  badge counts no Theme, so Theme opens unticked. Ticking it is the way to apply the brand there.

**Tests.**
- `test-update-file.ts`: literal expectations. A file that matches opens Theme unticked and "Up to date". One that
  differs opens it ticked. With no recount, or a failed one, it is unticked. A file not set up ticks it. The badge
  count equals the ticked count (2 and 2 matching, 3 and 3 differing). Mutation: `defaultTicks` ticking Theme always
  fails `Q44 A ticks: a file that matches the brand opens with Theme unticked`, `Q44 A badge = ticks: … matches …` and
  two more, by name.
- `test:chrome` section 10: on a set-up file with no recount, Theme is unticked with no tag (Q44.2 A, below). After a
  recount saying the file matches, it is unticked and tagged "Up to date"; after one saying it differs, ticked, with no tag. The same mutation, built, fails `Q44 A Update file …` by name at
  every width and theme. The IA2 case plants the recount its unapplied Pill implies. Section 3170 unticks Theme only
  when it opens ticked.
- `test:verdict`: the arms that need a Theme run tick it by hand (`tickTheme`), as a designer forcing a re-apply would.
  The drivers that untick it do so only when it opens ticked.
- `test:chrome` cases that run the Theme step on the demo brand (sections 30b, 31, 3150) tick it by hand (`tickTheme`).

**Guides.** `apply-a-theme.md` and `update-a-file-safely.md` said Theme is ticked each time the dialog opens; they now
say when it is, and that it reads "Up to date" otherwise. The other guides' citations into `update-file.ts` follow the
lines this change moved (`lint-guide-claims`).

**After review: two recommended options, built as their own commits. The owner confirmed both on 2026-11-05 (Q44.1 A,
Q44.2 A).**

- **Q44.2 A: "Up to date" only when measured.** The tag rendered on `!themeDueOf(live)`, which is also true before the
  recount answers, when it failed, and on the demo brand: nothing had been compared. It now renders on
  `themeMatchesOf(live)`, a recount that read the file and found it matching. The tick is unchanged. Mutation: the tag
  back on `!themeDueOf` fails section 10's `Q44 A Update file … no recount has measured …` by name at every width.
- **Q44.1 A: the signal reads what was written, not only the input.** The recount's `theme` compared the saved brand
  input alone (`holdsInput`), so an engine update that moves the variables under an unchanged brand read "matches", and
  #3428's themeBlocked sets could not ride: merged with #3428, its gate failed 9 checks. Apply Theme now stamps the
  print of the plans it wrote beside the input (`apps/plugin/src/theme-emission.ts`, FNV of the plans' JSON). The
  recount (`themeDue`) reads Theme due when the input differs or the stamp is not the print of what this plugin would
  write for the panel's brand. The print is planned once per brand asked about (about 0.2 s; memoized for the same brand).
  - Gates: `test-build-completed.ts` `q44.1/engine moved`, `q44.1/no print`, `q44.1/control`, through the real
    `main.ts`; `test-readback-parity.ts`, the real Apply Theme stamps; `test-update-kept-run.ts` opens with the recount
    `main.ts` would send in its world, so #3421's ordering fix fires again. Mutations: the recount reading the input
    alone fails `q44.1/engine moved`, `q44.1/no print`, `order/theme due` and #3428's arms; Apply Theme not stamping
    fails each brand's `#3422 Q44.1 A` arm.
  - The MCP paste stamps the same print: `mcp-paste.ts` works it out in Node from the plans it cuts, and `runPersist`
    writes it. `test-mcp-paste.ts`'s parity arms, which compare the paste's shared data with the plugin's, caught the
    paste without it. `theme-emission.ts` keeps its own copy of the ledger's FNV so the paste bundle does not carry the
    ledger.
  - **What the print covers.** The delta review hashed `colorPlan` alone in `emissionOf`, and all five gates that read
    the print passed. `test-build-completed.ts` now moves each of the seven plans Apply Theme writes in turn, by literal

    mutation fails the six arms after `colorPlan` by name.
  - **Trap:** a brand saved with no print reads as differing: a file themed by a plugin before this one. Theme counts
    once there, until a Theme run stamps the print.

**Version.** `engine: patch`, as #3428 now declares too: the repo's practice for a plugin behavior change.

## (2026-11-05) — Update file: a Theme run updates the sets it unblocks; Keep lists what it held back (#3421, Q39 A)

The reference brand's master, after #3402 (`interactive.*.indicator.*`), showed three faults in one Update file. The owner decided Q39 A.

### What was wrong, and why

- **Ordering.** The dialog runs its scoped check as it opens, before any step writes. radio-control, switch-control, tag and tab-item bound indicator variables the file did not hold yet, so the check marked them blocked (`fileBlockers`: "3 variables the plan binds are not in this file"). `updateDefsOf` passed only unblocked sets to the update step. Theme then wrote the variables, and the four sets stayed due.
- **Keep was silent.** Under Keep, a node edited by hand is not written, so on radio-control and tag the selection mark never got the indicator binding. `main.ts` still recorded every set the apply acted on as current, so the next check showed 0 due.
- **radio-control's 60 misses** are its kept hand edits, not an executor fault. Each kept dot reads back `bound <member>/dot.width -> DISCARDED`, which #3086 already moved out of the update's verdict, but the set's `build` record in plugin data still filed them as misses. The gate's third mutation reproduces the owner's record line for line. `wiredMembers: 0` is correct: radio-control has no text, boolean or swap properties, only variant axes, so no property reference is wired. switch-control's 24 and tab-item's 18 misses have the same shape, but they were not reproduced against the owner's file.

### The change

- **Ordering.** The dry run marks a set `themeBlocked` when every blocker is a variable or a text or effect style the plans name (`update-plan.ts`). With Theme ticked, the update step takes such a set (`updatableOf`). The step checks again after Theme (`recheckFirst`), and accepts the changed hash only for those sets (`recheckHolds`, now shared by `apps/studio/src/main.ts`). The row says "Updated after Theme — Theme writes the variables and styles it binds first". A set still blocked after Theme is refused by name in the verdict.
- **Kept edits.** Under Keep, `heldOf` names what the dry run's `conflict` hand edits hold back: the members, and each change on that node in the designer's words (`border → color/…`, `dot: size → …`). The verdict names every one, and the headline adds "· N sets kept edits over changes". `ledgerAfter` (moved out of `main.ts`) records the entry with `held`, and `dueOf` reads such an otherwise-current set as `kept`. Update file lists it under a new **Kept edits** group with its own Keep / Overwrite / Accept as baseline select, sent as `UpdateChoices.sets`. A line under the hand-edit select says what each choice does.
- **The build record.** In update mode the executor files a bound read-back on a kept node under `kept` (`keptCount`, five named), not `misses`, through one test shared with the verdict (`keptBoundOf`). This is an executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` rises to **53**, above main's 52 (#3399). `executor-reach.json` gains `"53": []`, and main's 52 entry stands; the reach lint measured 0 sets redrawn.

### The gate

`apps/plugin/test-update-kept-run.ts`, in the plugin's `test`, runs a full Update file in the component shim, then the check. radio-control and tag are built from their pre-#3402 plans in a file without the indicator variables, and the designer has recolored radio-control's checked rings and resized its dots. The run takes both after Theme. Then the check finds 0 due, tag current, and radio-control under Kept edits. The 12 held members are counted from the plans, and the rings are read off the host. Mutations, each failing by name:

- the ordering fix dropped → `order/in the run`, `after/0 due`;
- a kept set recorded as current → `after/kept listed`;
- kept read-backs filed as misses → `record/kept apart`.

The Theme step is modeled as the variables arriving (`liveVars`, a new shim option). What Apply Theme writes is `test-readback-parity.ts`'s subject.

**The wiring, after review.** That gate calls `ledgerAfter` and `recheckHolds` itself, so it checks the helpers, not the wiring: reverting `main.ts`'s `acted` to record each acted set without `held` passed it, and so did the seven plugin tests that load `main.ts`. Two more checks drive the wiring:

- `apps/plugin/test-update-kept-main.ts` posts the run to the real `main.ts` under the strict shim: the check, the Theme step, the check again, `update-sets`, then `file-sets`. It reads the ledger off the root's plugin data and the due state from `main.ts`'s own answer. `acted` built without `held` fails `main/held recorded` and `main/kept listed`. `update-sets` dropping the per-set choices fails `main/overwrite chosen`, which reads the rings off the host.
- `test:chrome` section `ia2` gains an arm where a set only Theme blocks rides the run. The Studio driver's re-check done by strict hash equality fails it by name.

**Trap:** under the strict shim, the root's own search answers a set's members as references, with ids that are not the nodes'. So an in-place update through it reads every member as "not built by Prism3". The new test gives each page its own search over its real nodes, as Figma's does. The run's read then searches a page at a time (`run-read.ts`), and the components the sets nest are real ones on a page of their own. No host method is patched.

**Version.** The PR first declared that no engine bump was owed. The review found it disagreed with #3432, and the repo's practice is a `patch` change note for a plugin behavior change (#3128, #3137, #3145), so it carries one (`packages/engine/changes/claude-update-leaves-due.md`).

**Filed while doing this:**
- #3435: switch-control's and tab-item's misses, not reproduced here.
- #3436: a second Keep run over a kept set records it as current.

### Owner decisions (2026-11-05)

- **Q3421.2 A, Q3421.5 A:** the verdict line and the Kept edits set's line say the kept edits "keep out N of the plan's values", not "hold back N changes the plan makes". Some named entries are values the plan bound before and after, which the hand edit dropped, so they are not changes this update makes. The headline stays as drafted, and the result stays ✓.
- **Q3421.1, .3, .4, .6 A:** as drafted.
- **Q3421.7 A:** Kept edits sets are not counted in the badge, because Keep changes nothing on a run.

## (2026-11-05) — A gate for contract tokens nothing reads: lint-token-consumers (#3409)

**Status:** a new engine gate, wired into `verify.ts`, `ci.yml`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3, `CLAUDE.md` and the PR template.
Owner decision Q33 A. No engine behavior moves and no artifact changes, so no change note is owed; the contract and
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` are untouched.

### What it checks

Every path in `schema/token-contract.json`'s `guaranteed` set is READ, or it is declared unread in the gate's own
register, `UNREAD_BY_DESIGN`, with a reason. Three readers, each scanned live:

- **defs** — any string in any component def, so a `tokens` binding and a code-only binding a def states in prose
  (Dialog's backdrop, `color.scrim.default`) both count.
- **aliases** — a DTCG alias in any committed `out/*.tokens.json` (every brand, every overlay), so a primitive a role
  aliases is read.
- **preview** — `schema/preview-spec.json`, the sample components the plugin and the playground render.

The `.ai.json` metadata and the style-guide pages describe every token, so they are not readers: counting them would
read the contract back to itself (`docs/34` shape 1).

### Why the register is independent (`docs/34`)

The register is authored: a path or a pattern, the COUNT of unread tokens it claims, and the reason. Nothing in it is
read from the contract, a def or an emission. A pattern carries its count so a family cannot quietly absorb a new
unread member (shape 15): `color.inverse.**` claims exactly 120.

### The census (measured 2026-11-04, on main at f029acf3)

621 guaranteed tokens: **381 read** (223 by defs, 163 by aliases, 56 by the preview, with overlaps) and **240
unread**. The register's first contents, 28 entries:

- **225 by design**, families a consumer expects whole: the inverse mirror (120), core ramp, dimension and font-role
  steps (34), the status and brand families' full role sets (17), and scale steps no component uses (motion 13,
  opacity 11, space 6, shadow 4, grid 5, container 2, radius 2, glass 2), plus the label and caption `-link` text
  styles designers set on a text range (5), unused rungs' line boxes (3) and the large caption (1).
- **15 held** as owner questions (below), never deleted.

### Owner questions (held in the register, each passes until answered)

- **Q-TC1** `color.icon.link.visited` — Link's visited state is code only and colors the text; should a standalone
  link's trailing icon take the visited icon color too?
- **Q-TC2** `color.interactive.{primary,neutral,destructive}.fill.focused` — no control paints a fill at focus (focus
  is the ring). Bind one at focus-visible, or keep for consumers?
- **Q-TC3** `color.interactive.destructive.indicator.{rest,hover,pressed}`, `color.interactive.{neutral,destructive}.fill.selected`
  — no neutral or destructive control selects. A matrix kept complete, or a missing control?
- **Q-TC4** `color.text.tertiary`, `color.foreground.tertiary` — no component uses the third step; muted text binds
  secondary. Should a quieter part (helper text, a placeholder) bind it?
- **Q-TC5** `control.size.lg.{inset,track,width}`, `size.xs.height` — rungs no control offers. Add the sizes, or keep
  the rungs for consumers?

### Mutations, each failing by name

- Slider's `size.large.thickness` rebound off `border-width.x-heavy` (its only reader):
  `unclaimed: 'border-width.x-heavy' is in the guaranteed contract and nothing reads it`.
- The `opacity.*` register entry dropped: 11 × `unclaimed: 'opacity.0' …`.
- The `shadow.*` count lowered to 3: `register: 'shadow.*' claims 4 unread token(s) and declares 3`.

### Limits

A def mention counts as a read, so a sentence that says "not X" reads X. The gate proves a name is mentioned, not that
the binding is right. A reason is prose, and review is its only guard.

An alias is a read whoever holds it, so a primitive aliased only by an unread contract token counts as read. Measured
(review of #3434), **13 of the 381 reads** hang only on unread holders: `core.dimension.{5,28,72,80,88,96}` (the
`control.size.lg.*`, `size.xs.height` and `space.900`–`1200` rungs), `core.font.weight.{300,900}`,
`core.font.line-height.{165,175}` and `core.font.letter-spacing.{neg-15,neg-40}` (the font roles' unread ends), and
`core.palette.info.550` (`color.inverse.{text,icon}.info-subtle`). `core.dimension.5` and `.28` hang on Q-TC5's held
tokens. The gate reports this list on every run, measured as a fixed point over the alias graph, and asserts nothing
on it; if a holder leaves the contract, the pinned `core.dimension.*` and `core.font.**` counts fail by name.

## (2026-11-05) — A focused field draws a 2px focus edge in place of its border (#3399)

Built as the owner decided on #3399 (Q22 A, Q22.1 A), replacing #3328's ring inside the border (#3372). The focused field's
own stroke becomes the focus edge: 2px (`focus.ring.width`), drawn inside from the outer edge at the field's own radius, so
the box keeps its size and the corner gap #3399 reported cannot occur (the edge and the field share one radius by
construction). A default field draws it in `border.focus`; an error, warning or success field in its status border, so the
status stays visible while focused. Text field, Password, Search, Card number, Textarea, Select, the Code input cell and
Counter (outline). Counter's ghost and every underline-edge field keep the outside ring (#2695 Q3, #3328 Q-F1 A).

### How

- **The edge is the border's weight, per state.** `strokeWidth: 'border-width.{state}'`, with `fieldEdgeWidths` (in
  `text-field.ts`) binding the focus states to `focus.ring.width` and every other state to the hairline. The paint was
  already right: `border.focus-visible` and the status-led `{status}.border.focus-visible` keys existed. The Counter gained
  `outline.border.focus-visible` → `border.focus`; until now its outline edge stayed at the rest color under the ring.
- **Two schema widenings, each argued at its rule.** A `strokeWidth` key may name `{state}` (the footprint reason
  `strokeEdges` already had: drawn inside, out of layout). An `absolute` part may take a VARIANT `presentWhen` (the
  Counter's ring on ghost only); `present()` already AND-composed it with `when`, so the old "early return" refusal was
  stale. A `presentWhen` on `state` stays refused.
- **The ring moved into `applyFieldStyle`.** The outline def draws no ring, so the underline style ADDS the shared ring
  (`UNDERLINE_RING`, last in the frame, as every field had it), and its plans are as before.
- **`borderInset` / `absoluteBorderInset` removed** from the schema, the projection, both executors, the readback and the
  ledgers, with `lint-absolute-inset`'s `MUST_SIT_INSIDE_BORDER`. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 51 → 52 (see the PR for the
  collision with #3380's reservation); `executor-reach.json` names the 9 sets, measured clean.

### The default field's 2.4.13 (Q3399.1 A)

**The default field's rest border → focus change is 1.19–2.21:1, not ≥3:1, in every corpus brand and mode.** The
decision's premise was a `neutral.400` border going to near-black (~5.6:1). Here `border.focus` is the brand's action color,
and `field.border.rest` is a mid-gray held at 3:1 against the page, so the two sit close in luminance. The inner 1px
(fill → focus) changes at 4.56:1 or more everywhere. The owner took option A (2026-11-04): the default field falls under the
trade-off Q22.1 A accepted for status fields, AA met and SC 2.4.13 resting on the inner 1px band.
`#3399 field focus 2.4.13` now asserts fill → focus ≥ 3:1 (a literal from SC 2.4.13) and the 2px width, and reports
rest → focus without asserting on it. Every def the edge reaches records the trade-off in `notes.contested`
(`FOCUS_EDGE_DEFAULT_NOTE`), and the arm holds it there by the decision's name. Options B (a darker field focus role) and
C (a wider edge) were not taken.

### What a Field style switch now does

Switching Field style in place (#2695 Q16 A) still keeps the set, every member and every other node, but the 24 focus
members gain the ring going to Underline and lose it going to Outline, since only Underline draws one.
`test-update-apply.ts` holds both directions to the literal 24. This follows from two decisions already taken (Q22 A: the outline
edge draws no ring; #3328 Q-F1 A: the underline edge keeps one), so it is the expected result, not a defect. The ring holds
no designer content, so nothing a designer authored is lost. No change and no owner question.

### Traps

- The test stub models host truth for a bound weight: `strokeWeight` splits across the four per-side keys (#1332). An arm
  reading `boundVariables.strokeWeight` sees nothing.
- On the plugin path a root-frame member (the Code cell) sits inside a component set, so `page.children[0]` is the set.
- Textarea's grip sits 1px in from the corner (`grip-inset`, the hairline), so at the 2px focus edge its 16px artboard
  overlaps the edge by 1px. Measured: the drawn glyph's farthest point is 19.71 on its 24-unit artboard, so it stays 3.86px
  in from the outer edge and never reaches the edge's pixels. The inset stays the hairline; `#3399 textarea grip clears the
  focus edge` holds the glyph more than the literal 2px in, in every corpus brand.

## (2026-11-05) — Plugin window: Minimize shrinks in place, and the strip returns where it was dragged (#3416)

The owner tried #3342's placement in real Figma. The strip landed slightly off-screen and over Figma's bottom toolbar,
and the inward clamp made the window jump on each toggle. The owner's decision on #3416: the first Minimize in a file
shrinks the window in place, and later ones put the strip back where the user last dragged it, kept per file. There is
no inward clamp. The one fallback is for a remembered spot whose top-left is off the visible canvas: the strip shrinks
in place instead, and if that top-left is off the canvas too, it starts at the canvas's top-left. Restore still
centers.

### What the API gives

`figma.ui.getPosition()` returns the UI's top-left as `{ windowSpace, canvasSpace }`, and throws when no UI is open
(Plugin API reference, `figma.ui`; `@figma/plugin-typings` `UIAPI.getPosition`). So the iframe reports nothing:
`main.ts` reads the position at each toggle. The strip's spot is read at Restore, which is where the user last left it.

**This comes from the API reference and the typings, not from the host.** Three things the strip leans on have not
been observed in real Figma, and the test shim builds each one in, so no headless arm can fail on them:
- (a) `getPosition()` reflects a drag by the user, not only the last `reposition`;
- (b) `getPosition().canvasSpace` and `reposition(x, y)` address the same point of the window (both the iframe's
  top-left, or both the title bar's);
- (c) `windowSpace` is stable within a session.

So the first Minimize of a reachable window doesn't depend on any of them: shrinking in place is `resize` alone, with no
`reposition` (review of #3420, S2). Had it repositioned to `canvasSpace`, a host where (b) is false would move every
first Minimize by the offset between the two, the jump #3416 rules out. The return to a remembered spot depends on all
three. They are the owner's real-Figma checks.

### What landed

- `apps/plugin/src/window-place.ts`: `stripPlacement(bounds, zoom, here, spot)` and `restorePlacement(bounds, zoom,
  size)`, both pure. `windowPlacement` and `STRIP_MARGIN` are gone. The spot is kept in window space, because "where the
  user dragged it" is a place on the screen, and a canvas position moves with every pan and zoom. It is turned back
  into canvas units through the window's own position, read in both spaces: `here.canvas + (spot - here.window) / zoom`.
- `main.ts`: Minimize reads the position before the resize. In place, it only resizes; otherwise it repositions the
  strip. Restore keeps the strip's window-space
  spot in `clientStorage` under `prism3:strip-at:<file id>`, then centers. The spot is read once at start, so
  Minimize answers at once.

### The file id: a deviation from the issue's example

The issue suggests keying by `figma.root.id`, but the document node's id is `0:0` in every file, so it can't tell
files apart. `figma.fileKey` is for private plugins only. So the file's id is a random one, kept in the root's plugin
data under `prism3:file-id` and made the first time a strip spot is kept in that file. That is a small write to the
file, like the ones `doc-settings.ts` and `as-built-ledger.ts` already make. The PR flags it for the owner.

### Gaps

- A strip closed while minimized (the plugin quit without Restore) isn't kept: the spot is read at Restore only.
- The headless tests hold the arithmetic, not the look. A real-Figma check is still owed, on the owner's machine:
  (a)–(c) above, and that the first Minimize keeps the window exactly where it was.

### The tests

`test-agent-link.ts`:
- `strip-place/*`: the first Minimize keeps the top-left, no clamp by the edge, the remembered spot at zoom 1 and 2,
  each fallback, and Restore centered. All against hand-worked literals.
- `strip-place/spot-edge`: a remembered spot by the canvas's edge isn't pulled inward.
- `strip/place-min`, `strip/kept-spot`, `strip/place-return`: the same rules through `main.ts`, with a `getPosition`
  shim. `strip/place-min` also checks that the first Minimize repositions nothing.
- `strip-relaunch/read`, `strip-relaunch/return`: `main.ts` launched a second time, into a host that already holds the
  file's id and its spot. The first Minimize lands on the stored spot. This is the cross-launch half of "remembered per
  file".

Mutations, from a `wip:` commit, each failing by name:
- the lower-right corner back → `strip-place/first`, `strip/place-min`;
- the inward clamp back → `strip-place/no-clamp`;
- drop the `/ zoom` → `strip-place/spot-z2`, `strip/place-return`;
- the spot never checked for reach → `strip-place/spot-off`;
- the canvas top-left fallback dropped → `strip-place/both-off`;
- the spot not kept at Restore → `strip/kept-spot`, `strip/place-return`;
- in place repositioned to `canvasSpace` again → `strip/place-min`, `strip/place-drag`, `strip/place-restore`;
- the start-up read of the stored spot dropped → `strip-relaunch/return`;
- a clamp on the remembered spot only → `strip-place/spot-edge`, `strip/place-return`, `strip-relaunch/return`.

Five public guides cite the plugin's `main.ts` by line, and the new lines moved them, so they move here too. Each was
re-pointed by content, against main's cited block, so the range-only ones `lint-guide-claims.ts` can't check are right
as well.

## (2026-11-05) — Banner's `width` axis is `edge`: contained or full-bleed (#3392)

**Status:** engine. A component API rename, owner decision 2026-11-04 on #3392. No token name moves, so
`CONTRACT_VERSION` stays; the executor's code does not move, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at main's number
(`lint-executor-revision` agrees). A `minor` change note.

### What changed

- **The name.** Banner's axis was `width` (`contained | full`), but what moves between its two members is the corners
  and which sides carry the edge; both members fill their container. #3383's rule names an axis for what changes, so
  the owner renamed it. Finalized as `edge` (`contained | full-bleed`), the owner's suggestion, checked against the
  canon: one lowercase word, so its Figma panel name is lowercase with no display rename (Q345); `full-bleed` follows
  the kebab-case of multi-word values already in the corpus (`apple-pay`, `from-top`). `edge` is new to the closed
  `VARIANT_AXES`, which is a schema change, so the owner's decision is what admits it; its header entry argues it
  against `width`, `shape`, `inset` and `placement`.
- **The migration.** Two `COMPONENT_RENAMES` entries: an axis entry `width` → `edge` and a value entry on the NEW axis
  `full` → `full-bleed` (an axis rename applies first in `renameCoordinate`). An update renames each built member in
  place, so placed instances keep their member. `component-axes.json` re-accepted.
- **The register.** `lint-axis-values` carries `edge` as a `sole` set for Banner, and Button's `width` falls back from
  `canonical` to `sole`, its only set again.
- **Token slot keys** follow the axis: `edge.{edge}.radius` and `edge.{edge}.edge-side` (same tokens bound).

### Verification

- Mutation: drop the axis entry from `COMPONENT_RENAMES` and `lint-component-renames` fails with
  `banner: axis 'width' is gone`; drop the value entry and it fails with `banner: edge=full is gone`.
- `test.ts`'s Banner literals and `test-roundtrip.ts`'s built widths read `edge=…`; their regexes take the hyphen.
