## (2026-11-05) — MCP paste: a set's page is placed by its own script, so a new component page no longer eats chunk headroom (#3414)

**STATUS: PR open, not merged.** Plugin and paste tooling only. **No engine change, no `out/**` change, no ENGINE or CONTRACT bump, no `EXECUTOR_REVISION` change** (`lint-executor-revision`: the executor's code is unchanged; `mcp-steps.ts` is not in its reach). Files: `apps/plugin/src/mcp-steps.ts` (a new step, `runComponentPlace`; `runComponentChunk` finds its page by name), `apps/plugin/mcp-paste.ts` (one `component-place` script before each set's first chunk; the chunk data carries `page`), `apps/plugin/test-mcp-paste.ts` (the `size/pages` arm), `apps/plugin/test-paste-reactions.ts` (runs the place step, and a chunk with no page), `tools/figma-mcp/plan.ts` and `README.md`, `docs/inventory/surfaces.md`.

**The cause.** Every component-chunk script carried the whole file taxonomy, because `runComponentChunk` called `placeOnPage`, which calls `resolveComponentPage`, which reads every section and leaf to anchor a created page. So each new component page took its taxonomy entry's characters out of every chunk of every set. Dialog's one-member chunks were left 46 characters under `SCRIPT_CEILING` (44,954 of 45,000, as numbered), and #3380's one new page (75 characters) put them over.

**The option built: placement as a step of its own (the issue's A).** One `component-place` script per set-built def, before its first chunk, runs `placeOnPage` and checks it landed on the page the generator planned. Each chunk is handed that page name in `__D` and switches to it by name. A chunk never creates a page: if the page is absent, it throws an error naming the place script. A def the taxonomy doesn't map still builds on the current page, with no place script, as before. This follows `runComponentReactions`' precedent, a step of its own to keep code out of every chunk's budget. Emit (icon) and reactions scripts still place themselves; neither is near the ceiling.

**Options turned down.** *Only the needed taxonomy entry in each chunk:* `resolveComponentPage` and `ensureSectionHeader` need the whole taxonomy to anchor a created page or section header after the earlier ones. Narrowing it changes where pages land, and the defaulted `TAXONOMY` parameter keeps the full object in the bundle anyway. *`pack` splitting a single member:* a member is one variant, built by one payload, and can't be divided. This option also leaves the cause in place: chunks would keep shrinking, just in more pieces. *Raising `SCRIPT_CEILING`:* ruled out by the issue.

**Measured.** The chunk step bundle went from about 7,700 to 2,630 characters. For one example brand, a full build went from 1,418 chunk scripts (160 of them one-member) to 698 (12 one-member) plus 57 place scripts: 1,590 component scripts down to 927. The largest one-member chunk is now 40,108 characters, 4,892 under the ceiling. Peak chunk headroom is the same for all 8 example brands: before, 46 (dialog 18/24); after, 84 (link 10/19). Multi-member chunks still pack to within about 100 characters of the ceiling, by design: `planSetChunks` fills the budget it's given. That number is packing slack, not shrinking headroom. **Adding #3380's page entry to the taxonomy, simulated:** on main, the peak went 44,954 → 45,029 (over by 29, dialog 18/24), and the chunk count went from 1,418 to 1,482. On this branch, every chunk script was byte-identical (same hash).

**The gate.** `size/<brand>` is unchanged. A new arm, `size/pages`, has a literal expectation. A minified taxonomy leaf ships as `page:"<name>"`, and a script's JSON `__D` can't match that pattern, because its keys are quoted. The arm expects **0** such entries across all 698 chunk scripts. To show the pattern can find them, the place bundle must carry them (Dialog's and Buttons' among its 42). The arm also checks that every set is placed exactly once, before its first chunk, on the page its chunks switch to, and checks Dialog's page literally. Mutation, from a `wip:` commit: `runComponentChunk` calling `placeOnPage` again (the full taxonomy back in every chunk) → `✗ size/pages: no chunk script carries a taxonomy entry (1625 of 1625 do — focus-ring 1/1: 42 entries)`, plus all 8 `size/<brand>` arms over the ceiling. `test-paste-reactions.ts` now runs the generator's place step before the chunks. It adds two arms: `#3414 code-input-cell is placed … once, and every chunk builds there`, and `#3414 a chunk whose page is not in the file throws, naming the place step`.

**Filed, not built: #3418.** The issue also notes that `pack`'s at-least-one-variant rule silently ships an over-budget chunk, though `mcp-paste.ts`'s header says an indivisible unit that won't fit is a thrown error. The size gate still catches it, at the finished-script level. That is a separate concern from this PR.

## (2026-11-05) — Activity causes as data, the writer side (#3326 PR 1)

**STATUS: plugin and panel data only; nothing drawn changes.** First of the four PRs in #3326's build plan (the
2026-11-03T03:14Z proposal, §4). Owner decisions Q3326.1–.9 A, and #3308's Q3308.1 A / Q3308.2 A. No engine change, no
executor change: the PR takes no executor revision.

### What it does

A verdict that is not clean now says why as data: `causes` beside `lines` on `component-result` and
`component-update-result`, each `{ kind, subject, what, reasons[], step?, why?, stays?, todo? }` (`Cause`,
`apps/plugin/src/messages.ts`). The drawer could only find a warning by position: it took the first line as "the reason",
so the owner's library run showed "Button: 4 updated in place." as the reason for a warning that was the last line.

- **The template line** (`canvas-furniture.ts`): `withTemplateWarning`, the one place a missing template turns a run `⚠`,
  now also adds `templateCauses`: one cause per set that lacked a template, its reason that set's template line. The
  same predicate does both, so a run is never turned `⚠` by a template without its cause.
- **The build** (`main.ts`): a set with real misses or a stale note is "built with problems"; no set at all, a refused
  def, or a throw is "could not be built", the host's words first.
- **The applied update** (`update-apply.ts` `applyVerdict`): a set stopped, not verified, or not updated, each with the
  clauses its lines already print after the set's name; a whole-run refusal is the run's own cause (`subject: null`).
- **The panel's queue** (`build-queue.ts` `runCauses`): each set that failed or had problems carries the causes its own
  build sent, so "Badge: built with problems." finally has its reasons behind it (#3308.1); each set a stop left is one too.
- **The adapter** (`write-adapter.ts` `causesOf`) checks every field and drops a list with a malformed entry whole, as
  `linesOf` does. `host-session.ts` carries the causes into each verdict slot.

### Decisions taken here, and why

- **`subject` is a def id, never words.** The drawer names it from its catalog (PR 2), so no writer words a set's name and
  the plugin and the queue agree on one key.
- **The agent's envelope is unchanged.** `forAgent` drops `causes` with `lines`; an agent reads the same facts as
  `activity`'s `problems` (#3309). Gated by `#3326 causes/<cmd>` in `test-agent-link.ts`.
- **A cause only on a verdict that is not `ok`.** A dependency built first with misses is in `activity`'s `problems` but
  does not turn the build's `ok` false, so it is not a cause here. Filed as #3386, not changed here.
- **A stop names the sets it left by def id** (review S1). A library names its sets its own way ("Button" for
  `button`), so `halted` carries `leftDefs` beside `left`, and a cause's subject never falls back to a set's name.
- **The plugin's cause rules live once**, in `causes.ts` (review N1). The panel's queue and its refusal import
  `mergeCauses` and `CAUSE_WHAT` (a pure module) rather than copying them, so PR 4's rewording moves every writer.
- **The web bundle reads one plugin file, `causes.ts`** (second review S1). So `apps/studio/vercel-ignore.sh` now
  watches it: a commit that changes only `causes.ts` builds the site (exit 1) where it was skipped (exit 0), measured
  against the script before and after. The gate gap behind it (`check:ignore` checks engine files only) is #3407.
- **Draw specs carries no causes yet.** It is outside PR 1's four writers. Filed as #3404.
- **"updated with problems"** is the one phrase not in the approved draft: the update's form of the build's
  "built with problems". It is not shown until PR 2, and PR 4 owns the words.

### Gates, and the mutation that fails by name

`test-canvas-furniture.ts` `templates/cause …` reads `causes` only. Dropping the template line from `templateCauses`'
reasons while leaving its prose fails `templates/cause build`, `templates/cause update` and `templates/cause merge`,
while every `templates/missing …` prose arm stays green, which is what shows the gate is not reading the prose
(`docs/34`). Also: `causes/…` in `test-update-apply.ts` and `test-build-completed.ts` (the posts `main.ts` makes),
`causes/run …` in `test-component-groups.ts`, and the adapter's arms in `test-write-adapter.ts`. After review:
`causes/halted` (a set named "Tag set" for `tag`), `causes/idle`, `causes/refused`, `causes/unknown`, `causes/misses`,
and in both suites `causes/every verdict`, an invariant over every verdict each suite reads: one not `ok` names at least
one cause, each subject a def id. Each of the review's four surviving mutations now fails one of them by name. Second review: `causes/run merged` in
`test-component-groups.ts` (a set two builds name is one cause; `runCauses` returning its list unmerged fails it).

Third review: eleven guide citations that quote nothing still carried main's line numbers after this PR moved the
code. `lint-guide-claims` checks such a citation for range only, so it could not see them (#3417). Each is re-pointed
by mapping main's cited line through the diff, merged with #3353 so it carries both PRs' shifts.

### Trap for PR 2

`step` is empty from every writer: Update file's step names are the panel's. PR 2 fills it where it groups the steps.

## (2026-11-04) — Update file: the check's progress in the dialog's foot (#3302)

On the template, opening Update file spent about 20 s checking every set. Every row read "Checking what changes…" until
the single answer landed, and nothing said how far the check had got. The owner decided Q3302.1–.4, all A, on
2026-11-02. The strings were approved as written.

### The change

- **Foot** (Q3302.1 A, Q3302.3 A): the dialog's foot, before Cancel, carries the chrome's own bar (`p3-op-prog`), as
  wide as the status strip's. Beside it:
  - "Reading this file…", with the bar empty, until every set is found;
  - then "Checked n of N sets", with the bar filled by sets.

  At 380 the buttons wrap under it.
- **Rows** (Q3302.2 A): only the set being checked reads "Checking…". A checked set shows its result as it lands, with
  the existing fade (#3150). A set not reached yet shows no line. The old "Checking what changes…" is gone.
- **Order** (Q3302.4 A): this comes after #3313's faster check. It is built on that branch.
- **Host**: `previewUpdate` now finds every target first. That covers the file's read and the single-component defs'
  reads, which is the "Reading this file…" stretch. Then it reads and checks each set in turn, nested first as #3343
  orders the check, and calls a `progress` hook:
  - `done` 0 once every set is found;
  - then once per set, with that set's own preview and the next set's id.

  The hook hands the thread back after each call, so the panel hears each reading before the next set. `checkSets`
  posts each reading as `update-check-progress`. Its `set` is `checkedSetOf` over that set's own preview, its
  consumer-breaking line included. The answer (`update-check`) still replaces every line. The sets' moves and a blocked
  panel's clearing are worked out only over every set, so the answer can change a line. On the template stand-in it
  changed none of 60.
- **Motion** (#3150): no motion is driven by time. The bar's value moves only when the host reports a set.

### Gates

- `test-chrome.mjs`, section `ia2`, Figma light and dark: five arms check the foot's text as literals and the bar's
  value, max and label.
  - Before the first set: "Reading this file…", the bar at 0 of 1, before Cancel.
  - Then "Checked 0 of 2 sets" and "Checked 1 of 2 sets".
  - The rows' text and `data-state` (`waiting`, `checking`, `checked`).
  - No animation or transition on the bar, and the same foot and rows 600 ms later.
  - The foot's progress is gone once the answer lands.
- `test-open-large-file.ts`, `check/progress`: the template's check posts done 0 of 60 and then 1 to 60, in order. Each
  reading names its set and the next, sits in its own turn, and lands before the answer. Since the merge with #3343 the
  readings come nested first (`nestedFirst`), not in the targets' own order; a premise holds that the two orders differ
  on the template (first at the fourth set), and walking the targets' own order again fails `check/progress` by name.
  A row reading "Checking…" can jump down the list and back as a result: the owner's call, Q3353.1 on the PR.
- `test-open-large-file.ts`, `check/progress refused`: with one def the engine can't plan, the count starts at 1 of 60
  and still reaches 60 of 60, and the answer names that def refused. Added after review: no arm held the refused term.

Mutations, each failing by name:
- every row reading "Checking…" while the check is out → `#3302 Q3302.2 A` (and Q3302.3 A);
- the foot left at "Reading this file…" → `#3302 Q3302.1 A`;
- the first reading dropped → `check/progress`;
- the hand-back after each set dropped → `check/progress`.
- the refused defs left out of the count (`done: p.done`) → `check/progress refused`.

## (2026-11-04) — Divider: bold and subtle strengths, the rule drawn as a stroke (#3382)

**Status:** Divider def + Accordion and Dialog nest variants + tests + the axis register. ENGINE minor (change note).
CONTRACT unchanged: no token name moves. `lint-executor-revision` passes with no raise, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What changed

- **Owner decision Q15 revised A (2026-11-03, on #3382):** the divider gets subtle and bold variants, each bound to its
  own border role, with no brand setting, and the rule is drawn as a stroke instead of a filled box.
- **The axis is `emphasis: bold | subtle`.** bold binds `color.border.secondary`, the color every divider drew before;
  subtle binds `color.border.primary`, the lighter edge. The routing named the axis `strength`, but `VARIANT_AXES`
  already has `emphasis`, which Badge carries as `subtle | bold` for the same question (how strongly a thing reads), and a
  second name for one question is the #756 failure the closed list exists to stop. The name is held for the owner on
  the PR; renaming is mechanical.
- **bold is the default and leads the axis**, so it is the code default and Figma's default member. Every placed
  divider, and the Accordion and Dialog dividers, keep their color. The two hosts now name `emphasis: 'bold'` in their
  nest variant; their plans differ from main only by that coordinate (diffed, 90 lines, nothing else).
- **The stroke.** The rule and the labeled divider's two lines paint the `border` slot with `strokeWidth` bound to
  `border-width.hairline`. Both executors draw strokes inside the node, so a box one hairline thick is covered edge to
  edge by its stroke: the pixels the fill drew. The border roles are scoped to strokes, so they now show in Figma's
  stroke picker and a designer can rebind the rule by hand. Code keeps painting a box, since CSS has no scoping.
- The code-only separator binding is renamed `separator.fill` → `separator.rule.border`: a two-segment key would read as
  `{emphasis}.{slot}` with emphasis `separator`, which the validator refuses.
- The Figma set grows from 7 members to 14. `component-axes.json` and `component-surface.json` accepted after reading
  each diff: a pure addition, so no rename ledger entry.

### Verification

- New `#3382 divider` arm in `test.ts`, with literal expectations: every rule and line in all 14 members is a hairline
  stroke with no fill, bold on `color/border/secondary` and subtle on `color/border/primary`, and every plain member
  stays one hairline thick across.
- Mutations, each failing by name: the rule back to `paintSlots: ['fill']` fails `#3382 divider stroke`;
  `subtle.border` bound to `color.border.secondary` fails `#3382 divider strength`.

## (2026-11-04) — Studio labels an override by the palette it names (#3391)

On the reference brand's master, after the action palette moved to Neutral, Theme › Color › Interactive labeled overrides "Override · neutral 350". The file, and the ratio Studio showed (3.03:1), were `brand-neutral 350`. The label was wrong, and a designer couldn't see that the overrides still pointed at a palette they were about to remove.

### Diagnosis

An override is stored as `{ palette, step }`, and the engine resolves the palette it names. For a plain override row, `color-interactive.ts` built the label from the row's *own* family (`interactivePaletteOf(row)`, which follows the action palette) and the stored step. So it dropped the stored palette. The inverse fill's rows already read the stored palette. The same wrong `current` also reached the step picker, which marked the row family's step 350 as current.

### Fix

- `interactive-input.ts` gains `overrideHeldOf(mode, row)`, the palette and step the override names, and `overrideLabel(held)`. Both kinds of override row use them for the label and for the picker's current step. The picker offers the row's own ramp only, so when the override names another palette it now marks no step as current.
- The brand-color remove confirm (`removalEffects`) lists the roles still overridden to the color, in one line: "N roles are still overridden to it: … — the brand won't build until each is re-picked." Overrides are **not** cascaded on removal. That stays the owner's call (Q-block on the PR). The claim is the engine's own answer: the modes refuse to resolve with "unknown palette".
- Section 9 of `test-interactive-input.ts` uses a fixture brand color named `brand-neutral`, with an override on the primary border that points at it. The engine's resolution is the oracle for the palette. The label must read `Override · brand-neutral 350`, including after the action palette moves to neutral. Mutations: strip the family from `overrideLabel`, or label by the row's family again; both fail `#3391 label` by name.
- Section 3391 of `test-chrome.mjs` (review S1) reads the label on screen. It seeds the same override into the stored input, under the primary family and with the action palette on neutral. The button must read `Override · brand-neutral 350`, and the picker must mark no step current. The oracle is the override the page persisted. Section 9 tests the helpers, so it could not see the original bug put back at the button's own site in `color-interactive.ts`; this section fails by name on it, all four checks. Section 9 also covers the inverse fill's rest row now.

### Trap

`brandTheme` alone accepts a brand whose override names a missing palette. The refusal comes in `resolveAllModes`. A check that stops at `brandTheme` reports the dangling override as fine.

## (2026-11-04) — The real-Figma canary: a scripted Mac job, a run file keyed by command, and a judge that checks the protocol's shape (#3215)

#3304 shipped the canary's path rule, its judge and the Mac's job as prose. This follows the owner's decisions of 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-03 (Q-C2 C: the owner switches Agent link on for each run; Q20 A: runs use the owner's normal plugin build, gated by a build-stamp check, with no separate checkout) and turns the Mac's half into a script. It's still a tool, not a gate: nothing here is in `ci.yml` or `verify.ts`, and nothing in the plugin changed.

### What changed

- **`job.ts prepare <full sha> --run-dir <dir> [--file-key <key>]`**: builds nothing and checks nothing out (Q20 A). It writes `request.json` (the commit asked for) and `commands.json` into the run folder and prints the steps. The scratch file's key is a run-time argument, used for one printed link and written nowhere.
- **`job.ts check --run-dir <dir>`**: the stamp check, run on the first `status` before anything else. Unless the build stamp the plugin reports names exactly the commit asked for, from a clean tree, in the scratch file, it says `stop` with what to ask the owner (rebuild from the commit, or open the scratch file), and the Mac sends nothing else. A later commit isn't accepted.
- **`job.ts collect --run-dir <dir>`**: gathers the responses the session saved, verbatim, into one `run.json` keyed by command, with the commit asked for.
- **The run is bracketed by two `status` calls** (`status`, then `status-after` last). The bridge serves whichever plugin holds it (#3297), so both ends must name the scratch file and report the same build.
- **`judge.ts` reads the run file.** It now also holds when the commit the job was asked to check isn't `--expect`, and when a response doesn't parse as a result envelope. It keeps the commit check on both `status` responses' build stamps, so what ran is what was asked for, with no job build to compare against. The envelope's shape is literals in the judge (`PROTOCOL_V`, `TRANSPORTS`, `ERROR_CODES`, the fields), never read from `agent-protocol.ts` (`docs/34`). The scratch file's name is the default `--file-name`. The safe line reads `checked, safe to rebuild from <commit>`.
- **Fixtures, one bad run per check:** `bad-commit`, `bad-error`, `bad-file` (the closing `status` in another file) and `bad-shape`, beside `pass.json` and #3209's run. `selftest.ts` holds each by name, plus the job's stamp check and collect. 63 assertions.
- **The README's job text** now follows the script, and the owner switches the link on (Q-C2 C). The "can the Mac switch it on?" step from Q-C2 A is gone.

### Verification

- `prepare`, `check`, `collect` and the judge ran end to end over a scratch run folder: `prepare` wrote only `request.json` and `commands.json`, and the test key appeared in no file; `check` said `stop … ask the owner to rebuild` on a stale stamp (exit 1) and `go on` on the right one; `collect` then the judge gave `checked, safe to rebuild`. The git tree stayed clean.
- Mutations, each failing by name: an empty `EXCEPTION` list fails `3209/update-components`; a commit compare that accepts anything fails `bad-commit/status`; the file compare limited to the opening `status` fails `bad-file/status-after`; the transport check dropped fails `bad-shape/readback`. For the Q20 A rework: the run's requested-commit compare dropped fails `asked/run`; the stamp check's commit compare dropped fails `check/stale`, its file compare `check/file`, letting a stamp with no usable commit through `check/dirty`, its `cmd` guard `check/wrong-cmd`; a commit compare that accepts any commit fails `bad-commit/status` and `check/later`.

### Calls made where the decision was silent

- The brief's optional `should-run.ts` already exists as #3304's `needs-check.ts`, with its own fixture arms. It wasn't renamed or duplicated.
- The progress fragment for this branch name already existed, from #3304 and not yet folded, so this entry has its own file instead of overwriting that one.

## (2026-11-04) — The variant rule is written guidance; the engine's defs audited against it (#3383)

Owner decision Q3 A: a component gets a variant only when its layout or structure changes. Show/hide becomes a
boolean, text a text property, a nested choice an exposed nested instance, width the container's, and a color-only
state or status stays a variant. No axis is named for a viewport or a width (`desktop`/`mobile`): where the layout
changes between breakpoints, the axis names the layout (`stacked`/`inline`) and the parent picks the member. It came from a Figma rebuild whose local components were heavily over-varianted
(an order row at 23 variants where the rule gives 6; a bag line item at 32 where it gives 4).

### What changed
- `skills/prism3-build-component` §6: the rule as a table mapping each kind of difference to the def field it
  becomes (`variantAxes`, `booleans`, `texts`, `nest-exposed`, no axis), with Button's slot axes named as
  holding to it (the slot moves the padding). The closing checklist checks it.
- `skills/prism3-rebind` §3: the rule for a local component built where Prism3 has none, with the member count
  recorded in the log. §11 step 8: auditing a rebuild's local sets against it, read-only first, with reduction
  held for the owner and run through the snapshot-and-restore steps.

### The audit
Every def's Figma set projected with `figmaAnatomySet`; for each projected axis, the members that differ only on it
compared field by field. No axis moves nothing. One axis is width-only (dialog `size`); seven only forward a nested
component's coordinate; a group of color-only style axes (`appearance`, `surface`, `emphasis`, `tone`, the veil's
three) waits on the owner's reading of the color-only clause. All filed in #3392; no def changed here.

### No gate, and why
The independent version (each projected axis changes at least one field of the plan) passes every def today and
also passes every shape the rule targets: a show/hide axis adds a child, a width-only axis moves a width, a
forwarding axis moves a nested coordinate. That is `docs/34` shape 10, an oracle measuring a symptom instead of
the rule. Testing the rule itself needs a hand classification of plan fields (width, paint, structure) and a call on
when forwarding is legitimate, and its first run would fail on an axis the owner decided (dialog `size`, Q303).
Reconsider once #3392 settles those answers.

## (2026-11-04) — Update check: a variable's value edited in the Variables panel drops the kept views (#3364)

Found in #3348 (#3313). The check reuses the member reads the hand-edit pass made at open ("kept views"), and drops them on any change Figma reports to a component, set or style. Figma reports no document change when a variable's **value** is edited in the Variables panel, yet every member bound to that variable re-resolves: a size, a padding, an opacity. So the next check could lay its plans against a read that held the old value, and call a set current when it isn't, or the other way round.

### The fix

- **The file's variables, printed** (`member-views.ts`, `variablesPrint`): each local variable's id, type and values by mode, and each collection's id, modes and default mode.
- **The pass prints them before it reads** (`handEditsPass`, `noteVariables`).
- **Each check prints them again as it starts** (`previewUpdate`, through `KeptViews.under`; `checkSets` passes it). A print that differs from the one the views were read under drops every view. So does a print the host refuses.
- **A view is kept only under a print.** A read with nothing to compare against is never reused.
- I chose to drop every view rather than only those that read the edited variable. A member can reach a variable through an alias, a nested instance or a style, and tracing that is the same problem #3348 avoided for components. The cost is one read of every variable per check, against a full re-read of every set only after a value actually moved.

`EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at 48: `lint-executor-revision` reports the executor's code unchanged. The cites in three public guides move by the lines `main.ts` and `test-update-apply.ts` gained.

### Not covered

A **library** variable's value is not a local variable, so it is not in the print. Whether accepting a library update is heard as a document change on the members it moves has not been measured on the host. Filed as #3376.

### Gates

- `test-update-apply.ts`, `values/…`, on the strict shim: two checks with a value edited between them. A float variable the member binds is rewritten (`setValueForMode`, no change heard), and the member re-resolves.
  - `values/unchanged`: the first check keeps the view and gives a fresh read's answer.
  - The premise: laid against the kept read with no print taken, the check reads 0 moves where a fresh read reads 44.
  - `values/edited`: the second check drops the view and gives the fresh read's answer, whole.
  - `values/unreadable`: a refused print drops every view.
  - `values/no print`: a read with no print to compare against is never kept.
- `test-open-large-file.ts`, `check/values`: the same through `main.ts`'s own check on the template stand-in, which gains one variable for the arm. Every set's read is kept, a value is edited, and an unedited set's member re-resolves its opacity with no `documentchange`. The second check equals a fresh read.
- The existing `views/…` arms now print the variables before they keep a view.
- `test-open-large-file.ts` clears the kept views and the print before the template's open, so `check/views` and `check/calls` measure the reads kept under the pass's own print, not one an earlier arm's check left in the module.

Mutations, each failing by name:
- `noteVariables` not dropping on a moved print → `values/edited` and `check/values`;
- `previewUpdate` not printing as the check starts → `values/edited` and `check/values`;
- `checkSets` passing a no-op `under` → `check/values`;
- a refused print kept → `values/unreadable`;
- `keepView` not asking for a print → `values/no print`;
- the pass's own `noteVariables(await variablesPrint(figma))` removed → `check/views` (0 kept) and `check/calls` (2,002,325 host calls).

## (2026-11-04) — Update file reads the dialog body's scroll back (#3388)

Update file reported "1 set not verified" on the dialog, listing `…/body.overflowDirection: ∅` on all 24 members. In the real file, every body holds `VERTICAL`. The write landed; the read was wrong.

### Diagnosis

The SLOT in the title was incidental. The update's dry run and its verify never diff a live node. They diff `snapshotMember`'s copy (`apps/plugin/src/member-baseline.ts`), and that copy holds only the fields in `SNAP_KEYS`. #3163 added `overflowDirection` to the plan, the executor and the read-back's `FIELDS`, but not to `SNAP_KEYS`. So the snapshot read it as ∅ on any node. The dialog body is the only node that plans it, and it happens to be a SLOT.

`test:roundtrip` passed because every diff in it read the live shim node, never the snapshot. The shim already gives a SLOT `overflowDirection` the way Figma does. What was missing was the read path.

### Fix

- `'overflowDirection'` joins `SNAP_KEYS`. It is read, not hashed: adding it to the hash (`AS_IS`) would move every built frame's baseline and make every member look hand-edited.
- New check, `roundtrip/snapshot reads as live`: every member the corpus builds (80 defs) is read a second time as Update file's snapshot. It must diverge from its plan exactly where the live read does. The live read is the oracle; the snapshot is the subject. Mutation: drop `'overflowDirection'` from `SNAP_KEYS`, and the check fails by name, listing the 24 dialog `panel/body.overflowDirection: ∅` divergences.
- The check found a second gap, filed as #3393: sign-in-button's mark `literalTint` reads through `findAll`, which a snapshot doesn't have. It sits in the check's known-gap ledger by def and field. A second assertion fails once that entry stops firing, so the entry can't outlive the issue.

`EXECUTOR_REVISION` is unchanged: `lint-executor-revision` exempts `member-baseline.ts`. The strip's "Stopped at the update" wording for a run where every set updated is left to #3326's PR 4.

## (2026-11-04) — FieldMessage: the status glyph centers on the message's first line (#3360)

**Owner decisions Q-FM1 A and Q-FM1.1 B.** The field message's status glyph centers on the caption's FIRST line. A
one-line message reads exactly centered, and a wrapping one keeps the glyph beside its first line. Option B, centering
the glyph on the whole block, floats the glyph between the lines of a two-line message. Q-FM1.1 B: no new tokens just
for the field message, so the offset is computed in the component, not baked into `type.caption.*`.

**The diagnosis.** The row was `align: 'start'`, so the glyph's top met the caption's top. That is centered only when the
caption's line is exactly the glyph's height. Every corpus caption.md line is shorter than the 16px glyph: 15.4px
(11 × 1.4) in four brands and 14px (10 × 1.4) on the reference brand. So the glyph sat 0.3px, or 1px, above the
first line's middle.

**The fix.** The glyph sits in `glyphCell` and the caption in `captionCell`. The row's new `PartDef.firstLine` names the
two cells, the caption and the glyph's size key. At paste, both executors read the caption node's own line height and
the glyph variable's value, and pad the shorter cell down by half the difference. This is the `minLines` division of
labor (textarea's rows): the plan carries names and stays brand-invariant, and the number is frozen per file because
Figma's padding binds one variable and takes no max or half of two. Code computes the same live from `1lh`. The line is
the unrounded one, as the text renders it, so the two middles agree exactly. The row stays top-aligned, as #1009 half 1
requires, and its glyph-height floor (2026-09-25, option (a)) is unchanged. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 51 redraws
`field-message` only, measured by `lint-executor-reach`.

**The gates.** `test.ts` `#3360 field-message glyph on the first line` runs the paste executor per corpus brand, with the
stub's text metrics set to that brand's caption composite and the glyph variable to its `icon.size.xs`. It then places
the glyph and the first line from the built nodes' own layout and paddings, for a one- and a two-line message, at
caption.md and caption.lg, and does the same from the def as code reads it. Tolerance 0.01px. `#3360 built` in
`test-write-components.ts` measures the plugin executor in the shim's layout model. The readback (`anatomy-readback.ts`
`firstLine`) re-derives the agreement from the host's text metrics, glyph height and paddings, and the round-trip
caught a shim that answered the glyph variable and the glyph's box from different tables. Mutations, each failing by
name: main's def, `firstLine` dropped, the row centered, and the line taken off `Math.round` in either executor.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies.** The shim's `resolveForConsumer` and a bound value come from different tables, so a
test building field-message must resolve `icon/size/xs` to the size it binds (`varOverrides`), or the inset is computed
for another glyph. A built Figma file was not measured; the def's `notes.unverified` records the first-line assumption.

## (2026-11-04) — Update's check counts what the same run adds: Wallet button no longer waits for a second run (#3343)

**What.** On the template file, Update listed Wallet button as "can't be updated in place yet". Its blocker was
`Not in this file: provider-logo/button/…`, the 11 provider-logo marks the same run adds. `fileBlockers` read the file as
it is before the run, so the check blocked Wallet button on what the run it was checking would supply, and the owner had
to run Update twice. This PR fixes defect 1 of the issue only. Defect 2, the panel's "the agent's update check says why"
string, belongs to the #3326/#3308 Activity proposal and is unchanged here.

**Fix.** `previewUpdate` (`apps/plugin/src/update-plan.ts`) reads the targets in `nestedFirst` order. Once a target's
read has no blocker, every component name it leaves in the file goes into `addedThisRun`. For a single-component def
that is each planned `<id>/<value>`, adds included, and for a set its own name. Each later target's `fileBlockers` counts
those names as present, the same way #2759's `renamedInto` counts a set this run renames. A blocked target credits
nothing, because the apply refuses it. The previews are still reported in the targets' order, so the hash and every
caller's `sets[i]` read as before. `nestedFirst` moved from `update-apply.ts` to `update-plan.ts`, so the check and the
apply share one order, and `update-apply.ts` re-exports it. It also now matches a single-component target by its `<id>/`
prefix. Before, it matched only a set's exact name, so `wallet-button`'s `provider-logo/button/*` named no target, and
the apply could have written Wallet button before the marks existed.

**Test.** `apps/plugin/test-update-apply.ts`, section `#3343`, on the strict host (the shim default; the copied host and
root are fixed again with `fixHostMethods`). provider-logo is built without its 11 `button/*` marks. wallet-button is
built from an earlier plan whose styled marks nest the provider's logo, so the current plan has 50 members due. The
targets are listed wallet-button first. The arms assert literals: the order puts provider-logo first; the check reads
wallet-button with no blockers and 50 to update, and provider-logo with 11 to add; one run adds the 11 marks and then
updates wallet-button's 50 with no miss and no content left; a second check reads all 68 current; and a run whose
provider-logo plans leave out `button/paypal-gold` still blocks wallet-button with that one mark named, word for word.
A blocked provider credits nothing: a run whose provider-logo is itself blocked (one mark nests a component the file
lacks) still blocks wallet-button on all 11 marks (`run adds/blocked provider`), since the apply would refuse
provider-logo and add none of them.
provider-logo's whole verdict is not asserted. The shim misreads 21 non-square outlines as drift Figma's importer does
not have, as the #2343 arms record, and that is the same before and after this run.

**Mutations** (each committed `wip:` first, restored from `HEAD`):
- `addedThisRun` never filled: `run adds/check`, `run adds/one run`, `run adds/settled` and `run adds/unsupplied` fail.
- `nestedFirst`'s `<id>/` match removed: `run adds/order` fails too.
- The `!preview.blockers.length` guard on the credit removed: `run adds/blocked provider` fails.

**Executor.** No file the executor reaches changed (`update-plan.ts` already imported `emitCoordValue`'s module), so
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays where it is. `lint-executor-revision.ts` agrees.

## (2026-11-03) — Agent link: a read-only `context` command, what the open file is (#3300 B)

**What landed.** `context` (no args) answers an agent's first question in a file: what it is. It is the owner's Q3300.2 A, a read-only command in #3293's family (`apps/plugin/src/agent-reads.ts`). It returns:
- `file`: name, current page and page count;
- `prism3`: the stored brand (`source: local | none | unreadable`), its id, name and modes, the plugin's engine and the newest engine any set was built with (`lastBuilt`), the variable collections, and whether the file is themed;
- `sets`: present, due with why, and queued. These come from the as-built ledger alone, as the read at open does (`ledgerDue`, now shared with `ledgerSets`), so `partial: true`;
- `protected`: what Q3147.11 protects by default: FINAL pages, locked nodes and `Original · …` copies, each `{ id, name, page }`, with counts;
- `commands`, split into read and write;
- `readFirst`, the bridge's resources (#3300 A);
- `engineMcp`, which points at `prism3-engine` and its `validate_brand`, `theme_brand` and `export_theme` (Q3300.4 A);
- `unreadable` and `truncated`.

It answers over the mailbox and the bridge, posts no verdict, writes nothing, and `AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 1.

**The protected walk.** It is one walk over every page, capped at 20,000 nodes (`truncated`), with at most 50 nodes listed per kind (the rest are counted). A FINAL page is listed and not walked, because all of it is protected. The walk does not go inside a locked node, an original or an instance. The rules are one exported constant, `PROTECTED_DEFAULTS`, for Phase 2b's guard to read too.

**Deviations from the proposal's illustrative example, each on purpose:**
- `protected.locked` and `.originals` are lists with `counts` beside them, not bare counts, because §7 asks for each to be "listed exactly".
- `engine.lastApplied` is `lastBuilt`. The file records no engine version for a theme apply, but the ledger records one per set.
- `protected.note` doesn't say writes refuse these, because the guard is Phase 2b and isn't built yet.
- `readback` is in the read list, because `commands.json` says it writes nothing.

**Version class: `minor`, not the proposal's `patch`.** By the change-note policy, a new command is a behavior change, and `commands.json`, a committed artifact, moves with it. `activity` (#3309) declared the same.

**Tests.**
- **The read loops.** `context` joins the read loops in `test-agent-link.ts` and `test-agent-bridge.ts`: `mailbox/context`, `bridge/context`, `envelope/context` and `no-write/context`, against `contextExpected` in `agent-read-fixture.ts`.
- **The fixture** gains a FINAL page, a locked frame with a locked child, and an `Original · Checkout` frame with a locked instance inside. A child inside a protected node is not listed apart.
- **Mailbox arms.** `context/protected/final`, `/locked` and `/originals` check each list on its own line. `context/brand` checks that a stored brand reads as `local` with its id, name and modes, and that a blob this build can't read says `unreadable`.
- **Bridge arms.** `context/commands` checks the read list against every command `commands.json` (the authored `WRITES` in `emit-agent-reference.ts`) says writes nothing, and the write list against every other. `context/engine-mcp` checks the server against the engine's `SERVER_INFO.name` and each tool against `commands.json`'s MCP tools.
- **Review arms.** `context/ledger/present`, `/due` and `/lastBuilt` read a stored two-set ledger: one set at today's engine with a moved definition, one at an older engine. `context/caps/list` and `/truncated` walk a page of 51 locked frames, 51 originals and 20,000 rectangles, so the 50-item list cap and the 20,000-node walk cap are exercised at their real values. Over the bridge, `context/read-first` checks each `readFirst` URI against the resources the bridge serves (`RESOURCES` in `server.ts`).
- **Docs.** `commands.json` is regenerated (`emit-agent-reference.ts` isn't part of `regen.ts`). The ecosystem map gains a `read-context` feature. The agent-link guide, the plugin README, the bridge README and the mailbox runbook list the command, and the guides' line citations into `main.ts`, `agent-dispatch.ts` and `agent-protocol.ts` move with the code.

**Mutations, each failing by name:**

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| The FINAL test dropped | `context/protected/final` |
| The walk going inside a locked node | `context/protected/locked` |
| The `Original · ` test dropped | `context/protected/originals` |
| `page.name` reassigned in the walk | `no-write/context`, on both transports |
| `readback` dropped from the read set | `context/commands` |
| The engine server misnamed `prism3` | `context/engine-mcp` |
| An unreadable brand reported as `none` | `context/brand` |
| `lastBuilt` keeps the oldest engine, or compares as strings | `context/ledger/lastBuilt` |
| The two due reasons swapped | `context/ledger/due` |
| The 50-item list cap dropped | `context/caps/list` |
| The 20,000-node walk cap dropped | `context/caps/truncated` |
| A `readFirst` URI the bridge does not serve | `context/read-first`, `envelope/context` |

## (2026-11-03) — The interactive preview draws the inverse outline and text buttons (#2907)

**What it is.** Owner decisions Q2907.1–.3, all A. Each button set on the interactive preview (Color › Interactive, and Brand's Style guide, which draws the same section) gains two rows after Inverse, each on its own inverse band, like the Inverse row. "Inverse outline" shows rest, hover and pressed with the edge `inverse.interactive.‹c›.border.‹state›`. "Inverse text" is the text button on the band, with no edge. Each state's ink chip carries its ratio badge on the band. The chips and row feet match the Outline and Text rows: `text.‹state›` chips, with `border` and `text` feet. Before this change, the color editor offered "Text · inverse" and "Border · inverse" (six roles per set) that the preview drew only when its ground picker was set to an inverse band. So a designer could change those roles and never see the result.

**The diagnosis that made it small.** The roles were already resolved, and the preview already read them: `outlineStateRoles(method, c, state, true)` is what the Outline and Text rows read on an inverse ground. The new rows call it with the ground fixed to the band, so their fill, ink and edge come from the same helper and cannot disagree with those rows. On an inverse preview ground, the new rows take the page's ground, as the Inverse row does.

**The guard.** Each specimen button now records the roles it paints, in `data-sg-binds` (`fill=…`, `ink=…`, `edge=…`). The new case in `test:chrome` section 19 runs on both hosts, previewing Light and Dark. It takes two lists of what must be drawn, each independent of the preview: the editor's rows as rendered (each column's `.p3-fillrow[data-role]`, `interactiveRowsFor` drawn) and the literal `COLUMN_ROWS`. Every role on either list must be bound by a shown specimen in its column's block, and at least one specimen binding it must paint it: its computed ink, edge or fill must be the emission's hex for the role in that mode. A role nothing binds, or that no specimen paints, fails. That arm passes as long as one specimen paints a role right, so a second arm holds each new row on its own. For each state of the Inverse outline and Inverse text rows, the roles bound are literal keys typed into the test, not read from `outlineStateRoles`: the band's text twin, the band's border twin on the outline row (no edge on the text row), and the band's overlay twin at hover and pressed (no wash at rest, under the default overlay wash). Each one's computed ink, edge and fill must be the emission's hex for that key. It also holds each new row's band to the emission's `inverse.background.primary`.

**Mutations,** each failing the new case by name. Dropping both new rows (the bug as filed) fails `… inverse.interactive.primary.text.hover is drawn … — is not drawn` for each of the 18 inverse text and border roles across the three sets. Dropping the Inverse text row alone fails `… "Inverse text" row draws rest, hover and pressed on its own band … read []`. The role arm stays green there, because those roles are still painted as the Inverse outline row's ink, which is the arm's job: representation by role, not by row. Reading the Inverse outline row's edge off the page twin fails `… inverse.interactive.primary.border.rest is drawn … — bound by 1, painted by 0`. Painting the Inverse text row in the page ink, with its bind unchanged, fails `… "Inverse text" rest binds and paints its own roles …`. Reading both new rows' wash off the page (the #1629 bug) fails `… "Inverse outline" hover binds and paints its own roles …`. The role arm alone passed both of these, which is why the per-row arm exists.

## (2026-11-03) — Field focus drawn inside the field, at its own radius (#3328)

**Status:** engine + plugin, built as the owner decided (Q3328.1 A, the "A′" geometry; Q3328.2 A). ENGINE minor
(change note). `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 49 → 50 (taken second, after #3369 took 49), reaching the nine sets that draw a field ring. No token moves, so
CONTRACT is unchanged.

### What changed

- **The focus sits inside the field.** A focused field's 1px border already took `border.focus`. Its focus ring used
  to sit just outside it (`focus.ring.offset-field`, 0, plus the ring's own 2px stroke compensated outward), with a
  concentric corner written as a literal: the reference brand's 1px field corner became an unbound 3. Now the ring sits
  one border width inside the field on every side, so the border plus the ring's 2px band read as one 3px edge, with
  no outer frame and no layout change.
- **The mechanism is `PartDef.borderInset`,** a binding key for the host border the ring sits inside. It projects as
  `absoluteBorderInset`. Where it resolves above 0, both executors place the ring that far inside the host, skip the
  outward `strokeInset` compensation, and bind the ring's four corners to the host's own corner variables. So the
  radius is the field's token, not a number. Where it resolves to 0, the ring is placed as before. A key rather than a
  flag, so Counter can follow its axis: `outline.ring-border` is the hairline and `ghost.ring-border` is
  `border-width.none`, so ghost keeps its 2px outside ring (Q283.10 A).
- **Controls:** Text field, Password field, Search field and Card number field (through `makeTextField`), Textarea,
  Select, the Code input cell, and Counter (outline).
- **Underline Field style is unchanged.** `applyFieldStyle` drops `borderInset` under underline. That edge has no side
  border to sit inside, and its inline padding is 0, so an inside ring would draw over the value. The ring stays
  outside at the control offset (#2695 Q3). This includes a Search field whose own style is underline. **Owner
  decision Q-F1 A (2026-11-03):** underline-edge fields, Search's underline style included, keep the outside ring, and
  outline-edge fields get the inset focus. This narrows #3328 Q2's "Search field (both edge styles)" to the outline edge.
- The `focus` accessibility lines on Text field, Textarea, Select, Code input and Counter now describe the inside
  indicator for code: an outline with a negative offset of the border width plus the band width.

### Traps

- **The paste shell has 57 B of headroom.** The ring code runs in every paste chunk's shell, and #1798 caps the
  indivisible unit at 37,800 B. This change trimmed four of the ring loop's paste-side miss strings to fit (the
  plugin executor keeps its long ones). Merged onto main after #3369, whose review fix freed 115 B of shell, the
  unit measures 37,743 B (provider-logo), and icon-button stays at 17 chunks. The next shell addition will need the
  ceiling argued, or bytes found elsewhere.
- The corner binding on an instance is a host write that has not yet been run on a live Figma host. The shim reads it
  back. The first Update of a file holding a focused field is that probe.

### Verification

See the PR's Ready comment for the full `npm run verify` table and every mutation. Two new `test.ts` arms:
`#3328 field focus geometry` (both executors, 8 controls) and `#3328 field focus 2.4.13` (8 controls × 5 brands ×
4 modes against literal 3:1 and 2px). `lint-absolute-inset.ts` gains `MUST_SIT_INSIDE_BORDER`.

A third arm, `#3328 Q-F1 underline keeps the outside ring`, came from the review: the underline exception was ungated,
so deleting `applyFieldStyle`'s `borderInset` drop passed every gate. The arm draws all 7 underline-edge fields under
underline through both executors. Each plan's ring must carry no `absoluteBorderInset`, and the ring must sit exactly
4px outside the field on every side (2px offset plus the 2px stroke, compensated outward). Mutation: keeping
`borderInset` under underline fails it by name on the plan and on both executors. The ring then lands at −1,−1, 1px
outside, which a looser "outside on every side" check would have passed.

## (2026-11-03) — Components: a box per set in families with two or more roots (#3306)

**Status:** plugin UI (`apps/studio/src/state/component-groups.ts`, `domains/components.ts`, `state/update-file.ts`,
`shell/update-file.ts`), shared by both hosts but drawn only in the plugin. ENGINE patch (change note): no committed
artifact, emission or component surface moves. The executor, `build-deps.ts` and the plugin's `main.ts` are untouched,
so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` does not move.

### What the owner decided

The proposal on #3306 (2026-11-02), answered on 2026-11-03 with Q3306.1–6 all A. It narrows #3129's R5, which had one
box per family and none on a part.

- **.1 Which families split.** A family gets a box per set when it has two or more ROOTS, its public sets that no other
  set in the family nests (`rootsOf`, `splitsOf`). On `main` that is Buttons, Icon button, Flush icon button and Icons &
  assets. A family with one root keeps one box, because ticking the root already builds the rest. The rule reads the
  catalog's `nests` and lists no family by hand. A private `_` part never gets a box.
- **.2 A needed set** is one a chosen set nests, transitively, that the file lacks, is buildable, and was not chosen
  itself. Its box is ticked and held (`aria-disabled`, the chrome's existing held style), and it counts toward its
  family's and its section's mixed state. A tick on it writes nothing.
- **.3 Needed sets are derived on read** (`neededOf`) from the queue and the catalog, never written to the queue.
  Unticking the set that needs one drops it, with nothing left behind. The walk matches `build-deps.ts`'
  `missingDependencies`: a set the file holds is not descended into.
- **.4 The tag reads "Needed".** The needing set goes in the box's name and title ("Button, needed by Button.Group", or
  "…, needed by 2 sets"), so the tag stays short at 380.
- **.5 The badge counts chosen sets only,** matching To add's rows. Under the rows, one line names the needed sets, inside
  the family and outside it. This fixes P3 of the proposal: a nested set used to be built without notice until the
  run's summary.
- **.6 A family box that is on takes out only the sets chosen in that family.** A set that a chosen set elsewhere needs
  stays held.

Every box is three-state again: R5's two-state row box is retired by .2. Strings are DRAFT.

### The owner's calls on the review (2026-11-03)

- **Copy approved as written:** the intro, "{set}, needed by {set}" / "{set}, needed by {n} sets", and the "Needed" tag.
- **One "Also adds:" line (A).** #3308 (merged first) drew its own line under To add, naming the sets `_Doc-block` is made
  from on a first run with panels on, on the same hook. The two are now one line, `alsoAddsOf`: everything the run builds
  alongside the picks, the needed sets and the `_Doc-block` sets together, each once, in Components' order, under the
  hook `update-add-also`. It reads "Also adds: Button, Divider, List Item, Spinner."
- **Private parts hidden from that line (B).** Accordion Indicator, Breadcrumb separator and Slider Thumb are still
  built, without being named.
- **Select all (A).** It queues the needed sets it covers as chosen, as before; an arm now pins it.

### Where a flat section's box goes

Buttons is a section with settings, so its sets are rows at the section's edge (Q8 A). Each set's box takes the fold
cell there, under the section's box, which stands for the family. Link is a section of one set with no family, so its
section box is the row's (R5), and that is the box that shows held when Banner is queued.

### Tests

- `test-component-groups.ts` §2b, one assertion per rule, each against a literal fixture typed from the proposal (the
  split families and their roots; the sample file's needed map; badge 3 and the Also line). Every rule has a mutation that
  fails by name, nine in all. The mutation that **stores the needed sets in the queue** (`toggleSets` writing
  `neededOf` along with the chosen set) fails `Q3306.3 A: a tick writes the chosen set alone …`. It also fails four older
  call-8 checks, because a family tick would then write sets outside the family.
- `test:chrome` §3129: R5's two-state check is replaced by a three-state check. New arms cover the set boxes in the split
  families, the held box (its state, name, title and Needed tag), a held tick that posts nothing, Buttons with only
  Button.Group chosen (a box per set at the section's edge, Button held, the badge counting 1 chosen set plus 2 due), and
  To add's Also line. Mutations fail by name: set boxes off in a family row; set boxes off in a flat section; held marking
  dropped; Also line not drawn.
- The review's fix round: a private part named in the line fails `Also adds (owner, A and B): one line …`; the line split
  in two (needed sets and `_Doc-block` sets each on its own `update-add-also`) fails `#3308, #3306: panels on …` at all
  six viewports. That arm and §3129's now read every `update-add-also` in the dialog, not the first. The vacuous private-root fixture gains one nothing nests (`rootsOf`
  without `isPrivate` fails by name), `neededOf`'s `buildable` skip is pinned by a planted set with no geometry, and
  Select all's needed-set behavior has its own arm.
- **One mutation stayed green, on purpose.** With the held box's click guard removed, the model still writes nothing for
  a held set (`toggleSets` holds it, by name, in `test-component-groups.ts`). The render can't see the guard on its own,
  so the arm's header says so instead of claiming it.

### Knock-on

- `apps/plugin/test-update-owner-run.ts` (#3308) replays the owner's ticks to build their exact nine-set queue. It ticked
  Checkbox row and Icon after the sets that nest them, and under Q3306.2 A those boxes are held and the ticks write
  nothing. The replay now ticks the two nested sets first, which reaches the same nine sets. The queue under test is
  unchanged.
- `docs/public/guides/*`: the Components guide quotes the new intro and lists Needed among a set's states. The other
  guides' line pointers into the four edited files are remapped by the diff's own line map, and `lint-guide-claims` holds
  every quote. `ecosystem.json`'s add-queue line names the set boxes and the held needed sets.

## (2026-11-03) — Dialog: the body clips and scrolls under the pinned footer (G14, #3163)

**Status:** engine + plugin executor change, `engine: minor` (change note `claude-3163-dialog-body-scroll.md`).
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` 48 → 49, and `executor-reach.json` names `dialog` for it. CONTRACT unchanged: no token is added and
no token name moves. Item 1 of the build order on #3130 (Q3130.9 A); owner decision Q3130.8 A (every placement).

### What changed

- **The bug (#3163):** on a rebuild of the reference brand's mobile screens, a full-screen Dialog with a long form drew
  its pinned footer over the form, and the fields spilled past the dialog. The body neither clipped nor scrolled
  (`clipsContent = false`, `overflowDirection = NONE`).
- **The schema:** a box part can declare `scroll: 'vertical'`. It projects as `overflowDirection = VERTICAL`. The
  validator refuses it on any kind but a box, refuses any other direction, and refuses it without `clipsContent: true`,
  because a frame that scrolls without cropping still draws its overflow over the footer.
- **Both executors** now write `overflowDirection` on every FRAME, `NONE` unless the plan says otherwise, the way
  `clipsContent` is threaded. The plugin's also writes it on a slot as it creates it; the paste payload carries it from
  the frame onto the slot (`__SLOT_FIELDS`) instead, because a second write in its shell pushed provider-logo's paste
  unit past #1798's 90% floor. A component set has no `overflowDirection` (`ComponentSetNode` lacks
  `FramePrototypingMixin`), so neither executor writes it there. The one write left in the paste shell moves
  icon-button's set from 17 chunks to 18, re-pinned in `test.ts` with a note, as the earlier shell-byte moves were.
- **Dialog's `body`** declares `clipsContent: true` and `scroll: 'vertical'` on all 24 members. At full and end the body
  already grows to the height the header and footer leave, so it is now the scroll region between them. Center and
  bottom hug, so the crop shows there only once a designer fixes the height.
- **The code projection** was already right in prose ("only the body scrolls"). The code note now names the shape: a
  flex-column panel, the body `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto`.
- **The component shim** now starts a frame at Figma's `overflowDirection: 'NONE'`, so writing the default reads as no
  change and only Dialog's drawing moves for `lint-executor-reach`.

### The gates

- `test:roundtrip` gains a Dialog block with its own model of Figma's auto layout, read off the host's fields: a FIXED
  column gives a `layoutGrow: 1` child the height its padding, gaps and other children leave. With 1,200px of content in
  the 360 × 640 full member and the 480 × 800 end member, the footer's top is at or below the body's visible bottom.
  Every member's body clips and scrolls. Mutations: the def's `clipsContent` removed fails
  `roundtrip/dialog body clips` (every member, and the footer top 580 against a visible bottom of 1320 at full); both
  executor `overflowDirection` writes removed fails `roundtrip/dialog body scrolls` and the corpus diff.
- `lint-unclaimed-defaults` gains an `overflowDirection` row (FRAME). With the writes removed it fails A1 on every def.
- `test.ts` pins the plan (every member's body slot carries both fields, no other def plans an `overflowDirection`)
  and each refusal arm by name. Mutation: the without-`clipsContent` refusal deleted fails `#3163 a box declaring scroll
  without clipsContent is refused BY NAME`.
- `lint-executor-reach` passes with entry 49 naming `dialog` alone, so no other set's drawing moved. With entry 49 set
  to `[]` it fails `dialog: drawn differently by revision 49 than by 48` in all eight arms.
- **The paste leg (review finding 1):** `test.ts` gains `#3163 paste leg`. Every Dialog member is pasted through the
  payload, and the stub host's body must read `SLOT VERTICAL clips`, a literal. The round-trip arms drive only the plugin
  executor, so before this an agent-pasted Dialog could lose its scroll silently. Mutation: `'overflowDirection'` dropped
  from `__SLOT_FIELDS` fails `#3163 paste leg: … (0/24) — … SLOT undefined clips`.

### The paste-unit ceiling (review finding 2)

This PR and #3372 each add one write to the paste shell, and together they took provider-logo's paste unit to 37,858 B,
past #1798's 37,800 B ceiling. The shell now names the four per-side stroke weights once (`__SIDE`), where three checks
had spelled them out. Nothing a host sees changes. Provider-logo's unit drops from 37,787 B to 37,672 B (−115 B), so the
two PRs fit under the ceiling in either merge order. icon-button's set goes back from 18 chunks to 17, re-pinned in
`test.ts`.

### Decided

- **The part name (Q3163.1 A, owner, 2026-11-03):** the part keeps the name `body`. No rename. The proposal's row 1
  called it `bodyViewport`, for an item 2 that would have put a `body` instance inside it. Q3130.1 was revised to keep the
  body a native slot, whose Figma property is named for its layer, so a rename would have changed the property designers
  see.

### Not proven

- **What a shim cannot prove:** that a real Figma host keeps both values on the native slot and scrolls the content in
  a prototype. That is in Dialog's `unverified` notes.

## (2026-11-03) — The contrast floor gets its own sub-heading and says what it checks (#3366)

**What it is.** Owner decisions Q3366.1–.6, all A. In Color › Surfaces & fills, the contrast floor (`surfaces.floorStep`) leaves the "Default" tier list for its own "Contrast floor" sub-heading, between Default and Inverse. Its row reads "Measured on", with "A setting, not a token" where a tier's token sits. Under the row, always shown, are three things. First, a line that names how many colors the floor checks. Second, the six groups those colors fall in, each with a count and a sample swatch: Links, Brand and status text and icons, Secondary and tertiary text and placeholder, Disabled text and icon, Bold fills, and Button fills. Third, a line naming what it does not check: field borders, button borders and the focus ring. Inspect › Contrast › Health gains a pointer under its mode list. It names the floor in Light and Dark, and "Change the contrast floor" closes Inspect, opens Surfaces & fills (on the Settings pane at the narrow tier) and puts focus on the floor's step button. Health now says "minimum" for a pair's own ratio ("All 884 pairs at or above their minimum."), so on that panel "floor" names only the setting. The bar's verdict line is not Health and keeps "floor".

**Where the list comes from.** It is read at draw time, so the count and the groups can't drift from the engine: `floorGroups` (`state/fills-input.ts`) takes every role in the previewed mode whose `against` is the floor. That floor is the one the engine measures `foreground.brand` on, which is how the page already read it for the Auto label. The roles are grouped by name. A governed role that no group takes is not hidden: it is counted in the total and listed as "Other", a fallback that no example brand reaches.

**The diagnosis that made it small.** The engine already records the floor on each governed role: its `against` is the floor's palette path (`neutral.050`). Other roles' `against` names a role (`background.secondary`), so nothing in the engine had to change. Across the three example brands, every mode gives the same 47 roles. The floor's info button and its sentence (QA-B6) are gone, because the line under the row now says it, always. The step button keeps the accessible name the owner chose for it on #2193 ("Contrast floor, Light: Auto · …"), so the row's new visible label did not move it.

**The gate.** `test-fills-input.ts` §12 holds `floorGroups` against a literal role list typed from the issue's measured table, group by group, in every mode of prism3, aurora and harbor (12 brand modes, with a floor on that count). The same section holds the "not checked" line to the engine: no field border, button border or focus ring is measured on the floor. Mutations, each failing by name: dropping `disabled` from `FLOOR_GROUPS` fails `… the "disabled" group (Disabled text and icon) holds exactly its 2 roles` and the total, in all 12 modes. Measuring `field.border.rest` on the floor in the engine fails `… the "not checked" line holds …` and the total. `test:chrome` reads the block as rendered on both hosts, holds it to the DRAFT copy and prism3's groups as literals, and drives the Health pointer from Type at 1280 and 380 on both hosts.

**Trap found while building it.** The group swatches first set `background` inline without `data-content`, which the chrome's runtime-inline-value check refuses outside brand content. They now carry `data-content`, like a fill row's swatch, and keep their color under forced colors.

The engine has always accepted `actionPalette: 'neutral'`: `theme.ts` checks the lever against every defined palette, and `neutral` is always one (the `t-red` corpus brand already builds that way). The owner decided it on 2026-11-03 while settling #3336: the reference brand's buttons and links are near-black, and the owner wants to pick `neutral` directly instead of keeping a duplicate gray palette.

**The change.** `paletteRefOptions` gives every palette picker the same list: `primary`, `neutral`, then the brand colors. A Stop or a refusal ends it as it ends the update. The chrome arm `#3308: a run that sets the file up and writes its theme ends with the cover` (section 10) holds the panel's posts after Theme and that the step's verdict ends the run, at every width and theme.

## (2026-11-03) — Studio: one settings rhythm, five named tokens and a gate on every place (#3337)

The owner's screenshot of Components › Button options showed settings stacked on each other: a segmented control's
bottom edge on the next setting's name, a readout line running into the next name, "Set it in …" links indented off
the column, and a read-only row's note drawn over its own name. The owner chose Q3337.1–.5 A.

### The diagnosis that made the fix small

One missing rule, not a scatter of margins. `.p3-bopts`, the root all nine option blocks draw their rows into, had no
CSS at all, so its rows sat in a plain block with no gap. The Theme pages only kept their 24px rhythm because each row's
parent (`.p3-lsec`, `.p3-icol`) supplied a grid gap; a container one level down skipped it, and nothing noticed.

### What changed

- **Five named chrome tokens** (`chrome/spec.mjs`, product rows over the space scale): `--p3-rhythm-label` (space.150),
  `--p3-rhythm-hint` (space.100), `--p3-rhythm-row` (space.300), `--p3-rhythm-group` (space.500) and
  `--p3-rhythm-section` (space.200). They are the values the Theme pages already used, so the Theme pages do not move;
  `.p3-lsec`, `.p3-icol`, `.p3-icols`, `.p3-levers-body`, `.p3-lever-ctl` and the L2 legend now read the names.
- **`.p3-bopts` is a grid at `--p3-rhythm-row`**, which fixes every Components option block at once.
- **"Set it in …" is a flush text link** (Q3337.2 A): `.p3-btn.p3-deplink` drops its inline padding and its edge, so its
  words start on the row's edge. It stays a whole target tall and underlined, with the chevron after it.
- **Read-only rows** (Q3337.3 A): in a group, a div lever's control already starts space-050 under its head, so its
  description takes no second pull. Three stacked pulls had put the note 4px over the name.
- **Export joins the rhythm** (Q3337.4 A): its settings are one `.p3-export-sets` grid at the row rhythm (12px → 24px),
  each label space-050 over its control, each note the hint rhythm under it. Before/after renders are in the PR for the
  owner's sign-off.

### The gate: `test:chrome` section `3337` (shard 2)

Both hosts, both themes, 1280 and 380, on every place that holds settings: Brand, Color × 3, Type, Shape, Depth,
Layout, Components with all nine option blocks open, and Export. Row → row is at least the emission's `space.300`, read
by section 30's `HT` oracle from `prism3.tokens.json`, never from `chrome.css`. It also checks that no control ends
within that distance above another row's name, that every "Set it in …" link starts within 1px of its row, and that a
read-only row's note starts below its name. Each option block is named literally with a floor of rows, and each place
has literal floors on rows and pairs. Color › Fills has a pairs floor of 0, because each of its levers is alone in its
section.

Mutations, each failing by name in all eight host × theme × width runs:
- `.p3-bopts`' gap dropped → `3337 figma light 1280 / components / button-options: "Button icons" → "Medium button label & icon" 0px < 24px (row → row, space.300)`;
- the link's inline padding restored → `… / components / shared-options: "Set it in Shape › Density" starts 16px in from its row (≤ 1px)`.

Run over `main`'s CSS (`chrome.css`, `bar.ts` and `spec.mjs` restored, both bundles rebuilt), the section fails 224 of its 649 assertions: 168 on Components, 32 on Export, and 24 for the three indented links on Shape and Type.

### Not here

The Weights read-only value runs past the card's edge at 1280. It is #3338, filed separately.

## (2026-11-03) — Update file offers a usage panel drawn by an older panel format, even when its set is current (#3205)

**What was wrong.** #3318 raised `PANEL_FORMAT` to 6 so that every usage panel would be due once. In the template, after
an Update with a build that included it, Dialog's panel still read format 5 with its specimens FIXED at 62px: Update file
never offered it. Update file decides which sets its check reads from the as-built ledger (`dueOf`), with no page loaded,
and the ledger knew nothing of the panel format. Dialog's set was current, so it was never ticked and never checked, and
`docPanelDue`, which does read the panel's format, never ran on it. #3318's tests drove `docPanelDue` and the redraw
directly, not this path.

**The fix.** Each ledger entry on a family's lead set carries the panel format it was checked at (`panel`), while
Documentation has the usage panels on (`main.ts`, `panelFormatOf` in `ledgerNow` and the build's record). `dueOf` gives a
set that is otherwise current a due reason of its own, `panel`, when its entry's format isn't today's: the format-due
credit. The full read, the read at open and the badge's recount all go through `dueOf`, so they agree. The check then
reads the set, `docPanelDue` finds the older plan, and the apply redraws the panel in place, or keeps it as "(edited)"
if a person changed it (#3317's rule). The apply records the set with today's format, so it reads current again. A write
with the panels off keeps the format the file holds. Studio shows the reason as "Engine update: Prism3 draws usage panels
differently" (the owner's Q3205.F1 A, 2026-11-02: keep the line as built).

**Cost.** Every lead set in a file with the usage panels on reads due once after this ships, because no entry recorded a
panel format before it. That is the redraw #3318 meant to make. Later raises of `PANEL_FORMAT` reach Update file the same
way.

**Tests and mutations,** each committed `wip:` first:
- `test-doc-panel.ts` `format due/…`, on the strict host: Dialog's set current, its panel at format 5 with collapsed
  specimens. The ledger read lists it due, the scoped check offers it, one apply redraws it with each specimen FIXED at
  560 with `minWidth` 560, and a hand-edited panel is kept. `test-build-completed.ts` `format due/…`, through the real
  `main.ts`: the build records the format, an entry without one reads due in `file-sets` and the badge's recount, and
  not with the panels off. `test-as-built-ledger.ts` `format due/…`.
- The format-due credit dropped from `dueOf` → `format due/offered`, `format due/redrawn`, `format due/edited kept`,
  `format due/main`, `format due/no format`, `format due/older`.
- `panelFormatOf` giving no entry its format → `format due/build`, `format due/main`.

**After review.**
- `main.ts`'s own apply record is now under test. `test-build-completed.ts` `format due/recorded by main` runs an update
  through the real `main.ts` over Badge's entry with no format. It reads due for its panel before, and current after
  with format 6 recorded. Mutation: the apply's record giving `panel: undefined` → `format due/recorded by main`.
- "Due forever" for a panel whose draw is still blocked doesn't happen. The check offers no panel while it's blocked,
  but it doesn't block the set either. Update file's apply runs on every ticked set the check didn't block
  (`updatableOf`), and `main.ts` records the format whether or not a panel was drawn. So the set is offered once and
  then reads current. `test-doc-panel.ts` `format due/blocked` covers it. Mutation: the check blocking a set whose panel
  draw is blocked → `format due/blocked`.

**Owed.** Real-Figma confirmation: after an Update in the template, Dialog's panel is offered and redrawn, and its
specimen reads FIXED at 560 with `minWidth` 560.

## (2026-11-03) — Password field's label row is the label's line again: the Show button's block padding zeroed on the instance (#3347)

**Engine 0.238.0.** Found by the owner's real-Figma check of #3014 (2026-11-02, build 89c83809). Q380 A
meant the label row to be one label line tall (18 / 21 / 24). It measured 26 on all 84 members, with the label at 21.

### Diagnosis
The host floors a hugging row at a STRETCHED child's own content height, not at the height it is set to. The Show
button is a small flush text Button: bound 36 tall, with `space.075` (6px) above and below its `label/sm` line (12 ×
1.15 = 13.8). So its floor is 6 + 13.8 + 6 = 25.8, which the host shows as 26. A taller label (27) passed it, which is
why the row followed the label there. Every offline model missed it: `test.ts`'s #2804 arm left a stretched child out
of the row's height, and the shim measured a stretched instance at its main's height.

### What changed
- **The fix, the smaller of the two the issue named.** A new `PartDef.nestPaddingBlock` binds a nested instance's top
  and bottom padding as an instance override. The toggle binds `toggle.pad-block` → `space.0`, so its floor is the
  13.8 "Show" line, under every label line. The row hugs the label again, still grows with a larger label style, and
  keeps the stretch #3014 measured as safe. "Show" stays centered on the row, as before. Button's own set is
  untouched. The other option, Q3014.2 A (drop the stretch and bind the nested Button's height to the label's line
  height), needs a line-height variable the emission doesn't carry, and it gives up growing with the label.
- **No executor change.** Both executors already bind a plan's `bound` on every node they make, an instance
  included. So `EXECUTOR_REVISION` and `executor-reach.json` don't move, and `lint-executor-revision` passes.
- **Shim:** `stretchFloorsHug` (opt-in, under `layoutModel`) models the measured rule. A child stretched across a
  hugging row takes the row's height, and the row counts it at its own content height: block padding (an instance's
  override, else its main's) plus flow content.
- **Test:** a `test:roundtrip` arm builds Password field on that shim, with every variable and line box from the
  default brand's emission, and asserts on all 84 members that `labelRow` is the literal 18 / 21 / 24, hugging, with
  the toggle as tall as the row. A self-check first clears the toggle's override and must read back the real file's
  26 (it reads 25.8), so the arm can fail. **Mutation:** removing `nestPaddingBlock` from the toggle fails the arm by
  name: `#3347 password-field label row … 84 off — status=default, size=medium, state=rest: the label row is 25.8,
  not 21`.

### Not done here
- A real-Figma re-check after merge, on a scratch file: the label row at 18 / 21 / 24, and the toggle's padding
  override held on the instance. Neither gate covers this: the shim's floor is modeled from one measurement.
