## (2026-11-03) — Update file builds _Doc-block's sets first on a first run, so every queued set gets its usage panel (#3308, Q3308.3 A)

**The defect.** The owner's first run built five sets "with problems", each for one reason: "No usage panels drawn: this file has no _Doc-block component". Set up file, the run's first step, cannot build `_Doc-block` until Badge, Tag, List item and Divider exist, and nothing later in the run builds it. The owner chose Q3308.3 A: with Documentation's usage panels on and no `_Doc-block`, Update file's run also builds those four first, listed as "Also builds", then `_Doc-block`, before the queued sets.

**The fix.** Update file's sets step asks each build for it (`build-components`' new `docBlock`, sent by `postCurrent` in the panel's `main.ts`). The plugin's `buildComponents` acts on the ask only while the panels are on, the file has no `_Doc-block`, and the file holds the theme the template binds (`docBlockThemed`). It then builds the four sets the file lacks first, each with the sets it nests, as a nested set is built, then `_Doc-block` on the File Components page (`ensureDocBlock`, found by `fileComponentsPageOf`), then this set. A set built before the template exists waits for its panel and is seated again once the panel's room can be measured (`docPanelReach` is 0 without the template). When the set asked for is one of the four, it is built before the template, which follows it. The verdict names what was built first ("Also built: …") and "Built _Doc-block". The file's read (`file-sets`) now says which of the four the file lacks when it has no `_Doc-block` (`docBlockLacks`). Update file's To add lists the ones the queue does not hold as "Also builds, when the file lacks them: …" (the existing words of `RUN_COPY.also`), and the run puts the queued ones first (`runOrderOf`), so a queued Badge builds the template itself and is not built twice. With the panels off, or without the ask (the Components page's build, an agent's), nothing changes (#3311).

**What a later reader should know.** A queue holding two or more of the four still builds the second one twice: the first post builds every one the file lacks, and the later post finds its set present ("✓ already built", clean). The ask cannot name the queue's later sets without the plugin waiting on sets that are not built yet. The owner's selection holds one (Badge).

**Tests.** `apps/plugin/test-update-doc-block.ts` drives the real `main.ts` under the strict host on a fresh file with the owner's ticks (nine sets), using #3323's host: `panels/on` (the read names the four, "Also builds" names Tag, Divider and List Item, Badge runs first, every queued set completes clean with no "No usage panels drawn" line, `_Doc-block` and the four are in the file, and each queued set's family has a live panel), `panels/off` (none of the extra sets, no template, no panel, the queue's order), and `no ask` (a build without the ask is as it was). The chrome arm `#3308: panels on/off, a file with no _Doc-block` (section 10) holds the To add line and the posts, at every width and theme. The shim gains one thing, scoped to a several-page file (`pages`): Figma takes a live component's own id as an instance-swap value, as the usage panel's Specimen sets it.

**Shim gaps met, not fixed.** The shim's search returns no frames, so a set built twice (Checkbox.Row after Checkbox group, the double build #3320 removes) cannot find the panel it replaces and reads it as in the way; and the shim's instances carry no children, so a drawn panel reports "_Doc-block has no text layer". Neither is this decision's, and the suite asserts around them by name.

**Mutations, each failing by name.** The build ignoring the ask (`blockFirst` false) → `panels/on: sets/…`, `_Doc-block`, and the panels. The ask ignoring the panels switch → `panels/off: nothing extra`. A waiting panel drawn at once → `panels/on: sets/badge` and the panels. `runOrderOf` keeping the queue's order → `panels/on: run order`. `docBlockAlsoOf` ignoring the switch → `panels/off: also builds`. `postCurrent` not asking → the chrome arm.

## (2026-11-03) — Update check: the file's names read once, the pass's member reads reused (#3313)

On the template the Update check took about 20 s before the dialog could show anything. #3302's measurement on the
template-sized stand-in from #3312 put it at 2.6M host calls. #3313 named where they went: reading every member again
(44%), and `fileBlockers` rebuilding every component's name once per set (28%).

### The fix

- **The names, once per check.** `previewUpdate` builds the file's component and set names once, after every set is
  located, and hands the set to `fileBlockers` for each set. It is the same list for every set in a run.
- **The pass's reads, kept** (`member-views.ts`). The hand-edit pass at open already reads every member's snapshot,
  stamp and record, which is the view the dry run lays its plans against. `handEditsOf` hands each set's view on, and
  `checkSets` passes `previewUpdate` a lookup by set node id. Every kept view is dropped together:
  - when a document change touches any component or set, or any node inside one. Figma never reports an instance
    sublayer updated by its main component, so an edit to one set can resize another set's members unheard;
  - on any style change. Figma never reports a node updated by a style either, so a text style's size can re-flow
    every member that uses it unheard (#3348's review: the check read no move where a fresh read read 41);
  - when a change can't be placed (a deletion, unreadable parents);
  - when a write starts or ends (`guarded`).

  A change outside every component and set (a canvas frame, a usage panel) keeps them.

  A read that was in progress during any drop is not kept (`viewEpoch`).
- **What a kept view doesn't hold is read every time** (`freshView`):
  - how each member draws against the file's variables (`drawn`), because a variable's value can change with no
    document change;
  - the set's publish status.
- **The apply never uses a kept view.** It reads each set again before it writes, under the check's hash, so a view
  kept wrongly makes the apply refuse, not write.
- **Sets only.** A single-component def's read depends on the plans the brand projects (`readSingleView`). The pass and
  the check can project for different brands, so those defs are read fresh.

### Measured

Template stand-in, every set ticked:
- on `main`: about 2.80M host calls (both fixes mutated back out);
- names once per check: 2.00M;
- both fixes: 0.84M.

The `drawn` re-read is about 137k of the remainder. It is kept so the check stays exact.

Not done: the issue's second item, `checkSets` projecting every target's plans in one turn before the read starts, is
left for its own change.

### Gates

New arms in `test-open-large-file.ts`, after the template's open:
- `check/calls`: at most 900,000 host calls;
- `check/views`: all 57 sets are kept, and each kept read, as handed on, equals a fresh `readSetView` field for field;
- `check/same`: the answer is the same over the kept reads, over them again, and over a fresh read of every set;
- `check/drops`: a hand edit heard as `documentchange` after the pass is in the next answer, as a fresh read gives it.

The stand-in gains one glyph vector reaching past its frame, so a `drawn` fault exists to lose. Mutations, each failing
by name:
- `fileBlockers` rebuilding the names per set → `check/calls` (1.64M);
- the check not given the kept reads → `check/calls` (2.00M);
- a kept view handed on without `drawn` read again → `check/views`;
- the listener's drop removed → `check/drops`.

After review, more arms:
- `test-update-apply.ts`, `views/…`, on the strict shim. A set's read is kept, then a member grows with no change of
  its own, as a re-flow grows it. Then the one change Figma would report is sent: a style change, a main component
  resized outside every set, another set's member resized, or a text inside another set's member edited. The check
  laid against the kept read must equal a fresh read, whole. The premise shows the kept read is stale with no drop
  (44 moves fresh, 0 against it). `views/canvas` keeps the view for a canvas frame's change; `views/epoch` refuses a
  read that ran across a drop.
- `test-open-large-file.ts`, `check/write start` and `check/write end`: a write drops every view as it starts, and a
  view kept while it runs is gone after it.

Mutations, each failing by name:
- `STYLE_*` changes skipped → `views/style`;
- a component change not dropping the views → the three `views/main …` arms;
- `keepView` ignoring its epoch → `views/epoch`;
- `guarded`'s drop at the start removed → `check/write start`; at the end → `check/write end`; both → both.

## (2026-11-03) — `lint-fill-under-hug` gains its height twins, Accordion's and Password field's rows named measured-safe (#3014)

**Engine 0.238.0.** Owner decision Q3014.1 A: measure first, and if both rows keep their hug, close #3014
as not a defect and add the height twins with these two named measured-safe. The owner measured on 2026-11-02 (plugin
build 89c83809): every Accordion `titleRow` (48) and Password field `labelRow` (84) main reads `counterAxisSizingMode:
AUTO` after the build, and on instances both rows grow with their content (Accordion's medium title row 20 → 66 with a
four-line title; Password field's label row 26 → 27 with a `body/lg/default` label), the stretched indicator and toggle
following. The host does not freeze a hugging height the way Q537 found it freezes a width.

### What changed
- **Gate** `lint-fill-under-hug.ts`: two more arms, `stretch-under-hugging-row` (a stretch across a row whose height
  hugs) and `grow-under-hugging-column` (a grow down a column whose height hugs). They are not a host rule: a height
  fill is refused only when it is unmeasured. `MEASURED_SAFE` names the three shapes the measurement covered, by def
  and part path, typed in the gate: Accordion's `titleRow > leadingIndicator` and `> trailingIndicator`, and Password

## (2026-11-02) — Tabs: the selected indicator overlaps the baseline (#3344)

The owner asked for Tabs to draw as Prism 2 did: the selected tab's 2px indicator overlaps the list's 1px baseline, with their bottom edges aligned and the indicator painted over the line. Engine `0.238.0`.

### Diagnosis

Both lines were already foot pins (#2928): the indicator across each tab's bottom edge, the baseline across the list's. What stacked them was the list's 1px `blockEnd` inset, which #2928 kept so the baseline would sit where it used to when it took a cell. The baseline was also the list's last child, so it painted over the tabs.

### What changed

- `tabs.ts`: the root drops its bottom inset, so the tabs reach the list's bottom edge and both bars end on the same line. The root's children become `['baseline', 'items']`, so the baseline draws first and every tab's bar paints over it. The list is 1px shorter.
- The baseline stays one part of the list, not a rule moved into each tab. That keeps the anatomy as it was: it still spans the whole list, including the empty sides of the centered bar. A tab placed on its own carries no line it doesn't need, and nothing is renamed.
- No executor code moves. Both executors already place a foot pin by name whatever its position among the children, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays where it is. Update file redraws Tabs because the plan moved.
- The spec sheet now lists `container/baseline` before `container/items`, because Figma's draw order is child order.

### Tests

`apps/plugin/test-tabs-indicator.ts` builds `tabs` and its `tab-item` through the real executor into the shim, with its layout model on and the two thicknesses at 1px and 2px. It checks every member (3 sizes × 2 alignments) with literal expectations:
- `#3344 tabs indicator bottom`: every tab's indicator bottom equals the baseline's bottom.
- `#3344 tabs paint order`: the baseline draws before the tabs.

Mutation: with the stacked layout put back, both arms fail by name (18 of 18 off: bar bottom 8, baseline bottom 9). Each half of the mutation fails only its own arm.

### Held / gaps

- **No web arm.** No web, React or Storybook projection draws Tabs yet; code delivery is still pending (#2454). The studio's component preview draws Buttons only. So the code side is the contract in the Tabs `codeOnly` entry for the selected underline, which now states the bottom alignment and the paint order. The web arm the issue asks for lands with that code layer.
- RTL is code only: the list mirrors, and the overlap doesn't depend on direction. Density doesn't move either thickness.

## (2026-11-02) — The desktop bridge describes itself: a connect note and five resources (#3300 A)

**What landed.** `tools/figma-bridge/server.ts` sends the owner's approved note (Q3300.1 A, verbatim) as `instructions` in the `initialize` and `server/discover` results and as `readFirst` in `figma_status`, all from one constant, `BRIDGE_INSTRUCTIONS`. It serves five static resources (Q3300.3 A) through `resources/list` and `resources/read`: the rebind and consume skills, `commands.json`, `figma-conventions.json` and `llms.txt`, each read once at start from the checkout and stamped with `ENGINE_VERSION`. Both handshake results now share one `CAPABILITIES` value, which adds `resources: { listChanged: false }`. An unknown URI fails with `-32002`; a file that cannot be read is named in the error rather than stopping the server.

**Why `readFirst` too.** The bridge answers Claude Code at `2024-11-05` (#3109), and `instructions` is newer than that version. Whether the host shows the field there is the first live check. `figma_status` already says "Call first", so the note reaches the agent either way.

**The note counts 903 characters, not the proposal's 904.** The text is the approved one character for character; the proposal's count included the code block's closing newline.

**The note names `context`, which arrives in B.** It is the approved text. Until B merges, `figma_run context` answers `unknown-command`.

**Gates.** New arms in `apps/plugin/test-agent-bridge.ts`, at the end of the suite because `figma_status` with no plugin connected issues a pairing code and `pair/on-demand` asserts that has not happened yet: `instructions/length` (≤ 1,200), `instructions/rules` (a hand-written list: FINAL, locked, `Original · `, detach, version, `avoid_when`, `core.*`, and no RFC 2119 words), `instructions/same` (both `initialize` versions, `server/discover` and `readFirst`), `resources/capability`, `resources/list`, `resources/resolve` (a sentinel phrase per resource, written in the test, plus the stamp and `-32002`), `resources/public-only` (every path under `skills/` or `docs/public/`) and `served/no-file-keys` (no Figma file URL in the note, `tools/list` or any resource). `lint-voice.ts` and `lint-us-english.ts` scan the note as served: `mcp-served.ts` gains `servedBridgeInstructions`, which spawns the bridge on a free port with a throwaway secret file and reads `initialize`. A reply without the note, or a note that does not name `figma_status`, makes both gates blind.

**Mutations, each failing by name.** The note padded to 1,201 → `instructions/length`. The `Original · …` line dropped → `instructions/rules`. `readFirst` cut short → `instructions/same`. `llms.txt` pointed at a missing path → `resources/resolve`. `llms.txt` pointed at `CLAUDE.md` → `resources/public-only`. A file URL appended to the note → `served/no-file-keys`. "Simply" in the note → `lint-voice.ts`; "colour" → `lint-us-english.ts`; `instructions` dropped from `initialize` → both prose gates blind, by name ("the figma-bridge connect note — the initialize reply carried no instructions").

## (2026-11-02) — At the narrow tier the Inspect menu stays inside the window (#3298)

**Status:** studio chrome fix (`apps/studio/src/chrome.css`), shared by both hosts, built as the owner decided
(Q3298.1 A), and a new `test:chrome` section, `3298` (shard 3). ENGINE patch (change note): no committed artifact,
emission or component surface moves.

### The defect

`.p3-menu` is `min-width: max-content` and hangs from the right edge of its button (`right: 0` in `.p3-popwrap`), so its
longest unwrapped line sets its width. In the Inspect menu that is the privacy note (#3138), 529px wide. At 380 the
menu's left edge sat at −161 on both hosts, and the page does not scroll sideways, so the clipped part could not be
reached.

### The fix

Three rules under `.p3-frame[data-w="narrow"]`, nothing at the wide tiers. The preview header becomes the menu's
containing block (`position: relative` on it, `position: static` on Inspect's wrap). The menu keeps `top: auto`, its
static position at the top of Inspect's wrap, and drops by the narrow button's height plus the usual gap
(`--p3-ctl-h-xs` + `--p3-space-050`), so it hangs where it did. It sits `--p3-space-150` from the header's right edge,
which is the header's padding at this tier, so Inspect's right edge. It is capped at the header's width less
`--p3-space-150` a side, with `min-width: 0`, so the note and the stamp wrap. All lengths are chrome tokens: the RAW
scan in `chrome/tokens.mjs` refuses `100vw`, which is why the cap is the header's width and not the window's.

Measured at 380, both hosts: the menu is 296px wide, from 72 to 368, its top unchanged (4px under Inspect). At 1280 the
menu, Inspect, the note and the stamp have the same rects as on `main`, and the screenshots are byte-identical on both
hosts.

### The arm

Section `3298`, both hosts, Brand, light chrome, at 380 (the Preview pane) and 1280, Inspect open. EXPECTED is the
window (`innerWidth`) and Inspect's own rect; ACTUAL is `getBoundingClientRect()` of the open menu, the privacy note and
the build stamp. Three arms per case: the menu inside `[0, innerWidth]`; the note and the stamp inside the menu; the
menu's right edge on Inspect's and its top below Inspect.

Mutation, failing by name: the fix reverted → `3298 web 380: the open Inspect menu stays inside the window, [0, 380]
({"l":-160.8,…})` and `3298 figma 380: …` the same. 1280 passes either way.

At 380 a fourth arm holds the decision's cap from both sides: the menu inside the preview header less 12px a side (12
typed in the test). The window alone passed a menu reaching the header's left edge. Mutation, failing by name: a cap
on the right only (`max-width: calc(100% - var(--p3-space-150))`) → `3298 web 380: the menu is capped at the preview
header less 12px a side` (menu `l 60`, header `l 60`) and `3298 figma 380: …` the same.

### Composing with #3294 (owner decision Q3298/3294 compose, A, 2026-11-02)

#3294 (now on `main`) gave `.p3-menu-privacy` `width: 0; min-width: 100%` at every tier, and the Inspect menu a ~320px
width at the wide tier (O2 B, already `:not([data-w="narrow"])`). At 380 the first rule let the items set the menu's
width: 164px on the web, with the note 14 lines tall. The owner decided the minimum is the wide tier's alone and the
narrow cap decides at 380, so `width: 0; min-width: 100%` now sits under `.p3-frame:not([data-w="narrow"])`, the same
scope as O2 B's rule. At 380 the note sets the menu's width up to the cap: 296px (72 to 368) on both hosts, the note 7
lines. 1280 keeps both of #3294's rules unchanged.

Two arms hold it. Section `3298` gains a fifth arm at 380: the menu reaches the cap's left edge (the header's left plus
12). Section `47-menu` gains a 380 case on both hosts: the menu inside the viewport, and at the cap with the note at
most 8 lines (8 is a test bound, not a design number: 7 at the cap, 14 without the scope). Mutation, from a `wip:`
commit, the scope dropped (`width: 0; min-width: 100%` back at every tier) → 38/40:
`✗ 3298 web 380: the privacy note sets the menu's width up to the cap, the preview header less 12px a side (menu
{"l":203.7,"r":368,…,"w":164.3}, …)` and `✗ §47 web light 380 Inspect: the open menu reaches the narrow cap … at most 8
lines (… "lines":14 …)`. The figma host lays out the same either way, because its build stamp already sets the menu to
the cap.

### Trap for whoever re-verifies

The margin that drops the menu below Inspect is the narrow button's height token. If Inspect's narrow height ever stops
being `--p3-ctl-h-xs`, the menu overlaps it or floats off it; the arm's "hangs below it" check catches the overlap only.

### Not covered

The arm holds only the Inspect menu. The Theme menu was measured once by hand at 380 (Brand, Preview pane) and fits on
both hosts: 50.5 to 304.5 on the web, 50.5 to 206.5 in the plugin.

## (2026-11-02) — Plugin window: Minimize parks the strip at the lower right, Restore centers the window (#3327)

The owner's decision on #3327: Restore brings the window back centered over the visible canvas, and Minimize parks the
strip at the canvas's lower right with a margin. The window is placed on the toggle only, so a window the user drags
stays where they put it until the next toggle.

### What landed

- `apps/plugin/src/window-place.ts`: `windowPlacement(toggle, bounds, zoom, size)`, a pure function. It returns the
  canvas position of the window's top-left. Every px length (the window's size and the 16 px `STRIP_MARGIN`) is divided by
  `zoom` before it is placed against `figma.viewport.bounds`, because `figma.ui.reposition` takes canvas coordinates.
  The top-left is held inside the bounds, so a window larger than the canvas keeps its top bar on screen.
- `main.ts`'s `setMinimized` calls it right after each `figma.ui.resize`, with the viewport as it is at that moment.
  A host with no viewport or no `reposition` (a test shim) is left where it is.

### The margin

16 px is chosen, not measured. A plugin cannot see Figma's bottom toolbar, so "clear of the toolbar" is a fixed right
and bottom margin, not an anchor. The toolbar sits at the bottom center, so the strip clears it only on a canvas wide
enough for both side by side. A real-Figma check is owed on the owner's machine: the headless tests hold the
arithmetic, not the look.

### The tests

`test-agent-link.ts`:
- `strip-place/*` holds `windowPlacement` for both toggles at zoom 1 and zoom 2, plus the clamp, against
  hand-worked literals.
- `strip/place-min` and `strip/place-restore` drive the toggles through `main.ts` at zoom 2 and assert the `reposition`
  arguments.
- `strip/place-drag` asserts that a drag places nothing.

Mutation, from a `wip:` commit: drop the `/ zoom` on the window's size. `strip-place/min-z2`, `strip-place/restore-z2`,
`strip/place-min` and `strip/place-restore` fail, by name.

Two public guides cite `main.ts` by line, and the new lines moved four of those citations, so they move here too
(`lint-guide-claims.ts`).

## (2026-11-02) — Update file's run goes on past sets built with problems (#3308, fix 2)

**The defect.** The owner's first run stopped at To add: "Stopped at To add · Built 9 sets · 5 with problems", "1 failed", and the style guides never drawn. Reproduced in the component shim under `fixHostMethods`, driving the plugin's real `main.ts` with the panel's posts: every one of the nine sets completed. Five (Button, Checkbox.Row, Checkbox.Group, Link, Badge) were "built with problems" for one reason each: "No usage panels drawn: this file has no _Doc-block component" (Set up file, the run's first step, cannot build `_Doc-block` until Badge, Tag, List item and Divider exist). Nothing failed. The run stopped because the sets step's verdict was the queue's `runVerdict`, whose `ok` is false for any set with problems, and `stepDone` ends the run on any step that is not ok. And Activity counted it a failure because the queue's headline had no "⚠" (D-RED A reads a warning by that mark).

**The fix.** A step result can be `warn`: not ok, but it did all it was asked. `stepDone` (`state/update-file.ts`) goes on past one. `main.ts`'s sets step marks itself `warn` when every queued set has a result and none failed (one set: `completed`). A failure or a stop still ends the run. `stripVerdict` (`state/status-strip.ts`) does not take a `warn` step for where the run stopped; the finished line becomes a warning, "File updated", with the step's own words after the steps. `runVerdict` (`state/build-queue.ts`) marks "Built n sets · k with problems" with "⚠" when nothing failed and nothing was left, as a single set's own "with problems" headline is, so Activity counts a warning.

**What this does not do.** Why each set had problems is #3308's other half (the reasons, a DRAFT Q-block), and the `_Doc-block` sequencing and the cover not drawn on a first run are held for the owner there. The theme step's own "⚠ n misses" still stops a run, unchanged.

**Tests, each failing by name on current main.** `run/warn goes on` (`test-update-file.ts`), `verdict/warn` (`test-status-strip.ts`, a literal line), the "with problems" headline marked a warning (`test-component-groups.ts`), and the chrome arm `#3308: a queue that built every set with problems goes on to the style guides, and Activity reads it as a warning` (section 10: a fresh file, Set up file then two queued sets each built with problems; Update file is still running, and the drawer's row kind is `warn`).

**The review's two blocking points (CHANGES at 7ebdc387).** The reproduction is now committed, under the strict host: `apps/plugin/test-update-owner-run.ts` drives the real `main.ts` on a fresh file with the owner's ticks (the Buttons family, Checkbox group, Checkbox row, Icon, Link, Badge: nine sets in Update file's order). Each set's answer, clean or with problems, and the `_Doc-block` reason are held against literals, as is Checkbox.Row's second build (six members ALREADY PRESENT, #3308 item 3). The answers go through the panel's `runVerdict` and `stepDone`: "⚠ Built 9 sets · 5 with problems", and the run reaches the style guides. On main's code it fails `run/verdict` and `run/goes on`. The suite adds what a fresh file has as properties the host lacks, and the shim's own `liveRoot` search now reads every page (`pages`, `component-shim.ts`), so a nesting set gets a component that makes instances. `test-update-fresh.ts`'s patched search can't do that (#3325). And "a failed set still ends the run" is held for a queue: a chrome arm in section 10 posts a set with problems, then a failed one (the last, so every set has a result). Update file is then free, the strip reads "Stopped at To add", and the row reads a failure. The review's R1 (`results.every(...)` → `true` in `main.ts`'s sets step) fails that arm at every width and theme.

**Mutations, each failing by name.** `stepDone` ignoring `warn` → `run/warn goes on`. `stripVerdict` counting a `warn` step as failed → `verdict/warn`. The "⚠" dropped from `runVerdict` → the component-groups arm. `main.ts`'s sets step passing `warn` false → the chrome arm, at every width and theme.

## (2026-11-02) — Release prep for the org-private "Prism3 Studio": a strict release build, the approved privacy note, a release record (#3147)

**What landed, by decision.** The owner's release decisions on #3147 (Q3147.15 to Q3147.21, all A), with nothing published:
- **Q3147.16, a strict release build.** `releaseCheck` in `apps/plugin/git-stamp.mjs` refuses a release when the stamp's commit is `-dirty` or `git-unavailable`, when the checkout is behind `origin/main`, or when it cannot tell (no fetch, no count). `build.mjs --release` runs it before anything is written, so a refused release leaves no bundle to import by mistake. The dev build keeps #3239's warning.
- **Q3147.17, the privacy note.** `PRIVACY_NETWORK` is the approved Q3147.7 wording, character for character. The manifest `reasoning` is untouched.
- **Q3147.18, the release record.** `tools/release/prepare.ts --figma-version <N>` checks the checkout and both builds (each bundle's stamp must name this commit). It writes the two zips and a draft release note under the git-ignored `tools/release/out/`, and prints the `git tag`, `git push` and `gh release create --draft` commands. It runs none of them.
- **Q3147.15 and .19 to .21** are documented in `apps/plugin/README.md`'s new release section: keep the id, publish on demand at most once a day after verify, publish Offline too, and publish without `ws://localhost` if Figma refuses it, recording that on #3147.

**Why strict only outside CI.** `verify.ts` sets `CI=1` for every gate and GitHub Actions sets `CI`. In both, the release build is a gate that is never published, and a branch that falls behind `main` while a 40-minute run goes would turn it red for nothing: `main` moved twice during this lane's own verify. So under `CI` the same reasons print as a warning and the build goes on. The owner's hand-run `build:release`, the one the publish steps use, has no `CI` and is always strict. `release/ci-warns` tests that boundary.

**The note needed a layout fix.** The Inspect menu sizes to `max-content`, so the approved 260-character note on one line made the menu 1534 px wide at a 1280 px viewport (measured in Chromium against the real `chrome.css`; the old note gave 529 px). `.p3-menu-privacy` now takes `width: 0; min-width: 100%`, so it wraps within the width the menu's items give it and never sets that width, whatever its wording. On web that left the menu 164 px wide and the note about 14 lines, so the owner chose O2 B: in the wide tier the open Inspect menu is at least 320 px wide (`calc(var(--p3-dlg-unit) * 2.5)`, the start window's width unit), and the note wraps to 6 lines on web at 1280. The figma menu's items already make it wider than 320 px. The narrow tier is left as it was, for #3298.

**Gates.** `test-git-stamp.ts` section 5 drives `releaseCheck` with stubbed answers: `release/clean`, `release/refuses-dirty`, `release/refuses-no-git`, `release/refuses-behind`, `release/refuses-unknown`, `release/every-reason`, `release/ci-warns`. `release/build-refuses` then runs the real `build.mjs --release` with a stand-in `git` (a shell script answering from literals) first on `PATH` and `CI` unset. It must exit 1 with the refusal and leave `release/main.js` untouched. `lint-network-reach.ts` now holds each build's bundle to its own note, against the approved text typed in the gate.

## (2026-11-02) — A multi-set build runs each set after the queued sets it nests, so none is built twice (#3308, fix 1)

**The defect.** The owner's first run (a fresh file, the Prism3 example brand, Buttons, Checkbox group, Icon, Link and Badge ticked, Update file) built Checkbox.Row twice: once as Checkbox group's dependency (`build-deps.ts`, #1633), then again from the queue, where its six members read "ALREADY PRESENT (skipped; this set has been written before)". Icon went the same way behind Button, quietly ("✓ already built"). Reproduced in the component shim under `fixHostMethods`: driving the plugin's real `main.ts` with the panel's posts, in the queue's order (the list's, review N1 on #2812), `checkbox-row`'s build answers `⚠ already built` with 6 skipped members and `icon`'s 46.

**The fix.** `depsFirst` (`apps/studio/src/state/build-queue.ts`) orders a run so each set comes after every queued set it nests, directly or through a set the queue does not hold, from the catalog's `nests`; otherwise the list's order stands, and a duplicate runs once. `startRun` takes the catalog and applies it; `runSets` in `main.ts` passes it, so Components' action bar and Update file's To add both get it. The plugin, the wire and the verdict copy are unchanged. In the shim, the owner's queue in this order builds every set once: no "ALREADY PRESENT" anywhere.

**Test.** `test-component-groups.ts`: `queue/deps-first` over the owner's nine sets (literal order: Icon first, Checkbox.Row before Checkbox group), through a set the queue does not hold (Checkbox (control) before Checkbox group), and the list's order kept with a duplicate dropped. It fails by name on current main, where `startRun` keeps the list's order.

**Mutation, failing by name.** `startRun` ignoring its catalog → all four `queue/deps-first` arms. `catalog` is required (review S1), so `runSets` dropping it (`startRun(kind, ok)`) → `typecheck-web`, at `main.ts`.

**Not this PR.** The other four "problems" in that run (each a missing usage-panel template) and why the run stopped are #3308's other fixes.

`run-progress` reading, then an agent's Update result with a reason, two console lines and a publish description,

15px and 12px values are literals typed in the test.

## (2026-11-02) — Brand marks: a paint baseline seeded from the owner's drop, so a retint of file and record fails (#3066)

`lint-mark-colors.ts` held each mark file to its `provenance.json` record, and both are typed in the same edit, so a
retint of the two together passed every gate (`social/spotify.svg` `#1ED760` → `#1ED761`). Owner decision Q3066.1 A:
an accept-only baseline seeded from the owner's own drop, commit `3675273d` (`incoming-marks/`), and no second copy of
the artwork.

### What landed

- `packages/engine/schema/mark-paints.json`: per mark file, its paints as `#RRGGBB` in painting order. 71 entries are
  as supplied and cite no decision (two carry `supplied`, the drop's `social/twitter*.svg`, renamed `x`). 15 cite the
  decision that moved them: the 11 `button/` marks (#3174 · Q3174.3 A, captured from the providers' SDKs, not in the
  drop), `provider/apple` and `provider/facebook` drawn black (#3134), `provider/facebook-blue` (Q831 A) and
  `social/facebook`'s blue (Q837 A).
- Arm (i) `PAINT BASELINE` in `lint-mark-colors.ts`: every `marks/**.svg`, read from the folder, and every document
  in `provider-logo-glyphs.ts` paints exactly its baseline list, and the folder and the baseline agree both ways.
- `--accept --decision <#issue | Qn X>` is the only writer, and stamps that ref on each entry it changes; regen never
  writes the file (docs/34 shape 6). `--seed-check` re-reads every undecided entry from the seed commit. It needs that
  commit (`git fetch origin refs/pull/3064/head`), so it is a local check, not a CI step, and says CANNOT DETERMINE
  without it.
- `lint-schema-classification.ts` lists the file in class 3 (pure data, no prose), beside `component-axes.json`.

### The trap

The gate's old reader (`colorsOf`, hex `fill` on `<path>` and `stop-color`, in document order) reads the drop wrong:
the drop paints with keywords, short hex, `<rect>` and `<use>`, puts gradients after the paths, and carries Figma clip
rects filled `white`. Read with it, 30 files "differ" from the drop. `paintsOf` is written for both spellings: clip
paths and masks paint nothing, a gradient's stops count where a shape uses it, keywords and short hex read as
`#RRGGBB`, and any paint it cannot read throws rather than reads as fewer colors. Read that way, every undecided file
equals the drop exactly.

### The mutation

From a `wip:` commit: `social/spotify.svg` `#1ED760` → `#1ED761` and the same change in its record's `colors`, then
`emit-marks.ts`. Arms (a), (b) and (c) stay quiet, and the gate fails by name: `social/spotify.svg: PAINT BASELINE`
and `social/spotify: PAINT BASELINE` (the emitted document).

## (2026-11-02) — The agent link's status holds still when two files share one bridge (#3297)

The owner saw the status under the Agent switch flip between "Listening · bridge" and "Listening · mailbox" every 2 s, with Prism3's link on in two files on one Mac.

**The diagnosis.** The issue guessed a refused second instance. The real cause was a loop between the two instances. The bridge server never lets an *unpaired* connection replace the plugin (#3204). A *paired* one does replace it, on purpose: a relay reconnecting after its socket died without a close must win over the dead socket (#2497). Both files were paired, so each retry from one evicted the other, and the evicted one retried 2 s later. The reproduction in `test-agent-bridge.ts` counted 26 status posts and 24 evictions in 2.5 s, in both relays.

**The fix keeps newer-replaces-older and adds a polite retry.** The server closes the replaced connection with a new code, `CLOSE.held` (4409), in place of 1000. The relay that gets it knows another instance holds the bridge. Until it is welcomed again, its hello carries `yield: true`. The server refuses a yielding hello with 4409 while a plugin is attached, and welcomes it when none is. Its proof is checked first, and a wrong proof is still 4401, so pairing does not change. The holder's own reconnects send no `yield`, so #2497 still works. While held, retries back off from 2 s to 30 s. The file that connected last keeps the bridge, and the other one moves to the mailbox once and stays there.

**The word moves only on a settled change.** The relay now keeps what it reported to the main thread separate from the live socket. A drop keeps `connected: true` for `holdMs` (5 s) and reports the loss only if no retry has been welcomed by then. A settled loss is reported at once: the link switched off, 4409, or a pairing refusal. Commands still depend on the live socket.

**New copy, DRAFT.** The waiting file's full line adds "The desktop bridge is connected to Prism3 in another file." The short word stays "Listening · mailbox". The PR's Owner Q-block asks about this.

**A second defect, found while writing the refused arm.** The relay's `onerror` closed the socket before its `ws !== sock` guard took effect. Node's WebSocket fires `error` again inside `close()` on a socket still connecting, so a refused socket recursed until the stack overflowed. It now marks the socket lost first. Browsers queue that event, so the panel probably never hit this, but the arm needs it.

**Mutations, each failing by name:** with no `yield` in the hello, `held/one-repaint`, `held/holder-steady`, `held/no-evict` and four more fail. With no hold, `flaky/held-word` and `real-change` fail. With the server ignoring `yield`, `held/server: a yielding hello is closed with 4409…` and the arms after it fail. With flat retries, `held/backoff` fails. Without the held note, `link/held-line` fails in `test-agent-link.ts`.

## (2026-11-02) — sets built over the Figma MCP are interactive: the paste path writes the plugin's prototype reactions (#2564)

**STATUS: PR open, not merged.** Plugin only. **No engine change, no `out/**` change, no ENGINE or CONTRACT bump.** `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 46 → 47 (`lint-executor-revision` requires it, since the reaction loop moved out of `write-components.ts`; #3274 took 46). `executor-reach.json` names no set for 47, measured by `lint-executor-reach`: 60 sets × 8 arms, 0 redrawn. Files: `apps/plugin/src/reactions.ts` (`writeSetReactions`, the loop lifted unchanged), `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts` (calls it), `apps/plugin/src/mcp-steps.ts` (a new step, `runComponentReactions`, and the `packNames`/`unpackNames` codec), `apps/plugin/mcp-paste.ts` (one `component-reactions` script after each in-scope set's last chunk), `tools/figma-mcp/plan.ts` (its result shape), `apps/plugin/test-paste-reactions.ts` (**NEW**, an arm of the plugin `test` step), `apps/plugin/README.md`, `executor-revision.ts`, `executor-reach.json`.

**The owner's call (Q238 A applied to paste, approved 2026-11-01).** A set pasted through `use_figma` gets the same reactions a plugin build gets: Rest → Hover while hovering, Rest and Hover → Pressed while pressing (or the def's `pressState`, #2428). They are unrecorded on a paste build, like everything else there, since that path writes no member stamp.

**Why no engine move was needed.** The issue's comment planned to move `reactionMap` into the engine so the engine's chunk payload could write reactions. Since #1553, though, the MCP path runs the plugin's own bundled runtime (`mcp-steps.ts`), which imports `reactions.ts` directly. So the plugin's loop became one function, `writeSetReactions`, and both paths call it: the executor after every other write, the paste runtime in its own step after a set's last chunk.

**When it runs, and what it needs.** A reaction names its destination by node id, so it can only be written once every sibling exists: after the last chunk's combine. It is a script of its own (`component-reactions`) right after that chunk, and only for a set in scope (21 defs). The plan's member names travel in it. Plain JSON was too big: the button family's 576 names are 68KB against a 45,000-character script. They are regular (`axis=value, …`, same axes, same order), so `packNames` sends one index per axis into each axis's value list: 9.5KB, lossless, and it refuses a list of any other shape.

**Trap: the first cut put the step inside `runComponentChunk`, and `test-mcp-paste.ts`'s size arm caught it.** Every chunk script grew by the reaction code's share of the bundle, and button's chunks went from a handful to 576 one-member scripts, still over budget. Each runtime step is bundled on its own and tree-shaken, so a separate step keeps every chunk script byte-identical to before. The cost is one more `use_figma` call per interactive set.

**Independent review, and what it changed.** (1) The step found its set among the page's top-level nodes, while the chunk payload searches the whole page (`findOne`). A set a designer had moved into a frame got members but no reactions. It uses `findOne` now. (2) A re-paste overwrote reactions a designer had edited. The paste keeps no record, so it can't tell an edit from a stale reaction. The conservative option is built: a member that already has reactions is left alone, the same rule the chunks apply to members already in the set. The alternative (overwrite) is an owner question on the PR. (3) A planned member the set doesn't hold was skipped silently. It is a miss now.

**The test.** `test-paste-reactions.ts` builds `tag` (squeezed into many chunks) and `code-input-cell` (press goes to `focus-visible`) twice into the component shim. One build is `applyComponentPlan`; the other is the engine's chunk payloads run through `runComponentChunk`, then `runComponentReactions` with the data parsed from the script `mcp-paste.ts` generates. Expected side, literal: 27 reactions on 18 of 45 members, 12 on 8 of 28 (the numbers `test-reactions.ts` pins), plus named reactions for named members, spelled out. Mutations, each from a `wip:` commit, each failing by name: the write removed from `runComponentReactions` → `paste path: tag … carries 27 reactions … (got 45/0/0)` and three more; the generator emits no reactions script → those four plus `… reactions script comes after its last chunk script`; the script emitted before the chunks → `… reactions script comes after its last chunk script`. The review fixes, the same way: a top-level lookup in place of `findOne` → `a set inside a frame gets its reactions`; the keep-existing rule dropped → `a re-run leaves a designer's edited reactions as they are`; the absent-member misses dropped → `a planned member the set does not hold is reported`. On the first cut (the step inside every chunk), reactions written before the last chunk read `(63 misses — … NOT WRITTEN …)`, which is why the ordering arm exists.

**Trap.** The component shim's `getNodeByIdAsync` answers components only, with no parent, so `readReactions` reads every destination as dangling. The test host answers from the page tree, parents included, as the live host does.

## (2026-11-02) — The preview's mode control keeps focus when it switches between its radios and its select (#3013)

**Status:** studio fix (`apps/studio/src/shell/preview.ts`), shared by both hosts, and a new `test:chrome` section,
`3013` (shard 3). ENGINE patch (change note): no committed artifact, emission or component surface moves.

### The defect

The preview header's mode control shows its radios when they fit and a select otherwise (#2383). `fit()` hides the
one that gives way with `display: none`, and Chromium drops focus from a hidden control to the body. A keyboard user on
a mode radio who narrowed the plugin window lost their place (WCAG 2.4.3), and so did someone on the select when the
window widened. #3005 fixed the test probe that tripped on the same race. This is the product side.

### The fix

`fit()` notes whether focus was inside the control when it began. If it was, and the control now shown does not hold
it, focus moves to the shown control: the checked radio (the roving `tabIndex` 0), or the select. Focus that was
elsewhere is never pulled in. The issue left where focus goes to the owner. The batch of 2026-11-02 decided it: focus
stays on the control, as the issue proposed.

### The arm

Section `3013`, both hosts, Depth & motion, light chrome. The checked radio is focused at 1600 px, then the window
narrows 100 px at a time until the select shows (1300 px on both hosts). Focus must be on the select. Widened back to
1600, it must be on the checked radio. The control: Inspect focused through the same switch both ways stays focused.
The widths are found by narrowing, never read from the code.

Mutations, each failing by name:
- The focus move dropped → `3013 <host>: narrowing to 1300 px … focus moves from the checked radio to the select …
  ({"active":"BODY"})` and the widening arm, on both hosts. That is #3013's own reproduction.
- The `had` test dropped → `3013 <host>: … focus on Inspect stays there …`, since focus was pulled into the select.

## (2026-11-02) — A usage-panel example keeps its width once its panel is on the page (#3205 follow-up)

**What was wrong.** #3211 fixed each specimen at its member's width and set that width as its `minWidth`. The test host
honored that. In the template, after an Update with a build that included #3211, Dialog's specimen read
`layoutSizingHorizontal: FIXED` at **62px** inside a 687px stage. The width and the floor were both gone, and the
instance was frozen at the width it hugs (#3265's re-scan). Toast, Select, Textarea and the fields didn't change either.

**The host behavior modeled (`apps/plugin/test-doc-panel.ts`, `hostReset`).** When a tree is appended or moved to a new
parent, each instance inside another instance in it, such as a block's specimen, loses its size overrides. Its floor
goes back to its main's, and it is frozen FIXED at what it hugs, which is the state the scan read. `drawDocPanel`
sizes every specimen while the panel is still off the page, then moves the panel there (`parent.appendChild(panel)`).
So under this model every size it set is lost. With the model in, current main fails 24 arms, including
`collapse/dialog` ("example 1 is 40px wide, under the 560 its def declares"), `collapse/after reset` and
`update/redraw in place`. The #3211 arms run on this file's own host, not on `component-shim.ts`, so the model lives
here. **This trigger is inferred from one observation, not measured.** It is the first one consistent with what the
scan saw, and the plugin's last structural move before the markers.

**The fix (`apps/plugin/src/doc-panel.ts`).** The draw records each specimen with its member and sizes it again right
after the panel lands on the page: fixed at the member's width, with its floor. That happens before the markers, which
are placed from the specimens' final boxes. `PANEL_FORMAT` goes to 6, so Update redraws every usage panel once,
including the ones #3211 drew collapsed.

**Mutations,** each committed `wip:` first:
- the second sizing removed → the 24 arms above fail by name;
- `PANEL_FORMAT` left at 5 → `update/redraw in place` fails (the #3211-era panel isn't due).

**Owed.** Real-Figma confirmation: after an Update, read Dialog's specimen in the template and check that it is FIXED at
560 with `minWidth` 560. If it is still 62, the reset has another trigger (a later property write or a mode pin, say),
and the model and this fix move with it. Also note: with every panel due once, a panel whose print predates #3303 and
whose nested components changed is kept as "(edited)" by that PR's safe rule, so #3303 should land first.

## (2026-11-02) — The chrome suite can no longer hang silently: a section watchdog, bounded Shape key presses, a step limit (#3044)

**Status:** test and CI change only (`apps/studio/test-chrome.mjs`, `chrome-shards.mjs`, `ci.yml`, `lint-doc-gates.ts`).
No engine change note: no engine, studio or plugin code moves, so no bump is owed (CONTRIBUTING §2). `EXECUTOR_REVISION`
stays.

### What happened

On #3040's CI the chrome suite printed `Shape (S7)` and then nothing for 74 minutes, with no assertion failed, until
the run was cancelled. A re-run of the same commit passed. The step had no `timeout-minutes`, so it would have held the
job for GitHub's six hours, and the log could not be read while it ran.

### What can wait without a bound

`bounded` (#2550) holds the inputs it wraps, and test-chrome.mjs wrapped one (S6.3's `selectOption`). Section 24
(Shape, S7) sends five raw `page.keyboard.press` calls, and `test-bounded.mjs`'s header names exactly that: "a key
press has no bound at all". The run that hung cannot be replayed, so which call stalled is not proven. A raw key press
fits, but so does a `page.evaluate` waiting on a frame that never comes. So the fix bounds what is known to be
unbounded and adds a backstop for the rest.

### The fix

- **A section watchdog.** `enter()` arms a timer at every section guard. A section that reaches no further guard
  within 600 s fails by name with the last check it reached, `✗ section <id>: no progress for 600s, so the run stops
  here (#3044); the last check it reached: "…"`, and the run exits 1. 600 s is 2.8x the slowest healthy section
  measured locally (18-s4f, 217 s). `CHROME_SECTION_LIMIT_S` overrides it.
- **Its self-check, section 3044 (shard 3).** The suite runs itself with `--stall-self-check`: one section, entered
  through the real `runs` and `enter`, awaits a promise that never settles, under a 1 s limit. The arm requires
  exit 1 and the named line, within 30 s. The timer is not `unref`'d. In the self-check nothing else holds the event
  loop, and an unref'd timer would let Node exit 13 without the named failure.
- **S7's key presses bounded.** The Edits and reveal cases call `watchStalls` and send their five presses through
  `bounded`, so a press the renderer never takes fails by name and says where the page was. Their catches skip an
  error `bounded` already reported.
- **A step limit.** `ci.yml`'s chrome step gets `timeout-minutes: 30`. 120 healthy shard runs on main and PRs peak
  at 651 s, and 30 minutes is 2.8x that. `lint-doc-gates.ts` arm 9 holds it: `STEP_TIME_LIMITS` is a typed register
  of the steps that must carry a limit, read from the parsed tree, with a self-check that a dropped, zero or renamed
  limit is named.

### Mutations, each failing by name

- The watchdog's `setTimeout` dropped from `enter` → `✗ 3044: a section that never returns fails by name …` (exit 13).
- Its `process.exit(1)` dropped → the same arm.
- `watchStalls` dropped from S7's Edits case → `✗ S7 Shape edits: ArrowRight on radius softness, in Light: the page was
  never given watchStalls …`, one per press.
- `timeout-minutes` dropped from the chrome step (`main`'s `ci.yml`) → `❌ 1 step(s) that can hang have no time limit
  (#3044): "New shell chrome suite (UI redesign S1.2)" (\`chrome\`) has no \`timeout-minutes\` …`.

### What it does not prove

What stalled on #3040's run. If it recurs, the log now ends on the section and the last check instead of running on.

## (2026-11-02) — Plugin open paces its projections and member reads on a full library (#3301)

The owner opened the plugin on the Prism3 template with a dev build: the panel hung while it read the file, and the
status strip's progress started only after a while. #3110 and #3170 had paged the read after open, but their stand-in
held 50 sets of one member each, no usage panels and no style guides.

### Where the time went

Measured on a new stand-in shaped like the template (`test-open-large-file.ts`, the template section): every def with
Figma properties (60 sets, 4,391 members built from their own plans, each stamped and recorded), a usage panel beside
each set, 8 style-guide pages of 1,500 nodes, 67 pages, and a ledger naming every set under an older engine, as a dev
build finds it. Every node is a `Proxy` that counts host calls, and the test's clock moves 10 µs per call. On `main`:

- **The strip spoke late.** The read's page 0 ("Reading this file…") was posted when the page read began, after the
  ledger answer had projected every engine-moved set.
- **One projection was one turn.** Button's 576 members took about 0.24 s to project and print in Node, in one turn, and
  the print hashed its accumulated strings at the end for about 0.2 s more.
- **The hand-edit pass projected every set's plans** only to read the set's name, which is its def's id.
- **24 members per hand-back.** `readSetView` handed back every 24 members, whatever their size: a field's 24 members are
  thousands of host reads. `readSingleView` read every component's parent in one turn, and every lookup over the read
  (`rootOver`) read every node's type again. Worst turn: 30,789 host calls (about 0.3 s at 10 µs a call).

### The fix

- `ui-ready`'s own turn posts the strip's page 0, before any projection or page load; the read posts pages from 1.
- The engine's `figmaAnatomySet` is now `figmaAnatomyMembers` (a generator, a member at a time) drained, then
  `checkAnatomySet`; and `printOf` is `printSteps` drained, with every hash fed as it goes (`fnvStream`). The plugin's
  print at open drives both a plan at a time and hands back once about `PACE_MS` has run (`pace.ts`, which now holds
  `PACE_MS` and a `pacer`). Every print is unchanged: compared with `main`'s for all 60 defs under 4 brands.
- The hand-edit pass's target carries no plans for a set (`passTarget`): `locateSets` finds it by `t.def`. A
  single-component def's plans are still projected, paced.
- `readSetView` and `readSingleView` also hand back once about `PACE_MS` has run, and the read keeps each node's type and
  name from its page's turn, so `rootOver` and `presentNames` read no node.
- `ledgerNow` keeps each def's entry per read, worked out ahead of `needsPrint` and `dueOf` with the same pacing.

After: worst turn 5,443 host calls; longest event-loop stall on the template stand-in 209 → 72 ms, on the 60-page
stand-in 523 → 86 ms (wall clock, measured, not asserted). The remaining two are the brand's materializer, built once,
and the end of the page read.

### Gates

`open/strip-first`, `open/member-paced`, `open/print-paced`, `open/pass-light` and `open/hand-edits`. On `main` the first
four fail. Mutations, each failing by name: the early page 0 dropped → `open/strip-first`; `readSetView`'s `PACE_MS`
hand-back, `readSingleView`'s, or `rootOver`'s kept types → `open/member-paced`; the projection's tick → `open/print-paced`;
the pass's target from `updateTargets` again → `open/pass-light`. Not asserted, measured only: `ledgerNow`'s pacing and the
streamed print hashes, which make no host call and showed only as wall-clock stalls.

### Not done

A page's own search is Figma's and cannot be split, so a page holding thousands of components is still one turn. Pure
JavaScript in Figma's plugin sandbox may run slower than in Node; the shim cannot say by how much, so the fix paces by
the clock rather than by a count. Engine patch (change note): no committed artifact moves. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` as
`lint-executor-revision.ts` requires.

## (2026-11-02) — Both executors' suites read back that no literal was written over a bound corner (#3048)

**Status:** test infrastructure only: `apps/plugin/component-shim.ts`, the paste stub and a new arm in
`packages/engine/test.ts`, a new arm in `apps/plugin/test-write-components.ts`, and the theme simulation in
`apps/plugin/test-update-components.ts`. No executor code moves, so
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` is unchanged. ENGINE unchanged (no change note: nothing emitted or projected moves). CONTRACT unchanged.

### What changed

- **The gap.** Both `claimDefaults` passes run after the bindings and zero every corner the plan leaves unbound. The
  only thing keeping them off a bound corner is a guard: `!(corner in bound)` in the plugin executor and `!(k in B)` in
  the paste payload. On the host a literal write after `setBoundVariable` detaches the variable, which is the rule #1228
  relies on for the stroke weight. Neither stub modelled it for corners (both kept the binding through the write), so
  removing either guard left every suite green while 35 defs would ship their radii unbound at 0.
- **The stubs model the host.** The #1388 per-corner setter in both the plugin shim and the paste stub now drops that
  corner's `boundVariables` entry on a literal write, as #2695 did for the stroke weight. `setBoundVariable` writes
  `boundVariables` only, so a binding survives until something writes a literal over it. The first attempt put the
  setter in its own block. #1388's later `defineProperty` silently replaced it, and the guard mutation passed. Probing
  the node directly found it, and the detach now lives in #1388's setter itself.
- **Read-back arms, one per executor.** Each walks every def whose plans bind a corner (discovered from the plans) and
  compares `node:corner=variable` from the plan's `bound` with the built node's `boundVariables`, roots keyed `<root>` on
  both sides. The plugin arm builds every member: 35 defs, 15620/15620 bindings held. The paste arm pastes the first
  binding member of each def. Each has a floor typed from #3048's list (`text-field`, `select`, `badge`,
  `provider-logo`), and the paste arm also fails on a paste that threw, so a harness gap can't pass as held or read as
  lost.
- **A harness trap, recorded.** The first paste run lost `card-number-field`'s four control corners. The payload had
  thrown (`getMainComponentAsync is not a function`) because its slot's swap target, a provider logo, was not in the
  stub's components. With swap targets passed, it pastes clean and holds.

- **One suite simulated the host the old way.** `test-update-components.ts`'s theme section imitates Apply Theme by
  writing a literal number into every bound field. For a corner that is now a hand edit that detaches the binding, as
  it would be on the host, so 45 members read as hand-edited. That section now moves a bound corner's variable value,
  which is what Apply Theme does. Its premise still moves 810 bound values.

### Verification

- `test-write-components.ts` exit 0; `test.ts` 635629 passed, 0 failed.
- **Plugin guard removed** (`else set(corner, 0)`): `#3048 every corner a plan binds is still bound …` fails by name,
  15620 lost, along with the executor's own `DISCARDED` read-back misses and the #1015 and #2343 radius arms that read
  the same nodes.
- **Paste guard removed** (`else set(k,0)`): `#3048 paste: every corner a plan binds is still bound …` fails by name,
  160 lost, along with #2343's paste tile arm, the two #1388 ring arms and the #1393 lockstep arm. On `main` the same
  mutation gave 0 failures (the issue's measurement).

## (2026-11-02) — Update redraws a usage panel nobody touched in place, the components it nests rebuilt (#3303)

**What was wrong.** A print was already recorded at draw time (`docPanelPrint`, the second form, #2927). Update did
not compare a panel against what the new engine would draw: it compared the panel against that recorded print. But the
print read every layer inside the panel's instances, including the `_Doc-block` blocks, the List.Item rows, the Badge
chips and the markers. Each of those layers takes its fills, padding, fonts, names, structure and default text from its
**main component**, and Update rebuilds those components. So once one of them changed, an untouched panel printed
differently, and Update kept it as "… (edited)" below a fresh panel. That is the 23 sets in the template on 2026-11-02.
The test hosts didn't catch it because their instances were copies, and nothing inherited from a main.

**The fix (`apps/plugin/src/doc-panel.ts`).** The print has a third form. Every frame and text that belongs to the panel
itself is read as before (`printView`). An instance is read only through what it sets itself, Figma's
`InstanceNode.overrides`: each layer that overrides something, flat and in order, with the names of the fields it
overrides and only those fields' values. Prism3's draw writes text, properties, visibility and sizing, and those are
overrides, so they are stable. A designer's later change is an override too, so it moves the print. Inherited values,
a layer the main adds or drops, and a property left at its default stay out. Size and placement fields stay out, as
`printView` leaves them out of a frame. A Specimen swap reads by type only, since its value is a member's id, which is
the set's. A host that reports no `overrides` on an instance has it read whole, which is the safe direction.
`printMatches` compares a print in the form it was recorded in, and spec panels use it too (`spec-panel.ts`).

**The safe rule for panels drawn before this change** (second-form prints). A panel is compared in its own form. It is
replaced while it still matches, and kept, as before, once a component it nests changes. The second form can't tell a
rebuild from a hand edit, so this rule never draws over a designer's change. It costs one more round of "(edited)"
copies for any such panel whose nested components change before its next redraw. After that redraw, a panel carries
the third form. A looser rule, read by text and by overrides the way #2968 reads first-form prints, would remove that
round. It is lossy, though, for edits to the panel's own frames, so it's left to the owner (flagged on #3303).

**Tests (`apps/plugin/test-doc-panel.ts`, `own draw/…`).** The suite's host now models instances as Figma does, for
these arms. Each layer of a block holds an inherited value and an override, writes are overrides, and `overrides` lists
them. `mainMoves` changes the inherited values (fills, padding, radius, font size, template text), adds a layer to each
block's main and repoints the swap. Tag is built by the executor, its panel is drawn, then engine N+1 makes it due and
rebuilds what it nests. One Update, run as `main.ts` runs it on a host and root whose methods are fixed
(`fixHostMethods`, #3295 not yet merged), gives:
- `untouched`: one panel, in place, with no "(edited)" copy;
- `text edit`, `fill edit`, `hidden layer`: kept aside;
- `v2 unchanged`: replaced;
- `v2 rebuilt`: kept, per the safe rule.

**Mutations,** each committed `wip:` first:
- the print read whole again (`printView` in `panelPrint`) → `own draw/untouched` fails with the template's symptom,
  "Tag usage (edited) | Tag usage";
- overrides ignored → `own draw/text edit`, `fill edit` and `hidden layer` fail;
- a second-form print read in the third form → `own draw/v2 unchanged` fails.

**Not done.** The template's 23 spurious copies are the owner's to clean up. Nothing in any Figma file was touched.
Real-host confirmation that `overrides` reports what this reads is owed: the agent link's `inspect` can read it on a
drawn panel.

## (2026-11-02) — Update file honors Usage panels off, and a test now holds it (#3017)

**Status:** plugin fix and a new `test-build-completed.ts` arm, `docs/panels off (update)`, with its control. ENGINE
patch (change note): no committed artifact, emission or component surface moves. The component executor is unchanged,
so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What the issue asked for, and what the test found

#3017 asked for a test that Update honors Documentation's Usage panels switch, because nothing held `updateTargets`'
`panels && leadsPanel(d.id)`. The arm, written beside the Build arm `docs/panels off`, removes Badge's panel and runs
the real `main.ts` Update (dry run, then apply) with the switch off. It **failed on `main`**: the dry run listed no
panel to draw, and the apply drew one anyway.

The cause is the apply's `furnish` hook. It redraws a set's furniture for every set the apply touches, and passed
`panelFor` to `furnishUpdate` whatever the switch said. `updateTargets`' gate only reached the dry run, through the
target's `doc`. So a file with panels off got a removed panel back on its next Update.

### The fix

`furnish` passes `panelFor` only for a target that `updateTargets` gave a `doc`. The switch is read once, and the
check and the apply both follow it.

### The arm and its mutations

- `docs/panels off (update)`: switch off, no panel listed and none drawn. `docs/panels on (update control)`: the
  same Update with the switch on lists the missing panel and draws it, so the off arm measures the switch.
- Mutation 1, the issue's: `updateTargets` without `panels &&` → `✗ docs/panels off (update) … (1 listed, 1 drawn)`.
- Mutation 2, this fix reverted (`furnish` always passes `panelFor`) → `✗ docs/panels off (update) … (0 listed, 1 drawn)`.

### Overlap

Open #3288 (#3137) has Update file offer the missing usage panels while panels are on, and Clean up remove them while
off. This builds on `main`. Whichever lands second rebases. That PR's census lists sets only while panels are on, so
the two agree on what the switch means.

## (2026-11-02) — The plugin test shim's host is strict by default; a shrink-only register holds the opt-outs (#3215 Q-C8 A)

`makeShim` in `apps/plugin/component-shim.ts` now fixes its host's methods and its root's methods by default: own data properties, neither writable nor configurable, as Figma defines `figma`'s. Before this, only the three arms #3214 opted in could see #3209's class of bug, a `Proxy` over the host that hands back a bound copy. Any new wrapper around the host, in any action, now fails in the plugin's own tests the way it fails in Figma. This is test-harness only: no plugin or engine behavior moves, so there is no change note.

### What changed

- **The default reads a fixture.** `apps/plugin/host-descriptors.json` records each host surface as `fixed` or `plain`, and where that came from. `figma` is `measured` (#3209's real-host error names `getLocalTextStylesAsync` as read-only and non-configurable). The root is `assumed` fixed, the stricter case #3214 already tested. Nodes are `unmeasured` and stay plain. The canary's descriptor read (`tools/figma-canary`) is the measurement that will settle the root and nodes.
- **The opt-out is named and registered.** A suite that patches a host method after building the shim passes `makeShim({ looseHost: '<reason>' })`. An empty reason throws. Each call site opts out alone, so the rest of the suite stays strict.
- **The register can only shrink.** `apps/plugin/loose-host-register.json` lists each opting-out suite with its reason. `test-loose-host.ts`, now in the plugin's `test` step, fails `register/unlisted` for an opt-out not in the register, `register/stale` for an entry nothing uses, and `register/shrink-only` for an entry that is not in the register at the merge base. The base is read from git history, not the tree, because a ceiling in the tree gets edited in the same commit as the entry it should refuse (`docs/34` shape 6). Until the register reaches main, the base is the seed measured below.

### The seed: 10 suites, not the proposal's 9

Each suite that imports the shim was run alone with the strict default and no opt-out, on main `fa3c934b`. Ten failed, each on a host method it reassigns after building the shim (or, in `test-run-read`, a `Proxy` over the root that substitutes its search):

- `test-build-completed`, `test-open-large-file`, `test-run-progress`, `test-update-fresh`: `root.findAllWithCriteria`;
- `test-native-slots`: `createComponentFromNode`;
- `test-roundtrip`, `test-slot-constraints`: `combineAsVariants`;
- `test-run-read`: a `Proxy` over the root substituting `findAllWithCriteria`;
- `test-update-apply`: `loadFontAsync` and `createNodeFromSvg`;
- `test-write-components`: `createNodeFromSvg`.

The proposal's grep counted 9 by a different measure and named a different set: `test-cover-frame`, `test-library-about` and `test-canvas-furniture` pass strict, since what they patch is a node or a copy rather than the shim's host; `test-open-large-file`, `test-roundtrip`, `test-run-progress` and `test-update-fresh` reassign the root's search or `combineAsVariants`, which the grep missed.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies this:** spreading a strict shim (`{ ...shim }`) makes plain properties again, so a suite that builds its host as a spread copy is loose without opting out. #3214's arms call `fixHostMethods` on their copies for that reason; a new arm that copies the host should too.

## (2026-11-02) — test.ts (21)(d): the generalize layout-alias arm matches rooted names and counts its rows (#3053)

**Status:** `packages/engine/test.ts` only. ENGINE unchanged (no change note: a test-only change owes no bump,
`packages/engine/changes/README.md`). CONTRACT unchanged.

### What changed

- **The defect.** Block (21) EMIT-FIGMA GENERALISE, arm (d), selected layout rows with
  `v.name === 'grid/gutter' || v.name === 'grid/margin'`. Since #1097 every emitted Figma variable name carries its
  brand's root (`ads/grid/gutter`, `wds/grid/gutter`), so the filter matched nothing, the bad list stayed empty, and
  the arm passed for any emission. It printed no row count, so nothing showed the empty selection (docs/34 shape 15).
- **The fix.** The arm matches `${theme.root}/grid/gutter` and `${theme.root}/grid/margin`, with the root read off the
  theme as arm (e) does. A literal root would be wrong here: aurora's root is `ads` and wendys' is `wds`, not the
  `prism` default the block header still names. It asserts the selected count equals `layout.length * 2` and prints it
  (12/12 aurora, 10/10 wendys). Since #3052 (Q785 A) a grid alias may point into `core/dimension/*` when no spacing
  step has the value, so a target in either collection passes; which of the two is right stays with (19g).

## (2026-11-02) — The real-Figma canary: a path rule, a Mac job and a judge, run before the owner rebuilds (#3215)

`tools/figma-canary/` builds the owner's decisions of 2026-11-01 on #3215: a slim, as-needed check in real Figma before the owner is told "ready to rebuild". #3209 passed every gate and broke every Update on real Figma, because the tests' host is more permissive than Figma's sandbox. Nothing between merge and rebuild touched a real host. This is a tool, not a gate: a live Figma host isn't in CI, and nothing in the plugin changed.

### What's in it

- **`needs-check.ts`**: given the last checked commit and the candidate, applies the owner's path rule and says whether a check is needed, with a reason per file. The rule is two literal lists, `SKIP` then `CHECK`. It also catches a raised `EXECUTOR_REVISION` and a `figma.` API that nothing under `apps/plugin/src/` named before.
- **`judge.ts`**: reads the Mac's raw result envelopes and prints a per-command table, then `safe to rebuild from <commit>` or `held: <reason>`. It holds on any of: a missing or doubled envelope; a host `error`; `ok` not true; an exception's text anywhere in a verdict, refusal, blocker or log line; a build stamp whose commit (#3253) isn't the one asked for, or is dirty; the wrong file; or a command that wrote. `--commands` prints the four read-only commands, with the house brand compiled in for the prune preview.
- **`README.md`**: the rule verbatim, the owner's one-time scratch-file setup (house brand, 5 sets), and the Mac's job text: a dedicated checkout, `git checkout --detach <sha>`, a clean tree, `npm ci`, build, open the scratch file, link on, then `status` (stop unless it's the scratch file), `readback`, `update-components { confirm: false }`, `prune { confirm: false }`, plus a recorded host-descriptor read for #3295's fixture.
- **`selftest.ts`**: the judge over fixtures, and the rule over literal paths. `fixtures/3209.json` carries #3209's real-host error verbatim and must be held on `update-components`, quoting the invariant. The other 20 judge arms each make one edit to `pass.json`.

### Calls made where the decision was silent

- #3293's read commands haven't merged, so the canary uses the four existing read-only commands: `status`, `readback`, the update dry run, and the prune preview (the Apply Theme plan read, from the proposal's §3).
- A file on neither list needs a check. So engine code that isn't token values needs one: the plugin bundles it, and only token values are on the decision's skip list.
- The fifth seed set is `tabs`, a family lead whose usage panel lists its item.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies this:** in #3209's envelope, the headline is `✗ check failed` and the invariant is in the summary. The first draft of the judge quoted the first string matching an exception pattern, which was the headline, so it held without naming the error. `3209/update-components` now asserts the quote carries `'get' on proxy: property 'getLocalTextStylesAsync'`.

## (2026-11-02) — Update re-lays a provider-logo block still on the old 48px grid (#3145)

#3142 measured the single-component grid's pitch, so a fresh provider-logo build no longer overlaps. A file built
before it kept its overlaps through every Update: the in-place path restamps and keeps positions, and the measured
pitch only placed components the plan gained. The owner approved the fix on 2026-11-01; the re-lay rule is a technical
call within the hand-edit rules.

- **What moves.** `relayOldGrid` in `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts`, called at the top of the emit branch on an
  update, before new components are placed. It takes the components Prism3 built (stamp and record, `builtByPrism3`, as
  the page move reads them) and acts only while two of them overlap, so the icons, which the 48px pitch fits, are never
  touched. Each mark keeps its row and column off the old grid, at the measured pitch, from the block's top-left corner.
- **Hand edits.** The as-built record leaves x and y out (`member-baseline.ts`), so no record says where Prism3 put a
  component. The old grid is the evidence instead: the pre-#3142 executor placed every component at the block's corner
  plus whole 48px steps, and a page move carries a block whole, so Prism3's placements share one offset modulo 48. The
  largest group sharing an offset is the grid. A mark off it was moved by hand and stays, as does any component Prism3
  did not build. A designer who rearranged marks within the grid keeps the arrangement; only the spacing changes.
- **When something is in the way.** If a new spot meets anything else on the page (a hand-moved mark, another block, a
  note, each widened by the 24px gap new components keep), nothing moves and the outcome carries a miss naming the mark (`… .position -> NOT RE-LAID`). Nothing is pushed
  aside to make room.
- **Reaching old files.** `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 45 → 46, and entry 46 names `provider-logo`, so a block drawn under an
  earlier revision is due, and its Update runs the re-lay.
- **Trap for re-verifiers.** A designer who drags a mark to another spot exactly on the old grid, in both axes, is read
  as Prism3's placement and re-laid with the rest, keeping that new row and column. The block's own header (#3172) is not
  resized: it is a fixed-width instance a designer may have edited, and the block grows right and down, clear of it.
- **Tests.** `test-update-apply.ts`, `relay marks/…`: the provider logos at the old pitch, stamped at revision 45 (so
  only reach entry 46 makes them due, and the dry run must read all 86 due), a designer's own mark on the grid's offset
  clear of the block, then Updated; a Prism3 mark moved off the grid where a neighbor would land; and an icon block at the old pitch beside a wider hand-made icon, which measures the
  pitch past 48. Mutations, each failing by name: the writes dropped → `relay marks/no overlap`, `relay marks/spacing`;
  every Prism3 mark taken as on the grid → `relay marks/hand moved`; the obstacle check dropped → `relay marks/blocked`;
  the obstacles not widened by the gap → `relay marks/gap`; the ownership filter dropped → `relay marks/theirs`; entry
  46 emptied → `relay marks/due`; the overlap guard dropped → `relay marks/icons kept`; the hand-moved marks left out
  of the re-lay's check → `relay marks/hand blocks`.

## (2026-11-02) — Agent link: four read-only node commands, so the master needs one plugin (#3147 Phase 2a)

**What landed.** `inspect`, `component-keys`, `audit-frames` and `snapshot`, with the args and results drafted in the Phase 2 proposal on #3147 and approved as drafted (Q3147.10 A, Q3147.14 A). The Mac mini's queue showed that in the master an agent only reads: component keys, instance properties, variable bindings. These four answer those reads, so the master can run Prism3 alone. They live in `apps/plugin/src/agent-reads.ts`, are routed in `agent-dispatch.ts` and validated in `parseCommand`, and need nothing transport-specific: the mailbox and the bridge both carry them. `commands.json` is regenerated, and the ecosystem map, the agent-link guide, the plugin README, the bridge README and the mailbox runbook list them.

**Write nothing, proven by a log rather than by reading the code.** `file-shim.ts` gains `NodeShim`: a page tree behind Proxies that log every assignment, `defineProperty`, `delete`, and every call to a method outside a short read list. Each command runs over both transports against it (`test-agent-link.ts` through the real `main.ts` and the mailbox, `test-agent-bridge.ts` through the real server, socket and relay), and the `no-write/<cmd>` arm requires the log to stay empty, no root plugin data to move outside the mailbox's own keys, and no `ACTIONS` handler to run. The one exception is stated: the bridge suite skips `prism3agent/link`, the link record the agent link rewrites after every command whatever it is. The FileShim did not model nodes, so the node model is a new class beside it rather than a second variables model.

**Expectations are literals.** `agent-read-fixture.ts` holds the fixture file and each command's `result.data`, typed by hand, shared by both suites so the transports are held to one answer. The PNG's base64 is Node's encoder, not the plugin's hand-written one. Arms beyond the envelope: `inspect/unreadable` (a layer that throws on read is listed and its sibling still read), `inspect/cap`, `keys/fixture` (a name list and `missing`), `audit/each-count/<count>` (one planted defect per frame counts exactly one), `audit/clean`, `audit/legacy-lists`, `snapshot/scale`, and six `refuse/<case>` arms.

**Calls made inside the draft, for the owner to correct.** The draft named `inspect`'s `fields` values without saying what each adds. Here, absent means all five, and each adds one key: `props` → `componentProperties`, `bindings` → `boundVariables`, `styles` → `textStyle`, `layout` → `layout`, `text` → `characters`. Each entry also carries `parentId`, so a flat depth-first list can be put back into a tree. `component-keys`' `sets: true` lists each set's `members`. `audit-frames` does not walk inside instances (their layers are the component's), and with no `nameRule` it counts frames still carrying a Figma default name. A snapshot of a node that is not in the file fails `bad-args`, through a `ReadRefusal` the dispatcher maps to that code instead of `handler-threw`.

**Not in this PR.** The write-command guard (protected-node defaults, Q3147.11; version first, Q3147.12) is Phase 2b's first step in the proposal's order, so it waits for 2b. `run-code` stays dev-only (Q3147.13 A).

**Mutations, each failing by name.** `readOne` assigning `n.name = n.name` → `no-write/inspect` on both transports. `locked` dropped from `readOne`'s entry → `envelope/inspect` on both transports.
