## (2026-11-02) — lint-guide-claims: the designer guides fail CI when they stop describing the app (#3264 part 3)

**Status:** a new gate, built as the owner decided on #3264 (decision 3, A). Wired into `verify.ts`, `ci.yml`,
`CONTRIBUTING.md` §3, CLAUDE.md's list and the PR template together; `lint-doc-gates.ts` holds them equal. No engine
behavior moves, so no change note. Stacked on #3264's guides PR, which it passes on.

### What it checks

The guides are the subject, the code the oracle (`docs/34` shape 1). Four arms, each named in its failures:

- **LABEL.** Every **bold** span is a UI label, and must be a whole string literal (or HTML text node) in
  `apps/studio/src`, `apps/plugin/src` or `apps/tokenpress/src`. A small tokenizer of its own reads the literals and
  skips comments, so renaming a label's literal fails even while a comment still says the old words. A label with no
  placeholder must equal a plain literal; an italic part is a placeholder, and a label with placeholders matches only
  a template with as many `${…}`, its static chunks keeping their spaces. A plural suffix (`item${…'s'}`) counts as
  static text. HTML offers its text nodes and `aria-label`, `title`, `placeholder` and `alt`, never a class or id. A
  bold span ending in a period or colon is a lead sentence and is skipped.
- **CITE.** Every `<!-- src: path:line -->` names a git-tracked file and lines inside it, and the cited lines still
  hold one of the claim's quoted strings, code spans or bold labels, read with comments removed, so a comment keeping
  the old words can't hold the claim. A number or `…` in a quoted example is a placeholder, and the example may fill a
  cited template's holes. A leading `↳ ` is dropped from page names, since the code adds it.
- **COUNT.** "<n> component sets" equals `componentDefs.length`, and at least one guide makes the claim.
- **SCOPE.** Every guide `index.md` lists is read and cites something, and each source tree yields literals, so a
  moved folder fails instead of passing on nothing.

### Mutations, each failing by name

- `tabClean: 'Clean up'` renamed to `'Tidy up'` in `state/update-file.ts` (two comments still say "Clean up"): 7
  LABEL failures for **Clean up**, plus the CITE lines that quoted it.
- One line inserted above `RESTORE_OFF_HINT` in `apps/studio/src/main.ts`: the two citations of `main.ts:1756` fail.
- A citation path misspelled: "is not a file git tracks". "60 component sets" changed to 59: the COUNT arm.
- From review: `handEdits: 'Hand edits'` renamed (LABEL and CITE fail), and again with a trailing `// formerly Hand
  edits` (still both); a made-up bold **Brand settings**, which the old template fallback let pass; a bold class
  name from `ui.html`; a renamed refusal string whose comment keeps the old words (CITE).

### Limits

- A claim that quotes nothing is checked for existence and range only: 139 of the 311 citations today. The summary
  line prints the number, so a rise is visible.
- A label is checked for existing somewhere in the three trees, so a label drawn in several places doesn't fail when
  one copy is renamed. CITE is the backstop.

## (2026-11-02) — The plugin build skips the behind-check fetch when git can't run, and under --watch (#3261)

Two nits from the independent review of #3253 (#3239), which added the commit to the build stamp and the warning when
the checkout is behind `origin/main`.

### What changed

`git-stamp.mjs` gains `behindCheck(buildId, { watch }, run)`, which `build.mjs` now calls in place of `behindStamp`:

1. **Git cannot run.** When the stamp's commit field is `git-unavailable`, the build has already printed the `⚠ git did
   not run` pair. The fetch would fail for the same reason and add a second note, and where git hangs it would wait out
   its 20 s timeout. It is now skipped.
2. **`--watch`.** The review found that the Ready comment ("each non-watch build fetches") and the code disagreed: the
   fetch also ran once when a watcher started, after the `watching …` line, and blocked for up to 20 s. Of the two
   remedies, skipping the fetch under `--watch` is the simpler one. It is a one-line condition, it makes the description
   true as written, and it keeps a working loop from blocking. A build that runs once still fetches.

The side effect the issue notes is unchanged for a build that runs once: `git fetch origin main` updates the checkout's
`origin/main` ref.

### The gate

New `skip/…` arms in `test-git-stamp.ts`:

- `skip/no-git`: a `git-unavailable` stamp runs no git at all and adds no note.
- `skip/watch`: under `--watch`, nothing is fetched.
- `skip/one-shot`: a build that runs once with a commit in its stamp still fetches and counts.
- `skip/stand-in`: a real `git` executable, first on PATH, that logs each call and refuses every one as the license
  prompt did. The build's stamp and behind check run against it through a real process, and the arm requires the one
  warning pair, no "Could not fetch" note, and no `fetch` in git's log.

New `build/…` arms run the real `node build.mjs` with a stand-in git first on PATH, so `build.mjs`'s half of the fix
is held too. The independent review found that reverting it passed every `skip/…` arm, because those drive
`behindCheck` directly:

- `build/fetch-seen`: the control. A one-shot build with a working git fetches, and the stand-in's log shows it.
- `build/no-git`: with a git that refuses every call, the build never fetches and prints no "Could not fetch" note.
- `build/watch`: `node build.mjs --watch`, stopped 1 s after `watching …`, stamps the commit and never fetches.

The build writes `dist/`, so the test moves the checkout's `dist/` aside and puts it back after.

Mutations: `build.mjs` calling `behindStamp` again fails `build/no-git`. `build.mjs` passing `{ watch: false }` fails
`build/watch`. Without the `git-unavailable` test, `skip/no-git` and `skip/stand-in` fail (git saw a fetch, and three
lines were printed). Without the watch test, `skip/watch` fails. By hand, a real `node build.mjs` with the failing
stand-in on PATH ran only `rev-parse` and finished in 3 s. `--watch` with a pass-through git ran `rev-parse` and
`status`, then no fetch.

## (2026-11-01) — The Update verdict's counts agree with their verbs (#3243)

Filed from the review of #3236. With one fault, the apply's verify line read "text-field: 1 field still differ from the
plan". #3236 makes that line come up more often, because a nested instance on the wrong member is now one of its fields.

### The fix

The verdict picks its verb from the count: "1 field still differs", "2 fields still differ". The issue asked for every
sibling count string in the same copy to be checked. Two more had the same fault, with a pronoun instead of a verb:

- the set line's "N left as they are", which read "1 left as they are";
- the dry run's line (`previewLine`), which the Update verdict repeats for a set it entered with nothing to write. Its
  "N not built by Prism3, left as they are" read the same way, beside an Adopt clause that already said "it" for one.

Both now say "it is" for one. These are grammar fixes to approved copy, with no new wording. The other count strings in
the verdict were already right or carry no verb ("N updated", "N parts not written as planned", "N members not
finished", which already has its own singular line).

### Out of scope, filed

The capture-baseline and Adopt verdicts (`update-plan.ts`) have the same "N left as they are" fault. They are separate
verdicts, so they are filed as #3275 rather than fixed here.

### The gate

New `verb/…` arms in `test-update-apply.ts` check outcomes written by hand: one field and two, one member left and two.
Four existing arms pinned "1 left as they are" and now pin "1 left as it is". The `unbuilt/verdict` arm in
`test-canvas-furniture.ts` asserted that no line contains "left as they are". It now matches both forms, so it would not
go vacuous for a count of one. Each form reverted fails by name: `verb/differs 1`, `verb/differ 2`, `verb/left 1` (with
`recordfail/prefix` and `idle/furniture`), and for `previewLine`, `converged/adoptable one` in
`test-update-components.ts`.

  2026-10-21 build the owner tested (`2d58f4e1`, the bar's Apply Theme), at 1280 and 380, in both themes, with the
  main thread blocked for 1.5 s mid-run to imitate the plugin's iframe while a write runs: the cell, its "…" and the
  words never share a pixel. The cell's CSS has not changed since then. So the overlap the owner saw comes from
  something the test hosts don't draw, and this lane makes no product change it can't show is needed. Renders are on
  the issue.
- **Which busy signal to keep** (the cell's "…"/arc, the label's own "…", or both) is owner design. The issue says to
  flag it rather than pick, so it is asked on #2908 and nothing here changes it.

### What changed

- **`BUSY_OVERLAP`**, a probe in `test-chrome.mjs`. While a control is busy, it takes the "…" cell's box, the box of
  the "…" text inside it (so dots spilling out of their cell count), and the words' text box (a Range over the label's
  text nodes), and returns their shared area. Expected: the literal `BUSY_OVERLAP_MAX = 0`. Nothing is read from the
  stylesheet. A control that isn't busy, or has no cell or no words, returns `null`, which fails by name.
- **The arc too.** The visible spinner after about 300 ms is `.p3-spin::before`, absolutely positioned with
  `inset: 0`, which has no rect of its own and stays in the cell only while the cell is its containing block. So the
  probe also reads the arc's used box from `getComputedStyle(spin, '::before')` (width and height plus its border) and
  requires it no larger than the cell, and requires the cell not `position: static`. Measured: 16×16 in the 16px cell.
- **Two arms in section 10, on the figma host**, at every width the section sweeps (1280, 640, 380) and both themes:
  Update file while its run is out ("Updating…"), and Draw specs while it draws ("Drawing specs…"). That's 12
  assertions. The web host draws no busy control: its only writes are the plugin's.

### Mutations

Each after a `wip:` commit, both bundles rebuilt, section 10 run alone:

- **M1:** `.p3-spin`'s `position: relative` changed to `position: absolute` in `chrome.css`, so the cell leaves the
  label's flow and draws over its first letters. Result: `#2908 figma light 1280: the busy spinner sits beside
  "Updating…", not over it (shared area 405px², at most 0; …)` and its Draw specs twin, all 12 arms, with no other
  failure.
- **M2:** `position: relative` changed to `position: static`, so the arc's containing block becomes an ancestor and
  the arc draws across the control while the cell and its dots stay put. Result: all 12 arms fail by name, reading the
  shared area 0 but the arc's box larger than the cell (`arc 1164×32 in a 16px cell, cell position static`). Section
  10's four `S1.4 … locator.click: Timeout` arms also fail under M2 (the stray arc intercepts a click); that is a crash
  shape, not the catch.

## (2026-11-01) — The action-anchor note names a pinned step, not the auto step (#1894)

When `actionPalette` names a brand color, `brandTheme` wrote the action-anchor note from a local `actionAnchorStep` that is always the brand color's auto-placed step, so `input.actionAnchorStep` never reached it. With a pin of 300 the note said "step 450 … moved only if it misses 3:1", while `modes.ts` applied 300 exactly (`restFill`, `exact`, #331) and never moves a pin. The note now branches on the pin: pinned, it names the pinned step and says it is applied exactly, with the miss reported rather than corrected; unpinned, it keeps the approved row-45 wording byte for byte.

The new pinned wording is a DRAFT for the owner (Q-block on the PR). `test.ts` holds both cases as literals; reverting the branch fails `#1894: a pinned actionAnchorStep is reported as the pinned step…` by name. No corpus brand pins a brand-color action step (the one example with a pin, `nb-redesign`, uses `actionPalette: neutral`, which writes no anchor note), so `regen --check` is clean and the bump is a patch.

**Trap:** `theme.ts` keeps a LOCAL `actionAnchorStep` (the auto step, fed to `roleAnchorStep.action`) beside `input.actionAnchorStep` (the pin, passed through as `theme.actionAnchorStep`). The two share a name; the note has to read the input. The same shape exists for `linkAnchorStep`, which has no pin lever, so it is not affected.

## (2026-11-01) — the CLI paste path migrates renames through the plugin's own rename pass (#1024)

**STATUS: PR open, not merged.** ENGINE 0.238.0 (minor, `packages/engine/changes/claude-1024-paste-rename-migration.md`), CONTRACT stands. Files: `packages/engine/rename-map.ts` (the apply functions, moved in), `packages/engine/rename-runtime.ts` (**NEW**), `packages/engine/materialization-renames.ts` and `packages/engine/figma-names.ts` (one source exporter each), `packages/engine/materialise-to-figma.ts` (the `migrate` pass), `packages/engine/package.json` (one export), `apps/plugin/src/write-figma.ts` (calls the engine), `apps/plugin/test-rename-parity.ts` (**NEW**, an arm of the plugin `test` step), `docs/10-figma-materialization.md`.

**What was wrong.** One rename had two outcomes. The plugin executor moved a renamed variable in place (#1013), keeping its id and every binding. `materialise-to-figma.ts` was create-or-update-by-name, so it created the new name beside the old one and orphaned every binding. Nothing compared the two paths, so nothing saw it. The MCP paste bundle (#1553) never had the gap: it bundles the plugin's executors. This was the hand-written CLI path only.

**The fix shares the code instead of copying it.** The apply half of the pass (`beginMigration`'s validation and atomic collection pre-pass, `upsertCollection`'s variable renames) moved from the plugin into `rename-map.ts` as `openMigration` / `renameCollections` / `renameVariables`. The plugin calls them. The paste payload can't import, so it ships their source (`Function.prototype.toString`, the move `nestVariantMatchSrc` already makes) and calls them in the file, in a new first pass, `migrate`. The materialization rules ship the same way, with the three constants they close over serialized from the constants themselves.

**Two traps in shipping source under tsx, both found by running the payload.** (1) A reference to an IMPORTED name compiles to `(0, import_x.name)(…)`, an object the payload doesn't have. So every shipped function may call only functions in its own module: that's why the apply functions live in `rename-map.ts` and take `root` as an argument rather than calling `rootOf`. (2) tsx wraps a nested named function in `__name(fn, "…")`, a helper it injects at module scope. The runtime defines an identity `__name`.

**Size.** The map is ~21KB and the color axis's planned names ~11.5KB, so the pass is packed by bytes per axis, like `color-create`. Planned names travel as tails under one root per axis, and contract rows as `[from, to, since]`. The reference brand's pass is one 41.7KB payload; three of the four committed brands take two. An axis is indivisible, so the existing `materialise budget` arm in `test.ts` (every pass, every chunk, at most 45,000 bytes) is what would catch one axis outgrowing a payload. Every chunk re-runs the collection pre-pass, which is a `source-absent` no-op after the first, so chunks are order-free.

**The gate.** `test-rename-parity.ts` seeds one old-names file and materializes it twice into `file-shim.ts`. One write is the plugin's `beginMigration` plus all four variable executors. The other is the paste path's real `migrate`, `palette`, `color-create`, `dims-create`, `font-vars` and `motion-vars` payloads. Both read the same plans (`variablePlans`, newly exported). The expected side is nine literal old → new pairs plus the collection rename, each checked against the register that states it (a `COLLECTION_RENAMES` entry, a `DEPRECATIONS` row, or a materialization rule). The pairs cover color, a float collection, and all three `core` slices, so the owned-group scoping is exercised. Variables are followed by id, so a path that recreates instead of moving fails. Mutations, each from a `wip:` commit, each failing by name: the `migrate` pass removed → `paste path: every old name in the fixture is MOVED` and 3 more; its `renameVariables` call dropped → the same; the float axes dropped from `migrateAxes` → the same; the font axes dropped → the same; the owned-group filter removed from the payload → `the migrate pass reports what it moved … (refused 3)`; the plugin's `renameVariables` call dropped → `plugin path: every old name in the fixture is MOVED` and the parity arm.

**Trap for whoever squashes next.** `git fetch --unshallow` (which `lint-release-notes` asks for) moves `origin/main`. A `git reset --soft origin/main` after it squashes onto the NEW main and silently reverts whatever landed in between. Independent review caught exactly that here (#3220 reverted whole). Squash onto the branch's own merge base, then rebase.

**Not changed.** The pre-#1097 un-rooted `core` names are still invisible to both paths (#1109): the parity is exact, including that gap.

## (2026-11-01) — Every prop-backed state has its prop, unless admitted (#2757)

**What.** A `test.ts` arm, `#2757`, walks every def in `componentDefs`. For each state in `states` that a code
consumer sets through a prop, it requires that prop: `disabled`→`disabled`, `read-only`→`readOnly`,
`pending`→`isPending`, `inactive`→`isInactive`. #2708 pinned the Rows' and Textarea's props against a literal;
this covers the next def, too. A state with no prop can be reached in Figma and not in code.

**The oracle is a literal.** `STATE_PROP` is written by hand and not derived from the defs (docs/34 shape 1).
The names follow no single rule (`readOnly` is camel case, `isPending` is not), so a derivation would have to
guess and would move with any rename.

**Admissions.** `STATE_PROP_OK` maps `def:state` to a reason, in the `ZERO_OK` / `RESERVED_ROOT_OK` shape. The
walk found two, both already decided:
- `field-label:disabled`: #1339. The label dims from its field, and the old prop was removed.
- `pagination-item:disabled`: call 9 A and Q414 A. Previous and next at an end use `isInactive` with
  `aria-disabled`, not native disabled. Figma draws that as `disabled`.

An admission must be live (the def declares the state and lacks the prop), or it fails as stale. Each mapped
state must also be reached, with its prop, by at least one def, so a dead map entry fails instead of passing.

**Mutations.** Each was committed `wip:` first and the subject was restored from `HEAD`.
- Drop Textarea's `disabled` prop: `#2757` fails and names `textarea` (with #2708's two pins).
- Drop Counter's `disabled` prop: `#2757` is the only failure, naming `counter`. Nothing else pinned it.
- Delete the `pagination-item:disabled` admission: `#2757` fails and names `pagination-item`.

## (2026-11-01) — Update's dry run reads which member each nested instance is (#3242)

Filed from the review of #3236 (#3206), which gave the apply's verify `nestedMemberFaults` and named the dry run as out
of scope. The dry run judges each member through `diffAnatomy`, which holds a nested instance to its set (`nestTarget`)
and not to the member inside it (`nestVariant`). So a member whose stamp and record read current, but whose nested
FieldLabel sat on `emphasis=secondary` where the plan says `primary`, read **current**. The dry run listed nothing to
update, so the apply never ran and its new verify never saw the member.

### The fix

`nestedMemberFaults` moves from `update-apply.ts` to `update-plan.ts`, unchanged in what it reads, and now returns
each fault as data (`part`, `set`, `member`, `plan`). `nestFaultLine` formats it, so the apply's verify line is the same
text as before. The dry run calls it per member, beside the stamp, revision and reaction checks: a fault makes the member
`update` where it would otherwise read `current` or `revisionUnknown`, and each fault is listed as a `nestVariant`
change on its part, from `<set>/<member>` to `<set>/<coordinate>`. It is not a bare re-apply, so `reapplied` does not
count it. A member that is hand-edited, has no record or is damaged keeps the state it had. The apply already writes such
members. A part the record shows as edited by hand is passed as kept, as the apply keeps it by default. The expected side
stays the plan's own `nestVariant`, never `resolveNestMember`, so the check stays independent of the executor
(`docs/34`).

### The gate

A new `nest dry run` section in `test-update-apply.ts` covers Text field and Select. Each is built with the label at
`secondary`, then every member is given the stamp today's plan writes, so its stamp and record read current. All 84
labelled members must read `update` and be listed as a `nestVariant` change from secondary to primary, with no bare
re-apply. The apply must then swap every label to primary with no nested fault in its verify, and the next dry run must
read all 84 current. With the dry run's call removed, `nest dry run/<host> to update`, `… named` and `… applied` fail
on both hosts.

## (2026-11-01) — One placeholder ink: `field.placeholder` takes `text.secondary`'s fit (Q3212.5 A, #3220)

With `secondaryTextGround: page` (#3212) the reference brand's `text.secondary` moved to `neutral.500` in light, but
`color.field.placeholder` kept its own fit at `neutral.550`. The field hosts bind `text.secondary` for the
placeholder, and Studio's Fields section draws `field.placeholder`: two placeholder inks. The owner took Q3212.5 A.

- **Chosen: the same fit, not an alias.** `field.placeholder` is picked by `pickMinPass(textCands, pageSecondary.rgb,
  cfg.secondaryMin)`, the exact call `text.secondary` makes. `pageSecondary` is hoisted above it in `modes.ts`, so one
  ground decides both. Why not alias `text.secondary`: the engine emits every semantic color as an alias of a
  palette step, never of another semantic role. A role-to-role alias would be a new emission shape for consumers,
  Style Dictionary and the Figma writer to handle. The same fit keeps the shape, the name and the guaranteed surface,
  and `token-contract --check` passes unchanged.
- **It moved more than the issue expected.** Main's HC already disagreed in **every** brand. `text.secondary` fits
  the HC floor (`neutral.050`/`.900`), but the placeholder was fitted on `background.secondary`, which is white/black
  in HC. So each brand's HC placeholder now steps one darker, to `text.secondary`'s value (prism3 hc-light `650` →
  `700`, hc-dark `350` → `300`). The components already drew that ink, so no component moves. Only the token, its
  `.ai.json` and the style guide do. Light and dark move only for the reference brand.
- **Metadata follows.** In the reference brand, `field.placeholder` is now contracted on `background.primary` (4.59:1)
  and its `sits_on` narrows to it. Its description names the shared ink there, and a floor brand keeps the old wording.
- **Arms that encoded the old fit, updated as fallout.** The `field(#1341)` arm's placeholder check now asserts
  `text.secondary`'s ink and ground. The `#63` light declaration adds `placeholder on field`, the same Q-TXT1 A
  shortfall as `body on card` (one ink, the same `neutral.050`). The `#3049` raised-surface sweep extends its
  page-fit exemption to `field.placeholder`.
- **Gates.** A new engine arm, `Q3212.5 A: field.placeholder resolves to text.secondary …`. It covers page and inverse
  pairs, every mode, over the reference brand and the redesign seed (`page`, the seed since #3219) and the corpus and
  prism3 (`floor`), and both grounds must be represented. On the seed, the placeholder moves with `text.secondary` to
  `neutral.500` in light, and its light preview shortfalls are the same pair the reference brand declares (`body on
  card`, `placeholder on field`, both 3.78:1). `body on card` is the consequence #3219 accepted; the placeholder is the
  same ink on the same ground, so it is that shortfall, not a new one. No gate pins the seed's preview shortfalls. A Studio smoke arm checks that the Fields section's placeholder is drawn in
  `text.secondary`'s emitted value, page and inverse. Mutation: restore the placeholder's own ground (`asGround('background.secondary',
  cfg.bg.secondary.rgb)`), and the engine arm fails by name.

## (2026-11-01) — Update file at 380: a due set's tag stays inside the dialog (#3133)

**Status:** panel fix (`update-file.ts`, `chrome.css`) and a new `test:chrome` section, `3133` (shard 3). ENGINE patch
(change note): no committed artifact, emission or component surface moves. The plugin's main thread is unchanged.

### Diagnosis

A due row is the checklist's `check()` button: its box, then the set's name, then its why-tag, all on the button's one
flex line. That line cannot wrap, and the tag is `flex: none` (`.p3-sg-tag`), so the name (`min-width: 0`) gave up its
width first and the tag then ran past the body's edge. At 380 the body's content box is 330px wide; "Engine update:
recorded before Prism3 noted what it drew" drew from x 98 to 439 against a right edge of 355, and the name read "Se".

### The fix

The name and the tag now sit in one `.p3-check-text` span, the wrapping line the lever kit's check rows already use.
Where both fit, nothing changes: the tag stays at the line's end, the same 12px from the name. Where they do not, the
tag drops under the name, and a tag wider than the line shrinks and wraps its words inside its fill. No copy, color or
size changes; the run's Due/Updating rows (`update-run-row`) carry short tags and are left as they are.

### Test

`test:chrome` section `3133`: the plugin at 380 and 1280, light and dark, three due sets (one per reason), Update file
opened and its check answered. Each tag must be drawn whole inside the body's content box and its own row, each name
whole, and no sideways scroll; at 1280 each tag stays on its name's line. Mutation (after a `wip:` commit): the name and
tag handed to `check()` as two spans again, not the wrapper → `#3133 figma light 380: each due set's tag is drawn
whole, inside the Update dialog's body and its own row …` and `… each due set's name is drawn whole …`, light and dark.

## (2026-11-01) — The plugin build stamps the git commit, and warns when the checkout is behind main (#3239)

From owner decision Q-SI1 A. On 2026-10-31 the owner rebuilt the plugin after #3214 merged, and the rebuilt plugin still had the bug: a license prompt on the build machine had silently blocked `git pull`, so the checkout was stale. The stamp, `tree-<8 hex>`, hashes the folder path (#836, #1117), so it read the same on every build and could not show it.

- **The stamp.** `build.mjs` now stamps `<ISO seconds> tree-<8 hex> <commit>` into both bundles, on every build (`build`, `fresh`, `build:release`). The commit is the short sha, `<sha>-dirty` when the tree has uncommitted or untracked changes, or `git-unavailable`. The tree stays: #836's argument holds, since two worktrees on one commit are normal and only the tree separates them. The commit answers the other question, how current the checkout is.
- **Where it shows.** Every surface already reads `PRISM3_BUILD` through `apps/studio/src/build-identity.ts`, so the parse gained a `commit` field and the renderings carry it: the menu stamp (`tree-7a00f94d 76a1636b 11-01 04:10Z`), the verdict note and console line (`Built from tree-7a00f94d (commit 76a1636b) at …`), and the title. The agent link's `link` record carries the whole stamp in its `build` field, so an agent reads the commit from the file. An older stamp without the field still parses, with `commit: null`.
- **Behind main.** After the build, `git fetch origin main` and `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main`; a checkout behind prints a warning naming the count. The build never fails on it, and a fetch that cannot run is one plain note.
- **Git cannot run.** The stamp says `git-unavailable` and the build prints a warning carrying git's own first line, rather than stamping nothing.
- **Tests.** The git calls live in `apps/plugin/git-stamp.mjs`; `test-git-stamp.ts` (in the plugin's `test`) drives them with a stubbed git, so nothing depends on the machine. Mutation: `composeBuildId` dropping the commit fails `stamp/commit`, `stamp/dirty`, `stamp/no-git`, `stamp/no-binary` and `link/commit` by name. `test-build-identity.ts` pins each rendering, and its source scan now names the new composition.

**Wording is DRAFT for the owner**, listed verbatim in the PR.

## (2026-11-01) — test:chrome: the font read waits for laid-out text (#3255)

Section 3170's "updating" arm failed twice in CI (`chrome (3)` on #3252 and #3256, light and dark) with `p3-status-what`, `p3-status-n` or `p3-status-stop` "drew nothing", and passed locally. It wasn't a paint race in the usual sense, and no sleep fixes it.

### The cause

`fontsDrawn` reads each probed element's fonts with CDP `CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode`. That call counts the glyphs of the element's **laid-out** text and does not run layout itself. While a run is out, the status strip repaints once a second (`shell/status-strip.ts`, `TICK_MS`) and replaces the text nodes of its words, its count and its Stop: exactly the three elements in the failures. A font read that lands after a tick and before the next layout sees those elements with no laid-out text and reports no font at all. The node itself, its attributes and its markup all read whole, so #3069's "the node went" guard never fires. The "reading" arm has no clock and never ticks, which is why it never failed.

Shown directly: a standalone page whose span's text is changed and then read by CDP reports 0 fonts until `offsetHeight` forces layout, then 1. In section 3170, a loop reading the strip's three elements by CDP for 5 s came back empty 4–8 times per arm, clustered a second apart (one cluster per tick).

### The fix

`fontsDrawn` now reads against a laid-out tree. In one page task it numbers the probed elements, installs a `MutationObserver` (childList and characterData) and forces layout. After the read, each probed element whose text changed under the read is read again (fonts only, by the node id it was first read as). Each re-read happens after a forced layout in the same task that collected the changes, until a read of it sees no change. If every round in `AGAIN` (6) still has a change, it returns null, as for a node that went, and `measure` re-probes and then throws its named "re-rendered under the font read" error rather than a false "drew nothing". An element whose text did not change under its read is reported as read, so a real absence still fails on the first read. The fix is in the shared reader, so every `measure` in the suite gets it, not just 3170's.

A first version waited two frames between rounds and counted changes during the wait. That never settles when the tick is faster than a frame pair: a change before the layout point doesn't matter, so the window now starts at the forced layout.

### Verification

- **The race, made deterministic** (a `wip:` mutation, `TICK_MS` 1000 → 25, section 3170 alone): `main`'s reader failed every run with the CI message (`… / updating: … p3-status-what … drew nothing | … p3-status-n … drew nothing`). The new reader passed 2/2 unthrottled and 3/3 under `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` 4. Before the "null past `AGAIN`" change, 3 of 7 throttled runs exhausted the rounds and printed a false "drew nothing". Now it re-probes instead.
- **A real absence still fails by name** (a `wip:` mutation, `.p3-status-n { content-visibility: hidden; contain-intrinsic-size: … }`: the element keeps its box, its text draws nothing): `✗ 3170 figma {light,dark} 1280 / {reading,updating}` and `light 380` all fail with `<span class="p3-status-n" … drew nothing`, 6 of 465. "Updating" is the arm where `n` changes every tick and goes through the re-read path.
- Section 3170 alone at the real tick: 465/465, repeatedly, unthrottled and at 6× throttle.

## (2026-11-01) — Chrome motion: exits for the surfaces the shell removes (menus, dialogs, the unread dot) (#3207)

**Status:** studio and plugin chrome, from one stylesheet. Stacked on #3217 (both edit §3150 and the motion block).
ENGINE patch (change note): no token, emitted tree or component surface moves, so CONTRACT is unchanged. No executor
change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. This closes the gap #3213 disclosed (Q3213.1 A): the approved inventory gives
these surfaces an exit on `motion-fast` with the exit curve (Q3150.1–2 A), and until now they left at once.

### What changed

- **A deferred removal, `leave()` in `shell/dom.ts`.** It marks the node `data-leaving` (the stylesheet gives it its
  exit), makes it `inert`, waits for the node's own finite animations to finish, then removes it. With nothing running
  (the motion durations at 0s, or a node that is not drawn) it removes the node at once, as before. `unleave()` takes the
  mark back, and a per-node counter keeps an exit already under way from removing a node that has since opened again.
- **While it leaves it reads as closed.** The shared menu button's `isOpen` is false for a leaving menu, so a click mid-
  exit opens it again (the leaving one goes at once and a new one enters). `inert` keeps focus and clicks out of it.
  The bar's brand menu returns focus to the switcher when the item that held it is leaving, not only when it is gone.
- **Where it applies:** the Theme and Inspect menus (`menuButton`), the brand menu (`bar.ts`), Update file
  (`update-file.ts`, which used to empty its layer), the start window and its guard (`start.ts`), and the bar row's
  unread dot (`activity.ts`). The dot is redrawn on every repaint, so the paint that drops it keeps the drawn node in
  place, unhooked, through its exit. A moved node would restart its style and its exit with it.
- **The exits (`chrome.css`):** a menu leaves as a fade, opacity only (the proposal's "Shift … leaves as a fade"). A
  dialog's scrim fades and the dialog shrinks back to 96%. The dot shrinks to nothing. All three use `motion-fast` and
  the exit curve. Under reduced motion each is a 100ms fade (Q3150.3 A), with the dialog's and the dot's exit scale
  dropped so neither snaps.

### Where the dot's exit shows

At 1280 the bar row stays when the drawer opens, so the dot shrinks away there. At 380 the open sheet hides the bar row
(`display: none`), so the dot goes with it at once. Nothing is drawn to animate, and `leave()` removes it immediately.

### Gates

`test:chrome` §3150 gains LIVE and REDUCED arms for each exit: the Inspect menu and Update file on the plugin at 1280,
the unread dot at 1280 (and its at-once case at 380), and the brand menu and the start window on the web. Each arm reads
the surface the moment it closes: drawn, marked leaving, inert, focus outside it, its control reading closed. It then
reads the exit's timing and curve (or, reduced, a 100ms fade with no transform), and checks the node is gone once the
motion settles. A reopen mid-exit is read too. DECLARED lists the four new exit rules.

"Gone after Escape" still holds in every other `test:chrome` section: they run with the motion durations at 0s, where no
exit runs and `leave()` removes the node at once. The live harnesses that read a closed surface by its absence now read
a leaving one as closed. Three readers in `test-start-screen.mjs` (`readStart`, `waitStart`, `readHome`) and its two
brand-menu "closed" reads skip nodes inside `[data-leaving="true"]`. `test:smoke` and `test:verdict` needed no change.

Mutations, each failing by name in §3150:
- the menu's `leave` back to `menu.remove()` → `LIVE`/`REDUCED figma light 1280: the Inspect menu, closed by Escape, stays drawn through its exit …` and its fade arms;
- `isOpen` reading a leaving menu as open → `… a click on Inspect during the menu's exit opens it again …`;
- `leave` setting no `inert` → every exit's `… reads as closed` arm (10);
- the menu's exit rule dropped → `DECLARED: rule .p3-menu[data-leaving="true"] declares motion …`, and the Inspect and brand menus' LIVE and REDUCED arms;
- the dot not kept through its exit → `… the dot stays drawn through its exit …` and `… the status dot shrinks away …`;
- Update file emptying its layer again → `… the Update file dialog, closed by Escape, stays drawn …`, `… scrim fades out …`, `… scales down …`;
- the reduced scale override dropped → `REDUCED … the leaving dialog keeps its size …` and `… the status dot … not even a snap`;
- the start window's dismiss removing at once → `LIVE`/`REDUCED web light 1280: the start window, closed by its X, …`;
- the brand menu removed at once → `LIVE`/`REDUCED web light 1280: the brand menu, closed by Escape, …`.

### Gaps

The start window's guard and the Theme menu are not driven live. The guard shares the start window's `leave` call and
its rule, and the Theme menu shares `menuButton` with Inspect.

## (2026-11-01) — Update file's badge: a set deleted or added by hand is counted at the next recount (#3091)

**Status:** plugin fix (`apps/plugin/src/main.ts`) and a new arm in `test-build-completed.ts` (section 6d). ENGINE patch
(change note): no committed artifact, emission or component surface moves. The executor is unchanged, so
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### The problem

The badge's live recount (`fileDue`, #3081 Q810 A) reuses the sets the last read of the file found (`presentCache`), so a
setting change never loads every page. Only a plugin write cleared that cache. A set deleted by hand stayed in it, and its
ledger entry made the next recount count it as due; a set added by hand was missed. Both lasted until the next
`file-sets` read (the checklist opening, or a run).

### The fix

`main.ts` listens for Figma's `documentchange` and drops the cached sets (and any read in flight, as a write does) when
the edit can change which sets the file holds:

- a component or set created, or a created node that holds one (a frame pasted with sets in it);
- a component or set deleted, or a deleted frame, group, section or page (a removed node's children cannot be read);
- a component or set renamed, since the build finds its sets by name (`presentNames`).

Any other edit keeps the cache, so drawing on the canvas never makes the next recount read the file. The listener does
nothing while no sets are cached, which covers a plugin write's own changes (`guarded` clears the cache at its start).

Under `dynamic-page`, Figma accepts a `documentchange` listener only once every page is loaded. So the listener is
registered after the first read of the file's sets (`readPresent`), which loads them all, and never at open (#3110 kept
the open from loading every page). A host that refuses the listener keeps the behavior from before this fix. Of the
issue's three options, this is the first. A timer would still miscount between ticks, and would read a large file on a
schedule.

### Test

`test-build-completed.ts` section 6d, through the real `main.ts`, with the shim keeping the listeners `main.ts` registers.
A read registers one listener. A rectangle drawn and a frame renamed keep the cache (the recount loads no page). Switch
row's set taken off its page with a `DELETE` fired: the next recount reads it neither present nor due. Put back after a
read without it, with a `CREATE` fired: the next recount reads it present. Mutation (after a `wip:` commit): the
listener's body a no-op → `hand/delete` and `hand/add`.

## (2026-11-01) — Running a lane: escape review on bug fixes, a corrections log, owner decisions re-read before Ready (#3240)

Owner decision Q-SI1 A, the process half of a self-check loop. `CONTRIBUTING.md` §4 gains "Running a lane", four rules for every lane:

- **Escape review.** A PR that closes a `type:bug` issue fills a new **Escape review** section in the PR template: which check should have caught the bug and why it didn't, and what was added or filed so it can't escape that way again. `.claude/commands/review-pr.md` has the reviewer check both answers against the diff.
- **Corrections log.** `docs/corrections.md` holds one line per owner correction to agent behavior: date, correction, where it became a rule, PR or issue. It is seeded with the five corrections from 2026-10-31, each citing stance-skills #15, the only record of them. None has a rule in this repo yet, so each says "Not yet" for the weekly retro to close.
- **Re-read before Ready.** Immediately before posting Ready, a lane re-reads the PR's and the issue's comments for owner decisions posted since it started, and applies each or says why not. The incident is #3204's Q3204.4–6. The reviewer checks the same, and a missed decision is blocking.
- **No stalls.** A lane never ends its turn while a long command is still running. The incident is the two stalls of 2026-10-31.

`CLAUDE.md` principle 6 gains one line pointing to the section.

**`lint-doc-gates.ts` arm 8.** The three places that carry the escape review (the template's heading, CONTRIBUTING's rule and the review step) must each keep their marker, as authored literals. It cannot check a PR body, which is not in the tree, so whether a bug fix filled the section in stays the reviewer's call. Mutations: renaming the template heading fails the arm naming the template, and dropping the bold marker from `review-pr.md` names that file. A self-check that cannot fail (`escapeReviewGaps` returning nothing) fails the gate's own self-check by name.

  absent from `release-offline/`.

### Trap

A guard read from a `const` (`const BRIDGE = typeof PRISM3_NETWORK === 'boolean' ? PRISM3_NETWORK : true`) does not
work. esbuild folds the `typeof`, to `BRIDGE = !1`, but does not inline the const, so every branch and the key stay in
the offline bundle. The first try did that, and the new marker caught it. The offline `main.js` still carries the
two message names as empty `case` labels. They hold no token code, and the marker reads the key, not the names.

### Gates

Mutations, each failing by name:
- the three guards replaced with `true` → `[bridge-token] is absent from release-offline/main.js`;
- `PRISM3_NETWORK` dropped from the main entry's define only → the same one arm (the fallback reads it as the network
  build).

`test-agent-bridge.ts` (139 assertions, its `pair/relay` arm reading and writing the token through `main.ts`) and
`test-theme-pref.ts` pass unchanged.

## (2026-11-01) — Update's apply verify reads which member each nested instance is (#3206)

Found by the independent review of #3203: with Update's in-place nested swap skipped for `field-label` only, every
host's nested FieldLabel stayed on its old member, the harness's `<host> leads/primary` arms caught it on all 12 hosts,
and `<host> leads/verdict` stayed green. The apply's own verify told the designer the Update had landed.

### Why the verify missed it

Verify (b) holds each updated member to its plan through `diffAnatomy`, and `diffAnatomy` checks a nested instance's
SET (`nestTarget`, read off the host's main component since #1781) but not the MEMBER inside it: `nestVariant` is listed
as unread, because which member the executor picked is an id on the host and the reader has no independent name for
it. Every FieldLabel member is in the right set, so the wrong one passed.

### The fix

`nestedMemberFaults` (`update-apply.ts`) walks each updated member's plan beside its snapshot. For a planned
`NESTED_INSTANCE` with a `nestVariant`, it takes the main component the snapshot already read (`getMainComponentAsync`
through `mainOf`), parses its name into a coordinate and compares it with the plan's, axis by axis: the same axes, each
with the plan's value, in any order. A mismatch is a content line, `<member>/<path>.nestVariant: <set>/<member>
(the plan says <set>/<coordinate>)`, so the verdict reads "not verified" as for any other field. The expected side is
the plan's own coordinate, not the executor's resolver (`resolveNestMember`), so the check does not agree with the
executor by construction. An instance of a plain component is not read: the executor takes a plain component of that
name first, and it has no coordinate. An instance kept as a hand edit, or under a kept part, is skipped by the content
check's own rule; a kept member root still has its parts read, which is the case the leads section's root edit holds.

### The gate

No new arm: the leads section's `<host> leads/verdict` already asserts a clean verify. Under the issue's mutation (the
in-place `swapComponent` skipped for `nestTarget === 'field-label'`) it now fails on all 12 hosts, with 83 of 84 members
listed on a text field (the 84th is the hand-edited label), as do the label section's `<host> label/verdict` arms on the
four fields with a disabled label. Dropping the hand-edit test from `nestedMemberFaults` fails `<host> leads/verdict` on
all 12 too, the kept label listed. Unmutated, `test-update-apply.ts` passes its 944 assertions.

The trap: the dry run uses `diffAnatomy` the same way, so it does not hold a nested member either. A member the stamp
reads current is not re-checked there; this change is the apply's verify only.

## (2026-11-01) — Chrome motion follow-ups: the closed drawer no longer sinks at boot; the verdict wait fails by name (#3217)

**Status:** studio and plugin chrome, and two harnesses. ENGINE patch (change note): no token, emitted tree or component
surface moves, so CONTRACT is unchanged. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. The three nits from the
independent review of #3213.

### What changed

- **The drawer's exit plays on a real close only.** `p3-drawer-down` (wide) and `p3-strip-down` (380) were keyed on
  `data-open="false"`, which also matches a drawer drawn closed at boot, and one the width changes under. The move was
  0px, so nothing showed, but every settle-wait waited for it. The drawer now marks `data-closing` in the paint that
  turns it from open to closed, and clears it on the exit's `animationend` (or `animationcancel`). Under reduced motion
  the mark is not set: that path plays no animation, so nothing would ever clear it.
- **`test-build-verdict.mjs`'s drawer wait** is the capped `settleMotion()`, the same capped wait as `test-smoke.mjs`
  and `test-start-screen.mjs` (5000ms). The old wait timed out after 3000ms and measured whatever frame it got,
  silently. A tripped cap now fails by name, listing what was still running.
- **`test-smoke.mjs`'s #1069 comment** said the stylesheet transitions no opacity. True when it was written, not since
  #3213. It now says why the carve-out still stays out: the chrome's fades run to full opacity and `settle()` waits
  for them.

### Gates

`test:chrome` §3150 gains three arms on the plugin at 1280 (at boot the closed drawer plays no exit; a narrow → wide
resize under it plays no exit; once the exit ends the mark goes) and one at 380 (the strip appearing closed plays no
exit, which replaces the arm's old carve-out for `p3-strip-down`). DECLARED names the two rules by their new selectors.

Mutations, each failing by name:
- the exit keyed back on `data-open="false"` → `#3150 LIVE figma light 1280: at boot the closed drawer plays no exit`,
  `… a narrow → wide resize under the closed drawer plays no exit`, `#3150 LIVE figma light 380: the strip appearing
  closed plays no exit`, and DECLARED on both selectors;
- the shell never setting `data-closing` → `#3150 LIVE figma light 1280: the drawer sinks on 100ms` and
  `… 380: the sheet sinks back into the strip on 100ms`;
- `SETTLE_CAP_MS` at 1 in `test-build-verdict.mjs` → `#1890 apply-result: every finite animation settles within 1ms
  before measuring — still running: … p3-drawer-up on div.p3-drawer`.

### Trap

Reading the boot arm by running animations alone would pass on the old CSS: a 100ms move has finished long before the
page is ready. The arm reads the closed drawer's computed `animation-name`, which names the exit for as long as the
rule matches.

## (2026-11-01) — Apply Theme hands the thread back inside every stage (#3208)

The owner's Update run froze in "Writing color variables": the strip's timer stopped for long stretches and Stop could
not be clicked. #3170 gave Apply Theme a hand-back before each of its seven stages and one every 200 color variables,
and nothing else.

### Where the time went

Measured first, over the file shim, which now counts every host call (`FileShim.calls`: each method called on the
file, a collection, a variable or a style, and each property written). The longest run of calls with no chance to hand
back, per stage, on the example brands into an empty file: float 1,042–1,068 (it never handed back), color 1,571–1,591
(the 200-variable tick, but a color variable writes a value per mode, and the alias pass alone was 2,165 calls when its
tick was dropped), type variables 338–429, motion 215–223, text styles 54–83, styles 64–76, grid 21–25. A whole apply
is about 6,500–7,700 calls. The shim cannot say how long a call takes in Figma, so the fix does not try to guess which
stage is slow: it puts every stage on the same clock.

### The fix

Every Apply Theme executor (`applyFloatPlan`, `applyWritePlan`, `applyStylesPlan`, `applyGridStylePlan`,
`applyVarCollectionPlan` for type variables and motion, `applyTextStylePlan`) takes an optional `tick` and offers it after
each variable or style written, and after each collection rename on the way in. `main.ts`'s `themePace.tick` hands the
thread back only once about `PACE_MS` (50 ms) has run since the last hand-back, which is what `paced` does for a
component write, so the strip ticks and Stop answers whatever a stage writes. `COLOR_YIELD_EVERY` is gone. A caller with
no tick (the paste harness, every other test) writes in one turn, as before.

`write-styles.ts` is reached by the component executor (`bindGradientStops`), so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` rises to 45. No set
draws differently, so `executor-reach.json`'s entry for 45 names none and no file is told a set is due.

### The gate

`test-run-progress.ts`: `apply/cadence <stage>` runs every example brand's apply into an empty file and again over its
own, reads `FileShim.calls` at each stage and tick, and fails a stage whose worst gap is over 32 calls (the heaviest row
is a `layout` variable across its breakpoint modes, 25). Through `main.ts`, with the component shim given a file shim's
variable and style surface for two runs: `apply/inside`, the panel hears a stage again inside it once about 50 ms has run
on the test's stepping clock; `apply/paced`, with a clock that stands still each stage is heard from once. Mutations,
each failing by name: the float pass-A tick, the color alias tick, the text-style tick, the float stage passed no tick
(`apply/cadence float|color|text-styles`); `themePace.tick` never handing back (`apply/inside`); the `PACE_MS` test
dropped (`apply/paced`).

The trap: the budget counts calls, not milliseconds. A single Figma call that is slow on its own (a `getLocalVariablesAsync`
over a very large file) is still one turn, and no tick can split it.

## (2026-11-01) — Badge gains an inline status style: a dot and plain text on the text line (#3199)

Badge has a new authoring axis, `style: contained | inline` (owner decisions Q-ST1 A and Q1–Q8 A on #3199). An inline badge is an 8px status dot and the label in body text, with no fill, padding, radius or edge. It is as tall as the line it sits in: 24px at medium and 21px at small. The label is `text.primary` in every tone. The dot is the tone's icon role (neutral `icon.secondary`), bound to `space.100`. `excludeCoordinates` keeps `inline` off the count and dot and off bold and surface, so the set grows from 40 to 50 members. The approved §4 guidance copy ships without its DRAFT markers.

**The diagnosis that shaped the paint.** Inline members sit at `emphasis=subtle`, the one emphasis coordinate left to them. Under the old single grammar `{tone}.{type}.{emphasis}.{slot}`, an inline root would therefore resolve the subtle label's tint and edge. A leading inline template would not fix it either: `paintOf` falls through to the next template for any slot the first leaves unbound, so the root's `fill` and `border` would still reach the subtle keys. So `{style}` joined the one grammar (`{tone}.{type}.{style}.{emphasis}.{slot}`), every contained key gained `contained`, and the inline keys bind only a label and an `indicator`. The dot paints through `indicator` (the radio dot's slot) so it never shares the root's `fill`. The padding, corner, gap and type keys gained the style segment the same way.

**The first line.** The root is now top-aligned, and the dot sits in `dotCell`, one line box tall (`type.body.*.line-box`, fixed), which centers it. This is the checkbox row's #1201 construction, so a wrapping label keeps the dot on its first line. A contained badge holds one child in a box that hugs it, so the alignment change does not move it. `badge.surface` left #1009's centered-row exemptions, since it no longer centers.

**The rename needs no ledger entry.** An update adds a new axis to every existing member at the plan's first value, renaming each in place with its id kept (`update-plan.ts`). Nothing leaves the projection, so `lint-component-renames` asks for no entry, and the ledger has no "add" kind to write. `test-update-apply.ts` holds it on the shim: the 40 old members are renamed in place with their ids and keys, a hand edit survives, and the 10 inline members are built.

**Tests, each mutated to fail by name.** `test.ts` gates the inline label at 4.5:1 and the dot at 3:1 against `background.primary`, `background.secondary`, `foreground.primary` and `foreground.raised` in 5 brands × 4 modes (lowest 14.05:1 and 3.16:1). It also holds the markup contract (the dot aria-hidden with no role or name; the label unhidden, never `role="status"`), the inline projection against the issue's literal geometry, and the six footprint cohorts. A new `test:chrome` section, `3199`, lays each projected inline member out in the browser from its own plan and the committed emission, for the default brand and the reference brand. It checks the box is 24 / 21px on one line, and that at 210px a wrapping label keeps the dot's center on the first line.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies:** the `test:chrome` section's label is longer than the docs' "Out of stock at this location". In the runner's fallback face that phrase is 192px, which fits beside the dot at 210px, so it would not wrap there, though it does in the brands' faces. The section's premise arm proves the wrap before it measures.

**Held for the owner:** the `size` prop's description still reads "medium = 12px text, about 30px tall. small = 11px text, about 19px tall", which is true of the contained style only. Rewording it is copy, so it is not changed here. The `type=dot` size finding (Q8 A) is #3226.

## (2026-11-01) — Desktop bridge ships in the network build, with pairing (#3147 Phase 1)

**Status:** transport and build only: `apps/plugin/src/agent-link-ui.ts` (the relay's gate, the link word and the
pairing prompt), `apps/plugin/src/agent-bridge-relay.ts` and `bridge-auth.ts` (pairing), `apps/plugin/manifest.json`,
`tools/figma-bridge/server.ts`, and the gates `test-agent-bridge.ts`,
`test-agent-link.ts`, `test-manifest.ts`, `lint-release-bundle.ts`, `lint-network-reach.ts` and `test-chrome.mjs`
section 31. ENGINE patch (change note). CONTRACT unchanged. `AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 1. No executor change, so
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. Step 3 of the owner's Phase 1 build order on #3147, after #3168 (the two builds) and #3187
(#2497, results kept across a reconnect). Pairing is Q3204.1 A, which supersedes Q3147.2 A (revised): the review of
#3204 showed that an `Origin: null` check does not keep web pages out.

### What changed

- **Relay.** `if (PRISM3_DEV)` became `if (PRISM3_NETWORK)`. The relay ships in the dev build and "Prism3 Studio"
  (`release/`), and drops from "Prism3 Studio Offline" (`release-offline/`), which offers the mailbox only (Q3147.5 A).
- **Manifest.** `ws://localhost:17331` moved from `devAllowedDomains` to `allowedDomains` (Q3147.3 A: exactly the two
  Google Fonts hosts and the bridge). Figma's manifest docs allow a localhost domain in `allowedDomains` when a
  `reasoning` is given, so the reasoning now names the local connection, in wording the owner approved (Q3204.3 A). The manifest
  lists no `devAllowedDomains` any more; the release build still deletes the key if it comes back.
- **Pairing (Q3204.1 A).** The server keeps a random secret in a user-only file (0600, under the user's config
  directory; `--rotate` replaces it) and prints a one-time code (8 characters from a 30-symbol alphabet with no
  look-alikes, about 39 bits) only on demand, from a `figma_status` call while no plugin is connected or a `--pair`
  start, and `figma_status` names it (Q3204.6 A). A code lasts 10 minutes; 5 wrong codes retire it, and after 3
  retirements pairing closes until the next request; a plugin proving its token leaves no code live (Q3204.5 A). Every connection opens with a challenge.
  The plugin asks for the code once per machine, sends an HMAC of it over the nonce, and keeps the token it gets back
  in `figma.clientStorage`, never in the file. Each later hello carries an HMAC of the token over the nonce. A
  connection without a valid proof is closed (4401) before it is sent a command, and it never replaces a paired
  plugin. The plugin's HMAC-SHA-256 is written in `bridge-auth.ts` (the iframe's
  opaque origin may have no `crypto.subtle`); the server uses `node:crypto`.
- **Origin check, now defense in depth.** The server answers 403 before the handshake to any upgrade whose `Origin`
  is not `null`; a request with no `Origin` is refused too. A page's sandboxed iframe sends `null` as well, so this
  check alone never kept web pages out: the pairing proof does. Node's own `WebSocket` sends no `Origin`, so the
  test's real-relay arm sends `Origin: null` explicitly, as the iframe does. Loopback-only bind kept.
- **Link word.** The Activity drawer's bar-row word names the transport: "Listening · bridge" while the bridge is
  connected, otherwise "Listening · mailbox"; "Prism3 Studio Offline" reads "Listening · mailbox only" (Q3204.2 A).
  The manifest reasoning, these words and the 403 body are approved (Q3204.3 A). The pairing prompt's words are
  approved (Q3204.4 A, with the reviewer's two edits); the wrong-code line, reworded for the 10-minute window, and
  the window's stderr lines and `figma_status` description are approved too (Q3204.7 A).
- **No arbitrary code in a release** (Q3147.4 A). `run-code` stays behind `PRISM3_DEV`, and `lint-release-bundle.ts`
  still holds it absent from both releases.

### Gates

- `test-agent-bridge.ts` `origin/refused`: a web page's origin, a localhost page's, and none are each refused with
  403 and never become the plugin. An `Origin: null` client with no token, and the review's page (a sandboxed iframe
  on an ordinary page, in Chromium), each pass the origin check and are closed with 4401, never become the plugin and
  never receive a command. `pair/*`: the secret file's mode and rotation, a wrong code refused, a hello or pair proof
  captured on one connection refused on the next (`pair/replay`), 5 wrong codes on 5 connections retiring the code
  (`pair/limit`), a code issued only on demand (`pair/on-demand`), expired after 10 minutes on an injected clock
  (`pair/expiry`), pairing closed after 3 retirements and the next request reopening it with the full allowance (`pair/cap`),
  no code issued by a `pair` message on the socket, only by `figma_status` (`pair/no-request`), a paired plugin not evicted by an unpaired one, the real relay pairing with the printed code to the token the test derived itself from
  the secret it wrote, and the token never written to the file's plugin data. The plugin's shim tests now run after
  the Chromium install in `ci.yml`, since this arm drives a browser.
- `test-agent-link.ts` `link/word-offline`: the offline build's word.
- `lint-release-bundle.ts`: the relay's two markers moved from `DEV_ONLY` to a new `NETWORK_ONLY` list, which must be
  present in `dist/` and `release/` and absent from `release-offline/`. `run-code` stays in `DEV_ONLY`.
- `lint-network-reach.ts`: `ALLOWED`, the network manifest's list, is an authored literal with the bridge's origin
  in it, and `release/ui.html` must carry the relay's socket, so the offline build's lack of one means something.
- `test-manifest.ts`: the three domains as a literal, no `devAllowedDomains`, and a reasoning that names localhost.
- `test-agent-link.ts` `link/word-transport` and `test-chrome.mjs` section 31: the word, as literals.

### Trap for whoever re-verifies

`openClient(origin = 'null')` with an explicit `undefined` argument takes the default. The first draft of the
"no Origin" arm sent `Origin: null` and the server let it through, which looked like a server bug. The sentinel is
`null` now.

### Not verified live

Whether Figma desktop lets the iframe open `ws://localhost:17331` from `allowedDomains`, in a dev import and in the
org-private published build, and whether the iframe really sends `Origin: null`. Both are among the owner's Phase 1
live checks (Q3147.8 A). If the iframe sends something else, the server refuses it and `figma_status` stays
`connected: false`, so the failure is visible, not silent. The pairing prompt has not been seen in Figma either.

## (2026-11-01) — verify: suggest --unsharded on a shard's failure (Q-CI2 A)

Follow-up to #3224's review (#3227). Since #3216, `npm run verify` runs the chrome suite as three shards side by side. When one failed or timed out, the only hint was `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SCALE`. On a 2-CPU machine the shards compete for the CPUs, so the better way out is one whole run.

**The hint.** `combineShards` adds `UNSHARDED_HINT` to a sharded row's output when the row is a FAIL. A time-out is a FAIL, so one branch covers both cases. A PASS or SKIP row prints no hint. The per-shard time-out message from `classifyRun` is unchanged, so `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SCALE` is still named next to the new line:

> chrome runs its 3 shards side by side, so on a machine with few CPUs they compete for them and a healthy shard can fail or time out. To run it once, whole, rerun with `npm run verify -- --unsharded`. To give every gate more time instead, set VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SCALE (see point 5 in verify.ts).

**The arm.** Three self-checks in the #3216 block: the hint after a FAILED shard, the hint after a timed-out shard, and no hint under a PASS. Each checks a literal, `` rerun with `npm run verify -- --unsharded` ``, not the constant, so rewording the command away fails it as well (`docs/34`). Mutations, each after a `wip:` commit: removing the line fails the first two by name, printing it on every outcome fails the third, and rewording the command fails the first two.

**Comments.** `chrome-shards.mjs`, `test-chrome.mjs` (file header and the modes block) and `test-chrome-shards.mjs` said `npm run verify` runs the suite whole. They now describe the sharded default and the `--unsharded` fallback.

## (2026-10-31) — verify runs the chrome suite in CI's shards, side by side; reviewers lean on CI for the full gate list (#3216, #3183)

Owner decision Q-CI1 A. A PR paid for three full gate runs (author, reviewer, CI), and locally the chrome suite was most of each.

**Sharded chrome in `verify.ts`.** The `chrome` gate carries `shards: { env: 'CHROME_SHARD', ids, clean }`, with `ids` the keys of `apps/studio/chrome-shards.mjs`, the map CI's shards already read through `test-chrome.mjs`. The runner empties `apps/studio/chrome-record/`, starts one `test:chrome` per shard at once (each its own process tree under the gate's limit, classified as a whole gate would be), and prints one row, a PASS only when every shard passed, with a line per shard beneath it (`combineShards`; a FAIL anywhere is the row's FAIL, a SKIP anywhere without a FAIL is a SKIP, no shards is a FAIL). `chrome-shards` then reads the `shard-<n>.json` records exactly as CI's job does, including `--merge` for the end-of-run checks. `--unsharded` runs the suite whole, as before. Default: parallel, because it measured faster here with the same verdicts (numbers below).

**The shard map check.** `shardMapProblems` holds each sharded gate's ids to `ci.yml`'s `shard: [...]` matrix (hand-written, read as text: the independent side, docs/34) and to the map's keys, by name: a shard dropped, doubled, missing from CI, or missing from the map. `lint-doc-gates` drives it as arm 7, and `verify.ts` runs it before anything (so CI's `verify.ts --list` step runs it too). Mutations, each failing both by name: shard 1 dropped from verify's ids (`does not run shard 1, which ci.yml's chrome matrix runs`), shard 2 doubled (`runs shard 2 more than once`), shard 3 renamed in the map, shard 3 dropped from CI's matrix (`runs shard 3, which ci.yml's chrome matrix does not run`), the `shards` field removed (`no gate in GATES is sharded`). `combineShards` with FAIL and SKIP swapped fails its self-check by name.

**#3183, raised rather than split.** `plugin-test`'s healthy runs: 440 s (the shared machine), 708 s (this container, inside verify), 810 s (an author's machine), 1211–1292 s alone on two review machines. The 1200 s default timed healthy runs out. `timeoutS: 3500` is 2.7× the slowest, the margin point 5 already uses. Splitting would need new CI steps; CI's own step is unchanged. A self-check holds the limit above the literal 1292 s, and dropping `timeoutS` fails it by name.

**Review.** `.claude/commands/review-pr.md` and a new CONTRIBUTING §3 subsection: the reviewer relies on CI (every check green on the exact head, `gates` success) for the full list, runs locally on the PR merged with current main the gates the change touches plus its own mutations, and runs the full verify only when the merged tree differs from the head in files the change touches. Its independence now comes from mutations and reading (docs/34): a second identical run compares what CI compared. Authors still run the whole list (CLAUDE.md §4, unchanged).

**Measured, same base tree, this container (4 CPUs, 15 GB), `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3` before, none after:** before, the whole list in 3729 s wall with `chrome` 1755 s unsharded; after, 2705 s wall (−27%) with `chrome` 709 s as three shards side by side (666 s, 589 s, 709 s), every shard PASS, load average about 4.3 at its peak. `plugin-test` took 708 s and 727 s in the two runs. ## (2026-10-31) — Capture baseline and Adopt read the file once, a page per turn (#3189)

**Status:** plugin and panel. ENGINE patch (change note): no committed artifact, emission or component surface moves. The
component executor is unchanged, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at 44 (`lint-executor-revision` agrees). The strip shows an
agent's run (Q3210.1 A), in copy the owner approved as worded (Q3210.2 A), listed below.

### What it does

- **One read per run.** `captureBaselines` and `adoptMembers` (`update-plan.ts`) now read through `runHost(file, breathe)`,
  as `previewUpdate` does since #3177: every page loaded and searched a page per turn, once per criterion of
  `UPDATE_READ`, then shared by every set. Before, `main.ts` loaded every page (`loadPagesYielding`) and handed `figma`
  straight in, so `hostPorts` and then `locateSets`/`locateView` per target each searched the whole file in one turn.
  Both commands write plugin data only, which adds no node, so neither needs `rereadAfter`.
- **Readings.** Each posts `run-progress` with its own `run` (`capture`, `adopt`): `check` before the read, `work` as each
  def is reached (`done` counting the defs before it, the thread handed back after it), `finish` with every def done.
  Both are agent commands (the panel starts neither), so `main.ts` posts the readings to the panel directly, never
  through the agent's sink, which would take each one for a verdict.
- **The strip.** `stripView` takes an agent's reading (`StripAgent`) and draws it as the read after open is drawn: the
  passive kind, no Stop (the panel holds no run of its own to stop) and no clock. A panel run wins over it; it wins over
  the read after open. It clears when the agent's command ends (`agent-finished`): `agentHeard` in
  `state/status-strip.ts` holds both the set and the clear, so `test-status-strip.ts` reaches it (the #3210 review's M-C).
- **On Figma's host.** Both commands now read through `runHost` → `withRoot`, which since #3214 is a facade, not a
  `Proxy` (#3209). A `Proxy` over `figma` throws on Figma's fixed methods; on main before this PR neither command went
  through it, so the new arms hold that they still run on a host whose methods are fixed.

### Measured on the stand-in (`test-open-large-file.ts`, 60 pages, 50 sets, every def)

| | whole-file searches | most pages searched in one turn | each page searched | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capture, before | 61 | 60 | 61 times | ~20 s |
| Capture, after | 0 | 1 | 3 times | ~2.9 s |
| Adopt, before | 58 | 60 | 58 times | ~19 s |
| Adopt, after | 0 | 1 | 3 times | ~2.9 s |

The answer and the verdict digest the same before and after (capture `48e8f46b` / `ea8490a8`, adopt `137c86a5` /
`488854b1`).

### Strip copy (`STRIP_COPY`, approved as worded, Q3210.2 A)

- `agentRun.capture`: "Recording the sets as built…" and `agentRun.adopt`: "Adopting members…". These are the words
  Activity already gives the two commands (Q114 A), reused for the strip.
- `agentSub`: "An agent runs this. Details in Activity." (new).
- The count reuses `of`: "16 of 60", counting defs.

### Gates

`test-open-large-file.ts`: `capture/no-walk`, `capture/one-read`, `capture/answers`, `capture/progress` and the same four
for `adopt/`, then `capture/fixed` and `adopt/fixed`: both again through `ACTIONS`, over a `figma` and a root whose methods
are fixed (`fixHostMethods`), each giving the plain host's answer. `withRoot` put back as a `Proxy` fails both by name. A no-walk arm needs an answer first: a run that threw searched nothing, and must not pass for one that
searched no whole file. `test-status-strip.ts`: `agent/check`, `agent/work`, `agent/finish`, `order/agent`,
`order/agent-run`, `agent/none`, `agent/heard`, `agent/kept`, `agent/cleared` (the clear on `agent-finished` dropped

## (2026-10-31) — Usage panels: no example narrower than its component declares (#3205)

The owner found Dialog's Anatomy example about 60px wide in the template file, its title, supporting text and content
one letter per line and the callouts running down the column.

- **The cause.** The Specimen block's placeholder is a Badge, which hugs, and the swap keeps that hug. #3029 fixed
  Banner by reading the member's own sizing: a member that reads FIXED gets a fixed specimen at its width, one that reads
  HUG hugs. That makes the specimen's width depend on one read of the member. If the read says HUG, or anything sets
  the instance back to hug, a member built at a width lays out at its narrowest. Dialog's is about 40px in the test
  host and about 60px in the file: the close button plus a letter. **Not reproduced from a real file.** Both test hosts
  read Dialog's members as FIXED and draw 560. The test host shows the symptom only when the specimen hugs, and the
  owner's 60px matches that, so the hug is inferred. Why the file's specimen hugged is not established. One lead:
  Banner carries a bound `min-width` that every instance inherits, and Dialog has no floor, so a hugging Banner
  specimen would not have collapsed and a hugging Dialog one would.
- **One rule (`exampleFloor`), read off the def, never off the member's reported sizing.** A def that builds its root
  at a width (`placementWidth`, `builtSize` naming the member's value, or `center` naming it) gets a fixed specimen at its member's width,
  plus that width as the specimen's `minWidth`, so a later reset to hug cannot collapse it. A def with a literal root
  `minWidth` gets that floor on a hugging specimen. Any other member is handled as before.
- **The audit**, every lead's panel in the test host with the specimen left hugging (the collapse): 19 defs have an
  example under the width their def builds at, 81 examples in all. Each one is a def that builds its root at a width:
  the fields, Field label, Field message, Textarea, rows, Select, Accordion, List, Segmented control, Dialog, Toast,
  Pagination's built-width member, Progress, Banner and Slider. The table is in the PR. With the rule, none collapses.
- **The gate** (`test-doc-panel.ts`): `collapse/<def>` for every lead fails by name when an example is narrower than
  its member's built width or literal floor, or a wrapping text box is narrower than 4em and does not hold its text on
  one line. The oracle reads the projection's own root (`placementWidth`, `minWidth`), kept on each member when the
  test host builds it, never the panel. `collapse/hug read`: Dialog's members read as hugging, and the examples are
  still 560. `update/redraw in place`: a Dialog panel the executor built, aged to the earlier format with its examples
  collapsed, is due, and one Update redraws it where it was, not kept as "(edited)". The test host now applies
  `minWidth` as Figma does and copies a main's floor onto its instances. `collapse/after reset` (review X1): every lead
  built at a width is drawn, then every specimen is set back to hug, as a host reset would, and no example may fall
  under its width. Only the specimen's `minWidth` holds it. On its first run it found Pagination's simple member,
  built at 428 through `center` (#2518), which the rule had missed: the member got a fixed specimen only because it
  read FIXED, and no floor. The rule now reads `center` too.
- **Mutations**, each failing by name: the specimen left hugging → `collapse/dialog` (40px against 560) and 18 other
  `collapse/<def>`, plus `width/banner`, `width/checkbox-row`, `collapse/hug read`, `update/redraw in place`; the rule
  dropped (back to the reported sizing) → `collapse/hug read`; `PANEL_FORMAT` not raised → `update/redraw in place`;
  the specimen's `minWidth` never set → `collapse/after reset`.
- `PANEL_FORMAT` goes to 5, so every drawn panel redraws once on the next Update. An unedited panel is replaced in
  place, and an edited one is kept as "(edited)", as before.
- Not in scope: whether the template file holds every component and its usage guide. The owner checks that in the file.

## (2026-10-31) — Update check and apply: no Proxy over the Figma host (#3209)

On real Figma, built from `dcbeaf76`, every Update check threw `'get' on proxy: property 'getLocalTextStylesAsync' is a
read-only and non-configurable data property on the proxy target but the proxy did not return its actual value`, so
Update file applied Theme and left every ticked set Due.

- **Root cause.** #3177's read-once run wrapped the host in a `Proxy` (`withRoot`, and `readRun`'s root) whose `get`
  trap returned `v.bind(t)` for every method. The substitute was not the trigger: the bind was. On Figma the host's
  methods are own data properties, neither writable nor configurable, and a `Proxy` must return such a property's own
  value. The shim's host was a plain object, so every test passed.
- **Fix.** `src/host-facade.ts`: a plain object with a getter per host member (bound to the host) and the overrides as
  own values. A member the host does not list falls through to the facade's prototype, a `Proxy` over an empty object,
  which no invariant can bind. `withRoot`, `readRun`'s root and `componentFigma` (`mcp-steps.ts`, the agent paste path,
  same exposure) now use it. `doc-panel.ts`'s `printView` already proxies an empty object and is left alone.
- **Test.** `fixHostMethods` in `component-shim.ts` fixes a copy's methods as Figma does. `test-update-apply.ts`
  `fixed/…` runs a check and an apply over a fixed host and executor (on `main`: the exact error, by name);
  `test-mcp-paste.ts` `components/fixed` does the same for `componentFigma`. Mutations: `withRoot`, `readRun`'s root
  or `componentFigma` put back as a `Proxy` each fail by name.
- **Trap.** Opt-in: many suites patch a shim method after building it, so `fixHostMethods` runs on a suite's own copy.
  Whether Figma's node objects (the root) also fix their methods is not known; the test fixes the root too, the
  stricter assumption, and the facade holds either way. #3208 (the Apply Theme freeze) is a separate cause.
