## (2026-10-31) — Chrome motion: the drawer, menus, dialogs, fold-outs and the reduced path (#3150 part 2, Q3150.1–11 A)

**Status:** studio and plugin chrome, from one stylesheet. ENGINE patch (change note): no token, emitted tree or component
surface moves, so CONTRACT is unchanged. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. Part 1, the brand library's
animation styles (#2857), waits on the owner's three in-app checks.

### What changed

- **Five motion variables** in `chrome/spec.mjs` (PRODUCT_VARS), from Prism3's default theme, never the edited brand:
  `motion-panel` (`motion.duration.normal`, 200ms), `motion-fast` (`motion.duration.fast`, 100ms), `motion-reduced`
  (`motion.duration-reduced.fast`, 100ms), `ease-enter` and `ease-exit` (`motion.easing-role.enter` / `.exit`). Their own
  names rather than `dur-fast`, so the spinner's timing and the surfaces' are read apart, and so `test:chrome` can settle
  the surfaces without touching the spinner. `chrome.css` still carries no raw duration.
- **The surfaces** (`chrome.css`, the "chrome motion" section at the end), each by the wireframe's timing:
  - the Activity drawer slides up (a keyframe animation on `data-open`, 200ms in, 100ms out), at 1280 and as the 380
    sheet; the body stays drawn through the exit (`transition-behavior: allow-discrete`); the chevron turns with it;
  - the 380 strip shifts in with the first run; the bar row's unread dot pops in;
  - menus (Theme, Inspect, the brand menu) shift in; tile tooltips fade in and go at once;
  - dialogs (Update file, the start window and its guard) scale in over a fading scrim;
  - the error strip fades in and out, its notices row held through the exit;
  - Update file's rows fade in when the file read lands, and a set's line when its check comes back;
  - fold-out content (Show advanced on Palettes, Type and Elevation; an operation's lines; Earlier results and their
    entries; Draw by table title) fades in a short step down, its height snapping; a collapse is at once.
- **Reduced motion:** the drawer's slide, the chevron's turn and the dialog's scale drop, and every surface crossfades
  on `motion-reduced`. A surface whose exit is a display change keeps it as a fade; one that enters only still goes at once.

### Diagnosis: what made each surface replay, and the fixes

- **Redrawn surfaces replay `@starting-style`.** Update file's dialog, the bar row (its chevron and dot), an operation's
  Earlier results and every lever page are drawn afresh on each repaint, so a plain `@starting-style` replays on every
  tick. Two marks fix it: `data-still` on a repainted Update file scrim (set once a frame has shown the open dialog),
  and `data-enter` (`armEnter` / `enterMark`, `shell/dom.ts`), armed by the toggle or the host answer and held until
  the next frame, because one change often repaints twice in one task. A redraw after that frame (an edit, a run's
  progress, a page change, the sheet opened again) draws the surface unmarked. A first try gated fold-outs on
  `:focus`; it failed because the lever pages restore focus after the redraw has already been styled.
- **The chevron** was a new node each repaint, so it had nothing to transition from; it is now one node for the
  drawer's life, with the row's other parts drawn around it.
- **The Activity tile's dot is not drawn** since Q3113.9 A; "the status dot" is the bar row's unread dot now, so Pop
  lands there.
- **The drawer's slide is a keyframe animation, not a transition,** because a transition would leave a transform on the
  drawer at rest, and the drawer deliberately makes no stacking context (the preview header hangs over it). The closed
  offset is the bar row's own height, so the exit's end is where the closed drawer already sits.

### Held, and gaps filed

- **A surface the shell removes leaves at once:** menus, dialogs and the unread dot. CSS cannot play an exit on a removed
  node; it needs a deferred removal in the shell. Filed as #3207.
- **No Agent popover and no Figma menu exist any more** (T7 and the rail removed them), so Q3150.1's "the Agent popover"
  has no surface. Export is a page since #2909, and the prune review is Update file's Clean tab, so both ride the
  Update file dialog.

### Verification

- `test:chrome` §3150 (shard 3), 193 assertions: DECLARED (every rule in the stylesheet that declares motion, by
  selector and context, against a typed list), LIVE and REDUCED on the plugin at 1280 and 380 and the web at 1280 (the
  page's animation clock slowed through CDP so a 100ms move is read whole, then each surface settled and its end state
  held), and SETTLED.
- Every other section opens its pages with the three motion durations at 0s (`SETTLED_MOTION`), so each surface lands
  on its end state in the frame it changes and nothing measures mid-move.
- `test:verdict`'s #1890 arm read the drawer's place straight after a verdict opened it, which now lands mid-slide; it
  waits for every finite animation to finish first (bounded), so it reads the end state.
- `lint:live-css` passes unchanged: its scope is `styles.css`, and this change adds no rule there. The DECLARED arm is
  what holds the new `chrome.css` rules.

**The plugin.** The executor already draws `literalPaints`, so it needs no change and no `EXECUTOR_REVISION`. The
update verifier's "a paint the plan does not give" check (`update-apply.ts`, #2369) read only bound and gradient
paints, so it reported every styled member's literal ground as unplanned. It now counts a literal fill or stroke as
planned. SignInButton had the same shape, but no update test built it. The plugin build tests read the new axis, and
`wallet build/ground` holds each built member's ground and edge to values typed in the test.

**What the capture found that the proposal did not have.**
- Google Pay draws a 1px inside edge on both styles: #757575 on black and #3c4043 on white. The records carry both.
- The proposal's logo heights were the SDK's logo element boxes. The files carry the ink inside them:
  - Apple 21.5
  - Google 20.9 (in a 22 box)
  - PayPal 16.6 (in a 20 box)
  - Shop Pay 21.1 (in a 22 box)
- Only Apple scales its logo in proportion to the height:
  - Google keeps 22px of padding.
  - PayPal steps its logo per size (18, 20 and 24).
  - Shop Pay's logo is 22 high at every height.

  So at 36 and 56 the decided ratio reads the 44 render, not those SDKs' drawings.
- Google Pay's and Shop Pay's SDKs draw nothing under 40px: a 36 request renders 40. Shop Pay already had no small
  member. The owner took Q3195.3 A, so Google Pay has none either.
- All four SDKs pass the radius through without clamping.

**#3175 is not in this PR.** PayPal's 150 floor needs a per-provider `minWidth`, and today `minWidth` is keyed by size
only, so it is a schema and projector change of its own. It is recorded in the def's `codeOnly` and `contested`.

## (2026-10-31) — Plugin busy states: the status strip, Stop after a set, and the yield cadence (#3170 part 2)

**Status:** plugin and panel, built as the owner decided (Q3170.1–6, all A). Copy is DRAFT under the voice standard. ENGINE
patch (change note): no committed artifact, emission or component surface moves. The component executor is unchanged
(`update-apply.ts`, `apply-theme.ts`, `write-figma.ts` and `main.ts` are outside its reach), so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What it does

- **A status strip at the panel's foot** (`shell/status-strip.ts`, first in the Activity drawer, above its bar row). It
  reads the read after open ("Reading this file…", indeterminate until the first page, then "page n of N") and Update
  file's run: the set or stage, n of N, a native `progress` filled by sets (or stages) done, never by time, and the
  elapsed time from the panel's own clock. After 3 s with no reading it adds "Still working on <set>". When the run ends
  it becomes the verdict line, which stays until the next action the panel starts.
- **Update file's rows** read Due, then Updating, then Updated, in the overlay's run view.
- **Every writing control is off while the run is out**, with "Update is running" on hover: Components' boxes and tier
  actions, Documentation's switches and Draw specs, the Style guides tab, and Clean up's Delete and Remove. It rides the
  one reason the panel already used after a failed restore (`writeOff`), so a new control has one place to read.
- **"Stop after <set>"** posts `update-stop`. The host reads it at the next set boundary (and before the first write, during
  the check), so the set being written finishes and the rest are not touched. The verdict names the sets it left.
- **The yield cadence.** The update posts `run-progress` and hands the thread back at every set boundary, and inside a
  set after about 50 ms of work: the executor is asked after every member (`chunk: 1`) and `paced` hands back only once
  50 ms has run, repeating the set's reading. Apply Theme hands back before each of its seven stages and every 200
  color variables (`COLOR_YIELD_EVERY`). An agent's run yields the same way and posts nothing.

### Honesty, and what #3177 still costs

The strip says only what a post told it. While the update checks the file before its first write it reads "Checking n
sets before writing", with no count and no fill: that check still runs whole-file searches in one turn (#3177), so the
strip claims nothing more until the first set boundary. Inside one member a write cannot be split, so "about 50 ms" is
50 ms or one member's write, whichever is longer.

### Decisions taken inside the arc

- The overlay still closes when the run starts (#2909's behavior); the rows' states show when it is reopened, so the
  panel stays readable and navigable (Q3170.3 A).
- A Stop during Apply Theme stops after the whole Theme step, never between its stages: a theme half written is not one
  the file can use. Its label says "Stop after Theme".
- The indeterminate bar draws no motion: what moves is what the run said.

### Tests

- `apps/plugin/test-run-progress.ts` (new, in the plugin's `test`): through the real `main.ts` over the component shim,
  the check reading (posted before the run's first page read, `progress/check-first`), one reading per set boundary, the finish reading, the readings inside a long set under a stepped
  clock and none under a still one, no reading for an agent's run, Stop at a boundary (the next sets' stamps and records
  untouched), Stop before the first write (no version saved), and a stray Stop stopping nothing. Over the file shim:
  Apply Theme's seven stages in order, one hand-back per 200 color rows, and a paced apply writing exactly what an
  unpaced one does.
- `apps/plugin/test-open-large-file.ts`: `open/read-progress`, page 0 to 60 of 60 once each before the full read.
- `apps/studio/test-status-strip.ts` (new): the strip's words and rules.
- `test:chrome` section 3170 (shard 3): every state as drawn, light and dark at 1280 and light at 380, the controls held
  and released, and the chrome audit in the reading and running states.
- 21 mutations, each failing by name (listed in the PR).

## (2026-10-31) — Docs guides: each guide's markdown drawn as a page at serve time and at site build (#3176, PR 2 of 3)

**Status:** new `apps/studio/docs-markdown.mjs` and `docs/public/guides/_page.html`; `docs-route.mjs` and
`build-site.mjs` draw `guides/<name>.html`; guide styles in `docs/public/docs.css`; new arms in `test-docs-route.ts`.
No engine change, no committed artifact (so `regen --check`'s count holds), no change note. Owner decisions
Q3176.3, Q3176.4 and Q3176.5, all A.

### What changed

- **A guide opens as a page.** Before, `/docs/guides/<name>.md` opened as markdown source, with every `src:` citation
  showing and links pointing at other `.md` files. Now `guides/<name>.html` is drawn from `guides/<name>.md`: by
  `serveDocs` on request in dev, and written by `build-site.mjs` for the deploy, through the same `renderGuide`.
  The `.md` files are unchanged and stay canonical: agents, `llms.txt` and GitHub read them. Each page links its
  source.
- **The renderer covers the guides' subset and nothing more** (about 130 lines, no dependency): headings, paragraphs, `-`
  and `1.` lists, tables, bold, italic, code, links (a `name.md` link becomes `name.html`; anchors are GitHub's
  slugs, so `#fragment` links keep working). HTML comments are dropped: the citations stay in the source.
  - `> text` is a message the plugin shows, labeled "Plugin message" (Q3176.4 A: no callout syntax yet).
  - `*[Screenshot placeholder: …]*` is a dashed frame with its caption until the image lands (Q3176.5 A).
- **Every string a page adds lives in `_page.html`:** its slots, and `<!-- part:name -->` fragments for the pager,
  breadcrumb, frame and message, which the renderer cuts out and fills. So `lint-us-english` and `lint-voice`, which
  walk `docs/public/`, scan all of it. A `_`-named file is neither served nor copied by the site build.
- **The page:** the guide list in `index.md`'s order (folded into "All guides" under 760px), the article at 68
  characters a line, "On this page" from the `##` headings (hidden under 1180px), Previous and Next in index order.
  The landing page's guide links move from `.md` to `.html`. `lint-ecosystem.ts`'s DOCS arm now reads `_page.html`
  too, and the new styles draw no pair it doesn't check: table heads sit on `--bg`, frames and messages on `--surface`.

### A trap the mutations found

The first renderer's paragraph branch could take zero lines. A `|` row with no separator under it matched no branch
and stopped the paragraph at once, so the loop never advanced: the "table branch removed" mutation hung the test
instead of failing it. A paragraph now always takes its first line. The `<!--` check was also too weak: a comment the
renderer kept came out escaped, as text, which a check of the raw HTML for `<!--` can't see; the visible-text pattern
now includes it.

### The arms (`test-docs-route.ts`), and the mutations each fails by name

The oracle is the `.md` files on disk, listed and parsed with the test's own patterns, never the renderer's.

| Mutation | Fails as |
|---|---|
| the table branch removed from `renderMarkdown` | `guides/<name>.html has no markdown left in its text`, for every guide with a table |
| HTML comments kept in the source lines | the same line, for every guide |
| `.md` links no longer rewritten | `every link on guides/<name>.html resolves` |
| the nav reversed | `guides/<name>.html's nav lists the guides in index.md's order` |
| the site build writing other bytes | `public/docs/guides/<name>.html is what GET /docs/guides/<name>.html answers, byte for byte` |

| the `_` guard removed from `docsPath` | `GET /docs/guides/_page.html is refused: the template is not a page` |
| the part pattern without `-` (empty breadcrumb) | `guides/<name>.html's breadcrumb names the page` |
| the bold pass back to a lazy `\*\*(.+?)\*\*` | `guides/build-components.html's article tags nest well formed` |
| single-`*` italics left as stars | `guides/<name>.html converts every *italic* span: no * left in its text`, for the 4 guides that use them |
| numbered lists drawn as `<ul>` | `guides/<name>.html draws its N numbered step(s) in an <ol>` |

## (2026-10-31) — Single-component blocks are placed clear of the page, and Update extends them in place (#3192)

**Status:** `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts` (the `emitAsComponents` branch of `applyComponentPlan`),
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` 43 → 44 with its `executor-reach.json` entry, two test arms. Patch change note; no emission,
token or contract change.

### The fault

The emit branch placed a fresh build's grid at `x = (i % cols) * pitchX`, `y = floor(i / cols) * pitchY`, from the
page origin, and an Update that added a member scanned that same origin-anchored grid with a column count taken from
the fresh members alone (one, in an Update that adds one). Neither read the rest of the page. Since #3148 put `icon`
and `provider-logo` on one page, a second block landed on the first, and in the reference brand's master the added
`provider-logo/provider/facebook-blue` sat at 0,0 on `icon/arrow-down` while its siblings were at y=144, x=2128.

### The rule chosen

Taken from how each case already lays out, with no new layout:

- **Fresh block** (the def has no component on the page): the same square grid at the measured pitch (#3134), its
  origin from the rule `relocateSets` (`page-moves.ts`) already uses to put a single-component block on a shared page:
  `SET_GAP` right of everything on the page, header included, level with the top set or component. Empty page: the
  origin, as before. `placeNewSet` was tried first and dropped: under a header it scans the row below the header,
  so a block can land under a wide page header, and the block header #3172 then draws above it would sit on the
  page's own.
- **Existing block**: it stays. A new component goes one pitch right of the last component in the row holding its
  kind's last member; if that spot is taken, or the def's names carry no kind (`icon/arrow-down`), it takes the first
  free slot of the block's own grid, anchored at the block's top-left with the block's own column count. Free means the
  component widened by the 24px gap meets no page node.

The page is read after the build loop with this run's components left out.

### Reach

The reach gate measured ten sets beyond the two named in the issue: banner, breadcrumb-item, breadcrumbs,
card-number-field, code-input, counter, dialog, pagination, slider, toast. Each one's fresh arm prebuilds its
dependencies (icon, spinner, and the rest) onto the one shim page. Their blocks no longer overlap, so the set
the build then places beside them moves right. Only the top-level `x` differs (diffed per set), and the update arms read
the same. The gate requires them, so entry 44 names all twelve. The cost is one re-apply with no field difference.

| Mutation | Fails as |
|---|---|
| fresh block's placement dropped (`fromPage` false) | `#3192 fresh build` (33 overlaps) |
| `write-components.ts` as on main | `#3192 fresh build` and `#3192 update add` (at 0,0, over icon/arrow-down) |
| kind step off, block grid read from the page origin | `#3192 update add` (outside its block) |

## (2026-10-31) — Desktop bridge: a reconnect mid-run no longer loses the result (#2497)

**Status:** transport only: `apps/plugin/src/agent-bridge-relay.ts`, `tools/figma-bridge/server.ts`, the gate
`apps/plugin/test-agent-bridge.ts`, the bridge README. ENGINE patch (change note). CONTRACT unchanged.
`AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 1. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. Phase 1 of #3147 depends on
this (owner decisions on #3147, 2026-10-30, build order step 2).

### What changed

- **Relay (plugin side).** The commands it delivered survive a lost socket; only switching the link off forgets
  them. It keeps the last 8 results by command id, even ones it sent, because a socket can read OPEN and still be
  dead. On every connect its `hello` carries `held` (ids running or kept) and it re-sends every kept result.
- **Server.** A disconnect no longer fails the call in flight. The call waits `--grace-ms` (default 120000) for the
  plugin to return; `figma_status.awaitingReconnect` lists the ids. At the new connection's `hello`, a held id is
  adopted and an unheld one fails with the reason (it never arrived, or the plugin reloaded). A result resolves its
  call once, by id; a repeat is logged as `a repeated result, already delivered: ignored`. Commands are never
  re-sent, so nothing runs twice.
- **Why the protocol stays at 1:** the command and result envelopes are unchanged. The only wire addition is the
  optional `held` on the relay's `hello`, a server↔relay message outside the envelope. An older relay sends no
  `held`, and the server then fails the orphaned call at the hello, as it did before.

### Gate

`test-agent-bridge.ts` gains `resend/hand` (hand-rolled client: drop without a close frame, reconnect holding the id,
the result sent twice → the MCP call answered once, the command not re-sent, the repeat logged) and `resend/e2e`
(the real relay and the real `main.ts`: a `run-code` that waits 800 ms, the socket dropped at once and kept down until
the main thread has answered → the result arrives after reconnect, exactly one MCP reply, one run). The server now
runs with `--grace-ms 3000` in the test, and `disconnect` asserts the failure names the grace.

Mutations, each failing by name:
- relay re-send removed → `resend/e2e: the result arrives after the reconnect` (timeout);
- relay forgets its commands on a lost socket (the old `mine.clear()`) → the same arm (fails at the hello);
- server ignores `held` → `resend/hand: the re-sent result is the call's answer`, `… logged as a repeat`, and `resend/e2e`.

### Not verified live

The trigger in #2497 (the iframe missing the socket while the main thread is busy) is still not reproduced against
Figma desktop. A drop longer than the grace still fails the call; the plugin's link record keeps the headline.

## (2026-10-31) — Provider logos: their own section header on Icons & assets, moved by Update from Brand marks (#3172)

**What.** Owner decisions Q3172.1–3, all A. Icons & assets now carries two Size=Medium `_Section-header`s: the icons'
(the page's lead header, as before) and "Provider logos", 80px over the logo block. Build draws it. On a file built
when the logos had their own page, Update and Set up file move that page's header with the marks (the same node and
id), rewrite its Title while it reads the placeholder or the old name ("Brand mark", "Brand marks") and its Description
while it reads the placeholder, keep any other text a designer typed, and report `Brand marks` as safe to delete. It is
never deleted. A second Update does nothing, and the header is the one a fresh build draws.

**How.** `TaxonomyLeaf.blockHeaders` names a non-lead def with a header of its own and its title (the plural title is
the owner's call, Q3172.2 A, so it is data, not `displayName`). A block's header is tagged with its def (`headerFor`
in the `prism3` namespace). That tag is how a rebuild finds it, and how the page's own header tells it apart: the
lead's present-check and first measure skip tagged headers and the block's components. `blockHeadersDue` is read by
the Update dry run (in the hash, listed, counted as work, with a named version), and `placeBlockHeaders` runs right
after `relocateSets`, so the header is placed over the block where the move left it. It runs whether or not a set moved
this run, which is what fixes the owner's file: an Update before this change moved the marks and left the header
behind, so no move is due now, but the header still is.

**Why a header moves only when it would be the last thing left.** A former page that still holds anything a designer
put there keeps its header, and the block gets a new one. Moving it would strip their page of its title.

**Held for the owner.** All wording is DRAFT: the "Provider logos header: moved from Brand marks to Icons & assets."
line, the "Would place 1 section header" / "✓ 1 section header placed" headlines, and " Section headers placed." in the
version description. The Description is rewritten only while it reads the placeholder. An older Prism3 summary
("…sign-in, wallet, card and social…") is kept as if a designer typed it, because nothing marks which text Prism3 wrote.

**Found, filed separately.** A fresh build of a single-component def lays its grid out from the page origin, so a
provider-logo build onto a page that already holds the icons draws over them. That's the executor's placement, so it's
out of scope here and filed as #3192.

## (2026-10-31) — The Update check and apply read the file once, a page per turn (#3177)

**Status:** plugin read layer only. ENGINE patch (change note). CONTRACT unchanged. The executor's code is unchanged
(`update-plan.ts`, `update-apply.ts` and the new `run-read.ts` are outside `write-components.ts`' reach), so
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. Built on #3181 (#3170 part 1), which must merge first.

### Why Update locked the panel

#3181 took the whole-file searches off plugin open. The Update check (`previewUpdate`) and apply (`applyUpdate`) still
searched the whole file several times per set, each search in one turn of the main thread: `hostPorts`, `locateSets` and
`fileBlockers` in the dry run, `findDocBlock` for the usage panels, and in the apply `liveFor`, the executor's own
lookups, the verify and the furniture. And nothing yielded between sets, so on a large file the check was one turn.

Measured on `test-open-large-file.ts`'s stand-in (60 pages, 50 sets; 20 ms a page load, 5 ms a page search), an Update
check and apply over every set, as after a theme change:

| | check before | check after | apply before | apply after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole-file searches | 102 | **0** | 354 | **0** |
| Most pages searched in one turn | 6 120 | **1** | 21 240 | **1** |
| Times each page is searched | 102 | **3** | 354 | **3–6** |
| Longest stall of the event loop | 30 823 ms | **558 ms** | 106 588 ms | **484 ms** |
| Total time | 32 603 ms | **3 031 ms** | 108 275 ms | **3 944 ms** |

The answers are the same before and after, digested whole: check `ec208d1a` (previewHash `54ce985f`), apply `d8a3e491`.
The stand-in's sets have no variables, so its apply refuses each set at the preflight and writes no member. The writes
are #3170 part 2's lane. The stall left is not a search: no turn searches more than one page (5 ms here).

### The change

- **`run-read.ts`:** `readRun` loads each page in a turn of its own, then searches it once per criterion, each search
  in a turn of its own. The root it returns stands in for the file's. Its pages, plugin data and every other member are
  the file's own. Only `findAllWithCriteria` is answered from the read, filtered live: a node renamed reads under its
  new name, one removed is left out, pages reordered answer in their new order, and a page made during the run is
  searched when first asked for. A search it does not cover goes to the file. `rereadAfter` searches again the pages
  that nodes sit on, or every page.
- **`update-plan.ts`:** `UPDATE_READ` names what a run searches for: components and sets, the canvas furniture by its tag,
  and the usage panels by theirs. `runHost` wraps a host in one read. `previewUpdate` reads through it, unless its host
  already reads a run's.
- **`update-apply.ts`:** `applyUpdate` reads once, and its dry run shares the read. The executor's port shares it too,
  when it is the same file (as `figma` is both in the plugin). The page a set sits on is read again after its write, and
  again after its furniture is drawn. The whole file is read again after #2989's move between pages: without that, a set
  moved to a page the run made answers twice, and `furnishUpdate` skips a set it finds twice.
- **`main.ts` (shared with the part-2 lane):** `checkSets` and `updateComponents` drop their `loadPagesYielding()` (the
  read loads the pages). The furniture and the usage panel draw through the run's host, so `panelFor` takes an `api`
  that defaults to `figma`.

The check and the apply each read once. They do not share a read: the file can change between the check and the
confirm, and the apply's hash check needs the file as it is when the confirm runs.

### Gates

- `test-open-large-file.ts`: `update/check-no-walk`, `update/apply-no-walk`, `update/search-yields`, `update/one-read`
  and `update/answers`. On #3181's head the first four fail.
- New `test-run-read.ts` (in the plugin's `test`):
  - the read against the whole-file search as the oracle (`run/*`);
  - an apply that writes, on a set the executor built, with one object as host and executor, against a twin read by
    whole-file search (`apply/same`, `apply/no-walk`, `apply/reread`, `apply/moved`).
- The update fixtures pass unchanged: `test-update-apply.ts` (815 assertions), `test-update-components.ts`,
  `test-update-fresh.ts` and `test-apply-summary.ts`. `previewUpdate` and `applyUpdate` read through the run's root
  themselves, so every fixture runs on it.

Each mutation was made on a committed `wip:` tree and failed by name:

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| dry run without the run's read | `entry/check`, `update/one-read`, `update/answers`, `apply/no-walk`, `apply/reread` |
| executor handed the file's root | `apply/no-walk` |
| apply without the run's read | `update/apply-no-walk`, `update/search-yields`, `update/one-read`, `apply/no-walk`, `apply/reread` |
| a page's criteria searched in one turn | `update/search-yields` |
| the apply's dry run reading again | `update/one-read`, `apply/reread` |
| `rereadAfter` doing nothing | `run/reread`, `run/order`, `run/new-page`, `apply/reread` |
| no re-read after a set's write | `apply/reread` |
| no re-read after its furniture | `apply/reread` |
| no re-read after a move between pages | `apply/moved` |
| furniture drawn on `figma` | `update/apply-no-walk`, `update/search-yields`, `update/one-read` |
| removed nodes kept | `run/live` |

### Not in this change

- Capture baseline and Adopt still load every page and then search the whole file per set (`captureBaselines`,
  `adoptMembers`). Filed as #3189.
- The executor's `findAll` by name runs on its failure path only (a nest or swap target it cannot find), and still
  searches the whole file.
- Nothing was run in Figma. One page's search cannot be split, so a very dense page still holds one turn for its search.

## (2026-10-31) — Plugin open searches the file a page per turn, and paints before any read (#3170 part 1)

**Status:** plugin main thread only. ENGINE patch (change note). CONTRACT unchanged. The executor is unchanged
(`main.ts` is outside `write-components.ts`' reach), so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### Why #3111 did not end the hang

#3111 took the page loads off the path to the panel's first answer and spread them one per turn. The stand-in it added
priced a page load and nothing else, and its search of the whole file cost nothing. In Figma, a document-wide
`findAllWithCriteria` walks every node of every loaded page inside one turn, and the open path still ran it:
- once per read in `presentNames`, and again in `isSetUp` for the read after open;
- **once per set in the hand-edit pass** (`handEditsOf` → `locateSets`), about 50 times on the 60-page stand-in;
- in a second read beside the first: the badge's live recount (#3096) asks about 250 ms after the ledger's answer, before
  the read after open has filled `presentCache`, so `fileDue` started a full read of its own.

The hand-edit pass also projected every present set's plans in one turn (`updateTargets(present)`), about 0.5 s in Node.

The stand-in now prices a page search too (`SEARCH_MS` a page, so a whole-file search is that times 60, in one turn), and
the panel's live recount arrives at open as the studio sends it. At 330 ms a page load and 20 ms a page search:

| | before (`main`) | after |
|---|---|---|
| Panel's first answer | 411 ms, 0 pages loaded | 416 ms, 0 pages loaded |
| Whole-file searches, open to the pass's end | 57 | **0** |
| Most pages searched in one turn | 120 (2 400 ms held) | **1 (20 ms held)** |
| Longest stall of the event loop | 3 612 ms | **338 ms** (one page load) |
| Hand-edit pass done | 89 397 ms | **23 459 ms** |

Before, the thread was handed back, but each turn after the full read held it for 1.2 s or more for about a minute, so
the file and the panel read as hung.

### The change (`apps/plugin/src/main.ts`)

- **`searchPagesYielding`:** each page is loaded, then searched, in a turn of its own. The readers that took a root
  (`presentNames`, `isSetUp`, the hand-edit pass's `locateSets`) get `rootOver(nodes)`, a root that answers from that
  one read. A host whose pages cannot be searched one at a time (a Node shim) is searched in one go, as before.
- **`readPresent`, one read at a time:** a caller that asks while a read is going shares it. That covers the badge's
  recount, the checklist's request and Style guides' catalog. A write starting or ending drops the read in flight, and
  a read begun before a write does not leave its answer as `presentCache` (`presentGen`).
- **The hand-edit pass** finds each set in that read and projects one set's plans per turn.
- **`ui-ready` paints first:** its own turn posts only the root reads (the brand, the link state and the settings).
  The variable read-back, the font list and the ledger's answer then each start in a turn of their own.
- **Style guides' catalog** reads `isSetUp` from the same paged read.

### Gates (`apps/plugin/test-open-large-file.ts`)

New arms:
- `open/paint-first`: the turn that answers `ui-ready` loads, searches and projects nothing.
- `open/no-walk`: no whole-file search runs from open to the pass's end, the live recounts included.
- `open/search-yields`: no turn searches more than one page.
- `open/one-read`: each page is searched at most twice (the read after open and the pass).
- `open/plans`: the pass projects one set per turn.

Mutations, each run on a committed `wip:` tree, each failing by name:
- the reads moved back into the `ui-ready` turn → `open/paint-first`;
- `readPresent` back on one whole-file search → `open/no-walk`, `open/search-yields`;
- the pass searching `figma` again → `open/no-walk` (50 searches);
- no shared read → `open/one-read`;
- every set projected in one turn → `open/plans`;
- `isSetUp(figma.root)` in `fileSets` or in Style guides' catalog → `open/no-walk`.

On `main`'s `main.ts`, all five arms fail.

Two other suites' hosts changed, and neither of their arms was loosened:
- `test-style-guide-page.ts`: the cell sets now sit on the first page, as in a Figma file, and the catalog arms release
  the turns the catalog's paged read hands back.
- `test-agent-link.ts`: a 0 ms timer runs on its own turn. Only the poll loop's timers (1 000 ms) are held, so
  `ui-ready`'s reads can start.

### Not measured, and left open

- Nothing was run in Figma. A page's search cost there depends on its node count, and one page's search cannot be
  split, so a page of tens of thousands of nodes still holds one turn for its whole search.
- The first projection of a session costs about 180 ms in Node (module warm-up). It is the longest turn left before
  the first answer.
- The variable read-back and the font list are async host calls. The shim cannot price them.
- The Update check (`previewUpdate`) still searches the whole file several times per set (`locateSets`,
  `fileBlockers`, `hostPorts`, `findDocBlock`). That is the Update half of #3170, filed as #3177.

## (2026-10-31) — Docs landing page: restyled, eight guides listed, a gated shared stylesheet (#3176, PR 1 of 3)

**Status:** `docs/public/index.html` restyled, new `docs/public/docs.css` and `docs/public/docs.js`, a DOCS arm in
`lint-ecosystem.ts`. No engine behavior, emission or contract change, so no change note. Owner decisions Q3176.1–9,
all A (2026-10-30); this is Q3176.9's first PR.

### What changed

- **The landing page** (Q3176.6 A) lists the eight guides inline, in `guides/index.md`'s order and with its own copy,
  so a task is one click from `/docs/` instead of two. Feature reference moves up beside the Ecosystem map and the
  Agent reference, and Release notes and Reports get their first links: both pages existed with nothing pointing at
  them. Their lines are each page's own first sentence (the Reports line drops the component count, which moves).
  The guide links still open the `.md` files; PR 2 renders them as pages and moves the links to `.html`.
- **A shared header** with an Auto · Light · Dark switch. Auto follows `prefers-color-scheme`; Light and Dark pin a
  theme in `localStorage` (`p3-docs-theme`). `docs.js` loads in `<head>` without `defer`, so a pinned theme is set
  before the first paint. The guide pages reuse both files in PR 2.
- **`docs.css` holds every style** the landing page draws. The page carries none of its own.

### The DOCS arm, and why the old comment was not enough

The landing page's header comment said it "uses the same values for the same roles and adds no pair of its own".
Nothing checked that. The DOCS arm does, against the ecosystem page, whose values the CONTRAST arm already checks:

- each token in each of `docs.css`'s three `:root` blocks equals the ecosystem page's value in the same block, its two
  dark blocks match, and every `var(--…)` it reads is one it defines;
- every text-on-ground pair it draws is in `PAIRS`. A rule that sets `color` and `background` together draws that
  pair; every other ink may land on every ground set without an `--on-*` ink beside it, so the arm counts each of
  those pairs as drawn. That is conservative on purpose: CSS inheritance can't be resolved without a browser, and the
  over-count costs nothing while the landing page draws seven pairs;
- no color is a literal, and each page in `DOCS_PAGES` loads `docs.css` and carries no `<style>` or `style=`.

It is an arm, not a gate, so `ci.yml`, `verify.ts`, CONTRIBUTING §3, CLAUDE.md and the PR template don't move.

| Mutation | Fails as |
|---|---|
| `--text-muted` in the light block → `#6a707a` | `DOCS: light: --text-muted is #6a707a in docs/public/docs.css, #545a65 on the ecosystem page` |
| `--bg` in the toggle's dark block only → `#101115` | `DOCS: the two dark blocks in docs/public/docs.css differ …` |
| a rule drawing `--link` on `--surface-raised` | `DOCS: docs/public/docs.css draws --link on --surface-raised, a pair the CONTRAST arm does not check` |
| a `<style>` added to `index.html` | `DOCS: docs/public/index.html carries a style of its own …` |
| a literal `color: #777777` | `DOCS: '.z' sets a color as '#777777' — use a token …` |
| a token the ecosystem page lacks | `DOCS: light: --brand in docs/public/docs.css is not an ecosystem page token` |
| the `docs.css` link removed | `DOCS: docs/public/index.html does not load docs.css` |

### Next

PR 2 renders the guides (Q3176.3 A). PR 3, the report form, waits for the owner's intake address.

## (2026-10-30) — Two plugin builds, and a brand face the preview can't show, said (#3138, #3140)

**Status:** plugin build and manifests, a new gate (`lint-network-reach.ts`), the studio's font helpers and five
preview sections, the plugin's font list, the engine's serif tail. ENGINE minor (change note): the example brand's
serif faces move to the serif tail. CONTRACT unchanged: no token is renamed or added.

### What changed

- **The owner's network model (Q2's replacement): two plugins from one codebase.** `build:release` now builds
  "Prism3 Studio" (`release/`, `allowedDomains` exactly the two Google Fonts hosts, no `*`) and "Prism3 Studio Offline"
  (`release-offline/`, `["none"]`), with distinct names and ids so both load at once. `--offline` is a release variant:
  `PRISM3_NETWORK` false, and `manifest-offline.json` supplies the name, id and `networkAccess`. Each manifest's
  `reasoning` says what is sent where, and so does a line at the foot of the Inspect menu.
- **The gates.** `lint-network-reach.ts` (new, in ci.yml, verify.ts, CONTRIBUTING §3, CLAUDE.md and the PR template):
  the offline bundles carry no request primitive and no allowed host; every host the network bundles name is a listed
  domain or a reference-only host with its reason; the manifests carry their names, ids and domains. The `["none"]`
  literal in `lint-release-bundle.ts` moved to the offline build, and both releases are held to the dev-only markers.
  `lint-sandbox-reject.ts` scans the offline `main.js` too.
- **Q1 A:** a line whose face can't load here says so ("shown in a fallback font"); the web studio and the network
  plugin first ask Google Fonts for it (`ui/web-fonts.ts`). **Q3 A:** a face shown without the asked cut draws the
  nearest real cut with `font-synthesis: none`, plus a note. **Q4 A:** the plugin's `font-list` carries style names, so
  the Type settings weight control names the cuts a family has and the weights with none. **Q5 A:** the drafted strings.
- **#3140, Q3138.6 A:** `font-class.ts`, a curated family-name map; a known serif family takes the serif tail.

### Worth knowing

- **esbuild tree-shakes before it drops a dead branch.** The loader's URL first lived in a module constant, then in a
  helper; both survived into the offline bundle with the host in them, because the dead `PRISM3_NETWORK` branch still
  named them when tree-shaking ran. The gate failed on each, by name. The URL is now written inside the gated branch.
- **A failed request logs a console error.** The browser suites count those, so every suite's browser answers the
  Google Fonts hosts with an empty stylesheet (`apps/studio/test-web-fonts-stub.mjs`): the loader reads "not on Google
  Fonts", exactly as offline, and a run never depends on the runner's network. §3138 serves its own fixture.
- **"A face the device already paints" depends on the device.** §3138 first asserted the loader never asks for Inter.
  CI has no Inter installed, and the chrome registers its embedded copy under an alias (`chrome/tokens.mjs`), so a
  brand's Inter is rightly asked of Google there. The arm now reads which families the device painted (CDP, in the web
  arm) and holds the loader to never asking for one of those.
- **CDP reports a variable face by its named instance** (`Inter Medium`), so §3138 compares the drawn name's head.
- **The Google Fonts CSS API (`/css`, not `/css2`)** answers a request for all eighteen cuts with the ones that exist,
  so one request per family also tells the preview the family's cuts.
- **Q3138.7 and Q3138.8** (on #3138): the plugins are named "Prism3 Studio" and "Prism3 Studio Offline", keeping the
  2026-10-04 product name, and the network build keeps the existing id; the privacy line's words are DRAFT, and it
  sits just above the Inspect menu's build stamp, because C3 A keeps the stamp last.
- **Q3138.9:** the owner's 2026-10-02 rule (no "face" in visible copy, held by `test:chrome`) beat the drafted
  "shown in a fallback face"; the notes say "fallback font".
- **A new `styles.css` rule needs a `lint:live-css` re-sweep to accept,** so the type sample's note sets its small
  text inline instead. `chrome.css` refuses raw lengths (`32ch`): its values are tokens.

  arm resolves the regular composite's own size × line height against the line-box leaf, per brand.

### How a partly hand-edited set updates

The as-built record is per **node**, not per member. A designer's edit to the header's padding changes the `header`
node's hash only. The title is its own node, which nobody edited, so the Update rewrites its text style on the edited
members as well. It keeps the header (`keep`, the default, reported as a hand edit) and keeps every member's and node's
key and id. The new `test-update-apply.ts` section builds the set on the emphasis style, hand-edits 30 of the 48 headers'
block padding (as the reference brand's master is) and updates. All 48 titles land on the regular style, the 30 headers
keep the designer's padding and are listed as kept, the other 18 headers do not take it, and the next dry run reads 18
current with the 30 hand edits still reported.

### Gates

- `test.ts` `#3180 accordion title weight`: the token and the Figma text style per size, typed as literals, against the
  def and all 48 projected members. `#3180 accordion title line box`: the regular composite is one line of the line box
  in every brand.
- Mutation: the def's three title bindings back on `.emphasis` fails `#3180 accordion title weight`,
  `surface/accordion` (`lint-component-surface`) and `accordion weight/premise` (the plugin's update arm), each by name.

### Not in this change

The design's 56px row spacing, missing dividers and thinner chevron stay instance-level choices in the brand's files
(the issue's "for context only").

## (2026-10-30) — Option rows: a 14px label, a cell that follows the label's line box, and the description in Figma (#3153)

**Status:** engine defs (Checkbox.Row, Radio.Row, Switch.Row), the token tree and the Figma `control` collection.
ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT 14.12.0 → 14.13.0 (MINOR, seven added paths). The component executor is unchanged,
so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays: the update rides the existing insert-and-move path (#2595).

### What the owner decided, and what was built on the recommendation

Q852 set one label size per row size for every brand, with no lever: the medium label moves from 16 to 14 and the control
stays at medium. The cell follows the label's own line box. Q853 A projects the description. The open questions went to
the issue as a Q-block, with renders, and each was built as its recommendation:

- **Q3153.1 A:** small and large step down too, to 12 and 16. The description is one step under the label, floored at
  12, because the body ladder has no 10px rung.
- **Q3153.2 A, revised during the build:** Switch.Row's label moves to 12 and 14, but its cell stays a fixed line-box
  height. The first proposal grew the cell to the track as on the option rows, and the #2894 ladder gate measured what
  that costs: a 32px track plus 8px pads makes the medium switch row 48px, off the 44px ladder. The track keeps
  overhanging its cell, so #1439 stays open.
- **Q3153.3 A:** Checkbox.Group and Radio.Group are unchanged.
- **Q3153.4 A:** CONTRACT MINOR, because paths are added and none removed or retyped.

### The construction, and why the inset is a token

The cell's line box became its floor (`minHeight`) and the cell hugs the control, so Figma computes max(control, line)
without help. The label's set-down, (control − line) ÷ 2 when the control is the taller, is a half of a difference,
which a Figma variable cannot express. So it is baked per rung as `control.size.*.label-inset`, beside the edge it is
taken from, as `inset` is for the switch thumb. The other route was a literal per brand written before projection (the
`applyMinWidthRatio` route). It would need the brand's type ramp in all three materialize chains and a literal top
padding in both executors, so it was not taken. The inset is 0 in every corpus brand at comfortable density (boxes
16/20/24 against lines 18/21/24). It bites at spacious density, where a 24px medium box sits beside a 21px line, and the
#3153 test measures it there. Like `line-box`, it carries no per-mode override: a literal may not re-value by mode
(#296), and the `control` collection is single-mode. So a `controlsByMode` brand (none in the corpus) keeps the default
mode's inset.

### Traps for whoever re-verifies

- `type.body.*` is no longer composites only, the same as `type.label.*` since #2586. A walker that reads each key
  under a body rung as a composite must skip `line-box`, as the #2266 test now does.
- The description paints through the `indicator` slot, Dialog's slot for its muted description. The projector's paint
  slots are a closed list, and a new `description` slot paints nothing (the validator says so by name).
- The #2894 update section rebuilds the pre-#2894 file from today's def. It now first puts the pre-#3153 row back
  (`before3153` in `test-update-apply.ts`), because its target is the row as #2894 built it.

## (2026-10-29) — Gate: the redesign seed's leading, label weights and viewports match the stored input (#3146)

**The gap.** #3080 synced the reference brand's redesign seed to its stored input (Q821 A): `lineHeights`,
`leadingShift`, label weights `[default, emphasis]` and `minViewport: 375`. Reverting the seed to the #3080 base still
passed `test.ts`, because the #3077 arm pinned only size and tracking.

**The fix.** The fix is test-only, so no engine bump is owed. The #3077 type table now carries each composite's
leading rung and value (`display.2xl → snug 1.2`, `body.md → relaxed 1.65`, `label.md → snug 1.2`, …), written as
literals. Arm (a) checks the seed against the table. Arm (b) checks the stored input, patched, against the same
literals, so the table is confirmed from the other side without either one being read into it. Arm (a) also gains
two assertions: the fluid clamp is 375–1440, and the label weight-role set is `default,emphasis`, both emitted and
declared.

**The trap in the label check.** The engine's default label weights are also `default, emphasis`. So a seed with its
`label` line dropped emits the same pair, and an emitted-set check alone passes. The assertion therefore also reads
the seed's parsed input for an explicit `label` entry. Without it, the seed silently follows the engine default
instead of the stored input.

**Mutations.** Each mutation fails its arm by name:
- The seed reverted to the #3080 base (`5837a115`) fails the type table (leading), the viewport arm and the label arm.
- `minViewport` alone set back to 402 fails only the viewport arm.
- The `label` weight line alone dropped fails only the label arm.

## (2026-10-29) — Components chooses what to add; Update file shows To add and Due (#3129)

Builds the owner-approved wireframe on #3129 (Q832 A, Q833 A; Q3129.1–13 all A), with the owner's revisions R1–R7 and
Q835 A of 2026-10-28, and Q3129.14 B, Q3129.15–18 A of 2026-10-29. Engine `0.238.0` (patch: no emitted artifact moves).

### What changed

- **The add queue lives in the file** (`apps/plugin/src/add-queue.ts`, new and pure). Shared plugin data on the root,
  namespace `prism3`, one key per set, `addQueue.<defId>` = the ISO time it was queued. One key per set so two teammates
  ticking at once never lose a tick; shared so an agent in the file can read it. The order is not stored: it is shown and
  built in Components' list order (`inListOrder`).
- **Reads never write.** `fileSets`, `ledgerSets` and `fileDue` report the queue minus the sets the file holds and the
  defs the engine cannot build. The keys are cleared where the ledger records a set that landed whole (beside
  `recordSets`), and by a queue write, which also clears stale keys; every Update file run ends with one carrying no ids.
- **Components (plugin):** boxes come back from #2700's markup, acting on the file's queue through `add-queue` instead of
  the session's selection (`sel` is retired, and with it the dead Build bar and Build all). One box per family (R5): a
  family's row, or a set alone on its row, two-state (`familyBox`); a family's parts have none, and a family partly in
  the file queues its missing parts. Section boxes stay three-state; a section of one family carries that family's box.
  A row with nothing to add keeps an empty cell, so names align. Each tier's caption line carries Select all and
  Deselect all (R1, replacing the page control); the shared settings sit under a Component settings tier (R2). The page
  title moves to the left of the levers header with the search flush right (R3, Q835 A), and Components shows no mode
  control (R4). Its preview always shows Light (Q3129.14 B, replacing the first build's A), by Palettes' own pin
  (#2321's `pinsLight` row in `shell/frame.ts`): the mode Theme had comes back on the way out, and dark components are
  checked on Theme's pages, with no line saying so (Q3129.18 A). The component settings' derived-mode hold and line stay
  as the guard for a mode written while the pin is up (Q3129.17 A); test:chrome section 26 writes HC light past the pin
  and holds them to it, #2096's refused write included. The boxes wait for the host's full read (#3110's ledger-only
  answer draws none).
- **Update file:** Theme, Components (To add and Due as its subtitles, R6), Style guides. To add has Remove (focus moves
  to the next row's Remove) and Remove all from two rows up; an empty queue on a set-up file shows no To add (R7); a
  fresh file starts with nothing queued and offers Add all. Due uses Components' display names. The badge adds the
  queue, and its name is split (`badgeParts`, `badgeName`).
- **The web studio is unchanged** (Q3129.12 A).

### Traps

- **The test harness hears the UI's own posts.** In `test:chrome` and the render scripts, `parent.postMessage` from the
  UI lands on the UI's own `message` listener. `add-queue` is both the request's and the answer's type, so the parser
  drops an `add-queue` with no `queued` list; without that, every tick was answered by its own echo as an empty queue.
- **The run's queue write needs the file's sets.** `addQueue` reuses `presentCache`; after a run it is cleared, so that
  one write loads every page (one per turn, #3110), as the read after the run does anyway.

### Not covered

- An agent command that queues sets (the storage allows one; the wireframe did not add it).
- #3123 (the size pass) was open while this was built: it and this PR both edit `shell/update-file.ts` (the hand-edits
  choice, which #3123 moves into the foot as a select). Whichever lands second resolves it.

## (2026-10-29) — Update file: an executor change makes due only the sets it redraws (#3101, follow-up to Q811.1 / Q820 A)

**Status:** plugin main thread, the update's dry run, a new gate and a new tool. ENGINE patch (change note). CONTRACT
unchanged. The executor is unchanged, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at 43: the new files are not reached from
`write-components.ts`, and `lint-executor-revision.ts` agrees. No user-visible string changes; fewer sets read due.
Proposal, measurement and the weighed approaches: the comment on #3101.

### What changed

- **A record of which sets each revision redraws** (`apps/plugin/src/executor-reach.json`, read by `executor-reach.ts`):
  per `EXECUTOR_REVISION` above a floor, the def ids whose drawing that revision changes, or `"all"`. `reaches(def,
  from, to)` answers whether any revision in `(from, to]` names the set. A revision with no entry, a range crossing the
  floor, or a revision that moved back reaches every set, which is Q820 A's reading. An entry keeps the ids it was
  measured under; a later def rename is followed through `COMPONENT_RENAMES` (`currentDefId`), so Tab's entries at 25
  and 27 still reach a Tab item set.
- **The ledger** (`as-built-ledger.ts`): a revision move makes a set due for the executor only when it reaches the set.
  Otherwise the set reads as if the revision had not moved: current, due for its definition, or (the engine moved too)
  read by its print, so `needsPrint` prints it. `quietOf` and `restampQuiet` (`main.ts`) re-record such a set under
  today's revision after the next write, never at load.
- **The dry run** (`update-plan.ts`): a member stamped under another revision is "to update" only when a revision since
  reaches its set, so the checklist, the badge and the full check agree. Reaction differences, drawn damage and plan
  moves are read as before.
- **`test-reactions.ts`'s `converge` premise** stamped Tag's members at `EXECUTOR_REVISION - 1` to stand for a
  plugin from before reactions. Revision 43 does not redraw Tag, so the members with no reaction difference now read
  current and keep their records; the premise now stamps 14, the revision reactions (#2466, 15) followed.
- **The record is backfilled from a measurement** of the last 20 revisions (24 → 43), floor 23. A file drawn at 40 and
  read at 43 now has 3 sets due for the executor (brand-mark, wallet-button, sign-in-button), not every set.

### The measurement (`apps/plugin/reach-draw.ts`, `tools/executor-reach/history.ts`)

Two executors draw every projected def into the component shim over the same plans: the parent commit's
`apps/plugin/src` (exported with `git archive`) and the commit's own. Eight arms per def, each old against new from one
start: a fresh build; an in-place update of a file the old executor drew, every stamp at revision 0; an update across a
lever change, both ways; and an update over a drawing an earlier update left, both ways (the convergence-fix shape,
#2976). Two brands: none, and every structural lever away from its default (`LEVERS`). The drawing is every enumerable
field of every node under the set, its reactions and plugin data, in key order; only the stamp's revision and build
timestamps are normalized. A def that throws the same way on both sides, or draws nothing, is `error`, never `same`.

`history.ts --last 20 --jobs 4` (about an hour): 8 of 20 revisions redrew no set, 6 redrew one, one each 2, 3 and 4,
and three 15 to 16 (the reactions at 25 and 27, the Field style lever at 30). Median 1 set, mean 3.1, of 41 to 60.
Revisions 40 to 43 agree with an earlier fresh-build-only run, set for set. Two arms were load-bearing, each checked per
arm for one set: 38 (the update clears a min/max the plan dropped) changes no fresh Tag and shows only when an update
crosses a lever change; 30 changes Text field only where the lever brand is drawn.

### The gate (`apps/plugin/lint-executor-reach.ts`)

`lint-executor-revision.ts` keeps its role (the executor's code moved only with a raised revision); this one starts
where it ends. SUBJECT: the entries above the base's revision, as committed. ORACLE: `reach-draw.ts`, the base's
executor against the tree's, over the tree's plans, for every def no new entry names, in up to four workers. A def that
drew differently in any arm, or could not be drawn, must be named. The gate never writes the record (docs/34 shape 6),
and entries at or below the base's revision, and the floor, may not change. A base executor that does not load against
the tree's engine requires `"all"`. Base: merge base, or the first parent on main (`comparison-base.ts`). Cost: a read of
two files on most PRs; about 5 minutes on 4 cores when the revision rose (59 sets, measured with the base at 42).

What it shares with its subject is the host model (shape 17): a write the shim does not record reads the same on both
sides. Stated in `executor-reach.ts` with the author's answer (declare the set, or `"all"`). Not added to
`lint-push-base.ts`'s replay: on main's push run the first parent already gives it a real base, and its history arm
compares the record, not a squash's diff.

### Mutations, each on a committed tree, each failing by name

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| G1: an executor change that redraws Badge (a set field), revision 44, entry `[]` | `lint-executor-reach`: "badge: drawn differently by revision 44 than by 43 (fresh/default; fresh/levers) … Add "badge" to entry 44"; control with `["badge"]`: clean |
| G2: an in-place update change on Divider only (`update-apply.ts`) | `lint-executor-reach`: "divider: … (update/default; update/levers; update/default>levers; repair/default>levers; …)", no fresh arm |
| H1: entry 42 narrowed | "entry 42: … at the base, … here. An entry at or below the base's revision (43) does not change" |
| H2: floor moved | "floor: 39 at the base, 38 here" and "entry 39: missing" |
| H3: entry 41 dropped | "entry 41: missing" |
| H4: a misspelt def | "entry 43: sign-in-buton is not a def Prism3 builds as a set" |
| H5: an entry above the revision | "entry 44: above EXECUTOR_REVISION (43)" |
| M1: `dueOf` back to `was.rev !== is.rev` | `test-as-built-ledger.ts`: `reach/ledger`, `reach/range`, `reach/quiet`, `reach/engine` |
| M2: `update-plan.ts` without `reaches` | `test-update-apply.ts`: `reach/dry run 42` (45 to update, not current) |
| M3: `restampQuiet`'s stale filter without the revision | `test-build-completed.ts`: `reach/restamp` (rev stays 42) |
| M4: `quietOf` without the revision | `test-as-built-ledger.ts`: `reach/quiet` |
| M5: `needsPrint` back to `was.rev === is.rev` | `test-as-built-ledger.ts`: `reach/needs-print` |
| M6: `reaches` ignoring the lists | `test-as-built-ledger.ts`: `reach/record` and five more |

The history arms (H1 to H5) ran with `GITHUB_BASE_REF` pointed at a local ref holding a committed record, since main has
none yet. Two first attempts at G1 were mutations that changed nothing (a component name spelt `Badge`, then a set
opacity a later write resets), and the gate rightly passed both; each mutation since was confirmed to move the drawing
before the gate ran (docs/34 shape 19).

### Gaps

- **The shim's limit is the record's limit.** A write the shim does not model, or an executor branch only a lever
  combination outside the two brands reaches, reads as unreached. The author's answer is to name the set or `"all"`.
- **A member's stamp keeps its revision** when the update leaves it current, so the dry run reads ranges from older
  revisions over time. The record is append-only, so the answer does not drift.
- **The backfill is a measurement, not a gate result**: those revisions merged before the gate existed. `history.ts`
  reproduces it; revisions below 24 were not measured, hence the floor.
- **A reason line naming what changed** (Q3101.1 B on #3101) is not built: new copy, the owner's call.
- **CI time**: about 5 minutes on an executor PR, on the job that runs the revision gate.

## (2026-10-29) — Divider: a vertical labeled member, upright label between two lines (#3143)

Built from the #3143 proposal and the owner's Q3143.1–.7 (all A). The set grows from 6 to 7 members: `orientation=vertical, inset=none, labeled=true`. The label stays upright with a line above and below it; the root is a column (`directionWhen`, Button group's #2661 field) that hugs the label across (a new, narrow `PartDef.sizingWhen`: hug only, resolved before projection beside `directionWhen`), 68px tall (`size.xl.height`), with `space.150` (12px, density 8/12/16) between the label and each line. Docs state a 56px minimum and keep the vertical label to "Or" between alternatives. The Q3051.2 accessibility contract is unchanged, and the wrapper carries no `aria-orientation`. Engine version 0.238.0.

### Build check 1: a bound main-axis size on a growing line
Each line now binds a thickness key per orientation on both axes, so one orientation's cross axis is the other's main axis. The offline shim records a binding but has no model of a bound size turning a filling child FIXED, and it doesn't fill a frame with no layout of its own in either direction. So it can't measure the flip, and no real host was available here. The proposal's fallback is applied anyway: the projection writes no bound size on the axis a part grows along. That write is dead where the host keeps the fill (the parent decides the length), and it would leave the horizontal lines 1px long where the host flips it. A corpus-wide plan dump before and after the rule shows only the divider's plans move, and the horizontal labeled member's plan is byte-identical to main's. **Trap:** re-measure on a live file before relying on a growing child's bound main-axis size anywhere. The rule hides the question; it doesn't answer it.

### Build check 2: the plain vertical members on update
Measured with the real update dry run against a shim file built from main's plans: the two plain vertical members change `layoutMode` HORIZONTAL→VERTICAL and the root's `itemSpacing` binding space/300→space/150 (one child, so no pixel moves). The four other members re-apply with no field difference, and the new member is added. The as-built ledger reads the set `due` for the definition until the fold, then for the engine, naming all five parts. The print is keyed by plan index, so the inserted member shifts every later plan and the reason line over-names (the label's `type` facet included).

### Gate notes
`test.ts`'s `#990` width census excuses a growing part's `width` by name and holds it in its own arm instead: a line binds the hairline across its root and nothing along it. The roundtrip's new `#3143 divider` arm reads the shim's layout rather than diffing against the plan. A diff can't catch a plan that turns the column back into a row, because the host follows the plan.

## (2026-10-29) — SignInButton: Continue with Apple, Google or Facebook, drawn to each provider's rules, on a literal record (#2343 PR 5)

PR 5 of #2343, stacked on the branded-button helpers (#3122). It follows the proposal on #2343 (2026-10-28) and the owner's decisions: Q-S1 to Q-S12, all A, and Q831 A (all eight pairs ship), which supersedes Q-S5 A's wait for artwork; then, on 2026-10-29, Q-S13 to Q-S17, all A, and Q846 A (one black glyph per provider, painted white on a dark fill). The owner saw the wireframe before the build started.

### What it is
- **SignInButton** (`packages/engine/components/sign-in-button.ts`) is a Prism3-drawn button for Apple, Google and Facebook.
  - **Axes:** provider × style × size × state. The style axis uses the providers' own names; invalid pairs are excluded with `excludeCoordinates`.
  - **96 members:** 8 pairs × 3 sizes × 4 states.
  - **Its own page:** "Sign-in button", under Components.
- **Every pair ships (Q831 A); the membership stays data (Q-S5 A).** Facebook white carries `provider/facebook-blue`, derived from `social/facebook`, scaled by 23/24 to the provider glyphs' 0.5px inset and centered where its `provider/` sibling sits; shape and colors are unchanged. Apple white and outline carry the black `provider/apple` itself (Q846 A dropped the derived `provider/apple-black`, its duplicate after #3134). A pair is still a member only when the mark set holds its glyph (`makeSignInButton(names)` reads the vocabulary), so a future provider whose artwork is not in yet is excluded, never stood in.
- **The derived glyph.**
  - Its `provenance.json` record says "derived from social/<name>, scaled to the provider inset" and names `derivedFrom`; `lint-mark-provenance` checks both.
  - **Colors (#3066):** `lint-mark-colors` arm (f) compares each derived file's paints, in order, with its social source file, so the source file is the oracle rather than the record alone.
  - **Geometry:** `lint-glyph-geometry`'s DERIVED arm measures the files. The derived glyph's body (its first path) spans its `provider/` sibling's ink box within 0.01px (INSET), and every path is its source's under one uniform scale and move (SHAPE). Pure scaling about (12, 12) would leave Facebook 0.07px off vertically (and Apple 0.10px off horizontally, while it was derived), because the provider files center their ink box on the artboard; so the derivation also centers it, which moves and never reshapes.
- **What Prism3's tokens drive:**
  - the height (`size.*.height`, shared, so a stack lines up)
  - Apple's and Facebook's padding and gap, which are Button's and move with density
  - `radius.md`, the 140 width floor and the shared focus ring
  - the brand's label emphasis style, for Apple and Facebook
- **What the provider fixes (literals):**
  - the fill, the 1px inside edge, the label ink and the wording ("Continue with <Provider>", with no text property, Q-S8 A)
  - Google's padding (12 at both sides, fixed)
  - Google Sans Medium 14/20 at every size, with a Roboto Medium fallback (Q-S7 A)
  - the hover and pressed wash, which lies over the fill; the fill itself never changes (Q-S6 A)

- **The dark-fill tint (Q846 A).** #3134 drew `provider/apple` and `provider/facebook` black, so Apple black and Facebook blue would draw a black glyph on black and on blue. Each provider keeps one black glyph, and SignInButton paints it `#ffffff` where its fill is dark.
  - **Engine:** `LiteralEntry.markTint` (opaque `#rrggbb`), read by `PartDef.literal: 'mark'` on a nested brand mark that states `fixedPaint`; the plan carries `literalTint` in place of `fixedPaint`. The validator refuses `literal: 'mark'` on any other part and a translucent or malformed tint.
  - **Both executors** paint every VECTOR in the nested glyph with the tint as an unbound solid, report `mark.literalTint -> … (no VECTOR …)` when there is none, and read it back by value (`… DISCARDED (literal … set, not retained)`). `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 42 → 43 (#3142 took 42 on main first).
  - **`lint-mark-colors` (g), its own by-name gate.** A host may carry `literalTint` only if it is in `TINT_HOSTS` (SignInButton alone) and the mark is a `brand-mark/provider/*` glyph: any other def that tints fails `HOST TINT … only sign-in-button may tint a mark`, and SignInButton tinting a non-provider mark fails `HOST TINT … not a brand-mark/provider/* glyph`. A tint host that tints nothing fails too. (d) is unchanged for every other node: no `descendantFills`, no paint, `fixedPaint` stated.
  - **`Q846 A dark-fill styles draw white`** (`test.ts`): typed from the decision, Apple black and Facebook blue carry `#ffffff` at all 24 members and no other style tints. The contrast arm alone cannot hold this: black on `#1877f2` is about 4.95:1, over 3:1, and Facebook's white-on-blue is a brand rule.
  - **#3142's `provider glyph contrast` arm reads the tint from the plan**, so it judges the painted color: white on black and on `#1877f2` pass, and a dropped tint fails it at 1.00:1. Its review nits are fixed here: the failure line names `brand-mark/provider/apple` (not `provider/provider/`), and a fixture covers a themed fill nested under a literal one (review M2).
  - **Executor arms:** `sign-in build/literal` checks the glyph's vectors read `#ffffff` on the dark fills; `#2343 PR 5 paste executor` does the same through the paste payload, with the provider marks in the stub file, and checks Apple white's and Google's glyph stay untinted.

### The engine change (Q-S2 A)
- **The literal record.** `ComponentDef.literal` is a record keyed by a template over the projected axes (`{provider}.{style}`). `PartDef.literal` opts a part into it: `'surface'` on a box (fill, edge, `wash[state]`) or `'label'` on a text part (ink, copy, font).
  - The projector writes `literalPaints` (plain hex, bottom to top) and `literalFont` onto the plan, in place of `paints` and `textStyle`.
  - A projected member whose coordinate names no entry throws.
  - The validator refuses: a literal beside the paint grammar, the wrong part kind, a def with no record, an uppercase or malformed color, an opaque wash, a wash at a state the def lacks, a key on an unprojected axis, and a line height under the size.
- **Both executors** write literal paints as unbound solids, and a `#rrggbbaa` color's alpha becomes the paint's opacity. They load the literal font, falling back and reporting when the face is not installed. Each reads the result back by value.
  - The #865 defaults treat a literal channel as claimed.
  - The paste executor splices all of this into a payload only when its plans carry a literal, so every other payload is byte-identical.
  - `anatomy-readback.ts` classifies both fields. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 41 → 42 (#3132 took 41 on main first), then 43 for the tint (#3142 took 42).
- **`NestingRelation.variantWhere`**, a joint host-coordinate mapping. Apple white and Facebook white carry different glyphs, so the glyph depends on provider and style together. `variantWhen` maps one axis at a time and rightly refuses one child axis set from two host axes. `variantWhere` requires every entry to name the same host axes, so at most one matches a member. It is refused on an unprojected axis, an unknown value, a repeated `when`, or a `set` axis that `variant` lacks, that `follow` names or that `variantWhen` also sets.
- **The spec model** (`component-specs.ts`, which feeds `specs.json` and the docs page) carries `variantWhere` as `where` and the literal record as `literal`, so the code side gets the provider's values and each member's glyph. The roundtrip's spec read-back resolves `where` like `when`.
- **`lint-paint-placement`** learns literal paint as its own placement kind. It also fails a node that carries both a literal and a bound paint on one channel (arm L).

### Gates
- **Joined:** `lint-hit-target` (INTERACTIVE, SMALL_SIZE), `lint-rung-names` (MUST_COVER, Q1B, ICON_OFFSET_DEFS), `lint-standalone-floor`, `lint-paint-placement`, `lint-absolute-inset` (both lists), `lint-mark-colors`, `lint-axis-values` (new provider and style sets; WalletButton's provider set becomes `canonical`), `test.ts` (TIER 2, BRANDED, the spacing tables and their #325/#326 rules, the type-key grid, the centring register, the default bridge), `CANVAS_FURNITURE`, the taxonomy and the studio catalog.
- **`#2343 PR 5 provider rules`** (`test.ts`). Every value is typed from the providers' guidelines, never read off the def. The arms:
  - ARTWORK: 96 members, all 8 pairs; and (data-driven) 84 over the mark set without the derived glyph, each pair mapped to its own glyph
  - COLOR, WASH (the four wash values typed), FONT, WIDTH, PARITY, MARK (with the typed tint), WORDING and NAME
  - CONTRAST: Facebook's 4.23:1 is a recorded provider shortfall, not a failure
- **`#2343 PR 5 literal paint`:** the allowlist plus the validator refusals. **`#2343 PR 5 variantWhere`:** that mapping's refusals.
- **`#2343 PR 5 paste executor`** (`test.ts`) and **`sign-in build`, `sign-in build/literal`** (`test-write-components.ts`): the two executors, against typed values.
- **Fault injection, in both executors** (the shims gain `unavailableFonts` on the paste side and `discardLiteralFills` on both):
  - **Font fallback:** with Google Sans refused, the label lands in Roboto Medium 14/20 (typed), the miss `label.font -> Google Sans Medium (…)` is reported, and the member still builds. These are `#2343 PR 5 paste executor font fallback` and `sign-in build/font fallback`.
  - **Literal read-back:** a host that drops the container's literal fill is reported as `container.fills -> DISCARDED (literal … set, not retained)`, by value. These are `#2343 PR 5 paste executor literal read-back` and `sign-in build/literal read-back`.
- **Also joined:** `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` / `ci.yml` 224 → 225 (the new docs page), the ecosystem members list, the reaction map (96 members, 48 sources, 72 reactions), the studio's used-by index, component groups and spacing classification. Brand mark's single-consumer page exemption (`STANDALONE_NESTED`) is dropped, because two components nest it now. SignInButton's spacing is per provider, so the studio's set list shows none for it.
- **Baselines accepted:** `lint-component-surface` (sign-in-button: no set → 96; brand-mark 74 → 75), `lint-paint` and `lint-component-renames`. `lint-axis-values`: the style set gains `white` and `outline` (now a superset of the field's `outline`), and the brand-mark name set gains `provider/facebook-blue`.

### Mutations (each committed first, then restored)
- **Round A, five def mutations, each aimed at a different arm.** Google light's edge to `#757575`, Google's font to 15, `minWidth` to 120, Facebook blue's glyph to `social/facebook`, Apple's continue wording to "Sign in with Apple". Each fails its arm by name (COLOR, FONT, WIDTH, MARK, WORDING); ARTWORK and the paste executor arm also catch the changed values; `lint-component-surface` fails `surface/sign-in-button`.
- **Round B:** the dark pressed wash set equal to hover fails WASH. Exclusions from a hard-coded list instead of the vocabulary fail ARTWORK (data-driven), at 60 instead of 96. The projector's `variantWhere` step disabled fails MARK (Google nests the Apple glyph). The paste executor's literal-fill line removed fails `#2343 PR 5 paste executor`.
- **Plugin executor:** the literal-fill line removed fails `sign-in build` (the executor's own `container.fills -> DISCARDED`) and `sign-in build/literal`.
- **Q846 A, the tint** (each committed first, then reset):
  - **Apple black's tint dropped:** fails `Q846 A dark-fill styles draw white` (`tint none, want #ffffff`), MARK, the paste executor arm, and `#3134 provider glyph contrast` (`brand-mark/provider/apple (#000000) over the literal fill #000000 is 1.00:1`).
  - **Facebook blue's tint dropped:** fails `Q846 A dark-fill styles draw white`, MARK and the paste executor arm; the contrast arm passes it (black on `#1877f2` clears 3:1), which is why the white rule has its own arm.
  - **The tint on a light style** (Apple white): fails `Q846 A dark-fill styles draw white` (`tint #ffffff, want none`), MARK, the contrast arm, and the paste executor arm (`glyph tinted … on a light fill`).
  - **A non-provider mark tinted** (Apple black on `social/apple-mono`): fails `lint-mark-colors` (`HOST TINT — … brand-mark/social/apple-mono #ffffff, which is not a brand-mark/provider/* glyph`).
  - **Another def tinting** (WalletButton with a tint record): fails `lint-mark-colors` (`HOST TINT — … only sign-in-button may tint a mark`).
  - **The plugin's tint write removed:** fails `sign-in build` (`mark.literalTint -> DISCARDED`) and `sign-in build/literal`. **The paste payload's removed:** fails `#2343 PR 5 paste executor`.

### Decided by the owner (2026-10-29: Q-S13 to Q-S17 all A, Q846 A)
- **Q-S13 A:** a literal hover and pressed wash, black at 10% and 20% on a light fill and white on a dark one, which does not flip with the mode.
- **Q-S14 A:** Google's 8px gap, with 12px at both sides.
- **Q-S15 A:** "Continue with Facebook" in Figma.
- **Q-S16 A:** glyph heights 16/20/24, Button's one-rung offset (an `ICON_OFFSET_DEFS` owner exception in `lint-rung-names`).
- **Q-S17 A:** code offers only the styles whose artwork is in the design file, all eight today.
- **Q846 A:** provider glyphs may be tinted, inside SignInButton only; see "The dark-fill tint" above.
- **Next:** #3136 (Facebook `#0866FF`) follows this PR.
- **Open item:** whether Google Sans may be used outside Google's own assets is unverified (Q-S7). Recorded in the def's `notes`.

### Traps
- **The base moved during this work.** `git fetch --unshallow` (needed for `lint-release-notes`) moved `origin/main` five commits, and a soft reset onto it briefly put PR 1's old-base tree on top of the new `main`. That push would have reverted #3108 and four others. It was caught by diffing the trees, rebuilt as a patch on the new `main` and force-pushed before any PR existed. Compare trees after any fetch that can move the base.
- **The first full verify caught a real gap the unit arms missed.** The roundtrip's spec read-back (#2830) found the code-side spec model naming the Apple glyph on every Google and Facebook member, because `component-specs.ts` did not know `variantWhere`. A new nesting field has three readers, not two: the projector, the validator and the spec model.
- **`test.ts` passes print nothing.** The `#1268` assertion-site arm is what proves every new `ok()` ran.
