## (2026-10-29) — The Activity drawer, direction A: glyphs and words for verdicts, split counts, next steps, a sheet header at 380, and a sanctioned shadow (#3113)

The owner approved #3113's wireframe on 2026-10-28: Q3113.1–Q3113.10 are all A. This builds direction A, the refined
drawer, in `apps/studio/src/shell/activity.ts`, `apps/studio/src/chrome.css` and `apps/plugin/src/agent-link-ui.ts`, with
one lend in `apps/studio/src/main.ts`. The drawer only draws in the plugin; the studio runs no write, so its drawer stays
undrawn. All new strings are DRAFT.

- **Verdicts (Q3113.2 A).** A verdict is a glyph in its status ink (check in `ok-icon`, alert triangle in `warn-icon`,
  alert circle in `bad-icon`, the running ring for a run) and the headline's words without its leading mark. Only a
  failure's words are in `bad-text`. The pill is gone from the drawer (the style guide page still draws one). A warning is
  a bad result whose headline leads with "⚠" and reports nothing it was asked to make as failed (`kindOf`, the owner's
  D-RED A), so P3's red warning is gone.
- **Counts (Q3113.3 A).** "1 failed" in the error ink after the error glyph, "1 warning" in the text ink after the warning
  glyph, and "n running" only while more than one runs. The counts are inline, so they keep the row's one baseline (#2213).
- **Rows.** Attention first (failures, warnings), then what runs, then the rest, each in the order it first ran. A row that
  moves keeps its focus, and a next step that starts its run hands focus to its row's header.
- **A bad result (Q3113.4 A, Q3113.5 A).** Its first line is its reason, in the UI face at the emphasis weight (500); the
  rest stays mono (#2177). Then the next steps: Apply again, Build again, Set up again, or Run again (style guides, Prune
  stale, Specs), then Copy details. A rerun goes through the call the panel already makes (`activityAgain` in `main.ts`:
  Update file's run for the theme, Set up file and the style guides, the Components run for the last panel build's sets,
  Clean up's dry run, Draw specs). No new message. It is offered only on a panel result (an agent's ran with the agent's
  input), and only while nothing else runs. The read-back has no rerun.
- **History (Q3113.6 A).** Each earlier result is one line (its mark, time, words and Agent tag), which opens its own lines.
- **The agent link (Q3113.7 A).** The bar row shows the link's glyph, a dot and one word: "Listening", or "Not listening"
  and "Error" in the error inks. At 380 it shows the glyph and the dot, and the word is clipped the way `.p3-sr` clips text,
  so it stays in the accessible name. The full line (`agentLinkStatusText`) heads the open drawer after the same glyph and
  dot, in operation words with a relative age, for example "Listening for agent commands (file mailbox, every 2 s). Last:
  Build set, built 48 variants, 2 min ago." The minimized strip (#2949) and the announced short status (#2275) are
  unchanged.
- **The 380 sheet (Q3113.8 A).** A header row with a 24 × 24 Close (named "Close Activity"), "Activity", the counts and the
  agent dot takes the bar row's place while the sheet is open. Row headers wrap, and the Settings/Preview toggle hides.
  Focus that the sheet would strand goes to Close.
- **Launch and unread (Q3113.9 A).** The plugin draws the bar row from launch, closed, reading "Activity", above the narrow
  tier. A dot on the bar row marks a result nobody has opened, with "New result" in its name. **At 380 the strip waits for
  the first run.** The full suite found that a strip drawn from launch leaves the 380 × 420 window only 29px of levers
  under an error line, where #2105's floor is 40. The build keeps that floor and asks the call as Q3113.15 on the PR.
- **Found by drawing it from launch.** The bar row had no chrome focus ring of its own. It now draws Prism3's ring inside
  its edge, as the scrolling panes do, because it spans the window's bottom edge. The drawer is a named region "Activity"
  only while it is open, as #2487's Q197 has it; closed, it is a control row, not a region.
- **Sizes (Q3113.10 A under #3083's decisions).** Drawer text at 12, and the bar row stays at 56 (Q3083.2 B). A parallel
  lane builds #3083's size pass; whichever PR lands second resolves the overlap in `chrome.css` and `test-chrome.mjs`.

### A sanctioned shadow: the drawer's top edge

The owner added a subtle shadow along the drawer's top edge, so it reads as an overlay that slides up and over the
preview. It applies to the open drawer, and to the strip and the sheet at 380, where they overlay content. **The owner's
clarification on #3113 rewords T5: shadows are used sparingly, and only where they carry meaning.** T5 is a rule of
thumb, not a prohibition, so this shadow is a sanctioned use, not an exception. It is recorded where T5 lives:
`SANCTIONED_SHADOWS` in `apps/studio/chrome/spec.mjs` (each use with its rule and its reason), the T5 row of
`docs/superpowers/ui-redesign/decisions-2026-09-30-v4-review.md`, the `chrome.css` header and the RAW comment in
`chrome/tokens.mjs`.

- The shadow is `0 calc(-1 * space-025) space-150 calc(-1 * space-050) scrim`. Its color is the chrome's existing
  `--p3-scrim` (`color.scrim.default`, black at 40% in light and 60% in dark). No token and no pair is added.
- The build's [raw] scan lets each recorded rule through word for word (`withoutSanctionedShadows`). A recorded value
  must be chrome spacing variables and the scrim, and its canary (`SHADOW_CANARIES`) checks that the recorded rule alone
  passes. No new gate forbids a shadow elsewhere. The [raw] T5 pattern in `tokens.mjs` and `test:chrome`'s older
  "no chrome element draws a shadow" check predate this PR and stay; whether to keep or retire them is asked on #3113.
- `test:chrome`'s T5 probe lets through only the drawer's own box-shadow, while the drawer is open or at the narrow tier. In
  every probe state, a new check gates it: the open drawer (or the strip) casts the shadow up from its top edge (a negative
  y offset, no x offset, a blur) in the emission's scrim for the chrome theme drawn, and the closed bar row draws none.
  The scrim's value comes from this suite's own walk of the committed emission.
- **Dark, measured.** In light, the shadow takes the page from 255 to about 220 at the edge. In dark, the page is near
  black (13), and a black shadow can only take it to about 10. Over the cards and swatches it covers, it does read in dark,
  and the hairline still marks the edge. A stronger geometry made light heavy. This is raised as a question on the PR.

### Gates that moved

- `test:chrome` section 10: the plugin's launch state, verdict words and marks, the split counts, the reason line's face
  and weight, the next steps, "Set up again" posting exactly Set up file's message, the one-line history, the 380 header

- `test:verdict`: reads the verdict's words, and a bad result's reason with its lines (#2177, #2281, #1890).
- `test-agent-link.ts`: the full line's words and relative age.
- `lint:contrast`: no new pair. The marks are `ok-icon`, `warn-icon` and `bad-icon` on `bg-page`. The words are `text` and

## (2026-10-29) — Brand marks: tile edges only where the fill needs one, black Apple and Facebook glyphs, a canvas grid that clears wide marks (#3134)

The owner previewed the template file and gave three directions, all decided on the issue.

- **Tile edges.** The 1px edge exists so a white tile reads as a card on a white page. `PartDef.tileEdge` gains `edgeWhen`, which narrows the stroke alone: a tile it leaves out keeps its bound corners and its crop and draws no stroke or weight. BrandMark computes the list from each file's first fill against white, under 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11's non-text floor), so a provider added later is judged the day it lands. Computed per tile: white tiles (Affirm, Amazon Pay, Apple Pay, Diners Club, Discover, Google Pay, Maestro, Mastercard, PayPal, Visa) 1.00:1, edged; Klarna `#FEB4C7` 1.67:1, edged; Venmo `#008CFF` 3.39:1, Amex `#1F72CD` 4.83:1, Shop Pay `#5A31F4` 6.60:1 and the generic card `#545454` 7.57:1, no edge. The generic card has no ground: its first fill is the card body itself.
- **The gate is independent of the def.** `lint-mark-colors.ts` (e) re-reads the raw file with its own regex and its own luminance arithmetic, and holds both directions: an edge on a tile that needs none fails, and a missing one fails. The executor arms (`test-write-components.ts`, the paste twin in `test.ts`) type the four edgeless tiles by name.
- **Black glyphs.** `provider/apple` and `provider/facebook` were drawn white and vanished on the canvas. They are `#000000` now, records updated (`mono-black`; the source line says why). A consumer tints them as needed, per the owner.
- **Overlap with #3125 (SignInButton, open).** That PR nests `provider/apple` as the white glyph on Apple's black button and, per Q831 A, adds a derived `provider/apple-black`. Once this lands, `provider/apple` is the black glyph, so #3125's Apple-black member needs a white glyph (or a tint) and its `apple-black` duplicates `provider/apple`. Built on main as it is; noted on #3125.
- **Canvas grid.** The emit branch of the component executor placed every standalone component on a fixed 48px pitch, which fits the 24px icons and nothing wider: Discover's 54px logo sat over Google Pay. The pitch is now the widest and tallest component of the def on the page plus 24, so icons keep 48 and marks clear each other; an update's free slot is found by box overlap, not by an exact coordinate. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 40 → 42 (41 went to #3132 on main while this was in review). A file built before this keeps the old fixed-pitch layout until a fresh BrandMark build; filed as #3145. The MCP paste path (`mcp-steps.ts` `runComponentEmit`) keeps its own fixed 48 pitch; filed as #3139.
- **Order with #3125.** This lands first; #3125 takes the next `EXECUTOR_REVISION` and the white-glyph fix for Apple's black button.
- **Provider glyph contrast (review).** `test.ts` gains "#3134 provider glyph contrast": for every def nesting a `brand-mark/provider/*` glyph (nest or swap) under a literal fill, the glyph's strongest file color must reach 3:1 against the nearest painted ancestor's literal fill (a themed fill is the contrast contract's). No def on main nests one, so it passes vacuously and says so: 58 defs, 4102 plans, 104 nested brand marks, 0 provider glyphs. A self-test of six fixtures holds it (black on black and on #131314 fail; black and Google on white pass; a themed fill is skipped; a swap two levels down is caught). Mutations: the threshold dropped to 1:1 fails the self-test by name; the walker blinded fails the main arm on 0 nested brand marks.
- **Mutations, each committed first and restored from it.** `edgeWhen` dropped from the def (every tile edged again) fails `lint-mark-colors.ts` by name, eight `TILE EDGE` lines, two each for Amex, generic, Shop Pay and Venmo. The white glyphs restored with their records and module moved too, so `lint-mark-colors.ts` stays clean, fail "#3134 provider glyphs: provider/apple and provider/facebook are drawn in black…" in `test.ts`. The fixed 48 pitch restored fails "#3134 brand-mark canvas: no two of the 74 built marks overlap…" (Discover over Google Pay, the PayPal wordmark over its neighbor). Baselines accepted: component-surface (brand-mark plans move, 74 members) and the paint census (brand-mark 15 → 11 edge strokes).

## (2026-10-29) — Update file: an engine update makes a set due only when its drawing would change (#3082 part 1, Q811 A)

**Status:** plugin main thread and shared studio shell. ENGINE patch (change note). CONTRACT unchanged. The executor is
unchanged, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What changed

- **The ledger records the drawing, not only the version.** Each as-built entry (`apps/plugin/src/as-built-ledger.ts`)
  now carries a print of the plans the set was drawn from (`printOf`): one 64-bit hash of the projection, which decides,
  and per part a 4-hex chunk per facet (size, color, text, effects, layout, contents) plus one for the plans' own
  fields, which only word the reason. Build records it from the plans it hands the executor (`project`); the in-place
  update from each target's plans. The record format stays `v: 1`: a print is an optional field, so an older plugin
  reads the record as before.
- **What is due (`dueOf`).** Same engine and revision: as before (current, or due for its definition). Engine moved,
  revision not: the set's plans are projected now, against the same brand the read uses, and printed; the same print is
  `current`, another is `due` for the engine with what moved (`movedOf`: each part and facet, parts added and dropped,
  the variants). Only those sets are projected (`needsPrint`), a set at a time with the thread handed back between them
  (`fileSets`). An entry with no print (one from before this change) reads `due` for the engine with nothing named once
  the engine has moved past it, so the next update records it with its print (below).
- **An entry from before this change heals in one update** (review finding 1). Built: keep it `due` for the engine,
  the pre-Q811 behavior, with no `moved` list and its own line, DRAFT: "Engine update: recorded before Prism3 noted what
  it drew". A due set is ticked, the apply acts on it whether or not a member changes, and records it with its print.
  The review's first proposal, recording from the apply the unrecorded sets its scoped check read up to date, was not
  built: those sets are outside the apply's `defs`, so its hash guard (the file moved since the check) does not cover
  them and it would record from a check it did not re-verify; and when the check finds nothing to change, as after a
  patch that moves no plan, there is no apply at all, so nothing would record them. Reading them "Not checked yet" was
  also untrue: they were recorded.
- **The reason line** is worded in the panel (`engineWhy`, `state/update-file.ts`), DRAFT: "Engine update: focus ring
  size", "Engine update: label text and color, adds leading icon", three items at most, then how many more. A revision
  move reads "Engine update: Prism3 draws components differently"; a setting stays "Due · its settings changed".
- **The quiet re-record waits for a write.** Chosen over writing at load: the read at load (and each checklist opening)
  is a read, and a read that wrote the file's root plugin data would make opening the plugin an edit of the document, be
  refused on a file the person can only view, and, for the panel's read, record against a brand not yet applied (Q699
  A). So a set current by its print shows as current at once, and `restampQuiet` (`main.ts`) records it under today's
  engine after the next Apply Theme, build or update apply (not after the update's check, which is a read). It records
  against the stored brand only the sets whose plans print as recorded, so it is right after any write. It also gives an
  entry from before this change, under today's engine, its print (`q811/migrate`). Until then each load prints the stale sets again.

### Q811.1 — does an executor revision still make every set due? Decided: yes (A)

**Decided A (owner, 2026-10-27, Q820 A); C filed as #3101.** An `EXECUTOR_REVISION` change keeps every recorded set
due, as built. The follow-up, #3101, records which sets each executor change reaches, so only those come up.

```text
Q811.1. An EXECUTOR_REVISION move: due, or read by the plan?
   A (owner) Every recorded set is due ("Engine update: Prism3 draws components differently"). A plan print cannot
             see the executor: the revision moves exactly when the code that turns a plan into layers moves
             (executor-revision.ts: 7 of 22 pipeline commits changed the executor alone and moved no plan byte), and
             the update's own dry run reads every member stamped under another revision as one to update
             (update-plan.ts, revField !== rev). Calling such a set current would hide a drawing change and disagree
             with the full check and the agent's update-components.
   B         Read a revision move by the plan print, as an engine move. Fewer due sets; misses executor-only
             drawing fixes until the set's plan next moves.
   C (#3101) A revision names the sets it reaches (a declared list beside EXECUTOR_REVISION, lint-enforced), and
             only those are due. Precise, but a new declaration for every executor change: its own PR.
```

The evidence for C: `EXECUTOR_REVISION` rose 36 times between 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-26, about twice a day, so under A
almost every release between two of the owner's rebuilds still marks every set due, now with a reason that says why.
Q811 A's saving lands on releases that move only `ENGINE_VERSION`.

### Integration with #3096 (the live badge) and #3111 (open loads no page)

Both landed on main first, in the agreed order, and #3096's entry recorded what this PR owes them.

- **`fileDue` prints** (#3096's recount): `needsPrint`, the prints a set at a time, then `dueOf(…, print)`, against
  the panel's brand, as `fileSets` does. Without it, `print` defaults to `() => null` and an engine-moved printed set
  reads `unrecorded`: the badge would not count a set the checklist lists as Due. Git merges `main.ts` clean there and
  the plugin typechecks either way, so the arm below is the only thing that holds it.
- **`ledgerSets` prints too** (#3111's answer at open), against the stored brand, as the full read after it does.
  Chosen over leaving it print-less: a print projects plans in memory and loads no page, so open stays page-load-free
  (`test-open-large-file.ts`: 12 of the stand-in's entries are recorded with a print under an older engine, so
  `open/ready` reaches the print path, and `open/printed` holds that they read current from it); without one, every printed set under a moved engine reads
  `unrecorded` ("not checked yet") at open and the first answer disagrees with the full read on what is due. On a large
  file the full read waits on every page (about 20 s on the 60-page reference master), so the ledger's answer is the
  only correct one the panel has for that long. The cost is time to that first answer, measured below.
- **Prints are memoized across reads** (`printMemo`, `main.ts`), by the materialized def's JSON, the same identity the
  ledger's `def` hash uses: a set's plans are a function of that def, and the engine's code is fixed for the session.
  So the ledger's answer, the full read and each recount project a stale set once per distinct brand, not once each.
  Bounded at 256 prints. `printYielding` hands the thread back only after a projection: a yield per memoized set made
  each recount wait on 56 timers (about 105 ms median before, 29 ms after).

Measured in Node, not asserted: 56 buildable sets present, every entry printed under an older engine, the example brand
stored, the panel one lever apart (`density: compact`), 70 pages at no load cost:

| Read | Before (no print) | With prints |
|---|---|---|
| Ledger answer at open (0 pages loaded) | about 10 ms | 1.0 s: 56 sets projected, about 16 ms each, yielding between |
| Full read's due step after it | | 6 ms: every print memoized |
| First recount, the panel one lever apart | 11.8 ms median (#3096) | 0.93 s: the 56 sets the lever moves project again |
| Each recount after that, same brand (50 runs) | | median 28.8 ms, p90 38.7 ms, max 45 ms |
| Recount with the panel on the stored brand, after open | | 20.7 ms |
| First recount with no read before it (cold memo) | | 1.1 s; then 31 ms median |

So the first recount after an engine move projects every stale set the panel's brand moves, once; the memo then holds
(`q810/memo`). The badge's 250 ms debounce is unchanged.

### Gates and mutations

Each mutation was made on a committed tree and failed by name:

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| `dueOf` calls any engine move due (the pre-Q811 rule) | `test-as-built-ledger.ts`: "q811/same-plan: an engine version bump with an identical plan leaves the set current", "q811/quiet" |
| `dueOf` calls an engine move current whatever the print | `test-as-built-ledger.ts`: "q811/changed-plan: a changed plan makes the set due for the engine, naming what moved", "q811/parts" |
| `dueOf` reads a revision move by the print, as an engine move | `test-as-built-ledger.ts`: "q811/executor: an executor revision bump with an identical plan still makes the set due (Q811.1)" |
| `fileSets` calls `restampQuiet` (a write at load) | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q811/load: the read records nothing; the quiet re-record waits for a write" |
| `restampQuiet` a no-op | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q811/restamp: the next write records the quiet set under today's engine" |
| The update records no print, and `restampQuiet` a no-op | `test-build-completed.ts`: "ledger/print" (either alone is covered by the other) |
| `engineWhy` drops the facets | `test-update-file.ts`: "Q811 A why: an engine update names the part and what moved in it" |
| Review finding 1: `dueOf` reads a print-less entry under a moved engine `unrecorded` | `test-as-built-ledger.ts`: "old entry: an entry with no print, once the engine has moved past it, reads due for the engine …"; `test-build-completed.ts`: "q811/unprinted: a print-less entry under an older engine reads due for the engine" |
| Review M5: the deciding hash drops `paints` | `test-as-built-ledger.ts`: "q811/facet color: a plan that moved only in container's paints makes the set due for the engine, naming color" |
| Review M6: `fileSets` prints against the stored brand (`printNow()`) | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q811/panel brand: under an engine move, a lever changed in the panel and not yet applied makes the set due …" |
| `dueWhy` words a missing list as an empty one | `test-update-file.ts`: "#3090 finding 1 why: an engine update over a set recorded with no print says so …" |
| The adapter invents an empty `moved` list | `test-write-adapter.ts`: "file-sets with an engine due reading and no moved list keeps the set due with none" |
| `restampQuiet`'s stale filter loses `!ledger[id].print` (review's nit) | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q811/migrate: the next write gives a print-less entry under today's engine its print" |
| `fileDue` calls `dueOf` without `printNow(input)` (#3096 into #3090) | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q810/engine: under an older engine, a printed set whose plans the panel's brand changes is due for the engine, and the badge counts it …" and "q810/engine control: … is current, and the badge does not count it" (both read `unrecorded`) |
| `ledgerSets` calls `dueOf` without the print | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q810/engine at open: the ledger's answer at open prints the engine-moved set as the full read does …" (`unrecorded` vs due) |
| `ledgerSets` calls `dueOf` without the print, on the large-file stand-in | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "open/printed: the 12 sets recorded with a print under an older engine, plans unchanged, are printed at open and read current" (`unrecorded`) |
| `printYielding` calls `figma.loadAllPagesAsync()` after each projection | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "open/ready: the panel's first answer lands with no page loaded" (60 of 60) |
| The test's wait for a panel-driven write's tail removed (#3131 releases the guard at the verdict) | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q811/panel brand: …" (5 of 20 loaded runs, `{"state":"due","reason":"definition"}`) and "fixture: the panel's build reached the action table, and the test waited out its tail" (20 of 20) |
| `printNow` projects on every call (`printMemo` unused) | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q810/memo: a second recount against the same brand projects no plan again" (1 projected by the second) |

`paints` belongs in the deciding hash: a paint binding the engine moves is a drawing change. The hash is the whole
projection; the per-facet arms (`q811/facet <facet>`, one per facet plus the variants' own fields) hold that each
family of fields decides on its own. `q811/unprinted` drives finding 1 end to end through `main.ts`: due on the read,
not recorded by a write or the check, recorded with its print by the update's apply, current on the next read.

`test-write-adapter.ts` holds the wire reading of `moved`; `test:chrome`'s Update file arm shows the engine reason on
the checklist row.

### Gaps

- Nothing was run in Figma. Projecting every stale set at load is untimed there; in Node all 57 buildable defs project
  in about 0.85 s, and the ledger's answer at open waits on them (above).
- A set whose definition moved for a lever and for the engine in one release reads as an engine update: the ledger
  holds no brand to tell the two apart.
- The reason names parts by their plan names ("container", "focus ring"), and facets coarsely; it cannot say "now 2px",
  as the ledger keeps hashes, not values. Wording is DRAFT (Q2909.10 A).

## (2026-10-29) — Brand mark build: no false artboard misses on logos drawn at their own width (#3127)

**Status:** plugin executor and the paste executor. ENGINE patch (change note). CONTRACT unchanged.
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` 40 → 41: `write-components.ts`'s code moved, so `lint-executor-revision.ts` requires it.

### Diagnosis

The issue suspected the read-back assumed a square artboard. It does not: each glyph's expected box is the plan's own
`glyphViewBox`, which is already right per kind (square for icons, `social/` and `provider/`; the mark's own width ×
24 for `logo/`; 32 × 20 for `payment/`). The defect was precision. Figma stores a node's width and height as 32-bit
floats, and the read-back compared them with `!==` against the plan's double. A logo whose width float32 cannot hold
exactly comes back a hair off: 34.97 reads 34.970001220703125, the number in the owner's report.

All 7 misses are `logo/` marks, and exactly the 7 whose widths are not exact in binary: amex (34.97), apple-pay
(25.51), discover (53.85), paypal (10.17), paypal-wordmark (49.49), shop-pay (27.27) and visa (27.4). The other 7
logos are integers or exact binary fractions (32.5, 34, 18.75, 25.5, 36, 39.75, 24) and passed. Every `payment/`
tile is 32 × 20 and passed. Measured from the plans with `Math.fround`, and reproduced in the shim: the exact compare
reports these 7 and only these.

### What changed

- **The artboard read-back compares at Figma's precision** (`atArtboard`, `ARTBOARD_TOLERANCE` = 0.001,
  `write-components.ts`), on both the fresh build and the in-place import, and in the paste executor's twin
  (`anatomy-figma.ts`). float32's error at these sizes is under 1e-5; a glyph sized to its ink misses by whole
  pixels.
- **The miss names its kind's box.** A square glyph keeps "every host binding a square would distort it"; any other
  says "a host binding its 27.4x24 box would distort it". Before, a logo's miss blamed a square it never had.
- **The shim's importer can store float32.** Neither shim modeled it, which is why no gate saw this. The arms wrap
  the importer to store the artboard at float32 instead of changing the shared shims: rounding every `resize` in them
  would move geometry many other gates read.

### Gates and mutations

Each mutation was made on a committed tree and failed by name:

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| `atArtboard` back to the exact compare | `test-write-components.ts`: "#3127 at its own width: every brand mark imported at float32 reads back at its artboard …" (7 misses, the 7 logos above) |
| `atArtboard` passes anything | `test-write-components.ts`: "#3127 sized to its ink: a square-kind mark (provider/apple) … fails, named" and "… a logo whose frame is sized to its ink still fails, named for its own box" |
| The paste executor's compare back to `!==` | `test.ts`: "#3127 paste at its own width: a 34.97 × 24 logo imported at float32 …" |
| The paste executor's read-back dropped | `test.ts`: "#3127 paste ink: a square-kind mark and a logo whose frames are sized to their ink each still miss …" |

### Gaps

- Nothing was run in Figma. The float32 reading is the host's documented storage and the owner's numbers match it
  digit for digit; a fresh BrandMark build in Figma should now report no artboard miss.
- The `EXECUTOR_REVISION` raise makes every recorded set due for the executor on the next open (Q811.1, Q820 A),
  although only the read-back moved and no member's output did. #3101 would narrow that.

Engine 0.238.0. Owner decisions 2026-10-27 on #3077: Q802 A (title.2xs is 18px on mobile), Q803 B (label
moves to +1% too), caption A and tracking A.

### What changed
- **`typography.sizes.caption`** (caption A): md and lg take one brand-level size each. The value must be a ladder
  step, at least `CAPTION_SIZE_FLOOR` (10px), and the caption ramp stays strictly increasing. caption.xs and caption.sm

- **`typography.tracking`** (tracking A): `Partial<Record<TypeGroup, LetterSpacingKey>>`. A pinned text type uses that

  24–56 with their mobile sizes, sizeFloor 8) plus the patch: titleFloor 16, title.2xs 20 / 18 mobile, caption.md 10,
  display/title/body/caption/label pinned to `open`, and `trackingShift` reduced to `eyebrow: -1`. Leading stays on the
  engine default, as the seed's owner note says. The legacy fixture takes caption.md 10 and the tracking pin + eyebrow
  nudge only.

  nudges, both DRAFT copy), the prism3-theme skill, `.ai.json` notes.
- **The 10px caption floor's refusal.** While caption md is set to 10px, the 10px floor would add caption sm at 10px
  below it, which the engine refuses (the ramp must strictly increase). The Type page now disables that chip and draws

### Why a pin, not a nudge
No nudge reaches +1% (`open` was kept off the nudge path in #2322 so nudging brands don't move), and display's derived
rung splits at 96px, so one nudge can never make display uniform. The pin replaces both for the category it names and
nothing else; re-anchoring three roles (the issue's route B) would have made `snug` and `normal` mean +1% for the brand.

### Held for the owner
- **The legacy fixture's title.2xs.** Its type is the engine default (title.xs 18), so a 20px 2xs can't sit below it.
  It stays without one; pinning the stored title ramp into the fixture would be a wider change than this issue.
- The field-message glyph beside a 10px caption is for the orchestrator to re-check in Figma.
- The 10px caption floor's refusal wording (DRAFT): "Caption md is 10px, which you set individually, so the engine
  refuses a second 10px caption."

### Traps

  and caption.md are held to the decided values written in the test, code still to the fixture.

## (2026-10-28) — Update file: a fresh file's update-everything run no longer stops at its second set (#3128)

**Status:** plugin and panel fix, a new plugin test (`test-update-fresh.ts`) and a `test:chrome` arm (section 10). ENGINE
patch (change note): no committed artifact, emission or component surface moves. The executor is unchanged, so
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What the owner hit

A new, empty file, the example brand, Update file with every box ticked. Set up file landed, the theme landed, and Icon's
45 components landed. Then the run sat on BrandMark for good: no `brand-mark/*` component, no as-built ledger, and a
main thread that still answered the mailbox in 1 ms.

### Diagnosis: not BrandMark, and not a promise in the plugin

Nothing in BrandMark's build hangs. In the shim it builds in about 150 ms. BrandMark is simply the **second** set in
catalog order, the first one the panel's build queue (`runAfterResult`, #2700) posts **after** another set's result.

- `buildComponents` posts its verdict, then awaits the settle probe (`verdictBeforeSettle`, #908): console telemetry
  that writes nothing.
- The run guard (#1957) holds `build-components` until the whole function returns, so it holds through the probe.
- The queue posts BrandMark the moment Icon's verdict lands, inside that window. The plugin answers `refused`.
- The panel's reducer keeps a request refused behind the panel's own run `pending`, waiting for that run's verdict. Icon's
  verdict had already arrived, so nothing came. The queue's run never ended and Components read BrandMark as building
  for good.

The empty ledger fits: Icon is an `emitAsComponents` def, and its result's `id` is `''`, so `recordSets` never runs for it.

The same window also refused Update file's `update` step when it followed the sets step, and a Build clicked straight
after a single build's verdict.

The behavior reproduces through the real `main.ts` in the shim, at main and at the owner's build (`11175559`, the last
merge before the build's 11:26Z stamp). Each set is posted once, the moment the last answer lands. Icon is answered;
BrandMark is answered `refused`.

### The fix

- **Plugin (`run-guard.ts`, `main.ts`).** The guard gains `release(cmd)`, and `buildComponents` releases the build's guard
  right after its verdict posts. Everything after that point is telemetry. Holds are now tokens, so a run's own `finally`
  never releases a later run's hold. A next build can now start while the last one's settle probe is still sampling.
  That probe's number then measures some of the next build's work too, which is acceptable for a diagnostic.
- **Panel (`apps/studio/src/main.ts`).** No step of a run may wait on a verdict that will not come. When the host refuses a
  set the build queue posted, `runRefused` ends the run. That set is recorded as failed with the host's words, the rest
  as not built, and the Build set row stops running. Update file's sets step already ended on the same refusal.

### Tests

- `apps/plugin/test-update-fresh.ts` (in the plugin's `test`). A fresh file, Set up file, then every buildable set in
  the panel's catalog order, each posted once, straight after the last answer. Each must be answered by a
  `component-result`, and Update file's `update-sets` straight after the last must be answered by a
  `component-update-result`. Mutation: the `guard.release` call removed → `sets/brand-mark: answered by
  component-result` and `update/after the last set: …`, both refused.
- `test:chrome` section 10. Two sets ticked; the first lands and the second is refused. Update file must be free, the
  Build set row must not be running, and its summary must carry the host's words. Mutation: the `runRefused` call in
  `handleHostMessage` removed → `#3128: a set the host refuses ends the run…`.

## (2026-10-28) — Settings search reaches every lever, Dialog surface included, and Color links to it (#3093)

The owner searched for the dialog color and found nothing. Dialog surface (`raisedSurface`) lives in Components ›
Dialog › Dialog options, and Components' search never looked at its settings.

### The cause

Each page searches its own levers. Components' search (`domains/components.ts`) filtered only the **set rows**
(`rowMatches`: a row's label, its page and its sets' names). The settings blocks after a section's sets (Button, Field,
Search, Tag, Dialog and Banner options) were never searched, and they stay closed until opened by hand. So "dialog" kept
the Dialog section for its one set, with its block closed ("1 setting matches", and no lever in view), and "dialog
surface", "white" and `raisedSurface` matched nothing.

### The fix

- **Components searches its blocks' levers.** `leverBlock` already builds each lever's searchable words (`said`: label,
  description, key). It now records them by the block's element (`saidOf`), so the Components page reads them from
  whatever its blocks drew, with no list of keys to keep. A section shows when a set row or a lever in one of its blocks
  matches; the search opens a block that holds a match, the way it opens a family (call 7 on #2812), and the block shows
  only the matching levers. Each matching lever counts as a hit. The shared block also matches a lever's key. A block
  redraws its levers after an edit, so the page filters again after `brand` and `mode`.
- **The sweep found four more gaps, outside Components.** It searches every lever's manifest label on every page.
  - A page that draws its own label or description hid the manifest's words from search: Page surfaces (drawn as
    Background fills), Font families and Disabled contrast. `leverBlock` now adds the manifest's label and description
    to `said` when the page replaces them.
  - Two blocks hid themselves unless one of their rows matched, even when the block's own words matched: Font families
    and Interactive palettes.
  - Underlined link styles and Italic-only text types have no block of their own. Their words now ride on the block
    that draws their control (`alsoSays`, as Pin a neutral's ride on Neutral hue's since #2175).
- **Color › Surfaces & fills links to the setting.** Before this PR, the page drew no row for `foreground.raised`. The
  "set by Dialog surface" reason lived only in `test-fills-input.ts`. Scrim now ends with a read-only row for the panel
  over the scrim: its swatch, its name and role, and in place of the picker a link, "Set by Dialog surface". The link
  opens Components › Dialog options and focuses Dialog surface's checked chip, as Field options' link to Control shape
  does. The row's name ("Dialog panel") and the link's words are **DRAFT** for the owner.

### The gate

`test:chrome` section `6b` (shard 3, so `test:chrome-shards` holds it to one shard):

- **Sweep.** It reads every lever from the manifest (`levers.ts`, committed as `schema/lever-manifest.json`), visits
  every place, and searches each lever's label. Each lever must show on exactly one page, its home. A typed sample pins
  labels and homes, Dialog surface first, plus every Components block the issue audits. A typed `SEARCH_STANDS_IN`
  names the levers whose control sits in another lever's block: three at first, and Outline hover fill once #3105 landed (its block draws only under the opaque fill; Outline hover's description names it).
- **The issue's four queries.** On Components, "dialog", "dialog surface", "white" and `raisedSurface` each show Dialog
  surface.
- **The Color row.** On both hosts, the row is read-only, the link reads "Set by Dialog surface", and the link lands on
  Components with Dialog options open, Dialog surface in view and its checked chip focused.

Mutations, each on a `wip:` commit, each failing by name:

- Components ignores block levers → the four queries and seven Components levers, e.g. `searching "Dialog surface"
  shows raisedSurface's lever on one page, its home (shown on no page)`.
- The manifest relabels Dialog surface → `raisedSurface's label is "Dialog surface"`.
- The link no longer opens the block → `the link opens Components › Dialog options…`.
- The link's words change → `…its "Set by Dialog surface" a link`.
- The manifest's words are dropped from `said` → Page surfaces, Font families and Disabled contrast.

The new row joins the suite's existing literal lists: `READONLY_ROW_ROLES` (section 18) and `FILLS_LEVERS_CONTROLS`, and,
as a "way to" link that edits nothing, the derived-mode exceptions (`RO_EXCEPTIONS`, section 35; `FILLS_STAYS_LIVE` in
section 18's Q59 arm, which also asserts the link stays live).

### Left as is

Search is still per page, as S1.2 built it. A lever is found on its home page, not from another page. Cross-page
results are a design call for the owner, not part of this fix.

## (2026-10-28) — Radio dot size, one brand setting: the reference brand's dot is 14px at medium (#3086 part 1, Q816 A)

**What.** A new value lever, `radioDot` (Default = 50, then 60 / 70 / 80): the checked radio's dot as a share of
the box edge, applied to sm, md and lg alike, snapped to the 2px sub-grid and capped at the box minus its 2px ring.
It moves the values of the existing `control.size.{sm,md,lg}.dot` only, so no token name is added and
`CONTRACT_VERSION` holds (`token-contract --check` and `lint-contract-version` both clean). The reference brand sets 70
in `nbThemeFrom` and in `examples/nb-redesign.design.md`. Its home is a new Radio section on the Components page,
Radio options, in the Studio and the plugin. Copy is a DRAFT.

| Share | compact 12/16/20 | comfortable 16/20/24 | spacious 20/24/28 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 (Default) | 6/8/10 | 8/10/12 | 10/12/14 |
| 60 | 8/10/12 | 10/12/14 | 12/14/16 |
| 70 | 8/12/14 | **12/14/16** (the reference brand) | 14/16/20 |
| 80 | 8/12/16 | 12/16/20 | 16/20/22 |

**The diagnosis that decided the snap.** "Snapped to the dimension ladder" and "14 at medium" cannot both hold on the
reference brand's own grid: its comfortable `core.dimension.*` runs 10, 12, 16, so the nearest step to 14 is a tie
between 12 and 16. Feeding 14 into the grid (as #910 fed the half-dot px) mints `core.dimension.14`, a new
brand-dependent path that `token-contract --check` reports, against the owner's "no new token". So the dot snaps to the
2px sub-grid the control corner already rides (`snap2`, #1015). A dot on the grid aliases its step (sm 12, lg 16); one
off it is a plain px through `controlLeaf`'s literal branch (md 14), flagged `offScale` with the share on its
extension. The grid keeps feeding the DEFAULT half dot whatever the setting says, so moving the setting removes no
primitive either (`core.dimension.10` is guaranteed).

**Default brands byte-identical.** At 50 `radioDotPx` is `edge × 0.5` exactly, not a rounding that happens to agree,
and the Theme carries no `radioDot`. `regen` moved only the reference brand's files.

**Gates (test.ts 19h).** G1 the reference brand's dot is 12/14/16 in DTCG and in the Figma control collection, for the
legacy fixture and the seed. G2 every default corpus brand's dot is half its box with the #910 line and no share, and
`radioDot: 50` written out is byte-identical to unset. G3 nine share × density brands against a hand-worked table, per
rung. G4 dot ≤ box − 2 × ring, the ring read from `border-width.thick` and Radio.Control's binding. G5 (from review)
a dark mode with its own density carries the share, read from the dot leaf's `modes.dark` entry against the same hand
table. G6 (from review) the Figma dot line names the share, read from the emitted control collection. Mutations M1–M7
in the block header, each failing by name. `test-component-groups.ts` holds the Radio section to the defs that nest
`radio-control`, and pins the defs binding `control.size.*.dot` to Radio.Control, Badge and List.Item.

**Trap for later.** Badge's dot and List's bullet bind the same tokens, so the reference brand's badge dot is now 12
(was 8) and its bullets 12/14/16. That follows from "no new token" and is named in the lever's description. Splitting
them off would need a new token. At sm the 70% dot (12 in 16) fills the ring's inside with no gap. Both are open for
the owner on the PR.

## (2026-10-28) — Interactive: the Outline hover chips keep their rows whatever is picked (#3115)

**Status:** studio/plugin UI fix (one shared implementation) + a `test:chrome` section (`3115`, shard 1). No engine
change, so no change note: no committed artifact, emission or component surface moves. CONTRACT unchanged. No wording
changes: where Outline hover lives and how it reads is the owner's, held on #3116.

### What changed

- **The bug:** on Color › Interactive, picking "Neutral overlay wash" dropped "No hover fill" to a second row. The
  selected chip of a `.p3-choice` is bold, and since #1975 a chip is never narrower than its label
  (`min-width: fit-content`), so the selected chip grew by the bold label's extra width (192px against 188px for
  "Neutral overlay wash"). Where the four chips only just fit on one row, those few pixels moved the wrap. "Solid fill"
  (#3105's fourth option) does the same. The fourth option is the trigger only because four chips need about 575px,
  which puts the one-row edge inside ordinary window widths (about 1627 to 1631px in the headless browser's fonts).
- **The fix:** every option of a `.p3-choice` reserves its label's bold width. `choice()` and the style guide's `seg()`
  write the label to `data-label`, and `chrome.css` draws it again as `::after`, bold, hidden, with no height and
  empty alternative text, under the label in a column. The selection then never changes any chip's width. This covers
  every `choice` in the chrome, not only Outline hover. Renders at 1280 and 380 are pixel-identical to `main` on both
  hosts. The only layout that moves is at the edge, where the four now take two rows whatever is picked, instead of
  one or two depending on the pick.
- **The fallback is unchanged:** where four don't fit (1280: two rows of two; 380: one, two, one), the chips wrap, as
  every `choice` has since #1975. That is the chrome's fallback for a choice too wide for its column. Switching to a
  select by width would be a new control behavior, and it belongs with #3116's rethink.

### The arm and its mutations

- `test:chrome` section `3115`: on both hosts, at 1280, at 380, and at the chips' own tightest one-row width, each of
  the four options is picked in turn and the chips' rows (distinct tops) are read. The rows must not change with the
  pick. The tightest width holds the group at its `max-content` width, read with "No hover fill" picked, so the edge
  does not hang on a font's metrics. A fixed window cannot catch this: the band where `main` breaks is about 4px wide.
  The arm also checks each radio is named by its label once, because the reserved copy is generated content.
- On the unfixed rule (the `::after` content removed), it fails by name:
  `#3115 web tightest: the Outline hover chips keep their rows whatever is picked — none 1, overlay-neutral 2,
  solid-tint 1, opaque-fill 2`, and the same on figma. At 1280 and 380 alone it passes on `main` too, because the
  chips wrap there whatever is picked.
- With the copy visible and no empty alternative text, it fails by name:
  `#3115 web 1280: each option is named by its label once (… radio "Neutral overlay wash Neutral overlay wash" …)`, on
  every host and width.

## (2026-10-28) — Update file's badge counts everything it would change, live (#3081, Q810 A)

**Status:** plugin panel and main thread. ENGINE patch (change note). CONTRACT unchanged. The executor is unchanged, so
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What changed

- **The badge counts what Update file would change (Q810 A, the owner's decision of 2026-10-27).** It counts the
  component sets due against the brand the panel holds (Q699 A), plus one item for Theme changes the file does not hold
  yet (`badgeCount`, `state/update-file.ts`). The button's accessible name says the same count ("Update file, 3 due").
  Before this, the badge was the ledger read at load, against the stored brand. It did not move when a setting changed,
  and it never counted Theme.
- **A cheap recount, its own message.** The panel sends `due-request` with its brand and a sequence number. It sends it
  after a setting changes (`brand`, and `identity` for a name typed without a rebuild) and after each write's verdict
  (`DUE_AFTER`). It waits 250 ms after the last change of a burst (`DUE_DEBOUNCE_MS`), so a drag or quick clicks ask
  once. The main thread answers with `file-due` (`fileDue`, `main.ts`): one root read for the ledger, one for the stored
  brand, and each present set materialized once. It reuses the sets the last `presentDefs` found (`presentCache`), so it
  never loads every page or walks the file, and it never runs the full check. A write starting or ending clears that
  cache (`guarded`), so the next recount reads the file again. The panel keeps the newest answer by sequence.
- **Apply Theme does not reset the `isDirty` baseline.** That was unverified in #3007's entry. `provenance` is
  reassigned only by a load (`loadInput`, `initSession`, `clearOrigin`); `apply-result` leaves it alone. So the Theme
  item does not come from `isDirty`. It comes from the main thread's reading of the file's stored brand (`holdsInput`,
  `persist-figma.ts`): both brands go through the same serialize and parse, compared with keys sorted. Apply Theme stores
  the brand it wrote (`persistInput`, `apply-theme.ts`), so the recount after Apply drops the Theme item. An agent's
  Apply counts the same way, because the answer reads the file, not the panel's own record.
- **No count before a brand is chosen.** On a fresh or library file the load's `file-sets` can land before the host's
  restore answers, while the panel holds only the boot placeholder. The panel neither asks nor shows a live answer until
  a brand is chosen and resolves (`liveShown`). Found by the independent review. The same holds after a failed restore
  (a stored brand the engine refuses in resolution): a setting change asks nothing, and the badge keeps the load's read.
- **The checklist is untouched.** It still reads its own `file-sets` and `update-check` answers, so #3028's Theme-unticked
  behavior (Q701 B) holds. A live answer landing while the checklist is open moves the badge and nothing in the
  checklist.

### Measurements

The recount, in Node, at the largest size it can see: all 57 buildable sets present, a full ledger, the example brand
stored, the panel's brand one lever apart, 50 runs. Median 11.8 ms, p90 13.2 ms, max 41.5 ms; the stored-brand compare
alone is 0.2 ms. It does not grow with the file's size, because the page load and the document-wide search are skipped
(`q810/cheap`: 0 page loads per recount). With the debounce, a burst of edits costs one recount.

### Gates and mutations

Each mutation was made on a committed tree and failed by name:

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| `badgeCount` drops the Theme item | `test-update-file.ts`: "Q810 A badge: unapplied Theme changes count as one item …" |
| `badgeCount` reads the load's read over the recount | `test-update-file.ts`: "Q810 A badge: it rises when a setting changes …" |
| The reduce keeps an older `file-due` answer | `test-update-file.ts`: "Q810 A recount: an answer overtaken by a newer request never shows" |
| `fileDue` reads the stored brand whatever the panel sends | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q810/rises" |
| `fileDue` reads the file's sets every time | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q810/cheap" |
| `guarded` keeps the cached sets after a write | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q810/after a write" |
| `holdsInput` compares without sorting keys | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q810/theme" |
| Apply Theme stores no brand (`apply-theme.ts`) | `test:readback-parity`: "#3081: before Apply Theme the fresh file holds no brand; after it, the file holds the brand applied …" |
| `recountDue` asks at once, no debounce (`apps/studio/src/main.ts`) | `test:chrome`: "IA2 figma … Q810 A: three quick changes ask for the count once …" ("3 asked") |
| No recount on `brand` | `test:chrome`: "IA2 figma … Q810 A: three quick changes ask for the count once …" ("0 asked") and "… the badge rises on a setting change …" |
| `DUE_AFTER` emptied | `test:chrome`: "IA2 figma … Q810 A: after a run, the panel asks for the count again …" and "… the badge drops after a run …" |
| The shell paints the load's read (`badgeCount(…, null)`) | `test:chrome`: "IA2 figma … Q810 A: the badge rises on a setting change …" |
| The checklist reads the live answer for its due sets | `test:chrome`: "IA2 figma … #3028 Q701 B: with Theme unticked, a live answer landing while the checklist is open …" |
| `liveShown` reduced to `!restoreFailure` (asks with the boot placeholder) | `test:chrome`: "IA2 figma … Q810 A: before a brand is chosen … the panel asks for no count and shows no live answer …" ("early":1) |
| `!restoreFailure &&` dropped from `liveShown` (review's MC) | `test:chrome`: "IA2 figma … Q810 A: after a failed restore (the stored brand does not resolve), a setting change asks for no count …" ("asked":1, badge "4"), light and dark |
| `guarded`'s end-of-write clear dropped, the start clear kept (review's MF) | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q810/mid-write: a recount asked during a write answers from the sets cached mid-write …" (0 page loads after) |
| No recount on `identity` (`subscribe('identity', recountDue)` dropped; review's MID) | `test:chrome`: "IA2 figma … Q810 A: a brand name typed with no setting changed asks for the count once, after the debounce, carrying the new name …" ("asked":0), light and dark |
| `fileDue`'s `catch` posts no `error` (review's MX) | `test-build-completed.ts`: "q810/error: a recount whose read of the file fails answers with the error, and nothing due" ("error":null) |
| `recountDue` sends `dueSeq`, not `++dueSeq`: every ask goes out as 0 (review's MS) | `test:chrome`: "IA2 figma … Q810 A: two asks in a row carry a rising number, the later one higher" ([0,0]), light and dark |

The chrome rows ran as mutated builds in the same worktree, each rebuilt and restored, never pushed.

### Owed by #3090 (due by plan), which lands after this

The agreed order is #3089, this PR, then #3090. #3090 gives `dueOf` a fourth argument, `print`, defaulting to
`() => null`, and with no print a printed entry under a moved engine reads `unrecorded`, never `due`. `fileDue` here
calls `dueOf(…, ledgerNow(input))` with three arguments, and nothing flags it: git merges `main.ts` clean and the plugin
typechecks. So when #3090 lands, it owes:

- `fileDue` passing `printNow(input)` into `dueOf`, as `fileSets` does (`needsPrint` with `breathe()`, then the print);
- a `q810` arm in `test-build-completed.ts`: a printed entry under an older `ENGINE_VERSION` whose plan the panel's brand
  changes is counted, and the same entry with an unchanged plan is not;
- the recount's cost measured again: a print projects each engine-moved set's plans (about 0.85 s for every def in
  Node, by #3090's review), which the 11.8 ms median above does not include, and `q810/cheap` counts page loads only.

Without the first, the badge never counts an engine-moved set whose drawing changed, while the checklist lists it as
Due.

### Gaps

- Nothing was run in Figma. The recount's cost is measured in Node; inside Figma, the root reads are the only file access
  it makes.
- A set added or removed by hand is not seen by the recount until the next `file-sets` read (the checklist opening, or
  the read after a run) or a write.
- A file that holds no brand counts Theme as one item once a brand is chosen (Q810.1 on the PR, built as A).
- The badge's words ("3 due") are DRAFT, part of the pending wording pass (Q2909.10 A). This PR adds no new words.

## (2026-10-28) — Glass fills: a typed name, the shipped glass's row, and a picker that keeps its pick (#3106, Q827 A)

The owner's review of #3088's Glass section in the plugin (#3106) found four layout bugs and settled how a glass fill is named (Q827 A). Studio only: the engine, its validation and the emission are unchanged.

- **Q827 A, the name.** Add glass fill no longer names the fill (`card`, then `card-2`). It opens a Name field that starts empty, with the hint "e.g. card, header, overlay" (DRAFT), and previews the token, `color.glass.<name>`, as it is typed. `glassNameRefusal` (`state/glass-input.ts`) refuses an empty name, a name that isn't a lowercase slug (the engine's own `GLASS_ROLE_NAME`), `surface`, and a name the brand already has, each in its own line (every line a DRAFT). The check runs as the designer types and is drawn in place, so typing never redraws the page. Enter or Add adds the fill, and Escape or Cancel closes the field and writes nothing. Stored names keep working: the reference brand's `card` loads and renders unchanged.
- **The row.** An added fill is drawn as the Glass surface row: its swatch, then "Glass card" over `glass.card` through the shared `tokenLabel`, in the same type and on the same left edge. The remove button is a small square icon button on that line, as a gradient's is. Color and opacity sit on a line under the name. The old row put five children in `.p3-fillrow`'s three-column grid. The opacity field wrapped into the swatch column, which was the "empty swatch", and × stretched across the name column. The name was a `p3-hex-input`, which is uppercase. The row now has its own grid, so a snug pane keeps the remove button beside the name.
- **Diagnosis: the picker reading "Page color".** A plain pick reads back correctly on both hosts and after a reload, so the cause was timing. The name field committed a task after its `change` (`onCommitted`, #2487). A click on the color picker blurred the field, and the rename redrew the row while the menu was open. The pick then landed on the replaced `<select>`, whose handler still named the old fill, so `setGlassSource` found nothing and wrote nothing. The picker read the stored "Page color" though Card color had been chosen. Reproduced in the browser before the fix. The row has no rename field now, so this cannot recur. Renaming a fill is remove and add again; an in-row rename is left to the owner.
- **Gates.** `test-glass-input.ts` (new, in the studio `test` script) holds 17 typed names to literal verdicts and lines, checks that the engine's `brandTheme` agrees with every slug and `surface` verdict, covers Add's writes (nothing for a refused or empty name, no auto-name, order kept), and reads the reference brand's `card` from its design.md. `test:chrome` section 18 (shard 1, no new section) adds an arm for each of the five points. The picker arm includes a pick made on a select that the opacity commit has just replaced, and a figma-host restore of a file whose input holds `glassRoles.card`.
- **Mutations** (each on a `wip:` commit, each failing its arm by name): remove moved to the controls line → (1); the opacity field beside the swatch, and the controls line under the swatch → (2); the name in capitals → (3); a pick on a replaced select dropped, and the picker showing the wrong option → (4); no duplicate, `surface`, slug or empty check → the unit cases by name; auto-naming back, no token preview, and the duplicate refusal not drawn → (5).
- **Trap.** `test:chrome` reads the built bundles, so rebuild the studio and the plugin before a re-run. A mutation that moves `pf` above its `const` dies in the temporal dead zone and reads as a different failure.

## (2026-10-28) — prism3-rebind: slot defaults, stale slot handles, stalled import loops, plugin restarts, paragraph links

Four new trap rows for `skills/prism3-rebind` §4, and one widened row, from rebuilding a brand's sign-in and account-creation screens (14 screens across two breakpoints) onto a published Prism3 library:

- **Slot defaults:** a placed component's slot already holds sample content (tabs, list rows, a dialog body placeholder), so append the design's items first, then remove the samples and set the selected item.
- **Stale handles after a slot edit:** handles inside the same instance go stale once its slot changes, and a later `findOne` throws. Look up the other parts first and check `.removed`, the same idiom as stale references after a placement.
- **Serial import loops,** folded into the existing "A new library import never settles" row rather than a second row for the same trap: one stuck import stalls the whole loop (0 of 98 after 80s). In parallel, with per-item timeouts, 70 of 98 landed in 22s. While imports stall, take mains, styles and variables from instances already in the file, filtered by the library's collections, because a legacy library shared the name prefix.
- **Plugin restarts:** a restart clears `globalThis` (a UI reload doesn't), so keep the helpers in a resendable bootstrap.
- **Paragraph links:** in a long paragraph, text pieces plus `link` instances don't wrap. Use one text node with the emitted `*-link` text style on each link's range.

Documentation only: no engine or emission change.

## (2026-10-28) — Plugin open loads no page before the panel is ready (#3110)

**Status:** plugin main thread and the shared studio shell. ENGINE patch (change note). CONTRACT unchanged. The
executor is unchanged, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### The cause, measured

The owner saw the plugin and the file freeze for about 20 s on opening the plugin in the reference brand's master
(about 60 pages), on a fresh Figma session. It was not every time: Figma keeps a page loaded for the rest of a session,
so only the first open pays. The read at load, `file-sets` (#2909, #3007), called `presentDefs`, whose first line was
`figma.loadAllPagesAsync()`. Figma loads pages on the main thread, so that one call held the plugin and the canvas
until every page was in.

The stand-in (`apps/plugin/test-open-large-file.ts`) is a 60-page file in the shim: 6 dividers, 50 sets one per page,
and a root ledger naming 45 of them, 3 due. Loading a page burns `PAGE_MS` of main-thread time, as Figma's load does, and
the document-wide search refuses until `loadAllPagesAsync` was called, as under `dynamic-page`. At 330 ms a page,
which is the reference file's 20 s spread over 60 pages:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Panel's first answer (`file-sets`, the badge's count) | 19 810 ms, 60 pages loaded | 11 ms, 0 pages loaded |
| Most pages loaded in one turn of the main thread | 60 (19 800 ms held) | 1 (330 ms held) |
| Full read of the file's sets | is the first answer | 19 833 ms, one page a turn, after the panel is ready |
| Hand-edit pass done | 20 431 ms | 20 599 ms |

The stage that took the time is the page loads: 19 814 ms of the 19 822 ms `file-sets` stage. The ledger read took
0–1 ms, materializing and reading what is due 7–10 ms, the document-wide search 0–1 ms, and the hand-edit pass's own
work 766 ms (one member a set in the stand-in). The test runs at 20 ms a page by default (1211 ms → 11 ms to the
first answer, worst turn 60 pages → 1). The total work does not shrink. What changes is that none of it happens before
the panel is ready, and no turn holds the thread for more than one page.

### The fix

- **Open answers from the ledger alone (`ledgerSets`, `main.ts`).** At `ui-ready` the main thread reads the root ledger
  and posts `file-sets` with no page loaded. The sets it names are present, and what is due is read against the stored
  brand, as the read at load always was. It is marked `partial`: the ledger cannot see a set built before it or by hand,
  nor one deleted since, and `setUp` needs a document-wide search, so it is not read (sent false). The badge counts from
  it at once.
- **Pages load one per turn (`loadPagesYielding`).** Every place in `main.ts` that needs every page loads them this way:
  `presentDefs` (the full read after open, the checklist's own read, the hand-edit pass), the scoped check, Style
  guides' catalog, Build style guides and its cleanup, prune, and each write's entry. The agent link's component
  payloads (`mcp-steps.ts`) still call `loadAllPagesAsync` directly: the link is off by default, and they are out of
  scope here. It loads the pages one at a time with `breathe` between them, then
  calls `loadAllPagesAsync`. The executors' own `loadAllPagesAsync` calls, which run after their entry, then have
  nothing left to load. That last call has nothing left to load, but under `dynamic-page` the document-wide searches after
  it (`presentNames`, the update's `locateSets`) need it called.
- **The reads after open are tagged (`atOpen`).** The full read after open now yields, so a checklist opened during it
  can be answered first, under the panel's brand (Q699 A), while the read after open measures the stored brand. Both of
  the host's reads after open carry `atOpen`. A read after open never replaces an answer the panel asked for
  (`host-session.ts`), and the checklist never takes one as its answer (`awaitingRead`). Answers to a request stay
  untagged, as before. Before this, `loadAllPagesAsync` held the thread, so the read after open always landed first.
  The independent review found this race.
- **The panel shows Checking (DRAFT).** While the answer is partial, a set the ledger does not name reads Checking
  (`UPDATE_COPY.status.checking`, already a placeholder, Q2909.10 A), never Not in file. Update file's checklist waits on
  the full read with its existing "Checking the file…" (`awaitingRead`). A partial answer never replaces a full one
  (`host-session.ts`).
- **Stage timings, behind a flag.** `timed` in `main.ts` keeps each stage's time only when `PRISM3_OPEN_TIMINGS` is an
  array on the global. The stand-in sets it and prints the stages; a normal run times nothing.

Unchanged: the checklist still sends its own `file-sets-request` and reads under the panel's brand (Q699 A). Theme
unticked still reads the stored brand (#3028, Q701 B). The background hand-edit pass still runs after the full read.

### Gates and mutations

Each mutation was made on a committed `wip:` tree and failed by name:

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| `ui-ready` reads the file first (`fileSets()` in place of `ledgerSets()`) | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "open/ready: the panel's first answer lands with no page loaded" (60 of 60) |
| `loadPagesYielding` as one `loadAllPagesAsync` | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "open/yields: no turn of the event loop loads more than one page" (worst 60) |
| `ledgerSets` drops `partial` | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "open/partial: that answer says it is the ledger's alone" |
| `statusesOf` reads a partial answer's missing set as Not in file | `test-update-file.ts`: "#3110 status: at open, a set the ledger does not name reads Checking …" |
| `awaitingRead` ignores `partial` | `test-update-file.ts`: "#3110 checklist: it never opens on the answer at open …" |
| `host-session` lets a partial answer replace a full one | `test-host-session.ts`: "#3110: an answer at open arriving after a full read leaves the full read in place" |
| `host-session` lets a read after open replace an answer the panel asked for | `test-host-session.ts`: "#3110: the host's read after open, landing after an answer the panel asked for, leaves that answer in place" |
| `awaitingRead` takes a read after open as the checklist's answer | `test-update-file.ts`: "#3110 checklist: the host's read after open, landing after the checklist asked, is not its answer" |
| The full read after open posted untagged | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "open/full: the full read follows, tagged as the read after open …" |
| `styleGuideCatalog` back on one `loadAllPagesAsync` (asked mid-read) | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "open/yields: … the reads asked mid-read included" (worst 51) |
| `checkSets` back on one `loadAllPagesAsync` | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "entry/check: it loads every page, one per turn" (worst 60) |
| prune back on one `loadAllPagesAsync` | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "entry/prune: …" (worst 60) |
| `styleGuide` without `loadPagesYielding` (its run's own `loadAllPagesAsync` loads them) | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "entry/style-guide: …" (worst 60) |
| `styleGuideCleanup` without `loadPagesYielding` | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "entry/style-guide-cleanup: …" (worst 60) |
| The read after open's error answer posted untagged | `test-open-large-file.ts`: "open/error: a read after open that fails is still tagged as the read after open" |
| The adapter's inbound `file-sets` drops `partial` | `test-write-adapter.ts`: "accepts file-sets at open, the ledger's alone, keeps partial and atOpen" |
| The adapter's inbound `file-sets` drops `atOpen` | `test-write-adapter.ts`: the same arm |
| The adapter keeps a `partial` that is not `true` | `test-write-adapter.ts`: "accepts file-sets with a malformed partial and atOpen leaves both off" |

The `entry/*` arms run each entry on the stand-in with its pages unloaded again, as on a fresh open. The independent
review's mutants MC–MG all survived before these arms; each now fails by the name above.

### Gaps

- Nothing was run in Figma. The stand-in burns a fixed time per page. In Figma, a page's load time depends on what is on
  it, and the plugin cannot yield inside a single page's load.
- The full read and the hand-edit pass still load every page after open, now one per turn. Whether the pass should wait
  until Components or Update file is opened, so that a plain open loads no page at all, is a held question for the
  owner (Q3110.1 on the PR).
- The other entries that now load pages one per turn (each write's entry, `drawSpecs`, `fileSetup`,
  `captureBaseline`, `adoptMembers`, `updateComponents`) have no `entry/*` arm of their own; a revert of one of them is
  not caught.
- A set the ledger names but that was deleted by hand shows on the badge until the full read lands, about 20 s later on
  the 60-page file. #3091 tracks the same gap for the live recount.

### Coordination with #3096 and #3090

Neither had merged when this was written. Whichever lands second owes:

- **#3096.** `git merge-tree` shows textual conflicts in 8 files: `main.ts`, `messages.ts`, `shell/update-file.ts`,
  `state/host-session.ts`, `state/update-file.ts`, `write-adapter.ts`, `test-host-session.ts`, `test-update-file.ts`.
  Every hunk resolves as keep both: `presentDefs` keeps `timed('page loads', loadPagesYielding)` and adds
  `presentCache = …; return presentCache;` with its declaration; the `file-sets` message type keeps `partial`/`atOpen`,
  then #3096's `file-due`; the `HostSession` field keeps `partial`/`atOpen`, then `liveDue`; the `reduce` `file-sets`
  case keeps #3110's two guards and tagged return, then #3096's `case 'file-due'`; the shell's import list is the union
  (`awaitingRead`, `badgeCount`, `LiveDue`); `state/update-file.ts` keeps `awaitingRead` above #3096's reworded
  `dueCount` doc; the adapter's type and `INBOUND` keep both.
- **#3090.** git flags nothing here, because `ledgerSets` is new code. In #3090, `fileSets` prints each set
  `needsPrint` names (`print(id); await breathe();`) before `dueOf(…, print)`, and `dueOf` reads an engine-moved, printed
  entry as `unrecorded` when `print` returns null, its default. So the second to land does one of:
  - **(a)** give `ledgerSets` the same `needsPrint` loop and `printNow()`. On the first open after an engine release,
    the ledger's answer then projects every engine-moved set before it posts: the independent review measured 45 sets at 251–346 ms in Node (worst
    set `button`, 39–59 ms), the thread handed back between sets, and slower in the sandbox;
  - **(b)** leave `ledgerSets` without a print. Engine-moved sets then read `unrecorded` at open and change when the
    full read lands.

  Either way, `open/agree` gets an engine-moved arm. Which one is the second PR's call.

## (2026-10-28) — Grid margin note: a correction note for #3065's 41px sentence (#3070 follow-up)

**What.** #3065's change note `claude-grid-margin-lever.md` says the reference brand's md margin of 44 gives
"whole-pixel 41px columns at 1440 with 24 columns and 16px gutters". #3070 found that true only of the brand's
two-mode desktop spec, not of the engine's 5-breakpoint grid (md is 8 columns; a 44 margin gives 71px columns at
768), and fixed the code comments, but left the note because a merged note is not edited. This PR adds
`claude-grid-margin-note-correction.md`, an `engine: patch` note that names the sentence and corrects it.

**Why this route.** It is the one the rules already sanction: `packages/engine/changes/README.md` ("To correct it,
add a note of your own") and `lint-emission-version.ts`'s ONE WRITER refusal ("the fold writes both under the same
version"). No gate or fold change was needed, so the gate's independence is untouched. The wrong sentence still
reaches `CHANGELOG.md`, with the correction beside it in the same version's section; editing the original note
would have needed ONE WRITER loosened, which is a bigger change than the error.

**Class.** `patch`, because no committed artifact moves (`regen --check` clean). The fold takes the highest class in
the batch, and #3065's own note is `minor`, so the correction adds no version of its own if both fold together.
If the fold consumes #3065's note first, this note folds alone and costs one patch version.

## (2026-10-28) — The figma-bridge MCP server negotiates the handshake like the engine server (#3109)

Claude Code refused to connect to `tools/figma-bridge/server.ts`. Its `initialize` answer kept the fallback #1867
removed from `packages/engine/mcp.ts`: it echoed `2026-07-28` when asked for it, and answered `2026-07-28` to any
version it did not know, including the `2025-11-25` Claude Code sends. `2026-07-28` has no handshake, so a client
that sent `initialize` cannot use that answer.

- **The rule is shared, not copied.** `mcp.ts` exports `negotiateHandshakeVersion`, and both servers call it. The
  bridge already imported `mcp.ts`'s protocol constants; what drifted was the one line it copied. The engine server's
  answers are unchanged.
- **One probe table for every server.** `packages/engine/mcp-handshake-probes.ts` holds four `initialize` probes
  (`2024-11-05`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-11-25`, `2026-07-28`) with LITERAL expected answers, not computed by the rule
  they check (`docs/34` shape 1). `mcp-test.ts` and `apps/plugin/test-agent-bridge.ts` drive them over each server's
  real stdio.
- **A register, checked against the tree.** `MCP_SERVERS` maps each server to its suite. `mcp-test.ts` scans
  `packages/`, `apps/` and `tools/` for `initialize` handlers (a `case 'initialize'` or an `=== 'initialize'`
  comparison) and fails by file on one the register does not name, on a
  registered server the scan cannot find, and on a suite that no longer reads the probes.
- **Where it runs.** No new gate. The bridge was already gated: `test-agent-bridge.ts` is an arm of the plugin's
  `test` step, which `verify.ts` and `ci.yml` both run, and `mcp-test.ts` is an engine gate in both.

**Mutations, each failing by name:** the bridge echoing `2026-07-28` again fails three bridge probes
(`2025-06-18`, `2025-11-25`, `2026-07-28`); dropping the `!== LATEST` clause from the shared rule fails the
`2026-07-28` probe in BOTH suites; an unregistered `case 'initialize'` under `tools/`, an unregistered `=== 'initialize'` handler under `tools/`, and a bridge suite that stops
reading the probes each fail the register check.

## (2026-10-28) — Opaque outline hover fill: `outlineInteraction: opaque-fill`, and the reference brand at `neutral.050` (#3071)

The owner's decision on #3071 (Q824 A, 2026-10-27) picks the proposal's option B: an opaque fill picked by step. Neither wash can be pointed at a step, and the reference brand's hover is `neutral.050` (not 025, its card ground, where a hover would vanish).

- **The shape, and why a method.** A fourth `outlineInteraction` value, `opaque-fill`, plus a per-mode step lever, `outlineHoverFill: { <mode>: { hover, pressed? } }`. A method rather than a free-standing lever because the families are exclusive for the controls they reach and `outlineFillFamily`'s exhaustive switch makes every consumer re-read on a new value (`opaque: true` is the field it kept for exactly this). Keyed by mode like `modeAnchors` and `overrides`, editable modes only: a light step on a dark page is a white block, and HC is generate-only.
- **The fill.** `interactive.<c>.hover-fill.{hover,pressed}` and `inverse.` twins, per column, put after the override layer. A named step is the brand's; unnamed, the neutral step nearest 1.15:1 on the ink's side of the ground; pressed the next step toward the ink. On the reference brand: light page 050 / 100, band 850 / 800; dark page 850 / 800; HC 050/100 and 900/850.
- **The ink.** The control's own `text` / `icon` at hover and pressed is measured on the fill and clamped along its own ramp to the nearest step that clears its `min` (#1510's walk), and carries the fill as `alsoAgainst` (#1745). So pressed is gated too (Q3071.6 A), and the existing sweep, `tree.ts`'s mode checks, `lint-ratio-truth` arm F and the `.ai.json` `contrast_with` lines (from both ends) all see the pair with no new machinery. No corpus ink moves: the clamp is proved synthetically ("#3071 (B)").
- **The wash stays.** The method still emits the overlay family and the selected tint: `applyOutlineInteraction` rebinds only `OPAQUE_FILL_DEFS` (Button, Icon button, Flush icon button, each family), so Tag, Segmented control and Pagination keep the neutral wash (Q3071.4 A), and the text button follows under `buttonTextHover: fill` (Q3071.3 A) because `applyButtonLayout` copies the outline's slots after the rebind.
- **Style guide.** `outline-roles.ts` no longer switches a band member to page roles on an opaque fill: that rule was for the pre-#1614 tint with no band twin. The opaque fill has one, measured on the band.
- **Contract.** Brand-dependent (docs/30, decided): 12 paths in the baseline's `brandDependent`, `CONTRACT_VERSION` 14.12.0 unchanged, `token-contract --check` level none, `lint-contract-version` clean. Only the reference brand's artifacts move.
- **Studio and plugin:** Color › Interactive gains a "Solid fill" chip and, under it, Outline hover fill: Hover and Pressed selects for the mode the preview shows, Auto naming the default step, and the worst label ratio on each. Leaving the method drops its picks. Every string is a DRAFT for the owner.
- **Gates** (`test.ts`, "#3071 (A)–(F)"): every label and icon on its fill in every brand × mode × ground at the ink's own floor; the clamp; the reference brand's 050 / 100 in the committed DTCG, the Figma light file and the redesign seed; no other brand's emission carries the family and the method is additive over each corpus brand's own resolution; the family absent from the guaranteed set; three refusals, and `outlineHoverFill` under another method ignored with a note (refusing it broke the lever sweep and the plugin's variant builds, which vary one lever at a time). The (10h), #1608, #1387 and #2926 sweeps take the fourth method.
- **Mutations caught a real gap:** a mid-gray pick walked a dark-mode label darker until it cleared the fill and failed its page, which Tag and Pagination share. The clamp now takes only a step that clears both, and otherwise leaves the ink and warns ("#3071 (B2)").
- **Trap:** the corpus arms read the committed emission, so mutate the engine and run `regen.ts` before `test.ts`.
