## (2026-10-28) — Update file: a tick keeps the checklist's scroll (#3082 part 2)

**Status:** plugin UI fix + `test:chrome` arm. No engine change, so no change note: no committed artifact, emission or
component surface moves. CONTRACT unchanged. #3082 part 1 (what an engine update does to the due count, Q811) is the
owner's open question and is untouched here.

### What changed

- **The bug:** in Update file's checklist, ticking a set (a new component far down the list, for example) jumped the
  dialog back to the top. `paint()` in `apps/studio/src/shell/update-file.ts` rebuilds the whole overlay on every
  change, so the new body started at `scrollTop` 0. Focus already survived: the focused `data-key` was restored with
  `preventScroll`.
- **The fix:** `paint()` reads the old body's `scrollTop` before it rebuilds and sets it on the new one after, when the
  tab is the same (the body carries `data-tab`); a new tab still starts at the top. Every repaint goes through `paint()`
  (a tick, the hand-edit choice, and each host answer on the topics it subscribes to: a check landing, hand edits, the
  file's sets), so the one change covers them all.
- **The arm** (`test:chrome` section `ia2`, shard 1, figma host, both themes): it opens Update file on a file that holds
  4 sets, so every other set is listed as new and the checklist is taller than the dialog; asserts the last new set
  starts below the fold, scrolls the body down, ticks it, and asserts the scroll moved by at most 1px and focus is on
  that box (`set=<id>`). A second assertion repaints from a host answer (the check again) and holds the scroll and focus
  there too. With the restore removed, both fail by name (`#3082: ticking a set below the fold keeps the body's scroll`,
  `#3082: a host answer's repaint keeps the body's scroll`).

### The narrow tier

- At the narrow tier, `.p3-frame[data-w="narrow"] .p3-bardlg-col { overflow: visible }` would stop the body scrolling,
  but `chrome.css`'s `.p3-frame[data-w="narrow"] .p3-bardlg-col.p3-upd-body` rule restores `overflow-y: auto`, so the
  body stays the scroller there too. Measured at 400×700: the arm passes, and fails without the restore. The arm now
  runs that narrow pass as well as 1280×900.

## (2026-10-28) — A kept hand edit is reported as kept, not as a discard (#3086 part 2)

On Update file with "Keep" hand edits, a radio whose dot size a designer had edited was kept, as asked, but the run report said `60 parts not written as planned — bound … dot.width -> DISCARDED (set control/size/md/dot, not retained on the live node)`. The run did what it was told and the report called it a failure.

### The diagnosis

A node kept as a hand edit is not written (`build`'s `kept` guard in `write-components.ts`). The build's bound read-back, which runs after the combine for every member it wrote, still reads every binding the plan gives each part and reports any it cannot find. On a kept node the plan's binding is absent by design, so every kept bound field read as a dropped binding. The read-back has no notion of a kept node, and it should not: it is the executor's check that the host held what was written, and it is right for every node the build did write.

### The fix

The report side sorts it, in `applySet` (`apps/plugin/src/update-apply.ts`), which already holds each member's kept paths. A `bound <member>/<part>.<field> -> DISCARDED` miss whose part is one of that member's kept paths moves out of `misses` into the outcome's new `keptBound`. The verdict names those properties with the hand edits kept: `1 hand edit kept (dot size)`, where a width or height reads as the part's size (DRAFT wording for the owner). Any other miss, and a bound miss on a node no one edited, stays a part not written as planned, and the set stays not verified.

### Plain words for every property (owner Q826 A)

The clause names each kept property in plain words, the layer name first, never a code name. `KEPT_FIELD_WORD` in `update-apply.ts` covers every field a plan binds: width and height read "size"; "min width", "min height", "gap"; the four padding sides merge into "padding", the scalar and per-side stroke weights into "border width", the four corner radii into "corner radius". For example, `1 hand edit kept (container padding)`. A field with no word yet names the layer alone, never its key. The wording stays DRAFT.

### The check

Two cases in `apps/plugin/test-update-apply.ts`, `kept report/…`, on a built radio-control. In the first, a designer unbinds the checked medium member's dot width and height and sizes it to 14; the update runs under Keep; the verdict lists no part not written and reads `radio-control: 60 updated in place, 1 hand edit kept (dot size).`, verified. In the second, no member is edited and the host drops the dot's width binding on one member; the miss is still reported, and the set is not verified. A third case, `kept report/two members`, holds the per-member scoping: one member's kept dot does not hide a binding the host dropped on another member's dot. An arm per property family (`kept report/size`, `/min width`, `/min height`, `/gap`, `/padding`, `/border width`, `/corner radius`) asserts its typed word, once, for each field alone and for the family together. `kept report/no raw key` reads the field list from every def's plan (18 fields today), not a typed list, and asserts the clause names each in a word, with no field key and nothing camelCase. Mutations, each failing by name: a padding side falling through to its key (`kept report/padding`, `kept report/no raw key`); the split removed (`kept report/no miss`, `kept report/named`), the property left unnamed (`kept report/named`), the split taking every bound miss whatever was kept (`kept report/real discard`).

### Not changed

The component executor did not change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` is not raised: `lint-executor-revision.ts` reads the executor's files and none of them moved. The radio dot size itself (#3086 part 1, Q816) is an open owner question and is not touched here.

## (2026-10-28) — Card number field: TextField with the payment tile at its trailing edge (#2343 PR 4)

**Engine 0.238.0.** The card-number half of #2429, built from its 16 recommendations (owner Q-B10 A) and the
2026-10-27 artwork calls: `card-number-field` (CardNumberField), a third output of the field factory. 84 members,
TextField's count; medium first. The PaymentField group (expiration date, security code, postal code, name on card) is
the follow-up, the proposal's PR 4b.

### What it is

- **A third factory edge, `mark`.** TextField's trailing glyph is replaced by `cardMark`: a swap slot that binds its
  height alone (`size.{size}.mark-height`, 20 / 20 / 24, the field's only added keys), carries the aspect lock, so the
  instance takes its own component's proportion (8:5 for a tile), and keeps the tile's paint (`fixedPaint`, at every
  state, disabled included). The `card mark` switch is on by default; `↳ swap card mark` sits under it.
- **It starts at the generic tile**, the owner's "no card type yet" artwork, which replaced the core `bank-card` glyph
  the 2026-10-25 proposal planned. `swapDefault` on a `fixedPaint` slot now names a brand mark and projects as
  `brand-mark/<kind>/<name>`; an icon name there throws at projection.
- **Card networks only (Q-C7 A, the owner, 2026-10-27).** PR 3's tile kind holds every accepted-payments tile (Q780 A),
  wallets and pay-later services included, and a card number only ever detects a network. So the `brand` prop takes a
  typed list in the def (`generic`, `amex`, `diners-club`, `discover`, `maestro`, `mastercard`, `visa`), each checked
  against the mark set's tiles. The tile kind is still read by artboard (`BRAND_MARK_KINDS`), so PR 3's `card/` →
  `payment/` rename reached the slot's default without an edit. A network the owner adds joins by one line in the def
  and one in the gate.
- **The code contract** (in `codeOnly`, `accessibility` and the props): `cc-number`, `inputmode="numeric"`, never
  `type="number"`, `dir="ltr"`; grouping as the user types with digits-only values; detection from the leading digits;
  the network named in a visually hidden `aria-describedby` description, never a live region; a hosted-input shell
  (`renderInput`) as the documented default, with the native mode marked outside SAQ A.

### Gates

- **`lint-mark-slots.ts`** (new, in CI): the tiles are read from the marks folder by the gate's own `viewBox` reader
  (32×20). NETWORKS ONLY: the host's `brand` prop offers exactly the gate's own literal card-network list, each a tile
  in the folder, so a wallet tile fails. GENERIC FIRST: it defaults to `generic`, and every
  member's slot and the set's swap property start at `brand-mark/<tile folder>/generic`. A TILE'S SHAPE: height alone,
  the listed icon rung per size, under the aspect lock. Every def that swaps in a tile is a listed host, both ways.
- **`lint-mark-colors.ts`** host arm (d): a carried mark takes no `descendantFills`, no fill or stroke paint and no paint
  variable, and its node states `fixedPaint`; `MARK_HOSTS` lists the hosts by hand, both ways, so the arm is no longer
  vacuous.
- **`test:roundtrip`**: the payment tile is read back on all 84 members, an instance of the generic tile locked at 1.6,
  its height bound to the size's icon rung. `aspectLock` is now a checked plan field (locked to a real ratio), and
  `fixedPaint` an unchecked one with its reason.
- **`test.ts`**: the token block (TextField's plus exactly the three height keys), the members, the panel, the props,
  the factory's refusals and the projection throw.

### Traps

- **The round-trip measured the harness at first.** The tile instance read "NOT LOCKED" because the brand mark was a
  catalog name with no node behind it, so the lock had no main to read. The harness now prebuilds the marks (as the
  plugin does) and serves plain components live; the shim's live component then needed an `id`, or the swap
  property's default was refused.
- **The paste-payload stub in `test.ts`** had no `getMainComponentAsync` on an instance: the first real `aspectLock`
  host threw there. The stub now answers with the main's artboard (a mark's box, else 24×24).

### Held for the owner (Q-blocks in the PR, A built)

The tile keeps its colors at the disabled member; the `card mark` switch; the page placement ("Card number field" under
Components); the draft wording; and the PaymentField group as the follow-up.

- **Figma.** Apply Theme moves `color/scrim/default`'s alias on the same variable (`test-write.ts`, #3050 arms).

## (2026-10-28) — Link underline thickness and offset as brand tokens; the reference brand sets 5% / 25% (#2942)

**What.** Owner decisions Q1–Q6 A, Q800 A and Q801 A. `typography.underline: { thickness, offset }`, each a share of
the font size or `auto` (default both). `resolveUnderline` (theme.ts) holds a set value to a whole percent and clamps
it to `UNDERLINE_BOUNDS` (thickness 1–20%, offset 0–50%), like the column-count clamp. A set field emits
`core.font.underline.<field>`, `$type: number`, shaped like `core.font.line-height.*` (a `style-part` with its
PERCENT). The `-link` composites' `$value` is unchanged; their `figma.baked` list names the two fields when set.
`emit-figma-font.ts` puts PERCENT on every UNDERLINE style; `write-plan.ts` turns absence into an explicit `'AUTO'`;
the plugin's `applyTextStylePlan` and the paste pass write `{ unit: 'PERCENT' }` or `{ unit: 'AUTO' }` after
`textDecoration`, on UNDERLINE rows only. The reference brand sets 0.05 / 0.25 (`nbThemeFrom`, `nb-redesign.design.md`).
Studio and plugin share one panel: a "Custom underline" switch and two whole-percent fields in Theme › Type › Weights
and styles, a read-only line in a new Components › Link section, and a Link underline sample at 14/16/18px in the
Type preview. All copy is a DRAFT placeholder (Q2 A).

**Diagnosis that kept it small.** Line height already had the exact shape: a unitless DTCG number that Figma bakes
into the style as PERCENT, with no variable. The new fields ride the same `bound: false` style properties, so no
component set is due and Link and Breadcrumbs follow through the text styles.

**Deliberate.** Absence means AUTO in `text-styles.json` (not an explicit AUTO object), so every other brand's committed
file is byte-identical. The plan, not the file, makes AUTO explicit. Neither field is written on a plain style:
Figma's API reads both as null when the text is not underlined.

**CONTRACT stays 14.12.0.** Auto emits nothing (Q5 A), so 9 of the 10 corpus members lack the paths and the gate files
them as brand-dependent: `token-contract --check` reports no guaranteed move, and `lint-contract-version` refuses a
raise over a `none` level. The baseline gained the two brand-dependent paths through `--accept` at 14.12.0.

**Verified in a live file.** Figma does not document what `textDecorationOffset` PERCENT is measured from. A live
measurement on 100px text (the orchestrator's comment on #3075) settled it: PERCENT is a percent of the font size,
measured from the alphabetic baseline to the line's top edge, which is CSS's zero position under
`text-underline-position: auto`. So 25% and 0.25em draw one line, and no conversion is applied or needed.

**Stored corrected.** The Studio's field corrects a value past a bound before it stores it (the orchestrator's call on
the review's item 4): 40 typed saves 0.2, so a saved brand or an exported design.md never carries an out-of-range share.

**Gates.** `test.ts` #2942 (clamp table, the clamp reaching the tokens, off = no token and AUTO rows, on = 18 rows at
5/25, other brands' committed files untouched, paste-path read-back); `apps/plugin/test-write-typography.ts` #2942
(read-back on 18 built `-link` styles, plain styles untouched, re-applying an auto brand writes AUTO); `apps/studio/test-smoke.mjs` #2942 (the switch stores and exports 0.05 / 0.25, 40 and 60 read back 20 and 50, are stored as 0.2 and 0.5 and export them, off exports no underline, the Components › Link line follows). The TokenPress reader's gap is #3085.

## (2026-10-27) — Brand glass roles: the `glassRoles` lever, and the reference brand's card glass (#3073)

The owner's decisions on #3073 (Q806, the glass taxonomy; Q807 A; the 70% correction of 2026-10-27) replace the closed #3074, which gave every brand a fixed `color.glass.card`. Prism3 ships one glass role, `color.glass.surface` (white or black glass), unchanged. A brand adds its own through a lever.

- **`glassRoles`** (Color, an object lever): `{ <name>: { role | palette, alpha } }` adds `color.glass.<name>`. `role` reads a semantic role's palette color per mode (`foreground.primary`, the card ground); `palette` names one color (`neutral.050`, `white`, `black`). The alpha is a whole percent, 1–99, the same in every mode.
- **The alpha lives in the value.** A bound Figma paint with paint opacity renders opaque (the 10/27 finding on the issue), so the role aliases a palette alpha step: `tree.ts` mints `<palette>-<step>-alpha.<n>` through `alphaLeaf`, only for the steps a mode reads, and on white or black it reuses `white-alpha` / `black-alpha` (an alpha off that ramp's steps is refused). `glassAlphaFamily` in `modes.ts` names the family, and the tree mints through it, so the alias always resolves.
- **Put after the override layer**, so a role source reads its role's final step: an override of `foreground.primary` carries to the card glass. An override aimed at a brand glass role is refused, naming its source. `color-order.ts` opens `glass.0` so a brand role lands after `surface`.
- **Validated:** `surface` and non-kebab names are refused, as are both or neither sources, an alpha off 1–99, a source in the glass group, a translucent or missing role, and an unknown palette step.
- **The reference brand adds `card`** (fixture and redesign seed): light `neutral-050-alpha.70`, dark `neutral-900-alpha.70`, high contrast `white-alpha.70` / `black-alpha.70`. Apply Theme writes `color/glass/card` in the color collection, plus two hidden primitives.
- **Brand-dependent, not guaranteed:** `color.glass.card` and the two minted steps join `brandDependent`; `CONTRACT_VERSION` stays 14.12.0 (`token-contract --check` level `none`). `docs/30` records it as a decision.
- **Gates** (`test.ts`, "#3073 …"): `glass.surface` is value-identical in every brand (spelled rgba per mode); each added role's opaque color equals its source's per mode and its alpha the declared one; brands without the lever emit no extra glass role or alpha family; the guaranteed contract's glass group is `surface` alone. A Figma arm reads every color mode file. Two older arms exempt the brand's own glass by a spelled per-brand list (`BRAND_ADDED_GLASS`): the shared role-set arm and the inverse register.
- **Studio:** Surfaces & fills gains a Glass section: the white glass read-only, then each added fill's name, color, opacity and a remove button, and Add glass fill. Every string is a DRAFT for the owner.
- **Trap:** the gates read the committed emission, so mutate the input and run `regen.ts` before `test.ts`.

## (2026-10-27) — WalletButton: the provider's express-checkout button, as a sized slot and a layout stand-in (#2343 PR 4)

**Status:** new def `wallet-button` (20 members), a new axis name `provider`, one projector change (a nest of a
standalone-component def names the member component), and the spec model and roundtrip taught that nest. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: only existing
roles are bound. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. PR 3 (the owner's marks) and #3047 have merged.

### What was built, and the calls held for the owner

- **Owner decisions it rests on:** two components from one factory (Q-B4 A), and in code a slot that mounts the provider's own element, Prism3 adding only the focus
  ring and layout (Q-B8 A). The proposal's §2.1 rule table is the source for the limits. Q-B5 A decided valid
  provider × **style** pairs only; with the style axis held by Q-W1, the build reads it onto provider × size (the two
  height exclusions), so Q-B5 A is in effect deferred by Q-W1 A.
- **Q-W1, the Figma member (built as A):** a layout stand-in, the provider's area at its size and corner with the
  provider's logo nested unaltered, and no fill. Two findings decided it: none of the four providers publishes its
  button colors as values (Google Pay says "dark and light"; PayPal's v6 reference says "gold" and "white with
  border"), and all four forbid a hand-drawn copy of the button, which a Prism3-painted ground would be. Every logo in
  the owner's set is drawn for a light ground (Apple Pay and Shop Pay one ink, Google Pay five colors, the PayPal
  wordmark three), so a dark-style stand-in would need a light logo the set does not hold.
  B: the owner supplies each provider's own button artwork per style, and a `style` axis draws it. C: Prism3 paints the
  fills, which needs a literal-paint engine field (`gradientFill`'s path through both executors) and colors the
  providers do not publish.
- **Q-W2, heights (built as A):** a size outside a provider's range has no member: Shop Pay starts at medium (40
  floor), PayPal stops at medium (55 ceiling); the code clamps. Density moves every rung (harbor: compact 28/36/44,
  spacious 44/56/68), so the exclusions hold at comfortable only, and at compact and spacious the code's clamp is what
  keeps the provider's range; the Figma member shows the brand's rung. B: density-invariant wallet heights, which need
  a token the tier does not have.
- **Q-W3, the factory:** SignInButton is PR 5, so the shared factory lands with its second component, not as an
  abstraction with one user.
- **Q-W5, shape (built as A):** no shape axis; the corner is the brand's `radius.md`. The proposal's §2.3 gave
  WalletButton `shape: rectangle | pill`. B: a `shape` axis whose pill binds `radius.capsule`, clamped to half the
  height for Google Pay.
- **Q-W4, the page:** "Wallet button", its own page under Components (DRAFT). Brand mark now has one consumer, so it
  joins `STANDALONE_NESTED` to keep its Foundations page (Q-B12).
- **Tier 2** generation priority (a top-level component placed on its own); width floor 120 (the largest provider
  minimum, Shop Pay's logo button; Apple Pay plain needs 100); radius `radius.md`. Harbor's is inside Google Pay's
  half-height cap at every density, but a soft brand's is not (`baseMd` 12 × `radiusScale` 2 gives 24px against a
  28px compact small), so the code clamps Google Pay's `buttonRadius` to `min(radius, height / 2)`.

### The engine change

`figmaAnatomySet` wrote `nestTarget: 'brand-mark'` and `nestVariant: { name }` for a nest of `brand-mark`, which an
executor resolves inside a component SET. `brand-mark` emits standalone components, so there is no set, and the nest
missed. The projector now resolves such a nest to the member's own component, `brand-mark/logo/apple-pay`, and writes
no `nestVariant`, the way `nestedSwapTarget` names a swap's. Both executors already make an instance from a component
found by name, and `build-deps.ts` already maps `<id>/<value>` to its def, so neither moved. No other def nests a
standalone-component def, so no other surface digest moved.

### What the first full run found, and the fixes

- **The spec model and the roundtrip had never met a standalone nest.** `component-specs.ts` recorded the first
  member's `nestTarget` as the nested component, so the model said every provider nests `brand-mark/logo/apple-pay`.
  It now names the def (`brand-mark`) with its variant and `when`, and `test-roundtrip.ts`'s spec read-back resolves
  each member's own `<def>/<value>` from them.
- **PR 2's `aspectLock` and `fixedPaint` had never been projected by a shipped def,** so the roundtrip's field floor
  had not classified them. `aspectLock` is now CHECKED in `anatomy-readback.ts` (the host must hold a
  `targetAspectRatio`). `fixedPaint` is declared unchecked with its reason: it promises the plan carries no paint, so
  the host has nothing of the plan's to echo. The roundtrip harness builds a def that locks to its main with the
  nested components pre-built and answering as themselves (`liveComponents`). Against a bare catalog name the
  executor has no size to read, reports a miss and leaves the instance unlocked. Mutation: the plugin executor's
  `lockAspectRatio` call dropped → the roundtrip fails `aspectLock` on all 20 members.
- **Hand lists a new set joins:** `CANVAS_FURNITURE` (headers like Button's), `test-canvas-furniture.ts` (55 sets),
  the studio's component groups (a "Wallet button" row) and `used-by.ts`, and the ecosystem map's definitions.
- **`test.ts` floors:** Figma's default member must carry the code default on every axis. `provider` is required in
  code (a wallet button always names its wallet), so a recorded BRIDGE entry says apple-pay stands in.
  `brand-mark`'s `planned` list loses `wallet-button`, now registered, which moves to its `ai.commonPartners`. A
  `codeOnly` entry that read like a state admission ("hover — not projected") now leads with "the provider's own
  states".

### Gates, and the mutations that fail them by name

`packages/engine/test.ts`, `#2343 PR 4 provider rules`, its rules typed from the providers' guidelines, never read off
the def. Each mutation was made on the def and fails its arm by name:
- PayPal's large exclusion removed → **HEIGHT** (`provider=paypal, size=large … at 56`);
- `minWidth: 90` → **WIDTH**;
- `radius.capsule` → **RADIUS** (Google Pay, `radius 999 over height 36` at compact);
- `fixedPaint` dropped from the logo → **COLOR**;
- PayPal's logo pointed at the monogram → **MARK** (`nests brand-mark/logo/paypal`);
- the Google Pay clamp removed from codeOnly → **RADIUS (every brand)** (`radiusScale 2 × baseMd 12`, members over
  half their height);
- an inked `label` text part added → **WORDING** (it was caught only under COLOR before);
- the a11y contract inverted (aria-label on the container to the provider name) → **NAME** (nothing failed before).
The def joined `lint-hit-target` (INTERACTIVE, SMALL_SIZE), `lint-rung-names` (MUST_COVER, DEFAULT_FIRST),
`lint-axis-values` (`provider` sole, `size` canonical), `lint-standalone-floor`, `lint-paint-placement`,
`lint-absolute-inset` (MUST_COVER, MUST_CLEAR_STROKE) and the `generationPriority` tier list. `regen --check` counts
223 artifacts (the new docs page): `verify.ts` and `ci.yml` together.

### Traps

- A projected plan's `coord` carries the variant axes the grid does not lay out; the size is `plan.size`, not
  `plan.coord.size`. The first HEIGHT arm read `coord.size` and found every member missing.
- A new def file must be `git add`-ed before `lint-axis-values.ts` sees it: it counted 57 defs and passed while the
  file was untracked.

## (2026-10-27) — IA v2 rail polish: 9px labels, 24px icons in square marks, Agent and Minimize swap places, wider Theme tabs (#2909)

The owner's first hands-on look at the IA v2 chrome, built as stated, on both hosts (the plugin and the web studio share
the chrome).

- **Rail labels** at 9px and -0.01em. The engine's type scale stops at 10px, so the size is `calc(var(--p3-fs-12) * 0.75)`,
  three quarters of a scale step rather than a raw length the build's scan would refuse. Tracking is the existing
  `ls-snug` role (`letter-spacing.neg-10`, exactly -0.01em).
- **Rail icons 24 x 24 in a square mark.** The cause of the landscape box: the mark took `min-width: ctl-h` (40) and
  `min-height: ctl-h-xs` (28), two different tokens on the two axes. It is now fixed at `width` and `height` both
  `--p3-rail-tile` (`core.dimension.32`, new in `spec.mjs`), `flex: none`, so neither the label nor a line height sizes it;
  the icon is `--p3-icon-md` (`icon.size.md`, 24). A 32px mark leaves a 4px inset on the selected fill, and the tile
  stays about as tall as before (32 + one 9px line against 28 + one 12px line), so the plugin's 420px rail keeps fitting.
- **Agent and Minimize swap placements (Q731).** Minimize now sits at the rail's foot, where the Agent tile was. The
  Agent tile sits on the top bar, after the brand switcher and before Update file, where Minimize was before this PR. A
  first build read the brief's "swap" as Update file ↔ Minimize; the owner clarified it and that swap is reverted. The
  change is in where the frame places the two slots (`frame.ts`, `bar.ts`). Minimize's slot hook is now `rail-minimize`,
  so the old `bar-minimize` name doesn't point at the bar. Both controls behave as before: Minimize works with the link
  on or off, and the Agent tile keeps its toggle, `aria-pressed`, green dot and Activity status.
- **Agent's on state on the bar (Q738 A).** While the link is on, the bar's Agent tile fills its mark with `fill-2`, the
  fill the rail drew behind an on tile (Q2909.22 A), and keeps the green dot. The fill comes from the same `chrome.css`
  rule as the rail's. On the bar the mark is a square around the 16px glyph, and a negative margin takes back its padding,
  so the tile keeps its size, including the glyph-only 28 x 28 tile at 380.
- **An edge on the bar's on mark (Q788 C).** The review found `fill-2` is the dark bar's own color (`bar-bg`, 1.00:1) and
  faint on the light one (1.14:1). So while the link is on, the bar's Agent mark also draws a 1px inset outline in
  `edge-bar`, the top bar's control edge, which `spec.mjs` already holds at 3:1 on `bar-bg`: 3.18:1 in light, 3.52:1 in
  dark. It shows on only, at every width, and the rail is unchanged.
- **Mirror glyphs.** Minimize draws `collapse` (`dom.ts`), Restore's two arrows turned inward, each arrowhead's arms 4 long as
  Restore's are, so the mirror is exact. The strip's Restore keeps
  the outward pair. `test:chrome` reads both drawn SVG paths, takes each arrowhead's corner as its tip, and checks the
  direction against the shafts' reach. A glyph name can't satisfy that check.
- **Whole labels (Q732 A).** "Components" and "Appearance" drop the wireframe's manual break. Each fits one line at 9px.
- **Theme tabs:** the panes row's gap from `space.150` (12px) to `space.200` (16px), one step on the chrome's scale.

`test:chrome` gains an arm for each change, and each was mutated to fail by name. The arms cover: Minimize first at the
rail's foot and never on the bar; Agent on the bar between the brand and Update file and never on the rail; `BAR_ORDER`;
the two glyphs differing and pointing the right ways; no hyphen in any rail label; and the bar's Agent tile carrying the
on fill at 1280 and 380 while the link is on, and not while it is off. That last arm compares the mark with the ground
it is drawn on: its edge or its fill must clear 3:1 on the first opaque background behind it, in both themes.

## (2026-10-27) — Divider: the labeled variant, a rule broken by a short centered label (#3051)

**Status:** Divider def, a schema admission (`paintGroup`), tests and baselines. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT
unchanged: every binding is an existing token name. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What changed

- **Owner decision (2026-10-27, on #3051): build the labeled divider on the proposal's recommendations**, all seven
  held in the PR as a Q-block for confirmation: Q3051.1 A a `labeled: false | true` axis plus a `label` text property
  and string prop; Q3051.2 A no role on the wrapper, both lines `aria-hidden`, the label read as plain text; Q3051.3 A
  center only; Q3051.4 A `type.label.md.default` with `space.300` between the label and each line; Q3051.5 A
  `color.text.secondary`; Q3051.6 A horizontal, inset `none` only; Q3051.7 A "Or", sentence case.
- The set goes from five members to six. The plain members keep their pixels: the root is still a fixed row with the
  rule filling it, now `align: center` (which a stretched rule ignores) and binding `space.300` as its gap, which lays nothing out
  around one child. The labeled member draws
  `leadingRule` (grows), `label` (hugs) and `trailingRule` (grows), and its root is one label line box tall
  (`type.label.md.line-box`, the baked px the checkbox row's #1201 construction uses), so the hairlines sit on the
  middle of the label's line. The gap follows density (20 / 24 / 32).
- Plugin: `test-canvas-furniture.ts`'s thin-row case (Q258 A) built the whole divider set and found its 1px row. The
  labeled member is 16px and shares the horizontal row, so no row of the real set is thin any more; the case now builds
  the five plain members only, so the rule it holds still has a row to hold it on.
- In code there is no `labeled` prop: a non-empty `label` is the labeled divider. `#2752`'s BRIDGE says so.
- Accordion and Dialog nest the divider at `labeled: false` (their nested coordinate must name one member).

### The trap: one surface in pieces

`anatomyErrors` refuses two boxes claiming one paint slot (#933): `paintOf` is blind to which part asked, so they bind
one variable. The plain rule and the two lines are one rule split by the label, so binding one variable is the intent.
Rather than route a line through another slot (an `overlay` that only happens to land on `fills`), the schema gains
`paintGroup`: claimants of a shared slot are admitted only when every one names the same group, and the validator
refuses a group off a box, on a box that paints nothing, of one member, or whose members' `paintSlots` differ. Flagged
in the PR as an engine-mechanics call the owner may want to see.

### Gates

`test.ts` `#3051 divider labeled` holds each owner call against typed literals: the label and both lines present only
at `labeled=true` (and the plain rule only at `false`), lines that grow in flow on either side of a hugging label, the
label's `color/text/secondary` ink and `label/md/default` style, the `type/label/md/line-box` root and `space/300` gap,
the "Or" text property, the code API, the a11y contract, and `text.secondary` at 4.5:1 or better against
`background.primary` and `background.secondary` in every mode of every example brand, recomputed from the roles' hex.
Each arm was mutated from a `wip:` commit and failed by name (table in the PR).

## (2026-10-27) — Grid margin per brand: the reference brand's md margin is 44, linked to core/dimension/44 (#3052)

**What.** The owner's Q785 A replaces #3052's first answer (a raw 44 with no link). A per-brand grid margin or
gutter links to the first of: (1) a `space/*` step with that px, (2) the brand's `core/dimension/*` step, (3) a
plain px flagged off-scale. Never snapped. The reference brand sets `marginOverrides: { md: 44 }` in `nbThemeFrom`
and in `examples/nb-redesign.design.md`; `grid/margin` md now aliases `nbds/core/dimension/44` in the Figma `layout`
collection and the md grid style's offset is 44. sm stays 16 on `space/200`. Every other brand: no diff in `out/`.

**Diagnosis that kept it small.** The lever already existed (`layout.marginOverrides`, #1593), and `tree.ts`'s
`gridSpaceAlias` already fell back to a raw leaf; only `resolveGap`'s throw stood in the way. The rule lives in one
helper, `gridGapLink` (theme.ts), which both the token builder and the decisions note read. `emit-figma-dims` needed
no change: it copies whatever the DTCG alias is.

**Bind vs gate (technical call).** The grid style's offset is not bound to `grid/margin`. A grid style is a static
per-breakpoint copy; a variable bound inside it resolves in the frame's layout mode, so the `md` style would show
`sm`'s margin on an `sm` frame. The two emitters are gated to agree instead (test.ts 19g, G1).

**Gates (test.ts 19g).** G1 margin/gutter variable == grid style offset/gutterSize per brand × mode; G2 the reference
brand md == 44 → `core/dimension/44`, sm unchanged; G3 a link reaches `core/dimension/*` only when no `space/*`
step has the value (read from the emitted Figma `space` collection), and a plain value is flagged; G4 every other
brand's link table pinned as shipped. Mutations M1–M4 recorded in the block header.

**Trap for later.** The generalise arm (21)(d) compares unrooted names (`'grid/gutter'`) against rooted emitted
names, so it selects no rows and cannot fail. Filed as #3053 rather than fixed here.

## (2026-10-27) — Brand marks: the owner's artwork, kinds renamed payment and logo (#2343 PR 3)

**Status:** data drop plus the kind rename. 74 SVGs under `packages/engine/marks/`, each with its provenance record;
`card/` → `payment/` (Q780 A), `wallet/` → `logo/` (Q783 A). ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no token
name moves. `brand-mark` 19 → 74 members, accepted on `lint-component-surface.ts` and `lint-component-renames.ts`. One
plugin reader change (the Update reads a mark under a renamed value), no executor change. Merges after #3047.

### What changed

- **The set:** 15 `payment/` tiles (32×20, full-bleed), 14 `logo/` logos (24 high, hugging the artwork, width per
  record), 3 `provider/` sign-in glyphs, 42 `social/` marks (21 providers, full color and `-mono`). Owner decisions
  Q778–Q783 (2026-10-27). Provenance as the owner decided: assembled from several public sources and hand-edited, the
  sources not recorded, the provider the rights holder, dated the day supplied.
- **Normalized only as far as the emitter and the gates require**, every step written into the record's `normalized`
  list, built by a script and checked by rendering each original and its normalized file in Chromium:
  - the export's `<g clip-path>` dropped where the clip was the artboard (a no-op), and on 11 logos where it was the
    frame, with the artboard set to the frame's width: the export rounds a 25.51-wide frame up to `width="26"`, and a
    logo hugs its artwork (Q781 A). Geometry proves no ink sits past the narrowed artboard;
  - the tile grounds' `<rect>` written as `M0 0H32V20H0Z`; `white` / `black` as `#FFFFFF` / `#000000`; the Diners Club
    logo's four `<use>` inlined; Messenger's `gradientTransform="translate(4.02 24) scale(26.4)"` on a unit circle at
    the origin folded into `cx`/`cy`/`r` (the same circle);
  - gradient `<defs>` moved before the paths (Discover logo, Messenger): `lint-mark-colors.ts` compares paints in
    document order, and the emitter writes `<defs>` first, so the export's order read as a changed color;
  - Pinterest and YouTube spilled past the 24×24 artboard by 0.0198 and 0.0238, ink the dropped clip had trimmed. The
    coordinates past the edge are clamped to it, in those paths only (each absolute `M/L/C/H/V/Z`, sampled first), so
    the outline stays inside by the Bézier hull property and nothing moves further than it spilled. Clamping every
    path whose control points stray (a first cut) would have moved Snapchat by 0.1 for no reason; measured, then
    narrowed.
- **`social/twitter*` is the X glyph**, so it ships as `social/x` and `social/x-mono` (the placeholder name).
- **`payment/generic` is the owner's card silhouette with no ground**, not a full-bleed tile, so it fails Q720 A's
  ground check as drawn. Its record says `fullBleed: false` (allowed only on `payment/`, only `false`), which skips the
  ground check alone: every path then counts as a later path, so none may span the artboard or sit within 1 of it, and
  the flag cannot hide a ground. Put to the owner on the PR (Q-P1).
- **The rename, per docs/30:** `COMPONENT_RENAMES` gains value renames `card/*` → `payment/*`, the black wallet
  lockups → `logo/apple-pay` and `logo/google-pay`, `wallet/paypal` → `logo/paypal-wordmark` (the lockup is the
  wordmark), `wallet/shop-pay` → `logo/shop-pay`, and drops for the white lockups and `provider/apple-white` (the
  owner's `provider/apple` is the white glyph). A single component's reader (`readSingleView`) skipped any value with
  a second slash that was not a plan coordinate, so a mark built before the rename was invisible to Update and would
  have been rebuilt beside itself; it now admits a value the ledger renamed or dropped.

### Gates, and the mutations that fail them by name

- `lint-glyph-geometry.ts`: a rounded ground on `payment/visa` → **TILE BAKED**; a border ring over `payment/amex` →
  **TILE BORDER BAKED**; `fullBleed: false` on `payment/visa` → **TILE BORDER BAKED** (the flag hides nothing).
- `lint-mark-colors.ts`: `tileEdge` removed from the def → **TILE EDGE** on every tile; `#1434CB` → `#1434CC` in

- `lint-mark-provenance.ts`: `social/x.svg`'s record removed → "has no record"; new self-checks for `normalized` and
  `fullBleed`.
- `emit-marks.ts`: `logo/visa`'s width stated 28 → refused, by file.
- `lint-icon-count.ts`: "74 marks" in the description → fails by field. Its brand-mark scope reads `description`,
  props, part notes and `codeOnly`, not `summary`, `docs`, `ai` or `notes`, which also ship; filed as #3062.
- `test-update-apply.ts`, new section: a payment tile and a logo built under their former names are renamed in place,

### Traps for whoever re-verifies

## (2026-10-27) — Documentation › Specs draws spec panels for the current page (#2830, Q2830.3 A)

**What.** Phase 1 of IA v2 shipped a Specs tab whose description said "Coming later". #2994 shipped the `draw-specs` agent command. Q2830.3 A says specs are drawn only on request, by their own "Draw specs", and that this action becomes Documentation's Specs tab once that area exists. This PR makes the Specs tab a real control:
- **Draw specs** (`apps/studio/src/shell/documentation.ts`) posts a new panel message, `draw-specs`. The host runs it through the agent's action, `ACTIONS.drawSpecs`, under the build's guard. The button reads "Drawing specs…" until the host's verdict lands. The verdict then shows as the result line under the button (`specsState` in `host-session.ts`). A refusal shows the host's words.
- **For the current page.** `drawSpecs` takes a scope. The agent's command stays `'file'` (every family in the file, unchanged). The panel's is `'page'`, and `specTargets` then keeps only the families whose lead set is on `figma.currentPage`, matched by the page's id. Two sets of one name are counted over the whole file first, so the panel and the agent's command skip the same families (the independent review's Nit 1 and gap).
- **Never beside another components write.** While a build, an update, an agent's run or an Update file run is out, the button is unavailable. While the specs draw, `componentBusy()` holds Build and Update file's update step too, so no other `component-update-result` can be read as the specs' verdict.
- **Never by Build or Update.** `specs/never on build` and `specs/never on update` still pass.
- **The ecosystem map** (`docs/public/ecosystem/ecosystem.json`): the `draw-specs` feature gains its figma lane, because the command is now a panel message too (`lint-ecosystem.ts` requires it).
- **Activity: a Specs row of its own** (Q713 A, refining Q3034.1 A). Draw specs gets its own "Specs" row in the Activity drawer, like Style guides: "Drawing specs…" while it runs, then its verdict. It never runs on, or lands on, the Build set row. `specs` is a new Activity operation (`OpKey`, `OP_TITLE` in `shell/activity.ts`, `activityReading` in `main.ts`). The verdict is a `component-update-result`. While Draw specs is out, the reducer writes that verdict to `specsState` alone, leaving `componentUpdate` and `componentLatest` untouched. An agent's `draw-specs` is the same operation: its run is the Specs row's, its verdict lands in `specsState` (as an agent's style guide lands in `styleGuideState`), and while it runs `componentBusy()` holds Draw specs, Build and Update file's update step. A panel build that the host declines because an agent's Draw specs holds the build's guard is not left pending.
- **Owner decisions built:** Q2830.10–.12 A (on #2830): the button sits in the Specs card under its description, it draws the current page only, and it shows its own busy label with one result line. Q3034.1 A and Q713 A: the run gets its own row in Activity.
- **Copy stays DRAFT** (Q685 A). The description drops "Coming later", which is no longer true, and the two new strings are placeholders.

**Tests.**
- `test-agent-link.ts` `specs/panel`: the panel's `draw-specs` reaches `ACTIONS.drawSpecs` scoped `'page'`, and its verdict comes back. `specs/agent`: the agent's reaches it scoped `'file'`. Mutation: the panel's case scoped `'file'` → `specs/panel` fails.
- `test-build-completed.ts` section 8: Badge and Switch row on pages of their own, the current page Switch row's. The panel's Draw specs tags a spec panel for Switch row alone. Mutations: the case scoped `'file'`, or `specTargets` ignoring `page` → `specs/this page` fails.
- `test-host-session.ts`: the verdict that lands while Draw specs is out is Specs' result, a refusal of the panel's request is too, and an agent's refused command leaves it out. Q713 A (`specs/Q713 A`): that verdict leaves the components operation's slots alone; an agent's `draw-specs` runs the Specs operation, its verdict settles the run and is Specs' result; and a panel build declined behind an agent's Draw specs is not left pending. Mutations: the agent command's `draw-specs` entry removed, the verdict also written to `componentUpdate`, and the refusal's guard check without the Specs operation each fail by name.
- `test-build-completed.ts` section 9: two sets named Badge on two pages are skipped by the page scope as by the file scope (`specs/one rule`), and the page is matched by a fresh object carrying its id (`specs/page by id`).
- `test:chrome`: on the plugin, Specs offers Draw specs, posts `draw-specs` alone, reads as drawing, and shows a planted verdict as its result line. `test-style-guides-page.mjs` reads the tab's new text. Added for the independent reviews, each failing by name under its mutation. Q713 A: Activity's own Specs row runs "Drawing specs…" and then carries the verdict (mutation: the Specs row removed). While Draw specs is out, the Build set row does not run it (mutation: the components row running on `specsState`). Draw specs' verdict does not land on the Build set row (mutation: the verdict also written to `componentUpdate`). An agent's `draw-specs` runs on the Specs row and holds Draw specs unavailable (mutation: `componentBusy()` without `agentRunning('specs')`). The earlier review's arms: while Draw specs is out, Update file's sets step posts no build (C3: `componentBusy()` without `specsState`); with an agent's components run out, Draw specs reads unavailable and a click posts nothing (C2: `paint` ignoring `busy`), and the draw's own guard posts nothing from a control left available (C4). The review at `4291c315` (M1): with an Update file run on its setup or theme step and its dialog closed, where `componentBusy()` is false and the run itself holds the button, Documentation › Specs reads Draw specs unavailable and posts nothing, even from a control left available, until the step's verdict ends the run (mutation: `updateRun` dropped from `specs.read`'s `busy` and `specs.draw`'s guard).

## (2026-10-27) — prism3-rebind: lessons from a commerce checkout rebuild

A checkout rebuild (cart, shipping, payment, review; desktop and mobile) onto a Prism3-generated brand
library tested `prism3-rebind` as written. This PR folds the generic lessons in (stacked on #3046).

- **§2, items 14–19:**
  - inventory a large source page by structure: labels at mid-row, a separate screenshots section, content bounds rather than frame size, states named from unique texts;
  - pick key screens by pattern;
  - read keys from instances already in the consuming file;
  - map a source in another typeface by role and size;
  - keep source copy exactly, typos included, as an owner question;
  - leave plugin widgets out of the build.
- **§3:** fill each breakpoint from its own source. Cloning desktop to mobile carried the wrong product.
- **§4, six trap rows:**
  - a layout-direction change keeps FIXED sizing and flips `layoutGrow` to height;
  - FILL text in a wrap row collapses;
  - a pending import blocks text-style and later calls, and timed-out calls resume and duplicate nodes;
  - `exportAsync` hangs while another call is stuck;
  - a collapsed disclosure exposes no slot;
  - a text property may not drive a nested label.

**Gaps filed alongside:** #3054–#3059. Scrubbed of client, file, brand, product and page names, node IDs and keys.

## (2026-10-27) — Card marks: full-bleed tiles, corners and edge drawn from tokens (#2343, Q720 A)

**Status:** `brand-mark` def, a schema field, the four card files, two gate arms. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT
unchanged: only existing token roles are bound. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. Lands before PR 3 (the
provider artwork), so the owner's files drop in full-bleed.

### What changed

- **Owner decision Q720 A (2026-10-26, on #2343):** card tile files are full-bleed (square corners, no border, the
  tile's ground kept, since a colored ground is part of the provider's mark), and the card-mark host draws the corner
  radius and the border from tokens, so every tile gets the same edge at every size and mode.
- **The four `card/*` placeholders are re-exported full-bleed.** The rounded ground path (radius 3) became the
  artboard rectangle `M0 0H32V20H0Z`; the colors did not move, so `provenance.json`'s `colors` hold. Each record's
  `source` and a new `_note` line record the re-export. Followed the "replacing a placeholder" steps: regen, `--accept`
  on `lint-component-surface.ts` alone (19 members, same count; `component-axes.json` does not move), change note.
- **Where the edge lives: the glyph's own frame.** A mark is built from its SVG by `createNodeFromSvg`, which returns
  a FRAME at the artboard. That frame is the node a host instances and resizes, so it is the host. A new `PartDef`
  field, `tileEdge: { when, radius, strokeWidth }`, on a `vector` drawn inline, makes the projector bind that frame's
  four corner radii and its `strokeWeight`, stroke it with the def's `border` paint, and set `clipsContent`, at the
  coordinates `when` names. `brand-mark` names its card members, read from the vocabulary by kind (`CARD_MARKS`), so a
  network added to the set is a tile the day it lands. Square and wallet plans are byte-identical.
- **Tokens:** `tile.radius` → `radius.sm`, `tile.border-width` → `border-width.hairline`, `tile.border` →
  `color.border.primary` (through `paintKeys: ['tile.{slot}']`; the artwork still takes no ink, by def id). **Owner
  decision Q-T1 A, Q-T2 A, Q-T3 A (2026-10-27, on #3047):** `radius.sm`, `color.border.primary`, and the 1px hairline
  on every tile, as built.
- **Both executors already carry it**, which is why there is no executor diff: each applies a node's `bound` and
  `paints.strokes` on any node type, and each `claimDefaults` reads `clipsContent` from the plan on every FRAME and
  leaves a bound corner alone. The GLYPH's artboard is a FRAME. Shown by mutation, below.

### Gates

- `lint-mark-colors.ts` arm (e), CARD TILE EDGE: on every `card/*` member the mark's frame binds all four corner radii
  to a `radius/*` variable and `strokeWeight` to a `border-width/*` variable, strokes in a `color/border/*` variable
  and clips; on every other member it clips nothing. Card-ness is typed in the gate (`card/` prefix), not read from
  `BRAND_MARK_KINDS`. Arm (c) admits exactly those properties on exactly that node, so the mark is still never retinted.
  "Every size": the plan has no size coordinate; a host binds the height (20, 24, 32) on its instance, and a bound
  radius and weight hold their value at each, where a baked edge scales with the artwork.
- `lint-glyph-geometry.ts` mark arm, read from the SOURCE file: CARD TILE BAKED (the first path is not the full
  artboard as one shape whose vertices are exactly its four corners) and CARD BORDER BAKED (a later path spans the
  whole artboard, or sits inside it by at most 1px on every side: a tile drawn over a ground that shows as its rim).

- Executor tests, one per executor: `test-write-components.ts` (plugin shim) and `test.ts` (paste payload) build the marks
  and read the frame back: four corners, the weight (scalar or all four per-side keys, #1332), the stroke paint and the
  clip, against names typed from the decision, and no edge on a square or wallet mark. The plugin test reads which
  marks are cards from the `.svg` files in `marks/card/` (none hard-coded, Q-B7 amended): each must build as a tile.
- Fallout: Studio's committed `used-by` index (`apps/studio/gen-used-by.ts --write`) lists brand-mark under `radius.sm`.

| Mutation (each on a committed tree) | Fails, by name |
|---|---|
| `card/visa.svg` ground back to the rounded tile | `lint-glyph-geometry` — CARD TILE BAKED |
| `card/visa.svg` gains a full-artboard ring path over the ground | `lint-glyph-geometry` — CARD BORDER BAKED |
| `tileEdge.radius` dropped from the projector (the frame's radius unbound) | `lint-mark-colors` — CARD TILE EDGE |
| the edge's stroke paint dropped | `lint-mark-colors` — CARD TILE EDGE |
| plugin `claimDefaults` writes `clipsContent: false` on the mark's frame | `test-write-components` — #2343 Q720 A plugin executor; `test:roundtrip` |
| paste payload's `claimDefaults` writes `clipsContent: false` | `test.ts` — #2343 Q720 A paste executor |
| a fifth `.svg` in `marks/card/` that no member builds | `test-write-components` — #2343 Q720 A plugin executor |
| `card/visa.svg`: ground in the border color under a white rounded tile inset 1px (review M10) | `lint-glyph-geometry` — CARD BORDER BAKED |
| `card/visa.svg`: chamfered straight-line ground spanning the artboard (review M7) | `lint-glyph-geometry` — CARD TILE BAKED |

### Traps for whoever re-verifies

- The frame's stroke is drawn INSIDE and over the artwork, by design: the edge sits on the tile, not around it, so the
  mark's footprint does not grow.
- `component-specs.ts` keeps radius and stroke width out of `specs.json` for every def (its header), so the spec shows
  the edge's color only; the radius and width reach code through the token-usage report and the def's tokens.

## (2026-10-27) — CI runs the chrome suite in three shards, and a gate holds every section to exactly one (#2898)

After #2883 split the gates into parallel jobs, `chrome` was the whole critical path: its suite step took 1,436 s (about 24 minutes) on main, against 12 minutes or less for every other job. It could not be split, because `apps/studio/test-chrome.mjs` is one top-level script of about 15,600 lines with no way to pick a section.

**How the suite splits without changing an assertion.** A one-off transform (TypeScript's parser over the file, not committed) wrapped each section's top-level statements in `if (runs('<id>'))`. The ids are the section numbers, made unique where two sections shared one (`29` and `29-pinned`, `47` and `47-menu`; `18-readonly`, `18-s4d` and `18-s4f` for the three banners inside 18). A declaration that any other section reads stays at the top level, outside every guard. The transform found 202 of them, computed to a fixed point, and all are free of side effects except two `esbuild` bundles of engine source, which make no assertion. Inside a guard, nothing is indented, so the diff is the guard lines and blame still points at the code. Only five things carry state across sections: the check-box counts, the hooks seen, the exemptions, the lowest readings and the assertion counters. They are the end-of-run checks' inputs. A shard writes them to its record, and `test-chrome.mjs --merge` runs those checks once over every shard. The whole suite still runs them itself.

**The shards.** `CHROME_SHARD=<n>` is set in the step's `env:`, not as an argument, so the command is the one `verify.ts` runs whole, and `lint-doc-gates`' argv arm stays exact. `chrome-shards.mjs` gives each of three shards about a third of one whole local run's 1,969 s. The split was greedy, longest section first. Three shards, not four: the `plugin` job (about 12 minutes) is the next longest, so a fourth shard would not move the critical path.

**The gate, `test:chrome-shards`.** Its expected list is the unsharded suite's own: `test-chrome.mjs --list` reaches every guard and runs none. Its actual list is what each record says ran. It never reads the shard map. It fails by name on a section in no shard, a section in two, a section the suite does not list, an assertion outside every section, or a shard that ran the end-of-run checks. A shard that crashed or never reported leaves its sections in no shard. Locally it reads the whole run's record (`all.json`).

**Proof that every assertion still runs exactly once.** Main's suite was run whole, unchanged except for one line that logs each label: 39,693 assertions, all passing, in 1,969 s. Then the three shards and the merge were run from this branch: 39,693 assertions, all passing, in 629 s, 582 s and 653 s. `compare-chrome-assertions.mjs` compares the two sides as multisets. Many labels carry a reading of their own run, such as the Activity bar's clock, a server port or the frames a glide took. So an assertion's name is its label with every run of digits masked. The diff of names is empty, and the sorted name lists are byte-identical. The exact labels have 36,513 distinct values on each side, and 126 of them differ in count. Every one of those 126 is a reading. For scale, the same comparison between two whole runs, main's baseline and this branch's unsharded run inside `npm run verify`, gives 136 exact labels that differ and 0 names.

**Mutations, each failing by name**, each on a `wip:` commit, with the mutated shard re-run for real: `47-menu` dropped from every shard gave `section "47-menu" ran in no shard`. `47-menu` in shards 1 and 3 gave `section "47-menu" ran in 2 runs (shard 1, shard 3)`. Before either of those, the gate caught a real miss: the first balanced map left out section `27`, the focus-ring sweep, because its header has a computed title the timing script could not read. The gate's first run reported `section "27" ran in no shard`.

Also checked, as the issue asked: smoke flake #2629 is not worse since #2883 started smoke earlier. Of the 317 CI runs from 2026-10-21, 5 failed in the smoke step, and all 5 were real failures on PR branches (a missing hook, a place not offered). None showed #2629's stall signature ("rendered no frame", "could not pause").

## (2026-10-27) — The chrome suite waits for the mode control to settle before it reads it (#3033)

`web light 380 / brand, 4 modes: every mode is choosable in the preview header, none clipped` went red on main and on several PR heads, reading `hc-dark` as clipped. The control's `fit` (`apps/studio/src/shell/preview.ts`) picks radios or the select in a `requestAnimationFrame` scheduled by a `ResizeObserver`. At widths up to 560 the check clicked `pane-toggle-preview` and read the control straight away, so it could land before that frame and see the radios the select was about to replace.

Section 17 of `apps/studio/test-chrome.mjs` now reads through `settled`: it re-reads the control a frame apart until the select shows, or radios show with none clipped, for at most 2 s, then reports what it read. The 5- and 6-mode checks used to wait a fixed two frames; they use `settled` too, because the measurement below showed two frames is not enough under a slow frame. While this was in review, #3037 added a fixed two-frame wait before the 4-mode read on main, and #3028 then added a bounded wait for the same condition after it. The merge replaces both with `settled`: the two-frame wait for the reason above, and #3028's wait because it duplicates `settled`'s check.

### How it was proved

Section 17 was run on its own (the suite's head plus that section) against a build with `fit` delayed 300 ms after its frame, which stands in for a slow CI frame:

- Without the wait, the 4-mode check failed with the reading from the issue (`{"radios":4,"clipped":["hc-dark"],…,"select":false}`). The 5- and 6-mode checks failed the same way even with their two-frame wait.
- With `settled` on all three reads, all 162 assertions passed.
- With `fit` never running on resize, a real clip, all three checks still failed by name after the 2 s bound. The wait does not hide a control that never settles.

## (2026-10-26) — prism3-rebind: snapshot and restore around a structural library publish

`skills/prism3-rebind` gains the procedure for the case where a library publish replaces a component's
layers, so every per-instance override on the replaced layers resets when the owner accepts it. It
lands in §11 (auditing and repairing a rebuild), plus two §4 trap rows.

- **§11.5, snapshot first:** key records by path inside the component, never by layer name (names
  repeat, and a name-keyed record overwrites itself; the first real snapshot lost values exactly this way
  and was retaken). Store values, not node IDs, for anything the publish replaces. Locate instances by
  container and slot index. Validate by re-reading random instances with independently written code.
- **§11.6, restore by diffing:** prove the in-memory snapshot is the one on disk (hash both), re-measure
  after the accept, then read → write only differences → read back, reporting each field as carried /
  restored / failed. In the run this came from, photos, markers and price texts *carried* (their layer
  paths survived); what needed writing were the values the new component *defaults differently* (status
  visibility, price type). Verify with a mapped-value fingerprint derived from the snapshot alone,
  against a fresh read, and mutate one instance to prove the check fails by name.
- **§11.7, "path gone" is a library regression:** a state overlay vanished from the published variant.
  No override was lost, so only the failed paths and a screenshot showed it. Report it, keep the values
  ready, never rebuild it as a lookalike. The library restored it, and a re-check then carried every field.
- **§4 rows:** there is no single-field override reset (`resetOverrides()` clears slot swaps too), so an
  override equal to the main's value is left as inert; and a multi-megabyte result goes to disk via the
  harness and is processed by script rather than read.

The toggle trick for an explicit override that survives an update was already in §4 (#2987), and §11.6
points to it rather than repeating it. Scrubbed: no client, file, brand, product or page names, node IDs
or keys.

**Q-B1 B is written down where it will be seen.** The marks are committed because the repository is internal for
now; if it goes public, the set is refactored to placeholders plus recorded terms first. That condition is in
`marks/NOTICE.md`, `marks/provenance.json`'s `_note` and `icons/NOTICE.md`, and `lint-mark-provenance.ts` fails if
`NOTICE.md` or the `_note` loses it.

**The diagnosis that kept the projector change small.** The `vector` part path already builds a GLYPH from an SVG
document through `createNodeFromSvg`, and a GLYPH node only takes ink through `descendantFills`. So a mark is a GLYPH
whose document carries literal fills and whose part takes no ink: one branch keyed on the def id (the `ICON_DEF_ID`
precedent), resolving the glyph against `BRAND_MARK_DOCUMENTS` and skipping `paintOf`, rather than a new node type.
The hand-edit record and the artboard read-back apply to marks unchanged. The in-place update path needed one
line (independent review, B1): Update File's single-component reader dropped any member value with a `/`, so every
`brand-mark/<kind>/<name>` read as "not a member" and a recolor never landed. It now accepts a value that is one of the
def's own plan coordinates, and `test-update-apply.ts` reads every mark and takes a recolor in place.

**Gates and their independence.** `lint-mark-provenance.ts` walks the folder itself and compares it with the typed
records both ways, field by field against its own literals. `lint-mark-colors.ts` re-parses each source SVG with its
own reader and compares the fills with the record, the generated module (in order, spelled as supplied) and the
`brand-mark` Figma plans (no paint, no bound variable), and holds that no host pushes `descendantFills` into a
`brand-mark/*` instance (vacuous until a host carries one; its detector is proven by a self-check). The
`lint-glyph-geometry.ts` arm types its own artboard table (square 24×24, card 32×20, wallet 24 high at the recorded
width) and measures the ink with a walker over the whole SVG path grammar (relative commands, smooth curves, arcs),
because provider artwork is exported by whatever tool the provider used. Each was mutated to fail by name; the
mutations and their failing lines are in the PR.

**Held for the owner** (Q-block on #2343): the page the marks sit on in the file (built: a "Brand marks" page under
Foundations, after "Icons & assets", so each Foundations page holds one set and the web list reads "Brand mark"), the
def's shipped prose, which is DRAFT, and the placeholder names the owner's files must match.

**Trap for whoever drops the real files in.** A wallet lockup's width is stated once, in its provenance record
(`width`), and both the emitter and the geometry arm compare the file with it. Change the record with the file.

## (2026-10-26) — Update file with Theme unticked measures against the stored brand (#3023, Q701 B)

**What.** Q699 A had Update file's due read, its scoped check and its update all measure against the panel's brand, because the run's Theme step stores it first. But Theme can be unticked, and then the update laid the panel's plans while the file kept its stored brand, so the next load's due read flagged the sets the update had just written. Q701 B (the owner's decision, 2026-10-25): with Theme unticked, all three measure against the stored brand, the one the run leaves in the file.

- `brandFor(theme, panel)` (`apps/studio/src/state/update-file.ts`) is the one rule: the panel's brand when Theme is ticked, else `undefined`, which the host already reads as "the file's stored brand" (`brandOf` in `apps/plugin/src/main.ts`, as for an agent's update). The host is unchanged.
- `apps/studio/src/main.ts`'s `panelBrand(theme)` uses it everywhere the panel sends a brand. The check and the scoped check take Theme's tick from the checklist. The update, its re-check and the due read after a run take it from the run's own steps.
- **A Theme toggle checks the file again** (`shell/update-file.ts`). The checklist goes back to "Checking the file…", asks for the due read under the brand the toggle picks, ticks the due sets afresh from that answer, and asks the scoped check over them. So the counts shown are the ones the run writes. While it checks, the Theme box is gone from the dialog, so focus falls back to the dialog itself and never leaves the modal.

**Tests.**
- `test-build-completed.ts` section 6b: stored A, the set built under B, the panel on B with Theme unticked. Each message is built through the panel's own `brandFor`. The update lays A's plan (the ledger records A), and the next load (the read with no brand, as at load) reads the set `current`. Mutation: `brandFor` returning the panel's brand whatever Theme says → `q701/update writes A` and `q701/next load` fail by name.
- `test:verdict`'s two checklist drivers (`test-build-verdict.mjs`'s `runSets`, `test-style-guides-page.mjs`'s `runGuides`) untick Theme, so each now answers the re-check as the main thread does before it ticks on.
- `test:chrome`: Theme unticked, ticked again, then unticked. Each toggle sends a fresh `file-sets-request` and `update-check-request` with no brand, then with the panel's, then with none again; focus stays in the dialog while it checks; and the update then posts with no brand.
- `test:chrome`, after the independent review: the update's verdict ends the run, and the due read after it carries no brand; a toggle whose answer finds Tag due too ticks Tag; and an update of fewer sets than were checked re-checks them with no brand. Mutations, each failing by name in both themes: `endStep`'s due read sending `panelBrand(true)` → `… after a run with Theme unticked, the due read asks against the file's stored brand …`; the run's re-check sending `panelBrand(true)` → `… the run checks the fewer sets again against the file's stored brand …`; the re-tick from a toggle's answer deleted → `… a Theme toggle ticks the due sets from its own answer …`.

**Scope.** Only the brand selection and the re-check. The consumer-breaking flags in `update-plan.ts` and their checklist line (#2831, #2864) are another lane's.

**A probe race, fixed while here.** CI's `test:chrome` failed twice on this branch with `web light 380 / brand, 4 modes: … none clipped` (`hc-dark` cut off). The PR doesn't touch that page, and the run passed locally. At 380 the probe clicks the preview pane's toggle and measures at once, before the shown pane's header has laid out and the mode control has picked radios or the select. The probe now waits, bounded at 3 s, for every radio to sit inside the control or for the select to show. A radio still clipped at the bound fails the arm as before.

## (2026-10-26) — Fixed paint, the slot aspect lock, and keep-own on rebuild (#2343 PR 2)

**What landed.** The host side of the brand marks, from the #2343 proposal (§1.2, §4 PR 2), built independently of
PR 1's pipeline so the two could run in parallel: nothing here names a mark.

- **`fixedPaint`** on a `slot`, `overlay` or `nest` part: the projector pushes no `descendantFills` into it, and the
  plan says `fixedPaint: true`, so a gate reads the promise and the outcome as two facts. A slot or overlay otherwise
  takes its host's icon ink on every vector inside, which on a brand mark is the retint the provider forbids. Refused
  on any other kind and beside a `paintSlot`.
- **`aspectLock`** on a `slot` or `nest` part: the part binds `height` alone, and both executors read the proportion of
  the component the instance instances, resize to it, lock it and then bind the height, so Figma derives the width.
  The box lock (`aspectRatio`) takes its ratio from a variant axis; a slot's belongs to whatever the designer swaps in,
  so it is read at build time. A slot may now bind a `height`, but only under the lock (without it the height still
  reaches no node, and is still refused).
- **Keep-own on rebuild** (owner decision Q-B3 A). The as-built record (`member-baseline.ts`) gains `art`, one hash per
  node holding vectors, over their geometry. A designer who redraws a glyph inside its main component changed paths no
  node hash read, so an Update laid a fresh import over the drawing; now the redraw reads as a hand edit at the frame
  and is kept and reported under owner decision Q1, as a recolor already was. Beside the node hashes, on `reactions`'
  precedent: a record written before it makes no claim, so no existing file reads as edited.

- **A recolored mark takes the new colors.** In place, an untouched glyph keeps its vectors when a fresh import draws
  the same paths, so an override on one survives; that comparison read paths and boxes only, which is right for an
  icon (its fills are the host's binding, written after) and wrong for a mark, whose fills are the document's. A glyph
  that takes no host ink now compares fills too, so a provider color change is not kept under a current stamp.

**The diagnosis.** Keep-and-report already existed for every node (#2265, Q1); it missed exactly one kind of edit, the
geometry, because `vectorPaths` was never in the signature. Adding it to the node signature would have changed every
vector's hash and made every glyph in every file read as hand-edited until `BASELINE_V` moved; a separate field
scoped the change to records written from now on.

**Scope, stated.** The artwork hash applies to every glyph, the icon set's too, not only marks: Q1's rule is the same
for both, and a redrawn icon was silently overwritten before. No def sets `fixedPaint` or `aspectLock` yet; the first
hosts are the branded buttons and card fields (#2343 PRs 4–6). EXECUTOR_REVISION 40 (#3019 took 39).

**Tests.** `packages/engine/test.ts` (#2343 PR 2 arms, on a Button clone whose leading slot is a mark slot, with the
real Button as control), `apps/plugin/test-write-components.ts` (`mark slot/…`, the real executor against a live 32×20
main in the shim) and `apps/plugin/test-update-apply.ts` (`redraw/…`, `recolor/taken`). Each mutation and its failing assertion is in
the PR.

## (2026-10-26) — Glass: a background-blur effect style bound to a blur token (#2869, Q464 A)

Owner decision Q464 A: a "glass" treatment for text set over the bottom of a photograph, a light veil fill plus a background blur (the source comp: `#f7f7f7` at 69%, 32px). The naming and the fill/style split are the owner's decisions Q2869.1–5 A (2026-10-26, on #2869; the name `glass` is Q2869.4 A): one token `blur.glass` = 32px, not a ramp and not a lever; the fill a color role `color.glass.surface`; one Effect Style `glass`, blur only.

- **The alpha lives in the value, not on the paint.** The 10/21 evidence on #2869 is that Figma forces a variable-bound color paint to opacity 1 on every instance, so "a surface at 69%" cannot be a bound paint plus an opacity. `color.glass.surface` aliases a `white-alpha` / `black-alpha` step, the way `scrim.default` does: white 70% on the light family, black 70% on the dark, 90% in high contrast. It varies by mode on purpose, which is what separates it from `veil`: glass is a surface that follows the page polarity, so `text.primary` reads on it in every mode.
- **An Effect Style cannot carry a fill**, so the glass in Figma is the `glass` style plus a frame fill bound to `color/glass/surface`. The style's description says so. No paint style is emitted (Q2869.2 A).
- **The binding is by name in the emission, by id in the file.** `shadow-styles.json` carries the glass blur's `boundVariables.radius` as a by-name alias (`<root>/blur/glass`), the same convention as every other emitted binding. Figma cannot read that, so both writers (`write-styles.ts` and the paste path in `materialise-to-figma.ts`) strip it and bind through `setBoundVariableForEffect`. A file without the variable reports a miss and keeps the literal 32px. `blur` is a new FLOAT collection (scope `EFFECT_FLOAT`), written by the FLOAT plan before the styles step.
- **The glass rides in the one Effect Style file** (`shadow-styles.json`), because Figma has one Effect Style list. Tests that assumed "every effect style is a shadow" now name glass as the one exception rather than filtering by prefix.
- **Gates, each mutated red by name** (wip commit first, then the mutation): `test.ts` "glass <brand>: the effect's radius BINDS <root>/blur/glass, not a literal" (the emitter writing a literal radius); "color.glass.surface resolves in every mode … to a translucent primitive" (a dangling alias, and an alias to opaque black); "<root>/blur/glass is a 32 FLOAT …" (the committed Figma value drifting to 31). `check-consumability.mjs` "[#2869] the glass blur reaches CSS as a length" (`blur.glass` retyped to a bare number). `test-write-styles.ts` "glass: its radius is bound to blur/glass by variable id" (the executor skipping `setBoundVariableForEffect`).
- **The accessibility claim is gated, not just stated.** The roles record glass at `ratio: 1` against itself, so no mode contract measures text on it. `test.ts` now composites `color.glass.surface` over every gray ground 0–255 in each brand and mode, with the WCAG math written out in the gate, and asserts `text.primary` ≥ 4.5:1 ("glass <brand>: text.primary reads ≥ 4.5:1 on color.glass.surface composited over the worst-case ground"). Two sibling arms spell the Q2869.3 A steps per mode (white-alpha.70 / black-alpha.70 / white-alpha.90 / black-alpha.90) and that the glass polarity follows the page. Swapping the polarity in `modes.ts` fails all three by name in every brand; lowering the alpha to 60 fails the step arm by name. The corpus floor today is 7.9:1 (NB fixture, dark mode over white).
- **A trap for whoever re-verifies:** mutating `modes.ts` to a nonexistent alpha step does not turn the `test.ts` glass gate red. `regen.ts` throws on the dangling alias, so the committed artifacts the gate reads never change; `every-example-compiles` and `regen --check` catch that case instead. Mutate the committed artifact to test the gate itself. Also, `tools/exporter-comparison/gate.ts` does not compare a FLOAT variable's value, so a drifted `blur/glass` value passes it; the `test.ts` arm is the one that holds it.
- **Inverse:** `color.glass.surface` has no inverse counterpart, and is registered in `INVERSE_GAPS` as UNDECIDED: a glass band inside an inverse band has not been asked about.
- Contract 14.11.0 (MINOR: two added paths). The executor revision rises to 39 (`write-styles.ts` changed). The drift-gate artifact count rises to 220 (a `blur.json` per Figma brand).

## (2026-10-26) — Published libraries: a removed layer listed as breaking, and a checklist line per set (#2831, #2864)

**Status:** plugin dry run (`update-plan.ts`), Update file's checklist line (`checkedSetOf`, `messages.ts`, one line of `main.ts`'s
`checkSets`, the studio adapter and shell), tests. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` unchanged:
the executor is not touched.

### What changed

- **What #2839 already covered.** `breakingOf` listed drops, layer replacements, property removals and retypes, and a
  rename to a `_` or `.` name, on published sets only (`getPublishStatusAsync`), in the check's section, the headline
  and the confirm. Q394 A's slot-item rule is already enforced by `lint-naming.ts`. This PR adds the case it missed
  and the checklist surface.
- **#2864, a removed layer.** A layer the plan no longer has is a `children` change (`removed — not in the plan`),
  never a `type` replacement, so `breakingOf` did not count it. It now adds a `layer` entry per removed path, with how
  many members lose it. Layers the plan adds under the same parent are named as the likely new name, and the line says
  a declared `part` rename keeps the layer in place. That is the safest available action: the ledger is how a
  rename stays in place (#2759, Q350). A layer moved into an inserted frame is a move (`MOVES`), not a removal, so it
  is not listed. The shim arm is the real case from #2864's reproduction, Tag's `check` → `checkGlyph`: with no ledger
  entry, 15 members are listed. With the shipped entry, nothing is listed. On an unpublished set, nothing is listed.
- **Counted per member the update acts on, not read off `changes`.** The first version summed the `children` removal
  changes, and the shim showed a false positive: a layer a designer added by hand also reads as "removed — not in the
  plan". The update skips that member whole, under every hand-edit choice (§5), so nothing is removed. So the dry run
  now keeps its own uncapped per-path count, `SetPreview.removedLayers`, and leaves out members with a structural hand
  edit. The count is absent when there are none, so a set with no removals keeps its preview hash. The replace arm
  has the same overcount, and it reads a capped list. That is filed as #3025, not fixed here.
- **A private rename, end to end in the shim.** The earlier private arm put a `setRename` on a preview by hand. A
  new arm runs it through a ledger `def` rename to `_tag`, so the set is found under its old name, and the rename is
  listed on a published set but not on an unpublished one.
- **The checklist line.** `CheckedSet.breaks`, one line per published set from `breakingSummary`: each case counted,
  with what breaks and what the update does (a drop is kept and marked deprecated, so consumer instances still
  resolve). The checklist draws it under the set's row. The wording is DRAFT, waiting on the owner's wording pass.
  The mapping moved from `main.ts` into `checkedSetOf`, so `checkSets` changes by one line and the field can be tested,
  which keeps clear of the #3023 lane.
- **Q2831.1, posted on #2831:** whether Update should refuse, untick by default, or ask for an extra confirmation
  when a change breaks consumers in a published file. A (rec), built here: flag only. Nothing reaches a consumer file
  until the library is published in Figma, and Update saves a named version before it writes.

### Verification

Each detector was mutated after a `wip:` commit and failed by name in `test-update-apply.ts`. The new arms: the
`layer` arm, the same-parent lookup, the structural-skip guard, the summary's layer clause, and `checkedSetOf`'s line.
#2839's arms, re-run against the new arms: the publish guard, private, drop, replace, and property removal. The adapter
dropping the field fails `test-write-adapter.ts` by name. The shell drawing the line is asserted in `test:chrome`, which
passes; it was not mutation-run, because that takes a full chrome rebuild and run. `npm run verify` in full.

  bound`; the version write skipped on an unedited cover → `update/version refreshed on an unedited cover`;
  `coverPrint` reading the slot → `logo/content in the slot is not a hand edit`; `setName` writing `id` →
  `the Brand name field writes name, not id`; the fallback back to the id as written → `name/the readable fallback`.

### Held

- **The subtitle is in the fingerprint.** Retyping it marks the whole cover edited, so the name stops updating. The
  wireframe's "What Update keeps current" board proposed judging each part on its own (the subtitle written once, then
  the team's). The Q-block did not ask it, so this keeps the one-fingerprint rule and raises it as a question.
- **Layout options** (centered, low-left, framed) are the owner's follow-up, filed separately.
