## (2026-10-26) — Usage panels: specimens at their own width, a family as one component, markers on their parts (#2970, #2916)

Items 1 and 4 of the owner's first usage-panel QA round, after the owner chose A on Q1–Q5 (2026-10-24), and the anatomy
marker gate #2916 asked for. One PR: the width rule and the family title both reshape the same panel, and the marker
gate reads the same specimens.

- **Why Banner went one letter per line.** The Specimen block's placeholder is a Badge instance, which hugs. The swap to
  the documented member kept that hug, so a member built at a width (Banner 480, Checkbox.Row 320) hugged its content,
  and its fill-width text collapsed to its narrowest. The draw now gives a fixed member's specimen that member's width
  and a hugging member's specimen hug. **Not confirmed in a real file**: the test host now keeps the placeholder's
  sizing through a swap and reproduces both reported symptoms (Banner's "Title" at 24px, the Row's label at 12px); that
  Figma does the same is inferred from the symptoms matching.
- **The width rule (`panelLayout`).** Each anatomy specimen's stage is its member's width plus the stage padding, with
  room on the left for each bracket tier. Tiers are counted from the member's own layers, the way the draw assigns them:
  stacked siblings share a tier, nested or side-by-side brackets do not. Theming adds twice the default stage plus
  16px, unless that makes the panel 960 or wider; then the modes stack. The panel is the widest of these plus its
  padding, and never under 560. Banner's comes to 657 and the Row's to 800 (the Row's Theming row sits side by side).
  Q2's worked example has Button.Group's row at exactly 960 and stacked, so the threshold reads "960 or wider".
- **One number for every reader.** The rule reads the set alone, so Build's `seatNewSet`, the dry run's
  `pageSetMoves` and the apply's re-spacing take the same reach per set (`docPanelReaches`). A drawn panel narrower than
  the rule now gives (a member built wider) is reserved at the new width, and the spec column past the wider of the two.
  The panel records the width it was drawn for, so a member resized since makes it due. The draw still measures the
  real Badge and widens further if a gutter needs it (two-digit markers wider than the 24px it allows); then Update
  spaces by the drawn panel's own box.
- **A family as one component.** The title is the taxonomy page's name and the lede the lead's summary (Q3 A). "In
  this family" is a bulleted Field like Related: the lead first, then the page's order, each part by its name less the
  page's ("Row"), a colon, and its summary's first sentence, the name linked to its set (Q4 A). In Related, a member
  reads as its family, linked to the lead's set, once per list, and the panel's own family is dropped (Q5 A), so
  Checkbox loses "Built from" altogether, as the wireframe drew it. Who is listed and in what order was not part of
  Q1–Q5: posted on #2970 as Q6, with the build following its A (rec).
- **Markers (#2916).** The fix itself landed in #2932; this adds the gate the issue asked for. The oracle now checks
  containment: a leader's tip inside its part's box at the part's middle, a bracket exactly its part's height with both
  ticks ending inside it, and the root always bracketed. Breadcrumbs is pinned by hand: six entries, the `items` slot's
  among them, numbers 1–6 drawn on two specimens. A specimen squeezed narrower than its member, or wider than a 560
  stage, also put parts where no marker could follow; the width rule removes that cause.
- **Mutations**, each failing by name: the width forced to 560; the specimen not sized; a slot part's marker placed
  against its slot; marker 1 dropped; the own-family drop removed; the de-duplication removed.
- `PANEL_FORMAT` goes to 4, so every drawn panel redraws once. An unedited panel is replaced and an edited one kept as
  "(edited)", as before (#2956).

## (2026-10-26) — Figma MCP tools run without a permission prompt in single-repo cloud sessions

The owner added `"permissions": { "allow": ["mcp__Figma"] }` to `.claude/settings.json`. Every Figma call (`use_figma`, screenshots, metadata, sessions) had been stopping for approval, which repeatedly stalled agent work in the Figma files. Agents are not allowed to edit this file, so the owner made the change by hand and an agent carried the PR.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies this:** a cloud session reads a repository's `.claude/settings.json` only when the session holds exactly one repository. An orchestrator session started with both this repo and the knowledge base ignores the rule and keeps prompting. Start such sessions with this repo alone, and attach the second repository mid-session when it's needed. The bare server name `mcp__Figma` allows every tool on that server, so new Figma tools need no edit here.

- **One home per lever (Q2909.3 A, .4 A, v2's table).** Control shape writes no token, so its one home is Components' new
  "Shared by every component" block (`domains/shared-options.ts`), with Density's read-only line. Elsewhere a lever is a
  read-only line whose link opens its home and switches the rail's area (`ui/home-line.ts`): Control shape under Shape ›
  Radius and in Field options, Density in the shared block and Button options, the weights under Control label weight,
  Outline hover after Text button hover.
- **What is due (Q2909.8 A).** The plugin keeps an as-built ledger in the file's root plugin data
  (`apps/plugin/src/as-built-ledger.ts`, `prism3:asBuilt`): one entry per set, the hash of its def after the brand's
  levers (`materializeForBrand`, before projection), with `EXECUTOR_REVISION` and `ENGINE_VERSION`. Build records each
  set it lands whole (no stale member); the in-place update records each set it acts on. `file-sets` answers each present
  set's state from one root read (current, due for its definition or for the engine, or not recorded), at load and as the
  checklist opens. After load a background pass reads hand edits a set at a time (`handEditsOf`, `update-plan.ts`), and
  stops when a write starts. Update file's button carries a badge of the due sets; its checklist lists them first,
  ticked, asks the full check (`update-check-request`) for them alone, waits on it, shows what changes, and offers one

  panel sends the brand it holds with `file-sets-request`, `update-check-request` and `update-sets`, and the main thread
  materializes against it (`brandOf`, `main.ts`). The counts the checklist shows are then the ones the run writes after
  its Theme step stores that brand, and a lever changed but not yet applied shows its sets as due on the first opening.
  Before this, the check read the file's stored brand and the update the brand Theme had just stored, so one run with a
  lever change was refused ("the file changed since the check"). The ledger still records the brand that was applied. An

## (2026-10-26) — Accordion: the indicator pair is a property on the Accordion (#2878)

**Status:** Accordion def, its indicator's notes, `lint-axis-values.ts`, tests, regenerated artifacts. ENGINE minor
(change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no token is added or renamed. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` unchanged: no executor code moved.

### What changed

- **The ask (#2878, owner go Q695 A):** on a published library, a designer switching an accordion to + / − had to find
  the nested `_accordion-indicator` inside each instance. Accordion now carries an `indicator` variant axis
  (`chevron | plus-minus`, chevron first), and the nested indicator **follows** it per member, as it already followed
  `expansion` and `size`. This is Button's `surface` → focus-ring mechanism, not a new one. Figma has no other enum
  property: a boolean or text property cannot pick a nested instance's member, and an instance-swap property swaps
  between components where the indicator is one set.
- **Q-block A on the issue (posted, built as recommended):** the axis replaces Q183's exposed nested property, so there is
  one control, not two that can disagree (option B kept both through a `variantWhen` start value). The set doubles to 48
  members, which Q183 had avoided. The choice now also survives an icon-position switch, which the exposed override was
  expected not to (two parts, two nested instances); that `unverified` note is gone.
- **Additive for library consumers (#2839):** `chevron` leads, so Update gives the 24 existing members
  `indicator=chevron` in place (`update-plan.ts` §2, as Link's `selection` landed in #2872) and builds the 24 plus-minus
  members. Nothing is dropped or replaced and no component property is removed or retyped, so "Breaks library consumers"
  stays empty. Each header's nested indicator keeps its node id, so a consumer's earlier plus-minus override on it stays.
- **Code:** Accordion already had an `indicator` prop (default `chevron`); it is unchanged.
- Accepted through their gates: `component-surface.json`, `component-axes.json` (the new axis, 24 → 48, no property
  removed), `paint-census.json`; the studio's component catalog regenerated.

### Gates

- `#2878 accordion indicator` (`test-roundtrip.ts`): the indicator set and the Accordion built into one file by the
  real executor; on all 48 members the header's nested instance is the indicator member at the Accordion's own
  indicator, expansion and size, drawing the glyph typed in the arm. Mutation: `indicator` dropped from the nests'
  `follow` → this arm fails by name (48 off: every plus-minus member on a chevron).
- `published/accordion indicator additive` and `… in place` (`test-update-apply.ts`): a published 24-member Accordion,
  projected from the pre-#2878 def shape, updated to 48.
- `#2417 accordion` and `#2417 accordion indicator` (`test.ts`) moved to 48 members and to `follow` on `indicator`; the
  accordion arms in `test-update-apply.ts` and the header measurements moved to the doubled counts.

**What.** `apps/plugin/src/spec-panel.ts` draws one spec panel per family in its own column (Q2830.1 B): `SPEC_WIDTH` (880) wide, `SPEC_GAP` (40) right of the family's live usage panel and top-aligned with it. It reads the phase 1 spec model (`componentSpec`), with each def materialized for the file's brand. Per set of the family, it draws:
- **Anatomy:** the usage panel's numbers, from `anatomyMarks`.
- **Spacing and size:** a live specimen per size, without and with a leading visual, redlined in a fixed magenta. Each redline is labeled `variable · px`, with the px read off the specimen.
- **Color:** a table per value of the color key's non-state axes. Rest is shown in full; each other state shows only what changes.
- **Nesting and properties.**

The agent command `draw-specs` runs it. Build and Update never do (Q2830.3 A). Owner's answers: Q2830.1 B, Q2830.2–.7 A (2026-10-24); Q2830.8 A, Q2830.9 A (2026-10-25). Wireframe: https://claude.ai/artifact/5HwWQduNSyWnp9Vv27g6mL

**The color table (Q2830.8 A and Q2830.9 A).**
- One row per binding, in fixed columns (`COLOR_COLUMNS`): State 128 · Part and role 192 · Variable 368 · Value 120. Each is sized from the widest string any set's panel writes, measured in the default brand's body/sm (Inter 14). The longest variable, `color/inverse/interactive/destructive/overlay/pressed`, is 351px.
- The Value cell is a swatch bound to the variable, plus the hex the file resolves for the panel when it's drawn (`hexFor`, `resolveForConsumer`).
- The draw measures each string in the template's face, and names any wider than its column in the run's result. A gradient takes a row per stop, so no cell holds two names.
- A (part, role) bound at rest that a state leaves unbound gets a row whose Variable cell reads "none", with no swatch (Q2994.1, built on its recommendation A, pending the owner's answer). Without it, a disabled selected Tag's table said nothing about its fill.

**Every set moves once.** `PANEL_REACH` now spans both columns (40 + 560 + 40 + 880). Update reserves the spec column for every lead set (`pageViews`), drawn or not, so the first Update after this spaces every row once.

- An unedited earlier panel is replaced. An edited one is kept as "(edited)", retagged `kept`, moved below everything in the spec column, and named in the result.

## (2026-10-25) — The contrast floor is the one text promise (#2991, Q689 A)

**The decision.** #2991 measured the derived resting link at 4.05–4.32:1 on `background.tertiary` / `inverse.background.tertiary` in light and dark, in every corpus brand. The first answer, Q2991.1 A, stepped every link darker to clear the third tier. The owner replaced it with Q689 A: the contrast floor stays the single text promise. Floor-gated inks are promised their bar on the floor surface (`surfaces.<mode>.floorStep`, default `neutral.050` = `background.secondary` / `foreground.primary` in light, the mirror in dark) and on anything nearer the page. Deeper surfaces (`background.tertiary` = `foreground.secondary`, `foreground.tertiary`, and their inverse twins) carry no text promise by design. A brand that needs text deeper moves the floor. No ink value moves. Q419 A stands as narrowed. #3012 (`text.secondary` on the third tier) closes as by design under the same decision.

**What the PR became.** The derivation commit was reverted with a normal revert commit after merging `main`, so every committed artifact is back at `main`'s values; `git diff origin/main --stat` shows docs, `ai-metadata.ts`, the gate and the regenerated `.ai.json` only.

**The statement.**
- `docs/06` §3 gains the floor-promise table and the carve-out; CR-02 in `docs/16` is marked resolved by Q689 A, citing Q419 A. The border half of that finding (L-04) is not covered.
- `.ai.json`: each floor-gated ink's `avoid_when` names the surfaces deeper than its floor and the lever that moves it. The list is computed in `ai-metadata.ts` (`belowFloor`): a ladder surface farther from the page than the role's own floor in any mode. It is not typed, so a brand whose floor sits on another tier names its own surfaces. On the band the lever is `inverseSecondary`, because the band's floor is its own second tier; `floorStep` does not move it.
- `prism3-consume` states the promise and the carve-out, and its self-check no longer claims a passing role exists below the floor. `prism3-theme`'s `surfaces` row and the designer guides' index say the same.

**The gate, `test.ts` (Q689).** Ink names and bars are literals (body 4.5:1, 7:1 in HC; tertiary 3:1, 4.5:1 in HC; every non-primary icon at the non-text bar under `iconContrast: '3:1'`), never a role's `against` or `min`. The floor surface is the one the lever names, read from the emitted hexes; HC uses its family's standard floor. Swept over the token-contract corpus plus the default example:
- **On the floor.** Every floor-gated ink clears its bar on the floor and on every neutral tier no farther from the page, in every mode, page and band.
- **Deeper floor.** `floorStep` moved to the `background.tertiary` step: every floor-gated ink in that family's standard and HC modes clears its bar on the old tertiary hex, and at least one text ink moved. The band's twin moves `inverseSecondary` to the band's tertiary step.

**Mutations, each failing by name:** the resting link pinned one ramp step lighter in `modes.ts` fails the on-floor arm on the link cells; `resolve()` ignoring `cfg.floorStep` fails the deeper-floor arm for every brand and family.

**Ported, not authored here:** `test:chrome` failed twice on this PR's head, each time on a different `#2321 … Shift+Tab from Inspect lands in it false` case at the plugin's 380 width, though this PR's own change touches nothing under `apps/`. That is the race #3005 diagnosed, and #3015's one-function fix to `pmShiftTab` is carried here unchanged. It becomes a no-op once #3015 lands.

## (2026-10-25) — test:chrome: the #2321 Shift+Tab probe waits for the mode control's fit (#3005)

Since IA v2 phase 1 (#2995), the `chrome` job failed one check at random, always on the figma host and at a different viewport each run: `#2321 figma <theme> <width> on <page>: the mode control is live (… Shift+Tab from Inspect lands in it false …)`. No control was ever disabled. Only the Shift+Tab probe missed.

**Root cause: a race in the test, not an unreachable control.** A focus and fit timeline, logged in the page while the section looped, showed the same order on every failure. Focus started on Inspect, so the issue's lead was not the cause: `isVisible()` had picked the right start. Shift+Tab then landed on a mode radio. About 1.5 ms later the control's `fit()` switched to the select (`data-fit="select"`, `data-row="own"`) and hid the radios, and Chromium dropped focus to the body. `fit()` runs in the frame after the header's ResizeObserver reports, a deferral #2383 made on purpose to avoid the "ResizeObserver loop" error. So for a frame after a place change, or after the narrow Preview toggle shows a header that measured 0 while hidden, the control can still show radios that do not fit. #2995 put Contrast into the plugin's preview header, which now settles on the select at 1280 and at 380 on the plugin. That gives the stale radios a frame in which to be wrong.

**The fix.** `pmShiftTab` waits for that fit before its walk. It makes a ResizeObserver on the preview header, which is notified after the control's own (observers are notified in the order they were created), and waits one frame after that, by which point the fit the control asked for has run. A header that never reports rejects within 5 s and stops the case by name. The assertion is unchanged, and the diff is that one function.

**Proof.** The section was extracted and looped, five copies in parallel for load. Before the fix, 12 of 15 runs failed, with 22 failures between them, all on figma at 380. After it, 25 runs passed with no failure (7,800 checks). Three product mutations, each after a `wip:` commit: with the radios and the select taken out of the Tab order, all 88 live cases fail, each on "Shift+Tab from Inspect lands in it false". With the control held on Depth & motion as well as Palettes, exactly the eight `on depth` cases fail. With it held everywhere, every case stops by name at choosing a mode.

**Filed, not fixed here (#3013):** when the fit switches between the radios and the select under focus, the focused control is hidden and focus falls to the body. A keyboard user on a mode radio who narrows the plugin window loses their place. It is the same mechanism the probe met, reached by a resize, and where focus should go instead is the owner's call.

## (2026-10-25) — The brand-invariant stroke steps are pinned in px, and Slider's nested inputs and range text key are asserted (#2965, #2967)

Both issues came from the review of the Slider (#2792), and both are `test.ts` arms, so they share a PR.

### #2965 — the stroke steps, in pixels

No gate asserted a `border-width` step's emitted px. `BORDER_PX` in `test.ts` only feeds the executor stub, and #2792 pinned the Slider's three track rungs only, so `none` (0px) and `hairline` (1px, the border floor) moved freely. A new arm holds a literal table against every composed `out/<brand>.tokens.json` (not the base or the overlays), following each alias to its `$value` and holding any per-mode override to the same number:

- `border-width` none / hairline / thick / heavy / x-heavy → 0 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 6px.
- `focus.ring` width / offset / offset-field → 2 / 2 / 0px (the 2px SC 2.4.13 floor and the two fixed offsets).

`tree.ts` writes each as a constant, so none is a brand setting. The table is typed from the decisions, never read off `tree.ts` (`docs/34` shape 1). The arm asserts it walked at least five brands and a leaf count of brands × 8, so an empty walk cannot pass.

**What is deliberately not pinned.** The issue's broader "other brand-invariant steps" (it names `tree.ts`'s grid steps) does not hold as stated: one corpus brand already ships its own breakpoints and grid, so those are brand settings, and a pin would be wrong. `container.min` (320px) is already pinned by #2971. The `radius` steps vary by brand; its `round` and `capsule` sentinels are pinned by existing arms.

### #2967 — Slider's nested inputs and the range text key

1. **The inputs' size.** Only `lint-component-surface`'s plan digest held the nested TextFields at `medium` (Q550), and `--accept` clears a digest. A semantic arm now walks every Slider member's plan for nests of `text-field` and asserts each is `size: medium`, with a floor of 45 inputs (15 single members × 1 + 15 range members × 2).
2. **The keying.** `texts.defaultValue → figmaName: 'range text'` is forced: a texts key must be a declared prop, and the two readouts need different placeholders. A Code Connect projection would read it as "the range readout maps to `defaultValue`". Slider's `notes.projection` (the maintainer-only list for how a fact is projected, #2411) now says the keying is mechanical, not a prop mapping. A `test.ts` arm asserts the keying is still `range text` and that exactly one `notes.projection` entry carries the literal phrases (`range text`, `defaultValue`, `not a prop mapping`, `Code Connect`). The issue offered `notes` or `codeOnly`. `codeOnly` was tried first and dropped: it moves Slider's projected plan digest (`lint-component-surface`), which would make a one-sentence warning a `minor` surface change. `notes` reaches only `schema/component-maintainer.json`.

### Mutations, each failing by name

Wip commit before each. Each diff was checked non-empty first. The first M1 attempt matched nothing (a string anchor against the file's indentation), its green was discarded, and it was redone as a JSON edit (`docs/34` shape 19). Files were restored from `HEAD` with `git show`, and the regenerated tree with `git stash -u` + drop.

- **M1.** In one brand's composed tree, `border-width.hairline` → `{…core.dimension.2}` → `#2965 brand-invariant steps: … (5 brands, 40 leaves; 1 off — harbor.tokens.json border-width.hairline 2px (want 1px …))`. It was the only failure.
- **M2.** A `wireframe` mode override of 2px on one brand's `focus.ring.offset-field` → `#2965 …: aurora.tokens.json focus.ring.offset-field in wireframe 2px (want 0px …)`. The CLI byte-identity check also fired, as expected for a hand-edited artifact.
- **M3, the issue's shape.** `tree.ts` `border-width.none` written at 1px, regenerated → `#2965 … 5 off`. It was the only failure, which confirms the issue's measurement that nothing else held it.
- **M4.** `inputNest` `size: 'medium'` → `'small'` → `#2967 Q550 slider inputs: … (45 inputs; 45 not medium — type=single, size=medium, state=rest: small; …)`.

## (2026-10-25) — lint-hit-target measures the underline Tag's box and × slot (#2947)

`lint-hit-target.ts` reads each def as authored, which for Tag is the pill: `INTERACTIVE['tag']` and `INNER_TARGETS['tag.dismiss']` both measure `size.{size}.height`, 36 / 44 / 56px. Under `tagStyle: underline`, `applyTagStyle` builds a tag that hugs its content (owner Q585 A, #2945), 20 / 26 / 32px, whose × slot is as wide as its glyph and drops `innerTarget`. The 24px minimum moved to code, as Link's did. No gate saw that box.

**The arm.** It materializes the tag with `applyTagStyle(def, 'underline')` and `applySpacingDensity` at all three densities (WCAG 2.5.8 has no compact exception), plans every select and dismissible member at rest, and walks each plan to the height it draws (`drawnHeight`: a bound height, else the hug of the children plus block padding and floor, a text node at its style's line box). The × slot is measured at the smaller of its bound width and its drawn height. Each size, body and slot apart, must clear 24px as drawn or be named in `UNDERLINE_CODE_SIDE`: the body at small (20px), the slot at small and medium (16 and 20px). It checks both ways: an unnamed sub-24px size fails, and a named size that now clears 24px is stale. A named size needs one `codeOnly` entry carrying the arm's literal phrases (the "hit-target expansion, Underline" entry, which states both).

**Independence.** EXPECTED is two literals: the 24px floor and the owner's named sizes. ACTUAL is a second derivation of the hug height from the plan's bound tokens, sharing nothing with `applyTagStyle` but the plan it reads. It measures 20 / 26 / 32px today, the decision's numbers, which `test.ts` also pins by its own walk. A self-check drives `drawnHeight` on three hand-built plans, and asserts the phrase check fails on an empty `codeOnly`. The arm also fails if `applyTagStyle` returns the pill unchanged, or if the tag's size axis stops being small, medium and large.

**Mutations, each failing by name** (wip commit before each, diff checked non-empty, file restored from `HEAD` with `git show`):
- **M1.** `size.medium.underline.inset` → `space.0` (medium hugs at 20px) → `tag/underline/medium box is 20px at comfortable select unselected, below the 24px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8), and UNDERLINE_CODE_SIDE.tag does not name medium`. `origin/main`'s gate on the same tree: exit 0.
- **M2.** `size.small.underline.inset` → `space.100` (small grows to 24px) → `tag/underline/small box is 24px … UNDERLINE_CODE_SIDE.tag still names small — a stale code-side entry`. `origin/main`'s gate: exit 0.
- **M3.** The `codeOnly` entry "The hit-target expansion, Underline" deleted → `tag: no codeOnly entry states the underline box's code-side 24px hit area at small` and the same for the × slot at small and medium. `origin/main`'s gate: exit 0.
- **M4.** `drawnHeight` neutralized to return 44 → two `drawnHeight self-check, …` lines and a stale-entry line.

**Not checked.** The code-side expansion itself: no emitted token can carry it, so, as for Link and the flush buttons, the gate requires the def to state it rather than measuring it.

## (2026-10-25) — lint-naming fails a second copy of a skill rule it reads (#2948)

`lint-naming.ts` parses four lists out of §6 of `skills/prism3-build-component/SKILL.md` (the root roles, the `_` prefixed set, the slot items, the exempt controls) and checks each against its own literal. Each regex took the **first** match, so when two PRs edit the skill in hunks git merges without a conflict, the second copy of a rule survives and nothing reads it. The delta review on #2761 measured this: a second "prefixed set" sentence naming `_accordion-marker` left the gate clean.

**The fix.** The gate now counts each anchor over the whole skill, not only §6, and fails when one appears more than once (`states the DECIDED_PRIVATE rule 2 times … expected once`). It also asserts the `## 6.` and `## 7.` headings each appear once, because the §6 slice is taken between the first of each: a duplicated §6 would put a whole copy out of reach. The expected count is the literal 1, never read off the skill.

**The self-check.** For each rule, the gate takes the real skill's own sentence, changes the first quoted name (`` `x` `` → `` `x-copy` ``), appends it, and asserts the copy count fails by that rule's name. It does the same with a second §6 heading. The expected count in the self-check is the real count plus one, so the self-check does not fire on top of a real duplicate and blur which arm reported.

**Mutations, each failing by name** (wip commit before each; diff non-empty and the duplicate counted present before running):
- **M1, the issue's case.** A second "The prefixed set is `_accordion-marker`." further down §6 → `skill: … states the DECIDED_PRIVATE rule 2 times (anchor The prefixed set is ([^.]*)\.), expected once`. `origin/main`'s gate on the same tree stays green (the converse: without the new arm, nothing fires).
- **M2.** The root row stated twice, the second adding `label` (the 12-against-11 disagreement the issue found) → `states the ROOT_ROLES rule 2 times`. `origin/main`'s gate: green.
- **M3.** A second `## 6.` heading carrying a copy of the slot-items sentence → `has 2 §6 headings, expected 1` and `states the SLOT_ITEMS rule 2 times`. `origin/main`'s gate: green.
- **M4, the self-check.** The copy-count arm neutralized (`n > 99`) → four `self-check: a second copy of the <RULE> rule … does not fail the copy count` lines, one per rule.

**Limit, said so.** The count is by anchor sentence. A second copy reworded so the anchor no longer matches is not counted; that is the same blind spot the original parse has, and review is its guard.

## (2026-10-25) — CI runs the Chromium install script's test, and its stall cases hold where PID 1 does not reap (#2981)

`install-chromium.sh` runs in all four browser jobs, and its test, `test-install-chromium.sh`, ran nowhere: a change to the script was gated by whoever remembered to run the test. The `engine` job now runs it as "The Chromium install script retries cleanly after a stall (#2981)". It needs no browser and no network, only a stand-in install and lock in `$TMPDIR`.

**The stall cases.** Under a subreaper that never reaps (`prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER)` and no `wait`), five cases failed on `main`: the four the issue names plus `stall/ok`. The stopped lock holder stayed a zombie, and the stand-in's `kill -0` still answered for it, so attempt 2 failed on the lock. A zombie holds no lock, because the kernel releases a process's locks when it exits, so apt would not wait on it either. The stand-in now reads a zombie (`ps` state `Z`) as not holding the lock. All cases pass under the non-reaping subreaper and without it. The container this was written in reaps orphans, so the plain run passed before the fix too. The subreaper is what reproduces the issue's containers.

**`lint-doc-gates`.** Its prose arm saw only `npm run` and `npx tsx` steps, so a step that runs a script was a gate no checklist had to list. The freshness battery was already listed, but nothing required it. A step whose line starts `sh` or `bash` and names a `.sh` script now counts, keyed by the script's path. The named install and aggregator steps are skipped, as they are in the runner arm. Arm 5 now accepts `bash` as an invocation. Dropping the new line from each of the three gate regions fails the gate, naming that region.

**Mutation.** With the clear before a retry dropped from `install-chromium.sh`, the test fails `stall/ok`, `stall/no lock error`, `stall/two attempts`, `stall/cleared` and `stall/repaired`. The PR's CI shows the same mutant failing the new step by name, and the revert after it passing.

## (2026-10-24) — A part one component nests shares its page (#2989)

Owner decision Q656 A set one rule for where a component's parts are built. A part only one component nests goes on that component's page. The Subcomponents section keeps only parts several components nest. Two earlier one-off calls move under the rule. Breadcrumb Item and its separator join the Breadcrumbs page, which Breadcrumbs leads (this replaces #2666 call 15 A). Code cell joins the Code input page (this replaces Q329 A).

### The check

`assertPartPages` in `apps/plugin/src/file-taxonomy.ts` fails by name on any def that exactly one def nests and that sits on a different page from it. It reads "nested by" off the defs' own `nests` at any depth (anatomy parts and default slot items) through `consumersOf`, and never off the taxonomy (`docs/34`). Three defs have exactly one consumer and still keep their own pages, because they are components a designer places directly. Badge is nested by Tab.Item (S8 O1), Button.Group by Dialog (#2661, Q363), and Text field by Slider (#2669, merged while this PR was open; the check caught it on the first run after the merge). All three are listed in `STANDALONE_NESTED`, each with its decision, and a listed def that no longer qualifies is reported as stale.

### The move on an existing file

`apps/plugin/src/page-moves.ts` is shared by Update and Set up file. It finds Prism3 sets still on a page an earlier taxonomy gave them (`FORMER_PAGES`) and moves each one to the page the taxonomy names now. A set's labels, backdrop and live usage panel move with it. The nodes are moved, never rebuilt, so ids, placed instances and hand edits are kept (#2956). The set lands clear of the destination page's existing nodes, and the Update's re-spacing tidies the row. A set on any other page, or one a designer built under the same name, stays where it is. **No page is deleted** (a standing owner rule): a page left empty is reported as "now empty, safe to delete". The Update lists the moves in its dry run, puts them in its preview hash and saves its named version first. Set up file saves its own version ("set up the file") before it moves anything.

### Not changed

The component executor did not change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at 38: `lint-executor-revision.ts` reads the executor's files and none of them moved. A step's old usage panel that lands on the Breadcrumbs page is replaced by the Breadcrumbs panel the next time that panel is drawn (#2927's family rule). Until then the two panels sit side by side.

## (2026-10-24) — prism3-rebind: lessons from a brand rebuild and its audit, and a new audit-and-repair section

**What changed.** `skills/prism3-rebind` takes the scrubbed lessons from a brand rebuild lane (35 items), each placed in the section it belongs to and merged with what was there:

- **§2** gains steps 6–13: keys for components the file has never instanced, per-component publish state, geometry computed before building, grid columns per breakpoint, screens on the page in scope, slot sizing, structure paired with screenshots, and the steps that need the owner's hands.
- **§3** gains two subsections: *Swapping in place* (measure first, hide the original, a per-node check within 2px before removal, override copying by child index, GRID ordering by position) and *Spacing* (the default majority-and-snap rule, both spacer forms, overlay refit, off-scale owner values applied raw and flagged).
- **§4** gains ten trap rows: hanging library imports, imported objects that vanish, timed-out calls that keep running, stacked image fills, FILL children in hugging slots, `resetOverrides()` renaming slots, same-value property sets, Sticky, screenshots of a second file, and node screenshots with no background.
- **§5**: contrast over photography is measured on a 2–8px ring and quoted at the brightest 5%; `textDecoration` before choosing a text layer.
- **§7**: rogue-item provenance, normalized detach checks, explicit modes, "update available" as NOT VERIFIABLE, classification by collection key (§8 step 5 now says where a hidden collection's key comes from), FPO and state exemptions, instance padding.

## (2026-10-24) — Badge: a size axis and a third emphasis, surface, for the status label (#2983)

Owner decision Q644 A makes the commerce-card label on a product image a `badge` type=status. The first draft added a separate `surface: default | media` axis. The owner turned that down on 2026-10-24. The white-container style is an `emphasis` level, its name must not say "media", and these labels are effectively small badges, so badge gets a `size` axis. This PR rebuilds to that direction (wireframe v2, a private Artifact linked on #2983). The owner answered A on every open call on 2026-10-24: Q660 A / Q2983.4 A (the name `surface`), Q2983.5 A (the small metrics) and Q2983.6 A (neutral + bold stays the page's inverse).

- **`size: small | medium`,** authoring. `medium` is today's label and leads the axis, so every existing member keeps its place. Small (owner decision Q2983.5 A, 2026-10-24) is `type.caption.md.strong`, the corpus's only 11px rung, at `space.025` × `space.100`, about 19px tall. The count and dot stay medium.
- **`emphasis: subtle | bold | surface`** (the name is owner decision Q660 A / Q2983.4 A, 2026-10-24). Surface is `background.primary` under `text.<tone>` (neutral: `text.primary`) with no edge. It shares the subtle and bold box, so `emphasis` stays runtime. Lowest text-on-fill across the corpus is 4.94:1. On a card the fill barely separates (1.22:1 at most), so there it reads as tone-colored text.
- **Neutral + bold is not near-black in every mode.** It is the inverse surface: near-black on light and hc-light pages, near-white on dark and hc-dark, with text at 12.33:1 or more. Owner decision Q2983.6 A (2026-10-24) keeps it, rather than adding a tone. `test.ts` holds today's behavior per mode with literal luminance bands.
- **Figma:** 20 → 40 members. The paint grammar is unchanged (`{tone}.{type}.{emphasis}.{slot}`); the padding and type keys gain the size (`{type}.{size}.pad-*`, `{size}.type`).
- **Trap:** nb-redesign ships its bold caption under a different role, so a hard `caption.md.strong` failed #1601 by name. `typeWeight: { group: 'caption', intent: 'bold' }` repoints it per brand, as Code input does for titles.
- **Trap:** the #910 presence sweep holds each def at its SECOND size, which for badge is `small`, where the count and dot do not exist. The sweep now reads a size-sparse coordinate at a size the set has.

## (2026-10-24) — Theme › Color: link rows gate every pick on the surfaces they sit on, in every mode (#2990)

Built on the recommended answers to Q2990.1–5 while they were open; the owner then chose A on all five and accepted the copy as drafted. Wireframe linked on #2990.

### What was already there
The issue's premise was that no Theme UI exposes link roles. It does. Color › Interactive › Links has had `Text link` and `Text link · inverse` rows since the S5 redesign, and the plugin mounts the same page. Pinning one already moves hover, visited and pressed by their derived step distance (`setLinkFamilyOverride`), and the engine already clamps a sub-floor link pin to the nearest clearing step (#1510). So the owner's inverse-link change was possible through Apply Theme already. What was missing: the row measured one mode and one ground; a sub-floor step could still be clicked, and the engine then landed a different step (865 times in the sweep); and nothing said the states follow.

### What changed
- The step picker takes extra surfaces (`against.also`) and rates each step at its worst across them. It also takes `blockBelow`, which marks a sub-floor step `aria-disabled` so it can't be picked. The step stays focusable, so arrow keys still move over it.
- The two text-link rows pass the family's primary and secondary surfaces and block sub-floor steps. Each now has a four-mode contrast strip and a state line. Icon-link rows are unchanged (wireframe scope): their pickers still let a sub-floor step through to the engine's clamp. An earlier push blocked them too, because they share the `link-family` write; independent review caught it, and test:chrome now asserts the icon picker blocks nothing.

### The surfaces question, held
Derived links measure about 4.1:1 on `background.tertiary` in four of five corpus brands, because the link walk gates on the floor ground only. Whether links sit on the third tier is the owner's call (Q2990.4), so it is filed as #2991. L-07 and the UI use primary and secondary only.

### Gate
`test.ts` L-07 recomputes contrast from resolved hexes against surfaces named literally. It doesn't read `ratio` or `against`, or any studio code. Mutation: removing the #1510 link clamp in `modes.ts` fails L-07 by name.

## (2026-10-24) — Slider: one control for a value or a range in three sizes, its thumb a nested component (#2669)

Built to the proposal on #2669 as the owner approved it on 2026-10-16, every numbered call at its recommendation (A):
one `Slider`, range from a two-value `value`; `type` [single, range] × five states = 10 members; one size; the value
as header text; a 2px rail and a 4px fill; a 24px filled thumb with a 2px page-colored ring; paired inputs behind an
`inputs` boolean; thumbs that stop at each other; the names and wording as listed. Cites the knowledge base's
`components/slider.md` (category Form), read for this build.

### Owner decision Q550 (2026-10-22): the look rebuilt

After owner QA (Q536), a wireframe of options and A on every item: (a) one track thickness in `field.border.rest`, the
selected part and the thumb in neutral ink (`interactive.neutral.border.*`), because with one thickness only color
tells the selected part apart and the primary fill is 1.15:1 against the track where ink is 4.23:1; (b) the thumb sits on
the track, no page-colored ring; (c) a 0px header gap, the 44px control row kept; (d) labeled milestones in place of the
end labels, off by default, no ticks; (e) a `size` axis, small / medium / large, thumb 18 / 24 / 30px and track 2 / 4 /
6px, medium first, which needed a new `border-width.x-heavy` (6px) and a CONTRACT minor (14.10.0, after Progress took 14.8.0 and #2973 took 14.9.0); (f) a halo in
`border.primary`, 4px at hover and 8px pressed, the shared focus ring, and disabled dimming the thumb and the selected
part together (`disabled.icon`). Slider 10 → 30 members, Slider.Thumb 5 → 15. Calls 3 A, 5 A and 6 A of the first
approval are superseded; the rest stand.

How it is built: the thumb's frame is exactly the disc's size, so the track segments never move with state; the halo is
two boxes around the disc, larger than the frame and unclipped, so it overflows like a box-shadow. The inner band is a
4px `border` stroke at hover and pressed, the outer band a `fill` padded `space.050` and painted only pressed. The bar
is square-ended so it meets the ink disc with no visible gap. The header, the control row and the milestones sit in a
`field` column at `space.0`; the inputs and the message keep `space.100` below it. Figma draws three milestones (the
ends and one between, evenly spaced); code draws one per value in `milestones`.

`lint-rung-names` learned a stroke family: a size-keyed `border-width.*` step has no `sm/md/lg` rung, so it is ranked on
a literal ladder (none, hairline, thick, heavy, x-heavy) the way a `space.*` step is ranked by its number, and the
Slider is admitted by name as a ladder its default cannot place on a tier.

### Why the thumb is its own component, `_slider-thumb`

Call 2 A puts the state on the maximum thumb while the minimum thumb of a range stays at rest. `paintOf` is
part-blind: two boxes in one def that take the same paint slot bind the same variable at a coordinate, so two thumbs
in the Slider could never differ. So the thumb is a nested component, Slider.Thumb, and each of the Slider's thumbs
nests it `nest-fixed` at rest with `variantWhen` moving it: the maximum thumb at hover, pressed, focus-visible and
disabled, the minimum thumb at disabled only. The focus ring lives inside the Thumb, so it lands on the thumb and never
on the track. It takes the `_` prefix by the Q349 rule (used only inside its parent).

The first build's Thumb had no variant, only its states, and the schema was widened to admit an empty `variantAxes`.
With Q550's size axis the Thumb has a variant again, so that carve-out was removed rather than kept unused.

### Why the track is flow, not offsets

Figma auto layout has no per-child main-axis offset, and `positionWhen` is three positions only. A first try put two
rail segments in the control row, which the validator refuses (two parts claiming one slot bind one variable, and it
cannot know that is wanted). What shipped: the control row (the `size.md.min-height` target) holds one `track` box,
2px tall, painted as the rail; inside it, growing unpainted spacers and the selected bar (4px, `indicator`) sit around
fixed thumbs, all taller than the track and overflowing it, which an auto-layout frame allows with clipping off. Single
is [bar, thumb, spaceEnd], range [spaceStart, thumbMin, bar, thumb, spaceEnd]. The thumbs land at the middle, and near
a third and two thirds; the placeholder text says "50" and "30 – 70" to match. Code draws one rail and positions the
bar and thumbs by value (`codeOnly`).

### Paint and contrast (the first build, before Q550)

Rail `color.field.border.rest` (slot `fill`), bar `color.interactive.primary.fill.rest` (slot `indicator`), value text
`color.text.primary` (slot `label`), end labels `color.text.secondary` (slot `body`); none moves with the state. Thumb:
an inner disc (slot `indicator`) in the primary fill at rest, hover and pressed, inside an outer disc in
`color.background.primary` (slot `fill`) padded `space.025`: that padding is the 2px ring. Disabled:
`color.disabled.fill` on rail, bar and inner disc, `color.disabled.text` on text; the ring keeps the page color.

The ring was first a 2px stroke in `color.background.primary`. The Q346 arm of `lint-paint` (#2749), which landed on
`main` while this PR was open, refuses it: a stroke must bind a variable scoped `STROKE_COLOR`, and the page color is a
surface role. No border role is the page color, so the ring became structure: the same 24px thumb and 20px disc, no
stroke. Measured in all 20 cells (five brands × four modes), lowest: rail 3.51, bar and thumb at rest 4.05, hover
5.80, pressed 7.95, focus ring 4.56, value text 15.98, end labels 5.00. Each is a literal floor in `test.ts`, measured
on the role the plan binds. The fill against the rail stays under 3:1 everywhere, as the proposal said; the thickness
and the thumbs carry it.

### Gates

- `lint-hit-target`: the Slider is INTERACTIVE `single` on its control row (`size.md.min-height`, 44px). The Thumb is
  a CODE_SIDE_TARGET, which needed two small widenings: a `single` entry for a def with no size axis (refused if the
  def grows one), and `centered on the (glyph|thumb)` in the rule's third phrase. The Slider's two thumbs and three
  nested TextFields are INNER_TARGETS; a single-size host's nested targets are measured at the size they nest.
- `NO_SIZE_AXIS` (both), `EXPECT_ANATOMY` / `EXPECT_PAINTERS`, `MUST_COVER` / `MUST_CLEAR_STROKE` (the thumb's ring),
  `UNREACHED_EXPLAINED` (the thumb's ring nomination), `GATED_EXPECTED` (the Slider's type-gated parts), the reaction
  map (10 / 4 / 6 and 5 / 2 / 3), the canvas-furniture count (41) and shared pages (11), the round-trip reaction
  read-back, the studio catalog and used-by index, and the artifact count, 200 → 202.

### Traps for whoever comes next

- A texts key must be a declared prop, and a set holds one default per text property, so the two readouts are two
  properties keyed by the props they read (`value` → "value text", `defaultValue` → "range text").
- The nested inputs show TextField's own label ("Label") and its message in Figma: a host can override a nested
  instance's text and swap properties, not a boolean or a property two levels down. Filed as #2781.
- Q550 contrast, measured with an independent script over the committed emission (20 cells, lowest): track 3.51,
  selected part and thumb at rest 15.98, selected part against the track 4.23, thumb at hover 13.20 and pressed 9.76,
  thumb at hover inside its halo 3.28, focus ring 4.56, readout 15.98, milestones 5.00, halo against the page 1.38.
  The pressed thumb inside its 8px halo is 2.52 in the high-contrast modes, held for the owner on the PR.
- No error members: Q354 puts an invalid control on `status`, and the approved 10 members have none, because a
  slider's own value is always in range. Held for the owner.
- Owner QA item 1 (2026-10-19): the readout sat outside the 320 box because the nested label is built at its own 320 and
  hugged, filling the header. The label now grows, so the readout sits at the header's end; `test.ts` measures it. The
  state mapping moved from `atState` to `variantWhen` with main's fold (#2427). Item 2 (state styling) was answered by Q550 f.
- No gate pinned a `border-width` step's pixel value, so a regenerated 5px `x-heavy` passed everything. `test.ts` now
  pins the three Slider track rungs at 2 / 4 / 6px in every corpus brand (Q550 e). The other steps (`none`,
  `hairline`) are still unpinned.

## (2026-10-24) — Banner gets a minimum width, bound to a new `container.min` (#2971)

Owner QA 2026-10-23 on #2971: Banner needs a minimum width, the same one for contained and full width, because a narrow host wrapped its body to a sliver. The owner decided Q2971.1–3 A on 2026-10-23, after a 1:1 wireframe on the issue.

- **The mechanism was already there.** `minWidthKey` (a token-bound Figma `minWidth`, code `min-inline-size`) has been in the schema, `anatomy-figma.ts` and the plugin shim since 2026-09-28, but no def used it once Tag moved to `minWidthRatio`. Banner's root now binds it, so all 8 members carry the floor. No schema change.
- **No token held the value,** so this adds one: `container.min`, 320px, beside `container.max` and `container.narrow`. It is in the DTCG tree and in the layout variable collection as `container/min`, for every brand. It is fixed, not a lever, because 320 is the WCAG 1.4.10 reflow width and does not vary by brand. `CONTRACT_VERSION` 14.9.0 (MINOR, one added path).
- **320 over 360 (Q2971.1 A).** The narrowest real host is a 320px phone. A contained banner sits in its 288px column (320 less `grid.sm.margin` on each side), and a full-width banner spans 320. At 360 every full-width banner runs 40px past that viewport.
- **Clamped in code (Q2971.2 A).** Both values are wider than the 288 column. So the code note is `min-inline-size: min(var(--container-min), 100%)`, not a plain floor that would scroll the page sideways there. Figma keeps the plain floor, since it has no `min()`.
- **Not done here:** the studio's container preview (`apps/studio/src/preview/sections/containers.ts`) lists `max` and `narrow` only. Showing `min` is a UI change, left out of this PR and filed as #2985.

## (2026-10-24) — test:chrome lands the pointer's pending move before it measures, so a tile's tooltip no longer flickers out of the font check (#2980)

`test:chrome` failed twice on CI (#2972, #2978) at "figma light|dark 380 / Figma menu open": the Agent tile's tooltip (`agent-toggle-tip`) "drew nothing" in the embedded-font check. #2962 had already moved the pointer off the tile before that state, so the move itself was not missing. It was late. Chromium holds a mouse move until the next frame and only then updates hover, while the key presses that open and walk the Figma menu are handled at once and draw no frame of their own. So the probe could still read the tile as hovered, see its tooltip drawn and mark it for the font read. A frame then landed the move, the tooltip dropped to `display: none`, and the CDP read found no fonts for it. Whether it failed was a race between the runner's frame clock and the test's round trips, which is why it passed locally.

Two changes, both in `apps/studio/test-chrome.mjs`. `measure()` waits two animation frames before it probes, so any pending pointer move lands first and the hover the probe reads is the one the font read sees, in every state. The Figma-menu state also waits until the Agent tile no longer matches `:hover` after the move, and asserts that by name, so a move that never lands fails there rather than in the font check. Nothing is excluded: a tooltip that is really drawn (the "Agent on" state hovers the tile on purpose) is still measured and held to the embedded face, and every visible label still is.

Mutation: a visible chrome label set to a device font fails "every chrome text element draws in the embedded Inter" by name.

## (2026-10-23) — Update clears a min/max size the plan no longer sets (#2976)

Owner QA found underline tags still 36/44/56px tall and 56px+ wide after a Pill → Underline switch and an in-place
Update; a fresh Build hugged (#2946). Two leftovers, one cause: the in-place executor only ever *removed* what a plan
stopped setting as a binding (`setBoundVariable(field, null)`), and the host keeps the number a removed binding wrote;
and a literal floor (Pill's `minWidth`, 1.5 × the rung height) was written only "when the plan carries it", so nothing
ever took it away.

### What changed
- `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts`: right after the stray-binding unbind, in place and outside an instance, each of
  `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight` that the node's plan neither binds nor writes literally is set to
  `null`. General, not tag-specific. Inside `own()`, so a hand-kept node is untouched; a parent's own writes onto its
  child (`maxWidth`, the reserved lines' `minHeight`) run after the child's build and still stand. `EXECUTOR_REVISION`
  37 → 38.
- `apps/plugin/component-shim.ts`: unbinding one of those four now leaves the bound value as a literal, as the host
  does. Without it the shim deleted the binding and the value together, so the Underline → Pill half of the defect
  (the label row's bound `minHeight` left behind) could not be seen offline.
- `apps/plugin/test-update-apply.ts` § min/max: builds Tag under each style, updates in place to the other, and
  compares all four sizes (value and bound-or-not) on every node of every member to a fresh build of the target style.

### Verification
Mutation (the clearing loop iterating nothing): both `#2976 min/max pill → underline` and `#2976 min/max underline → pill`
fail by name, 45 members off each.

### Trap
The paste executor builds fresh only, so it has no twin of this clear; if it ever gains an in-place path it owes one.
What the host does to `minHeight` when a bound `height` is removed was not re-measured here; the shim models only the
four min/max fields.

## (2026-10-23) — CI caches Chromium's system packages, so a slow mirror no longer fails the browser install (#2951)

The browser came from the cache since #2323, but `--with-deps` still downloaded about 26 MB of system packages (mostly CJK and Thai fonts) from Ubuntu's mirror on every run. On 2026-10-22 the mirror was slow, not stalled: `fonts-wqy-zenhei` took about 3 minutes, so no apt timeout from #2348 fired, and all three 240 s attempts ran out. The logs also show each attempt kept the packages the one before had finished downloading ("Need to get 14.8 MB/25.9 MB", then 11.8 MB). The archive directory already worked as a cache within a job. It just did not survive the job.

So `install-chromium.sh` points apt's archive directory at `~/.cache/prism3-apt`, which the runner user owns, and each of the four browser jobs caches the `.deb` files there with `actions/cache`. The key is the runner image (`ImageOS` + `ImageVersion`) plus the Playwright version, which together decide which packages `--with-deps` needs. `restore-keys` lets a new image start from the previous image's packages and save its own. On a hit, apt reads the index from the mirror and installs from disk. The script logs how many `.deb` files it found, so a run's log shows whether the cache hit.

Unchanged on purpose: the 240 s bound, the three attempts, the 15-minute step limit and the named failure. A cache miss runs the install exactly as before, so it is never a skip (#2323's rule). apt downloads as root here (`APT::Sandbox::User "root"`), because `_apt` cannot reach a directory under the runner's home. That is acceptable on a disposable runner.

**Gap.** A cold cache on a slow mirror can still fail: a new Playwright version with no earlier entry, or a cache that has been evicted. Once any job succeeds, every later run restores its packages. `test-install-chromium.sh` gains `config/archives` and `config/no archive`. Its four `stall/…` cases fail in a container whose PID 1 does not reap orphans, on `main` too: the stopped stand-in stays a zombie that still answers `kill -0`. GitHub's runners do reap orphans.

  text style, whose face and `title/…/strong` weight stay. Letter-spacing matches the studio: its 20px page titles use
  `--p3-ls-tightest` (−4%) and its 16px section titles `--p3-ls-tighter` (−3%), both from the default theme's
  `LETTER_SPACINGS`. So the panel title takes −4% and section titles −3%.
- **Do and Don't (item 2).** The block's own `Top padding` toggle is turned on: 16px over the section's 8px gap. Using
  the template's toggle means files whose `_Doc-block` already exists get the space without a template rebuild.
- **Related (item 3).** Each list is one Field block: the label, then one line per name as an `UNORDERED` text list.
  A name whose component has a set in the file is a `NODE` hyperlink to it, underlined; the set is found the way the
  executor finds it, by its exact name, and a name with none (or with two) stays plain. Replaces entries are plain.
- **Links stay current.** The plan holds def ids, not node ids, so a link target can change with no plan change. The
  panel records the sets it linked (`docPanelLinks`) and `docPanelDue` compares them, so a related set built later
  makes the panel due on the next update, which then links it.
- `PANEL_FORMAT` goes to 3, so every drawn panel redraws once with the new layout.

Built on `main` while #2969 (legacy panel prints) is still open; both touch `doc-panel.ts`, so the second to merge
takes a merge.

## (2026-10-23) — Usage panels drawn before phase 1 are replaced, not kept as "(edited)" (#2968)

**The bug.** On the owner's copy of the library file, the first Update after panels phase 1 (#2932) kept 42 older
panels aside as "… usage (edited)", each below a fresh one, though nobody had touched them. On Buttons, the members'
old panels stayed in place.

**The cause.** #2932 moved the panel's print to `printView`, which leaves out a specimen's content and every size, so a
rebuilt set no longer reads as a hand edit. A print recorded before that change was still compared whole. That print
covered the specimens, so after any rebuild it could never match, and every such panel read as edited.

**The fix.** A hash cannot say what moved, so an old print that no longer matches is set aside. The panel is read by
its text instead (`legacyUnedited` in `doc-panel.ts`). It is unedited when every text it shows outside its specimens
is one Prism3 writes there (`writtenTexts`): the def's plan in today's wording, the wording before #2932 (each
part's own anatomy line and caption, the def's own Do and Don't items and their count line), a chip row's "+n more",
the family line, a further specimen's "Shown on …" caption, a marker's number, or a text the file's `_Doc-block`
template holds. An unedited panel is replaced in place, and a family member's old panel is removed. A line a
designer typed or rewrote still keeps the panel aside.

**Checked against the old code.** In a scratch run (not committed), the pre-#2932 `drawDocPanel` drew a panel for each
of the 50 defs that build a set. Each panel got an old-form print, then its specimens were rebuilt. Every one reads
unedited. Before the old per-part captions were added, 7 did not (Checkbox.Group, Radio.Group, Tabs, List,
Segmented control, Breadcrumbs, Code input). The same run took the Buttons page through `previewUpdate` and
`applyUpdate`: the lead's panel is drawn, and 4 old panels are replaced, 0 kept.

**The test** (`test-doc-panel.ts`, `legacy/…`): Tag's old-print panel under a rebuilt set is replaced (1 replaced, 0
kept, 1 panel). With a line rewritten it is kept as "Tag usage (edited)". On Buttons, the lead's old panel and the
three members' are replaced (4 replaced, 0 kept, one "Button usage" panel). With Button.Neutral's lede rewritten,
3 are replaced and 1 is kept as "Button.Neutral usage (edited)". `family/kept` now edits its synthetic group panel's
text, because an old print alone no longer reads as an edit. The shim's `_Doc-block` variants now hold their layers,
as a file's do.

**What the text check cannot see.** On an old-print panel, a changed fill, a hidden layer or a deleted one is not
read, because the old print cannot tell those from the rebuild. A def whose docs changed since its panel was drawn
reads as edited, which is the safe direction. Panels drawn since #2932 carry the new print and are unaffected.

## (2026-10-23) — Pagination: numbered, compact and simple, on a new page cell in a native items slot (#2665)

Built to the proposal and wireframe on #2665, which the owner approved with every numbered call at its recommendation
(A). Cites the knowledge base's `components/pagination.md` (category Navigation), read for this build. Two defs, both on
a new `↳ Pagination` page under Components:

- **Pagination** (`pagination`), 12 members: `type` [numbered, compact, simple] × `style` [border, underline] × `size`
  [medium, small, large], the style on numbered only. As first built (superseded by Q414 A, below), numbered
  was a nested IconButton.Neutral (ghost, square, a left chevron through #2645's swap override), a native `items` slot of
  seven Pagination.Item instances showing page 5 of 10 (1 … 4 [5] 6 … 10), and a second IconButton.Neutral with a right
  chevron, 4px apart. compact put "Page 5 of 10" between the two buttons. simple was two nested Button.Neutral, text,
  "Previous" and "Next" with their chevrons, at opposite ends of a row built at 428px. Previous and next are
  `nest-exposed` on `state`, so a designer sets them to disabled at an end.
- **Pagination.Item** (`pagination-item`, unprefixed per Q394 A, the `items` slot's preferred item), 27 members: `type` [page, ellipsis] ×
  `selection` × `style` × `size` × state [rest, hover, pressed, focus-visible], the current page at rest and
  focus-visible only (call 7) in each style, and the ellipsis at rest only. A cell on IconButton's height rung with
  Tag's `minWidthKey` floor (as wide as it is tall, hugging past two digits). The current page has a border or an
  underline (below), its number in the emphasis weight with Tab's bold reserve holding the width; another page takes
  the neutral overlay wash.

### After QA: the current page is marked, not filled (Q381, 1 A and 2 A)

The owner's QA on the first build: a primary-filled current page competes with primary buttons, and it is a "you are
here" marker, not a selection. So it has no fill. It has a border in `color.border.tertiary`, and its number is
semibold (the emphasis weight). Pagination has a per-instance `style: border | underline`, passed only to the current
page. Underline is a 2px bar (`border-width.thick`) under the number in the same role. An empty 2px frame above the
number balances it, so the number stays on its neighbors' line. The border is `border-width.hairline`, drawn inside the
cell.

The role is the neutral border role with the least contrast that still clears 3:1 against `background.primary`, in
every committed brand × mode. Measured: `border.primary` is 1.38 to 4.63, `border.secondary` 2.00 to 10.14 (it fails in
every light and dark mode), and `border.tertiary` 4.21 to 19.60. No neutral role sits near 3:1, so the gray is darker
than "just meets" suggests; a role nearer 3:1 would be a new token. `test.ts` measures the bound role at 3:1 in all 20
cells, and asserts that no lighter rung of that typed ladder clears it.

### After the first host build: the ellipsis read "1"

The first plugin build reported two misses: `label` and its reserve "COLLAPSED". Pagination.Item gave the ellipsis its
"…" through `byVariant` on the one `label` TEXT property. A set-level TEXT property holds one default that every bound
member displays (#1567), so every member, the ellipsis included, read "1". The ellipsis now has its own text part,
`mark`, with its own TEXT property (Figma name "ellipsis", prop `mark`), and the number's box is on page members only.
A new corpus arm in `test.ts` holds the host's rule for every def: no TEXT property is behind two different captions
across its set.

### Owner decisions Q394 A, Q395 A and Q404 A (2026-10-17)

- **Q394 A** (on #2783): a slot item is not a part "used only inside its parent" in Q349's sense. So the item is
  `pagination-item`, unprefixed, and the `items` slot names it as its preferred item with preferred-only
  (`allowPreferredValuesOnly`), the Breadcrumbs shape. The #1392 paste harness now provisions a slot's preferred
  component as a keyed set in the file, its members from that def's own projection, as the real build makes it first.
- **Q395 A:** the current page keeps `border.tertiary` at 1px, as built.
- **Q404 A** (superseding Q396): the gap marker is the existing `more-horizontal` icon (`more-horizontal-filled`, the
  glyph Breadcrumbs' overflow uses), decorative, `aria-hidden` and not interactive. The ellipsis's text part, its TEXT
  property and the `mark` prop are gone. The item's one TEXT property, `label`, is bound on page members only, behind
  the one caption "1", so the build's caption collapse cannot recur. The icon is at IconButton's glyph rungs
  (`icon.size.sm`, `md`, `lg`, the chevrons' size) in `color.icon.secondary`; both are held for the owner.

Sizes lead with medium in both (Q347, Q359), which #2752 (Q1 B) has since made every ladder's order, so both join the
canonical size set, `lint-rung-names` DEFAULT_FIRST and the #2752 default-member rule's sized list.

### The one engine change: a state can be excluded from some members

The approved 21 members need a sparse grid on the STATE axis, and `excludeCoordinates` refused any axis but a variant
axis ("the state and slot axes have their own presence mechanisms"). The state axis has none for "this state on these
members only": `states` is per def. So the state became one more dimension of the grid, in four places that each read
it independently: the validator (`figmaPropertyErrors`, values from `stateAxis`, the first-member and code-default
checks over the full grid), the arithmetic count (`figmaVariantCount`'s inclusion–exclusion now multiplies the state
into each box instead of after it, which is the old number whenever no entry names the state), the projector
(`figmaAnatomySet` checks the exclusion inside the state loop; `figmaAnatomyPlan`'s refusal sees the state), and the
lint walkers' own one-line matchers (`lint-paint`, `lint-paint-placement`, `tools/binding-audit`). The walkers keep
their own matchers on purpose (they are the independent side of their gates); they now pass the state only when they
plan one, the projector's own reading of an unsupplied axis. The plugin needed nothing: its reaction planner already
drops a reaction whose destination member is absent, so the current page gets no hover or press reaction, and
`planSetLayout` places members by name. No executor file moved for this.

### Traps met

- **A `_` building block cannot be a slot's `preferred` component.** Figma leaves an underscore component out of a
  published library, and the projection refuses it by name. The first build carried `minChildren: 1` only; the owner's
  Q394 A resolved it by dropping the prefix on slot items.
- **Overrides inside a native slot were written twice.** The executor's slot pass (`toSlots`) runs `build` over the new
  SLOT and visits its items a second time, so a per-instance override inside a slot was applied, and its miss reported,
  twice. The corpus re-apply in `test-update-apply.ts` caught it (the update's misses outnumbered the build's).
  Pagination is the first def with overrides inside a slot; the fix is #2660's own (`instanceValuesWritten`). This
  branch carried a port of it until #2660 merged; since that merge the executor matches main and this PR moves no
  executor code.
- **Test worlds lacked the override glyphs.** `test-update-apply.ts`'s `world()` and `test-canvas-furniture.ts`'s
  rollout built no `icon/chevron-*` components, so the update refused a plan swapping to them; both now provision every
  glyph a plan's overrides name.
- **The studio catalog missed override swaps as nests.** `component-catalog.ts` walked `nestTarget` and `swapTarget`
  only, while the plugin's dependency pre-build (`planTargets`) has read override swaps since #2645. No def overrode a
  swap before, so it never showed; the catalog now walks them too, and Pagination nests `icon`.
- **`lint-paint` arm 1 does not admit a leading `type`.** Exempting `type` as a non-family axis was tried and the
  family tripwire caught it at once: List.Item's `type=icon` binds the `color.icon` family. So the item's paint keys
  lead with `selection` (`{selection}.{type}.{slot}.{state}`), as Tab's and the segment's do.
- **The #1392 paste harness gave nested components TEXT properties only.** Pagination is the first nest-exposed host
  whose override swaps a nested glyph, so the stub now also models each such nested component's INSTANCE_SWAP
  properties from its own def, and provisions the override glyphs.
- **A text part needs a TEXT property keyed by a prop.** The compact "Page 5 of 10" is the one shipped string with no
  prop in the approved table, so `getStatusText` (the translatable status string, which the brief's §9 asks for and
  the live region reuses) carries it. Held for the owner.

### Owner decision Q414 A (2026-10-18): Pagination draws its own previous and next

#2808 (Q386, merged in #2813) made it a gate that no component requires a Neutral button family, which approved call
2 A (IconButton.Neutral and Button.Neutral for previous and next) broke. The owner chose A on Q-2796-1: previous and
next are Pagination.Item cells. `type` gains `previous` and `next`: the same square cell with `chevron-left` or
`chevron-right`, in the neutral icon ink and the neutral wash, with the page cells' states plus `disabled`, which is how
Figma draws the inactive end (calls 9 A and 12 A: `aria-disabled`, still focusable, never native disabled; named
"Previous page" and "Next page"). simple's two text controls are the same cells with the word beside the chevron,
through a new variant axis, `labeled: false | true` (a nest sets only variant values, so a Figma boolean could not turn
the word on from the row). Each word has its own TEXT property ("previous label", "next label"), one caption each
(#1567). The item grows from 27 to 87 members; Pagination keeps 12, and the #2808 arms now pass for both defs.
`labeled` is the 28th axis name in `VARIANT_AXES`, registered as a `sole` set in `lint-axis-values.ts`.

### Owner QA on the copy file and decisions Q426 A, Q427 A and Q428 A (2026-10-19)

- **The underline was as wide as the cell.** The balance frame above the number has no children, so a hug width had
  nothing to hug and the host kept a new frame's default width. The label box took that width, and the underline
  stretched to it. The balance now stretches to the number, like the underline, so only the number sets the width. A
  `test.ts` arm holds it over every underline member: the label box hugs, its childless frames stretch, and only the
  number's reserve and text size it.
- **The gap icon is in the page numbers' ink.** It is `color.icon.primary`, the plain icon role, which resolves to the
  same color as the numbers' `interactive.neutral.text.rest` in all 20 brand × mode cells. `test.ts` compares the two
  resolved colors cell by cell.
- **Q426 A:** the labeled previous and next (simple's) draw no fill. Their word and chevron change ink at hover and
  pressed, so they read as text links. The wash is now keyed on `labeled: false` through a six-segment paint template.
  The cells and their 44px targets are unchanged.
- **Q427 A:** in the border style, the current page's border is `color.border.secondary`, the neutral border rung one
  lighter than `border.tertiary`. Against `background.primary` it is 2.00 to 2.40 in light and dark, and 9.84 and up in
  high contrast. It need not clear 3:1, because the number's emphasis weight is a second cue (WCAG 1.4.11; the
  reasoning is in the def's notes). The underline is that style's only cue, so it keeps `border.tertiary` and its
  3:1 arm. The old "lightest role that clears 3:1" arm is replaced by a Q427 arm: the border is the rung directly
  lighter than the underline, the current number is in the emphasis weight and every other in the regular one, and the
  notes record the reasoning. The exception is scoped to this part.
- **Q428 A:** the chevrons and the gap icon step down one icon-size rung at every size: `icon.size.xs`, `sm` and `md`
  at small, medium and large. Cell sizes and targets are unchanged.
- **Q537 (owner QA, 2026-10-22):** in a real file the underline ran under the 4, 5 and 6 cells. Cause: the balance
  frame and the underline stretched across a label box that hugs, and the host fixes a hugging frame at its width when
  a child stretches across it, here a childless frame's 100px. Now nothing in the label box stretches: the balance is
  fixed at zero width, and the underline hugs a zero-height, clipped copy of the number. A new plugin suite,
  `test-pagination-underline.ts`, builds the set on a shim that models that host rule (`fillFreezesHug`) and measures
  the underline's edges against the number's at every size and state. The glyph parts are renamed `previousGlyph`,
  `gapGlyph` and `nextGlyph` (Q350).

### After the Code input merge: the anatomy markers read a repeat by its settings, not its place

Code input (#2428) changed `test-doc-panel.ts` to read a merged repeat (`Item ×4`) as the next N parts of that name, in
order. The panel merges repeats by their settings, not by place (Q551 A on Q4), and Pagination's pages and gaps
alternate (item1, 3, 5, 7 are pages, item2 and item6 gaps), so the marker check sent the gaps' entry to item6 and item7
and failed. The check no longer guesses a run's members. A merged entry's marker must reach a part of its name that no
earlier entry reached, one name's entries reach their parts in part order, and their counts cover those parts exactly.
Which parts merge is pinned by hand in `marks/`, for Pagination and for Code input's two runs of two.

### Held for the owner (also in the PR)

The `labeled` axis name and its false/true values; the two words' TEXT properties and their props `previousLabel`
and `nextLabel`; the 4px gap between chevron and word; the chevrons at the gap icon's glyph rung in the neutral icon
ink; and the disabled inks at an end (all Q414 A follow-through).

The name Pagination.Item (the proposal said PaginationItem; the skill's Family.Part canon decides); the `getStatusText` prop and its Figma name "status text"; the
simple member's 428px build width; the item's label inset past two digits (`space.100`); the item aliases `page-item`
and `pagination-page`; the forced-colors system color on the current page; and the gap icon's ink role (`color.icon.primary`, the
numbers' color in every brand and mode, rather than their interactive role).

## (2026-10-23) — Every lever declares VALUE or STRUCTURAL (#2959, owner Q599 A)

The owner's concern: every component setting adds coded-component complexity. The rule now lives in
`skills/prism3-build-component` (its own section before §7, and the lever-kind table header) and on the `Lever`
type, as the owner's code test (Q610 A): **structural** = the coded component needs different markup, logic or
states per option; **value** = only token values differ (CSS changes, nothing else). A structural lever is what
the shared coded component implements and tests per option, and a new one needs the owner's explicit OK in its
wireframe. Prefer brand-wide settings over per-instance props.

### What was built
- `kind: 'value' | 'structural'` on every lever in `packages/engine/levers.ts`, emitted into
  `schema/lever-manifest.json` (and so `list_levers`). Engine `minor` via the change note.
- `test.ts`: a lever with no kind fails by name (`MISSING: <key>`); `STRUCTURAL_LEVERS` pins the structural set,
  so marking a new lever structural, or downgrading one, is a second edit a reviewer sees.
- `lint-skills.ts` check 8, opt-in by `classifies: levers` in a skill's frontmatter: the skill states the rule and
  holds one table row per live lever whose kind matches the manifest. It also requires the Q610 test's wording,
  so the definition cannot drift back to "anatomy or behavior". Self-checked both ways; a wiring floor
  fails if `prism3-build-component` stops declaring it.

### Classification
By the Q610 test. Four structural: `fieldStyle`, `searchFieldStyle`, `tagStyle`, `buttonIcons`. The other 48
live levers are value, `buttonLabelWeight` (now Control label weight, #2963) included; the retired
`radiusHairline` carries `value` too, and the skill table leaves it out. `buttonTextHover` and
`outlineInteraction` are value: Button's and IconButton's `codeOnly` prescribe no branch for either, and the
`do` lines and `applyButtonLayout` / `applyOutlineInteraction` only key, rebind or drop the overlay token in the
overlay paint slot every outline and text button already has, at the same hover and pressed states.

### Trap
`tsx` does not typecheck, so the required `kind` on `Lever` alone would let an unclassified lever through at
runtime. The `test.ts` arm is the gate, not the type.
