## (2026-10-23) — Plugin: minimize to a link strip while the agent link stays on (#2949)

**STATUS: branch `claude/minimize-link-bar-2949`.** Plugin + chrome (`apps/plugin/src/main.ts`, `agent-link-ui.ts`, `messages.ts`; `apps/studio/src/chrome.css`, one glyph in `shell/dom.ts`, one null validator in `write-adapter.ts`). Owner decisions on the issue: Q1 A (a compact link bar), Q2 A (the Activity drawer's short-status words plus the command), Q3 A (state, plus the running or last command, plus its age), Q600 A (a Minimize button beside the Agent tile, only while the link is on; the strip carries Restore and Turn off; Turn off also restores).

### What changed
- **Minimize** is a bar tile in the `bar-agent` slot, after the Agent tile, hidden while the link is off. It posts `minimize-ui`; the main thread resizes and answers `ui-minimized`, the authority as for the link itself.
- **The window** (`main.ts`). The main thread now tracks the size it last set (`uiSize`; Figma has no getter). Minimize keeps that size in `beforeStrip` and resizes to `STRIP_SIZE` (480×40), under the 380×420 floor, which is ours, not Figma's (Figma takes 70×0 up). The strip is never written to `UI_SIZE_KEY`: a `resize-ui` while minimized is ignored, and a size read from storage after minimizing goes to `beforeStrip`. Restore returns to `beforeStrip`. Any switch-off through `agent-link` restores first. It refuses to minimize while the link is off.
- **The strip** (`agent-link-ui.ts`) is built once and appended to `<body>`. `html[data-strip="true"]` hides every other body child (the live region excepted), so the whole UI stays mounted and Restore returns to the same page and state. Its line is `agentStripText` (pure): the short status; while not an error, `Agent running <cmd>… <age>` from `agent-started`/`agent-finished`, else `· last: <cmd> <age> ago` from `lastCommand.finishedAt`, else `· no command yet`. Ages are `Ns`, `Nm`, `Nh`, re-drawn each second while minimized. The full status line is the strip's tooltip.

### Why 480 and not the wireframe's 360
At 360 the approved line "Agent listening · last: update-components 2m ago" lost its age to the ellipsis, the one part Q3 A asked for, so "working" and "gone quiet" looked the same. `test:chrome` checks that the longest listening line ("… update-components 59m ago") fits whole at 480×40, with every control inside the strip.

### Poll independence
The poll runs on the main thread's own `setTimeout` (`agent-link.ts`), and `setMinimized` touches only `figma.ui.resize` and `beforeStrip`. `test-agent-link.ts` `strip/*` drives the real `main.ts`: the link and its record stay on, the poll stays armed, and a command sent while minimized is claimed and run. Mutation, from a commit: `setMinimized` calling `agentLink.setOn(false)` → `strip/link`, `strip/poll`, `strip/claims` and `strip/restore-link` fail by name. Review found that a minimize that switched the link off and straight back on slipped past all of these, since on and the timer are back by the time they're read. So `strip/since-*` now check that the link's `since` holds through Minimize and Restore, and `strip/no-bounce` that no `on: false` reaches the panel or the record in between. Mutation, from a commit: `setOn(false); setOn(true)` in `setMinimized` → `strip/since-min`, `strip/since-restore` and `strip/no-bounce` fail by name.

### Three test:chrome checks that had to learn about the strip
- **D6** ("nothing outside the frame names an agent or holds a button") caught the strip, which lives on `<body>` by design. It now exempts the strip by its hook, and only the strip; the strip has its own block of checks.
- **29d's `FIT_SEEN`** counted every `.p3-tile-label`, so the hidden Minimize tile read as an unlabelled tile and the bar classified as `other` at every wide width. It now counts the labels of drawn tiles. The frame's own fit was never wrong: it measures widths, and a hidden tile measures 0.
- **"Agent on"** passed locally but failed on CI's first run (`figma * / Agent on: … agent-toggle-tip drew nothing`, all six). Showing Minimize widens the bar, the bar re-fits a frame or more later, and the hover the click left on the Agent tile was re-read mid-measurement, so its tooltip changed between being listed and having its font read. It now measures once every bar control has held the same box for four frames, with the pointer moved back onto the Agent tile. Didn't reproduce locally, so this is reasoned from the failure line.

### Not measured
The issue's 10-minute claiming measurement on a real host (window minimized, desktop app in front) hasn't been run. That's the owner's to run. Release builds behave the same: nothing here is behind `PRISM3_DEV`.

## (2026-10-23) — Components page: Search options below Field options; Search field style leaves Shape (#2952)

The follow-up #2931 deferred (owner decision Q581 A). It builds #2905 Q5 A: Search field sits in Fields, and its own Search options block goes below Field options. It also applies Q578 to Search field style: component settings live with their components, not on Shape.

- **A section holds a list of blocks.** `SECTION_BLOCKS` (`state/component-groups.ts`) maps each section to its settings blocks in draw order. Buttons has `['buttons']`, Fields has `['fields', 'search']` and Tag has `['tags']`. `SECTION_SETTINGS` (`domains/components.ts`) is keyed by block now, not by section. Each block keeps its own disclosure line (Q7 A: one line per block), and open state and `data-key` (`opts=<block>`) are per block. ## (2026-10-23) — Code input: one input drawn as a row of cells, the cells in a native slot (#2428)

Built from the owner's decisions on #2428: Q321 A (all but cell count), Q329 A (cell count is a native `items` slot of
a Code cell part, 6 by default, 4 to 8), Q330 A (four sizes plus fill width), and the as-built wireframe approved
2026-10-16. Two defs in `packages/engine/components/code-input.ts`: `code-input` (48 members) and `code-input-cell` (28).
Built on #2660's items-slot pattern (merged), with current `main` merged in.

### What the build had to decide

- **The cell has no `_`.** Q349 gives a parent-only part the `_` prefix, and Q329 makes the cell the slot's
  preferred value. #2657's slot projection refuses a `_` id as a preferred value, because Figma leaves a `_` component
  out of a published library and a consuming file's slot could not offer it. Built as `code-input-cell` (recommendation
  A), confirmed by Q394 A on #2783. The rename sweep meets the same collision for the segmented-control segment,
  `_tab-item` and `_list-item`, each a preferred slot value in #2660.
- **The characters' type.** No guaranteed type role is above 18px (the contract guarantees body, label and caption),
  and the title roles' weights differ by brand (the default `strong`, prism3 `emphasis` and `strong`, nb-redesign
  `subtle` only). Q330's 20, 24 and 40px therefore bind `type.title.sm/md/2xl` with a new `typeWeight` (a fixed bold
  intent, resolved by `resolveWeightIntent` before projection, the rule `weightIntent` uses), so #1601 holds on every
  corpus brand. Small keeps Text field's `body.md.default`.
- **The cell sizes are literals** (`builtSize`, Dialog's construction, Q303.5 A): 48, 64 and 72 sit on no size rung.
  `lint-rung-names` gained `PINNED_LADDER_DEFS` for the families Q330 pins one rung below `md` (`title`, `icon.size` for
  the caret, `radius`) and `2xl` on its rung order.
- **Reactions on a set with no pressed look.** `reactions.ts` planned While pressing only to `pressed`. The cell's def
  names `pressState: 'focus-visible'` (pressing a cell focuses the code input), carried on the plan only where declared,
  so every other plan's `planStamp` is unchanged. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` is 37, one above main's 36 (#2957 raised main to 36; this PR moves `reactions.ts` and `write-components.ts` for `pressState`).
- **Default cells per member.** Each member's six cells show its state (`variantWhen` on `state`, which replaced
  `atState` on main in #2693): a fresh insert's picture of that
  state. A placed field's cells stay the designer's (Q329's accepted trade-off). Status has no nested mechanism, so an
  error member's default cells are not in error.
- **The cell's root part is `container`.** #2763's `lint-naming` names a root for its role; `cell` was the def's own
  noun. `container` is Text field's root name for the same bordered box.
- **Generation priority (#2713's scale).** Code input is 2, a top-level component an agent places on its own; the
  cell is 9, a part never generated alone. Its `pending` admission reads `pending — not projected: …` (#2711).
- **Active is spelled `focus-visible`.** The closed state vocabulary has no `active`; Text field's names for the same
  ring and caret are used, and the rename is held for the owner.

### Traps

- The #1392 paste check builds nest-exposed defs with a stub that keys no component, so a slot's preferred value read
  as a miss. Code input is the first nest-exposed def with a slot; the check now provides each preferred id as a built,
  keyed set, as the real build does.
- **Field style (#2719's Code input half, built here).** Q332 A names Code input a field and #2695's Q12 A sets its
  underline: one bottom line per cell, gaps unchanged, the 2px focus line and the 2px ring offset on the active cell,
  `border.danger` in error. The cell joins `FIELD_FRAME_PARTS` (`container`); `applyFieldStyle` now squares a per-size corner
  key (`size.{size}.radius`) rather than writing the template as a key. The field def binds no field chrome, so it and
  its gaps stay as authored. `test.ts` holds the cell's underline per state at every size (`#2719 code-input`).

### The digit's vertical position (owner QA 2026-10-16; option A on #2789; Q534 on 2026-10-22)

- **Measured cause.** The layout was already centered: the line box sits dead center in every cell, so the line height
  cancels (the leading splits evenly). What is left is the font. A centered line box puts a figure off center by
  ((descender − (ascender − figure height)) ÷ 2) × size. Inter is 0.0px at every size, by design. Playfair Display (prism3's
  title) sits 1.2 / 1.5 / 2.5px low at medium / large / xlarge with lining figures. The owner's test brand's display font
  sits high: its metrics are not in the repo.
- **The first fix (superseded below).** `verticalTrim: 'cap-height'` on the cell's character trims the box to the cap height and the baseline,
  measured 0.0px off center (±0.7 at the worst digit) in every font measured, at every size.
- **Host trap.** Figma stores vertical trim in the text style, and writing it on a styled layer detaches the style
  (#1567). So `claimDefaults` writes the plan's trim and the #1567 re-apply stands down for a trimmed node, in both
  executors. Both shims now model a style apply writing the style's own `NONE`, so a re-apply over the trim fails
  `#2428 code-input-cell` (plugin), `#2428 paste` (paste) and the round-trip's new `leadingTrim` predicate.
- **Paste chunks.** The trim adds about 130 B to every chunk's shell. After #2661's own shell growth that put Code
  input and Dialog over #1798's 37,800 B unit ceiling (Dialog had 76 B left on main). The strip pass now drops leading
  indentation as well as comments, on the same ground (no literal in the payload spans lines; the gate now also refuses
  a line ending in a backslash): about 1 KB off every shell. With the trim gone (below), `icon-button` packs into 16
  chunks.
- **Owner QA Q534 (2026-10-22): the character takes its text style.** In a brand's file the trimmed character had no
  style, so it kept the build's own font, the default brand's display serif. The character now carries its size's text
  style (`type.title.sm.strong` at medium, `type.body.md.default` at small, `type.title.md.strong` at large,
  `type.title.2xl.strong` at xlarge), which main's spec read-back (#2830) expects. A trim written on a styled layer
  detaches the style, so the Figma character is no longer trimmed: its line box is centered, and code still trims.
  The owner kept the style (Q560 A = Q-#2789.2 A, 2026-10-22), so `verticalTrim` and the executors' trim handling,
  which no def declared, are removed; both shims still model a style apply writing `NONE`.
  Held by `#2428 code-input` (plan), `#2428 paste` (paste executor), `#2428 code-input-cell` (plugin executor) and the
  round-trip's spec read-back.
- **Found and filed, not fixed here:** prism3's title font sets old-style figures by default, so several digits drop
  below the baseline (#2814).

### Main merge (2026-10-22)

- Code input's `status` [default, error] subset in `lint-axis-values.ts` is folded into main's identical entry for the
  choice controls (#2751), with its reason kept beside theirs.
- Main's #2714 register: the cell's child-only `whenToUse` takes the template, `onComplete` loses its code span, and the
  label pattern no longer writes an acronym in capitals.

### The one-input contract arm (review of #2789 on d3333d1e, S1)

- `#2428 code-input: the one-input contract` reads the field's and the cell's `codeOnly`, `accessibility`, `props` and
  `anatomy` against literals: exactly one `<input>`, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, `inputmode="numeric"` matching the

- Main's #2926 (every field's message off by default, owner decision item 1): Code input's `showMessage` defaults off,

- Main's #2938 (Link current, Breadcrumbs, Search field) and #2940: the registry lists take the union, `EXECUTOR_REVISION` is 36
  over main's 35, and the artifact count is 210.
- Main's Banner (#2786) and #2932, #2931 and #2851: the registry lists take the union, `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays 36 over

- `test-doc-panel`'s marker oracle read a merged repeat (×N) as one part, so Code input's second run of cells (entry 7,
  cell5–6) was checked against cell3. It now takes every part a ×N entry stands for; the drawing was right.
- **Owner decision Q-2789.3 A (2026-10-23):** Code input joins the studio's Fields section (`SETTING_SECTIONS`), and

## (2026-10-23) — Style guide group frames are painted by role (#2953)

Owner QA found the Style guide's group frames drawn with `fills: []`, `strokes: []` and radius 0: white on a white
canvas, so the page read as one sheet. The owner's hand-styled reference has every group filled by
`color/foreground/primary`, stroked 1px inside by `color/border/secondary`, radius 2; the standalone Effect styles guide
is unstyled there. This supersedes the transparent group of Q7 A.

- **Where it runs.** Not only in `drawGroup`: in the per-run pass over every group Prism3 drew (the one that refreshes
  titles), partial runs included. That is what paints groups drawn before the fix, which the issue asked for so no
  manual update is needed next time. `drawGroup` itself still clears the host's default white fill.
- **The rule is "bare or nothing".** A group is painted only while it has no fill AND no stroke. Any paint at all is
  read as a designer's, so the master's hand styling survives every later run. It is both roles or neither: painting
  the stroke alone when the fill role is missing would read as a designer's paint to the next run, which would then
  never add the fill. A missing role is named in the run's misses instead.
- **Radius** is set only on a corner that is still 0, so a designer's radius on a bare group is kept. Whether it should
  bind a radius token is held as an owner question on the PR (recommended: keep the literal 2, as the reference has it).
- **Adopted hand-made groups** are not `isOurGroup`, so the pass never sees them.
- **Resolver reused:** the `byTail` role match that `doc-panel.ts`, `doc-block.ts`, `cover-frame.ts` and
  `furniture-templates.ts` each define locally, copied as a local helper again rather than shared, to keep this a
  one-concern change.

Tests: `test-style-guide.ts` §42, with the role names typed as literals. Mutations: dropping the `paintGroup` call fails
"42: a first run paints all 3 group frames" (and two more); dropping the bare check fails "42: a second run leaves a
designer's fill, a designer's stroke and its own paints byte-identical"; setting the radius unconditionally fails "42: a
bare group with a designer's radius of 8 is painted, its radius kept at 8".

Not in this PR: Q596 A (Scrim and Veil in their own section after Inverse colors), filed as #2964.

## (2026-10-23) — Tag underline hugs its content (#2945, Q585 A)

Owner QA on a real library file found 18px of empty frame above a medium underline tag. #2937 had turned the pill's fixed height into a `minHeight` at the same rung. The owner chose Q585 A: under Tag style Underline the tag hugs its content, and the 24px target moves to code, as Link's does. A wireframe on #2945 measured the three sizes beside the pill and raised two follow-ups. Both were answered with A, which keeps what ships today, and built: the × slot keeps the rung height as its width (Q585.1), and the minimum width stays 1.5 × the rung height (Q585.2).

- **Heights:** 20 / 26 / 32px at small / medium / large (they were 36 / 44 / 56). That is the glyph-height label row (16 / 20 / 24, taller than every example brand's label line box) plus the inset (4 / 6 / 8). The label row keeps its glyph floor, so the label doesn't move when the check appears. The line stays inside the inset, so the 1px to 2px step never changes the height.
- **The trap behind the small diff:** `applyMinWidthRatio` multiplied the frame's `height ?? minHeight`. Dropping the floor alone would have thrown at materialization, because the ratio had nothing to multiply. A new `PartDef.minWidthBase` gives the ratio a base on a box that binds no height. The schema refuses it without `minWidthRatio` and refuses it beside a height. The × slot's height now hugs, so the schema's `innerTarget` rule (both sides bound) refuses the mark. The underline def drops it, and the target is code's.
- **Pill unchanged, proved independently:** `test.ts` pins the sha256 of the 45 pill members as `specMaterialize` builds them. It was computed on main before this change, and `lint-component-surface.ts`'s baseline didn't move.
- **Filed:** #2947. `lint-hit-target.ts` measures only the pill, so the underline's box and its code-side 24px target are not gated.

## (2026-10-23) — Update keeps a kept child's parent-written fields too (#2943)

**The bug.** On a library file, Update with `handEdits: 'keep'` listed checkbox-control's `focusRing` as a
non-conflicting hand edit, then wrote the ring's corners back to the concentric radius on the six unchecked
focus-visible members, the ones whose root the update rewrote.

**The cause.** The executor's `build` skips a kept node's own fields (`kept` guards `own()` and `claimDefaults`), but a
child's placement is written by its PARENT, after the child loop: the ring pass (`absoluteInset`) unbinds the ring's
size, resizes, places and re-corners it from the host; the pin, corner-pin, foot-pin, centered and inset-icon passes do
the same for their children, and the loop itself writes `layoutAlign`, `layoutGrow`, sizing, `maxWidth`, `minHeight`
and `opacity`. None of them asked whether the child was kept. The update's own content verify skips kept paths, so the
overwrite passed verify silently. Members the update did not rewrite never ran the pass, which is why the checked and
indeterminate rings survived.

**The fix.** The parent records each child it paired in place under a kept path (`held`) and runs none of its
child-placing writes on it. A kept child keeps every field, its parent's writes included. Executor revision 35 → 36.

**The test** (`test-update-apply.ts`, `keep/…`): a checked focus-visible checkbox, its root given a new fill by the
plan, with four hand edits — the ring's corners unbound and 0, the mark's fill red, its gap bound to `space/0`, the
icon's width and height bound to another variable. After Update with keep, all four read byte-identical to literals
typed in the test, the root still takes the new fill, and an unedited member takes the fill and keeps its concentric
ring. Mutation: the `held` skip removed → `keep/byte-identical` fails (the ring reads 32 on every corner).

**Not covered, by design:** an unbound width or height is outside the as-built record (`member-baseline.ts`), so a
size changed by hand without a binding is never seen as a hand edit, kept or not. Raised on #2956.

## (2026-10-23) — Progress: the progress bar and ring, to the approved wireframe (#2670, every call A)

Built to the proposal on #2670, which the owner approved on 2026-10-16 with every numbered call at its
recommendation. One `Progress` (category `feedback`, aliases `progress-bar`, `progress-indicator`, `linear-progress`,
`circular-progress`; `loader` stays with Spinner), on its own `↳ Progress` page under Components. Cites the knowledge
base's `components/progress.md`, read for this build.

**12 members.** `shape` [linear, circular] × `type` [determinate, indeterminate] × `status` [active, complete, error] ×
`size` [medium, small]. Two `excludeCoordinates` rows make the sparse grid: a linear bar has one thickness (no small),
and indeterminate work, bar or ring, has no end state. The first build had a third row, no indeterminate ring (a ring
always had a value; call 2 left that to the Spinner). Owner Q545 B (2026-10-22) removed it; see below.
Each axis lists its code default first (owner Q347), so the first member is the default bar: the code `type` default is determinate.

### How the still members show an amount

Figma has no percentage width, so a member cannot say "45%". The fill and the empty rest of the track each `grow`, so
they split the track evenly: 50% at active and error, and at complete the rest is absent and the fill runs the whole
track. The indeterminate frame is a lead, the segment and the rest, a third each. The value text reads 50% (100% at
complete) to match. A literal fill width was the alternative and was discarded: it would freeze when an instance is
stretched, where the grow split keeps its proportion.

### After the first host build: every member read "50%"

The owner's QA asked for the complete example to read 100%, and the first plugin build reported the reason it did
not: one `valueText` TEXT property drove every member's value, with "100%" at complete as a per-member default
(`byVariant`). A set-level TEXT property holds one default that every member bound to it shows (#1567), so every
member read "50%" and the plugin reported the bound parts as COLLAPSED. "100%" now has its own text parts,
`valueComplete` and `ringValueComplete`, present at complete only and bound to a second TEXT property, `complete value
text`. "50%" is present at active and error only. The `value` boolean hides all four.

The second property has no code prop, because code renders both values from `valueText`. So the engine now accepts a
`figmaOnly` TEXT property, held to the Figma-only boolean's rules (#2344): it must not be a declared prop, and it must
state its `figmaName`. The alternative, a code prop for the complete text that code does not need, is held for the
owner on the PR. `test.ts` now types each member's caption and checks that no TEXT property in the set is behind two.

### The ring: two glyphs on one square, because a stroke may not carry the track (Q346)

The Spinner draws its track as a layer of its own glyph at 20% of its own ink. Progress's ring track is a different
role (`color.background.tertiary`, call 5), so it cannot be a layer of the arc's glyph: one glyph takes one ink. The
first build drew the track as the ring box's inside stroke. Main then landed Q346's gate (a stroke binds only a
`STROKE_COLOR`-scoped role), and measured, no border role clears 3:1 against the fills (best case 1.01:1), so a
stroke could keep neither rule. The ring is now two component-owned glyphs on one square: the track, a full annulus in
the flow (`progress-ring-{size}`, ink `fill`), and the arc over it (`progress-arc-{size}`, or the full annulus again at
complete). Two small engine additions carry it, with no executor change: a `vector` may name its paint slot
(`paintSlot`, read as the text branch reads it), and may be drawn centered over its parent's in-flow child
(`stackCentered`, projected as the overlay's existing `absoluteCenter`). The band's outer edge is the artboard's edge
and its width is band px × 24 / ring px (2 units small, 2.4 medium). `lint-glyph-geometry.ts` gained a `RING_GLYPH`
arm that measures this against numbers typed in the gate, including that the arc is lifted over the track and the
track is not.

### The stop dot is a glyph because two boxes cannot share a paint slot

The first draft made the stop dot a box painting `indicator`, beside the fill box that also paints `indicator`. The
schema refuses that (#933: `paintOf` resolves a slot once). The dot became a component-owned disc glyph
(`progress-stop`), which takes `{status}.icon`, the same role as the fill in every status.

### The end state is a nested FieldMessage

Complete nests FieldMessage at `success` and error at `error`, so the glyph, ink and caption are FieldMessage's own:
an error on a progress bar looks like an error under a field (owner Q352/Q354). The cost, recorded as an owner item:
the error glyph is FieldMessage's triangle, where the proposal text named `error-circle`. The ring members carry the
message too (call 4 says never color alone), which the proposal's circular anatomy did not list.

### Motion tokens: a sweep pair beside the spin (CONTRACT 14.8.0)

`motion.duration.sweep` (1600ms) and `motion.duration-reduced.sweep` (2600ms), outside the tempo-scaled ramp exactly
as the spin is, plus the primitive `motion.duration-ms.1600`: three guaranteed adds, MINOR, accepted with
`token-contract.ts --accept`. `LOOP_ROLES` in `theme.ts` names both loop periods; the studio's duration table leaves
both out of its steps. Showing the sweep beside the spin in the studio needs new copy, filed as its own issue.

### Gates the def joined, and two it widened

The usual lists (hit target excluded, rung names, axis values, standalone floor, paint placement, paint provenance,
glyph geometry, taxonomy, canvas furniture). Two needed more than an entry:

- `lint-rung-names.ts`: the ring's medium default is 40px, `icon.size.xl`, two rungs above `md`. The proposal set it
  and the owner approved it, so it is a new admission, `RING_OFFSET_UP_TWO_DEFS`, checked both directions.
- `emit-analysis-reports.ts` threw on a glyph name templated inside a word (`progress-arc-{size}`); it now expands the
  template before deciding the glyph's source.

The furniture rollout test builds with the shim's `scaleConstrained` on (Progress is the first set to draw inline
glyphs; the host scales them on resize) and declares FieldMessage's `message` text property for the stub, which the
#2645 override needs.

### The default `type` and the linear footprint (owner QA, #2791)

The approved set leads with the determinate bar, so Figma inserts `type=determinate`; code used to treat a bar with no
`value` as indeterminate, so the two defaults disagreed and the first build recorded a named exception in the #2752
arm. The exception is gone. Code now has a `type` prop, `determinate` by default, and `value` is a plain number
(omitted, the bar rests at `min`); an indeterminate bar is chosen with `type`, not by leaving the value out. The
`shape=circular` + indeterminate refusal moves onto `type`. This is the recommendation put to the owner as a question
on the PR.

The two linear types measured different heights at the same size because the header held the label alone when
indeterminate, and the label and value together (baseline-aligned, the value on a taller line) when determinate. The
header now centers its row and carries a token-bound floor, `icon.size.md`, which the value line fits under, so both
types measure the same. Two named arms in `test.ts` hold both.

### Owner QA, 2026-10-22 (Q535, Q544, Q545)

- **Baseline header (Q535.1 A).** The header aligns the label and the value on their baseline instead of centering
  them. Its floor still holds the two linear types at one height.
- **The small ring's band, 2px → 3px (Q544 A).** The band is drawn in the glyph's outline (3 units on the 24-unit
  artboard), so it binds no variable. No token is 3px: `border-width` runs 0 / 1 / 2 / 4. The code note's `viewBox`
  stroke width is 3 at small, matching the outline. `lint-glyph-geometry.ts` measures it at 3px.
- **An indeterminate ring (Q545 B).** `shape=circular, type=indeterminate` at both sizes, active only, with no value:
  a still frame of the turning arc, a third of the circle from twelve o'clock (the Spinner's arc length), over the
  pale track. Its glyph is `progress-arc-indeterminate-{size}`, picked by templating the arc's glyph on `type`. The
  code note turns the arc with `transform: rotate` on `--motion-duration-sweep`, linear, and slows it to
  `--motion-duration-reduced-sweep` under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The docs say when to use the ring and when the
  Spinner: a ring for a named task that ends in complete or error, the Spinner for a short wait inside a control.
- **Glyph names (Q350).** `stop`, `ringTrack`, `arc` and `arcFull` are now `dotGlyph`, `ringGlyph`, `arcGlyph` and
  `fullRingGlyph`, which `lint-naming.ts` asks for. These are Figma layer names.

### Trap

Gate every part on the shape it belongs to, even when its parent is gated. `#910`'s presence test reads a single-axis
gate at a pinned coordinate for the second size, which for Progress is a ring: a `rest` or `stop` gated only on
`status` or `type` read as absent there and failed as a dead branch.

## (2026-10-23) — Plugin: every command that changes the file saves a version first, with a title that tells runs apart (#2828, Q442 A)

Update used to save "Before Prism3 updated <every set name>", so a broad Update filled the title and every one read the same in the history panel. Build, Style guide and Apply theme saved nothing.

### What changed
- `apps/plugin/src/version-title.ts` is the one builder and the only caller of `saveVersionHistoryAsync`. Titles: `Saved before Prism3 updated 47 sets` / `updated Dialog` (one set: its display name) / `added Pagination` / `added 6 sets` / `drew style guides` / `applied the theme`. The description is `Engine <ENGINE_VERSION>.` plus the set list (more than one set), `42 tables.`, or `Variables and styles.`. `versionTitle` in `update-apply.ts` is gone.
- Each command saves once, before its first write, and a host that refuses leaves the file untouched. Update: unchanged position. Build: `saveBeforeBuild` in `buildComponents`, after the dependency walk can be read and before anything is built; the count includes the missing sets the def nests. Style guide: `StyleGuideRun.beforeWrite`, called once after the plan is laid. Apply theme: `runApplyTheme`'s `beforeWrite`, inside the guarded write, so a pre-flight refusal saves none.

### Calls made inside the decision, for the owner to confirm
- A run whose only work is the page order reads `updated the page order`; sets plus a reorder add `Page order.` to the description.
- A one-set Build or Update shows no set list (the title names the set). A Build adds a set list whenever it adds more than one.
- Style guide saves only when the plan has at least one table; a run with no table to draw saves nothing.
- After merging main: an Update that also redraws the About frame (#2858) or the library cover (#2859) adds `About frame.` / `Cover.` to the description, not the title. An Update whose only work is either saves no version (Q498 B), so neither is ever a title of its own. `settle`'s re-spacing save (#2876) goes through the builder too.
- The Update verdict line still reads `Saved a version first: "<title>".`, which now repeats "Saved". Left as is; the line's wording is a separate copy call.

### How it is held
`test-version-title.ts` writes the titles out by hand per case, drives Apply theme and Build through the shims (one save, file empty at the save, refused leaves it empty, a pre-flight conflict saves none), and scans `src/` by AST: any use of `saveVersionHistoryAsync` outside `version-title.ts` fails `bypass/no second caller`, and each command's call into the builder is asserted by name. Update's order is asserted in `test-update-apply.ts` (`version/before first write`) and Style guide's in section 41 of `test-style-guide.ts`.

## (2026-10-23) — Usage panels, phase 1: one panel per family, markers on their parts, no stacked panels (#2927, #2916)

The first phase the owner asked for after deciding Q551 A on 1–10 (the wireframe on #2927): the P0 bug, the anatomy markers, and one panel per taxonomy page. Examples instead of chips, related links, the file-wide switch and drawn Do/Don't pairs are later PRs (checklist on #2927).

- **The stacked panels (P0).** A panel's "unedited" test was the style guide's whole-subtree fingerprint, which reads the specimen: the documented set's member, its layers, its main component, and every size it pushes up to the panel. A rebuilt or updated set changed all of that with no one touching the panel, so the next draw read the panel as hand-edited, kept it aside renamed "(edited)" and drew a fresh one: two panels stacked. The print is now taken through a view that leaves out a specimen's content, every width and height and every instance's main component (a rebuilt Badge or Tag did the same to the markers and chips). Text, fills, visibility and structure still count. A print in the old form is still compared the old way, so panels drawn before this are not all kept aside on the next update. **Not confirmed on the review copy**: the mechanism reproduces in the shim; that it is what Progress hit is inferred (Progress was the draft rebuilt most often).
- **Markers (#2916).** Three causes, all fixed: parts were found by layer name anywhere (now by the def's part path, step by step, so a slot child or a part inside a nested instance is reached and a same-named layer inside another part's nested component is not taken); positions summed relative x/y and centered the marker on the part's corner (now read from `absoluteBoundingBox`, the host's laid-out box); the root and any part not in the default member had no layer to mark (now a bracket for the root, a boolean turned on for a hidden part, and one more specimen per member for the rest, numbered across them).
- **Geometry.** Leaders go to the nearer of the top and bottom gutters at the part's middle; brackets go on the left, innermost nearest. A marker that would touch another moves one tier out, and the stage's padding grows to hold every tier. "Crosses no other layer" from the wireframe is not implemented: a leader may cross layers between the gutter and its part.
- **Families.** `lead` is data on the taxonomy leaf; `assertCoverage` fails by name on a multi-def page with none. The panel is drawn only from the lead; the dry run counts it due while a member still carries its own panel; only the lead's set reaches past a panel when Update spaces sets (`PageSet.lead`).
- **Gates (`test-doc-panel.ts`).** The host now lays nodes out itself (`absoluteBoundingBox` from its own auto-layout model) and builds every fake set's members from the engine's plans, so the marker oracle (each marker frame and its leader overlap the part's box, the Badge sits in its stage's gutter, off the specimen) is independent of the placement code. Ten mutations, each failing by name: summed offsets, the whole-subtree print, family panels not replaced, no merge, no reveal, no extra specimens, no gutter growth, a non-lead drawing, no bracket, every set reaching.

## (2026-10-23) — Build-component skill: the conventions the owner decided on 2026-10-15

`skills/prism3-build-component/SKILL.md` now states the component conventions the owner decided on the audit
umbrella #2706 and around it. It also fixes the eight skill-drift items the audit listed (S1–S8). Skill only:
no def, gate or artifact moves, so there is no change note.

### What the skill now says, and where each rule came from

- **Wireframe before build** (#2382): the owner sees a rough wireframe of the component as it will be built
  before the build starts.
- **Field order** (S8): summary before description, and the corpus's order for the rest. The Button and
  Icon button factories' order is named as the one to avoid (#2712).
- **Four `notes` buckets** (S4): `projection` joins contested, unverified and evolution.
- **Root names** (S1): "named for its role, never `root` or the component's id", picked from §6's closed
  list; a new role needs an owner decision (Q365).
- **Nesting:** every host nests FieldLabel `nest-exposed` with emphasis and weight exposed; fields default to
  regular, groups to bold (Q348). `variantWhen` is documented, host states included (main folded `atState` into it).
- **Borders** (Q346): a border never binds an icon or text role, and every disabled edge binds
  `color.disabled.border`. This is the same text #2753 adds.
- **Errors** (Q354): main's §5 bullet (#2755), plus one sentence: radio's group-only validation is the one
  stated reason a family differs, and a new def that departs states its own.
- **Selection weight** (S3): Tab and the Segmented control's segment set the selected label in the emphasis
  weight and hold its width with a reserve driven through `also`. That is the one exception to the
  constant-weight idiom.
- **Props for consumer-set states** (Q351): a Row restates `disabled` and `readOnly`. Only a part never placed
  alone (FieldLabel) takes the state without a prop.
- **Lowercase property names** (Q345, S5): main's §6 paragraph, plus one sentence: a property rename rides
  `COMPONENT_RENAMES`.
- **The naming table** (Q350) and the **`_` prefix** (Q349, Q355, Q394): main's §6 copy is the only one;
  this PR adds only that Radio row stays unprefixed.
- **Repeating children** go in a native `items` slot, never a boolean per child (#2660, Q307).
- **The rarer `figmaProperties` fields** (S7) get a table.
- **Prototype reactions** (Q344): Rest carries hover and press, Hover carries press, and the touch-prototype
  reason is given.
- **Pointers to the open conventions:** binding-key spelling (#2710), the "not projected" wording (#2711)
  and sibling test kinds (#2764, the remainder of #2715).

### Decisions and traps for whoever re-verifies this

- **One copy of each rule.** The PRs this one waited on (#2753, #2754, #2755, #2756, #2758, #2765, #2768,

  PR's copies of the Q354 bullet, the §6 naming table, the `_` prefix, slot items and lowercase names were

- **Q321, cited in the brief for items slots, does not exist** on any issue, PR or file. The record is Q307 A

## (2026-10-23) — Components page: a family's settings collapse behind a line under its sets (#2844, Q439 A)

The owner chose option A on #2844 with one change: the disclosure goes below the family's set checkboxes, not above them. #2838 had opened the Button options in the left rail at all times; they took too much room.

- **Where they sit.** In the family's list item: the row, then its sets when open, then one disclosure line ("Button options"), then the settings block. The line is outside the family's drawer, so the chevron still opens the sets and the line opens the settings; the two are independent. Opening the sets never opens the settings.
- **Closed on open.** The block stays mounted and `hidden` while the line is closed, so `aria-controls` always names a real element and the controls keep their subscriptions and their state.
- **The wireframe's three smaller calls, as built.** The line shows on every row that has settings, not only the focused one (`settingsOf` no longer asks which family the preview shows). Opening it also focuses its family, so the preview shows what the settings change; closing it leaves the focus alone. The open state is session state (`optsOpen` in `state/components-page.ts`), like open families: it outlasts a visit to another page and a redraw at the tier flip. Reused: the fold's chevron and its rotate-on-expanded rule, the page state's open-set pattern and the list's key-based focus restore (`data-key`), so a pressed line keeps its focus across the redraw it causes.
- **A trap for whoever re-verifies.** Focusing another family no longer takes the Button options away, as #2815's step 1 arm asserted: the settings are the family's, not the preview's. That arm is replaced by the #2844 arm. Tests that read the Button options now open the line first (`openButtonOptions` in `test-chrome.mjs`, `gotoComponents` in `test-smoke.mjs`).
- **Gate.** `test:chrome`'s #2844 arm, both hosts at 1280 and 380: closed on arrival, the line below the sets and the block below the line measured off the render, aria-expanded and aria-controls, focus kept on the line, Enter, Space and Tab, the line shown with another family in focus, the open state kept across a page visit, and the focus restores kept from #2815. Mutations are listed in the arm's header.

## (2026-10-23) — Banner: a persistent in-flow message in four tones, contained or full width (#2579, Q327)

Built from the proposal on #2579, approved as recommended (Q327), and the KB brief `components/banner.md`. 8 members,
`tone` [info, success, warning, danger] × `width` [contained, full], no size or state axis. The container is the
tone's subtle surface with a 1px edge in the tone's **border** role (Q346: an edge never binds an icon or text role;
`color.border.{tone}` exists in every example brand, so no owner question was needed). Title and body in
`color.text.primary`; the glyph in `color.icon.{tone}`. The body is a native slot. One nested text Button action
(small; Button.Neutral instead when the file has it, never required: Q386, Q398 resolved by Q419 A; one action only
per owner QA Q533.1) and a flush FlushIconButton.Neutral dismiss (owner QA 2026-10-19: flush, not round) with the close
glyph fixed and no swap (Q386, #2808), both off by default.

### Decisions the diff does not show

- **Glyph per tone follows FieldMessage**, not the proposal's tone-ordered list: danger takes the exclamation in a
  triangle, warning the exclamation in a circle. A danger banner and an errored field should show one mark. Held for
  the owner on the PR.
- **`width`, not a new `placement` axis** (Q327.3 A). It shares `full` with Button's `auto | full`, so Button's set
  becomes `canonical` and Banner's is declared `overlapping` in `lint-axis-values`, argued there. `tone` is a `subset`
  of `icon`'s canonical set.
- **Full width is a page-top bar** (owner QA Q533.4: the two widths looked the same). Built on the recommended
  answer, held for the owner on the PR: full is built at 960 where contained is 480, square, and edged top and bottom
  only, through the per-side stroke binding (`strokeEdges`, #2695) with the sides on `border-width.none`. That is the
  proposal's own top-and-bottom edge, which #2788 was filed for. `builtSize` now admits a width-only map on a row root
  (heights still need a column), so Banner's row root takes it; refusal and admission are tested by name.
- **The title-to-body gap is fixed at 4px**, outside `densitySpacing`: one step down at compact is 2px, under the
  owner's 4px gap floor. The test's spacing table caught it before the def did.
- **The title is padded down 4px** (`space.050`) to center its first line on the 24px glyph, the accordion's
  construction. The pad sits on a `titleBox`, which the `title` toggle hides with it, so a body-only banner has no
  stray offset.
- **One text action, no Button group** (owner QA Q533.1: the owner's research found no banner with two actions). The
  `second action` toggle, the outline action and the `action-gap` token are gone, and #2787's move into the Button
  group no longer applies. The action is made from `button` with `prefersWhenBuilt: 'button-neutral'`, so no file has
  to build the Neutral family (#2808 passes); the primary ink on the tints clears 4.5:1 through #2820's surface contract.

### Gates

`lint-paint`'s provenance check reads `foreground.info-subtle` as not carrying `info` (it compares whole segments), so
the four fills are admitted by name in `PROVENANCE_EXCEPTIONS`, as Badge's subtle fills are. `test.ts`'s spacing
ordering scope learned the bare `pad` tail, so a def whose one padding is named `pad` is now required to state its
orderings. Banner's own block in `test.ts` holds the 8 member names, each member's fill, edge, corner, glyph and inks,
the nested actions and dismiss, the defaults, the lowercase Figma property names (Q345), the first member being the code
default (Q347), the built widths and per-side edges, and 36 contrast pairs as literals over 5 brands × 4 modes: text
4.5:1 (lowest 13.92), the edge against the page 3:1 (lowest 3.75), the glyph on the fill 3:1 (lowest 3.31), the neutral
and primary action labels, and the dismiss glyph at rest, hover and press and its focus ring on each fill (Q533.5).
The studio's set list shows Banner's `pad` beside `gap` (the owner's C2 A: padding and gap only) and hides
`actions-gap`, as it hides Accordion's `panel-pad-end`.

### Harness

`test-update-apply.ts`'s `corpus/in place` builds each def in a shim file holding only the components its plans nest or
swap. Banner is the first def whose nested instance takes an INSTANCE_SWAP **override** (the dismiss button's close

file" and no member read current. The harness now adds override swap targets; the executor was right.
`test-canvas-furniture.ts` builds its pages the same way and took the same fix, and its literal count of defs that
build a set moves from 39 to 40.

`lint-component-surface`, `lint-paint` and `lint-component-renames` are accepted baselines, not regen output. A main

The #2894 entry, the three row defs' headers and the PR recorded the accepted update cost (Q?6 A) as "a per-instance override on the nested control may not carry over". That was the risk while #2595 was open. Since #2595 (landed as #2691), an Update on a file built before #2894 **moves** the label and the control cell, nested control included, into the new `content` box and keeps every node's id, as it does for Accordion's `titleRow`. The independent review of #2917 measured this in the shim.

- **Pinned now.** `apps/plugin/test-update-apply.ts` gains an "option rows" section, modeled on Accordion's #2594 one. It rebuilds Radio.Row, Checkbox.Row and Switch.Row as they stood before #2894 (top-aligned, no floor, the control cell and label directly under the row, the constant 12px pad, none on Switch.Row) from today's defs. It then asserts:
  - the dry run lists both children as "moves into content, kept", with nothing removed;

## (2026-10-22) — Link: a current state for navigation, a 2px bar (#2872)

**Status:** Link def, a new box placement (`PartDef.foot`) in the schema, the projector and both executors, tests,
baselines. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no token is added or renamed. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 34 → 35.

### What changed

- **Owner decisions Q507 (2026-10-21), on the Q480 A wireframe:** a navigation row marks the page the user is on.
  - **1 C:** a 2px bar (`border-width.thick`) at the foot of the line box, in `color.icon.link.*` stepped by state.
  - **2 A:** the runtime `selection` axis on standalone links only; inline links stay out through
    `excludeCoordinates`. Link goes from 96 to 144 members.
  - **3 A:** the values are Tab's and Tag's, `unselected | selected`; the code prop is `current`, rendering
    `aria-current="page"`. `lint-axis-values.ts` adds Link to that register entry, and `test.ts`'s `#2752` BRIDGE maps
    `current` to the axis.
  - **4:** hover on a current link changes the color only. The label's type key now names `{selection}`, and a current
    link stays on the plain body style at every state, so no 1px underline joins the bar. It stays a real link in code.
- **`unselected` first, on purpose:** the plugin's Update gives existing members an added axis at the first plan's
  value (`update-plan.ts` §2), so a published Link's 96 members become `selection=unselected` in place. Selected
  first, the 48 inline members would land on an excluded coordinate and be dropped.
- **The bar is a filled box, not a stroke.** The first build drew it as the container's bottom stroke (`strokeEdges`,
  #2695's mechanism). `lint-paint.ts` arm 5 refused it: a stroke never binds an ink role (Q346), and the link icon role
  is scoped to fills only, so Figma's stroke picker would not offer it. Tab's border role is not the link color in
  every brand and mode, so swapping the role would have changed Q507.1's look. So the bar is Tab's construction, a
  filled frame, present on current members only (`presentWhen`), so the 96 existing members gain no layer.
- **`PartDef.foot`, a fourth out-of-flow placement** beside the ring's inset, the overlay's center and the corner pin:
  a box lifted out of the flow and pinned across its parent's bottom edge at its own bound height, constrained
  `STRETCH`/`MAX`, so it moves no box. Projected as `FigmaNodePlan.footPin`; both executors lift it before the focus
  ring's pass and size it after (placed before, a focus-visible member's bar ran 8px past the link); the paste executor
  splices it only for a payload that carries one (#1798). `resize` writes both dimensions, so the bound height is
  bound again after it. Read back as ABSOLUTE with `STRETCH`/`MAX`.
- **Measured:** the bar clears 3:1 on its ground in all 16 brand × mode cells at every state and on both surfaces,
  lowest 4.26:1 (aurora light, inverse surface). The hover step on a current link (hover ink against rest ink, text
  and icon, both surfaces) is 1.33:1 to 1.50:1, under 3:1, which Q507.4 accepts: the bar is the cue.
- Accepted through their gates: `component-axes.json`, `component-surface.json`, `paint-census.json`; the studio's
  component catalog regenerated; `test-reactions.ts` counts Link at [144, 72, 108].

## (2026-10-22) — Breadcrumbs, BreadcrumbItem and BreadcrumbSeparator, from the approved wireframe (#2666)

Built from the proposal on #2666, which the owner approved on 2026-10-16 with every numbered call at its
recommendation (A), then given a choice of separator by owner decision Q382 A (below). Three defs: `breadcrumbs`
(`path` full | parent × `separator` chevron | slash × `size` medium | small, 6 members), `breadcrumb-item` (`kind`
ancestor | current | overflow × `separator` × `size`, 10 members) and `_breadcrumb-separator` (`type` chevron | slash,
2 members). No state axis on either: the nested Link
and FlushIconButton.Neutral carry their own, exposed (`nest-exposed`, `expose: ['state']`), the Dialog precedent.

### What the build settled

- **The items slot follows #2649's pattern, which had not merged.** PR #2660 was still a draft, so the trail uses the
  slot machinery already on main (`contentSlot`, `slotSettings`, `preferred`, from #2417 and #2646) and declares its
  `items` prop as a plain `slot`. #2660 has since landed, so the prop now carries `anyOf: ['breadcrumb-item'],
  minItems: 2`.
- **Size order is medium first.** The proposal listed small first; Q347 A and Q359 B (#2752, decided the same day)
  make every size axis lead with the code default, medium. Both defs join the medium-first lists in `test.ts`'s #2501
  arm, `lint-rung-names.ts` DEFAULT_FIRST and `lint-axis-values.ts`, which the Q359 sweep will absorb.
- **Two new axis names, `kind` and `path` (named `layout` in the proposal, renamed by Q424 A because the Button group holds that name),** the approved proposal's own, argued in `VARIANT_AXES`' header the way
  Dialog's `placement` and `footer` were.
- **No `_` prefix on the item, held for the owner.** Q349 gives a part used only inside its parent the `_` prefix,
  and the lane's brief expected the item to take it. But the projection refuses a `_` id as a slot's preferred item
  (`slotPreferredOf`): Figma leaves `_` sets out of a published library, so a file using the library could not insert
  more steps. The item keeps a plain id until the owner rules (#2783). The same conflict waits for `_list-item` (the naming
  sweep) against List's items slot (#2660).
- **Contrast is measured from the committed emission,** not from the theme the engine computes: the arm reads each
  `out/<brand>.tokens.json`, resolves the mode aliases itself, and asserts 20 cells literally. Link ink 4.5:1 on
  `background.primary` at every state and on `background.secondary` at rest; `text.primary` on both; the back
  chevron's `icon.link.default` 3:1. The separator is decorative and held to no floor.

### After QA: a choice of separator (Q382 A)

The owner's QA on the first build asked for a choice of separator, as Prism 2 had, and decided Q382 A: a separate part,
`_breadcrumb-separator`, in two looks, `type: chevron | slash`, and one `separator` setting on Breadcrumbs for every
step, chevron by default, both in `color.icon.secondary`. The overflow item and the ``parent` path stay as built.

- **How the setting reaches each step.** `follow` passes an axis by its own name, and Q382 names the part's axis
  `type` and the trail's setting `separator`. So Breadcrumbs and BreadcrumbItem both carry a `separator` axis, the
  trail's default ancestors follow it, and the item nests the separator twice, the chevron look at `separator=chevron`
  and the slash at `separator=slash` (`presentWhen`). No engine change. The current page and the parent path have no
  separator, so neither has a slash member: the item is 10 members, the trail 6, the separator 2. `separator` is the
  thirtieth axis name, argued in `VARIANT_AXES`' header.
- **The slash glyph is not Remix's.** Remix 4.9.1 has no plain slash (`code-s-slash`, `slash-commands` and `divide`
  are the nearest). So `icons/slash-line.svg` is drawn for this project: one parallelogram on the 24px grid, a 2px
  stroke like `chevron-right`'s (1.995px measured across the stroke), and `icons/NOTICE.md` records it beside the
  textarea's grip, the set's other drawn glyph. The owner made it a permanent icon on 2026-10-22 (below).
- **Naming.** The id is the owner's, `_breadcrumb-separator`. The display name is BreadcrumbSeparator: the
  `component-names` family rule would make `Breadcrumb.Separator` force `Breadcrumb.Item` too, and the item's name
  waits on #2783. It shares the Breadcrumb Item page, first, as the Accordion indicator shares the Accordion's.
- **The icon set grew to 46,** so the icon-count pins in `test-update-apply.ts`, `test-update-components.ts` and the
  studio catalog moved by one, as they did for `menu`.
- **The studio catalog missed override swaps as nests.** The item's chevron used to be an icon instance, which hid the
  gap: the overflow's dots come from a #2645 swap override, which the catalog did not walk. Pagination (#2796) fixed
  the same line; the fix is ported as is.

### Shipped (owner QA Q531, 2026-10-22)

- **`slash` is a permanent member of the icon set,** with a standing rule: a glyph a component needs and the library
  lacks joins the icon set when the component is built. It is in `icon-set.ts`, in the Icon component set (46
  members), and in `icons/NOTICE.md`. BreadcrumbSeparator's glyph parts are instances of `icon/chevron-right` and
  `icon/slash`; `lint-glyph-geometry` refuses an inline copy by name.
- **The separator's glyph layers are `chevronGlyph` and `slashGlyph`** (Q350). The def is new, so no rename entry.
- **The overflow nest pins `surface: default`.** Toast (#2780) gave the flush icon buttons a `surface` axis; without
  the pin the overflow's nested button matched no member and built empty (`test:roundtrip`: 4 divergences).
- **Main's later rules, applied:** BreadcrumbItem and the separator sit at tier 9 and Breadcrumbs at 2 (#2713); the
  two child-only `whenToUse` lines follow #2714's template; no DRAFT in a shipped field; the Breadcrumbs summary ends
  with the items size note main gives every def with an items slot and a size.

### Traps for whoever re-verifies this

- **Two test fixtures did not model a nested glyph override.** Breadcrumbs is the first def on main with a #2645
  swap override (the overflow step's three dots). `test-update-apply.ts` and `test-canvas-furniture.ts` built a file
  holding only the plan's nest and swap targets, so the override's `icon/more-horizontal-filled` was missing and the
  set never read current. Both helpers now include override glyphs, as a real file holds the whole icon set. The
  engine's #1392 paste arm likewise now gives a swapped-into nested component its own declared properties and gives a
  slot's preferred def a keyed set.
- **A slot item's label cannot be set two levels down.** The slot's default ancestors read Link's "Link text", not the
  approved "Home" and "Category": a host's #2645 override reaches its own nested instance, not that instance's nested
  Link. The proposal named this gap; #2781 tracks it. The parent path's Link is one level down and reads "Parent page".
- **The collapsed-trail example is not on the canvas.** The proposal's §12 places one beside the set; the canvas
  furniture cannot place a configured instance yet (#2784).
- **The wireframe's CSS and the proposal's token table disagree on the separator gap.** The wireframe draws 4px either
  side at both sizes; the table says `space.050` small and `space.100` medium (DRAFT). The build follows the table.

## (2026-10-22) — Search field, with its own style lever (#2888, Q514)

**What landed.** `search-field` (SearchField), the shared field factory's third output, built on the owner's answers to
the wireframe (Q514: Q?1–Q?8 all A). 84 members (size × status × the seven field states, Q?6 A); a leading `search`
glyph shown by default (Prism 2's `leadingIcon: true`, `reference/Prism2/component-specs/search-field.json`); the clear
button as TextField's trailing glyph, starting at `close-filled` and built hidden (Q?3 A); a Figma-only `label` switch
that stands for the code prop `hideLabel` (Q?4 A, a visually hidden label kept in the accessibility tree); no submit
button (Q?5 A); the site header as a usage example in `docs.usage` (Q?8 A). Phase 2, suggestions on the generic combobox, is #2899 (Q?7 A). Its own page under Components. The code
contract ("Clear search", focus back to the input, "Search cleared" once, the browser's cancel glyph hidden, the search
landmark, `enterkeyhint="search"`) is in `codeOnly` and `accessibility`.

**The lever resolves, it does not redraw.** `searchFieldStyle` ("Search field style": Follow field style / Outline /
Underline, default Follow, the owner's copy verbatim) sits in Form right after Field style. `fieldStyleFor(defId,
input)` in `anatomy-figma.ts` picks the style a def is drawn in (the search field's own unless Follow, every other def
Field style) and `applyFieldStyle` draws it unchanged. The defaults live in that one function, so the plugin's
`materializeForBrand` and `lint-lever-sweep`'s restated composition both call it instead of each holding `?? 'outline'`.

**Follow is byte-identical, proved three ways.** `regen.ts` moved no token or Figma emission file, only the component
docs and reports a new def adds; the surface, paint-census and axes baselines moved by additions only; and the plugin's
`#2888 Follow keeps search identical to fieldStyle` builds the search field unset, set to Follow, and set explicitly to
the brand's own Field style, and compares the plans byte for byte under both Field styles. `#1812` also runs the
manifest default against the unset brand for every lever.

**The factory's three Search switches** (`leading`, `trailing`, `labelSwitch`) each spread nothing when absent; TextField
and Password field were serialized before and after and differ only by `composition` (search-field leaving `planned`
for `alternativeTo`, which the component-refs gate requires).

**Traps for whoever re-verifies.** Control shape's Boxed and Hairline corners reach fields through `FIELD_CORNER_REFS`,
keyed by def id; the search field is added there. Password field is not in that map, so it keeps `radius.sm` under
Boxed and Hairline while Text field squares; that is pre-existing and already filed as #2718, not fixed here. The Apply notice
for a search style change ("Search field style is now …") fires only when the lever moved AND the drawn edge changed; a
search field that follows a changed Field style is said once, by the field style notice.

**Review fix, and the message default.** The independent review found the clear button's target unstated: its glyph is
20px and it sits inside the input's own target, so WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception cannot apply, and a host sizing the
button to the glyph would fail. `codeOnly`, the `trailingIcon` description and the 2.5.8 line now state a hit area of at
least 24×24 CSS px around the glyph, adding no height to the field (review Q1 A); `#2912 search-field clear button` holds
it. The field's message is off by default (owner decision on #2926, item 1). #2929 moves the factory for every field;
until it lands, `search-field.ts` sets its own boolean and note, which turns into a no-op once #2929 is on main.

## (2026-10-22) — Tag style lever: Pill or Underline (#2887)

**What.** A Form lever, `tagStyle` ("Tag style", Pill / Underline, default Pill), after Field style, built to the build
plan in #2887's second wireframe with the owner's Q513 (1–8) and Q540 (Q8 A copy as revised, Q9 A inset
`space.050 / 075 / 100`, Q10 A the inset does not follow density). `applyTagStyle` runs after `applyFieldStyle` in all
three restated chains (`materializeForBrand`, `lint-lever-sweep.ts`, `specMaterialize`). Studio: a Tag style row after
Field style on the Shape page. Plugin: `tag-style-note.ts` states a style change in Apply's summary and points at Update.
**Its copy is a DRAFT for the owner.**

**How the tighter gap is built.** The wireframe's "content row held at the icon's height" lands on the label row
(`labelCheck`), not on the content row: a frame's `minHeight` includes its padding, so a floor on the padded content
row would let the label move by (glyph − line box) ÷ 2 when the check appears. The content row takes the block-end inset
and the unpadded label row takes the floor, which gives the arm's geometry exactly: label line box bottom = inset +
(glyph − line box) ÷ 2 above the frame's bottom, in all five example brands at every size.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies.** `applyMinWidthRatio` multiplied `p.height`; under Underline the container has a
`minHeight` instead, so the ratio now reads `height ?? minHeight`, and the schema admits `minWidthRatio` beside either.

**Mutations, each failing by name:** the unselected hover weight bound to `hairline` → `tag underline: hover and pressed
are 2px`; `applyTagStyle` changing the def under `pill` → `#2887 identity`; the focus-visible line thickened → `tag
underline: focus-visible keeps the line weight`; the container back to `align: center` → `#2887 underline label sits on
its inset` (an arm that first stayed green on that mutation, since its walk read NaN and a NaN comparison never
failed; fixed to ask for a measured match); `minHeight` dropped → the schema arm, `tag underline: the tag hugs above a
minHeight` and the inset arm; `applyTagStyle` dropped from the plugin chain → `#2887 underline tag reads back`
(`test-write-components.ts`) and the `tag style/…` Update arms (`test-update-apply.ts`). `test-roundtrip`'s chain
agreement cannot see that one: its null brand is on Pill, where the lever is the identity. `lint-hit-target.ts` does
not see a dropped `minHeight` either, because it measures the Pill def.

## (2026-10-22) — Option rows land on the control-height ladder (#2894, Q539)

Owner decision Q539 on #2894 (A on every question of the wireframe): Radio.Row, Checkbox.Row and Switch.Row now measure 36/44/56 at comfortable in both projections, where they measured 45/48/51 in Figma (Switch.Row 21/24) and floored only in code.

- **The floor sets the height, not the padding.** Symmetric padding cannot land on the ladder from the space ladder (the exact pads are 7.5/10/14.5), so the row binds `size.{size}.min-height` as its Figma `minHeight` (the Select and Accordion mechanism) and the pad becomes a per-size minimum (`space.075`/`100`/`150`) that only shows once a label wraps. No new token; CONTRACT unchanged.
- **Centering without breaking the first-line rule.** The row centers one inner box, `content` (Q?3 A), which keeps the control and label top-aligned: Accordion's Q276 A construction. `test.ts` #1201 now reads the alignment on the control cell's parent rather than on the root, and #1009 half-1 still catches a centered `content` by name.
- **Density.** `pad-y` joins `densitySpacing`, so compact rows compact (29/36/44; small is 1px over its 28 floor because 4 + 21 + 4 = 29).
- **Update cost accepted (Q?6 A).** Files that already hold these rows need an Update, which reparents the label and the nested control under `content`. A per-instance override on the nested control may not carry over; a dry run on a copy of a shipped file comes before any master update.

## (2026-10-22) — Field messages off by default (#2926 item 1)

The owner decided on #2926 that a field's status/helper message starts hidden. TextField, PasswordField (through
`makeTextField`), Select and Textarea flip `figmaProperties.booleans.showMessage.default` and the `showMessage` prop's
default from true to false; Counter was already false, so all five fields now agree. The `message` Figma property, the
part names and the member counts do not move, so the component-renames ledger and the token contract are untouched; the
four sets' plan digests move and are re-accepted through `lint-component-surface.ts --accept`.

### The gate

`test.ts` now carries a `#2926` family assertion that writes the five-field list out by hand and checks the registry
against it both ways, so a def that gains a `showMessage` boolean must join the list and take the default. That is
aimed at Code input (#2789) and Search (#2912), both open: each must land with the message off. For every family member
the boolean default, the prop default and the built node (`visible: false` at every member) must agree, and no prop
description or part note may still say the message is shown by default. The older `#1426` select assertions now pin
the hidden default, with the tracking mutation flipped to show the built visibility follows the boolean.

### Existing files

A boolean property's default is a set-level value. `test-update-apply.ts` builds each of the four sets as a pre-#2926
file (message on, the `true` typed as the old file's value), places three instances (untouched, turned off, turned on)
and runs Update: the dry run lists one edit, `message` true → false, and nothing else; the property keeps its id; every
member's message node is hidden; the untouched instance follows the new default while both explicit values are kept; and
a second dry run is settled. The trap: the shim records an explicit value even when it equals the old default, and
whether Figma does the same for a designer who turned the message "on" while it was already on is not measured here.

## (2026-10-22) — Button label & icon: clearer words and the brand's label sizes beside it (#2918, Q527 A)

The owner found `buttonContentSize` confusing: "Button label & icon" with "Match button size" | "One step smaller"
did not say what was being set. Q527 A ruled out an engine change. This PR changes the words and shows the sizes.

**Words (DRAFT, option A on #2918).** The label is "Medium button label & icon", the options are "Medium" and
"Small", and the description is reworded to match. The keys `match` / `smaller` are unchanged because brand inputs
persist them. The Button definition's note and the prism3-theme skill row named the old option label, so they move too.
That moves the lever manifest and the button docs emission, which is why there is a `minor` change note with no
behavior change.

**Readout.** Under the chips, a state line says what the brand's medium button gets: "Medium button label: 14px
(label/md). Icon: 20px." or "Medium button label: 12px, the small button's (label/sm). Icon: 16px." It uses lever-kit's
existing `setState(stateLine(…))`, so there is no new primitive. `contentSizeOf` (`state/button-input.ts`, no DOM) reads
the px from `theme.typography.composites`, the source the button specimen already uses, and the icon px from `ICON_SIZES`.
A brand that does not emit the rung reads `null`, and then no line is drawn.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies.** The label ladder is brand-invariant today (12 / 14 / 18). No brand input moves it,
so every corpus brand reads 14 / 12, and a corpus-only test cannot tell "computed" from "hard-coded".
`test-button-input.ts` §6 plants a theme whose label rungs are 16 / 14 and emits it. The oracle is that emission's
`type.label.<rung>.emphasis` → `core.font.size.*` alias chain. A planted 13 fails because 13 is not a font-size
primitive, and the alias dangles. Mutation: hard-coding 14 / 12 in `contentSizeOf` fails `planted 16/14 / match: the
readout says 14px; the emission's type.label.md.emphasis is 16px` and three more rows.

## (2026-10-22) — `_Doc-block` fills its block, and a file already set up is repaired in place (#2902)

**STATUS: branch `fix/doc-block-fill`.** Plugin only (`apps/plugin/src/doc-block.ts`, `apps/plugin/src/doc-panel.ts`, `apps/plugin/test-doc-panel.ts`). No artifact moves; a patch change note.

**The defect, seen in a real library file.** Set up file's `_Doc-block` came out with its stretched layers hugging: Do-Dont's `columns` at 100px inside the 512px block (the `do` / `dont` columns collapsed to ~42px, items overflowing), Field's `row` hugging, Chips' wrapping `chips` at ~986px so it never wrapped, and the `top-padding` / `bottom-padding` spacers FIXED 512. Field's `label` was resized to (120, 1), which leaves `textAutoResize` NONE: clipped at 1px.

**Diagnosis.** Each of those set `layoutAlign = 'STRETCH'` before the node was appended to its auto-layout parent. For a horizontal auto-layout frame its own primary-axis HUG then wins. The owner checked the fix by hand in the file before this PR: FILL after the append, and `HEIGHT` on the label after its width is fixed.

**The change.**
- Build: `layoutSizingHorizontal = 'FILL'` on those five layers right after each append; the label takes `textAutoResize = 'HEIGHT'` once the row is placed.
- Repair: `ensureDocBlock` used to return `present` for a set already there, so a file set up earlier kept the broken block. It now runs `repairDocBlock` on that set: those layers by name, each member's own (never inside a nested instance), brought to FILL / HEIGHT in place. Nothing is deleted or rebuilt, because usage-panel instances point at the set. This is the `stretchSwatches` pattern (#2268). It is idempotent and returns how many layers it changed. No stamp is needed: the repair reads the properties themselves.
- The repair is silent in Set up file's line, as `stretchSwatches` is. The count is in the run's `docBlock` result.

**The gate.** `test-doc-panel.ts` `template/fill` and `template/repair`. The template shim now throws on FILL outside an auto-layout parent, as the host does, so FILL set before the append fails the run naming the layer.

Mutations, each failing by name:
- `fill(chips)` dropped → `template/fill`.
- `chips` dropped from the repair's list → `template/repair`.
- The label's `HEIGHT` dropped → `template/fill`.
- FILL moved before the append → `columns: FILL outside an auto-layout parent`.

**Two usage-panel defects from the same file, fixed here after the independent review (owner decisions Q541).**
- Do and Don't items were never written: every panel reported `_Doc-block has no item text layer`. The panel looked for a layer named `text`, which is List.Item's text *property*; the layer is the part, `label`. The panel now reads the part from List.Item's def (`figmaProperties.texts.children.part`). The shim had copied the same wrong name into its fixture, so nothing caught it (docs/34). The fixture now takes the layer from List.Item's projected plan, and `panel/do-dont` checks every planned item is written (303 across the defs).
- A set's own tagged furniture no longer blocks its panel. `blockersAt` (shared by the draw and the dry run) skips nodes whose furniture tag names this set. An untagged `inverse-bg` still blocks (Q172.5), and so does another set's furniture. Prism3's backdrop is instanced as `_inverse-backdrop` and reaches only `BACKDROP_PAD` past the set, short of the panel's `PANEL_GAP`, so the `inverse-bg` the real file reported is most likely a hand-placed rectangle; that question is on the PR.
- The review's should-fix: `template/repair leaves hand edits` (a fill and vertical sizing on each repaired layer survive) and `template/repair stays out of nested instances` (decoy `row` / `columns` inside List.Item).

Mutations, each failing by name: the literal `'text'` restored → `panel/do-dont`; the own-furniture skip dropped → `overlap/own backdrop`; the skip widened to all tagged furniture → `overlap/other backdrop`; the repair clearing fills → `template/repair leaves hand edits`; the repair recursing → `template/repair stays out of nested instances`.

**Not covered.** Other layers still set `layoutAlign = 'STRETCH'` before their append: the block's texts, Do-Dont's `rule` and items, the Specimen `stage` and the Divider instance. The file showed none of them wrong, so they are left as they are. A shim can't verify how the block actually renders.

## (2026-10-22) — Toast: a short status over the page after the user's own action, on the inverse surface (#2668, every call A)

Built to the proposal and wireframe on #2668, which the owner approved with every numbered call at its recommendation
(A) on 2026-10-16. One `Toast`, category `feedback`, aliases `snackbar`, `notification`, `flag`, `flash-message`, on
its own `↳ Toast` page under Components. Cites the knowledge base's `components/toast.md` (category Feedback), read
for this build.

### What it is

- **2 members** on an `intent` axis, `neutral | success`, neutral first (the code default, so Figma's first member is
  the code default too). No size axis and no state axis: a toast is not interactive, and its nested controls carry
  their own states and prototype reactions (Q344 applies inside the nested Button and FlushIconButton.Neutral sets, with
  nothing authored here).
- **The card** is the inverse surface, `color.inverse.background.primary`, `shadow.lg` as an effect style,
  `radius.xl`, padding 8 / 16 / 8 (block, inline start, inline end), built 360 wide (`placementWidth`) and hugging its
  height. No border: the card is far above 3:1 against the page in every committed brand × mode.
- **Content:** success adds `check-circle` (the `checkCircleGlyph` part, named per Q350) on `color.inverse.icon.success` at `icon.size.sm`, 12px from the message;
  neutral has no glyph. The message is `type.body.md.default` on `color.inverse.text.primary` and wraps.
- **Controls**, 4px apart at the end edge: the action, a nested Button (text, small, `surface: inverse`), off by
  default and reading "Action" through a nested-instance override; the close, a nested FlushIconButton.Neutral (flush,
  small, `surface: inverse`), on by default, showing the close glyph through a swap override.
- **Figma properties:** `message` ("Status message"), `action` (off), `close` (on). All lowercase (Q345).
- **Code-side, in `codeOnly`:** the `Toaster` region and `toast()` API, the one shared polite live region present
  from app start, no focus steal, placement (bottom center below 768px, the bottom inline-end corner from 768px),
  one at a time with the newest replacing, the timer (6000ms default, 5000ms floor, pausing on hover, focus and a
  hidden window; no timer with an action), F6 in and Escape or Shift+F6 out, `scroll-padding-bottom`, motion.

### The close follows Q386 (owner decision Q436 (a))

The build brief named "Button / Flush icon button" for the nests and the approved proposal named IconButton.Neutral,
because FlushIconButton had no inverse surface. Q386 (#2808) forbids a component to require a Neutral button family, and
main's gate fails the IconButton.Neutral close, so the close is now FlushIconButton.Neutral, flush and small, as Dialog's
close is (Q385 A). A flush glyph on the dark card would have been 1.00:1, so FlushIconButton gains a `surface` axis
(`default | inverse`), appended last and following IconButton's: no fill, so the axis changes the glyph ink only, through
the projector's existing `color.inverse.*` rewrite. Counter and Dialog name `surface: default` on their nests. The axis
is Q436 (a). Also decided: the 8px gap between the message and the controls stays as built, Q532.1 A (the proposal
leaves it open; the wireframe draws 8px), and the action label lives on the nested Button rather than as a Toast text
property, Q367 (c) (a host text property can only drive the host's own text parts).

### Gates

- `test.ts` `#2668` arm: the member list, axes, names and aliases, no danger/warning/info anywhere; the card's width,
  sizing, fill, shadow, radius and padding as literals; the glyph only on success; the message ink; both nests' exact

  spacing order at every density; and contrast over every committed brand × mode, read from `out/<brand>.tokens.json`
  as files (light plus each mode under `$extensions.prism3.modes`), never through the def: message 4.5, glyph 3,
  action label rest/hover/pressed 4.5, close glyph rest/hover/pressed 3, focus ring 3, card against the page 3.
- Joined by hand: `lint-hit-target` `EXCLUDED`, `lint-rung-names` `NO_SIZE_AXIS`, `lint-axis-values` (a `sole`
  `intent` set: the axis returns as a variant axis after #1225 retired it from the button families), `lint-paint`
  `PROVENANCE_EXCEPTIONS` (`color.inverse.icon.success` carries `success` one segment later than the rule reads),
  `lint-paint-placement` both sets, `lint-glyph-geometry` `MUST_COVER` and `FIXED_GLYPH`, `test.ts` spacing tables and
  `GATED_EXPECTED`, the plugin taxonomy. Dialog, Badge and Spinner drop `toast` from `planned` (the component-refs arm
  fails a registered id there).
- One more committed artifact (`out/components/toast.md`), so `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` and the CI check move together.

- `apps/plugin/test-update-apply.ts` corpus arm: Toast is the first def whose nested instance carries a swap
  override (`icon/close`). The arm's fixture file held only the components a plan nests or swaps to itself, so the
  update refused the set ("component the plan swaps to is not in this file: icon/close") and both members stayed
  "to update". A real file holds the icon set; the fixture now holds each def's override swap targets too. The arm
  still re-applies every def.

  sets; its fixture file holds override swap targets for the same reason as the update corpus.
- The padding keys use the corpus spelling, `pad-y` and `pad-x`, so the studio's set list shows Toast's padding and gap

### Trap for whoever re-verifies

`lint-axis-values` reads the corpus through `git ls-files`, so an untracked new def file is invisible to it and the
gate passes over a def it never saw. `git add` the def before trusting a green run there.

### Deferred, filed

The proposal's canvas furniture (a 360 × 640 phone frame with the toast bottom center and a desktop frame with it in
the corner, like Dialog's scrim) is plugin work and is filed as its own issue rather than built here.
