## (2026-10-21) — CI runs the gates as parallel jobs, and `gates` waits for them all (Q503 A)

Owner decision Q503 A, item 1. CI was one job that ran every step in series: 34 to 50 minutes on the
last five runs on main, median 48. The chrome suite was the long pole, at a median of 1,408 s (about 23
minutes), followed by the plugin shim tests (470 s), the smoke suite (231 s) and the engine unit tests
(190 s). Every other step took under 30 s.

`ci.yml` now has five gate jobs and one aggregator:

- `engine`: the engine and doc gates. No build, no browser.
- `studio`: the web typecheck, unit tests and build, the contrast and live-CSS lints, and the smoke suite.
- `plugin`: the plugin typecheck, shim tests, both builds, the bundle lints and its three browser suites.
- `chrome`: the chrome suite, alone.
- `surfaces`: the gates that read both bundles or TokenPress. That is export parity, the two exporters,
  readback parity, and the US-English and voice gates. Those last two scan both built bundles.
- `gates`: needs all five and runs `if: always()`. Its one step, `.github/scripts/all-gates.sh`, fails
  when any job's result is not `success`, and names the job.

**The result, measured on this PR's first run (39597359183).** Wall time was 24 min 15 s, about half
the 48 min median. The jobs took: `chrome` 1,444 s, `plugin` 739 s, `engine` 315 s, `studio` 272 s,
`surfaces` 75 s, then `gates` 7 s. The chrome suite itself ran 1,402 s, so `chrome` is now the whole
critical path. Any further cut has to come from inside that suite.

**The `gates` name is kept.** The old single job had the id `gates`, so its check run was called `gates`.
The aggregator now has that id, so branch protection and any tool that reads the check named `gates` see
the aggregator. The five gate jobs report beside it under their own names.

**Each gate runs once.** The gate steps were moved with their comments and commands unchanged. Compare the
`(name, command)` pairs before and after: the same 85 gate steps appear, and the only new step is the
aggregator. Some steps now run more than once, and none of them is a check on its own: `npm ci` runs in
each job, the Chromium install runs in each of the four browser jobs, and `Build web` and `Build plugin`
each run in three jobs. A job builds the bundles it drives instead of downloading them from another job. A
build takes 2 to 3 s, which is less than an artifact upload and download. Downloading would also add a
serial build job in front of every browser job, and the downloaded bundle's mtime would come from the
download, which `assertBundleFresh` was never tested against.

**The chrome suite is not split.** `test-chrome.mjs` is one 15,000-line script with shared state at the
top level, and it has no way to select a subset of its sections. Splitting it would change the suite
itself, so it runs alone in its own job. That job is the floor for the run's wall time.

**`lint-doc-gates.ts` checks the aggregator.** Suppose a job is missing from the `needs` of `gates`. Every
existing arm stays green, because the job's steps are still in `ci.yml`. Yet that job can fail while the
merge rule reads green. `aggregatorGaps` reads the parsed tree. It fails unless `gates` needs exactly
every other job, runs `if: always()` and runs the script. We mutated the real `ci.yml` to drop `chrome`
from `needs`, to drop the `if`, and to rename the job. Each mutation failed by name. The aggregator step
is exempt from the runner arm by name, because it reads job results and asserts nothing about the tree.
`test-all-gates.sh` covers the script. A `failure`, `cancelled` or `skipped` result fails it, and so do
an empty or unreadable input. Each of three mutations to the script fails the test by name.

**Proved in CI as well.** We pushed a commit to this PR that made the exporter gate exit 1, then reverted
it. On that run (39600758928) `surfaces` failed, the other four jobs passed, and `gates` failed with "Not
every gate job succeeded: surfaces (failure)".

## (2026-10-21) — Library file cover: brand and version, kept current by Update (#2859)

Built from the approved wireframe and the owner's Q509 A, which accepted every recommendation: a new optional `BrandInput.name`, falling back to the `id` as written (Q?1); no logo, the wordmark in the brand's display face, the logo slot a follow-up (Q?2); the brand color as the ground with `text/on-brand` (Q?3); a hand-edited cover kept, with only its tagged version text refreshed (Q?4 B); drawn by Set up file and kept current by every Update (Q?5); "Prism3 0.238.0" (Q?6).

- **The cover** (`apps/plugin/src/cover-frame.ts`): a 1920 × 1080 frame named `Cover` with two texts and nothing else, tagged `prism3`/`cover` (the engine and name it was drawn for, and its fingerprint) and `prism3`/`cover-part` = `brand` | `version`. Every color and font is bound, so Apply Theme moves the cover live; a file with no theme yet gets placeholders that the first Update finding the variables binds, only while they are still the placeholder (the `bindBackdrop` rule).
- **The contrast is the engine's, asserted against it.** `test-cover-frame.ts` maps the cover's two variable tails to the engine's role paths and checks, for every example brand and mode, that `text.on-brand` is contracted against exactly `foreground.brand` at 4.5:1 or more, and measures the pair itself from the emitted hex with its own WCAG function, so the engine's `ratio` is the claim and not the measure.
- **An Update never replaces the frame.** The About frame (#2858) replaces an unedited frame in place, but the cover is the thumbnail, so replacing it would drop the thumbnail pointer. An unedited cover is refreshed in place (version, name, placeholder bindings); an edited one has only its tagged version text set. A cover-page-only run saves no named version, as Q498 B says for the About frame, and the lines name the cover. A cover-only run leaves a current About frame alone: no set changed, so its date has nothing new to say.
- **Its own fingerprint.** The style guide's `fingerprintOf` reads each text's font and size; a bound display face moves both when Apply Theme changes the family, so every theme change would read as a hand edit. `coverPrint` reads a bound font by its variable id and leaves text geometry and the version's characters out.
- **The thumbnail rule.** `setFileThumbnailNodeAsync` runs only while `getFileThumbnailNodeAsync()` is `null`. A designer's frame is named in the result and left.
- **The brand comes from the file.** Set up file and the Update read the saved brand (`persist-figma.ts`); a file with none gets no cover, it is not work, and the line says to Apply Theme first.
- **Trap:** the shim's text measures `characters.length * 6` at any size, so the long-name fit rule (240 px on one line, else 180 px wrapping inside the 120 px inset) is tested on a host written in `test-cover-frame.ts` that measures by size.

## (2026-10-21) — Skills: a consistency audit for rebuilt spec pages (#2886, Q506 A)

**What changed.** `skills/prism3-rebind/consistency-audit.js` is a read-only Figma plugin-API script an agent sends through the dev agent link's `run-code` over a set of rebuilt pages. It returns the frames it read (each classified desktop or mobile, and why), a findings list, a markdown findings table and a row for the Runs table on #2886. Four checks: (1) plain text outside any instance that repeats a control instance's label, with a heading/title allowlist; (2) the desktop → mobile text-style pair per element role is the same on every page; (3) at one breakpoint, each role has one text style, one component and variant, and one spacing to its parent; (4) every variable and style is the library's, inside instances too, and no visible raw solid fill or stroke outside an instance (on a text with mixed fills, per run; gradients and images are not read). The library match is configuration (`local`, collection/style keys, or name patterns), never a brand name. The rebind skill gains section 10 (when to run it, the definitions it relies on, how to read and log findings), and the consume skill points to it.

**The definitions, made concrete because the issue left them open.** An element role is the layer name, lowercased, separators as spaces, a trailing `copy`/`copy N` removed; a number stays (`Heading 1` and `Heading 2` are two roles). A layer Figma named (`Frame 12`, `Rectangle 4`, a text layer still named after its own characters) has no role, so checks 2 and 3 skip it and `coverage` counts the text ones. The heading allowlist matches the role or the text style name, so an unnamed heading layer is still skipped by its style. A frame is desktop/mobile by a breakpoint word in its name (`desktop`/`lg`/`xl`, `mobile`/`sm`/`xs`), else by width (≤ 767 by default). Frames whose names match once those words are removed are one page. "Expected" is what most frames use, so a two-page tie reports whichever came first; three or more pages make it meaningful.

**The test.** `apps/plugin/test-consistency-audit.ts`, in the plugin's `test` script, sends the file through the real `runCode` (`src/dev-commands.ts`) over a hand-built mock tree: three pages at two breakpoints, one pair inside a section, one mobile frame classified by width. The consistent set is quiet on every check; a drifted copy with one seeded drift per check reports exactly the findings written in the test (14). The mock `getStyledTextSegments` refuses a field outside the plugin typings, and the mock page records `loadAsync`. Nodes are Proxies that record writes, and the suite fails on any. Mutations, each failing by name: each check's function returns early (`drift/1 control label`, `drift/2 pairing`, `drift/3 component|spacing|text style`, `drift/4 raw fill|legacy variable|legacy style inside an instance`); the heading allowlist by style dropped (`consistent/1`); any trailing number stripped (`consistent/3`); Figma's default names kept as roles (`default-named layers … have no role`, `consistent/3`); the mixed-run paints dropped (`drift/4 raw run`); either page load dropped (`the page is loaded before it is read`, `frameIds: each frame's page is loaded`); a frame renamed by the audit (`the audit wrote nothing to the file`).

**Review.** An independent read-only review found the default-name, numbered-role, mixed-fill, unnamed-heading and page-load gaps above; each is fixed and has an arm. Kept as is: a `SPACE_BETWEEN` parent reports `gap auto (space between)` rather than a number.

**Ceiling.** Not run against a live file in this PR: the fixture models the plugin API calls the audit makes (`getNodeByIdAsync`, `getStyleByIdAsync`, `getVariableByIdAsync`, `getVariableCollectionByIdAsync`, `getMainComponentAsync`, `getStyledTextSegments`), and the first real run is the Runs table's row 1. Check 3's spacing in a frame without auto layout is the distance from the previous sibling, which moves with content height; the Runs table will say whether it is noise.

## (2026-10-21) — Component usage docs, phase 2: the usage panel beside each set in Figma (#846)

**What it is.** The second phase of the approved usage docs wireframe (#846, 2026-10-19). After a build or an update
lands a set, the plugin draws the component's usage doc beside it: a 560px frame, 40px right of the set and
top-aligned with it (`apps/plugin/src/doc-panel.ts`). Its sections come from the engine's doc section model,
`docSections`, which the Markdown page already renders, so the panel and the page cannot disagree. The panel leaves out
Building it in code, which is site-only (Q406.2 A), and cuts the rest the way the wireframe draws it: two sentences per
Overview row, four Do and four Don't items, one sentence per accessibility row, Styles pointing at the set. Theming
shows the default member in light and dark side by side, each instance pinned to its mode, and is drawn only when the
file's color collection has those modes: the phase-1 trap (the surface must pass modes) is held by `present/<def>`.

**Reused, not added.** The panel is canvas furniture: drawn on the set's parent after the labels, never inside the
set, reported through the furniture's outcome, its run line and its missing-template warning (`withPanel`,
`templatesLine`). The template is one more `↳ File Components` asset beside `_Label`. The hand-edit check is the style
guide's `fingerprintOf`, exported rather than restated. The dry run's check sits beside `furnitureDue` and feeds the
same "N to draw" line, and the room for the panel comes from the update's existing set spacing (`pageSetMoves`,
`respaceLive`), with the panel read as one more furniture box of its set. The component executor is untouched, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` does not move.

**Its own tag, on purpose.** The panel is tagged `prism3`/`docPanel`, not `furniture`: the labels' clear removes
whatever carries their tag, and a panel a designer edited must never be removed. A redraw removes an earlier panel only
while its fingerprint matches what was written; an edited one is renamed "(edited)", tagged `kept`, moved below
everything in its column, and named in the run's result. A kept panel is never touched again except to move it down
when a fresh panel would cover it.

**Never on top of anything.** Labels sit above and left of a set and backdrops reach 12px past it, so the spot right
of the set is clear of them by construction; another set may not be. A panel that would overlap any node is not drawn.
When what is in the way is a Prism3 set later in the row (or its labels or panel), the run says to update, and the
update moves that set to #2842's 160px visible gap past the panel: a live panel is part of its set's visible box, as
its labels are, and a set with no panel yet reaches as far as its panel will. Anything else is the designer's to move,
and the run says so. A blocked draw records the panel's height on the page, so the dry run counts it as due only once
the spot is clear or the update itself clears it, never on every run. A new set is seated with room for its panel
(`seatNewSet`), the panel is drawn after that, and a set's live panel moves with it whenever the update re-spaces.

**`_Doc-block`.** Set up file builds it from the file's own Badge (the part markers), Tag (chips), List.Item (the Do
and Don't rows) and Divider, with every fill bound to a semantic color and every text on a brand text style, so the
panel follows the brand (`apps/plugin/src/doc-block.ts`). It needs those four sets and an applied theme, and says which
are missing until then. Its properties are Q406.10 A's: Type × Size, Top padding, Bottom padding, Caption, and a
Specimen instance swap. Mode is pinned on the placed instance, as the style guide pins a swatch's, so there is no Mode
axis. The Do and Don't rows are List.Item instances rather than one List, because a List holds its items in a native
slot, and a slot's items cannot be overridden one by one from an instance.

**Tests (`apps/plugin/test-doc-panel.ts`).** `present/<def>` on all 41 defs that build a set: one live panel per set,
its section frames exactly the model's sections less the site-only one. `anatomy/held back`: none of 64 held-back
notes is in any panel, and all 152 reader-ready captions are. `hand edit/…`: the edit is kept, aside, reported, and kept
once. `overlap/…`: Badge and Tag built by the real executor with their labels and panels, nothing overlapping, and a
blocked spot draws nothing. `due/…` covers the dry run, blocked panels included. `room/apply` runs one real Update on a page laid out before
the panels and finds Badge's panel drawn with Divider 160px past it, then a dry run with nothing left; `room/panel
follows` moves a set and its panel together. `orphan/edited kept`: rebuilding a deleted set's def removes its
unedited panel and keeps the edited one. `seat/…` seats a new set where its panel fits. `template/…` covers the
template. `test-build-completed.ts` drives `main.ts`: `panel/build` finds the panel on its spot, `panel/update due` and
`panel/update drawn` run the real Update's dry run and apply on it.

**Mutations, each failing by name (exit 1):** the modes not passed (`present/<def>`, Theming missing) · the site-only
section drawn (`present/<def>`) · the fingerprint check dropped (`hand edit/kept`) · the overlap check dropped
(`overlap/blocked`) · the raw part note as the caption (`anatomy/held back`) · the panel's reach dropped from the
spacing (`room/with template`) · the dry run ignoring the plan (`due/plan`) · the build not drawing the panel
(`panel/build`) · `respaceLive` given no reach (`room/apply`) · the live panel not read as its set's furniture
(`room/panel follows`) · `clearOrphanPanels` removing edited panels (`orphan/edited kept`) · `updateTargets` giving no
target its def (`panel/update due`) · the blocker check dropped from `docPanelDue` (`due/blocked`) · `seatNewSet`
ignoring the panel (`seat/room for the panel`).

## (2026-10-21) — Naming sweep PR 4: layers named per the naming table, renamed in place by Update (#2759, owner decision Q350)

**What moved.** Every layer name `lint-naming.ts` listed for PR 4, plus the main-text renames it cannot check:
- **Glyph layers end in `Glyph`:**
  - Checkbox.Control: `mark`, `dash`
  - Field message: the three status glyphs (`iconError` → `errorGlyph`, and so on)
  - Textarea: `grip`
  - Select: `chevron`
  - Image placeholder: `marker`
  - Spinner: `ring`
  - Tag: `check`
  - Accordion indicator: its four glyphs
- **A Row's control cell is `controlCell`.**
- **Main text is `label`** for FieldLabel, Field message, Badge and List item.
- **Two roots are renamed for their role:** Divider `divider` → `container`, and FieldLabel `label` → `container`. The second frees `label` for its text. `label` leaves the gate's root role list and the skill table, since main text owns it.

`lint-naming.ts` drops its 18 PR 4 entries. Only the per-item booleans that #2660 removes are left.

**Owner calls built on a recommendation** (raised on #2759):
- **Q-N3:** main text where `label` was taken. Dialog keeps `title`.
- **Q-N4:** each glyph's name.

**A side effect of Q-N3.** FieldLabel's text is now named `label`, the same name as the `label` instance a field nests it under. That is #1428's collision shape: a host part and a nested part with one name. The executor's `findOwnPart` already scopes every find-by-name past nested instances. `test-roundtrip.ts`'s #1428 block now gives its colliding nested parts a `label` as well, so that scoping is exercised against the new name.

**The mechanism.**
- **Ledger:** `COMPONENT_RENAMES` gains a `part` kind. A def's part entries form one map, not a chain, so FieldLabel's text can take the name its root gave up. Naming a part twice is refused.
- **Dry run:** `renamedSnap` reads each member's snapshot under the new layer names. A renamed layer reads as the same node, where it used to read as one removed and one added. The record is compared as read, so no layer reads as a hand edit.
- **Apply:** the layers are renamed first, before the identity is captured. The verify then holds each renamed layer to its old id.
- **Skipped members:** a member the update does not configure is not renamed, because its record would no longer match.
- **Untouched:** the root (the member itself) and an instance's contents (its main's).

Before this change, a renamed part was listed as a replacement, and every override on it was lost.

**Proof through the shim** (`test-update-apply.ts`, "part rename").
- **Setup:** a Tag built from plans that say `check`.
- **No ledger entry:** the dry run removes `check` and adds `checkGlyph`.
- **With the shipped ledger:** nothing is removed, added or replaced, and nothing reads as a hand edit.
- **After the apply:**
  - all 15 selected members hold `checkGlyph` under the id `check` had;
  - every member keeps its key and id;
  - a second dry run reads all 45 members current.

`test.ts` checks that every `part` entry renames a layer the def no longer has into one it has now. The registry is the oracle there.

**Gate lists moved with the names:** `lint-glyph-geometry`'s per-part lists and `lint-absolute-inset`'s corner list. The paint census changed for exactly the 12 defs with a renamed painted layer, each "the same count of assignments, pointing somewhere else". So the census moved names, not paint.

**Not folded in.** #2710's binding-key spellings and #2712's field order and stated-empty keys are different mechanical edits from a layer rename. Each stays for its own PR. #2710 asks to land after #2660.

**Not enforced, said so.** The renames lint's baseline records axes, values and properties, not layer names. So a future PR that drops a layer without a `part` entry is not caught by a gate. That would make the lint demand an entry for every removed layer, which is a process change for other lanes. Filed as #2776 rather than added here.

**Consumer-visible names (published library, #2839).** No component property, variant value or set name changes in this PR. The layer names inside members change, as the table above lists: Checkbox.Control `mark`/`dash` → `checkGlyph`/`dashGlyph`; Field message `iconError`/`iconWarning`/`iconSuccess`/`text` → `errorGlyph`/`warningGlyph`/`successGlyph`/`label`; Textarea `grip`, Select `chevron`, Image placeholder `marker`, Spinner `ring` and Tag `check` → `…Glyph`; Accordion indicator's four glyphs → `…Glyph`; Checkbox.Row and Radio.Row `controlBox`, Switch.Row `trackBox` → `controlCell`; FieldLabel `text` → `label`; Badge and List item `text` → `label`. The two root renames (FieldLabel, Divider) rename no layer, since a member is its own root. Update renames each layer in place, keeping its id, and #2839's classifier lists nothing as breaking. Anything that finds these layers by name, such as a consumer's plugin or a Code Connect mapping that reads a layer, needs the new names. Layer overrides in placed instances surviving the rename is argued from the kept ids, not observed in Figma.

## (2026-10-21) — Naming sweep PR 3: Tab is renamed Tab item, in place by Update (#2759, owner decisions Q353, Q365, Q394)

**What moved.** `tab` is `tab-item`, with the display name `Tab.Item` (Q365 2). Tabs nests and offers the new id in its `items` slot. Q353 had named it `_tab-item`, and Q355 had prefixed `list-item` and `segmented-control-segment` too. Q394 A (2026-10-17, #2783) then decided that a slot's preferred item is not "used only inside its parent": Figma leaves a `_` set out of a published library, so a file using the library could not insert it into the slot (#2831). So nothing here takes the prefix: `list-item` and `segmented-control-segment` keep their ids, and only the tab's rename is left. `_accordion-indicator` keeps its prefix; it is not a slot item.

**File and export names are unchanged** (`tab.ts` exports `tab`). Renaming the exports would have touched hundreds of test lines for no reader-visible change.

**The mechanism.** `COMPONENT_RENAMES` gains a `def` kind (`{ def: <old id>, kind: 'def', to: <new id> }`), with `currentDefId` and `formerDefIds` (both follow chains, and the first refuses a cycle). Update's `locateSets` finds a set by the current id. When there is none, it tries each earlier id the ledger renames into it, nearest first. The dry run marks a set found that way with `setRename`, which counts as a change, and its line ends "Renamed from <old id>." (draft wording, an owner item). The apply renames the set node first thing in `applySet`, so the set and every member keep their ids and every placed instance keeps pointing at them. A set this update renames counts as present for `fileBlockers`, so a Tabs updated in the same run as its Tab item is not refused for lacking `tab-item`. Nested sets are still updated first. In that same run, Tabs' nested items are instances of members the run renames, not swaps: the readback's `nestTarget` check takes a `renamedSet` port, which the dry run fills from the sets it found under an earlier id, so those items read as `tab-item`'s and not as "the WRONG SET". The "def rename, nested" section asserts the together run lists no such line.

**The lint checks this rename.** The merge base's baseline holds `tab`, so `unaccounted` compares it against `tab-item` under the `def` entry. Without the entry, arm B fails naming the def. The id-keyed lists in other gates moved with the id: `lint-absolute-inset`, `lint-axis-values`, `lint-paint`, `lint-paint-placement`, `lint-rung-names`, `lint-standalone-floor`, `anatomy-figma`'s projected list, the plugin's `file-taxonomy`, and the studio catalog and used-by index (regenerated). `lint-naming`'s `SLOT_ITEMS` and the skill's §6 name `tab-item`.

**Proof through the shim** (`test-update-apply.ts`, "def rename"). A Tab item set is built by the real executor from plans naming it `tab`. With no ledger entry, the dry run cannot find it: the update would build a second set. With the shipped ledger:
- The dry run reads it under `tab`, marks it for renaming, and adds or drops nothing.
- After the apply, there is one set, named `tab-item`.
- The set and every member keep their keys and ids.
- A second dry run finds the set under the new id and reads every member current.

**Not checked here, said so.** The shim's instance records its main component by name at creation and does not follow a rename, so "a placed instance still points at its main" is argued from the ids being kept (Figma resolves an instance's main by id), not observed.

**Consumer-visible names (published library, #2839).** One: the component set `tab` is named `tab-item`. Update renames the node, so its key and every member's id stay, and #2839's classifier lists nothing as breaking. A consumer who reads the set by its name, such as search in the assets panel or code that looks it up by name, sees the new name after the next library publish.

## (2026-10-21) — Naming sweep PR 2: Figma property names are lowercase, renamed in place by Update (#2759, owner decision Q345 A)

**What moved.** Four property names: Switch.Control's `State icon` → `state icon`, Image placeholder's `Marker` → `marker`, Tag's `Check icon` → `check icon`, and Segmented control's `Label` → `label`. The code props are unchanged. Shipped prose that names them (Image placeholder's whenToUse, do and don't, and the switch and tag notes) follows. `lint-naming.ts` drops their four `PENDING` entries.

**The mechanism.** `COMPONENT_RENAMES` covered variant axes and values only, so a property name change was a delete and an add on Update: every placed instance lost the value a designer had given it. The ledger gains a `property-rename` kind (`renameProperty` follows chains and refuses a cycle). It is not `property`: #2649 took that kind on `main` for a property gone with no successor. The dry run (`dryRunSet`) reads the set's property under its old name as the new one when the ledger renames it, the plan wants the new name and the set has none. It lists it in `properties.rename`, which already existed in `SetPreview` and was always empty. The apply renames those first with `editComponentProperty(key, { name })`, before any delete or default edit. Figma keeps the property's `#id` through a rename, and references and instance values follow the id.

**The forcing function.** `schema/component-axes.json` records each set's properties by panel name and type (#2649 added the record on `main`). `unaccounted` fails a property that leaves a set unclaimed, and a `property-rename` entry now claims one; `danglingTargets` fails a rename whose target the set does not declare. `main`'s baseline already holds the old names, so the lint checks this PR's own four renames. `test.ts` checks the accounting on hand-built baselines, and the shim test below checks the apply.

**The shim, made to tell a rename from a delete.** `component-shim.ts` already renamed a property's key on `editComponentProperty({ name })`, but it left every `componentPropertyReferences` entry pointing at the old key, and an instance held its value by the full key. A renamed property would have read as wired to nothing, and every instance would have been reset. It now moves references to the new key and holds an instance's value by the property's id, as Figma does. `test-update-apply.ts` runs the same check for each of the four renames, typed in the test from Q345 A rather than read off the ledger, so deleting any shipped entry fails by its def's name (the lint cannot, once the baseline records the lowercase names). For each def it builds the set from plans that say the old name (the file as it was) and places an instance with the switch off. It first shows that with no ledger entry the dry run removes the old name and adds the new one. With the entry, the dry run lists one rename and nothing else. After the apply, the set has one property under the new name and the same id, the instance's switch is still off, the set and every member keep their keys and ids, and a second dry run reads every member current.

**The per-item booleans are gone.** #2649 replaced `Option N`, `Tab N`, `Item N` and `Segment N` with native `items` slots on `main`, so there is nothing of theirs to rename, and PR 1 deleted their `PENDING` entries.

**Consumer-visible names (published library, #2839).** Four component property names change, and nothing else: Switch.Control `State icon` → `state icon` (Switch.Row shows it through the nested control), Image placeholder `Marker` → `marker`, Tag `Check icon` → `check icon`, and Segmented control `Label` → `label`. Update renames each property in place, so its `#id` is kept and #2839's classifier lists none of them as breaking. Code or a plugin that sets these properties by their panel name, and Code Connect mappings that name them, must use the new names after the next library publish. Real Figma keeping a consumer instance's value across the rename is argued from the kept id, not observed.

## (2026-10-21) — One canonical colour-variable order, default and inverse alike (#2860, #2836)

The owner hand-reordered the default colour groups in the master file but not the inverse ones, so the two read differently, and `foreground` listed `danger` after the subtle tints. The order is what Figma's variable panels show, and it is the emission's write order, so the fix is in the emission (owner decisions Q453 A on #2836, and the reference order on #2860).

- **One module, `packages/engine/color-order.ts`**, replaces `COLOR_FAMILY_ORDER` and `orderedRoleKeys` in `tree.ts`. Families: background, foreground, text, interactive, border, icon, disabled, scrim, veil, field, inverse. Below the family, one sibling list per depth. The statuses are `SEMANTICS` from `modes.ts` (now exported), not a second copy. `inverse.<family>` is ranked as `<family>` with `inverse.` stripped, so the two cannot drift. A segment the module does not name throws, except the tone slot of `interactive`, which a brand can extend (`interactivePalettes`); an extra tone sorts after the named ones in build order.
- **Key order only.** Every moved file was read back and compared with `main` after sorting keys: 41 files, 0 differ in content. Token names, values, aliases and the contract baseline are untouched, so `token-contract.ts --check`, `nb-regression.ts` and `regen.ts --check` agree with the new emission.
- **Which files move:** `packages/engine/out/<brand>.tokens.json`, `<brand>.base.tokens.json` and the three `<brand>.*.overlay.tokens.json` for nb, prism3, aurora, harbor and wendys (the key order of `color`), and `out/figma/<brand>/color.{light,dark,hc-light,hc-dark}.json` for nb, prism3, aurora and wendys (the order of `variables[]`). No other committed artifact moves.
- **No code path sorted keys alphabetically before emission.** `emit-figma-color.ts` `byNumericKey` is a stable no-op for non-numeric keys, and the remaining `.sort()` calls in the write path are prune reports. The gate asserts hover precedes focused and success precedes danger, so a sort that comes back fails by name.
- **Gate:** the `#1150` block in `test.ts` gains a `#2860` block. Everything is a literal typed in the test, none read from `color-order.ts`. Per brand it asserts, on the DTCG tree and on each Figma mode file: every group is one run; statuses are brand, success, warning, danger, info in every group (bare, subtle and on-); each inverse group is the default group's order restricted to what the inverse has; scrim and veil are the only families with no inverse; plus design-UX spot checks. Mutations (each committed first, each run through `regen.ts` and `test.ts`): `foreground.danger` ranked last fails `statuses in canonical order` and `foreground lists danger with the statuses`; one inverse interactive part moved fails `inverse mirrors default`; alphabetical segment order fails the `design-UX order` lines; `border.primary` split off fails `inverse mirrors default`. `apps/studio/test-status-order.ts` (#2843) drops its `foreground` exception and now holds all eight groups to the canon.
- **Contiguity is guaranteed by the tree's shape.** The emission is nested, so a group cannot be split by building it; the master file's splits came from variables appended later by releases. The contiguity assertions are a regression guard for a flattening change, not something a ranking mutation can break.
- **Existing files (the plugin limit).** The Plugin API moves styles but not variables, so an existing file cannot be reordered by the plugin. The Update check now reads the file's `<root>/color/*` variables in the order the host returns them and lists the fewest to drag (`colorVariablesOutOfOrder`, a longest-run calculation), as one line: "Color variables: N out of order (…)". It is a report: nothing moves, and it is not in the apply's hash. A file built fresh from the emission reads clean. Documented in `apps/plugin/README.md`.
- **Downstream, and what it showed.** The style-guide page (Figma) draws its colour tables in the emission's family order ("in file order"), so its typed-out expectations in `apps/plugin/test-style-guide.ts` (tests 3, 9, 10 and 26: table order and the column each table sits in) failed by name and were updated to the new order, inverse tables included. The inverse table list there had been the old inverse order from the master file (background, foreground, interactive, disabled, field, text, icon, border); it now mirrors the default.
- **Traps for whoever re-verifies.** The throw messages in `color-order.ts` ship in the built bundles, so they are held to US spelling by `lint-us-english`. `studio test:smoke` fails one assertion in this sandbox (the "Not installed" font status is not drawn for harbor) and fails identically on `main`; it is a fonts-in-the-sandbox condition, not this change. `lint-release-notes` cannot run in a shallow clone (`git fetch --unshallow`).

## (2026-10-21) — Component specs, phase 1: the engine spec model, its emission and its read-back gate (#2830)

**Status:** engine module + emission + gate. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no token path moves.
No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. `regen --check` grows by one artifact (`out/components/specs.json`),
so `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` in `verify.ts` and the count in `ci.yml` move to 203 together.

### What changed

- **`packages/engine/component-specs.ts`** (new, exported as `@prism3/engine/component-specs`): `componentSpec(def)`
  builds one pure spec model from the def and its Figma anatomy plan — the four blocks of the approved wireframe
  (Q429 A): anatomy (every part by path, the members that hold it), redlines (padding, gap, height, width, min-width
  per size and slot case) plus a type block, colors (fill, stroke, ink, icon per part per state), and nesting
  (nested instances with their fixed variant, followed and exposed axes; swap slots with their property and
  visibility boolean; native slots; the set's component properties).
- **Token names only.** A value is the DTCG ref (`space.200`) when the plan binds a variable, and a px number labeled
  `literal` (a field's 120 floor, its 320 build width) or `derived` (Button's 88 / 104 / 128 floor, a "Locked to edges"
  reserve, Tag's ratio floor) when the build writes a number. A caller with a brand passes `px` to resolve tokens; the
  emission does not, so one file serves every brand.
- **Rows key themselves.** Redlines start at size × slot case, colors at every variant axis × state, type at size,
  and each key grows until every value is a function of it. Button's redlines key on `inset` too (flush drops the
  padding) and its type on `appearance` (the underlined text appearance); a row never claims one value for members
  that hold two.
- **Emission:** `out/components/specs.json` (one file, every projected def; payload, classified in
  `payload-manifest.json`) and a **Specs** section at the end of each projected def's `out/components/<id>.md`.
  No part notes or `codeOnly` prose ship (#1623); a code-only state is named, not explained.
- **`specMaterialize`** restates the plugin's `materializeForBrand(def, null)` in the engine (the engine must not
  import a surface), so the model describes what Apply builds for a file with no brand settings, Button's floor
  included.

### The gate: `apps/plugin/test-roundtrip.ts` SPEC READ-BACK

- The model descends from the plan, so it is checked against the HOST, not the plan (docs/34): every round-tripped
  def (66 rows, the lever and override variants included) is built into the shim and read back by a reader that
  shares no code with the model — its own Figma-key list, its own walk, its own member-name parse, names resolved
  through the host's catalogs.
- **Both directions, per member, by name.** DROPPED: every part, bound redline, unbound literal, text style, paint and
  instance the host holds must be in the one row covering that member. CLAIMED: every value a row states must be on
  every member it covers. Plus part counts per path, the set's component properties both ways, and every nest's host
  node type.
- **It found two model gaps on its first run**, both fixed before this entry: Button's pending spinner is an instance
  the build places by member (not a swap the designer drives), now a `fixed` nest listing its components; and a drawn
  glyph's color sits on the geometry inside it, which the reader now reaches.
- **Mutations of `component-specs.ts`, each failing `spec read-back: <def> — N disagreement(s)` by def:** dropping
  `paddingLeft` from the key map (Button ×3, Text field, …), dropping strokes (focus-ring, Button ×3, …), dropping the
  `label` parts from the anatomy, keying redlines on size alone (Button ×3 at 1,728 each, flush-icon-button, …), and
  dropping a nest's exposed axes (Text field, Textarea, Checkbox row, …). A hand-built "predicate speaks" block in the gate itself drops a part, a padding side and a stroke from
  Button's real model and asserts each fails by name. The two materializations are compared on all defs.
- **Where its coverage stops:** a wrong plan agrees with itself here (both sides descend from it); `test.ts` pins the
  wireframe's hand-read values (Button's slot-aware padding and floor, Text field's literals and nested label, the
  code-only states, Button's visual icon ink, Text field's and Counter's nest variants). A nest's `exposes` list is
  checked only as the host's one boolean; its fixed variant is read off the host only where the nested set is built
  in the same file (188 instances), and pinned in `test.ts` otherwise.
- **Review round (2026-10-20):** an instance's icon color, first counted as unreadable, is now read off the VECTORs
  inside the instance (`findAll`), both directions, with an `icons` scope floor (10,132). A nest's fixed variant is
  read back against the host's main-component name, which found a third model gap: the model dropped `variantWhen`
  (#2427), so Counter's ghost members, which nest the round shape, read as flush. A nest now carries `when`, and its
  Specs line says which host value takes which nested value.
- **After #846's section model landed:** each page renders the section model's sections, then Specs, last.
  `lint-component-docs.ts` F4 now expects a trailing `Specs` heading exactly on the pages of defs the committed
  `specs.json` covers. It reads the emitted file, not the emitter's condition, and fails `SECTION PARITY` by name
  both ways: a page that drops Specs, and a `specs.json` that drops a def.

through library imports by key (no REST, any plan) — planned in the PR body.

**What.** From the component consistency audit (#2706). The 13 defs built since Tag followed the build-component
skill's "What ships" rules; the older ones mostly did not. This PR brings 27 def files to the rules, one commit per file:
code spans out of the consumer fields, all-caps emphasis lowercased, "brief §N", "image.md §6" and "this def" reworded,
HC, SR and AT spelled out. It fills the content fields the audit found missing (`docs.contentGuidelines` on Icon, Focus
ring and Field label from the KB briefs' §7; `content.dialogPattern` on Dialog), lengthens Button's and IconButton's
summaries to the ~90-character line, makes the segment's summary agree with its description (emphasis weight, not
"bold"), and moves every child part's `whenToUse` onto two templates.

**How the bulk pass was done.** A scratch script removed the backticks and lowercased all-caps words outside an acronym
list, string by string against the def objects, and every resulting line was read in the diff before its commit. The
automated step gets three things wrong, each fixed by hand: a sentence that opens with an all-caps word ("GROUP-LEVEL
and specific" came out lowercase), an acronym missing from its list (AT, JSX), and brace patterns left bare by a removed
code span (`type.body.{sm,md,lg}` is now "from type.body.sm, md and lg").

**What did not move, and why.** Button's implementation `do` items (ten per Button def: the five brand settings' builds,
the text-button underline, the two hover lines and the flush hit-area pair) are held by owner decision Q362 on #2714.
They keep the exact wording they have on main, code spans included. The register gate exempts them by def and path
(`HELD_Q362` in `test.ts`), and the exemption is live: each exempt path must still carry a hit, so it cannot outlive the
hold. Where those lines belong is the owner's call.

**The gate** (`test.ts`, after `component-prose`). `#2714 component register` walks the seven consumer fields of every
def and refuses a backtick, an all-caps word outside a hand-written acronym list, a section reference, "def" and an
issue number; the acronym list must be live (an acronym no field uses fails as stale), and the walk must reach each
def's summary, description, docs.usage and whenToUse. `#2714 child-only whenToUse` holds the two templates and resolves
each named host against the other defs' anatomy, so a template naming a host that does not nest the part fails.

**Out of scope, filed.** `motion` and a part's `note` also ship (the plugin bundle carries them) and carry 84 more
strings in the old register; the gate does not read them yet (#2773).

## (2026-10-20) — Style guides: a group you made that wraps fits its widest row, not one long row (#2856)

The copy-file run after #2827 doubled the width of the owner's groups on the semantic-tokens page: Semantic colors 15160 → 30994, Borders 2427 → 4690 (its first guide moved up beside the header), Fonts 4759 → 9354, Space & size 4890 → 9392. Those frames are HORIZONTAL auto layouts with wrap on, FIXED wide: the `_section-header` takes the first row and the guides wrap below it.

**The diagnosis.** #2827's never-clip rule, `fitToContent` in `apps/plugin/src/style-guide.ts`, summed a HORIZONTAL frame's children along its axis, as if they sat on one row. For a wrapped frame that sum is the header plus the guides plus the padding: wide enough for both to share a row, so the guides moved up beside the header. #2827's fixture (section 39) had wrap off, so it passed.

**The fix, reusing #2827's code.** `fitToContent` keeps its shape: the same in-flow child filter, the same FIXED/HUG reading, the same never-shrink rule, and the same restore of a hugging axis after `resize`. Its one-row sum is now the `oneRow` helper, used as before for a frame that does not wrap. A frame with `layoutWrap: 'WRAP'` needs only its widest non-FILL child plus its horizontal padding across. Its height is its rows at the width it ends at: each row as tall as its tallest child, with `counterAxisSpacing` between rows (`itemSpacing` where the host leaves it unset), plus its vertical padding. The overlap and push-down passes after it are unchanged.

**Frames the bad run already widened.** #2827 stores nothing on a frame it resizes: no plugin data, no record of the width before. So the only sign of its widening is the width itself. A wrapped, FIXED frame that is exactly the old one-row sum of the children it holds now (to the half pixel), and wider than its widest row needs, goes back to the widest-row width. Any other width is taken as the owner's and kept. The width from before the bad run cannot be recovered, so the widest-row width is the target: it is the narrowest width that does not clip, which can be wider than the original (Semantic colors' 15160 clipped its 15676-wide grid). This is a guess about where a width came from, so it went to the owner as an Owner question on #2856. A is built; B removes the `widened` line.

**The trap for re-verifying it in the file.** The match uses the child widths of the current run. If a guide's width changed since the bad run (tables added or removed), the sum no longer matches and the frame is left wide for the owner to fix by hand. That is the safe failure.

**The test.** Section 40 of `test-style-guide.ts` builds a wrapped owner frame: padding 240, 48 between items, 96 between rows, an owner `_section-header`, and the drawn Guides grid. The shim gained its own wrap layout (`wrapRows`: x positions and the hugged height), written from the host's rule and not from the plugin's. The expected width is the rule itself, padding + widest child + padding, typed in the test. The cases: a clipping frame grows to 36127 and not the 70984 one-row sum, the grid stays on its own row, and the height is two rows 96 apart; a frame set to the one-row sum is put back to 36127; a frame 1000 wider than that sum is kept; each rerun moves and resizes nothing.

**Mutations, failing by name.** With the wrap branch dropped from `need`: "40: a wrapped frame you made grows to its widest row…" fails, and so do the height check and "40: a wrapped frame the one-row sum widened is put back…". With the repair disabled (`widened` forced false): "40: a wrapped frame the one-row sum widened is put back…" fails.

## (2026-10-20) — prism3-rebind covers a file that consumes Prism3 as a published library (#2854, Q446)

**What changed.** `skills/prism3-rebind/SKILL.md` assumed Prism3's variables, styles and components were local to the file. The common case is a file that consumes Prism3 as a published team library. New section 8 covers that path; the old section 8 (hand-back) is now 9 and gains one library line. Three existing lines gained a pointer to it: the detach guard in section 1, the mapping-table step in section 2, and the "legacy names look like Prism3's" trap in section 5.

**What was reused, not restated.** The never-detach rule, the font check, the breakpoint-mode rule (read the modes), the rogue-binding audit and the hand-back are unchanged. Section 8 says only what the library path alters: the library is enabled by a person, the mapping table's Prism3 side is a key, everything in it is imported before any screen, import comes before bind, fonts are checked after the import, and only published work is importable.

**The one real correction.** Both the detach guard ("confirm the main component is remote") and the section 5 trap ("tell them apart by `remote: true`") are wrong on this path: Prism3's library instances are remote too, so a guard on `remote` alone detaches the very components the skill says never to detach. The test becomes the key against a set built from the whole library (every Prism3 collection's variables, and every component, variant and style key), not from the mapping table, which omits Prism3's own nested parts: detaching a nested legacy-looking icon would detach the Prism3 component around it.

**Verified against the repo's plugin typings** (`@figma/plugin-typings`, the version in the lockfile): the four import signatures and their reject-if-unpublished wording, both `teamLibrary` methods and the `LibraryVariableCollection` / `LibraryVariable` shapes, "libraries can't be enabled through the plugin API", `key` and `remote` on components, component sets, styles and variables, `setBoundVariable` / `setBoundVariableForPaint` taking a `Variable`, `getVariableCollectionByIdAsync`, `setExplicitVariableModeForCollection(collection, modeId)`, `defaultVariant`, and `PublishStatus`.

**Not checkable from the typings, so stated as the owner's account, not as API fact:** that a consuming file takes a library update in the UI, and that a variant's `key` equals its instance's main component `key`. A first run on a real library file should confirm both.

**Also in the skill.** Capabilities are read from a set's variant properties, never its description (which can go stale, #2865). Keys may come from a design-system search the bridge offers, unconfirmed until imported. Under a `dynamic-page` manifest, `textStyleId` is read-only: use `setTextStyleIdAsync`. Text writes need a runtime with the brand fonts. Not checkable from the typings: that a remote collection reached through an imported variable exposes usable `modes`.

## (2026-10-20) — Studio smoke: the "⚠ Not installed" arm no longer depends on the host's fonts (#2837)

`test:smoke`'s font-status sweep (#2091, #2103) requires both labels drawn in every brand × mode. It forced Inter to read as installed (`INTER_INSTALLED`, a `measureText` stub) and left every other family to the host, relying on JetBrains Mono being absent. A container that ships Inter and JetBrains Mono (the cloud image does) drew "✓ Installed" for harbor and no "⚠ Not installed" at all, so the arm failed NOT EXERCISED in four harbor states.

- **Fix.** The same init script now answers the probe for every family: Inter's width widened by the existing 10px, any other family measured as the bare base font, so `fontAvailable` sees no change and the face reads absent. Both states are now forced, not inherited. Test-only; no shipped code, no engine change, no change note.
- **Reused, not new.** The mechanism is the existing `INTER_INSTALLED` stub (the issue's options 1 and 3 would add a fontconfig pin or a fixture brand); the arm's NOT EXERCISED guard is unchanged, so a state that draws neither label still fails.
- **Checked.** Passes on a host with Inter and JetBrains Mono installed (12025 assertions; ⚠ drawn in 12 of 12 states, lowest 4.99:1). Mutation: painting the ⚠ label a fixed `#b0b0b0` in `preview/sections/faces.ts` fails the arm by name in all 12 states, harbor included ("clears 4.5:1 on the brand's page color … 1.79:1", "is drawn in the brand's text.warning …"), and the mutation is reverted.
- **Trap.** The stub matches only the probe's font string (`72px "<family>", <base>`). A change to the probe's string makes the stub inert and the sweep falls back to the host's fonts; the NOT EXERCISED guard is what would then say so.

## (2026-10-20) — Unified errors: Checkbox, Switch and Radio take the fields' status axis (#2751, owner Q354)

**Status:** eight defs reshaped, a new `COMPONENT_RENAMES` kind, the skill's idiom, and the tests. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no new token, only existing roles (`color.border.danger`). No executor code moved (`apps/plugin/src` is untouched), so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays where main has it.

**What it builds (the approved wireframe, recorded on #2706):** Checkbox control and Switch control drop the `error` state for a `status` axis `[default, error]`, orthogonal to the states. Radio control gains it, and its header records that the Radio group sets it. The three Rows gain `status` and `follow` it into their control. Checkbox group and Radio group gain `status`, `follow` it into all eight rows, and nest a FieldMessage under the options, gated `presentWhen: { status: ['error'] }`, its own status following the group's. Every def carries the fields' `validation` prop over the first two values; the groups also carry `validationMessage`. Members: Checkbox control 54 → 90, Switch control 24 → 40, Radio control 30 → 60, the three Rows 3 / 2 / 3 → 6 / 4 / 6, both groups 3 → 6.

**The diagnosis that made the paint small:** the obvious status template, `{status}.{slot}.{state}`, has the arity of the controls' `{selection}.{slot}.{state}`, and the paint-key validator reads each key through every template of its length, so `error.border.rest` reads as `selection=error` and `unchecked.border.hover` as `status=unchecked`. The fields met the same trap and kept their two vocabularies at different lengths. So the controls' status template is four segments, `{status}.{selection}.{slot}.{state}`, bound per selection and per non-disabled state (12 keys on Checkbox, 8 on Radio and Switch). Verbose, and it states exactly the old per-selection `*.border.error` bindings, one per state.

**The diagnosis that made the migration small:** the update already matches members by coordinate, applies the declared renames, then gives every member an axis the plan added at the plan's first value. What it could not say is "this value left its axis for another", so a `state=error` member would have landed on `status=default, state=error`, a coordinate the plan no longer has, and been marked deprecated, breaking every placed error instance. One ledger kind, `move` (`state=error` → `state=rest, status=error`), applied after the renames in `renameCoordinate`, claimed in `unaccounted`, and checked in `danglingTargets`, is the whole change. The update itself is untouched: it reads the ledger, and the status axis then already exists on the moved member, so the added-axis default skips it.

**Owner items (recommendations built, flagged for the owner):**
1. **The code prop is `validation`**, the field family's name, over `[default, error]`; the groups add `validationMessage`. For Switch row the value is an outcome failure (a change that did not take), not a validation result; the prop name is shared anyway, and its description says what `error` means there.
2. **The groups' message shows only at `error`** (`presentWhen`), so a valid group looks exactly as before. Showing the same part at `default` as group helper text is the deferred group `description` (#1698 decision 3), still the owner's.
3. **Prototype reactions now run on the error members** (Rest → Hover → Pressed at `status=error`, as at `default`): an errored control still responds to the pointer. Checkbox 18 → 36 sources (27 → 54 reactions), Radio 12 → 24 (18 → 36), Switch 8 → 16 (12 → 24).

**Tests:** `test.ts` `#2751` replaces the #1698 block with literals for all eight defs (no error state, the projected `status` axis, the `validation` prop, every row and group nest following `status`, each group's message present only at `error`), the #1433a fill-under-error arm now covering radio again, `#2751 renameCoordinate` / `renames lint` for the `move` kind, and `a11y(#2751)`: every control member at `status=error` and a non-disabled state draws `border.danger`, and that edge clears 3:1 against `background.primary` and `background.secondary` (4.5:1 in HC) in every corpus brand × mode, the floor the field status borders are held to. `test-update-apply.ts` `status/*`: a checkbox and a switch control set built the old way (with `state=error`, no `status`) update in place through the real ledger: every member renamed, ids and keys kept, the node a placed error instance points at now at `status=error, state=rest` and still drawing the danger edge, the set offering `status [default, error]` and no `state=error`, all members current after. Counts moved in `test-write-components.ts` (#1011, #1348, #1781, #1633) and `test-reactions.ts`.

**A trap for whoever re-verifies:** the shim's `createInstance` copies its main's name at creation and does not link the node, so `status/*` models a placed instance as Figma holds it, by its main's node identity, not through a shim instance. A Row placed in a file before this change, whose nested control was switched to `state=error` by hand, points at that same control member, so it rides the same rename. Whether Figma keeps that nested override when the Row's own update sets the control's `status` by `follow` is a real-host question (`notes.unverified` on the groups names the symptom).

marker-column section; the two are independent sections and both are kept.

**Merged `main` at `64949a01` (cloud lane, landing train 3).** #2765 (#2715) landed first with Radio group's sibling
tests, written against the size-only group. Its two literal arms now state this PR's shape, as checkbox-group's twin arm

## (2026-10-20) — Update on a published set lists what breaks library consumers; slot items stay unprefixed (#2831, Q394)

Items 1 and 2 of #2831. Item 3, the library publish description, waits for #2828's version naming.

- **The publish status is read, and it decides everything.** The Update check reads `getPublishStatusAsync()` on each set (`UNPUBLISHED | CURRENT | CHANGED`). A single-component def reads as its most published component. A set that is not published gets no `publish` field and no breaking list, so its preview and its hash are byte-for-byte what they were. That is the "nothing changes for unpublished sets" arm. A published set carries `publish` inside its hashed body, so publishing a set between the check and the confirm refuses the confirm.
- **What counts as breaking (`breakingOf`, pure, over what the dry run already lists):** a component property removed or retyped, a dropped member, a layer replaced rather than updated in place, and a set rename to a `_` or `.` name. A set the check blocks lists nothing, because the update changes nothing there. A replacement of the member itself is also left out, because the update refuses that member.
- **Where it shows.** A "Breaks library consumers" section in the check's lines, a clause on the check's headline (`· N changes break library consumers`), and the same section and clause in the confirm's verdict. The confirm takes the list from the check it applied. Each set's list is capped at `DIFFERENCE_LINES`, as its differences are, with the rest counted. The data payload carries every entry. All the wording is DRAFT and is posted to the owner on the PR.
- **A drop is not a delete.** The update keeps a dropped member and marks it deprecated (Q2), so a consumer instance keeps working. The line says what the consumer gets: an instance pointing at a deprecated member. Whether that counts as breaking is the owner's call. It is built as the issue asks, and the question is on the PR.
- **The rename arm reads `setRename`, which #2769 sets.** Nothing on main renames a set, so the field is declared here in #2769's exact shape and wording, and `breakingOf` reads it. When #2769 lands, its rename feeds the arm with no further change, because `breaking` is computed after every set's preview is complete. The test drives the arm by setting `setRename` on a real dry run read through the shim.
- **The shim models publishing.** `component-shim.ts` gives every COMPONENT and COMPONENT_SET a non-enumerable `getPublishStatusAsync` that answers `UNPUBLISHED` until a test calls `publish(node, status)`. That is the host's answer for a file never published, so every existing suite reads unpublished and is unchanged. The brief said "file shim", but `file-shim.ts` models variables and styles only. Nodes live in `component-shim.ts`.
- **Q394 on main, without `lint-naming`.** #2763 has not landed. `slotPreferredOf` already refuses a `_` id in a slot's `preferred` list at projection (`#2646 projection: a building block`). The gap is the sweep's own failure mode: a slot item renamed to `_…` with its slot's `preferred` dropped or renamed with it. `test.ts` now reads every native slot in the registry (`preferred`, `preferredWhenBuilt`, and what its default items nest) and refuses a `_` or `.` id by name. It asserts the three items the sweep renames are among those read. When `lint-naming` lands, this arm can move there.
- **Mutations, each failing by name.** In `test-update-apply.ts`: the publish test always true → `published/unpublished no-op`; each `breakingOf` arm dropped → `published/drop`, `/replace`, `/property removed`, `/retype`, `/private rename`; the status not read → `published/status`; the status left out of the hash → `published/hash`; the apply's section dropped → `published/confirm`. In `test.ts`: the prefix test dropped → `Q394 slot items: a prefixed item is refused`; the nests arm dropped → `Q394 slot items: a prefixed item the slot's default items nest is refused`.
- **Review fixes (2026-10-20).** Five stated behaviors no test pinned now each fail by name under a mutation: the blocked-set guard dropped → `published/blocked`; the member-itself exclusion dropped → `published/member replaced`; `readSingleView` carrying no status → `published/single` (the icon set, published component by component, CHANGED over CURRENT); the `.` arm of the Q394 prefix test dropped → `Q394 slot items: a .-prefixed item is refused too`; `preferredWhenBuilt` not read → `Q394 slot items: the registry's slot items are read` (Button Group's `button-neutral`).
- **Delta fix (2026-10-20).** `breakingSection`'s per-set cap (8 lines, then `tag: N more breaking changes not listed.`, Q435 A) is pinned against literals from the approved copy: the cap dropped, or the overflow wording changed → `published/cap`.

## (2026-10-20) — Component usage docs, phase 1: one doc section model, Markdown its first reader (#846)

**The decision.** The owner approved the usage docs wireframe on #846 (2026-10-19) and phased it: the
section model and Markdown parity first, the Figma panel second, the docs-site page third. This is the
first phase.

**The model.** `packages/engine/component-doc-sections.ts` is one pure function, `docSections(def, ctx)`,
that returns the ordered sections (Overview, Anatomy, Styles, Usage guidelines, Accessibility, Content
guidelines, Theming, Related components, Building it in code) with the wireframe's field map, and a list of
gaps. A section whose fields are all empty is not returned, so no surface can draw it. Theming has no def
field: it is drawn only when the caller passes the brand's modes, and the Markdown page is
brand-independent (#1701), so it passes none.

**Calls past the wireframe's table**, built as the recommendation and put to the owner on the PR: Props in
Building it in code, Motion inside Accessibility, the remaining composition lists in Related, the purpose
line in Overview, and `composition.planned` off the page (the wireframe already said so). Building it in
code will also read `docs.implementation` once Q362 is decided; until then every def lists it as a gap
and Button's do-items stay where they are.

**Anatomy captions.** The part `note` is the caption, but 64 of 219 notes are written for maintainers
(issue numbers, doc paths, section signs, code spans). Those parts are listed by name without a caption
and their notes go to `docGaps`, until the rewrite the owner split out. The classifier reproduces the
wireframe's per-def counts exactly. Four more notes name a tool (Figma), which consumer prose may not
(#2411); `lint-tool-neutral-prose` caught them on the first full run, and they are held back the same
way, with the reason `names a tool`.

**The page.** `emit-component-docs.ts` renders the model's sections in order and nothing else, so all 43
pages change shape. `components.ai.json` does not move. `schema/component-maintainer.json` gains each
def's `docGaps`. The stale "no reader" comment on `ComponentDef.content` is corrected (#846 finding 1).

**The gate.** `lint-component-docs.ts` keeps arms A to E with its section map moved to the new headings,
and gains arm F. `RULE`, written in the gate, names each section's title, its fields, when it is drawn
and how to empty it. F1 checks every field value reaches its own model section, F2 that the model draws
exactly the sections with data, in order, F3 that each section emptied on every def is not drawn and
comes back as a gap (the corpus alone has almost no empty section), F4 that each committed page's `##`

## (2026-10-20) — Contrast: primary and link inks clear 4.5:1 on every surface a component places them on (#2817, Q415 A, narrowed by Q419 A)

**What was measured.** The outline / text primary ink was gated on the page (`background.primary`) and the link on the page floor, yet components draw both on more: Dialog's panel (`foreground.primary`, the footer's Button group) and, once Banner (#2786) lands, a status tint (`foreground.<status>-subtle`, its actions). On `main` the primary ink measured 3.76:1 on `foreground.primary` and 3.30:1 on a tint (aurora light), and the regression fixture's link 4.02:1 on the success tint. High contrast already cleared.

**The surface set (Q419 A).** The first cut held the inks on all 11 grounds, the literal reading of Q415's "`foreground.*`". Review found no component places them on `background.secondary` / `.tertiary` or `foreground.secondary` / `.tertiary`, and `foreground.tertiary` alone drove most of the cost (ΔE 8–15 in both modes of nearly every brand). The owner narrowed the contract to the seven surfaces components place the inks on: `background.primary`, `foreground.primary` and the five `foreground.<status>-subtle` tints. This also resolves Banner's Q398. A consumer who puts these inks on another ground gets no promise; a def that does adds the ground.

**The fix, in `modes.ts`.** No new rule: `pickBrand`'s existing `alsoClear` (the semantic-ink and `border.tertiary` mechanism) now carries the seven grounds (`INK_SURFACES`) for the primary text pick and the page link pick. The anchor stays where it clears them all; otherwise the nearest step on the same ramp that does. `pickBrand` / `chromatic` gain a trailing `alsoMin`, because the page keeps the mode's own bar (7:1 in HC) while the other grounds are held to the 4.5:1 body floor the owner set. The inverse band's twins are not placed on these grounds and do not move.

**What moves.** Dark mode is unchanged except aurora's primary ink (accent 450 → 400). In light mode the inks move one step: aurora's primary 500 → 600 and link 550 → 600, the regression fixture 550 → 600, the second client fixture 500 → 550. harbor and prism3 do not move. The only HC value that moves is aurora's hc-light 3:1 icon link (550 → 600). The hover and pressed inks (and the link's hover, pressed and visited) walk from the new rest. `interactive.primary.icon.*` / `.border.*` share the ink's candidate (#1471, #576), and `icon.link.*` runs through the same link derivation. `nb-regression` compares ramps and band contracts, not these roles, so its report does not change.

**The gate, `test.ts` (10g-iv).** Five arms, measured from the resolved hexes against the seven grounds written there as literals, never `INK_SURFACES`:
- **Coverage, from the defs.** It walks every def's own fill on a ground over the defs it nests (fixed nests, slot offers, a host's `nestItemPrefers`) and finds where a primary or link ink lands: today `foreground.primary`, through Dialog. Any such ground missing from the literals fails by name. So does a literal no component places the inks on, other than the page and the five tints pending Banner (`PENDING_2817`). A pending tint missing from the literals fails too, so the list cannot narrow below the seven. When Banner lands, its tints move out of pending, and an arm says so by name.
- **Per cell.** One `ok` per brand × mode × ink × surface, so a miss names all four.
- **Followers.** The icon and border followers must equal the text ink's hex, state for state. The icon link must clear its brand's icon bar on the same grounds.
- **Same ramp.** The hue holds; only the depth moves.
- **Just enough.** In light and dark, where the primary rest ink or the link base left its anchor, the step one notch back misses somewhere.

**Mutations, each failing by name:** dropping all five tints from `INK_SURFACES` (the per-cell arm); restoring the 11 grounds (the "just enough" arm); pointing Dialog's panel at `foreground.secondary` (coverage: not in the list); adding `foreground.tertiary` to the gate's literals (coverage: no component places them there); and dropping one tint from the gate's literals (coverage: pending but not measured). Two subject mutations are true no-ops and are not counted as tests: dropping `foreground.primary`, or any single tint, from `INK_SURFACES` leaves every pick unchanged, because the remaining tints are as strict in every cell that moved.

**Existing expectations that moved, each because the ink did.**
- **The legacy Figma fixture.** Its light link rows gain `default` and `focused` (550 → 600), and `hover` and `visited` step one rung further (700, 900). Dark and HC rows are unchanged.
- **#1895.** The rebased-action deep link in light sits one notch past its anchor (550 → 600). The pale link in dark is unchanged.
- **#1614 / #1646.** The solid-tint example's page hover wash goes from 10 to 20. The deeper hover ink clears the standard step, so the down-step no longer engages on the page. The inverse rows still exercise it. The plugin's Apply Theme survival arm expects hover 0.2 on the page and 0.1 on the band.
- **#2661.** Its known-gap pin (aurora's primary fallback Cancel on Dialog's panel, light and dark) is flipped: every pair now clears its floor.

## (2026-10-20) — Group labels exposed: Checkbox group, Radio group and Segmented control (#2748, Q348 A)

**The decision.** Audit O4 on #2706 found three ways a form part nests FieldLabel: the four fields
`nest-exposed` (emphasis, weight) at secondary/regular, the three groups `nest-fixed` at
secondary/bold, and Counter (#2693, open) `nest-fixed` at secondary/regular. The owner chose A: the
groups expose emphasis and weight like the fields, and bold stays their default.

**The change is the nesting relation only.** Each group's `label` part moves from `nest-fixed` to
`nest-exposed` with `expose: ['emphasis', 'weight']`, keeping `follow: ['size']` and the same starting
coordinate (secondary, bold, rest). No group looks different. The projected surface moves (each plan's
label carries `nestExpose`), so `component-surface.json` is re-accepted under an `engine: minor`
note. No executor code moved: both executors already mark a `nest-exposed` instance exposed, on a
fresh build and in the in-place update branch, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

**Update, proved in the shim.** `test-update-apply.ts` gains a section per group: built from today's
def with the label put back to `nest-fixed`, then updated with today's plans. The dry run reads all
three members as updates, the apply keeps every key and every node id (the label included), each
label reads `isExposedInstance === true`, and the next dry run reads all three current.

**The trap in that test.** The section's first draft read the label's coordinate off
`mainComponent.name` and got `field-label`: in `world()` every nest target is a plain stub component,
so there is no member to read. The fix gives `world()` a `fileSets` option that puts FieldLabel's
real set in the file (its member names from `planComponentName`) and drops the stub of the same name.
With the stub left in, the executor kept instancing the stub.

**Mutations, each failing by name.** The in-place branch's expose pass skipped: `<group>/exposed` ×3
(plus each `/verdict`, which verify catches as `label.nestExpose: isExposedInstance=false`).
`checkbox-group`'s label back to `nest-fixed`: `checkbox-group/dry run`, `checkbox-group/exposed`, and
`lint-component-surface` DRIFTED. `radio-group`'s starting weight moved to regular:
`radio-group/bold kept`.

**The decision has a by-name pin of its own (review round 1).** `isExposedInstance` is all-or-nothing, so the shim
cannot see WHICH axes were listed, and the surface baseline is re-accepted with any change note, so it does not
remember them either. `test.ts` now holds each group's label to the decision, as Select's #1438 block does: typed
`nest-exposed`, `expose` = [emphasis, weight], `follow` = [size], starting weight bold. Mutation: Segmented control's
`expose` cut to `['emphasis']` → `❌ Q348 A segmented-control's label is nest-exposed: exposes [emphasis, weight],
follows [size], starts bold (got expose emphasis, follow size, weight bold)`.

**Delta round (merge of #2739).** The pin now holds the whole starting coordinate: a group label's starting
`emphasis` moved to primary used to pass `test.ts` (only the shim arm caught it), and now fails the same Q348 A line
by name. The merge with the Segmented control redesign had a trap in `test-update-apply.ts`: git matched the `}` the
`group labels` and `segmented control` sections share, so the `for` loop lost its closing brace. The brace is put
back by hand, and the surface baseline is re-accepted after regen.

**Follow-up.** Counter (#2693) should take the same shape when it lands; it is not edited here.

**Merge with #2660 (items slots).** Three conflicts were comment-only in the three defs (main's slot wording,
with the Q348 A clause put back), plus the `test-update-apply.ts` header and `world()` options (both kept), and the
generated report and surface baseline (main's, then regen and `--accept`). One real interaction showed up only in
`test.ts`. Once the groups' label is `nest-exposed`, the three defs join the `#1392 … runs CLEAN through the paste
payload` loop for the first time. That loop provisioned every nested target as a keyless plain component, so each
group's new `items` slot could not offer its preferred set and reported two misses. On main neither side alone
reached it. The loop now provisions a slot's preferred sets as keyed sets of their real members, as the real build
has them.

**Merge with #2693 (Counter).** One conflict, in `test.ts`'s `#1392` paste-payload loop. Main had widened that loop's

## (2026-10-20) — `ai.generationPriority` gets a written scale (#2713)

**What.** From the component consistency audit (#2706). `ai.generationPriority` is the agent's tiebreak between
candidate components, and the skill called each number "a judgment call", so each def's number was set alone: child-only
parts ranged from 2 to 9, and Focus ring sat at 2, level with Text field and Dialog. The skill now carries a scale table,
and the defs follow it.

| Priority | Tier | Defs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the default pick | Button |
| 2 | a top-level component | the field controls (Counter included), Button group, rows, groups, Tabs, Accordion, List, Link, Dialog, Icon, Button.Destructive and .Neutral, IconButton and .Neutral |
| 3 | a supporting top-level component, or a sibling that loses its family's tiebreak | Badge, Tag, Divider, Spinner, Veil, Image placeholder, IconButton.Destructive, Segmented control |
| 4–5 | a specialization for a narrower place | the flush icon buttons (Neutral 4, the others 5) |
| 6 | a part a host nests, alone only in a stated case | Checkbox, Radio and Switch controls, Field label, Field message, Focus ring |
| 9 | a part never generated alone | Tab, List item, the segment, the accordion indicator |

**How the order was kept.** Every relative order that read as intended stays: Button above its siblings, IconButton.Destructive
below the other two icon buttons, flush Neutral above flush primary and destructive, Segmented control below Tabs and
Radio group. What moved is the parts: nothing an agent should not generate on its own now ties with a top-level
component. Segmented control moves 4 → 3 because it is a top-level control, not a specialization of one; it still ranks
below the 2s it competes with. Counter moves 4 → 2 (merged from main with the tier list lacking it): it is a field
control, not a specialization of another def. Button group was already 2.

**The gate** (`#2713 generationPriority` in `test.ts`). A hand-written tier per def, so a number moving fails naming the
def; the list must name every registered def, so a new def has to choose its tier; a number off the scale fails; and a
def at 6 or 9 must be nested (`nests`) by another registered def, read from the hosts' anatomy, a fact independent of
the number.

**Owner item.** The scale is a judgment the issue proposed and left open to a comment. The 6 tier (a part that can stand
alone) is this PR's addition; it is posted as an Owner question on #2713 and built on.

## (2026-10-20) — The edit reveal anchors to the token's own card (#2832)

Editing a color on Surfaces & fills (for example `foreground.success-subtle`) pulled the preview back to the top of its section on every change. The cause was `revealSection`: it left the preview alone only when the section was wholly in view or filled the view, so a section scrolled partly past (its end on screen, as with the Subtle cards) was scrolled to its top on every edit.

- **Fix, `revealEdit` in `preview/follow-edit.ts`.** An edit on a lever that is one token's row now notes that token; the reveal targets that token's own card in the paired section, and does nothing when the card is already in view. Levers that are not a single token's row keep the section as the target, with the old wholly-visible and fills-the-view exceptions. A card out of view comes in a little under the body's top: at the section's top when the section is wholly off screen and the card still fits under it (so the earlier QA-B9 landings are unchanged), else at the card's own top.
- **Only a different lever moves the preview.** A further edit on the same lever, with the preview left where the last one put it, does nothing. If the viewer scrolled away in between, the next edit reveals again, which the existing Type checks hold (they scroll the preview home between edits on the same lever).
- **The plugin runs the same code.** `revealEdit` and the notes live in the studio's `preview/` and `shell/frame.ts`, and the plugin UI bundles that source, so the one fix covers both hosts.
- **Test:** a new `test:chrome` case (section 21b). It puts the Subtle success card mid-view with the Foreground section's top scrolled past, edits it three times and asserts the scroll position never moves and the card stays in view; then edits another lever whose card is off screen and asserts the preview moves to show it; then scrolls the preview away and asserts a further edit on that lever brings its card back. A second block edits Gradients, a lever with no card whose section is taller than the preview, twice and asserts the second edit issues no scroll at all. Mutations, each failing by name: the reveal back on the section's top fails `#2832: editing a Subtle foreground fill with its card in view does not move the preview` and `#2832: a second value change on the same lever leaves the preview where it was`; the `if (sameLever) return true;` line dropped fails `#2832: a second edit on a lever with no card never touches the preview`; `sameLever` reading the lever alone, without where the preview rests, fails `#2832: after the viewer scrolls the preview away, the next edit on the same lever brings its card back into view`.
