## (2026-10-20) — Container states are `[]`, and `codeOnly` admissions use one template (#2711)

**What.** From the component consistency audit (#2706). Two drifts, both settled one way and both gated.

1. **Containers with no state axis.** Checkbox group, Radio group, Tabs and Segmented control said `states: ['rest']`;
   twelve other components said `states: []`. `[]` wins: the schema's own instruction on `ComponentDef.states` and the
   validator's message both say `[]` for a component with no interaction of its own, it is the majority, and it does not
   claim a one-rung ladder the set never projects. `validateComponentDef` now refuses `['rest']` alone, and `test.ts`
   drives that on Checkbox group.
2. **The admission phrasing.** Every `codeOnly` entry that admits an unprojected axis or state now reads
   `<name> — not projected: <why Figma cannot carry it>. <what the code does>`. The `#2711 codeOnly admissions` block in
   `test.ts` holds it with three arms and a literal: an entry leading with a projected name is refused (the #867 trap),
   an admission off the template is refused, a template entry naming something the set projects or does not declare is
   refused, and the 27 admissions found must equal a hand-written list.

**Why the gate is in `test.ts` and not in `admits()`.** The plugin build cuts every `codeOnly` entry to its leading term
(`apps/plugin/strip-maintainer-prose.mjs`), and `figmaPropertyErrors` runs in the plugin on those cut entries. Tightening
`admits()` to demand `— not projected:` would have refused every admission in the bundle. So the template is checked on
the source defs, and `admits()` keeps reading the leading term only.

**A live #867 instance, found by arm 1.** Dialog's codeOnly entry `placement per breakpoint, no automatic switch — …` led
with `placement`, an axis Dialog projects, so `admits('placement')` returned true: dropping `placement` from
`variantAxes` would have passed the validator. It now leads with `per-breakpoint placement`.

**Out of scope, noted.** The control atoms' `read-only — deliberately not a state of this atom` (checkbox, radio, switch)
and switch-control's `pending —` lead with names the atom does not declare, so they admit nothing and the gate leaves them
alone; they say a different thing (absent, not unprojected). #2660 rewrites the four containers but not their `states`
line, so this change and it touch different lines.

## (2026-10-20) — One status order on every studio surface (#2833)

The studio listed the statuses three ways: the preview's Foreground, Text color, Icon and Border sections ran brand, danger, success, warning, info; the Foreground fills lever ran brand, success, warning, info, danger; the text, border and icon levers ran brand, success, warning, danger, info. The engine's `SEMANTICS` (`modes.ts`) is brand, success, warning, danger, info, and the emitted `text`, `icon`, `border` and inverse groups follow it, so that is the one order; no owner decision was needed. The preview's `SEM`, the Foreground fills lever's `SEM` and the preview's Icon and Border card lists now agree with it. The Icon and Border sections read `SEM` instead of restating the five names, so the preview has one source.

- **New gate, `apps/studio/test-status-order.ts`** (wired into the studio `test` script, so CI already runs it). The canonical order is a literal in the gate, checked against the committed emission's key order, then against the studio's row lists and `SEM` as built. Each row pattern (`foreground.*`, `foreground.*-subtle`, `text.on-*` and the rest) must be present and is named, so a dropped pattern fails rather than passing empty. Mutations: danger second in the preview's `SEM` fails `preview: SEM lists the statuses in the canonical order`; info before danger in the levers' `SEM` fails `levers: foreground.* rows list the statuses in the canonical order`.
- **One named exception, filed as #2836.** The emitted `color.foreground` group lists `danger` after the subtle tints. Reordering it moves every brand's emitted key order, so it is left alone and the gate records it as the exception; when it is fixed the exception's own assertion fails and says to delete it.
- Not touched: the Badge component's variant order (`info, success, warning, danger`) is the component's own API enum, and `STATUS_ROLES` (success, warning, danger, info) is already the canonical order without brand.
- The `test-smoke` and `test-chrome` literals that spelled the preview's old order now spell the canonical one.

## (2026-10-20) — Style guides: Inverse colors is its own group below Semantic colors, never clipped, never overlapping (#2810, #2818)

The owner ran the style-guide command on a real file after #2818. The semantic-tokens page showed three faults. The eight inverse guides sat in a second row inside the owner's own Semantic colors frame. That frame was a horizontal auto layout fixed at 15,160 wide that clips, so the 15,676-wide grid lost its right column (Field / Inverse field). The frame also grew from about 4,700 to 9,175 tall and ran over the owner's Borders and Fonts frames just below it. The owner decided that inverse colors get a parent frame of their own, directly below the defaults, each inverse guide under its default's column. Record: `docs/45-style-guide-generator.md`, "Decided (2026-10-19)".

- **Engine table.** `style-guide-groups.ts` gains Inverse colors (`under: 'semantic-colors'`), and Semantic colors loses `inverseRow`. `styleGuideGroupOf` reads a new `inverse` fact. That fact is structural, an `inverse` path segment, not a family name. Patch note: no emission moves.
- **Plugin.**
  - **The split.** An earlier build's second-row inverse guides move out into Inverse colors, and the grid closes to one row. A one-row or loose hand-made Semantic colors gets a one-row grid of its defaults, once, so the inverse guides have columns to sit under.
  - **Alignment, every run.** Inverse colors goes 320 below that frame, its grid's left edge on the defaults' grid's. The two grids share their gap and each shared column's FIXED width, the wider guide's. Columns are re-derived from the counterparts each run, so they follow a reorder or a close.
  - **Never clipped.** A FIXED frame that holds guides grows to fit, stays FIXED, and never shrinks.
  - **Never overlapping.** A frame the run changed pushes what it runs over, below it, down with everything beneath, keeping order and gaps. A group placed under another counts "below" from that other's bottom edge. A frame beside it, clear to its right before the run, moves right by a width growth instead, keeping its gap, and a group placed under another is never pushed: it follows its anchor, so a rerun moves nothing (review of `4be045f4`).
- **Why the overlap rule is generic.** #2818's push-down moved only frames Prism3 had placed, which is exactly why the owner's hand-made Borders and Fonts were run over. The new rule moves any top-level frame, but only one below a frame that changed this run, so a page nobody touched is never re-laid.
- **Trap for the re-verifier: the shim's auto-layout x.** The test shim now lays out an auto layout's in-flow children's x: left padding, then the widths and spacing before it, start-aligned. The column-alignment checks read every left edge off that model and the grid's track model, never off the plugin's arithmetic (the plugin reads the host's `x` chain). Before this, an auto-layout child's x read whatever was last written, so the alignment checks would have been circular.
- **Decided.** The title is "Inverse colors" (owner decision Q423 A).
- **Held.** What a frame beside a grown frame does is posted as an owner question on the PR; its recommendation, moving it right by the growth with its gap kept, is what is built. Removing the retired legacy Inverse table still waits on the owner's confirm (#2818), and a run does not move it.

## (2026-10-20) — Component tests: radio group, link, tabs, list item and the accordion indicator carry their siblings' test kinds (#2715)

**What moved.** Tests only; no def changes. #2715 (from the #2706 consistency audit) listed defs missing a kind of test that a direct sibling carries. This PR covers the five the issue's title names:
- **Radio group** gets checkbox group's block. It checks set size (three members, one per size), per-member nesting (one FieldLabel, secondary/bold/rest, then an items slot (at least one, preferred-only Radio.Row, stretched) holding three Radio.Rows following the size, none behind a boolean, per #2649), that rows are nest-fixed and never the control atom, and the group → row → control → ring chain.
- **Link** gets paint, nesting and measured contrast. The label ink on all 96 members comes from the link ramp, by state, and from the inverse ramp on an inverse surface. The link box paints nothing. A focus ring appears only on the 24 focus-visible members and follows the surface. All 8 link inks clear 4.5:1 on their own ground in all 16 brand × mode cells.
- **Tabs** gets its own paint arm. The baseline is the only node Tabs paints, as a `color/border/primary` fill. Measured: the selected bar beats the baseline's contrast against the page in all 16 cells.
- **List item** joins `test-roundtrip.ts`'s owner-decided text-style table. It is built by the real executor and its text (and an ordered item's number) is read off the host in the body style of its size.
- **Accordion indicator** gets a build test in `test-roundtrip.ts`: 12 members, each one icon instance (the Q183 glyph for its indicator and expansion) in a frame bound to the icon size of its rung.

**Independence.** Every expected value is a literal from the brief or the owner decision the def cites. The plan and the built shim are only ever the actual. The contrast arms read the committed Figma exports and name all 16 cells, so a missing export fails the arm instead of shrinking it. One literal I first guessed wrong was the radio group's member *order*. Order is not a design fact, so the arm compares the set of names, not their sequence.

**No defect found.** Every new arm passed on first run against main, apart from that order guess. Nothing is marked with an issue.

**Left for a follow-up.** The issue's other two rows are filed separately: measured contrast for dialog, divider, accordion, list item and field label, and prose checks for the icon buttons, field label and field message. So is its suggestion of a "tests a new def owes" checklist in the build-component skill.

## (2026-10-20) — Naming sweep PR 1: the naming table in the build-component skill, and `lint-naming.ts` (#2759, owner decisions Q345, Q349, Q350, Q355, Q394)

**What moved.** `skills/prism3-build-component/SKILL.md` §6 has a naming table: a root is named for its role from a closed list and never the def's id, main text is `label`, a glyph layer is `<shape>Glyph`, and a Row's control cell is `controlCell`. It also states the `_` prefix rule (a part that should not be used outside its parent takes it; a slot's preferred item and the checkbox and radio controls are exempt) and the casing rule (Figma property names are lowercase). §2's stale list of root names is replaced by a pointer to the table (audit item S1). `packages/engine/lint-naming.ts` is a new CI gate that checks every rule except main text.

**No def changed.** The renames come in PRs 2–4 of #2759, one kind each. The gate finds 22 breaches on `main` today: 4 property names (PR 2) and 18 layer names (PR 4). PR 3's one rename (`tab` → `tab-item`) breaches no rule this gate reads. Each is listed in the gate's `PENDING` ledger with the PR that clears it. A breach not listed fails by its arm's name. A listed entry that no longer breaches fails as `stale`, so the ledger cannot keep an entry the defs have outgrown.

**Why the rules are literals.** Each arm's expected value comes from the owner's rule, typed in the gate: `name.toLowerCase()`, the role list, the `Glyph` suffix, the `controlCell` name, and the two private-part wordings. Nothing is read off the defs, which are the subject (`docs/34` shape 1). The ledger is a waiver, never the oracle. The root list, the owner's prefixed set and the exempt controls are written twice, in the gate and in the skill's §6, so a sixth arm (`skill`) parses §6 and fails if either copy moves without the other.

**How the prefix rule is read.** "Should not be used outside its parent" is read off `ai.whenToUse`, which says it as "Never directly …" for the accordion indicator, the owner's one prefixed def. Both directions are checked: the wording without the prefix, and the prefix without the wording. The owner's set is a floor: each id must be registered (or be the target of a pending rename) and must be detected by the wording, so rewording a whenToUse to slip the rule fails. Radio row's "Always as a child of a Radio.Group" matches neither wording, and Q355 leaves it out of the set. That call is raised on #2759 as Q-N1.

**Slot items stay unprefixed (Q394 A, #2783).** The tab, the list item and the segmented-control segment are each a native slot's preferred item. Figma does not publish a `_` set, so a `_` slot item would offer nothing to insert in a file that uses the library (#2831). A seventh arm, `slot item`, reads every content slot's `preferred` and `preferredWhenBuilt` and fails by name if any of them names a `_` id. The prefix arm does not ask a slot item for the prefix, even though their `whenToUse` says "Only as a child of …". `SLOT_ITEMS` is the owner's list and a floor: each must be registered, unprefixed and offered by a slot. It is also parsed from §6.

**Main text is not checked.** Which text part is the main one is a judgment (a dialog has a title and a description), not a field. FieldLabel's root is already `label`, so its main text cannot also be `label` without a root rename. That is raised as Q-N3 with a recommendation.

**Liveness.** A self-check feeds each rule a known breach and a known pass. A floor asserts that the walk saw property names (226, the state axes included), every root, glyph layers (17), control cells (3), private defs by wording (4) and slot items (8). Mutations are recorded in the PR.

**What moved.** Text field, Password field (through the shared field factory), Select and Textarea each nest FieldLabel and used to fix it at `state=rest` on every member, recording the gap in `codeOnly` as a projection limit. Each now carries `variantWhen: { state: { disabled: { state: 'disabled' } } }` on its `label` part, so the label nests FieldLabel's disabled member on the field's 12 disabled members (size 3 × status 4) and its rest member everywhere else. Read-only keeps a full-contrast label, as it keeps a full-contrast value. The four `codeOnly` entries are gone, and `SHARED_CODE_ONLY` in `test.ts` drops the subject.

## (2026-10-19) — The DTCG `figma.scope` hint on font size and weight agrees with the Figma rows (#2736)

**What changed.** `packages/engine/tree.ts` no longer writes `$extensions.prism3.figma.scope` on the `core.font.size.*`
leaves (`fontSizeLeaf`, was FONT_SIZE) or the numeric `core.font.weight.*` leaves (`fontWeightLeaf`, was FONT_WEIGHT).
Their Figma rows carry `scopes: []` (size since #2602, the numeric weights since #2616, Q334 A), so the hint named a
scope no row had. The family leaves keep FONT_FAMILY and the fluid type composites keep FONT_SIZE, both of which their
rows still carry. Every emitted `*.tokens.json` moves (the five DTCG trees); no path or value does. Engine `minor`.

**Stacked on #2743**, which unscopes the numeric weights. On `main` alone the weight hint was still true, so the two
halves of this issue only agree with the emission once #2743 lands; stacking keeps the hint and the row in one state.

**The call made.** "Agree with the emission" and "drop the field" come out the same here: `figma.scope` is a single
string, and a string cannot say "none", so agreement for an unscoped row is the field's absence. The alternative, an
array `scopes` mirroring the Figma row on every font leaf, would rename a shipped field on the family leaves too; it is
listed as an owner item on the PR rather than built.

**Gate.** New arm (23c) in `test.ts`: for nb and every committed brief, each DTCG `core.font.{family,size,weight}` leaf
with a Figma row is compared, by path, to the `core` Default row from `figmaArtifacts`: `[figma.scope]`, or `[]` when
absent, must equal the row's `scopes`. Two independent writers (`tree.ts` and `emit-figma-font.ts`), and each group
must be represented per brand, so an empty match fails by name. Mutations: `scope: 'FONT_SIZE'` back on the size leaf →
`#2736 every DTCG core.font leaf's figma.scope …` fails (`… row scopes=[]`); `fontNode[g]` read from a wrong key →
`#2736 sweep floor` fails.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies.** `typeface` primitives also carry `figma.scope: 'FONT_FAMILY'` with `kind:
'style-part'` and have no Figma row of their own, so the arm skips them rather than comparing; the hint there describes
the style part, not a variable.

## (2026-10-19) — A refused property is a miss, a refused structure stops the set (#982)

Owner decision on #982 (triage Q319.2, a technical call delegated to engineering): a refused PROPERTY write is a miss and the member keeps building; a refused STRUCTURE call stops the member or set. The rule is recorded above `applyComponentPlan` in `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts`, with its one-line classifier: "does the node I am writing to still exist, whole, after this fails?"

- **Code that moved.** Three property sites propagated and now record: the `setBoundVariable` field loop (one refused binding used to end a 648-member build), `setTextStyleIdAsync`, and `setEffectStyleIdAsync`. A refused binding is not pushed to `wrote`, so the read-back does not also report a write that never landed; a refused text style leaves `appliedStyle` unset, so the #1567 re-apply does not retry it. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 32 → 33. Structure calls (`createFrame`/`createText`/`appendChild`, `createComponentFromNode`, `combineAsVariants`) are untouched and still reach the #913 guard.
- **Two older pins moved with it, deliberately.** The #680 pin ("a brand whose typeface is not installed loses the WHOLE component build") was written as the assertion that would invert once the style apply was guarded; it now asserts the build finishes and reports both the font load and the style apply. #913's small regime used that same missing-typeface throw to reach a mid-build failure, so it now drives a refused `createText` instead (a structure call, the class that still stops). Its assertions read the host and are unchanged.
- **A third pin used the same throw.** `test-update-apply.ts` "stop" stopped a run with a refused `setBoundVariable`. It now throws from `unlockAspectRatio` (called on every node, unclassified by the rule), which keeps its meaning — a host stop part-way — without leaning on the property class.
- **Pinned by name.** `test-write-components.ts` `#982` arms drive a host that refuses one call: `setBoundVariable` and `setTextStyleIdAsync` must finish with a REFUSED miss; `createText` and `combineAsVariants` must throw. The shim gained `refuse.createText`, `refuse.setBoundVariable` (by field), `refuse.setTextStyleId` and `refuse.setEffectStyleId`.
- **Review round.** The `#982` block moved above the #913 regimes so its STRUCTURE arms run under the mutation they are named for (they were unreachable behind #913's crash). The effect-style site is pinned with the #1007 probe plan, and each refused field is asserted to yield exactly one miss per member with no `DISCARDED` / `could not be re-applied` line. The rule, classifier and unclassified sites are recorded in `docs/32-component-build-learnings.md`.
- **Not decided here.** `resize`, `setBoundVariableForPaint` and the paint-array assignments were not reclassified: `resize` clears every dimension binding (a known blast radius) and the paint sites need their own host model. Neither is a structure call, so under the rule they are properties; moving them is a follow-up with its own measurement (#2824), not part of this concern.

## (2026-10-19) — Counter: a quantity between a minus and a plus button, nesting the flush icon button (#2427, owner decisions Q283, Q286 A, Q287 A)

**Status:** one new def, `counter` (Counter), plus a small schema field, `variantWhen` on nest relations, and gates. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no new token. No executor change (the plan carries the resolved nested coordinate, as it always has), so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays where main has it. One new docs page, so the artifact count moves by one in `verify.ts` and `ci.yml` together.

**What it is.** `appearance` [outline, ghost] × `size` [medium, small, large] × `state` [rest, focus-visible, disabled] = 18 members, on its own page under Components (Q283.14 A), alphabetical between Checkbox and Divider.
- The row is the Counter's height, `size.sm` / `md` / `lg.height` (36 / 44 / 56), which is the round flush icon button's diameter (Q287 A).
- Outline: the field's fill and edge (`color.field.fill`, `color.field.border.rest`, `radius.sm`), insets 12 / 12 / 16 (Q283.13 A). Ghost: no box paint, inset 0.
- The minus and plus: two nested FlushIconButton.Neutral instances, each `nest-exposed` with `state`, following `size`.
- The value: a text node in `type.body.{sm,md,lg}.default`, centered in a box at least 32 wide (Q283.13 A), text property `value`, default "1".
- The label (FieldLabel) is hidden by default (Q283.9 B); the message (FieldMessage) is off by default.
- The focus ring wraps the whole row: the field offset on outline, the control offset (2px) on ghost (Q283.10 A).
- Accessibility (Q283.8 A, Q286 A): the value is one element with `role="spinbutton"` and the only Tab stop (it is displayed, not typed, so not an `<input>`); the buttons are `tabindex="-1"` with `aria-controls`, and `aria-disabled` at a limit; a press announces through the app's shared polite live region.

**The open shape question, answered without a new question.** The wireframe comment asked how B's round buttons map onto #2457's flush button. #2457 settled it after that comment, by Q287 A: one component with `shape: flush | round`, "the Counter's outlined appearance nests flush, its ghost appearance round". So the mapping is one-to-one and needed no owner question.

**Why a schema field.** `follow` passes a value through by NAME, and the Counter's `appearance=ghost` must nest `shape=round`, a different axis with different values. Two other routes existed:
- Two nests per side, each gated by `presentWhen` on `appearance`. That is four nest parts, and the disabled member (below) would double it to eight.
- A flat `appearance` → `shape` rename. That contradicts Q283.4 A, which named the axis.

So `variantWhen` maps a host value to a partial child coordinate, merged between the fixed `variant` and `follow`. The same field fixes a second gap: **the disabled Counter starts both nested buttons at `state=disabled` and dims the nested FieldLabel.** Text field, Select and Password field still record the label's dimming as a projection limit ("the nested label reads at its rest configuration regardless"); with `variantWhen` that limit can now be lifted, filed as #2738 rather than widened into this PR. On a `nest-exposed` part the mapped axis may be an exposed one: the mapping sets the value the instance starts at on that member, and the designer still drives it.

The validator refuses six shapes, each a way to validate and never fire or fire and be overwritten:
- an unprojected host axis;
- an undeclared host value;
- an empty map;
- a child axis also in `follow` (follow runs after, so the mapping would read as working and never land);
- one child axis set from two host axes (declaration order would decide).
- a child axis the fixed `variant` does not name (the moved coordinate must still name every axis of one member; this rule came over from `atState`).

**One field, not two (merge with #2317).** The Password field landed `NestingRelation.atState` while this PR was in review: a host state value → a nested coordinate, applied after `follow`, refusing an axis that is followed or exposed. That is `variantWhen` keyed on `state`, with two rules that disagreed with this PR's. Keeping both would have left one type with two mapping fields and one `nestVariantOf` with two merge orders. `variantWhen` is the general form, so `atState` is gone and the Password field says `variantWhen: { state: { disabled: { state: 'disabled' } } }`. The Password field's projected plan digest is unchanged (`lint-component-surface` accepts only the Counter as moved), and its three refusal cases in `test.ts` now drive `variantWhen` on the Password field.
- **Order** is moot: the validator keeps a mapped child axis out of `follow`, so the two are disjoint and land the same either way.
- **Exposed axes** stay allowed, where `atState` refused them. A followed axis is the host's to drive at every member, so a mapping onto it is overwritten. An exposed axis is the consumer's after the instance is placed: the plan only picks the member it is placed at, which `variant` already does for every exposed axis, and the exposed property overrides it from there. Nothing is driven two ways at once.

**Counts on the merged tree.** This PR and #2317 each moved `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` 199 → 200 and the canvas-furniture count to 39 from different bases, and git took both lines cleanly. The merged tree emits both `counter.md` and `password-field.md`, so the artifact count was **201** (in `verify.ts` and `ci.yml` together) and the canvas furniture covers **40** sets. Main then moved it twice more: #2685 stopped committing `out/tokens.html` (main 199, this PR 200), and #2701 added `docs/public/reference/figma-conventions.json` (main 200, this PR **201** again, and that file now lists the Counter). Trap: a count both sides bump by one from different bases merges silently to the wrong number. The same merge produced a second silent collision: #2317 added its own `FLUSH_NESTS` to `lint-hit-target.ts`, a `Set` of hosts of a nested flush *Button* (they state the code-side rule in `codeOnly`), while this PR's `FLUSH_NESTS` is a `Record` of hosts of code-side *icon-button* targets (their center spacing is measured). Git merged both declarations cleanly and the gate failed to compile. They are different rules, so #2317's is renamed `FLUSH_BUTTON_HOSTS`, with its two messages; the Password field's pending fragment still says `FLUSH_NESTS` for it, and is left as written.

The projector change is three lines in `nestVariantOf`. No executor reads `variantWhen`: both read the plan's `nestVariant`, as before.

**The hit area.** There was no rule for a host that nests code-side targets. `lint-hit-target.ts` gains `FLUSH_NESTS`. #2457 had the nest arm treat a code-side target as needing an `INNER_TARGETS` entry, but that loop measures a part's side against the 44 floor and skips any part that nests a non-INTERACTIVE def. So an entry there would have been demanded and then measured by nothing. `FLUSH_NESTS` does three things:
- It lists each host's code-side nest parts, both ways against the anatomy.
- It measures each listed pair's center-to-center spacing off the projected plans on the comfortable build, against Q296 A's 44px literal. The measure is a lower bound: half of each nested box, plus each frame between at its minimum width and inline padding, plus the row's gaps. The Counter reads 60px at its tightest member (outline, small and medium: 10 + 4 + 32 + 4 + 10).
- A self-check drives the representation function both ways.

The Counter's row itself is INTERACTIVE on `size.{size}.height` (44 at medium on comfortable and spacious). `test-roundtrip.ts` measures the same spacing on the host shim's layout model, so the claim has a host-side ACTUAL too (closest 54px over the 18 members).

**A name collision, recorded for the owner.** The KB's badge brief lists "Counter" as an alias for a count badge, a number shown on another element. `test.ts`'s no-brief arm matched the Counter to that brief by alias and failed it. The name is owner-approved with the quantity meaning, so the arm admits that one collision by name (`ALIAS_COLLISIONS`), and the Counter's `ai.avoidWhen` and `docs.dont` send a count badge to Badge. An agent asked for "a counter" can still mean either; the trigger keywords lean on quantity.

**The glyphs, now that #2683 is on main.** The minus and plus are the nested buttons' icon swap, written as a per-instance override on each part: `overrides: { swaps: { icon: 'minus' } }` and `'plus'`. The first host to swap a glyph on a NEST-EXPOSED child surfaced a gap in `test.ts`'s `#1392` paste-payload harness: it gave nested instances their text properties (#2317) but no swap properties, so both overrides read as misses. The harness now declares each nested def's own swaps (from the nested def, never from the host's `overrides`), and provisions the glyph components the overrides name, as the real build does.

**Three more places that missed a swap override's glyph.** (Superseded on main by #2808, which taught the same three readers for Dialog's `icon/close`; the merge with `74056387` takes main's code for all three.) The first verify run after the merge found two more readers that walked `nestTarget` and `swapTarget` but not #2645's override glyphs, which `build-deps.ts`'s `planTargets` already counts:
- the studio's component catalog (`catalogOf`), whose `nests` for the Counter left out `icon`, so `test-component-catalog` disagreed with the plugin's pre-build. The walk now reads INSTANCE_SWAP overrides too, and the catalog data is regenerated.
- `test-update-apply.ts`'s `planComps`, so the corpus world held no `icon/minus` and the Counter's re-applied members never read back as current. List carries text overrides only, which is why it had not come up.
- `test-canvas-furniture.ts`'s `planComps`, the same gap: its `rollout/counter` dry run reported "components the plan swaps to are not in this file: icon/minus, icon/plus".

**`EXECUTOR_REVISION`: main's value since the merge with `74056387`.** This PR moves no executor file, so it takes main's 32 and raises nothing. The paragraph below is the history. **It was 28, raised on the orchestrator's instruction, not because the gate asks for it.** Against main `039a65c3` (27, #2744), `lint-executor-revision` reads "the executor's code is unchanged since the merge base": `variantWhen` is projector-only, and the Counter's `file-taxonomy.ts` page entry is not on the executor's import graph. The failure it printed during the first merge was against the old merge base, before the merge commit existed. The raise costs one dry run that marks members built at 27 as "to update" with no field difference. Dropping it back to 27 is a one-line revert, and the gate would still pass.

**Gates (each mutation-proven by name, see the PR):**
- `test.ts`, the Counter's decisions against literals:
  - `#2427 counter/axes`
  - `/nests`: outline → flush, ghost → round, disabled only on the disabled members
  - `/row`: 36 / 44 / 56; insets 12 / 12 / 16 and 0; value 32 wide
  - `/paint`: ghost paints no box; the outline disabled edge
  - `/ring`: the ghost ring at the control offset
  - `/label`: hidden by default
  - `/api`: min 0, `tabindex="-1"`, no remove prop
- `test.ts` `#2427 variantWhen`: each of the eight refusals fires on its own case (the follow-overlap fixture states its own `follow`; the no-values and empty-coordinate cases came in the second delta check), and the Counter validates clean.
- `test.ts` `#2427 counter/label-dims`: the nested FieldLabel's coordinate on every member, disabled only on the Counter's disabled members (added in review; it was held only by the roundtrip and the surface digest).
- `test-roundtrip.ts` `#2427 counter`: built over its really built nested sets with 0 misses. In every member both instances are exposed instances of the decided FlushIconButton.Neutral member. The FieldLabel dims on the 6 disabled members. The spacing is read off the host layout. Two arms added in the second delta check: each button's swap property reads back as `icon/minus` / `icon/plus`; and the Counter's members carry no reaction while the nested FlushIconButton.Neutral set carries exactly what `reactionMap` plans for it. That arm reads the chain from `reactions.ts` on purpose, so it holds under #2703's chain and under Q344's restored one (#2744) with no edit. The chain's literal stays in `reactions read-back`.
- `lint-hit-target.ts`: `FLUSH_NESTS` and the INTERACTIVE row.
- `test-file-setup.ts`: the page's alphabetical place.
- `lint-absolute-inset.ts` now fills any `{axis}` in an inset key from the member's coordinate, where it filled only `{size}`. The Counter keys its ring offset by `{appearance}`. `counter.focusRing` is in `MUST_COVER` and `MUST_CLEAR_STROKE`. `ZERO_OK` admits the outline members' field offset; the ghost offset is held in `test.ts`, because a ghost member rebound to the field offset would be admitted there.
- List entries:
  - `lint-rung-names` (`MUST_COVER`, and `DEFAULT_FIRST` for medium first, Q283.6 B)
  - `lint-axis-values` (the medium-first size set; a new `appearance` set, `overlapping`)

  - the studio's `used-by.ts` and component catalog
  - both baselines accepted
- `lint-nesting.ts` gains `nest-coordinate-resolves`: every nested instance a projected member asks for names exactly one member of the nested def's own projected set, matched with the executors' `nestVariantMatch`. It covers the whole corpus (1,410 coordinates), and it is where a `variantWhen` mapping onto a value the child lacks fails, per member. It has no per-def list, so the Counter needed no entry beyond being registered.

**Trap for whoever extends `variantWhen`:** the projector applies the mapping from `paintCoord`, which carries the grid axes, `state` and `size`. A mapping keyed on an axis the def does not project would never fire, which is why the validator holds it to `variantAxes` ∪ `state`, as `follow` is held.

**The merge with main `74056387` (27 commits).** 21 files conflicted. The semantic ones:
- **`atState` came back on main with a new reader.** #2660's items-slot check in `anatomy-figma.ts` refused a nested item carrying `atState`. ## (2026-10-19) — `packages/engine/package.json` no longer claims to track `ENGINE_VERSION` (#1019)

Owner decision on #1019 (triage Q319.2): delete the claim rather than keep it and add a gate. The `"//"` note said "Version tracks ENGINE_VERSION in version.ts" while `"version"` sat at `0.5.0`, 18+ minors behind, with nothing comparing the two.

- **What changed.** The note now says the field is inert: npm requires it, nothing reads it (`@prism3/engine` is consumed by workspace name, and the package has no build, #650), and `ENGINE_VERSION` is the only version that means anything. The `"version": "0.5.0"` value is left alone: it is not a claim once the note stops calling it one, and rewriting it would move the lockfile for no reader.
- **The gate.** `test.ts` reads the note off the file and fails `#1019 packages/engine/package.json claims its version tracks ENGINE_VERSION…` if a "tracks"/"version" pair comes back. The subject is the file's own prose and the pattern is authored here, so mutating either side fails it by name (checked: re-adding the old sentence fails exactly that assertion). It guards the claim, not the number, which is the point of choosing delete over sync.
- **Not touched.** `docs/inventory/surfaces.*` still list the drift; they are a snapshot by their own header. No `ENGINE_VERSION` bump: no committed artifact moves, so there is no engine change note.

## (2026-10-18) — Button.Group: the Dialog footer as a shared button group, Cancel falling back to the primary Button (#2661, Q363)

Builds the owner-approved wireframe on #2661 (Q363: every call A except 8 → C and 9 → B), with the 2026-10-16
amendment of call 8 and Q386 (#2808): no component requires the Neutral button families.

### What shipped

- **Button.Group** (`button-group`), public, category `form`, no KB brief. One `layout` axis, inline | stacked | fill,
  three members. Its content is a native `items` slot: one to three buttons, two by default, preferred-only. Inline is
  Cancel then Save at the end edge, 12px apart; stacked is Save over Cancel, full width, 8px apart (Q363.5 A); fill is
  Cancel then Save sharing the width, 12px apart. The buttons read "Cancel" and "Save" through #2645's overrides. It
  joins the Button family's page (Buttons), so the plugin's Components list shows it in that family.
- **Dialog** nests it: a `footer` box (padded like the header) holds `actionsInline` (layout=inline) or `actionsStacked`
  (layout=stacked). The old `footerInline`/`footerStacked` boxes, their four nested Buttons and the two footer gap
  tokens are gone. `actions` is now a slot prop of one to three Button elements (Q363.10 A).

### The mechanisms, and why each is its own field

- **The host decides the secondary (Q418).** Button.Group on its own makes Cancel the outline primary Button and prefers
  nothing. Dialog's nests of the group prefer Button.Neutral for the group's Cancel through `nestItemPrefers` (below),
  falling back to the primary Button; Banner, Card and later hosts declare their own. The first cut put
  `prefersWhenBuilt` on the group's Cancel; Q418 moved it to the host.
- **`nestItemPrefers` on a nest (→ `nestItemPrefer` on the plan).** The smallest mechanism that carries a preference
  through a nest of a nest. The group's default buttons are instances inside the group, so a host cannot reach them
  with `prefersWhenBuilt`, which replaces the component an in-flow instance is made from. `nestItemPrefers: { cancel:
  'button-neutral' }` names a `nest-fixed` anatomy part of the nested def and a sibling set that takes its coordinate
  (the projection checks it with the same `nestPreferOf` as `prefersWhenBuilt`, and refuses a part the nested def lacks,
  one that is not such a nest, and the item's own component). Once the nested instance exists, both executors resolve the
  sibling's member at the item's coordinate (`resolveNestMember`, shared) and `swapComponent` the one instance of that
  layer name inside it, through one shared writer, `applyNestItemPrefers`. No set in the file: the item stays the primary
  Button, no miss. Two sets, or no member: named once per instance, and the item stays. It is not `nests` or `nestTarget`,
  so `build-deps.ts` and the #2808 gate's readings never count it. The paste payload splices the writer in only for a
  payload whose plans carry it, so no other set's chunk count moves.
- **`prefersWhenBuilt` on a nest (→ `nestPrefer` on the plan)** stays in the schema for a part that nests a component
  directly, but no def uses it now. Both executors resolve the preferred set's member at the same coordinate first and fall back to `nestTarget` with
  no miss when the file has no such set; a set of that name that cannot yield the member (two copies) is named once
  per instance and still falls back. It is not `nestTarget`, so `build-deps.ts` never builds it first and the #2808
  gate's two readings never count it; the projection refuses a preferred set whose coordinates differ from the nested
  one's. The read-back accepts an instance of either set.
- **`preferredWhenBuilt` on a slot.** The slot requires the primary Button and offers Button.Destructive and
  Button.Neutral only when the file has them, with no miss otherwise (a missing `preferred` def stays a named miss).
  Destructive moved here too: no default button uses it, and a fresh Dialog build would otherwise report it. The
  read-back accepts any in-order subset of these.
- **`directionWhen` on a box.** A native slot is one SLOT property per part name, so a designer's buttons survive a
  layout switch only if all three members share the one `items` part. Its direction is resolved per member at
  projection (`directionAt`, beside `centeredAt` and `builtSizeAt`), so the executors see an ordinary `layoutMode`.
  The default buttons are one pair per layout, `presentWhen`-gated, because hug, stretch and grow belong to each child.
- **`layout` joins `VARIANT_AXES`**, argued in its header: Dialog's `footer` has `none` and is a Dialog word.

### Placed Dialogs

`COMPONENT_RENAMES` gains a slot entry with `within: 'button-group'` and two `from` layers. A nested group's slot
already holds the right defaults, so the update replaces nothing: it keeps only the labels a designer changed (a value
unequal to the set's default) and writes them onto the slot's default buttons in order, by property name. An unchanged
instance is left out, and a button swapped or hidden by hand is named. This is driven on a hand-built model in
`test-slot-migration.ts`, because the shim's placed-instance model has no nested slot. Writing into a nested
instance's slot items on a real host is not measured.

### Found, and filed

- **#2817:** the outline primary label (`interactive.primary.text.rest`) misses 4.5:1 on the panel
  (`foreground.primary`) in aurora: 3.76 light, 4.49 dark. That is Dialog's Cancel on `main` today and the fallback
  Cancel after this PR; the Neutral Cancel clears 14.05. Pinned in `test.ts` until the owner answers there.

### Traps

- `swapComponent` is said to keep an instance's overrides by property name, and the shim models it, so the swapped
  Cancel keeps "Cancel"; a real file has not been read. Update sees no plan difference when only the file changed, so a
  Dialog built before Button.Neutral keeps the primary Cancel until rebuilt (Q416 call 4, its own follow-up).
- The plugin shim and the paste stub gained `nestedItems`, which makes an instance of a built group carry its default
  buttons as real children; without it a Dialog's instance of the group has no Cancel to swap.

- The plugin executor visits a slot's items twice (`toSlots`), so the preference miss is pushed at the first-visit
  guard, after the instance is made. The paste payload pushes it at the same point, so the two agree.
- icon-button's paste chunk count moves 17 → 18: the preference code rides every chunk's shell.
- `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 31 → 32: both executors changed.
- The Buttons family now holds four sets, so the literals in `test-component-groups.ts`, `test-build-verdict.mjs`,
  `test-chrome.mjs` and `test-canvas-furniture.ts` that count it move with it. `test-roundtrip.ts`'s #1429 family
  regex matched `button-group` as a Button family and now names the three families exactly.

## (2026-10-18) — Style guides: inverse rows inside groups you made, and a confirmable cleanup of retired tables (#2816, Q412 A)

**What the first real run showed.** #2810 met a file whose designer had grouped the guides by hand. Its "Semantic colors" frame was one horizontal auto-layout row. The run adopted it, as Q4 A says, and appended the eight new inverse guides to the end of that row: about 15,000px wide, with nothing paired. The cause was one condition. `placeGuide` put a guide in the inverse row only when `home.ours`, so an adopted group took every guide "as its layout allows". The same run left the old single Inverse table in the designer's own Inverse frame, kept as a copy, and nothing in the plugin could clear it.

**The fix, in `apps/plugin/src/style-guide.ts`.**
- **The inverse row holds in any grid.** `placeGuide` drops `home.ours`, so a new inverse guide goes under its counterpart in an adopted grid too.
- **A one-time rearrangement.** After the tables are drawn and superseded ones judged, each hand-made frame is checked: one whose guides of a group with an inverse row sit in a non-grid container, with at least one default and one inverse among them. Its guides move into a new HUG grid inserted where its first guide was (`insertChild`, so an auto layout keeps its order), with the designer's own spacing. Defaults go in row 0, in the order they had. Each inverse guide goes in row 1 under its counterpart, or past the last column when it has none.
  - Because it only acts on a non-grid container, it runs once. A rerun finds a grid, so the designer's later moves stand.
  - A guide dragged out of the group is not in the container, so it is not pulled back.
  - The frame, its title, its other children and its place are untouched.
  - The group's change in height pushes down what sits below it, where the generator left it. The page's re-stack origin moves with it, or the full run's re-stack would pull Prism3's groups back up into it.
- **The cleanup offer.** A superseded table kept as edited, moved, a copy, or unrecorded now also goes into `StyleGuideResult.retired` as `{id, name}`, and the summary says it can be removed on the Style guides page once you confirm. The run's guards (no collection, nothing drawn) and a host refusal are not offered.
  - `removeRetiredTables(api, contract, ids)` re-reads the file and plans unfiltered, as Prune stale recomputes on confirm. It removes a listed table only while it still carries the key, is not drawn by that plan, its collection exists, and the plan draws something.
  - The page lists the tables behind "Review and remove…" and sends `style-guide-cleanup` only on "Remove N tables". The main thread runs it under the style guide's own run guard.

**Wording is drafted, an owner question on the PR:** the rearranged-group summary line, the offer line, and the page's three strings.

**Tests.**
- `test-style-guide.ts` §38: the measured state (defaults then inverses in one row, over 15,000px) becomes two aligned rows with the frame, title, place, layout and spacing kept. Also covered: a dragged-out guide stays loose; a rerun keeps a guide moved by hand and rearranges nothing; a new pair joins the adopted grid inverse-under-default; loose inverse guides adopted in the same run pair up too; the old Inverse table is offered and not removed by the run, removed only when named, and a still-drawn table is never removed even when named.
- `test-style-guides-page.mjs`: the offer is shown, the list opens and Cancel posts nothing, and Remove posts exactly the listed ids.
- The shim gains `insertChild`.

**Not verified offline.** Whether Figma's `insertChild` into a hand-made auto layout keeps a guide hugging inside the new grid cell. The owner tries it in the test file first.

## (2026-10-17) — Plugin: the Components page redesign, grouped, alphabetical, multi-select (#2700)

Built to the owner's approved wireframe on #2700, with every numbered call (1–17) at A. It replaces the radio list in the preview and the floating build bar.

- **The list lives in the levers pane (call 9 A).**
  - Two sections: **Components**, with 19 rows, and **Subcomponents**, with 7 rows including Icon (call 11). Together they hold the 41 sets.
  - Rows are grouped by the Figma page a build places them on, so a family such as Buttons, Checkbox or Accordion is one row that opens to its sets. Part sets stay in their family (call 12).
  - Rows are alphabetical, and so are a family's sets (note 2). Rows are labeled by page name, and sets inside a family by component name (call 14).
  - Each row shows its count and its "↳ page" (idea 12). Families start closed, and open when one of their sets is selected or the row is focused (call 15).
  - The grouping comes from a new `page` and `section` on each catalog entry. The plugin's iframe entry and the web's generator both read `file-taxonomy.ts`, so the Studio never imports plugin code at run time.
- **Selection:**
  - A box selects; it is three-state on families and sections (call 8). A name focuses the preview, and focusing doesn't select.
  - Nothing is selected on open (call 13). Selection, open families and focus last for the session (`state/components-page.ts`).
- **The action bar sits at the foot of the list pane, sticky as Draw is (idea 9).** It reads "Build N sets" (call 17), with the selection's cost and the sets a build makes first when the file lacks them (idea 7).
- **The run (`state/build-queue.ts`).** The plugin builds one set per request and its result names no set, so the Studio posts a selection's sets one after another, each when the last result lands. The wire and the plugin are unchanged.
  - Stop lets the set being built finish (call 16).
  - Between sets, Activity reads one running build, phased "Name (2 of 4) · …". A run of several sets ends with one combined verdict and a summary under the bar (idea 13). A one-set run keeps the plugin's own verdict.
  - Subcomponents' "Build all 9" runs at once and leaves the selection alone (call 10).
  - Every build control follows the busy rule (owner decision #4 on #1956): focusable, `aria-busy`, and never natively disabled while a build runs.
- **The preview pane shows the focused family** (Buttons by default, the one with a specimen). It draws the family's head, the Button specimen, Button options (moved into `domains/button-options.ts`) and "Sets in this family", in the approved set lines. At the narrow tier the same block opens inline under the focused row.
  - **The options sit on the card, in the chrome's inks, not on a specimen ground.** A ground is the brand's page for the previewed mode, and in a first build the chrome's light inks on a dark mode's page measured 1:1 (`test:smoke`). The options now sit between the specimen and the sets.
- **Search** (the Studio's settings search) now filters the list. A family stays while any of its sets matches, as the wireframe's edge state says. Before this, it never filtered the set list, though call 6's rationale assumed it did.
- **Derived modes:** Components left the frame's read-only hold. Its levers pane edits no brand setting now, so building stays available, as it was when the bar sat in the preview pane. The Button options hold themselves under the frame's own line.
- **Layout traps fixed on the way (each caught by a gate):**
  - The inline specimen widened the list at 380, so the list's grid tracks are `minmax(0, 1fr)` and the inline card scrolls on its own.
  - A one-line section head overflowed the 268px levers pane at 640 (#1975), so the head is a grid in which the title wraps.
  - TY2 A's L1 rule wants `space-300` after a section title, and a count wrapping under it broke that at 380, so the count sits inside the heading.
- **Removed:** the set radios, `chosenOf`, `componentSetsSection` and the `.p3-buildbar` CSS. Q23's heading pairs on Components ended with the move.

### The fix round on #2812

The owner's decisions on #2812 (all eight questions as recommended, then Q390, Q391 A, Q392 A) and the independent review's findings:
- **The Figma menu's item reads "Build sets…"**, to match multi-select (question 6).
- **A search opens the families its matches sit in** (question 7), so a match is shown, not folded away. The families stay open once the search is cleared, as one opened by hand would.
- **Under a search, a section's box acts on the rows shown** and reads checked, mixed or unchecked over them (Q391 A). Before this, a search for "badge" put all 32 Components sets one click away. It shows two rows, Badge and Tag, whose summary says "A static label is a badge."

## (2026-10-17) — Password field: a small text-style Show at every size, and a tighter label row (#2804, Q380)

Owner QA on the built Password field asked for less space between the label and the Show row, and a small Show
control at every field size. Owner decision Q380 A settled it: Show stays a Button in the `text` appearance (an
action, so a button for assistive tech; the text look reads as a link), small at every size, and the row tightens on
every Password field.

**Measured before.** The label row is a hugging auto-layout row, so it was as tall as its tallest child, the Button:
36 / 44 / 56px at small / medium / large, against a label line of 18 / 21 / 24 (body 12 / 14 / 16 × 1.5). The label
was centered in the row, so it sat 9 / 11.5 / 16px further from the box than the 8px root gap: 17 / 19.5 / 24px in all.

**Why a small button alone was not enough.** A small Button is still 36 tall (`size.sm.height`), and the small field
already nested it, so following Q380's first half alone would have moved medium and large to 36 and left small where
it was. The row had to stop taking the button's height. The toggle now stretches to the row (`crossAxisFill`, Figma's
`STRETCH`): a hugging row is sized by its children that do not stretch, which leaves the label, and the button takes
the row's height. Its "Show" is one `label.sm` line (about 14px), which fits every row. No new token was needed. A
fixed row height bound to the label's line box was the alternative, but there is no line-box token for the small
field's 12px label, and the stretch keeps the row hugging a wrapped label too.

**After.** The row is 18 / 21 / 24px and the label sits 8px above the box at every size, where TextField's sits. In
code the button in the row sets `block-size: auto` and `padding-block: 0`.

**The hit area (owner question on #2809, option A built).** The small Button's own flush rule is 24×24 (Q174 B), but a
nested flush Button owes 44×44 at medium and large (#1741, Q170 B), and `lint-hit-target` held both, so CI was red on
the first head. A 44 centered on the 21 / 24px row reaches 3.5 / 2px into the input box. So the code-side hit area
stays 44×44 at medium and large and 24×24 at small, and at medium and large it is anchored: its bottom edge sits on the
row's bottom edge, so it reaches up and sideways, never down into the box. `lint-hit-target` gains `CODE_SIDE_NESTED`:
a nested flush Button below the floor by decision is held to the code-side rule AND its anchor, both stated in one
`codeOnly` entry, and the entry goes stale by name if the box ever meets the floor.

**Pinned.** `test.ts` measures the row per member, as a hugging row is sized, from the committed emission (the label's
FieldLabel member's line box and the Button member's bound height), against typed 18 / 21 / 24. The toggle test now
expects `size=small` and `label/sm/emphasis-link` on all 84 members. Mutations: following the field's size again fails
"#2317 password-field toggle" by name; dropping the stretch fails "#2804 password-field label row" by name on all 84
members (row 36px).

Mutations on the gate: deleting the anchor sentence fails `password-field.toggle/medium … no codeOnly entry states the
code-side 44×44 together with its anchor`; deleting the `CODE_SIDE_NESTED` entry fails `password-field.toggle/medium …
is 36px, below the 44px floor`.

**Trap for a re-verifier.** Whether a live host lets the row hug the label while a stretched instance whose own height
is bound to 36px sizes to the row, with its label centered and unclipped, is modeled offline only; it is in the def's
`unverified` notes.

## (2026-10-17) — Style guides: grouped into titled sections, inverse under its default (#2801, owner decisions Q378)

**What moved.** Every style-guide run now draws its guides into titled groups. On Primitive tokens: Palettes, Dimensions, Fonts. On Semantic tokens: Semantic colors, Space & size, Borders, Fonts. Each group is a top-level frame (`Style guides — <title>`): a vertical auto layout, transparent, padded 88 / 160 / 160 / 160, a `_Section-header` Size=Large holding the title only, then a HUG grid of guides 160 apart. Groups stack down the page in the table's order, 320 apart. Effect and gradient styles have no group, and sit below the last one in decision 16's rows. The inverse table splits per family ("Inverse text", keyed `…/inverse/text`), and Semantic colors draws each inverse guide in a second row, under its default-surface counterpart.

**Where the table lives.** `packages/engine/style-guide-groups.ts`, a pure table and one function, `styleGuideGroupOf({ type, tier, allRadius })`. The plugin's planner sets each table's `group` from it. The rule reads type and tier, plus "every row is a radius" for Borders, never a family name. So an icon COLOR family lands in Semantic colors and an icon SIZE family in Space & size from the same rule, with no special case for "icon".

**Membership is read from the canvas, every run.** That is the design choice the rest follows from (decision 3: a guide a designer moved stays moved). A guide found inside any page-level frame stays there and is redrawn in place. The table is consulted only for a guide in no group. Two plugin-data records make the cases tell apart without stored defaults. A group Prism3 drew carries `prism3-style-guide-group` (its id) and a `<page>|<frame>` mark, so a designer's duplicate is never taken for it. A guide carries `prism3-style-guide-in-group`, the id of the group it was last found in. A loose guide with that record was dragged out by a designer and stays loose (Q5 A). A loose guide without it was drawn by an earlier build, before groups existed, and joins its group on the next run, at the place the old rows started. That migration is what the owner's main file will see.

**Adoption.** A group's home is the group Prism3 drew for it. Failing that, it is the hand-made frame holding the most of its guides, adopted with its title, place and layout untouched; new guides are appended as that frame's layout allows. Only then is a group drawn. Adoption is recomputed every run from the guides, so nothing marks a hand-made frame.

**Full and partial runs.** A full run removes a group Prism3 drew once it holds nothing but its own title and an empty grid. A designer's note counts as content. A hand-made group is never removed. The full run closes each grid over removed guides (empty columns dropped, order kept) and re-stacks Prism3's groups that are still where it left them. A filtered or stopped run does none of that. It only moves what sits below a group whose height changed, by exactly that change. The trap the test caught: a group drawn in the same partial run was already placed against the page as it stood, and the first build pushed it up into the group above it. Groups drawn this run are now left out of the push-down.

**The superseded check.** A guide in a group no longer has a meaningful x and y (the group's layout sets them). So a superseded guide in a group counts as the generator's while it sits in the group it was last found in, on its page, and is deleted when unedited. Dragged out or moved to another group, it is "moved" and kept, as before.

**Tests.** `test-style-guide.ts` §37 asserts each rule with typed literals: the table by type and tier (another brand's accent ramp, a semantic link family, icon sizes, border widths, radii); adoption, including a hand frame holding two groups' guides; a guide moved by hand into another group; a designer's note; a retitled group; an emptied group, which a filtered and a stopped run keep and a full run removes; an inverse family with no default; effect styles below the groups; and a header set with no Size=Large. Sections 10, 11, 13, 23, 24, 30 and 33 asserted the old page-level rows. Their intent now holds for the groups: column alignment, widening by exact deltas, the grid closing over a deleted guide, the push-down, and no page-level overlap. 21 mutations each fail a named check (PR body).

**Not verified offline.** The shim models a GRID's HUG tracks and auto layout, but not the host's x/y for grid children. Two things are live-checks: that a guide reparented into a grid cell keeps hugging, and that `setGridChildPosition` plus a lower `gridColumnCount` closes a gap the way the shim does. The owner tries this in their test file first.

## (2026-10-17) — Update: sets land below the page header, and missing backdrops count as a change (Q379)

**What happened.** Two Update defects found in a real brand file (owner decision Q379 A: fix in the plugin, then
re-run Update). #2802: on a Checkbox page whose `_section-header` is wider than its sets, an earlier build had put
`checkbox-control` 160px right of the header, at the header's `y`, and the Update's set move re-spaced its two
siblings beside it, so all three stayed in the header's row. #2803: an Update on a file with no `_inverse-backdrop`
said "Run Set up file, then update again", and once Set up file added the template the next dry run read "No changes
found", so nothing applied and the backdrops behind the button families' inverse rows stayed missing.

**The diagnosis.** #2802 is not the header counted as a row member: `respaceSets` (#2542) treated it as an obstacle
only, and its rules keep the first set of a row where it is and never change `y` ("the re-spacing only makes room",
Q248 A). A row that already sat beside the header was therefore left there. #2803: the dry run compared members only,
and the furniture was drawn only for sets the apply acted on, so missing furniture could never become a change.

**The fixes.** `respaceSets` now places a set in the header's row as `placeNewSet` places a new set under a header:
the top of the sets already below the header, else the header's bottom plus `PAGE_HEADER_GAP`; the first on the
header's left edge, each later one `SET_GAP` right of the one before. It is the one move that changes `y`. A set
wholly above or below the header's band stays as before. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 30 → 31 (main took 30 in #2721).
`furnitureDue` (`canvas-furniture.ts`) reads what a set's furniture lacks the way `drawFurniture` would draw it:
the same members, planner, template lookup and guards. A backdrop or scrim matches by its box, a column label by
its left edge, width and bottom, and a row label by its center and its column's right edge, column by column. The dry
run lists what is due on the set's line (DRAFT wording: "1 backdrop to draw", "41 canvas labels to draw"). It counts
as a change and is in the preview hash. The apply gives a furniture-only set an outcome and a named version and
touches no member. The furniture is drawn by `furnishUpdate`, the loop `main.ts` ran, moved where a test can drive
it. It now draws nothing when the confirm was refused.

**The trade-off.** A part whose template the file still lacks is not due, because the apply could not draw it. The
run's Set up file line already names it. Without this the dry run would list it forever. A label's text and its own
width are the template's and are not compared, so a label whose text a designer edited is not due.

**Tests.** `header row/…` (`test-update-apply.ts`) builds the three Checkbox sets fresh with the real executor as
the oracle, puts them beside a wider header as the live page had them, and holds the dry run and the apply to the
fresh layout relative to the header, ids kept, the header unmoved. It also checks one set alone in the row and a
row already under the header, which stays. `due/…` (`test-canvas-furniture.ts`) builds Button with the template
absent, adds it, and holds the dry run's line, an apply that draws the one backdrop and leaves every member's id,
place and stamp, the next dry run current, a set moved by hand listing all 42 parts again and converging, and a
refused confirm drawing nothing. `rollout/<def> due` holds that nothing is due right after a draw, on all 39 defs.
Mutations: `besideHeader` always false → `header row/dry run`, `header row/applied`, `header row/one set` (the
mutant reproduces the live layout); the check dropped from `previewUpdate` → `due/dry run lists`, `due/apply draws`,
`due/stale`, `due/stale converges`, `due/refused`.
Review fixes: a set the apply entered and wrote no member to stays "not updated" when furniture was drawn for it
(#2364's rule), pinned by `idle/furniture` (mutation: the idle count skipping a set with furniture due); and a set
lifted from beside the header joins a row already under it at that row's top, pinned by `header row/joins below`
(mutation: `underY` ignoring the sets below the header).

## (2026-10-17) — Gate: no component requires the Neutral button families (#2808, Q386)

Owner decision Q386: many teams will not build Button.Neutral or IconButton.Neutral, so no other component may
need them. A close or dismiss nests FlushIconButton.Neutral, which the plugin builds as a dependency, and a neutral
action uses Button.Neutral only as a fallback-only preference declared in its own field (Q363.8 on #2661).

A new block in `apps/plugin/test-write-components.ts` holds the rule per def, by name, on two readings that share
no derivation (`docs/34` shape 2):

- **Declared:** `anatomy.parts[*].nests`, read off the def.
- **Built:** `missingDependencies` over the projected plans in an empty file. This is the plugin's own transitive
  list of what it builds before the def. It reads `nestTarget`, `swapTarget` and swap overrides off the plan, so
  it also catches a requirement that arrives through a nested def.

A fallback-only reference is neither `nests` nor `nestTarget`, so neither reading counts it.

The floors:
- Both forbidden ids must be registered defs, so a rename cannot empty the gate (shape 9).
- The built reading must walk every projected def. The count is printed and held, 39 of 39 (shape 15).
- A fixture def nesting each forbidden id must fail both predicates.

The PR is stacked on #2806 and must merge after it. Dialog's close nests IconButton.Neutral until #2806 takes
Q385 (FlushIconButton.Neutral). On #2806's current head the gate fails by name:
`#2808 dialog declares no required nest …` and `#2808 building dialog into an empty file builds no Neutral button
family first …`.

Not covered: a native slot's `preferred` list. A preferred def the file lacks is a named miss when the slot is
written, but the slot is still written. No def uses `preferred` with a Neutral family today.

## (2026-10-17) — Dialog: the close control is always the X, no icon swap (#2609)

**Status:** Dialog def + tests. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no token path moves. No executor
change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays.

### What changed

- **Owner decision (2026-10-16, on #2609):** the control in the header's top-right corner is always the close X.
  Dialog has no icon swap for it; a team that wants another X changes the `close` glyph in its icon set or edits the
  component.
- **Owner decision Q385 A (2026-10-16, on #2806), settling Q377 A on #2609:** the close nests
  **FlushIconButton.Neutral** instead of IconButton.Neutral, so a file built without the IconButton sets still builds
  Dialog, and building Dialog no longer pulls IconButton.Neutral in. The variant is `shape: round, size: medium`, the
  closest to the earlier ghost medium IconButton: the same 44px box at the default density (so the header keeps its
  height and the close keeps a visible 44px target), the same neutral glyph ink and hover wash, and the shared focus
  ring. The one visible difference is round's decorative edge (`color.border.secondary`), which the ghost button did
  not draw; the flush shape would have dropped the edge but shrunk the box to the 20px glyph. Held for the owner's
  visual QA. Dialog depends on IconButton.Neutral nowhere now: the part's `nests`, every member's plan, `composesWith`,
  `commonPartners`, the docs, `.ai.json`, the dependency report and the Studio catalog. `lint-hit-target.ts`'s
  exclusion reason for Dialog names the new button.
- Dialog's `close` part (`nest-fixed`) gains `overrides: { swaps: { icon: 'close' } }`, the
  #2645 mechanism, so every one of the 15 members shows the close icon instead of the icon set's default glyph. The
  `close` boolean (show or hide) is unchanged.
- The "nested close button shows the file's default icon" note is gone; the footer buttons' half of it stays, as the
  Cancel and Save label overrides are still #2671's.

- **Fallout: two readers of the plans that #2645 missed.** Dialog's close is the first swap override on main (List's
  are text), so two places that read a plan's dependencies without `nestOverrides` surfaced here:
  - The Studio component catalog (`apps/studio/src/state/component-catalog.ts`) walked `nestTarget` and `swapTarget`
    only, so it listed Dialog as nesting icon-button-neutral, divider and button while the plugin's pre-build
    (`build-deps.ts`) also builds `icon`. It now reads each `INSTANCE_SWAP` value too, and the generated
    `component-catalog-data.ts` lists `icon`. `test-component-catalog.ts` failed by name on the stale walk.
  - `apps/plugin/test-update-apply.ts`'s and `test-canvas-furniture.ts`'s `planComps` left `icon/close` out of the shim file, so the corpus re-apply
    and the rollout read Dialog as blocked ("component the plan swaps to is not in this file"): 0 of 15 current. A real file
    holds it, because the build pre-builds the icon set; the harness now lists swap-override targets too.

### Diagnosis

Dialog never declared a swap property of its own: `figmaProperties` has no `swaps`, and the close is `nest-fixed`, so
it is not marked `isExposedInstance` and the nested button's `swap icon` does not surface on Dialog's panel. What the
designer saw was the nested button's default glyph. The fix is the override; the test pins both halves, so a later
`swaps` entry or a switch to `nest-exposed` fails by name. A designer can still select the nested button inside an
instance and use its own `swap icon`, which is Figma's behavior for every nested instance and matches the owner's
"go into the component".

### Verification

`test.ts` `#2609 dialog (Q385 A): the close nests FlushIconButton.Neutral, and Dialog depends on IconButton.Neutral
nowhere` reads the part, every plan's nest, swap and swap-override targets, and the selection fields against literals.
`test.ts` `#2609 dialog: …` — every member's close carries the literal swap to `icon/close`; Dialog's Figma surface
has no swap property; the close stays `nest-fixed`. Surface baseline accepted for Dialog only (15 → 15 members).

## (2026-10-17) — Docs: a /docs landing page, linked from the studio header and the plugin (#2637, owner decision Q384 A)

**Status:** Studio, plugin and `docs/public/`. No engine change, no artifact moves, no ENGINE change note, CONTRACT
unchanged, the executor untouched. The owner approved both link placements and the page, copy included, from
screenshots before the push (2026-10-16).

### What changed

- **`docs/public/index.html`, served at `/docs/`.** One plain sentence and three entries: Guides (`guides/index.md`),
  Ecosystem map (`ecosystem/`) and Agent reference (`llms.txt`). Its colors are the ecosystem page's for the same roles
  (light, dark, and the system preference), whose text pairs `lint-ecosystem.ts` already checks at 4.5:1. It adds no
  pair of its own. `REQUIRED_DOCS` now names it, so the site build fails without it.
- **A Docs tile on the bar, just before Export, on both hosts.** It uses the bar's tile parts (a new book glyph over
  "Docs", the glyph alone at the narrow tier, the tooltip) and replaces Inspect's Docs item, which is gone from both
  hosts.
  - **Web:** a link to `/docs/` in a new tab (`linkTile` in `dom.ts`), so the brand being edited stays put.
    `DOCS_HREF` moved from the guides' index to `/docs/`.
  - **Plugin:** a button that posts `open-docs`. The main thread calls `figma.openExternal` on
    `https://prism3-ds.vercel.app/docs/` (`DOCS_URL`, the production address in `apps/studio/README.md`).
- **Why the address is only in the main thread.** `open-docs` carries no URL, so the iframe cannot point
  `openExternal` anywhere else. `openExternal` needs no network permission, so the release build opens it too. The
  release manifest still allows no domains, and `release/main.js` carries the call.
- **`lint-ecosystem.ts` lists `open-docs` as plumbing.** The gate failed the first full verify: every `UiToMain`
  message must sit in a feature's figma lane or on its `PLUMBING` list. Docs is panel chrome, like `set-theme-pref`.
  It can't be a shared feature either: a feature that sends a plugin message cannot claim the web, by the gate's own
  rule.

### Why the slash redirect

Production serves a folder without its trailing slash and without a redirect: `/docs/ecosystem` answers 200, as
`/docs/ecosystem/` does. Served at `/docs`, the page's relative links would resolve one level up. The page carries
the ecosystem page's one-line redirect to the slash path, and every link to it is written with the slash.

### Tests and mutations

- `test-chrome.mjs`: the Docs section replaces the Inspect › Docs one (#2662).
  - **Web:** the tile is a link to `/docs/` in a new tab, just before Export, and clicking it opens `/docs/` in a
    new tab with the studio where it was.
  - **Plugin:** the tile is a button just before Export, and clicking it posts exactly `{"type":"open-docs"}` and
    opens nothing in the panel.
  - **Both:** Inspect lists no Docs item, and the file `/docs/` serves is on disk.
- `test-open-docs.ts` (new, in the plugin's `test`) runs the real `main.ts`:
  - `open-docs` opens the literal address;
  - an address sent with the message is ignored;
  - nothing opens before it.
- `test-docs-route.ts`: `GET /docs/` answers `docs/public/index.html`, byte for byte.

Mutations, from a `wip:` commit, each restored and failing by name. The test:chrome arms ran in a scratch copy of the
suite holding only its setup and this section.

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| the tile left out of the bar | `✗ web: the bar's Docs is a link to /docs/ in a new tab, just before Export — read null` |
| `DOCS_HREF` back on the guides' index | both web Docs arms, naming `/docs/guides/index.md` |
| the plugin button posts nothing | `✗ figma: Docs posts {"type":"open-docs"} … (posted [])` |
| Inspect lists Docs again | `✗ web/figma: Inspect lists no Docs item … read ["Docs"]` |
| the `open-docs` case dropped from `main.ts` | `✗ open-docs opens the docs landing page in the browser … (opened [])` |
| `DOCS_URL` on another address | the same arm, naming the address it opened |
| `docs/public/index.html` absent | `✗ GET /docs/ answers 200` in `test-docs-route.ts` |

### A trap for whoever re-verifies this

**A tile that is a link picks up the link hover underline.** The first web screenshot showed "Docs" underlined on
hover, unlike every other tile. `.p3-btn.p3-tile` now sets `text-decoration: none`.

`main.ts` runs them. The dry run reads moves only (576, 30, 24), every member keeps its id and key, both instances stay
on the page on live members, the decided default ends up top-left, and the next dry run reads up to date. The old
Button is the new plan list with each run of four slot members sorted back into the old order, because slot order is
no `variants` list; a premise check asserts each run of four holds one of each slot pair. Same limit as #2754's proof: a shim instance holds its main component by
reference, so this proves no member was rebuilt, not how Figma itself resolves the instance.
