## (2026-10-16) — Field style lever: Outline or Underline for every field (#2695, Q332 A, Q333)

**What landed.** A Form lever, `fieldStyle` ("Field style", Outline / Underline, default Outline), placed right after
Control shape in the manifest and on the studio's Shape page. Built exactly as the owner's sixteen calls (Q333, each
option A) say. Under Underline, Text field, Password field, Select and Textarea draw a 1px bottom line in the field's
own border roles (rest, hover, focus, the three status borders, read-only, disabled), thickened to 2px at both
focus-visible states, with the shared ring moved out to `focus.ring.offset` (2px). Inline padding goes to `space.0`,
corners go to `radius.none` whatever Control shape says, the hover wash and the disabled plate are dropped, and
Textarea's grip is inset 2px so it sits above the line. No token is added (Q15 A), and no Figma axis (Q14 A): 84 members
per field either way. Apply Theme now says "Field style is now Underline. Update components to redraw the field sets."
when the stored brand's style changed (Q16 A).

**The mechanism is Control shape's.** `applyFieldStyle(def, style)` rewrites a field def before projection and is the
identity under Outline, so every Outline plan is byte-identical and nothing brand-specific reaches the projector. It
runs right after `applyControlShape` in the plugin's `materializeForBrand` and in `lint-lever-sweep.ts`'s restated
composition, so its square corner wins. It reads the frame part's own keys (its corner key, the ring's inset key, any
corner-pinned child) rather than naming keys, and new keys (`underline.side`, `underline.line.<state>`,
`underline.pad-x`) carry the rungs. So density can't move the zero padding: density moves the old `pad-x` keys, which
the frame no longer binds. The field family is `FIELD_FRAME_PARTS`, keyed by def id as `FIELD_CORNER_REFS` is.

**One schema field, and why it's per side.** `PartDef.strokeEdges` binds the four stroke sides apart. Figma binds a
weight per side anyway (#1332: a scalar binding lands on the four per-side keys), so the read-back already reads those
keys and needed no change. The validator now admits `{state}` on a `strokeEdges` key, as it does on a type key. The
footprint rule refuses state-keyed geometry because it moves a box, and an inside-drawn stroke left out of the layout
size moves none. The focus-ring wall in `test.ts` that held `strokeWidth` as the only stroke field now holds exactly
two, both width.

**The trap, and the shim change that witnesses it.** Both executors write a literal `strokeWeight = 1` on a stroked
node whose weight was not written, and a literal write after a binding unbinds it (#1266). Their guards checked only
the scalar `strokeWeight`, so an underline control would have had its per-side bindings overwritten to a 1px box. Four
guards (two per executor) now check the scalar and all four sides. The component shim didn't model that unbinding: a
literal write left the per-side bindings in place, so the bug was invisible offline. The shim now models it, as the
host does. EXECUTOR_REVISION moves to 30 (main reached 29 while this was in review). The paste script grew by the five-key list. Against the old base that
made icon-button 18 chunks; merged over #2754, whose `ghost`-first member order packs one chunk tighter, it is 17
again (measured: the old order on the same merge packs into 18), so the pin did not move.

**How the tests stay independent.** Every expected name in the `#2695` arms (`border-width/hairline`, `/thick`,
`/none`, `space/0`, `radius/none`, `focus/ring/offset`, the border roles, `disabled/text`) is typed from the
decisions, never read off the materializer. The family is held by `color.field.fill`, the field chrome only the four
fields bind. `color.field.border.rest` was tried first and also matches Checkbox and Radio's unchecked box. Contrast is
recomputed from the roles' colors: the rest, hover, focus and three status lines each clear 3:1 on
`background.primary` and `background.secondary`, in every mode of every example brand. That agrees with the
proposal's measured floor of 3.16:1.

**One decision read two ways once in the code (Owner question on #2695).** Q14 A says the defs' `style` entry lists
both values as brand-set, and also that there is no per-instance prop. Listing `underline` in `variants.style` made it a
code coordinate: `lint-paint`'s census doubled each field's grid (108 → 216 coordinates) and `lint-axis-values` read a
two-value variant. Built: `variants.style` stays `['outline']`, and the codeOnly `style` entry names both values as the
brand's Field style setting. The register's reason now says why underline lives on the lever.

**Deferred, filed.** Password field's corner ignores Control shape's Boxed and Hairline on Outline brands (#2718,
pre-existing from #2648). Number input and Code input join the lever when they are built (#2719). The studio's Shape
preview has no field, so the lever has no preview effect there (#2720, an owner question).

**Review round (#2774 fixed here).** The independent review drove Update both ways through the shim. Outline →
Underline converged; Underline → Outline left the 12 hover members of each field set at 100% opacity, reported 12
content failures, and needed a second Update. The cause was on main (#2774): the host resets a bound paint's opacity to
1 on the first assignment that changes the paint's variable, and an in-place rewrite from the opaque `field.fill` to the
translucent wash is exactly that. The plugin executor now assigns a translucent bound paint twice, the rule the shim
already models from the host measurement (the second assignment finds the binding in place and keeps the opacity). The
paste executor is untouched: it only builds fresh, and the combine's re-resolve rescues a fresh build. Q16 A is now held
both ways in `test-update-apply.ts`, on all four fields: one Update, every key and id kept, every washed control
translucent, every disabled edge on `color.disabled.border` (Q346, which landed on main while this was open), and a
clean next dry run. Q8's disabled ink is now pinned per slot (value and placeholder `disabled.text`, glyphs
`disabled.icon`), so swapping the two fails by name. #2563 (members an Update ADDS) hits the same host rule and may be
helped by this fix, but its verify gap is separate and it stays open.

## (2026-10-16) — Repeating items as a native items slot: Checkbox group, Radio group, Tabs, List, Segmented control (#2649, Q307 A)

The five components that held their repeating children as a fixed stack behind Figma-only visibility booleans (#2344,
the "hidden nested instances" pattern Nathan Curtis names) now hold them in a native Figma slot, `items` (#2417's
`contentSlot`). Three items by default; Tabs and Segmented control with the first selected, as before. The row
booleans are gone. Header, label, description and message stay outside the slot, and Segmented control keeps its
`Label` toggle. Every other axis and token is unchanged, held by the rewritten literal arms in `test.ts`.

### The shape per component

- **Checkbox group, Radio group, List:** a new `items` box under the root (a column, `crossAxisFill`), holding the rows.
  The groups' gap is 0 and List's item gap moved onto the slot; the root keeps its own gap binding, so no token moved.
- **Tabs:** the `list` frame became the `items` slot (same layout, renamed).
- **Segmented control:** the `track` stays (it carries the border, radius and padding), and an `items` slot grows
  inside it, so the segments still grow along a bounded main axis and share the track equally (Q269.6). The segments
  were `nest-exposed` (`selection`, `state`); in the slot they are `nest-fixed`. Figma refuses a property reference on
  a slot sublayer (measured for text in #2417), and a designer now sets a segment's selection on the segment itself.
  Not measured for exposure on a real host: an owner item.

### In code: Curtis's spec shape

`PropDef` gained `anyOf`, `minItems` and `maxItems` for a `type: 'slot'` prop that is a children array. Each of the
five carries `items` (`anyOf` the item def, `minItems` 1, `maxItems` 6 for Tabs per Q179 and 5 for Segmented control
per its two-to-five rule). List's `children` prop became `items`; `children` stays the name for open content
(Accordion's panel). Button's `leadingVisual` was already `type: 'slot'` (a single instance swap), so the validator
asks for `anyOf` and `minItems` only once a slot prop declares any of the three. Emitted in `components.ai.json` and
the docs pages' Props table ("slot of `tab`, 1 to 6").

### The update carries placed instances across (`apps/plugin/src/slot-migration.ts`)

Figma carries nothing from the old rows to the new slot: the rows' layers are removed from the member, every override
on them goes with them, and each placed instance would fall back to three default items. So the update does it:

- **Capture, before the set is touched.** Every instance of a member (`getInstancesAsync`), its VISIBLE rows in the
  ledger's order, each row's variant, its own property values (the label) and its exposed instances' values (the
  checked state). Hidden rows are listed and left out: never resurrected.
- **Fill, after.** The slot's default items removed, one new instance per captured row made from the row's own
  variant, `setProperties` for its values, the default items' layout copied (stretch, grow). Read back: count, order,
  variant, every value; `limitViolations` named.
- **Never silent.** An override no component property carries (read off `InstanceNode.overrides` against each layer's
  `componentPropertyReferences`), an override on a layer the plan drops (Tabs' `list`), an instance inside another
  instance (it follows its holder), and a host that does not list overrides are each a named line, in the dry run and
  in the verdict. The capture is in the set's `previewHash`, so an instance edited between the check and the confirm
  refuses the apply.
- **What drives it is the ledger.** `COMPONENT_RENAMES` gained a `slot` entry kind: the slot, the layer that held the
  rows, the row layers in order and the removed booleans. `lint-component-renames.ts` now records every set's
  component properties in `component-axes.json` and demands a claim (a slot entry or a `property` drop) for any that
  leaves. Its base predates the field, so this PR's own removals are a BOOTSTRAP for that arm; `test.ts` drives it on
  hand-built baselines (the slot entry claims its booleans; without it each is named), and holds the five real entries
  as literals. `lint-component-surface.ts` now names each def's properties in its baseline, so a removed boolean or an
  added slot shows in the baseline's own diff.

### Verified on the shim, and what is not measured

`test-slot-migration.ts` builds each set the OLD way from a legacy fixture (today's def with the slot taken back out,
the booleans typed from #2344 and Q179), places designers' instances, and runs `previewUpdate` then `applyUpdate`
exactly as `main.ts` does. A Checkbox group with five visible rows (row 3 hidden by hand) becomes five items in order,
each with its label and checked state; Tabs keeps four tabs with the third selected; List carries all eight; Segmented
control carries four options, the second selected. The PLACED INSTANCES are a model the test supplies (a live view of
the member, as Figma propagates a main's change), the one thing the shim did not have. `test-native-slots.ts` builds
Tab and Tabs into one file and checks each slot item points at the right Tab member, which carries its own hover and
press reactions (#2466), with none written on the item.

**Not measured on a real host:** children written into a SLOT layer of an INSTANCE through the plugin API, and
`setProperties` on the fresh instances. The first update of the master file is that probe; a refusal there is a miss
by name, never a silent pass. Nor the exposure question above.

### Deliberate choices

- **`EXECUTOR_REVISION` is not raised.** The component executor's code (`write-components.ts` and what it reaches) is
  unchanged; the migration lives in the update. The members re-apply through their plan stamps anyway. A raise would
  mark every member of every set in every file as built by an earlier plugin, with no field difference.
- **Built on #2646.** Its branch appeared while this was in progress, so this branch was built on it (it has since merged) and
  uses its `slotSettings` and `preferred` rather than duplicating them: every `items` slot takes `minChildren` 1,
  `maxChildren` 6 on Tabs and 5 on Segmented control, `preferred` the item def and `allowPreferredValuesOnly`.
  `test-slot-constraints.ts`'s corpus table gained the five rows, and #2646's DRAFT note on List ("no slot to sit
  on") is gone, since List now has one. A carried item that is not the preferred def, or an instance left with no
  visible row, reads as a slot limit (`limitViolations`) in the verdict.
- **A gap in #2646's read-back, closed here because these are its first constrained slots.** The update's dry run
  and its verify read each member as a snapshot, which has no parent, so the read-back could never find the set's SLOT
  property and every constrained slot read as differing forever (`no component set above the slot`). `ReadPorts`
  gained `slotProperty`, which the dry run, Capture and the apply's verify fill from the set's own definitions
  (`withSetSlots`), read only where no set sits above the node. `hostPorts` gained #2646's `componentName` too, which
  it lacked, so a preferred set read UNREADABLE there. Held by `test-update-apply`'s `corpus/in place`: drop the
  fallback and the five sets fail it by name. Also the shim: with `identities` on, a stub component now carries the
  key its instances already read, as a real file's does, so the round-trip resolves a slot's preferred def.
- **`minItems` 1 for Segmented control,** as Q307 A says for all five, although its own rule is two to five. Flagged
  on #2649.

**Review round (CHANGES REQUESTED on `7178d04`).** The change note now names the breaking part outright: List's
`children` prop becomes `items`, and the row booleans are removed from each Figma set. `test-slot-migration`'s
converge step now also asserts the next dry run has no property left to remove; before, it compared counts only, so a
plan that stopped deleting the old booleans read "current" there and was caught only by `test-update-apply`. Mutation:
`applySet` stops deleting `properties.remove` → `✗ converge/booleans gone: the next dry run has no property left to
remove (Option 2, …, Option 8)`. The merge with `main` waits for fold #2582. Placed instances in files that consume a
published library are an open owner question on #2660.

**Delta round (CHANGES REQUESTED on `ed4935a`).** Merged `main` after the 0.237.0 fold. The five conflicts resolved as
the review's table says; `update-plan.ts` runs main's `fileBlockers` and then the slot-migration block. Because the
branch still carried #2646's pre-squash commits, a plain merge brought back #2646's pending fragment and change note,
which the fold had already written into the log and the changelog: both are deleted, or the next fold writes #2646 a
second time. `regen.ts` then moves the analysis reports main added after this branch's base (`docs/public/reports/**`),
and the component surface and axes baselines are re-accepted so Link's sets join them. A merge rather than a rebase:
the branch has been reviewed, and a merge keeps every review's SHA reachable.

A third merge of `main` (Dialog #2652, the agent reference #2644) conflicted on the slot-constraints corpus, where
both sides' rows are kept, and on the component surface baseline and comparison report, which are re-accepted and
regenerated. One step git does not flag: `component-axes.json` merges cleanly but is stale, because Dialog's entry
lacks the component properties this branch records, so `lint-component-renames` fails until it is re-accepted.

**Combined re-gate round (RED on `main` `4754d868` + `330e91a5`).** #2683 (#2645, per-instance overrides on nested
instances) landed on `main` and conflicts with this PR in behavior, though the text merges cleanly. Started from the
re-gate's mechanical resolution (`train/2660-merge-main`, `e25ab7f9`) and fixed its four failures:
- **The two executors disagreed on override misses (36 vs 18).** The plugin's `toSlots` runs `build` over each new
  SLOT to write the slot's own fields from the plan. That pass visits the items the slot holds a second time, so
  `applyNestOverrides` wrote again and pushed every miss twice. The paste twin `__slotsNow` only moves the items. The
  fix is a per-run `WeakSet` of the instances whose own values (`nestOverrides`, and `nestTexts` with them, the same
  per-instance write by the same path) are already written, which lets the second visit skip them. I chose this over
  narrowing `toSlots`'s `build` to the slot alone: the in-place pairing is what keeps the slot's children, and
  passing it an empty plan would remove them. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 27 → 28. Mutation: drop the `firstVisit` guard →
  `❌ #2645 parity: the plugin executor reports the same override misses as the payload (36 vs 18)`.
- **`test-slot-migration`'s legacy fixture** now carried today's number overrides onto rows whose stand-in declares
  no `number` property, so the premise build failed. The fixture strips `overrides` from its rows. That is the shape
  of the files this migrates: they were built from the defs before #2645, and the fixture's cloning of the second
  row would give every row "2." anyway, which no real file had. A row's number, typed or overridden, reaches the
  migration as the row instance's own `componentProperties`, which the placed-instance model already covers.
- **`test-update-apply`'s #2645 section** expected List's eight items as direct children. It now finds the three in
  the `items` slot, at the paths the dry run reports (`items/item2`).
- **`test-roundtrip`'s read-back predicate** found `item2` under List's root. It now finds it at any depth.
- **The re-gate's merge dropped this PR's surface baseline.** `component-surface.json` on `train/2660-merge-main` had
  taken `main`'s side, which records no component properties, so `lint-component-surface` failed on every set
  (`component properties not recorded in the baseline`) and `lint-push-base` failed with it. Re-accepted after merging
  `main` at `a6b2dc75` (#2690). A text merge of a baseline only this branch's shape carries needs a re-accept, the
  same lesson as the axes baseline in the Dialog round.
- **Merged `main` at Segmented control's redesign (#2739, Q336 A, Q342 A).** It conflicted in `segmented-control.ts`
  and `test.ts`. Both keep the redesign's track (filled with `color/background/secondary`, no outline) holding this
  PR's `items` slot of three nest-fixed segments, and the control arm asserts both. `component-surface.json` is
  re-accepted on the merged tree.
- **Merged `main` at `bf76f201` (cloud lane, landing train 3).** `component-schema.ts` conflicted: this PR's slot-prop
  checks (`anyOf`, `minItems`, `maxItems`) and #2747's typed-default check (#2707) are independent arms in the same

## (2026-10-16) — Gate scope lists name every def that qualifies, and an unlisted one fails by name (#2709, #973)

The component audit (#2706) found five hand-written scope lists that had fallen behind the registry. Each is a gate's memory of which defs it must see: if a listed def stops projecting the shape, the gate fails instead of reading clean. Defs off a list were still checked, but nothing would notice if they dropped out. The counts at `main` `0c66e5b0`:

| List | Listed | Qualifying |
|---|---|---|
| `lint-absolute-inset.ts` `MUST_COVER` | 7 | 21 inset parts |
| `lint-absolute-inset.ts` `MUST_CLEAR_STROKE` | 6 | 20 (Accordion's ring is drawn inside, with no `strokeInset`) |
| `lint-standalone-floor.ts` `MUST_PROJECT` | 26 | 41 projecting defs |
| `test.ts` `GAP_KEYS` | 12 | 15 (Password field, Accordion, Link) |
| `test.ts` `SH_DEFS` / `RO_PINNED` | 3 | 4 (Password field) |

The issue's table counted the Button and Icon button variants once each. The converse arms below counted each one separately, and they are listed one by one now.

**The fix has two parts.** First, every qualifying def is added to its list. Second, each list gets a converse arm: a def with the qualifying shape that is in neither the list nor a named exemption with a reason fails by name. The qualifying shape is read off the def, by each gate's own spelling of it: a declared `absolute` part with an `inset`, a successful projection, a `densitySpacing` key whose last segment ends in `gap`, a `status` axis with error, warning or success, a state axis with `read-only`. The lists stay authored and the registry stays the subject, so neither side is derived from the other (`docs/34`). The standalone-floor converse closes #973, which asked for exactly that arm.

**One exemption, with its reason.** Field message has a status axis but no state axis and no stroked edge, so there is no hover border for the #1782 status sweep to measure. It sits in `SH_EXEMPT`. Every newly covered def passed its gate as it stands, so nothing was filed.

**Mutations, each failing by name.** Each one removed one entry from a list, with the work committed first:

- `lint-absolute-inset.ts`, with `'tag.focusRing'` dropped from `MUST_COVER`: exit 1, `SCOPE NOT RECORDED: 'tag.focusRing' declares an absolute inset and is not in MUST_COVER.`
- `lint-absolute-inset.ts`, with `'radio-control.focusRing'` dropped from `MUST_CLEAR_STROKE` only: exit 1, `COMPENSATION NOT RECORDED: 'radio-control.focusRing' declares strokeInset 'ring-width' and is not in MUST_CLEAR_STROKE`.
- `lint-standalone-floor.ts`, with `'dialog'` dropped from `MUST_PROJECT`: exit 1, `SCOPE NOT RECORDED: 'dialog' projects today and is not in MUST_PROJECT.`
- `test.ts`, in one run: `link` dropped from `GAP_KEYS`, `password-field` dropped from `SH_DEFS` and from `RO_PINNED`, and Field message's `SH_EXEMPT` key renamed. That gave 3 failures, all three new arms, and no others: `the gap floor RECORDS every def whose density spacing names a gap (14 listed) — NOT IN GAP_KEYS: link`; `a11y(#1782, #2709): … NOT PINNED: field-message, password-field`; `a11y(#1710, #2709): every def with a read-only member is pinned in RO_PINNED — NOT PINNED: password-field`. Each arm reads only its own list, so one run shows every arm firing on its own entry.

The skill's gate table (`prism3-build-component` §7) now says each of these lists fails on an unlisted def, and it names the three `test.ts` lists, which it did not name before.

## (2026-10-16) — /review-pr: the fold checklist names the gate that catches a missed fragment, and authorship reads both session links (#2740)

**What changed.** Three corrections to `.claude/commands/review-pr.md`, found in the independent review of #2682:

- **A false claim, removed.** The fold checklist said a fragment merged after the fold's base is missed "and no gate
  catches that". `lint-progress-order.ts`'s LEAVES NOTHING PENDING arm (#2663, merged in #2667) fails exactly that case,
  on the merged tree, the branch and the push run. The step stays, as a cross-check of that gate.
- **The authorship signal.** "A session link that is your own means it is yours" read only the commit trailers. Lane
  commits carry the orchestrating session's `Claude-Session:` trailer, so a lane never sees its own link there and the
  signal cleared it to review its own PR. The command now names both places: the trailer may be the orchestrator's, and
  the PR body's `Generated by` footer, when it carries a link, names the session that wrote it. Ready comments usually
  carry only the bare footer, with no link, so the command does not point there (review of #2767).
- **A check the checklist lacked.** Re-run `fold.ts` in your own worktree at the fold's base and diff against the PR
  head. The base is `git merge-base <head> origin/main`, the newest `main` commit the fold carries, so a fold branch
  that merged `main` is re-run against what it merged. The approving review of fold #2582 ran it, and it is the one
  fold check independent of the fold PR's own claims. The one expected difference is the date: `fold.ts` stamps the
  day it runs into `CHANGELOG.md`'s "folded <date>" line and the release notes, so a re-run on a later day differs
  there and nowhere else (review of #2767, re-running #2582 a day later).
- **The fold's write list, kept current.** #2650 (merged while this PR was open) made a fold also write release notes
  under `docs/public/releases/`, and `lint-progress-order.ts`'s PURE arm admits them. The checklist's "it edits only"
  list now names them, so a reviewer does not flag a correct fold for touching them.

**Trap.** The commit trailer and the PR footer can legitimately name different sessions on the same PR. Neither alone
proves a PR is not yours. Only your own link in either place proves it is. A missing footer, or one with no link,
proves nothing either way: some lane PRs carry only the orchestrator's link, and Ready comments carry the bare footer.

## (2026-10-16) — Segmented control, Tab and Tag step their glyph down one rung, as Button does (#2725, owner decision Q337 A)

**Status:** three def bindings moved, one gate admission, tests. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no token added or renamed. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at main's number.

**What moved (Q337 A):** `size.{small,medium,large}.icon` on `segmented-control-segment`, `tab` and `tag` now bind `icon.size.xs` / `sm` / `md` (16 / 20 / 24px), where they bound the 1:1 rung `sm` / `md` / `lg` (20 / 24 / 32px). Button has done this since #1350. Icon button and Flush icon button keep their own rung.

**Tag's one rung sizes three parts.** `size.{size}.icon` sizes the leading icon, the check and the ×, so all three step down together; the rung was not split. Splitting it would need a new token key per glyph, which is a naming call, and a check larger than the leading icon beside it would be a design call. The owner confirmed this as Q356 A: all three step down together, and the ×'s 44px hit slot is unchanged. The `notes.contested` entry that held the ×'s size in its slot is removed, and Tag's `evolution` line cites Q356 A.

**Gates.** `lint-rung-names.ts` arm 3 expects every def's medium default on `md` unless the def is in `ICON_OFFSET_DEFS`; the three defs are added there, so a revert to `md` or a slip to `xs` still fails it by name. `lint-component-surface.ts` baseline accepted over the change note (7 surfaces drifted: tag ×3, tab, segment ×3).

**Tests.**
- `test.ts` `#2725` block: for each of the three defs, every projected member's glyph parts (Tag: leading icon, check, ×) bind the literal `icon/size/xs|sm|md` and resolve to the literal 16 / 20 / 24px in nb and every example brand. Icon button's three families are asserted at 20 / 24 / 32 in the same block, so the boundary holds both ways. A scope floor requires every named part at every size.
- The Tag rendered-width assertions encode the owner's 2026-09-29 worked examples, which used the 24px glyph at medium. They now read with the 20px glyph: select label + check 74 (was 78), icon + 67px label + check 145 (was 153), the check widens by 26 (was 30); dismissible with icon 86 / 108 / 128 (was 90 / 112 / 136). Label-alone widths and the floor are unchanged.
- `apps/plugin/test-write-components.ts` `#2380` rows for Tag's check and × named the 1:1 rung (`icon/size/{size}`); they now name `{size-1}`, the rung below, typed in the test as `xs` / `sm` / `md`.
- `apps/plugin/test-update-apply.ts` `stepdown/…`: each set built on the old 1:1 rung (the def with its three bindings put back), then updated through `previewUpdate` + `applyUpdate`. Every glyph is rebound and resized to the literal names and px, the set and every member keep their key and id, and the next dry run reads all current. `world()` gained a `varPx` passthrough so the shim carries the ladder's real px.

## (2026-10-16) — Update: children moved into a frame the plan inserts keep their ids (#2595)

**What happened.** The in-place update pairs a node's children with the plan's by name, under the same parent
only.  When a plan inserts a frame between a node and children it already has (Accordion's `titleRow`, #2594),
the new frame had no candidate, so it and everything in it were built fresh and the old children removed. On
an Accordion built before #2594 the indicators, their glyph instances, `titleBox` and `label` all got new ids,
and a placed instance's own choice on the nested indicator was lost.

**The fix.** `adoptions` in `write-components.ts` is the one rule, read by the executor and by the dry run: under a
node the file holds, a plan child FRAME with no child of its name is offered the node's unpaired children that the
FRAME names as its own, that no other plan child claims, and that the file holds under that name once. In `build`,
the fresh frame pairs them as an in-place node pairs its own, and each that fits is moved in (`appendChild` moves
a node in Figma) and configured in place. One that does not fit stays with its old parent, which removes it,
as before.  The dry run (`movesOf` in `update-plan.ts`) lists each move as `<part> · moves into <frame>, kept`
(the issue's option A, DRAFT wording, an owner item), drops it from the "removed" lines, and diffs the moved subtree
against its plan at the new path, so a field the apply changes on a moved node is still listed. `EXECUTOR_REVISION`
22 → 28 (main took 23 to 27 with #2652, #2648, #2703, #2683 and #2744 while this was open).

**The trade-off.** The dry run runs before the designer picks keep, overwrite or accept, so the move cannot depend
on the choice. A node with a hand edit at or under it is never moved (`edited`, every hand-edited path whatever
the choice, passed by the apply alongside `keep`): it is rebuilt as before #2595, and the dry run lists it as
removed on that member. That rebuild already loses the hand edit under "keep" on main while the verdict says
"kept"; filed as #2673 rather than widened here.

**A shim fix the test needed.** The component shim's `appendChild` pushed a node onto its new parent without
taking it off the old one, which Figma's does (its `insertChild` already modelled the move). Without the fix a
moved node read as in both places. No other suite moved with it.

**Tests.** `acc/dry run moves` holds the three move lines and that nothing reads as removed; `acc/moved children`
reads every node under the moved parts, by id, under the row; `acc/agree` checks the shim removed none of them;
`acc/edited dry run` and `acc/edited agree` hold the hand-edited title listed removed on its member and rebuilt
there, moved on the other 23.

**Review round (CHANGES REQUESTED on `a63c505a`).** The edit rule was written out twice, once beside each
`adoptions` call, and only its result was shared, so an edit *under* a moved node could stop blocking the move
on one side alone with every test green (the review's M3). `adoptions` now takes `edited` and the parent path and
applies the rule itself; the closure is gone from both callers. The hand-edit block runs twice, with the edit on
`titleBox` and under it on `label` (`acc/edited under dry run` / `acc/edited under agree`). `acc/moved diffed`
holds the claim that a moved subtree is diffed at its new path: a pre-#2594 title column with no top padding is
listed as `paddingTop` at `header/titleRow/titleBox` on all 24 members beside its move (the review's M5 passed
silently). `acc/adoptions …` drives the rule on hand-built inputs, one line per guard: the name held once,
the frame already present, a name another plan child claims, an edit under a child, an edit on a sibling that
only shares a prefix. The review's nit on the dry run's third type map is closed at the source: `adoptions`
never moves an INSTANCE_SWAP, whose host type (an instance or a placeholder frame) depends on whether its target
is in the file, which the dry run cannot read, so both sides rebuild it. No committed def moves a swap part,
so nothing moves today. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` is 28: main took 23 to 27 (#2652, #2648, #2703, #2683, #2744) while
this was in flight.

## (2026-10-16) — Update: the verify and the dry run agree on an axis the parent stretches (#2696)

**What was wrong.** On a real file, the confirmed Update reported Accordion "not verified": `…/header/titleRow/leadingIndicator.counterAxisSizingMode: FIXED (the plan says AUTO)` on the medium and large members. The dry run straight after read the set up to date. The two never compared the same thing:
- The apply's verify runs `diffAnatomy` on every updated member.
- The dry run runs it only on a member that is not current. A member whose stamp and record are current is never compared, and the record is taken after the apply, so it already holds FIXED.

**The rule.** The indicator is a row inside the row `titleRow`, with `layoutAlign: STRETCH`. Its counter axis is the axis the stretch fills, so its height is the row's whatever its own mode says. The plan says AUTO there (`fillsAxis` gives it no FIXED, because the row hugs). The executor writes AUTO, and the parent's child loop then writes the stretch. The read-back's two sizing-mode predicates (`anatomy-readback.ts`, `stretchedMode`) now accept FIXED for a planned AUTO when:
- the plan stretches the node;
- the host still holds that stretch;
- the field is the axis the stretch fills. That is the node's counter axis when it shares its parent's direction, and its primary axis otherwise. The parent's plan is threaded into `check` to decide this.

A planned FIXED is never relaxed, because a stretched node left AUTO hugs (#1751). The dry run and the verify both read `FIELDS`, so the one predicate makes them agree in both directions. That holds whether the dry run compares the member or reads it current.

**Why medium and large, not small.** This is inferred, not measured, because the shim models no heights. The host switches a resized axis to FIXED; the executor's `placementWidth` note records this. The title column is the label's line plus a 2px offset, which the def keeps within 1px of the glyph (16/20/24). Where the row comes out taller than the glyph, the stretch resizes the indicator and the host flips it to FIXED. Where it doesn't, nothing resizes and it stays AUTO. To confirm on the real file, read the indicator's height against its glyph's at each size.

**Owner decision Q357 A (2026-10-15).** The rule lives in the read-back, not the plan: relaxed only on the axis the stretch fills, only while both the plan and the host hold the stretch, and a planned FIXED never.

**Considered and not taken (Q357 B).** Making the plan say FIXED on a stretched axis, so the executor writes what the host ends at. That moves the plan of every `crossAxisFill` box, so every such member would read "to update" on the next dry run. It also changes what a hugging row means for its stretched child. That is a projection change, and it would trade this disagreement for one at small, where the host holds AUTO.

**Test.** A new `stretched mode` section in `test-update-apply.ts`, through the file shim. The test models the host itself: at medium and large, the indicator switches to FIXED when the stretch is written. Three controls hold their value whatever is written:
- one member's `titleRow` holds FIXED, and the host holds it stretched where the plan does not (a designer's stretch, with no `layoutAlign` comparison to catch it);
- that member's `header` holds FIXED (stretched on its primary axis, not its counter axis);
- an open member's `content` holds AUTO (the plan says FIXED on its stretched axis).

The expected lines are literals from the def.
- The verify names the three controls and no indicator.
- The next dry run reads 24 current.
- Forced out of date, the dry run lists exactly the three controls and the verify names the same three.
- An indicator whose host lost the stretch is listed and named again.

Mutations, each failing by name:
- the rule dropped → `stretch/verify`, `stretch/dry run`, `stretch/agree`, `stretch/lost`;
- the parent's plan not threaded → the same four;
- the axis ignored → the same four;
- a planned FIXED relaxed too → the same four;
- the host's stretch not required → `stretch/lost`;
- the plan's stretch not required → `stretch/verify`, `stretch/dry run`, `stretch/agree`, `stretch/lost`. The independent review found this conjunct untested (it survived with 257 passing); the `titleRow` control's host stretch is what pins it.

No executor file changed, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays. The change note is `engine: patch`, because no artifact or projected surface moves.

## (2026-10-16) — Boolean and number prop defaults ship as booleans and numbers (#2707)

The component audit (#2706) found six defs that wrote a boolean prop's default as the string `'false'` or `'true'`, and Badge's `max` as `'99'`. `PropDef.default` is typed `string | boolean | number`, so the compiler accepted all of them. Each string reached `out/components/components.ai.json` unchanged. An agent or codegen that read Badge's `showZero` got `"false"`, which is truthy, while every older def ships a real `false`. #1623 fixed the same defect in the first 19 defs. These six came later, so this is a recurrence.

**The fix.** The thirteen defaults are now literals: Tag ×4, Tab ×2, Segmented control option ×2, Segmented control ×1, Link ×2, Badge ×2. `regen` moves exactly two artifacts: `components.ai.json` and `docs/public/reports/component-comparison.json`, 13 values each. The note is `engine: minor`. No token name moves, so `CONTRACT_VERSION` stays where it is.

**The gate.** `validateComponentDef` now refuses a prop whose `type` is `'boolean'` or `'number'` when the default has a different JS type. The type field is free-form, so a union such as Accordion's `headingLevel` (`enum: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`, default `'3'`) is prose and out of scope, as the issue says. The registry loop in `test.ts` already runs the validator over every def. A new block adds ten literal cases: five that must be refused and five that must be accepted, on a copy of Badge. That way the rule is pinned even on a day when no committed def breaks it.

A stricter `PropDef` type was considered and set aside. It would catch the author at compile time, but defs also arrive as data (MCP callers, a brand's own component), and no compiler sees those. The validator covers both paths. A type-level check would be a second spelling of the same rule.

**Mutations, each failing by name** (work committed first):

- **A def regressing.** With Tag's `selected` default changed back to `'false'`, `test.ts` exits 1 with `component: Tag def is structurally valid — prop 'selected': type 'boolean' with a string default ("false") — write the default as a boolean, not a string, because it ships as written in components.ai.json (#2707)`. Six other Tag assertions fail on the same message, because they all validate Tag.
- **The rule removed.** With the validator's condition replaced by `false`, `test.ts` exits 1 with exactly one failure: `component props (#2707): a boolean or number prop refuses a default of another type, and accepts its own (10 literal cases) — WRONG: boolean default "false" accepted; boolean default "true" accepted; boolean default 0 accepted; number default "99" accepted; number default false accepted`. The registry stays green under this mutation, because no committed def breaks the rule anymore. The literal cases are what pin the rule.

## (2026-10-16) — Figma's default member follows the code default, and a gate holds it on every axis (#2752, Q347 A)

**Status:** three defs reordered, a new `test.ts` gate, a shim proof in `apps/plugin/test-update-apply.ts`. ENGINE
minor (change note): the projected sets' member order, the component docs and `components.ai.json` move. CONTRACT
unchanged. No executor code moved, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stands.

**What moved:** Icon button's `appearance` (and through the factory, the destructive and neutral siblings) is
`ghost, filled, outline`; Veil's `intensity` is `medium, subtle, strong`; Image placeholder's `ratio` is `4:3`, then
the rest tallest to widest. The code enums keep their own order. `lint-axis-values.ts`'s three register entries follow,
each citing Q347.

**Which member Figma inserts.** The plugin API's own typings document `ComponentSetNode.defaultVariant` as "the
top-left-most variant, spatially", the one dragged in from the library. That matches the #2501 lane's scratch-file
measurement (layer order does not move it). **Correction to 2026-09-27 "Component alignment: field family + switch
(#1699)":** that entry says `defaultVariant` is the set's first child. It is the top-left member. The two agree in
every set the engine builds today, because `planSetLayout` puts the first plan in row 0, column 0; the gate asserts
that agreement too, so a layout change that split them would fail.

**The gate** (`test.ts`, `#2752 <def>`): for every def that builds a set, the member in row 0, column 0 is read axis by
axis and compared with what the def's PROPS say. EXPECTED is a prop's own `default`, or, where the code form is a prop
of another name, an authored BRIDGE (`status` → `validation`, `selection` → `checked`/`selected`, `expansion` →
`defaultExpanded`); a slot axis expects `false` (an empty optional slot); the state axis expects `rest`. Nothing on the
expected side reads `variants`, so a reorder cannot carry its own expectation with it (docs/34 shape 1). An axis
neither answers fails as UNBRIDGED. A mismatch passes only as an exact EXCEPTION (defs, axis, both values, a reason),
and an exception no def hits fails as stale. `icon` and `spinner` build single components, so they have no default
member; that is asserted both ways.

**What the gate found beyond the three, held as owner questions on #2752, not fixed:**
- The size ladder: 27 sized defs insert `small` while code defaults to `medium`, by Q213 (#2501). Only the fields
  and Dialog lead with medium. Recorded as an exception citing Q213.
- Button ×3: the `leading icon` and `trailing icon` axes lead with `true`, so the inserted Button shows both icons
  while the code slots are empty. Recorded as two exceptions.

**Update reorders in place.** The shim section `default member` builds each set in its old order, places two
instances, and runs the dry run and apply as `main.ts` does. Each reads as moves only (216, 20, 5), every member and
the set keep key and id, the placed instances stay on the page pointing at members still in the set, and afterwards
the top-left member is the decided default. The instance model is the limit: a shim instance holds its main component
by reference, so this proves no member was rebuilt, not Figma's own instance resolution.

**Pins that moved with the order:** `#1515`'s cohort literal (4:3 first), and the `#1318` sparse-grid fixture, whose
intensity order is now typed as the pre-#2752 one so "the set's first member" and "the code default" stay two
coordinates in its refusal tests.

**Mutations (each committed first, restored after), failing by name:**
- Each of the three axes back to its old order → `#2752 icon-button` (and `-destructive`, `-neutral`): "appearance:
  Figma inserts filled, code defaults to ghost"; `#2752 veil`: "intensity: Figma inserts subtle, code defaults to
  medium"; `#2752 image-placeholder`: "ratio: Figma inserts 2:3, code defaults to 4:3".
- Icon button's prop default moved to `filled`, the order left ghost first → the three `#2752 icon-button…` arms

- `dialog` added to the size exception, which it does not need → **did not fire at first.** The stale check asked

## (2026-10-16) — Release notes per engine version, generated at each fold and checked against git (#2650)

**What it is.** Owner decision Q308.1 A: plain-language "What changed in <version>" notes, generated rather than written. `packages/engine/release-notes.ts` reads four committed records at the previous fold and at this one — the Figma sets and their variant properties (`schema/component-axes.json`), each set's surface digest (`schema/component-surface.json`), the coded components (`out/components/components.ai.json`) and the guaranteed token names (`schema/token-contract.json`) — plus `COMPONENT_RENAMES`, and lists every change as breaking, new or fix by docs/30's rule widened from tokens to every name (docs/30, "Release notes"). The folded change notes follow verbatim under "In detail". `fold.ts` now writes `docs/public/releases/<version>.md` and `.json` and the version's entry in `index.md` and `index.json`, before its regen and again after it, so the notes describe the tree the fold commit holds. The plugin's Update check adds "What changed in <version> for these sets", the version's breaking and new Figma items for the sets it would change, read from the bundled `index.json`.

**The diagnosis that made it small.** Nothing new had to be recorded: every fact the notes need is already a committed record that a PR moves and a gate guards, so a release is a diff of files at two commits. The two commits are found from `version.ts` in git history (the single-parent commit that set each version: its fold), which is ground truth on `main` and needs no stored state.

**The gate.** `lint-release-notes.ts` re-derives every release from git with its own code and never imports the generator (docs/34 shape 2). Mutations, each on a synthetic fold that removes a Figma value, so the release carries a breaking item: one breaking item dropped → `BREAKING CHANGE MISSING`; a fake breaking item added → `CLAIMED, NOT IN THE DIFF`; a removal classified as a fix → `MISCLASSIFIED`; a line dropped from the page only → `MARKDOWN`; the newest release deleted → `REPRESENTED` and `INDEX`. A fold run by the old `fold.ts` (with no notes) fails `REPRESENTED`.

**Review round: what the first gate let through.** Independent review found three holes, each now closed in the gate (the generator is unchanged). (1) `TEXT` checked only that a sentence *contains* its names, so a hand-edit that reversed one (`` `select`: `state` lost its value `focus-visible-filled`. ``) passed every arm, `MARKDOWN` and `INDEX` included, because the page, the JSON and the index all agreed. The gate now restates, per kind, the phrase its sentence must carry (`SAYS`: `value-added` must say "has a new value", `value-removed` "no longer has the value", and so on), with code spans stripped so a name never supplies the phrase, and refuses a phrase that belongs to another class (`NOT_IN`). `SAYS` restates the generator's templates, which are an open owner item, so rewording a template moves `SAYS` in the same PR; that is the point of restating it. (2) The date was checked only for agreement between the index and the release; it is now bounded by git as `DATE`: no earlier than the base fold's commit day, no later than the version's own fold commit day, or today for a fold not yet committed, all in UTC, as `fold.ts` writes it. (3) A shallow clone reported its missing history as `CLAIMED, NOT IN THE DIFF` and `NOTES … (unreadable)`, blaming the notes. The gate now checks `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` first and stops as CANNOT RUN, naming `git fetch --unshallow`.

**Second review round: a merge read as a fold.** Both the generator and the gate first took each version's fold from `git log --first-parent -G 'ENGINE_VERSION = '`. With `--first-parent`, git diffs a merge against its first parent, and on a feature branch that merged `main` across a fold that parent is the branch, so the merge commit itself read as the 0.237.0 fold. The notes generated on the branch then missed every change note `main` added after the branch's last sync (28 of 29 here), and CI's view (`refs/pull/N/merge`, whose first parent is `main`) rejected them; notes generated from `main`'s side passed CI and failed a local verify instead. No set of files passed both. The fix rests on `main` being squash-only: every fold is an ordinary commit, so a merge is never a fold. The generator walks the whole history with `--no-merges`; the gate, written separately, prints each record's parents and skips any with more than one. On `main` the two walks give the same 228 versions as the old first-parent walk, so no committed release moves. The same round closed a nit: a `token-added` sentence's type word was not checked (`/is a new .*token/`), so a dimension token called a color token passed; the gate now reads the type from the contract at the fold, and checks a retyped sentence's from and to in order.

**Trap found while building it.** The first fold integration computed the notes before `regen.ts`. A committed artifact that disagrees with the code (here, a hand-edited `components.ai.json` in the synthetic fold) is rewritten by regen, so the notes described a tree the fold commit did not hold, and the gate caught it as `CLAIMED, NOT IN THE DIFF`. The fold now writes them again after regen.

**Backfill.** 0.234.0, 0.235.0 and 0.236.0, from git. 0.233.0 and earlier are refused: `component-axes.json` did not exist at the 0.232.0 fold, so those diffs cannot be read reliably. The current pending batch becomes the first release a fold writes; `release-notes.ts --pending` prints it now (0 breaking, 29 new, 1 fix).

**What the next fold does differently.** Nothing by hand: `fold.ts --dry-run` prints the counts and each breaking item, and `fold.ts` writes the four files. A fold branch that merges `main` runs `release-notes.ts --refresh`, because the range then includes `main`'s newer record changes. The open fold PR from before this change (#2582) has no notes and fails `REPRESENTED` once this lands, so it is refolded on top.

**Limits.** Figma's boolean, text and instance-swap properties are in no baseline, so a change to one shows only as "builds differently". A coded prop rename has no ledger, so it reads as one removal and one addition, which is the right class but not paired. The plugin shows the notes for the version it builds at only, not for every version since a set was built.

**Merging #2644.** The agent reference (`emit-agent-reference.ts --check`) requires every file that reads `process.argv` to be listed as a CLI or excluded with a reason. `release-notes.ts` is a hand-run entry point (`--pending`, `--version`, `--refresh`), so it joins `CLI`, and `docs/public/reference/commands.json` lists its usage and flags.

## (2026-10-16) — A border never binds an icon or text color role (Q346, #2749)

The owner's decision Q346 (audit finding O2 on #2706): a border or stroke never binds an icon or text color role, every disabled edge binds `color.disabled.border`, and the disabled edge's strength is set by the theme, not chosen per component. It supersedes #1349 and #1697.

**Where the corpus broke it, measured.** Every stroke at every coordinate of the full grid, against the scopes the committed Figma emission gives each variable. The only strokes not scoped `STROKE_COLOR` were the disabled outline edges of Button ×3, IconButton ×3 and Tag, bound to `color.disabled.icon` and, on an inverse surface, `color.inverse.disabled.icon`. Nothing else in the corpus binds a stroke to an ink or fill role. All seven now bind `color.disabled.border`. The paint census moved for exactly those seven defs: same assignment counts, different hashes.

**The gate is `lint-paint.ts` arm 5.** ACTUAL is every `paints.strokes` variable off the emitted plans. EXPECTED is the token tier's own scope for that variable, read from the committed `out/figma/<brand>/color.<mode>.json` (16 collections), never from the scope table in `emit-figma-color.ts`. Text roles are scoped `TEXT_FILL` and icon roles fill-only (#2566), so neither can sit on a stroke. The arm is one step wider than the owner's words: a stroke on a fill role fails too. The corpus had none, so the wider form needs no exception list, and the narrower one would have needed a second classification of roles that the token tier already makes. It fails on an empty scope and on a variable missing from any emission.

**The 3:1 floor went with the binding.** `test.ts` measured the disabled edge's role at ≥3:1 against the page for Button and IconButton. It measured the icon role only to justify binding it to an edge. Disabled controls are outside SC 1.4.11, so the floor is removed rather than lowered. A by-name pin on all seven defs replaces it. The edge now measures 1.48–1.80:1 against the page, the same as every other bordered control's disabled edge.

**No lever drives `color.disabled.border` yet, and this PR does not pick one.** It resolves a fixed neutral step (`neutralLow()`, `min: 0`) matched to `disabled.fill`. Sweeping `disabledStrategy` and `disabledMin` moves the disabled inks and leaves the border unchanged. How the lever should set it is a contrast-target decision for every bordered control at once, so it is filed as an owner question, #2750.

**Update corrects existing files in place.** `test-update-apply.ts` section `edge/…` builds Tag, Button and IconButton from a def copy that still binds the icon role, then updates to the current def. Each disabled edge is rebound to the disabled border on its own surface, every key and id is kept, and the next dry run reads every member current.

**Also changed.** `tools/binding-audit` no longer admits the border-on-icon binding as "by design". Its README and `tools/CLAUDE.md` say so. `skills/prism3-build-component` states the rule.

## (2026-10-16) — Segmented control: a flat pill on a neutral track (#2724, Q336 A, Q342 A)

**What landed.** The selected look the owner approved in the wireframe: the control's track fills with
`color.background.secondary` and loses its 1px outline; a selected option's indicator fills with
`color.background.primary`, with no border and no shadow; the emphasis-weight label and its bold reserve stay as the
state cue. Unselected options keep the neutral wash at hover and pressed. The selected pill holds at hover, pressed
and disabled. This supersedes Q269.3's tint and 2px primary outline and the track outline Q278 kept. The header
comment, descriptions, WCAG lines and the forced-colors note say so.

**Why these two roles.** The brief asked for a track from a "neutral subtle-fill" family. No such family exists: the
only `subtle-fill` role is `interactive.primary.subtle-fill.selected`. The two neutral candidates were measured:
- `interactive.neutral.fill.rest` (the neutral button fill) puts one brand's light focus ring at 2.90:1 against the
  track. It is also the fill the `neutralEmphasis` lever darkens, which can take it to near-black, so the neutral
  ink on it would fail under that lever. Rejected.
- `background.secondary`, the quiet surface step, clears every floor. Chosen.
`background.tertiary` also clears, with less margin (about 3.26:1 for the same ring).

**What the test proves.** In `test.ts`, every pair is read off the plans and every value is resolved from the
committed DTCG trees. That is 14 pairs × 5 brands × 4 modes, 280 measurements:
- label 4.5:1 and icon 3:1 on the pill and on the track at rest, hover and pressed, the wash composited over the
  track; lowest label 5.28:1 (one brand, dark, on the track at pressed);
- focus ring 3:1 against the track and the page; lowest 3.76:1 (one brand, light, against the track).
The old arm read the Figma exports, which cover four brands, so it said 16 cells. This one reads the DTCG trees,
which cover all five.

**Update in place.** `test-update-apply.ts` builds both sets as main built them before this change: a tinted,
outlined indicator and an outlined track. It runs the real preview and apply and reads the shim's nodes. Every
indicator loses its stroke, every selected one is filled with the page surface, and every track loses its outline
and takes the fill. Keys and the indicator and track node ids are kept, and the next dry run reads everything
current. No executor code moved: the stroke neutralization that clears an unplanned stroke already does it. So
`EXECUTOR_REVISION` is unchanged.

**Mutations, each failing by name.**
- Selected label pointed at `color.text.tertiary` → `#2724 contrast over 5 brands × 4 modes`.
- 2px border put back on the selected indicator → `#2724 Q336/Q342 segment indicator`.
- The track's outline put back and its fill dropped → `#2418 Q269.7/Q269.8 control (#2724 Q336 track)` and the
  contrast arm.
- The executor's `set('strokes', [])` neutralization removed → `seg/border removed`, `seg/track outline removed`
  (and `seg/updated`, `seg/control updated`, whose verify catches it).

**Left for the owner (not blocking, recorded in `notes.unverified`).** In the high-contrast modes the surface steps
are one color, so the track and the pill both read as the page and the bold label is the only cue. In dark modes
the page surface is darker than the track, so the pill reads as set into the track rather than raised. A disabled
selected option keeps its pill, so the disabled control still shows its value.

## (2026-10-16) — Update apply: the verdict reads the build pass's misses (#2477)

**What happened.** `applyVerdict` built its headline and `ok` from `stopped`, `identity`, `content`, `refused` and the
counts, and never read `SetOutcome.misses`. A member whose as-built record the host refused kept its old stamp and
read out of date on the next dry run (#2373 holds that), but the verdict said `✓ updated 45 in place` and counted it.

**The fix.** In `update-apply.ts`, any miss makes its set "not verified", the headline the verify lines already use.
A miss of the form `<member>.asBuilt -> NOT RECORDED (…)` whose member the build listed as updated is that member
not finished: it leaves the set's "updated in place" count and the headline's, and gets its own line by name. Any
other miss is quoted on one line with its own reason. The owner's held question (comment on #2477) recommended A;
the wording is built as A and listed as an owner item on the PR, along with the line for other misses, which A
described only in outline.

**Dry run and apply.** Nothing in the dry run moves: a host refusing a write is not something a dry run can see.
The verdict now says what the next dry run will say, which is the agreement that matters here.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies.** Misses are named by node, not by member (`label.characters -> …`), so only the
record miss can be pinned to a member. The others stay at set level on purpose: guessing a member from a node name
would mis-count a set with two members sharing a part name.

**Found by the full suite, not by the arms written for it.** `unbuilt/relay left` (`test-canvas-furniture.ts`) went
to "⚠ 1 set not verified": the build's footprint check compared a member Prism3 didn't build, which the update left
as it is, with its sibling, and reported the size difference. That miss is about a member the update never touched,
the same class the outcome already dropped (`ALREADY PRESENT`, `STALE`). So `out.misses` now also drops any miss that
names a member this run skipped. On a real file, a designer's own member of another size would otherwise have made
every update read "not verified".

**Tests.** `recordfail/verdict` and `recordfail/set verdict` hold the headline, the count and the named line on the
icon and a set member; `misses/other` holds the set-level line from an outcome written out by hand; `unbuilt/relay
left` holds the skipped member's miss left out.

**The skipped-member match is by whole name (review).** The first cut matched with `includes`, and members are named
`name=<glyph>`: the shipped icons hold 20 prefix pairs (`name=check` ⊂ `name=check-circle`, `name=eye` ⊂ `name=eye-off`),
so a skip on `name=check` swallowed the refused record on `name=check-circle` and the verdict went back to ✓ with it
counted, which is #2477 again. `namesMember` now takes a name only where it starts the miss or follows a space, and ends
it or meets a space, `.` or `/` (the forms the build uses: `<member>.asBuilt`, `<member>/<part>.slot`, `footprint ->
<member> measures … but <member> measures …`). A `.` boundary alone would let `size=1` claim `size=1.5.asBuilt`, so where
a longer known member name matches at the same place, that one is named. Arms: `recordfail/prefix` (the review's probe
through the shim) and `misses/whole name` (the forms, by hand). Left as it was, and an owner call: a footprint miss that
names both a skipped and an updated member is still dropped whole, even when the updated member is the one whose size
moved.

## (2026-10-16) — Update: a damaged member with a layer added by hand reads as the apply treats it (#2413)

**What happened.** A member that draws wrong (#2379, for example a stored #000000 paint) and also has a layer
added or removed by hand was "to update" in the dry run, because damage was classified first. The apply's `plan()`
reads the structural hand edit and skips the member under every choice (§5: its paths can no longer be trusted
node by node).  So the dry run promised a repair the apply never made, and the apply's skip line said only
`a layer was added or removed by hand`, so a reader could not tell the member still drew wrong.

**The fix (the issue's option A, built and listed as an owner item).** In `update-plan.ts` a structural hand edit
outranks damage: such a member counts as `handEdited` ("N members edited by hand", existing wording), and its
damage stays in the difference lines. The state entry carries the damage as `faultLine` strings, so the apply's
skip reason reads `a layer was added or removed by hand, and it draws other than its plan (<faults>)`. The only
new words are ", and it draws other than its plan".

**Scope held back.** A member whose reactions dangle (#2466) is damage too and has the same order: dangling
reactions still read "to update" over a structural edit, and the apply still skips it. Left as it was and filed
as #2674, since the issue and the held question are about drawn damage only.

**Trap.** `faultLine` on a fault at the member's root writes `<member>/..fills` (part `.` joined with `.`). The
skip reason inherits that, as the verify lines already do (filed as #2675); the test reads the field and the
stored color, not the join.

**Tests.** `damage/under a layer dry run` holds the state, the counts, the paint line and the set line;
`damage/under a layer skip (keep|overwrite|accept)` holds the reason and that the member is left exactly.

## (2026-10-16) — Docs: a generated Figma conventions file for agents and tools (#2647, Q306.2 A)

Owner Q306.2 A, part of #2637. `packages/engine/emit-figma-conventions.ts` writes `docs/public/reference/figma-conventions.json`, served beside the agent reference and linked from `llms.txt`. It says how a Prism3 Figma file is laid out and named, so a spec tool, the rebind skill, TokenPress or an agent can read one without reading the engine.

**What it holds, and where each part is read from.**
- **Pages:** `TAXONOMY` and `NEST_PREFIX` (`file-taxonomy.ts`): the cover, each section's header and order (alphabetical or as listed), and every `↳ ` page with the defs it holds.
- **Components:** the projector itself. `figmaAnatomySet` and `planSetProperties` run over every def, so each set's name (its def id), member count, variant properties (read back from `planComponentName`'s `key=value` names), other properties (with an instance swap's target) and page are what the plugin writes. Code-only axes and states are the def's `variants` and `states` that `figmaProperties` does not project; the schema already refuses any that `anatomy.codeOnly` does not admit. The `_` building-block prefix is flagged per def, with the rule cited from `component-schema.ts`.
- **Icons:** `iconComponentName` (the namespace is `iconComponentName('')`, so a renamed namespace moves every glyph entry), `ICON_INSET_CHILD`, and the glyphs the icon def's plans build.
- **Native slots:** every `SLOT` property `planSetProperties` declares, with its settings and preferred defs.
- **Variables:** `figmaArtifacts` over the canonical default theme, the same function `emit-figma.ts` writes `out/figma/**` with, so each collection and its modes are the ones the plugin creates. The fallback root is asked of `brandTheme` (the default input with its root removed) rather than read off the source text: a first cut matched `input.root ?? 'prism'` as text, and the same string sits in a header comment of `theme.ts`, so a mutation of the code line passed.
- **Canvas furniture:** `CANVAS_FURNITURE`, the `_Label`, `_inverse-backdrop` and `_scrim-backdrop` templates with their properties and bound variables, the `_Section-header` and `_Headings` file templates, and the shared plugin data tag a reader uses to skip furniture.

**Its own gate, the agent reference's posture.** `--check` regenerates in memory and compares with the committed file, reporting per page, section, component, glyph, slot, collection, style file, furniture membership and template. It also fails by name when a promised section comes out empty, so a source that stops yielding data cannot pass as a smaller file (docs/34: represented, not counted). No engine version, for the reason `emit-agent-reference.ts` gives. It is also a regen step (review round 1): every component PR moves this file, so the documented path (regen, then commit) has to write it. It sits in a list of its own, `REFERENCE_ARTIFACTS`, as the analysis reports do in `REPORT_ARTIFACTS` (#2651), so `lint-emission-version.ts` never reads it as owing a bump. `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` and the ci.yml count rose by one together. `regen.ts --check` says the file drifted; `--check` here says which convention moved. The new file reads `process.argv`, so it joins the agent reference's `CLI` list and `commands.json` is regenerated.

**Mutations (committed first, restored with `git reset --hard`), each failing by name:** `NEST_PREFIX` changed → `changed in the code: pages prefix` and every page; the Veil page renamed → `missing from the file: page ↳ Veils` / `gone from the code: page ↳ Veil`; the icon namespace changed in `iconComponentName` → `missing from the file: icon glyph/arrow-down` and on; `LABEL_SET` recased → `furniture template _label`; `FURNITURE_KEY` changed → `furniture tag`; `link` dropped from `CANVAS_FURNITURE` → `gone from the code: furniture on link`; the fallback root changed in `brandTheme` → `variables root default`; the `opacity` collection renamed in the emitter → `collection opacities` / `collection opacity`; slots filtered to nothing → `nativeSlots.slots is empty`. Renaming `CORE_TIER` breaks the Figma emitter itself before this gate reads anything.

**Trap, met in this PR.** A mutation's `git reset --hard` after a failed `--check` in the same `&&` chain wiped an uncommitted edit to the generator itself; the commit that should have come first was after the check in the chain. Commit, then mutate, as separate commands.

**Stated limits.** A def's code-only *props* are not listed: no schema field links a prop to the Figma property that carries it, and inferring one by name gave false hits. Each component entry links its component doc, where `anatomy.codeOnly` admits them in prose. Mode names are the default theme's; a brand that opts out of dark or high contrast emits fewer. The knowledge-base source the issue cites for the reference shape was not in the knowledge base at its current head; the file follows the issue's list.

**The placement rule, corrected in review.** A first cut said a part shared by several components sits under Subcomponents. Nothing derives that: Flush Icon Button and Image Placeholder sit there and no def nests either, while Divider and Button are nested by two defs each and sit under Components. `file-taxonomy.ts` records section membership as the owner's call. The rule now says membership is set in the taxonomy, not derived from what nests what.

**Prototype reactions are not in this file.** `hover` and `pressed` appear only as values of the `state` axis. The reaction chain (#2703, reversed by Q344 in #2744) is written by `reactions.ts`, which this generator does not read, so neither chain is stated here and #2744 landing moves nothing in it.

## (2026-10-16) — TokenPress types unscoped font variables by path (#2616, Q334 step 1)

TokenPress typed a font variable's DTCG `$type` from its Figma scope alone: `FONT_FAMILY` → `fontFamily`,
`FONT_WEIGHT` → `fontWeight`. That is why Q292 A kept `core/font/family/*`, `core/font/weight/*` and
`core/font/weight-role/*` scoped while every other `core` row went unscoped. Unscoped, the exporter
agreement gate fails 69 rows across 4 brands: family as `string`, the numeric weight as `dimension` and
the weight-role alias as `number`. Reproduced on this branch by stripping the three groups' scopes from
the committed `out/figma/*/core.font.json` and running `tools/exporter-comparison/gate.ts`.

**Fix.** `TokenTypeDetector` gains `isFontFamilyVariable` / `isFontWeightVariable`, which match whole path
segments: a `font` segment followed by `family` or `weight` (or `weight-…`, so `weight-role` matches), or a
single `font-family` / `fontWeight` / `font_weight` segment. `mapVariableTypeToDTCG` uses them only after
the font scope checks (family, weight and style on a STRING; weight, line height, size and letter spacing on
a FLOAT), so a variable with a font scope types exactly as before. A variable with no font scope reaches the
name check. That covers an unscoped variable, and also one on Figma's default `ALL_SCOPES`, which is the
change most public files will see: `font/weight/700` on All scopes was a `dimension` and is now a
`fontWeight` (review on #2731; pinned by its own test). The FLOAT weight check sits *before* the
breakpoint rule, because that rule types any bare-number last segment as a `dimension`, and that is how
`font/weight/700` came back as one. The weight-role alias needed nothing of its own: with no scope on it
or its target, it reaches the same name check.

**Verified.** With the three groups unscoped in the committed emission (not committed here), the gate
reports 0 type disagreements in all 4 brands. With the scopes left as they are, the gate output is
unchanged. New `tests/unit/font-type-by-name.test.ts` (7, in the `ADDED` census), including an `ALL_SCOPES` case and a font-scope-wins case. Mutations: dropping the
FLOAT name check fails four of its tests by name, dropping the STRING one fails two, and moving the STRING
family check back above the FONT_WEIGHT / FONT_STYLE scope check fails the font-scope-wins test.

**Why two PRs.** The order matters. Unscoping the emission before TokenPress can type by path turns the gate
red, so this PR lands first and changes no engine output. The emission change (`scopes: []` on
`core/font/weight/*`) follows as its own PR. `core/font/family/*` stays scoped. This change would make that
scope removable for typing, so that call goes to the owner on #2616.

**Not changed, and one deliberate change.** A variable with an explicit non-font scope on a font path (say
`font/weight/700` scoped WIDTH_HEIGHT) now types by its name, `fontWeight`, where it was a `dimension`. That
is unlikely in a real file, and the name is the better signal there, so no code guards it. The one non-font scope
checked before the name is OPACITY: a FLOAT `font/weight/*` scoped OPACITY stays `number`, as before. A STRING
`font/weight/*` with no scope still types as `string`. Prism3 emits none, and the
existing `FONT_STYLE` route covers Figma's own string-weight convention. The cut rows (`font/style/*`) stay
`string`; they have no DTCG pair to agree with.

## (2026-10-15) — Style guides: the icon-size table is titled "Icon size" (#2728, owner decision Q341 A)

**What moved.** `planVariableTables` in `apps/plugin/src/style-guide.ts` titles a dimension table whose rows are all icon sizes (`varKind` → `iconSize`) "Icon size". Before this, a semantic dimension table took its collection's name, so the `icon` collection's table read "Icon", the same title as the icon color family's table on `↳ Semantic tokens`. The tables filter matches by title, so a filter for "Icon" drew both.

**Why the kind and not the collection name.** The rows' kind is what the table holds. A rule keyed on a collection named `icon` would miss a file that names it otherwise. A rule that renamed any dimension title that matched a color title would have to invent a noun for each case, and that is a naming call for the owner (filed as #2729). The rule also covers a primitive icon-size table, which was titled from its last shared segment ("Size") and would have collided with the size table's title.

**The key does not move.** It is still `dimension|<collection id>|<prefix>`. A rerun finds the earlier table by key and retitles it through the existing path: the frame name, the header title and the title record change only while they read what the generator last wrote. The table is not superseded, so #2704's delete path never sees it. §35e of `test-style-guide.ts` plants a table as an earlier build left it ("Icon" in all three places) and checks that the rerun keeps the same frame, retitles it, and deletes nothing.

**Collision audit.** Every brand emits the same Figma collections (one adds a layout mode). On `↳ Semantic tokens` the color tables are titled by family: Background, Foreground, Text, Icon, Interactive, Disabled, Border, Scrim, Veil, Field, Inverse. A semantic dimension table is titled by its collection: `space`, `radius`, `size`, `icon` and `control` give Space, Radius, Size, Icon and Control. The other tables there are titled by type (Border width, Font weight roles, Text styles). "Icon" was the only repeat. §35e plans phase 2's file, the icon collection and the color collections together and checks that every Semantic tokens title is unique. The mechanism stays general: a foreign file with a dimension collection named like a color family (`border`, `text`) would still repeat a title. Fixing that needs a noun for each case, so it is filed as #2729 rather than fixed here.

## (2026-10-15) — `out/tokens.html` is built on demand, not committed (Q319.6)

Owner decision Q319.6 on #2583: the 1.8 MB preview page leaves the committed set. `npm run tokens-html` (root `package.json`, documented in `packages/engine/README.md` and `visualize.ts`'s header) writes it to `packages/engine/out/tokens.html`, which is gitignored. Nothing user-facing served it — the site build (`build-site.mjs`) publishes only the studio bundle, and no app or doc linked it — so no owner question was needed.

- **Why a skip list and not just a removed step.** Taking `visualize` out of `regen.ts`'s `STEPS` is enough for CI, but a developer who runs `npm run tokens-html` then has a gitignored file in `out/`, and two walkers read `out/` wholesale: regen's comparison universe (whose count `verify.ts` and `ci.yml` pin) and `lint-payload-manifest.ts` (which would call it UNCLASSIFIED once its `preview` rule is gone, or STALE in CI if the rule stayed). So `ON_DEMAND_OUT` in `regen.ts` names it, and both walks skip it.
- **The trap a skip list sets, and the check that closes it.** A name both walks skip is invisible to the comparison, so re-adding `visualize` to `STEPS` would have been silent. `check()` now stamps each on-demand file's mtime before regenerating and fails `on-demand packages/engine/out/tokens.html (regen wrote it …)` if any step touched it. The mtime, not the bytes: a step that rewrites identical bytes is still a step writing it. A copy that gets **committed** (`git add -f`, a lost `.gitignore` line, a conflict resolved toward an older branch) is skipped by both walks too, so `check()` also reads `git ls-files` for each on-demand name and fails `on-demand packages/engine/out/tokens.html (git tracks it …)` (review on #2685). It reads the index, not the disk, so a local ignored copy still passes; a git that cannot answer fails closed.
- **`test.ts` read the committed page** for the #2586 check (no type specimen for a non-typography leaf under `type.*`). It now renders its own copy with `visualize.ts --out <tmpdir>`; a failed render leaves zero specimens and the check fails by its own name.
- `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` in `verify.ts` and the count in `ci.yml` both drop by one: 194 → 193 at the base this was written on, 195 → 194 after merging the Link PR's new artifact, 198 → 197 after merging the flush icon button and the CHANGELOG move, 199 → 198 after merging the agent reference (#2644), 200 → 199 after merging the password field (#2648). `docs/inventory/surfaces.*` still list the page as written by `visualize.ts:599`; it is a snapshot of `b020716` by its own header, so it was left alone.
- **The prose gates kept the page (review on #2685).** `lint-us-english.ts` and `lint-voice.ts` walked `out/` wholesale, so they used to scan the committed page. With the file gone they stopped seeing it in CI but still saw a local copy — so the same commit was green in CI and red on a laptop that had built the page (the reviewer's demonstration: `colour` in the page heading passes with no copy, fails with one). Under docs/34 that is a scope that shrank with no diff in either gate. Fixed by keeping the coverage rather than dropping it: both gates skip `ON_DEMAND_OUT` in their `out/` walk and scan a copy `regen.ts`'s `renderOnDemand()` renders into a temp dir, so CI and a laptop scan the same fresh bytes. A failed render is `blind`, and the render is its own `REQUIRED_SURFACES` line, so dropping it fails the scope check by name. Each run of either gate pays one `visualize.ts` render (a few seconds).
- **Merging #2644.** The agent reference (`emit-agent-reference.ts --check`) requires every file that reads `process.argv` to be listed as a CLI or excluded with a reason. `visualize.ts` now reads `--out` and is run by hand, so it joins `CLI`, and `docs/public/reference/commands.json` lists it. That file ships under `/docs`, so its header line now says "visualizer" and its bare usage line says what it writes rather than "the same".
