## (2026-10-15) — Agent reference: the style-guide `tables` example uses the default root, and a legacy namespace in it fails by name (Q313.2 A)

**What moved.** The `bad-args` refusal for `style-guide`'s `args.tables` in `apps/plugin/src/agent-protocol.ts` gave its example table title with a legacy client namespace as the root. `docs/public/reference/commands.json` quotes that refusal verbatim, so every agent reading the reference was shown another brand's root as the way to name a Prism3 table. The example now reads `['Primary — prism']`: `prism` is the default `theme.root`, and the title shape (`<collection> — <root>`, drawn when a file holds more than one root) is unchanged. The rest of the refusal text is unchanged. The reference is regenerated from the source, not edited.

**The check.** `emit-agent-reference.ts` now refuses to write, and `--check` fails, when the generated reference spells a legacy namespace anywhere, and names the entry that holds it (`legacy namespace '<ns>' in agent-link command style-guide`). The list (`LEGACY_NAMESPACES`) is typed in the gate, not read from the engine's brand inputs: a list derived from what the engine emits today would shrink when an input was retired and stop catching the name it exists for (docs/34). It matches a whole word in any case, so a scale name like `pds3` does not hit.

**Why not an existing gate.** No gate read `docs/public/reference/` for a namespace. `--check` alone would not have caught a return either: a source edit followed by a regen moves both sides together, and the byte comparison goes green. The new check reads the generated text, so it fails before and after the regen.

**The check checks itself (review on `69b6dad6`).** Because `--check` cannot see a source edit plus a regen, the matcher is the only thing that would catch a return, and a review mutation showed a one-character change to it (the `y` flag, so it only matched at index 0) shipped the legacy example green. `legacyNamespaceSelfCheck` now runs before the real scan, the `lint-skills.ts` pattern: every listed name, in lower and upper case and in the `<root>.<sub>` form, must be reported inside a refusal-shaped probe and named by its entry; `pds3`, `prism` and `prism.color` must not be. A broken matcher exits 1 with "the legacy-namespace check is broken" before any reference is read or written.

**Mutations (each committed first, restored with `git reset --hard`).**
- The example set back to the legacy root at the source → `--check` and the plain write both exit 1 with `legacy namespace '<ns>' in agent-link command style-guide`.
- The same root in upper case with its sub-namespace → the same failure, naming the upper-case spelling.

**Left alone.** Two doc comments in the plugin (`messages.ts`, `style-guide.ts`) still use the old title as an example. Neither reaches the agent reference, so they are outside this decision; filed separately if the owner wants them aligned.

## (2026-10-15) — Per-instance overrides on a nested instance: a text and a swap (#2645)

**Status:** engine schema + projection, both executors, the component read-back, the plugin shim, List. ENGINE minor
(change note). `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 25 → 26 (Dialog, #2652, took 23, Password field, #2648, took 24 and the prototype
reactions fix, #2703, took 25 before this merged; git merged the two identical `25` lines without a conflict,
which is the #2551 shape `lint-executor-revision.ts` checks against main's current number). CONTRACT unchanged: no token path moves.

### What changed

- **`PartDef.overrides`** on a `nest` or `absolute` part that is `nest-fixed` or `nest-exposed`:
  `{ texts?: { <nested texts key>: string }, swaps?: { <nested swaps key>: <icon glyph> } }`. The validator refuses it
  on any other kind or relation, and refuses an empty map or value. The projection (`nestOverridesOf`) resolves each
  key against the nested def in the registry, to the Figma property name the nested set declares (`figmaName`, else
  the key), and each glyph to `icon/<glyph>`; an unknown key or an undrawn glyph throws. Plans carry
  `nestOverrides: [{ property, type: 'TEXT' | 'INSTANCE_SWAP', value }]`, only where declared, so every other plan
  is byte-identical.
- **One writer, two executors.** `applyNestOverrides` finds the ONE key on the instance's `componentProperties` whose
  name before `#` and type match, resolves a swap's component name to its node id, writes `setProperties` per
  override and reads each back. None or two keys, an unresolvable component, a refusal and a discard are named misses.
  The plugin calls it; the paste payload ships its source, spliced in only when a plan carries overrides (the shell
  budget), so every other payload is byte-identical. Written during the build, unlike `isExposedInstance`:
  `setProperties` needs no containing component.
- **Update path.** The in-place branch writes the same call on the instance it keeps. An existing file whose nested
  instance has no override yet: the plan stamp moves, the dry run lists `nestOverrides` as a change on that part (no
  replacement), and Update writes it in place, every member and nested instance keeping its key and id. An override
  the designer typed by hand reads as a hand edit (the as-built record already hashes an instance's
  `componentProperties`) and is kept, as every hand edit is. A value the instance already holds is not written again.
- **Dependencies.** `build-deps.ts` counts a swap override's component as a target, so the icon set is built first.
- **Read-back.** `anatomy-readback.ts` gains `nestOverrides`, read off the instance's own `componentProperties`; a swap
  is named through a new `componentById` port (the host's catalog: `hostPorts` searches components on first use; the
  round-trip asks the host's `getNodeByIdAsync`).
- **The shim models the override API.** An instance's `componentProperties` are its main's definitions (a live
  member's set, or `componentProps` for a catalog name) at the value it was given or the default; `setProperties`
  refuses a key that is not a definition's full `#id` key, a VARIANT or SLOT key, a value of the wrong type, and a swap
  value that is no component id. Component ids are now one per component, stable across searches (they were the
  search's own counter, so two components could share one, which a swap value cannot survive). Set ids moved to `74:`.
  The engine's payload stub got the same model for the paste and parity arms.
- **List** (the one def on main with a decided value): items 2 to 8 override List.Item's `value` text ("number") to
  "2." to "8.". The two "neither executor writes" notes are gone, and List's Figma numbering note says the built items
  read "1." to "8.".

### Verification

- `test-roundtrip`: a plan with overrides is built with its nested sets first (`liveRoot` + `prebuildDependencies`), so
  each instance has the properties its set really declared; List (63 TEXT overrides) and a test-only List whose first
  item swaps its icon to `check` (9 INSTANCE_SWAP overrides) read back with 0 divergences.
- `test-update-apply` `overrides/…`: a List built from plans with the overrides stripped, one item hand-typed "2)";
  the dry run lists the change on items 2 to 8 and replaces nothing, Update writes "1." to "8." in place keeping every
  id and the hand edit, and the next dry run reads the other 8 members current.
- `test.ts` `#2645 …`: validator refusals, the projected plan (literals), projection refusals, the payload shipped
  only when needed, the payload's writes and its swap id, and plugin/payload miss parity.

### Dialog (#2652) and Password field (#2648), both merged before this PR

- **Not applied here** (filed as #2671): this PR's merge of `main` keeps both mechanisms side by side and moves no
  Dialog or Password field output.
- **Dialog:** `close` → `overrides: { swaps: { icon: 'close' } }` (IconButton.Neutral's `swap icon`); `cancelInline`
  and `cancelStacked` → `overrides: { texts: { label: 'Cancel' } }`; `confirmInline` and `confirmStacked` →
  `overrides: { texts: { label: 'Save' } }` (Q303.13's placeholder copy).
- **Password field:** #2648 landed its own text-only `nestTexts` (schema field, plan field, a branch in each
  executor, a `nestTexts` read-back predicate, a `compTexts` payload-stub model). The toggle's
  `nestTexts: { label: 'Show' }` becomes `overrides: { texts: { label: 'Show' } }`, and `nestTexts` with its rule,
  branches, predicate and stub model goes, leaving one mechanism. That is #2671's work.

### Traps

- **A named inner function breaks the shipped source.** The bundler wraps it in `__name(...)`, which does not exist in
  the paste payload; the first payload run threw `__name is not defined`. `applyNestOverrides` reads inline instead.
- **A catalog name answers before the live set.** With `liveRoot`, a `comps` entry named like a def resolves as a bare
  component first, with no properties. The round-trip's override rows therefore pass only the FPO swap target as a
  catalog name.

**Review round.** The test-only swap row first swapped to `check`, which is already List.Item's `swapDefault`. The writer skips a value the instance already holds, so the plugin executor's swap write never ran and the read-back passed on the default — an expected value equal to the subject's starting state (docs/34). It now swaps to `close`, and a premise line fails if the row's glyph ever equals the default again. The "two same-named keys is a miss" guard had no test; `test.ts` now drives the shared writer with a hand-built instance holding two TEXT properties named `number`.

**Combined re-gate with #2703 (cloud lane).** One mutation outside the author's table removed the writer's
per-override read-back, so a write the host accepts and does not keep went unreported. It passed every gate,
because no host in any test discards an override. `test.ts` now drives `applyNestOverrides` over a hand-built
instance whose `setProperties` keeps nothing, and the same mutation fails `#2645 discarded write` by name.

## (2026-10-15) — Style guides: a full rerun no longer crashes after deleting a superseded table (#2704)

A full style-guide rerun deleted one superseded table, then threw `in getPluginData: The node (instance sublayer or table cell) … does not exist` and stopped before the re-flow, so new tables landed over old ones. Each rerun deleted one more table and crashed again.

**The diagnosis.** The superseded-table loop walks `framesOn(page)`, which is `findAllWithCriteria({ types: ['FRAME'] })` gathered once, before the loop. That list holds every frame on the page, not only the tables: each table's grid, its cells, and the frames inside its `_Section-header` instance. After `f.remove()` the loop went on to the next frame in the list, a frame inside the table it had just removed, and read its plugin data. The host had invalidated the whole subtree with the table. #1795 fixed the reads off the removed frame itself; this is the same shape, one level down.

**The fix.** Before the remove, the loop records the ids of everything inside the table, and it skips any frame whose id is in that set. Ids stay readable on a removed node. Nested frames are still candidates, as before: a table moved inside another frame is still reported as kept (`moved`).

**The shim was too forgiving.** `test-style-guide.ts` invalidated only the removed node, so its descendants stayed readable and #1795's test 6a passed while the host failed. `remove()` now invalidates the whole subtree, and a second `remove()` throws. With the stricter shim, 6a fails on the old code too.

**The test.** Section 6b: a full run draws, two groups are regrouped so two tables are superseded (each header is an instance with a frame inside), and a full rerun must delete both, re-flow, report ok and leave no overlap. A second case covers recovery: a run crashes before its re-flow (the host refuses the delete), then the next full run deletes what is superseded and overlaps nothing. That second case passes on the old code as well. A table the crashed run created carries its position record (`AT_KEY` is written at creation), so the next full run re-flows it. No separate overlap defect was found for that case.

**Mutation, failing by name.** With the skip line removed, `6a: one run deletes two superseded, unedited tables and names both…` and `6b: a full rerun deletes both superseded tables, re-flows and reports ok…` both fail, each with the host's "does not exist" error, and so does the recovery case of 6b (its rerun hits the same read).

## (2026-10-15) — Ecosystem diagram: three interface lanes and a compare table, one data file checked against the code (#2637, Q300.4, Q304 A)

Lane 3 of #2637. `docs/public/ecosystem/` holds `ecosystem.json` and `index.html`, one self-contained page with two views, and a new CI gate, `lint-ecosystem.ts`. The first draft was a node graph; the owner's review (Q304) found it mixed interfaces, inputs, connections and checks into one layer. This entry describes the restructure.

**The shape (Q304 A).** Left to right: inputs (levers by hand, design.md, tool arguments) sit at the start of each lane; three interface lanes (Web studio, Figma plugin, Agent) each list their features, shared ones first and in the same order, then "Only here"; the engine hub; outputs, with the Figma file and the code library as groups. Connections (MCP, the command line, the agent link, the desktop bridge, the Figma MCP scripts) are labels on the agent lane's arrows, not boxes. Checks (contrast contracts, code scoring, CI gates, the token contract) are badges on the boxes they act on, behind "Show checks". "Compare interfaces" is a feature-by-lane table generated from the same `features` list. Traces follow the lanes. Below 900 px the diagram is a stacked lane list.

**The page draws arrows by measuring the layout,** not from hand-placed coordinates: boxes sit in a CSS grid by `column`, and the arrows are recomputed from their rects on every resize. That removed the old `at` and `via` fields and the trap that went with them (an edge passing behind a node it does not touch). An edge out of the agent lane to the Figma file takes `route: "under"`, below the engine column.

**Feature facts, from the code and the inventory branch (`docs/surface-inventory`).** One correction to the Q304 wording: "only Figma … updates" is not what the code does. Update, capture baseline and adopt are agent-only: they are agent link commands with no `UiToMain` message, so no panel button reaches them. The diagram shows them in the agent lane only, and the gate holds that. Everything else Q304 named matches: only the plugin (and the agent, through it) applies, builds, prunes, sets up the file and draws style guides; only the agent scores code. Web and Figma share every studio feature except two: loading a brand from a Figma file (planned, #677) and the agent link switch. "Keep the brand" is shared with different mechanisms (browser storage on the web, the file in Figma).

**The gate's new LANES arm, and why it is independent.** It reads three facts from code, never from the data: `toolDefs` (MCP tools), `AGENT_COMMANDS`, and the `UiToMain` union parsed from `apps/plugin/src/messages.ts`. MCP tools may sit only in an agent lane, and every tool is claimed. Plugin messages may sit only in a figma lane, and a feature that sends one cannot claim the web. An agent command that is also a `UiToMain` type needs the figma lane; one that is not must not have it. The gate also checks that the plugin still imports the studio's whole entry, so the premise of the host rule below cannot rot silently. The first run caught two real drifts: the two segmented-control defs that landed on main the same day, and `ui-ready` on a feature that both hosts have (`ui-ready` is boot plumbing; it is now in the gate's authored `PLUMBING` list).

**The REACH arm (added after review).** The review found that a feature could claim a UI lane the code cannot reach: `score-code` given web and figma lanes, both citing `preview.ts`, passed with exit 0, because the host rules fired only when one UI lane was present without the other, and any file with any `PRISM3_HOST` branch satisfied them. The fix reads the import graph. The gate walks each lane's bundle from its build entry points (`apps/studio/src/entry.ts`; `apps/plugin/src/ui/entry.ts` plus `main.ts`), following value imports and `@prism3/engine/*` through the engine's `exports` map. An authored `TOOL_MODULE` names the engine export each MCP tool runs, held against `mcp.ts`. A feature whose agent tools run an export can claim web or figma only if that bundle imports the export, and must claim it if the bundle does. Host-only features now name an `anchor` string that must sit within 8 lines after the matching branch. Two things were tried and dropped. Module-level reach was too coarse: the plugin reaches `eval.ts` for `normalizeRef` (through `component-schema.ts`) without scoring anything, so the check is by imported name. And a naive `/* … */` strip swallowed real imports, because a string held `/*`, so only comments that open a line are stripped. With that fixed, the walk's file sets equal esbuild's metafile inputs for both lanes (119 web, 212 figma), checked once by hand while writing it. The check is not wired in, since esbuild is not an engine dependency.

**Trap.** The `PRISM3_HOST` anchor rule only decides features that cite a source. A shared panel that quietly behaves differently per host passes. Read the code before claiming a UI feature is the same on both hosts.

**Drift after merging main (764513fc, then e4a2207).** #2635 landed while this was in review and made `figma-motion` false: motion now reaches Figma as TIMING (durations, in seconds) and EASING (curves, easing roles, springs) variables, through `emit-figma-dims.ts`. The node is now `shipped`, because the one family not written, a transition, has no Figma form by design (`MOTION_FIGMA_COVERAGE`). A re-scan of every other `purpose` against main's code found three more false claims that the gate cannot see, because it checks lanes and sources, not prose. `style-guides` listed four table kinds; #2353 batch 1 and #2584 added border width, opacity, effect and gradient (`PHASE_TYPES`). `figma-components` said one page per set; `file-taxonomy.ts` puts a family on one page. `agent-link` said nothing in a command is evaluated; that holds only for the release build, since #2544 added the dev-only `run-code`. One lane `via` was also overstated: the decisions log comes back from `theme_brand` by default, not always, because `include: []` drops it. **Trap:** `lint-ecosystem.ts` passing says nothing about whether a `purpose` sentence is still true. Re-read the prose after any merge that touches a node's sources.

No engine bump owed: no emitted artifact and no projected component surface moves.

**Delta round (CHANGES REQUESTED on `cf4e360f`): main moved again.** Merging `main` (`6ce33622`) turned `lint-ecosystem` red with four missing members, not the one the delta check saw: Link (#2632) and the three flush icon button families (#2607), which landed after that check's merge. All four are in `component-defs`, in `componentDefs` order. The cards were re-read against what else landed: the engine changelog's move to `packages/engine/CHANGELOG.md` (#2687) touches no card (`token-contract` cites `version.ts` for `CONTRACT_VERSION`, which stayed); Link has its own page and the flush icon button's three families share one, as the Buttons page does, so "each family on its own page" holds; and the skills card now names `.claude/skills/` (#2680), the links that make a session in this repo load the four skills. The generated reports under `docs/public/reports/` (#2654) appear on no output card; adding one changes the approved layout, so it is filed (#2694) rather than drawn here.

Then Dialog (#2652) landed before this push, and the members arm went red again on `dialog`. ## (2026-10-15) — Skills audit fixes: theme, consume, rebind, and the wrong claims in build-component (#2677, Q320.1)

**What changed.** The claims the Q320.1 audit found false or superseded on `main`, in four shipped skills, plus four `lint-skills.ts` checks for the classes a mechanical check can see. The full audit, including what is missing and the `prism3-build-component` rewrite plan, is the comment on #2677.

- **`prism3-theme`:** `radiusHairline` is retired (#2053), not an opt-in; a pinned neutral still needs `hue` and `chroma` beside `anchor` (the schema requires both); `controlShape` takes four values, not two, and reaches fields and checkboxes; the default-action note is quoted as the engine prints it; the `x-prism3:` block reads ten keys and drops any other without a warning; `theme_brand` returns contracts and notes by default, not the tree, and `theme_from_brief` and `export_theme` are named; the dead `inverse` entry left `omits:`.
- **`prism3-consume`:** primitives are `core.palette.*`, `core.dimension.*`, `core.font.*`; disabled inks carry a 3:1 contract (4.5:1 in the high-contrast modes, `modes.ts`'s `disabledTarget`), so the skill no longer tells an agent to drop them from the self-check; `text.secondary` and `border.tertiary` name the surfaces they are actually measured on; code builds from the base + overlay projection, not the single tree's `mode_overrides`; `export_theme` and `score_consumption` replace "call `theme_brand` for the tree".
- **`prism3-rebind`:** tabs now exist (and accordion, list, divider, segmented control), so they leave the "no component" list; `radiusHairline` gives way to `controlShape`; the layout mode is the one for the frame's width, named by the brand's breakpoints (`xs` in one brand); a legacy grid style maps to Prism3's grid style first; legacy effects map to `shadow/*`, `shadow-dark/*` and the gradient styles before being left on purpose.
- **`prism3-build-component`, WRONG items only** (the rewrite waits for #2660, #2645 and #2648): `KB_BRIEF_CATEGORY` is derived from `schema/kb-briefs.json` (#2488), not an authored table; image-placeholder's `ratio` has seven values; `lint-hit-target`'s exceptions are `SMALL_SIZE` and `FLUSH_MEMBERS`, not "the small Button"; axis order is #2501's fixed order with the three fields as the named exception, and Figma's default is the top-left member, not the first child; three baselines move with a projection, not two (`schema/component-axes.json`).

**The four new checks in `lint-skills.ts`**, each driven both ways by the self-check:
- *primitive without core* — a dotted name that resolves only as the tail of a `core.*` path fails. The suffix rule that lets a skill say `border.primary` for `color.border.primary` also passed `palette.primary.600` for `core.palette.primary.600`, which names nothing at the tree root. `color.` is a namespace a reader drops (the `.ai.json` drops it too); `core.` is what marks a private primitive. The counter-example exemption still applies, so "not `palette.*`" style teaching is unaffected.
- *retired lever* — a backticked lever that `levers.ts` marks `deprecated` must be called retired or deprecated on the same line. Read from the manifest, so the next retirement is covered without an edit here.
- *dead omission* — every `omits:` entry is a BrandInput property.
- *incomplete enum* — in a `documents: brandInput` skill, a table row whose first cell is an enum property lists every value the schema accepts. A wiring floor fails by name if no row is read at all. A dotted first cell (`typography.captionFloor`) resolves through nested `properties`: the first pattern took plain words only, so the two nested enum rows were never read (review on #2681). The values are read from the row's second cell only: the check first read the whole row, so `captionFloor` stayed complete with `10` gone from its values cell, because its description quotes "`10` adds caption.sm" (the reviewer's mutation, which passed for that reason too). Narrowed, it found `disabledStrategy`'s values cell listing two of four accepted values; the two legacy aliases were named only in the description, and now sit in the values cell as aliases.

**Mutations, each failing by name:** the three skills restored from `origin/main` (consume → four `primitive without core`; theme → `retired lever`, `incomplete enum` ×2, `dead omission`; rebind → `retired lever`); each new `findings.push` neutered → the self-check names the check; the theme table's rows reshaped → "the enum-row check read no table row in prism3-theme".

**Review round on #2681.** The disabled-ink line now gives the high-contrast 4.5:1. `prism3-build-component`'s hit-target exceptions name #2607's `CODE_SIDE_TARGETS` (44×44 at every size, stated in `codeOnly` and the shipped docs), `EXCLUDED` and `INNER_TARGETS`; the state ladder is an example pointing at `STATE_LADDER`; `component-axes.json` moves only on an axis, value or member-count change. `prism3-consume` says `export_theme` writes `tokens.json`, `ai-metadata.json` and `figma/` but no base + overlay set, and points a multi-mode build at the CLI's `--out` or the studio export; modes may also be more than four. `prism3-rebind` names Link and Flush icon button among the atoms.

**What stays out of reach, stated so nobody trusts the gate past it.** Prose claims about where a role sits (`text.secondary`'s surfaces), what a tool returns by default, quoted note text, the `x-prism3:` key set, and "Prism3 has no X component" are not mechanical names; review catches those. The audit lists cheap next extensions (a `documents: mcpTools` coverage mode, an opt-in `absent_components:` list).

**Filed, not fixed (one concern per PR):** the standard dialect drops unknown `x-prism3:` keys silently: #2678.

## (2026-10-15) — /review-pr matches how reviews are run now, and its file names are gated (#2677, Q320.1)

**What changed.** `.claude/commands/review-pr.md`, which review lanes now follow (owner decision Q320), had drifted from both the repo and the reviews actually being run. Fixed:
- **Wrong:** two doc names that were never files (`01-architecture`, `06-surface-model`); "all four" `@prism3/*` links (five); a hand-listed gate section whose baselines were off by about two orders of magnitude, that named `emit-dtcg.ts` and `cli.ts` as CI gates (neither runs in CI), and that built only the studio bundle before `lint-us-english` (it scans the plugin bundle too) without naming `lint-voice` at all; four brands' `tokens.json` as the whole byte-identity surface; `engine: major` as a declarable class (refused below 1.0).
- **Superseded:** the gate section is now "prepare, run `npm run verify` on the PR merged with current `main`, report N/N against the head SHA"; "commit before the first mutation" is now "before every mutation" (the 2026-08-24 incident), and a mutation counts only if it fails by name; the hand-edited-log paragraph is now the fold-review checklist, since only a fold writes the log (#1807); "post a `COMMENT` review, then squash-merge" is now "one verdict comment on the head SHA, delta checks after, merge only when your instructions say you may"; the empty-commit and `--force-with-lease` advice gives way to the CLAUDE.md rules (no empty commits; corrections as a follow-up PR; compare trees).
- **Added, from what tonight's independent reviews actually checked:** the `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` and `EXECUTOR_REVISION` pairs and their collisions across open PRs; the owner-decision boundary (design calls go to the owner as questions, new strings listed verbatim); filing out-of-scope defects; draft markers in shipped prose; per-hunk conflict recipes; reading check-runs on the head SHA; the authorship signals agents actually leave (trailers and session links, and branch prefixes beyond `claude/*`).

**The gate.** `lint-skills.ts` check 7 reads the command and fails by name on any backticked file name that does not resolve: a path from the repo root, a bare name (`verify.ts`, `lint-skills.ts`) in one of the places its reader would look. A self-check drives it with two dead names and one live one, and a floor fails if fewer than five names are read. It runs inside the skills gate because it is the same check as scan 3 applied to the one other agent-instruction file review lanes follow; a separate gate would have meant another `ci.yml` step and gate-list entry for a dozen lines.

**Mutations, each failing by name:** `docs/01-token-architecture.md` → `docs/01-architecture.md` ("[missing file] `docs/01-architecture.md` does not exist"); `lint-progress-order.ts` → `lint-progress-ordering.ts` (missing file, with the places searched); the check's `findings.push` neutered, and its pattern pointed at nothing ("the review-command file check is broken").

**Ceiling.** It would not have caught the original defect as written: "01-architecture" was a shorthand in prose, not a backticked path, which is why this PR writes the doc names as paths. The command's advice, like a skill's, is out of reach of any name check.

Also: a comment in `test.ts` cited `review-pr.md:133` for the fail-soft trap, a line number the rewrite moved; it now names the section.

## (2026-10-15) — Prototype reactions chain rest → hover → pressed (#2702)

Owner decision from QA of a real file: a Rest member reacts to While hovering only; the press is reached through Hover.
The change is one condition in `reactionMap` (`apps/plugin/src/reactions.ts`): `ON_PRESS` is planned from Hover alone.
Every source member now carries exactly one reaction, so per def reactions = sources (button 192, was 288; tag 18, was 27).

**Existing files need no new mechanism.** The earlier executor wrote and recorded both reactions on Rest, so a Rest
member read today matches its record (no hand edit) and differs from the plan (to update): the dry run names it as a
`prototype reactions` difference and the apply writes the plan's list over it. `test-reactions.ts` `chain/…` seeds
exactly that state (both reactions, record rewritten over them, older revision) and walks dry run → apply → clean dry
run. EXECUTOR_REVISION moves to 25 for the lint; the reaction difference alone would already mark the member.

**Gate independence.** `test:roundtrip` gains a `reactions read-back`: 16 interactive defs built with node ids, every
member's reactions read off the shim, destinations resolved among the set's members in the test, compared with a
literal per-state table (rest → hover, hover → pressed, else none), never the map. Mutation: the Rest press put back in
`reactionMap` fails `reactions read-back`, `chain/rest` and `chain/corrected` by name.

**Trap.** A designer who adds While pressing back on a Rest member by hand reads as a hand edit (kept by default),
which is the intended behavior, not a regression. Touch prototypes lose pressed feedback on Rest (no hover on a
phone): recorded on #2702, follow-up only if the owner asks.

## (2026-10-15) — Password field: TextField's factory, a nested Show button on the label row (#2317, Q301)

**What landed.** TextField's def is now the first output of a shared field factory, `makeTextField` in
`components/text-field.ts` (Q301.8 A, the `makeButton` pattern), and `password-field` (PasswordField) is the second:
84 members (size × status × the seven field states), no visibility axis (Q301.6 A), its own page under Components
(Q301.9 B). The box loses TextField's trailing slot; the label sits in a row with a nested Button at its end, outside
the box (Q301.2 B): text appearance, flush, primary, emphasis weight (Q301.3 B), its size following the field's. The
default member is the hidden state, "••••••••" and "Show" (DRAFT). The code contract (Show/Hide plus a visually hidden
" password", `aria-controls`, the polite "Your password is shown" / "Your password is hidden", focus kept on the
button, `type` password↔text, autocomplete required, paste never blocked, `::-ms-reveal` hidden, back to hidden on
submit) is in `codeOnly` and `accessibility`.

**The factory is byte-identical for TextField, proved before anything else moved.** The refactor commit serialized
`textField` before and after and compared the bytes; `regen --check` moved no TextField artifact and the surface and
renames baselines did not move for it. One later TextField edit is content, not the factory: `password-field` left
`composition.planned` for `alternativeTo`, because the component-refs gate refuses a registered def in `planned`.
The factory has ONE structural switch, `edge: 'trailing-glyph' | 'toggle'`, and nothing for Number input or Card
number: they add their own when they build. The eight code-only entries the two fields share are written out in each
def, because the plugin build cuts every `codeOnly` entry to its subject and refuses one that is not a string literal
(`strip-maintainer-prose.mjs`); a shared constant was tried first and broke the plugin build. `test.ts` holds the
shared entries identical in both defs instead, so a fix to one that misses the other fails by name.

**Two engine pieces the toggle needed, and why each is the shape it is.**
- `NestingRelation.atState`. The toggle must go disabled with the field and stay at rest everywhere else, read-only
  included. `follow: ['state']` cannot do it: the field's seven states are not Button's six (`filled` and `read-only`
  have no Button member). `atState: { disabled: { state: 'disabled' } }` maps the one host state that moves it.
  Projector-only (the plan carries the resolved coordinate), validated (a state off the axis, an axis the variant
  does not name, a followed or exposed axis are each refused by name).
- `PartDef.nestTexts`, the technical risk the proposal named. Exposing the nested Button surfaces its `label` on the
  field's panel (how a designer sets "Hide"), but a set has ONE default per text property, so the nested Button read
  "Button" on every member. Both executors now write `nestTexts` onto the instance with `setProperties` (the property
  found by its name before Figma's `#id`, TEXT only; a missing one is a named miss). `EXECUTOR_REVISION` 24: main reached 23
  (#2591, #2657, #2652) before this landed. The round-trip reads the value back (`nestTexts` predicate, 168 instances), the paste payload's
  own read-back is in `test.ts` beside the exposure write, and both shims model `componentProperties` from the NESTED
  def's declared texts, never from the host's override. This also unblocks List's ordered numbers (#2319's held
  follow-up), not taken here.

**Emphasis weight is Button's text appearance, not a new axis.** Button's text appearance already binds
`type.label.*.emphasis-link`, the weight Q289.3 gave the standalone Link. So Q301.3 B needs no weight field on the
nest; `test.ts` pins the nested member's resolved label style (`label/sm|md|lg/emphasis-link`), so a Button change to
the default weight fails the Password field's assertion by name.

**Hit target.** `lint-hit-target.ts` now measures a nested control with no side of its own through the NESTED def's
tokens at the size the host nests it at (the toggle: Button's `size.md.height`, 44), and requires a host of a nested
flush Button (`FLUSH_NESTS`) to state the code-side 44×44 / 24×24 rule in its own `codeOnly`, with Button's phrases.

**Traps for whoever re-verifies.** The paste shell grew with the `nestTexts` code, so icon-button packs into 17
chunks, not 16 (re-pinned with a note). The label row is `align: 'center'`: right for a one-line label beside a
44px button, and a wrapped label centers the button on the block; field labels are three words at most by their
content rule, so this was left as is and is the place to look if a long label reads oddly. Whether the live host keeps
a nested instance's text override when a designer swaps a placed field's variant is unverified (the standing nesting
caveat; `notes.unverified`).

Fix round (owner decision Q312, 2026-10-15). Q312.2 A: the "(DRAFT)" marker leaves the two strings that ship
(`accessibility.aria` and `docs.contentGuidelines`, which reach `password-field.md` and `components.ai.json`); it stays
in the file header, `notes` and `codeOnly`. `test.ts` walks every string on the def except `notes` and
`anatomy.codeOnly` and fails on "DRAFT", so a new field is covered without a list to keep. The review's keyboard nit
was mechanical: the KEYBOARD MODEL entry was TextField's copy and named Escape-to-clear, which this field does not
have; the clause is removed (nothing added), and the entry leaves the factory's shared code-only list in the test with
an assertion of its own. Q312.1 A (layer name `toggle`) and Q312.3 A (weight follows Button) needed no change. The
`codeOnly` "(DRAFT)" still reaches `schema/component-maintainer.json`, a maintainer file; left per the decision's scope.

## (2026-10-15) — Agent docs: `llms.txt`, a generated command reference, and `/docs` in the studio (#2637 lane 2)

Owner Q300 A, lane 2 of #2637. Three parts, one PR.

**The reference.** `packages/engine/emit-agent-reference.ts` writes `docs/public/reference/commands.json`: both MCP
servers' tools (`toolDefs()` in `mcp.ts`, `TOOLS` in `tools/figma-bridge/server.ts`), every agent-link command
(`AGENT_COMMANDS`, each `AgentArgs` member and its doc comment, the `bad-args` refusals `parseCommand` gives it, the
`AgentErrorCode` list, the `MAILBOX` layout, and the dev-only `run-code` from `dev-commands.ts`), and twelve CLI entry
points (each file's header usage lines and the flags its code compares `argv` against). Every entry carries its
source as `file#anchor`, the file plus the symbol to search for (`AgentArgs.readback`, `name: 'theme_brand'`,
`argv`). An earlier push wrote `file:line`, and review found the trap: main moved `verify.ts` by seven lines and
`--check` went red on a tree where no command had changed, and every PR that shifts a line in `mcp.ts`,
`agent-protocol.ts` or a CLI would do the same, and conflict on `commands.json` with every other such PR. The
noise also buried the signal: a fake tool reported itself plus six `changed in the code` lines for untouched tools.
The anchor still refuses to generate when its symbol is gone. The one authored part is `WRITES`, what each command writes to the file, because the handlers hold that in
code rather than data; a command with no entry, or an entry for a gone command, refuses to generate.

**Its own gate, not a regen step.** `--check` regenerates in memory and compares with the committed file, reporting
per tool, command, error code, CLI file and flag. It is not in `regen.ts` on purpose: regen's artifacts are engine
emission, read by the payload, version and prose gates as something a client receives, and `lint-emission-version.ts`
would then demand an engine bump for a reworded tool description. The file carries no engine version for the same
reason, so a fold never moves it. The CLI list is checked both ways against every `.ts` that reads `process.argv` in
the repo root, `packages/engine/`, `tools/figma-bridge/` and `tools/figma-mcp/`; gates (`lint-*`) and regen steps are
excluded by name or pattern with a reason. Stated limit: a CLI that reads no `argv` is not found by that check.

**Mutations, each failing by name:** a fake MCP tool added to `toolDefs` → `in the code, missing from the reference:
mcp tool prism3-engine/fake_tool`; `adopt-members` renamed in `AGENT_COMMANDS` → the generator refuses (`WRITES` has no
entry; an entry for a gone command); with `WRITES` and `AgentArgs` renamed too → `in the code, missing from the
reference: agent-link command adopt-memberz` and `in the reference, gone from the code: agent-link command
adopt-members`; a flag added to `fold.ts` → `in the code, missing from the reference: cli fold.ts --fake`.

**`theme_brand.brand` is the one schema not as sent.** The reference gives it as a `$ref` to `theme-schema.json`;
the wire carries `compactSchema(theme-schema)`, descriptions cut to their summaries. The header and the `$ref`'s own
description say so, in one sentence, because `compactSchema` runs over the `$ref` object too and keeps only a
description's first sentence.

**Serving.** `apps/studio/docs-route.mjs` is the one definition of `/docs`: the dev server (`build.mjs --dev`, now a
small front server over esbuild's) answers `/docs/*` from `docs/public/`, and `build-site.mjs` copies the directory to
`public/docs/` and lists each file in its publish manifest. `vercel-ignore.sh` now builds on a `docs/public` change,
with a case in its gate. `test-docs-route.ts` fetches both files through the dev route (byte-equal, typed, traversal
refused). A directory asked for without its trailing slash answers `301` to the slash path: served at
`/docs/ecosystem`, a page's relative `./ecosystem.json` resolves to `/docs/ecosystem.json` and 404s, which review
found with the ecosystem lane merged in. The deployed site's handling of the same path is not measured here; `test-prod-bundle.ts` checks the deploy build copied both. The studio's Inspect menu gains a **Docs** item
on the web host only, opening `/docs/llms.txt` in a new tab; its place and label are an owner item.

**Prose gates.** `lint-us-english.ts` and `lint-voice.ts` now scan `docs/public/**`, with `llms.txt` required by name.
The first run found two things. `catalogue` in the bridge's `figma_run` schema shipped unscanned, since the bridge's
`tools/list` was never in either gate (fixed at the source). And the reference names `materialise-to-figma.ts`, a file
name: rather than add `materialise` to `NOT_EN_GB`, which would hide the word in prose, `prose-rules.ts` masks the
whole tracked path (`EN_GB_FILE_NAMES`), sampled both ways in the self-check, with a stale entry failing the gate.

**Found, not fixed:** the bridge's `figma_run` describes its `args` for four commands of ten; filed as #2639.

## (2026-10-15) — Dialog: one panel, centered, as a bottom sheet or full screen, its backdrop drawn as canvas furniture (#2609, Q303)

Built to the proposal on #2609 as the owner decided it in Q303: one `Dialog` with a `placement` axis, `center | bottom |
full`, and **no side or drawer placement**. 15 members: center at three sizes (`medium | small | large`, 560 / 400 /
720px) × three footers (`inline | stacked | none`), and bottom and full at the default size only. No state axis.
Category `overlay`, aliases `modal`, `sheet`, `bottom-sheet`, `full-screen-dialog`, on its own `↳ Dialog` page. Cites
the knowledge base's `components/dialog.md` (category Overlay), read for this build.

### Measured first: can a set miss coordinates?

Yes. `figmaProperties.excludeCoordinates` (Badge's, then Button's flush) already removes coordinates from the cross
product, and it refuses only a removal that takes the set's default member or a whole axis value. Removing
`{ placement: [bottom, full], size: [small, large] }` leaves 15 members, and every count gate (`figmaVariantCount`'s
inclusion–exclusion) agrees. A bottom or full member's name still carries `size=medium`, the code default, so an
instance switched from center keeps a valid coordinate.

### What the construction is

- **The panel** is the root: `color.foreground.primary`, the `shadow.xl` effect style, padding top and bottom only
  (`space.300` centered, `space.200` on the two small-screen placements), a 16px gap. The header, body and footer pad
  their own sides, so the two dividers run edge to edge.
- **The size per placement** is a new root field, `PartDef.builtSize`: at each placement the root is built at that
  width (400 / 560 / 720 per size at center, 360 at bottom and full), and at full also at a height (640) with the body
  growing down the column so the footer sits at the bottom. The height needs a plan field the executors did not have,
  `placementHeight`, written in the same resize as `placementWidth` by both executors and read back. That is why
  `EXECUTOR_REVISION` moves, 20 → 21.
- **Corners per placement** bind top and bottom apart through `PartDef.radiusEdges`: center `radius.2xl` all round,
  bottom its top two, full none. The executors already bind each corner by name, so this is projector-only.
- **The shadow** is `PartDef.elevation`, a binding key resolved to an effect style name (`shadow.xl` → `shadow/xl`). The
  plan field and both executors' effect-style writes existed with nothing projecting them; this is their first user.
- **The header** is the accordion's title row: the title (wraps) and the description (off) in a column that grows
  beside the close button, top-aligned. The close is a nested IconButton.Neutral, ghost, medium, square, at rest.
- **The body** is a native slot, as the accordion's panel is, with a placeholder paragraph.
- **The footers** are two parts gated on `footer`, because node order is fixed per set: inline is Cancel (outline) then
  Save (filled) 12px apart at the end edge; stacked is Save over Cancel, full width, 8px apart.
- **One `dividers` toggle drives two rules.** The validator refused a boolean whose parts build in the same member, as
  "two affordances wearing one switch". The two rules are one affordance, so a boolean entry can now say `together`,
  which lifts that one refusal for that entry only; one part with the flag is refused.

### The backdrop is canvas furniture

The scrim is never a node of the set (Q303.2 A, Q303.3 A). File setup now builds a third template, `_scrim-backdrop`,
a square component whose fill binds `color/scrim/default` (black at 40% until a theme is applied). After a Dialog set
lands, the plugin places one instance behind each center and bottom member: 12px all round a centered panel, 12px
above a bottom sheet and flush on its other sides, none behind full (it has no visible backdrop, Q303.8). 12 is half
the grid's 24px gap, so no scrim reaches a neighboring member. A file without the template draws none and the run says
so once, in the existing missing-template line.

### Technical calls, and why

- **The title is `type.label.lg.emphasis`, not the drafted `type.title.sm.strong`.** The nb-redesign example emits
  titles at one weight (`subtle`) only, so `title.sm.strong` missed at build time (`test.ts` #1601). The accordion's
  title met the same gap the same way. Held for the owner.
- **Size order is medium, small, large in Figma** (the proposal's table, default first), with the code enum on the
  ladder, the fields' split. Dialog joins the Q221 B exception list and `lint-rung-names` DEFAULT_FIRST.
- **`lint-rung-names` gains `SIZE_BY_BUILT_WIDTH`.** Dialog's size binds no token (the widths are def-level literals by
  Q303.5 A), so the gate checks what the size does reach: a per-size width map naming exactly the three sizes, rising.
- **Hit target:** Dialog is excluded with its reason. The panel is not a pointer target; its close and footer buttons
  are IconButton.Neutral and Button, measured under their own names.

### Not done, and filed

- **The nested close shows the file's default icon, and the nested buttons read "Button".** Showing `close` and
  "Cancel" / "Save" needs a per-instance override on a nested instance (a swap and a text), which no def can ask for
  and neither executor writes. The List's ordered numbers need the same thing. Filed as #2645.

### Traps

- A def file the gates read from git (`lint-axis-values`, `typecheck-components`) is invisible to them until it is
  staged, as the List lane found.
- `title.sm.strong` resolves in four corpus brands and misses in the fifth; only `test.ts` #1601 sees it.

**After merging the slot-constraints work (#2646).** `test-slot-constraints.ts` requires a constraints decision for every native slot, and Dialog's body is the second one. Its row is `{}`: open, no limit and no preferred component, the same as the accordion's panel and the same as the def as built. Like every row there, it is a draft owner item. The footer's actions stay fixed nested Buttons (Q311), so they have no row until the items-slot follow-up.

**Evidence, for whoever re-checks this.** `git ls-files packages/engine/out | grep -iE 'skill|agents|claude|instruction'` returns nothing. No engine source writes a `SKILL.md` or an instruction file: the only engine files that name `skills/` are gates and tests that read the four hand-authored skills in this repo (`lint-skills.ts`, `test.ts`, `lint-us-english.ts`, `lint-voice.ts`, `lint-layout-claims.ts`). `schema/payload-manifest.json` has no skill or instruction kind. What does travel today is the agent *metadata* that #668 builds on: `out/{brand}.ai.json` (kind `agent-metadata`), `out/components/components.ai.json`, and the per-component pages in `out/components/*.md`, which the manifest calls "the seed for the per-brand payload skills (#668)". So the missing emission is already filed as #668, and this PR files nothing new.

**Trap.** The open CLAUDE.md trim (#2672) rewrites the same table row and keeps the old present-tense clause. Whichever of the two merges second must keep "not yet built", or the wrong claim comes back.

## (2026-10-15) — Flush icon button: a glyph-only action with no padding or fill, made to be nested (#2457, owner decision Q283.3 A)

**Status:** three new defs, `flush-icon-button` (FlushIconButton, primary), `flush-icon-button-destructive` and `flush-icon-button-neutral` (Q295.2 B, on IconButton's family pattern), plus gates. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no new token. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at main's 15. Three new docs pages, so the artifact count is **187** in `verify.ts` and `ci.yml` together, on the tree merged with main at `ba094cb1` (which brought Segmented control, #2418, at 184).

**Current shape, in one line:** three families, each `shape` [flush, round] × `size` × `state` = 30 members (90 in all), 18 reactions each, a 36-set furniture rollout, 38 defs in `used-by.ts` (on the tree merged with Segmented control), a paint census of 51 assignments per family. The first two sections below record the neutral-only pushes, when the bare id was neutral; where a figure there was later changed it is marked *superseded*, and the last section has the current one.

**What it is (Q283.3 A, on #2427):** "its own small def, ghost only, no padding, color-only hover, code-side 44x44 hit area." The three IconButton sets are untouched.
- `size` [small, medium, large] × `state` [rest, hover, pressed, focus-visible, disabled] = 15 members (*superseded*: 30 once the `shape` axis landed, below). No `appearance` axis.
- The box is the glyph square: `size.{size}.side` (*superseded*: renamed `size.{size}.flush`, below) → `icon.size.sm` / `sm` / `md` (20 / 20 / 24, Q283.13 A), and the swap slot binds the same key. No padding is bound, because none exists.
- The box declares no `paintSlots`, so it paints nothing at any state (*superseded*: it now declares `overlay` and `border` for the round shape, and flush still paints nothing; see "How flush stays unpainted" below). The glyph walks IconButton.Neutral's ghost ink (`color.interactive.neutral.icon.{rest,hover,pressed}`; neutral reflects inward since #2324, so hover does move), and `color.disabled.icon` at disabled.
- Focus: the shared focus ring, `nest-fixed`, at `focus.ring.offset`, as on IconButton.
- Reactions: nothing authored. `reactions.ts` derives scope from member names, and the set has rest, hover and pressed (#2574, Q238 A). `test-reactions.ts` `map/scope` now lists 12 defs, the new one at 15 members, 6 sources, 9 reactions (3 sizes × rest → hover, rest → pressed, hover → pressed). *Superseded:* 30 members, 12 sources, 18 reactions with both shapes.
- Canvas furniture: on, like every set (`CANVAS_FURNITURE`, Q212 A); `test-canvas-furniture.ts` counted 30 sets (*superseded*: 32 on the tree merged with List).
- Page: `↳ Flush Icon Button` under Subcomponents (Q283.14 A), alphabetical between Field Message and Focus Ring.

**The hit area is a stated rule, not a measurement.** No emitted token is its target: the box is 20 or 24px by design. `lint-hit-target.ts` gains a third classification beside INTERACTIVE and EXCLUDED, `CODE_SIDE_TARGETS`. A listed def is measured *below* 44 at every size on comfortable (so a box grown to 44 makes the entry stale by name), and must state the 44×44 rule twice, as literals the gate holds: in `codeOnly` (the maintainer record) and in the shipped `docs.do`. The second is the one that matters to an implementer, since `codeOnly` never ships. The nest arm now also sees code-side targets, so the Counter nesting two of these will have to list them in `INNER_TARGETS`.

**Nesting (for the Counter):** `test-roundtrip.ts` builds a fixture host, never registered, that nests the button twice (`decrement`, `increment`), both `nest-exposed` with `expose: ['state']` and `follow: ['size']`, against the button's own set. It validates clean, and on the shim both instances in all 3 members are marked exposed, are instances of the right set, and read back with no `nestExpose` or `nestTarget` divergence. **So two nests exposing the same axis coexist on the shim.** A real host is not measured: Figma lists each exposed instance's properties under its own layer name, which the shim does not model.

Reading the whole member would see the glyph's ink at every state and could never pass; reading only the glyph would miss a wash on the box.

### The round shape (owner decision Q287 A on #2457, a follow-up push on the same PR)

**What it is:** "one component with two shapes." The Counter's outlined appearance nests `flush` and its ghost appearance (the wireframe's treatment B) nests `round`. No new def, no new token, and no executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at main's 15.
- `shape` [flush, round] × `size` [small, medium, large] × `state` = 30 members. `shape` is an existing `VARIANT_AXES` name (IconButton's), placed first in `variantAxes`; flush leads its values because it is the code default and the shape built first. Size and state keep the #2509 order.
- **Flush is unchanged in every pixel.** Its box key was renamed (`size.{size}.side` → `size.{size}.flush`, the same `icon.size.*` rung), and because the shape axis now keys the corner and the stroke weight, a flush member also binds `radius.none` (a 0 corner) and `border-width.hairline` with no stroke paint, as a ghost IconButton does. The glyph's key is now `size.{size}.icon`, the name IconButton uses.
- **Round** is a circle the Counter's height across: `size.sm.height` / `md` / `lg` = 36 / 44 / 56, `radius.round`. The glyph inside stays 20 / 20 / 24 (Q283.13 A).
- **The edge is decorative:** `color.border.secondary`, the decorative rung of the edge ladder (#2569, Q259 C; about 2:1 against the page, no floor). The glyph identifies the control and carries the 3:1, as it does on flush. At disabled the edge takes `color.disabled.border`.
- **Hover and pressed:** IconButton.Neutral's ghost wash, `color.interactive.neutral.overlay.{hover,pressed}`, over the glyph's ink walk. Rest paints no fill.
- **How flush stays unpainted:** the box now declares `paintSlots: ['overlay', 'border']`, but the grammar leads with `{shape}` and every box key is `round.*`. The cross-cutting `disabled.border` applies only where the shape has an edge at rest (`restKey`), so a disabled flush member still paints nothing.

**Why the diameter equals the Counter's height, not the wireframe's 8px inset.** The wireframe drew the circle at height − 8 (28 / 36 / 48). That puts medium on `size.sm.height`, a default one rung below `md`, which `lint-rung-names` refuses without a new owner exception, and 48 has no rung. The Counter's own heights are rungs (36 / 44 / 56), so the circle is the row: a ghost Counter needs no height of its own, and the medium circle clears 44px on its own box. Held as an owner item.

## (2026-10-15) — The engine changelog moves out of `version.ts` into `packages/engine/CHANGELOG.md` (Q319.3)

Owner decision Q319.3 A on #2583. The ENGINE changelog was a 5,090-line comment between `version.ts`'s module header and `ENGINE_VERSION`. It is now `packages/engine/CHANGELOG.md`, and `version.ts` keeps the module header, the two constants and the contract surface around them (1,276 lines, from 6,365). `fold.ts` writes each fold under the FOLD MARKER in the new file, and `lint-emission-version.ts` reads it there.

**The move is byte-faithful under one stated transform.** It strips ` * ` / ` *` from each line, turns each block boundary (`*/` then `/**`) into a blank line, `---` and a blank line, and drops the opening `/**`, the closing `*/` and the constant's own first line. That line, "The code. Bumps on any behaviour change…", stays on the constant as its doc comment. Reversing the transform over the new file reproduces lines 75–5163 of `version.ts` at `e4a22077` exactly (5,089 lines, equal). The order is kept: a few pre-#1807 entries, then the folded section, then the rest of the pre-#1807 entries. The file's intro says so, and a reorder would be a separate decision.

**The gate proves the move rather than trusting it.** ONE WRITER compares the changelog region at the base and at HEAD. A base with no `CHANGELOG.md` (this PR, and `main`'s push run on its squash) is read the old way, then run through the same transform, restated in the gate and not imported. So this PR passes as a non-fold only if the move was faithful. One changed word in the moved text (`29` → `28` in the 0.237.0 header) fails ONE WRITER by name. In steady state the region is everything below the `<!-- ENGINE CHANGELOG (#1807)` comment. The intro above it stays editable, the way `version.ts`'s module header always was, and an intro edit passes.

**Mutations, in a throwaway clone with the move committed as `main`:**
- (a) A non-fold PR edits a fold header in `CHANGELOG.md`: `ONE WRITER — this diff edits the ENGINE changelog in CHANGELOG.md and is not a fold`.
- (b) A synthetic note (`engine: patch`) and fragment merge, then `fold.ts` runs. It writes `0.237.1 — folded …` under the marker in `CHANGELOG.md` with the placeholder filled, and moves only the constant line in `version.ts`. `lint-emission-version.ts` passes (`a fold — 1 note(s) consumed at patch`), and so does `lint-progress-order.ts` (`exempt — a pure fold`).
- (b2) The same fold with the note's second paragraph deleted fails `FOLD INTEGRITY — … its prose is not in the 0.237.1 section`.
- `lint-progress-order.ts` with `CHANGELOG.md` taken back out of `FOLD_WRITES` fails the real fold with `CARRIES AN ENTRY`. The list had to gain the file, or every fold would stop counting as pure.

**Dropped as a rule: "no `*/` in a change note".** It existed only because the prose was folded into a comment. Both `fold.ts` and NOTE SHAPE refused it, and both checks are removed with their reason.

**No change note.** No committed artifact and no projected surface moves (`regen --check` is clean). The fold and gate tooling is not engine behavior. The earlier tooling PRs that changed `fold.ts` or this gate (#2556, the #2583 archive move, #1816) carried none either.

**Kept in `version.ts`: the CONTRACT changelog** (the entries above `CONTRACT_VERSION`). Q319.3 names the fold's changelog. The contract entries are written by the PR that bumps the contract, in the same diff as its `--accept`. Moving them would put a per-PR writer into a file the one-writer arm guards, so that is a separate call if wanted.

**Coordination.** #2658 (release notes) reads only the `ENGINE_VERSION` constant out of `version.ts` and is unaffected. But it rewrites `lint-progress-order.ts`'s `FOLD_WRITES` line, which this PR also changes, so whichever lands second keeps both entries. #2672 (CLAUDE.md trim) rewrites principle 5. This PR changes one phrase there ("the changelog above it" becomes "its changelog, `packages/engine/CHANGELOG.md`"), and the trim should carry the path forward.

## (2026-10-15) — A fold that leaves a fragment or note pending fails by name (#2663)

**The hole.** The review of the open fold PR found it cut on one commit of `main` and headed for a later
one: two PRs had since landed a fragment each. Merged, the fold would have left both pending, and every
gate passed it. `lint-progress-order.ts` read the diff as "exempt — a pure fold", because FOLDED ENTRIES
checks only the files a fold deleted, and it cannot see a file the fold never had. `lint-emission-version.ts`
checks the class of the notes a fold consumed, not that it consumed them all. GitHub does not re-run a
PR's CI when its base moves, so the fold's own green run was stale as well.

**The fix.** A new arm in `lint-progress-order.ts`, LEAVES NOTHING PENDING. A diff that deletes a pending
fragment or change note is a fold. On the tree it merges into, no fragment or note may still be pending,
except one the diff adds itself (a fold's fragment for a semantic-conflict fix it carries). "The tree it
merges into" depends on the run:
- CI's merge ref: HEAD.
- A fold branch run locally: HEAD's pending files, less those the base ref has consumed since the merge
  base, plus those it has added.
- Main's push run: HEAD, over its first parent.

The push run is the one that sees the fold on the `main` it actually landed on. The arm is not skipped
there, unlike CARRIES AN ENTRY. A diff that consumes nothing prints n/a. The subject is the diff's
deletions, and the oracle is an `ls-tree` of both directories, so neither side reads `fold.ts`.
`fold.ts` is unchanged: it already refuses a HEAD off `origin/main`, so it consumes everything at its own
base. Only the gate can see `main` move afterwards. No engine behavior moved, so no change note.

**Partial restamps (the same review).** `lint-emission-version.ts`'s header gains a third limit. A fold
moves `ENGINE_VERSION` forward, so the gate passes it even when one emitted tree keeps the old stamp.
Only `regen.ts --check` (verify's `drift` row) fails that, so `drift` is load-bearing for every fold.

**Proof, on a synthetic fold in a throwaway clone** (`git clone` of the branch, `fold.ts` run for real).
Fold A was cut at M0. Then "main" moved to M1 with one fragment and one note. Fold B, re-cut at M1, is the
control. Each scenario ran main's gate and the fixed gate side by side:

| Scenario | main's gate | fixed gate |
|---|---|---|
| Fold A on its merge ref (CI) | exit 0, "exempt — a pure fold" | exit 1, LEAVES NOTHING PENDING: 2 file(s) |
| Fold A on its branch, `origin/main` at M1 | exit 0 | exit 1, LEAVES NOTHING PENDING |
| Fold A squashed on main, push run | exit 0 (the arm block is skipped on push) | exit 1, LEAVES NOTHING PENDING |
| Fold B, branch / merge ref / push | exit 0 | exit 0, "leaves nothing pending" |
| An ordinary PR on M1 | exit 0 | exit 0, n/a, not a fold |
| Fold B plus its own fix fragment | exit 0 | exit 0, its own fragment is not left behind |

**The first formula was wrong, and test.ts caught it.** The first version counted everything pending at
HEAD. `test.ts`'s #1880 fixture (a) is a branch that merged main and folded what that merge brought in. It
still holds two fragments that main's own fold had consumed since the merge base, so the merge deletes
them, yet the arm reported them as left behind. The arm now subtracts what the base ref deleted since the
merge base. **Committed cases**, in the same scratch-repo block (`test.ts` (f)): fixture (a) passes; a
stale fold fails by name on its branch, its merge ref and its squash's push run, naming the late
fragment; the re-cut fold passes. Each arm of the new code, mutated, fails a named case there:

- The arm disabled (main's behavior) → three failures. "#2663 leaves nothing pending: a fold cut before main
  moved fails by name on its branch, its merge ref and main's push run…" reads exits 0, 0, 0. The (a) case
  and the re-cut case fail too, because their pass line is gone.
- The push-run call removed → that same case, exits 1, 1, 0.
- The base ref's additions dropped → the same case, exits 0, 1, 1.
- Main's consumption not subtracted → "#1880 folded entries: one merge of main brings two fragments…" and
  "#2663 leaves nothing pending: a branch's fold beside main's fold of the rest passes…".
- Not in `test.ts`: the exemption for a fold's own added file. The synthetic harness above covers it
  (row "Fold B plus its own fix fragment").

**A trap for whoever reruns this.** A `node_modules` symlink in the clone shows as untracked, because
`.gitignore`'s `node_modules/` matches directories only. `fold.ts` then refuses a dirty tree. Add it to
the clone's `.git/info/exclude`.

**The fold being redone tonight is not touched.** This PR changes no fold file. A correct re-cut fold
(B above) passes all three runs.

## (2026-10-15) — The four engine skills load in every Claude Code session here (#2677, Q320.2)

**What changed.** `.claude/skills/` now holds one symlink per engine skill (`prism3-theme`, `prism3-consume`, `prism3-rebind`, `prism3-build-component`), each pointing at `skills/<name>`. `skills/` stays the single source and the only thing `lint-skills.ts` reads for claims. `lint-skills.ts` gains check 6, DISCOVERY: every `skills/<name>` must have a `.claude/skills/<name>` that is a symlink resolving to it, and any `.claude/skills/` link that dangles or resolves into `skills/` under another name fails. An entry that resolves elsewhere (a repo-local skill with its own home) passes. `.claude/settings.json` is untouched.

**Why a symlink, and how that was established.** Claude Code finds project skills only at `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; the repo-root `skills/` is invisible to it. Its skills docs say a skill entry may be a symlink to a directory elsewhere and that it reads `SKILL.md` from the target. Measured rather than trusted: a scratch repo with `.claude/skills/zz-probe-skill -> ../../skills/zz-probe-skill`, and a fresh `claude -p` session (Claude Code 2.1.300) listed `zz-probe-skill` among its skills. The same check in this worktree listed all four. Unknown frontmatter keys (`documents:`, `omits:`, which `lint-skills` reads) are ignored by Claude Code, per the same docs.

**Approach discarded.** A generated copy under `.claude/skills/` plus a drift gate. It would load identically, but it is two sources kept equal by a gate, and the gate would have to be added to regen's artifact count. A link has nothing to drift. The gate refuses a copy by name ("copy, not a link") so the discarded shape cannot come back quietly.

**Ceiling, stated.** The gate checks the links, not the host. If a future Claude Code stopped following linked skill directories, this stays green and the skills silently stop loading. On a Windows checkout without `core.symlinks`, git writes each link as a text file; the gate fails there, which is correct. Uploading these skills to claude.ai or the Skills API would reject the extra frontmatter keys; nothing does that today.

## (2026-10-15) — Link: a standalone link plus an inline look, two weights, underlined by state (#2580, owner decisions Q289, Q297)

**Status:** a new def, `link`, an engine extension the def needs, the gate lists it joins, and the Button `href` documentation. ENGINE minor (change note). CONTRACT unchanged: no new token. No executor change, so `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays where main has it.

**What it builds (Q289):** 96 members — `style` standalone | inline × `weight` emphasis | default × `size` small | medium | large × `surface` default | inverse × rest, hover, pressed, focus-visible. A row that hugs its label, one text line tall, no padding, optional leading and trailing icons (node-visibility booleans with the swap canon), and the shared focus ring following `surface`. Label "Link text". Ink is `color.text.link.*` / `color.icon.link.*`, `focus-visible` on the `focused` rung; the inverse twins come from the projector's one inverse rewrite, as Button's do. Visited, current, the router `asChild`, the external link and the 24px hit-area expansion are code only (`codeOnly`). Its own `Link` page under Components, canvas furniture, and Q238 A reactions derived from the state axis (48 sources, 72 reactions). Button's `href` prop now documents the anchor rendering (Q289.6 A, no LinkButton), and `link` leaves the five `planned` lists that named it.

**The diagnosis that made it small:** the proposal flagged that standalone swaps its text style by state (underline on hover), and asked whether the engine can key a type binding by state. It could not: the projector already fills a binding key from a coordinate that carries `state` (#1248), but the validator refused any placeholder that is not a variant axis. So the extension is two lines of rule plus one of resolution: `component-schema.ts` admits `{state}` in a part's `type` key only, expanded over the def's declared states, and `anatomy-figma.ts` resolves a structure-only plan (no state) at the first declared state. Type only, on purpose: a state-keyed height or padding would move one instance's box between before and after, which the footprint rule exists to refuse. The two styles a state picks between differ only in `textDecoration`, so the box does not move.

**Owner items (held, not decided here):**
1. **The weight axis's shape.** Named `weight`, values `emphasis | default`, emphasis first and the default (Q289.3 B's example taken literally). 2 values, doubling the set from the proposal's 48 to 96. `lint-axis-values` records it as disjoint from field-label's `regular | bold` (which is now `canonical`): `bold` there resolves to the heaviest body cut (`strong`), not `emphasis`.
2. **Both weights, and inline, bind the label tier** (`type.label.<rung>.<weight>[-link]`, one line, `snug`). The proposal had inline on `type.body.*.default-link`; the body tier has no emphasis-link role, and minting one would be a new token. The default weight matches body text in weight, not in family or line height on a brand whose label family differs.
3. **Placement:** its own `Link` page under Components. The proposal named a navigation section; none exists, and Tabs went under Components (Q177.14).
4. **Icon rungs:** small `icon.size.sm`, medium `icon.size.md`, large `icon.size.lg`, as Tab's. The proposal had sm / sm / md; medium on `sm` is the one-rung offset `lint-rung-names` refuses unless the owner admits it (`ICON_OFFSET_DEFS`). Gaps `space.050` / `space.050` / `space.100` as proposed, DRAFT.
5. **Icons on inline.** The brief says inline links carry no icons; the toggles exist on both styles (a node-visibility boolean, not gated by style) and the docs say not to add one. Gating them to standalone is an owner call (`notes.contested`).
6. **Size order** is small, medium, large with medium the default, the corpus's ladder, not the proposal's medium-first listing.

**Tests:** `test.ts` `#2580 link/*`, every expectation typed from Q289 and read off the real projection, never from `link.ts` (which builds its 48 type keys in a loop, so reading them back would be the loop agreeing with itself): `standalone` (plain at rest, `-link` at hover, pressed and focus-visible, all 48 members), `inline` (`-link` at every state, all 48), `weight` (emphasis first and the default, medium rest `label/md/emphasis` / `label/md/default`), `style` (exactly standalone | inline), `states`, `members` (96) and `identity` (names, aliases, category, label default, summary, "(opens in new tab)"). The #1248 type-key grid gains `style` and `state` in `TYPE_KEY_AXES` and a sweep over `state`. Joins `lint-hit-target` (EXCLUDED: one line tall by Q289.4 A), `lint-rung-names`, `lint-axis-values`, `lint-standalone-floor`, `lint-paint-placement`, `lint-absolute-inset`, the density spacing table, `CENTRE_OK`, the reactions map, the furniture rollout (72 members regroup, worked by hand: 2s + w = 3u) and `CANVAS_FURNITURE`. Regen count 182 → 183 (after merging List); `DEF_FLOOR` 34. Baselines accepted: component surface, paint census, component axes; studio catalog and used-by index regenerated.

**A trap for whoever re-verifies:** a `{state}` type key resolves at the first declared state when a plan has no state. Every def's first state is `rest` today; a def that declared another state first would get that look in its structure-only plans.

**Review fix: the `{state}` rule had no test.** The schema allows `{state}` only in a type key (`keyAxes` in `component-schema.ts`), and its comment leans on the footprint rule to refuse a state-keyed box. That rule runs only against a live Figma file, and the shim has no equivalent, so widening `keyAxes` to every binding key failed nothing. `#2580 link/state-type-only` validates a Link clone whose row gap is `size.{size}.gap.{state}`, with every slot that expansion would ask for supplied, and asserts the refusal names the placeholder. With every slot present, a validator that lets `{state}` through finds nothing missing, so the arm can't pass for the wrong reason. Mutation: `keyAxes` widened to every key fails that arm by name (`clone: no errors`), and nothing else in the suite fails. The icon props now say "Not for inline links", matching the docs, because the toggles exist on both styles.

**Owner decisions Q297, applied (review findings 2–4).** Items 2, 4 and 5 above are settled, and superseded where they differ.
1. **Body tier for both styles**, 14 / 16 / 18px, so a Link matches the body text and the text-range link in the same paragraph. No 12px link. `default` binds `type.body.<rung>.default[-link]`. `emphasis` has no `emphasis` role to bind in a default brand's body tier: there it is `strong`. In nb-redesign's brief (body weights `[default, emphasis]`) `strong` is never emitted, so a fixed `strong` binding fails test.ts #1601 at nb-redesign. That is the miss the 2026-10-11 accordion decision stepped around by staying on the label tier. **The diagnosis that made it small:** field-label already solved this shape with `weightIntent` (#1602, `bold` → the heaviest body weight the brand ships). It needed two things to fit Link. First, an optional `intents` map, because Link keeps its value names (Q297.3) where the validator wanted `regular | bold`. Second, the repoint keeps a `-link` suffix, which field-label never had. So `emphasis` resolves to `strong[-link]` in the four default brands and to `emphasis[-link]` in nb-redesign. **The tradeoff, deliberate:** in prism3 the emphasis link is now 600 (`strong`) where the label tier gave 500. That is the body text's own heavier weight, which is what "matching body text" asks for. Like field-label, a brand that ships one body weight drops the `weight` axis (`link@body-single`, 48 members).
2. **Icons: trailing only, standalone only.** The leading slot, its prop, boolean and swap are gone. The trailing slot carries `presentWhen: { style: ['standalone'] }`, so it is absent from every inline member, not just hidden by a toggle: the axis model expresses "standalone only" directly, as Accordion gates its indicators. Rungs are `icon.size.xs` / `xs` / `sm` (16 / 16 / 20px). They fit inside the body line (21 / 24 / 27px at 1.5) in all five brands. The `size` prop now states the height with an icon. The medium default on `xs` is two rungs below `md`, so `lint-rung-names` gains `ICON_OFFSET_TWO_DEFS` (`link`), sanctioned by Q297.2 and checked both ways, as `ICON_OFFSET_DEFS` is. Paint census 288 → 144 assignments (96 labels plus 48 standalone trailing icons).
3. **Weight wording** per Q297.3. The "matches body text" claims are gone.

Tests: `#2580 link/body-tier` reads each member's font size off the committed emission and compares it to the literal 14 / 16 / 18. `#2580 link/icons` checks trailing only, standalone only, and `icon/size/xs`, `xs`, `sm` against emitted 16 and 20px. `#2580 link/weight-intent` checks that a `[default, emphasis]` body brand gives `body/md/emphasis` at rest and `body/md/emphasis-link` at hover. `#2580 link/weight` now also holds the owner's prop text. Link joins #910's `presentWhen` list.

**Merge of main after Segmented control (#2591).** Both PRs added a def to the same lists, so the merge took main's lines and appended `link` after `segmented-control` (def order, the gate lists, `CANVAS_FURNITURE`, the reactions map). `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` is main's 184 plus `link.md`, 185, in `verify.ts` and `ci.yml` together. Two text merges: Tabs' `planned` is now empty, because both Link and Segmented control are built; Button's `avoidWhen` keeps this branch's Link and `href` sentence and takes main's "(or SegmentedControl)". The `out/components/*`, studio catalog and used-by index were regenerated, and the surface and paint-census baselines re-accepted, rather than resolved by hand.

**Q314 A: the `size` wording.** The prop text was "…one text line tall, or as tall as the icon where the icon is taller…". At the shipped 1.5 line height (21 / 24 / 27px) the icon (16 / 16 / 20px) is never taller in the five brands, so that clause described no shipped case. It now reads "The body type size: 14, 16 or 18px. The box is one text line tall; the icon (16px at small and medium, 20px at large) sits inside it." `#2580 link/size-wording` pins the string as a literal; no earlier arm read it. The second merge of main (#2618, #2657) conflicted only in `test.ts`'s KB-brief block, where main replaced the hand table with `schema/kb-briefs.json` (#2488); main's side was taken, and the catalogue already lists `link.md` under `navigation`. `EXECUTOR_REVISION` stays at main's 22 and `EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS` at 185: neither side moved past the other.

## (2026-10-15) — Short token names are tested on effect and gradient tables that share a root (#2659)

**The gap.** In short mode the style guide's Token column prints a row's name below its table's common
prefix (#2372). #2623 tested this for text styles (#2475). Its review named two wrong planners a
one-segment root cannot tell apart: M3 caps the common prefix at one segment
(`commonPrefix(…).slice(0, 1)`), and M4 always drops the first segment (`.slice(1)` for
`.slice(prefix.length)`). The issue asked the same of the other three Token-cell planners. Run on main
(afe5d369), against `apps/plugin/test-style-guide.ts`:

| Planner | M3 | M4 |
|---|---|---|
| `planEffectStyles` | exit 0, passed silently | exit 0, passed silently |
| `planGradientStyles` | exit 0, passed silently | exit 0, passed silently |
| `planVariableTables` | exit 1 | exit 1 |

The fixture's effect and gradient styles share no root (`shadow/…` beside `Brand/…`), and §36 tested
only the default, which prints the whole name.

**The variable tables needed no test.** M3 and M4 as written fail there, but through side effects:
`prefix` also builds the table title, and `token` feeds ramp order and sizing, so the failing lines are
about those. So each mutation was also run in a form that touches only the Token cell's short argument.
Both still fail by the short-name assertion itself: "34: short: the space step prints 025 (space/025)".
`pds3/space/` is two segments deep, so that fixture already separates the two readings.

**The fix (test only, so no change note).** §36 gains the #2623 shape for both tables. The same styles
are renamed under `lib/fx/`, a root two segments deep. Short mode must print the name below the root
(`shadow/xs`, `gradient/brand`), and the default the whole name. Short mode on the plain fixture, whose
names share no root, must print the whole name. The new cases sit in §36, clear of #2623's §34 hunk.

**Proof.** With the fix, each of the eight survivors fails by name. Those are M3 and M4 on each of the
two planners, in the issue's form and in the cell-only form:

- M3, either form → "36: short: effect styles under one root print the name below it, shadow/xs for
  lib/fx/shadow/xs (fx/shadow/xs)". The same holds for gradients, `(fx/gradient/brand)`.
- M4, either form → the same line, plus "36: short: effect styles that share no root print their whole
  name, shadow/xs (xs)". Likewise for gradients, `(brand)`.
