## (2026-09-25) — the textarea's resize grip and character counter in Figma (owner decisions (c) and (d))

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets, verifies live through the agent link, and merges).** Engine + plugin. **ENGINE 0.160.0 → 0.161.0** (a new glyph, three new schema fields, a new plan field, a def surface move → MINOR; main took 0.160.0 with #1668 while this was open, so the lane moved up one on the merge); CONTRACT STANDS at 12.0.0 (`token-contract --accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion`, level `none`). `schema/component-surface.json` accepted: `icon` (43 → 44 members) and `textarea` (and its two interaction-model variants) only — **field-message, text-field and select are byte-identical.** `schema/paint-census.json` accepted for the same two.

**What changed.** (1) A `resize-grip` glyph (two diagonal bars, ink in the artboard's bottom-right quadrant) joins the icon set. It is drawn for this project, not Remix Icon, and `icons/NOTICE.md` says so. (2) A new `PartDef.corner: 'bottom-right'` pins a `vector` out of the flow, `inset` in from its parent's corner. The plan carries the inset's variable name (`cornerInset`); both executors lift the glyph, place it at parent − artboard − inset, constrain it `MAX`/`MAX` and read the lift back. The schema refuses it on a non-vector, without an inset, on the root, and under a parent with no auto-layout. (3) Textarea draws the grip in the control's corner at `icon.size.xs` in `color.icon.secondary` (on-fill disabled ink at `disabled`), inset by the control's own `border-width.hairline`, behind a `resize handle` boolean, ON by default. (4) A new `messageRow` box holds the nested FieldMessage and a `counter` caption (`type.caption.md.default`, the `indicator` slot → `color.text.secondary`, page disabled ink), `space-between`, stretched. The counter is behind a `character count` boolean, OFF by default; its text is a `count` TEXT property keyed by `maxLength`, default "0 / 200" (the def's own counter format).

**The owner's answers (2026-09-25, on the PR).** (1) The grip stays two diagonal lines. (2) CHANGED: the counter must not depend on the message. Designers need message only, counter only, both or neither, with no stray empty row or gap; prefer a construction with no extra switch. (3) "0 / 200" stands. Answer 2 is built as follows.

**Why the first build could not meet answer 2, and what replaced it.** Two host facts decide it. A column's gap still applies before a visible child that is EMPTY (so an always-present row with both parts off leaves a stray `root-gap`), and a hidden child takes no cell and no gap. A Figma boolean toggles one layer. So the space above each part has to live INSIDE the layer its switch toggles: each switch now drives a CELL (`messageCell`, `counterCell`) that carries the stack gap as top padding, and the control and the message row sit in a new gap-0 column (`body`). With both cells off the row is empty, measures nothing, and has no gap above it. The second fact is placement: a `space-between` row with its first child hidden puts the one left at the START, so the counter would have jumped left with the message off. The counter's cell now GROWS across the row and justifies the caption to its end, so it trails in every combination. **No extra switch.** The owner's fallback (a `footer` switch holding the two) was not taken: it still needs the grow, and it still leaves a stray gap when the footer is on and both switches inside it are off.

**Two new schema fields, projector-only.** `PartDef.grow` (a box's `layoutGrow: 1`, `wrap`'s main-axis fill without the reflow) and `PartDef.paddingTop` (a box's top padding alone). Both executors already write `layoutGrow` on every created node and per-side padding from `bound`, so neither executor changed. `grow`'s precondition is `wrap`'s (a bounded parent main axis), widened by one case: a row stretched across a column (`crossAxisFill`) is as wide as that column. Each refusal has a by-name arm in `test.ts`.

**The diagnosis that kept field-message untouched.** The counter needs to trail the message, and the message is a nested instance, so there is nowhere inside it to put one without an opt-in change to field-message that text-field and select would then carry. A row OWNED BY TEXTAREA around the nested message does the job. (The first build put the `message` boolean on that row, so the message switch hid the counter too. The owner's answer 2 reversed that; see above.)

**Why the grip is not `kind: 'absolute'`.** That kind is an instance of a shared component sized BY its parent grown by `inset` (the focus ring), and the schema refuses `size` on it. A grip draws its own glyph and keeps its own square artboard, so the placement is a field on `vector` rather than a second meaning for `absolute`.

**The byte-budget trap from #1666 held.** The paste executor's corner code is spliced only into a payload whose plans carry `cornerInset` (`CORNER_SLOT`, beside `MIN_LINES_SLOT`), and the empty splice adds no bytes, so every other payload is byte-identical.

**Gates (oracles authored in the gate, docs/34).** `test-write-components.ts` "textarea grip/counter": the real executor, dependency-first, shim `layoutModel`. The panel names and defaults are typed in the test; the grip's artboard is the shim's `icon/size/xs` value; the inset is a number (3) the test sets through `varOverrides` so no other shim value collides; the corner is worked from the control's measured box. Arms: `grip default` (a `resize handle` BOOLEAN defaulting true drives the grip, all 20 members shown), `grip corner` (ABSOLUTE, MAX/MAX, at control − 8 − 3 on both axes), `grip footprint` (control and member measure alike with the grip on and off, with an 80-character value so the control is wider than its 320 floor, a seed arm asserting that), `counter default` (the `character count` layer holds the counter, hidden on all 20), `counter independent` (the `message` layer holds the message and not the counter, and the counter's layer holds no message), `counter row` (the counter's layer is last, grows, and justifies MAX in the stretched row), `counter text`, and `counter footprint` over ALL FOUR combinations at a caption line box under and over the glyph: the member measures label + gap + control, plus one gap and the taller shown part when either is shown, the gap being the shim's `space/100` typed in the test. The shim learned one host fact under `layoutModel`: a hidden child takes no cell. `lint-absolute-inset.ts` gains arm E: the plan's `cornerInset` is the def's own key, resolves to a FLOAT in every brand, and is ≥ the parent's stroke weight (read from the def's parent part), so the artboard never lies over the border; both directions of representation (`MUST_COVER_CORNER`). `anatomy-readback.ts` classifies `cornerInset` (ABSOLUTE, MAX/MAX), so `test:roundtrip` reads the pin back. `lint-glyph-geometry.ts` records `textarea.grip` in `FIXED_GLYPH` and `MUST_COVER`.

**The icon-count move, stated.** `test.ts`'s glyph-shape arm counts distinct rendered shapes: 40 → 41 (42 path strings), because the grip is a new shape; the three declared -fill/-line collisions stay the only ones. `lint-icon-count.ts` derives its expected from `ICON_NAMES.length` (now 44) and passes unchanged; the icon def's prose states no count. `lint-axis-values.ts`'s authored `name` register gains `resize-grip` in its sorted place — the register states the icon axis at full width by design, so a new glyph must be written into it.

**A packing defect #1666 left latent, found here and fixed.** `planSetChunks` measures its shell from an EMPTY slice, and `payloadBuildFor` splices the reserved-lines (and now the corner-pin) code only where a plan needs it — so the shell was measured without the spliced code, and every textarea chunk shipped over the budget it was packed to. #1666's splice alone fit inside the MCP paste's margin; with the corner code the textarea scripts reached 45,963 characters against `SCRIPT_CEILING`'s 45,000 and `test-mcp-paste.ts`'s `size/*` arms failed. `emit` now splices from the whole set's plans when handed no slice (the worst case), and the largest script is back to 44,970 (a color-alias script, unchanged).

**Mutations, each from a committed `wip:` HEAD, restored:** (1a) the plugin executor's corner lift removed (`kid.layoutPositioning = 'ABSOLUTE'`) → `textarea grip corner` (`AUTO … at (74, 12), want ABSOLUTE MAX/MAX 8x8 at (309, 85)`) and `textarea grip footprint` (`control 504x96 with the grip, 496x96 without`) fail by name; the executor's own read-back miss also reddens the 0-miss arms, and `test:roundtrip` fails `textarea (20)` on the `cornerInset` field. (1b) the same line removed from the paste executor → `test.ts` fails `#1392 the textarea set runs CLEAN through the paste payload` (`grip.layoutPositioning -> DISCARDED …`). (2) the counter defaulted ON → `textarea counter default` fails by name (`defaultValue: true; 0 hidden`), and `lint-component-surface` fails `surface/textarea` on the digest. (3) the stack gap moved from the cells back onto the `body` column → `textarea counter footprint` fails by name at both caption boxes, on exactly the neither combination (`message off, count off: 128, want 112`, 60/80). (4) the counter cell's `grow` removed → `textarea counter row` fails by name. (5) the `paddingTop`-beside-`padding` refusal disabled → `test.ts` fails `'paddingTop' beside 'padding' is refused BY NAME`.

**Not verified live.** That the host keeps an ABSOLUTE glyph in the corner of an auto-layout frame that grows after paste (a designer typing more lines) rests on the `MAX`/`MAX` constraint and is modeled offline only; recorded in the def's `notes.unverified`. The grip's optical weight beside the value text at 16px is unjudged by any gate. That the host collapses the empty message row to zero height with both switches off rests on Figma's hug rule; the shim models it (an empty hug frame measures its padding, here none). The shim does not model main-axis placement (`layoutGrow`, `MAX`), so the counter's trailing position is asserted from the built properties, not from a measured `x`.

## (2026-09-25) — the textarea's rows floor was kept by the host but reported DISCARDED (single precision)

**STATUS: merged by the orchestrator.** Plugin + engine paste payload + read-back. **ENGINE 0.159.0 → 0.160.0**; CONTRACT STANDS.

**What the owner saw.** The first live textarea build (their MCP testing file, via the build menu, agent link on) reported `⚠️ 20 misses (text.minHeight -> DISCARDED (set 79.19999885559082 for 3 lines, reads 79.19999694824219)`. The floor WAS kept. Figma stores `minHeight` at single precision: `Math.fround(79.19999885559082) === 79.19999694824219`. The executor compared with `!==`, so every kept floor read as dropped. #1666's one unverified point is now answered: the host keeps `minHeight` on a TEXT auto-layout child.

**The fix.** One tolerance, `MIN_HEIGHT_TOLERANCE = 0.01` px, in all three places that compare it:
- the plugin executor;
- the inlined paste payload;
- `anatomy-readback.ts`, which had allowed only `1e-6`, still under the ~2e-6 the rounding moves an 80px value.

A genuinely dropped or wrong floor misses by whole lines, so the tolerance hides nothing real.

**Why no test caught it.** The plugin shim stored `minHeight` as a double, and #1666's metric cases gave a float32-exact 72 for NB (24 × 3). The shim now stores `minHeight` through `Math.fround`, as the host does. The textarea rows gate gains the live case, 16px at 165%.

**By-name mutation** (committed HEAD, restored): reverting the executor to `!==` fails:
- `✗ textarea rows (18px at 140%) … 20 misses — text.minHeight -> DISCARDED`
- `✗ textarea rows (the live case: 16px at 165%) …`

**The paste path is gated too** (an independent review caught that it wasn't). The engine paste stub now stores `minHeight` through `Math.fround` and takes `textMetrics`. A new arm runs textarea's payload at the live 16px × 165%. Reverting `PAYLOAD_MIN_LINES` to `!==` fails `❌ anatomy/textarea paste: at 16px × 165% (79.2px, stored single-precision) the reserved-rows floor reads back as KEPT (["text.minHeight -> DISCARDED"])`.

## (2026-09-25) — the textarea builds in Figma (projection modeled on text field)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets, verifies live through the agent link, and merges).** Engine + plugin. **ENGINE 0.158.0 → 0.159.0** (a new def surface and a new plan field → MINOR); CONTRACT STANDS (every binding is an existing name). Five design choices are held for the owner and built as neutral defaults — they lead the PR body: which axes project, how many rows show, the resize handle, the counter, the default text.

**What changed.** `textarea.ts` gains text-field's anatomy and `figmaProperties`: the column (nested FieldLabel, the bordered control, nested FieldMessage following `status`), the status-led border, the five projected states, the focus-ring nesting and the 320 width floor — status(4) × state(5) = 20 members. To match text-field it also takes the hover wash (`overlay.hover`), a bare `border` rest key (spelled `border.rest`, the disabled branch found no rest border and dropped the edge at `disabled`), text-field's `value` and `showMessage` props (the Figma text property and message switch are keyed by prop), and drops its `focus-ring` color key (the nested ring owns its color; the `NESTED_WITHOUT_ANATOMY` entry retired with it). `size` left `variants` for text-field's #795 reason; `lint-rung-names` admits the ladder stated once. The panel needed no change: both `apps/studio/src/main.ts`'s catalogue and the plugin ask the projector, so the def is offered once it projects.

**The height, which is the one structural difference.** The control binds no height and hugs. A new `PartDef.lines` on the value text names the `rows` PROP (never a count, so the Figma box and the code prop read one number); the plan carries `minLines` (3); both executors write the text's `minHeight` = rows × the line height the host reports for the styled node (`PIXELS`, or `PERCENT` of `fontSize`), after the append. So the box is rows × line height + block padding in every brand, with no pixel in the def and no new token. `AUTO` line height is a named miss, not a guess.

**A byte-budget trap for whoever next touches the paste payload.** Button's #536 probe grid packed to 41,983 of `SET_CHUNK_BYTES`' 42,000 on main — 17 bytes of headroom. The reserved-lines write, unconditional in `PAYLOAD_BUILD`, pushed it into a second chunk and failed `test.ts`. So the paste snippet is spliced in (`payloadBuildFor`) only for a payload whose plans carry `minLines`, and every other payload is byte-identical. The next unconditional addition to `PAYLOAD_BUILD` will hit the same wall.

**Gates (oracles authored in the gate, docs/34).** `test-write-components.ts` "textarea rows": the real executor builds dependencies first into one live file under the shim's `layoutModel`; ROWS = 3 is hand-written, the line height is (a) NB's emitted `body/md/default` resolved through its own tree and (b)/(c) 18px at 140% and a 30px PIXELS line, and pad-y is the shim's own variable value. Every control must measure 3 × line + 2 × pad-y with 0 misses and 0 footprint misses; an in-test arm drops `lines` and requires a one-line box. The shim learned `styleMetrics` (a style's size and line height on the node) and a literal `minHeight` floor; the engine paste stub learned the same. `anatomy-readback.ts` gains a `minLines` predicate re-deriving the floor from the host node's own line height (40 nodes compared). `test.ts`'s #1009 arm names textarea's value text as the one `TOP` override, and #1608's wash-binder list gains textarea. Three hand-named registers move with the def, each by its own gate's demand: `lint-paint-placement`'s `EXPECT_ANATOMY` / `EXPECT_PAINTERS` gain textarea, and `lint-axis-values`' `size` register drops it (it no longer declares `variants.size`). `token-contract.json` moves only its `engineVersion` stamp.

**Mutations, each from a committed `wip:` HEAD, restored:** (1) executor writes `minHeight = 72` (NB's number, hard-coded) — NB arm passes, `textarea rows (18px at 140%)` and `(a 30px PIXELS line)` fail by name; this is why there are three line heights, not one. (2) projector emits `minLines: 1` — all three `textarea rows` arms fail by name. (3) `rows` default 3 → 4 — `lint-component-surface` fails `surface/textarea` (digest drift) and the `textarea rows` arms fail.

**Not verified live.** That Figma keeps a `minHeight` on a TEXT child of an auto-layout frame with `textAutoResize: HEIGHT` is modeled offline and recorded in the def's `notes.unverified`. The paste executor's arithmetic is covered only by its no-miss run in `test.ts` (the stub's metrics are fixed), so a hard-coded paste value would not fail there; the plugin path is the gated one.

## (2026-09-25) — the field-message row reserves its status glyph's height (text field and select keep one footprint)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** Engine + plugin test harness. **ENGINE 0.157.0 → 0.158.0** (projected surface moves → MINOR); CONTRACT STANDS at 12.0.0 (the floor binds an existing name, `icon.size.xs`; `token-contract --accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion`, level `none`). `schema/component-surface.json` `--accept`ed: `field-message` only (4 members → 4, plan digest moved because the row gains a binding). text-field and select plans are byte-identical; they nest the message as an instance. Gate count **STANDS**: the new arms live in `test-write-components.ts` (plugin `test`) and `test.ts`.

**What was measured (live, through the agent link, NB Approved MCP Testing File, owner's `nb-redesign`).** text-field built with 15 `footprint` misses and select with 12, e.g. `status=error, state=rest measures 320x99 but status=default, state=rest measures 320x98`. Read off the host: the nested field-message draws a 16px glyph beside its caption in the three validation statuses and none in the default one. This brand's caption line box is 15 (12px at `compact` 1.25), so a status row is max(16, 15) = 16 and the default row is 15. Any brand whose caption line box is under the glyph size hits this.

**Owner's decision (final): option (a).** Reserve the glyph's height in every status. Option (b), a smaller glyph, was declined. No other visual change.

**What changed.** A new `PartDef.minHeight`: a token-bound auto-layout height floor on a `box`, projected as a bound `minHeight` (`anatomy-figma.ts` box branch). Both executors bind `n.bound` generically, so neither needed a change. `anatomyErrors` refuses it on a non-box, on a box with no `layout` (the `minWidth` rules), and beside a bound `height`/`size`. Its key rides the same binding-key-in-tokens check as `height`. `field-message`'s row binds `minHeight: 'glyph-size'` (`icon.size.xs`). **A floor, not a fixed height, so no max has to be computed:** a hugging row under a floor measures max(floor, tallest child). The caption wins where it is taller, the glyph's height wins where it is not, and a wrapping message still grows. Alignment is untouched (`align: 'start'`); in the default status the caption sits at the top of a row one pixel taller than its line box. **Code side:** nothing emits CSS from the anatomy and the studio does not render field-message, so the change is the def plus its Figma projection. A code implementer reads the row's `minHeight` as `min-block-size: <icon.size.xs>`, which the part's comment says.

**The shim had to learn height (`component-shim.ts`).** Before, every frame hugged as a row, a TEXT node measured 0 tall and an instance measured 0. That is enough for every width claim and blind to this defect. Added: (1) opt-in `layoutModel`: a `VERTICAL` frame stacks (heights sum + `itemSpacing`, width = widest child), a TEXT node is `textLineBox[style]` tall, an instance of a member this run built (`liveRoot`) measures its main, and the literal `minWidth` floors a frame's width (without it, text-field's column followed the message's width and drifted 8px, which the host's 320 control prevents); (2) always on: a bound `minHeight` floors a hugging frame; (3) always on: **a bound width/height wins over an earlier `resize()`**. `resize()` used to replace the getters with data properties, so the SVG glyph frame stayed at its 24px artboard after the executor bound it to `icon.size.xs`. On the host the binding wins. Resize-then-bind is the only order the executors use, and the ring clears its bindings before it resizes, so every existing arm reads the same.

**Gates (oracles authored in the gate, docs/34).** `test-write-components.ts` "message-row" block: the real executor builds dependencies first into one live file (`prebuildDependencies`, `liveRoot`, `layoutModel`). The glyph height is the shim's own variable value, the caption line box is set one pixel under it, and the expected row is that max worked by hand. Arms: the seed is load-bearing (with no floor, the default row is one pixel short); every field-message status row measures the glyph; every text-field / select status member has its `status=default` sibling's box (compared from member names, not the executor's cohort key) with 0 footprint misses; the in-test revert reproduces the live report's **15 and 12** misses, hand-copied, in the owner's shape (`320x68` vs `320x67`); a caption taller than the glyph wins in every status (a floor, not a fixed height). `test.ts`: the plan binds `minHeight → icon/size/xs` on all four rows, plus the three refusal arms and the binding-key arm, each by name.

**Mutation, from a committed `wip:` HEAD, restored:** delete `minHeight: 'glyph-size'` from `field-message.ts`. Fails `message-row text-field/select: every field-message status row measures 8 … [status=default:7, …]`, `message-row text-field: every status member … keeps its default sibling's footprint (… 15 footprint misses — footprint -> status=error, state=rest measures 320x68 but status=default, state=rest measures 320x67 …)`, the select twin (12), and `test.ts`'s `field-message: every status row binds minHeight to icon/size/xs … (got [, , , ])`. Two refusal arms also went red under that mutation only because their fixture inherited the def's `minHeight`; they now set it themselves.

**Not verified live.** The host is expected to honor a variable-bound `minHeight` on an auto-layout frame (`minHeight` is a bindable node field). The offline shim models that; it has not been rebuilt in the owner's file.

## (2026-09-25) — component wiring outlasts the host's per-member refusal window (bounded back-off, #1664)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** Plugin + a stamp-only regen. **ENGINE 0.156.0 → 0.157.0** (plugin behavior → MINOR); CONTRACT STANDS at 12.0.0 (`--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion`). Gate count **STANDS**: the new arms live in `test-write-components.ts`, inside the plugin `test` step.

**What was measured (through the agent link, #1660).** Building Button (432 members) sometimes leaves one CONTIGUOUS run of members, in wire order, whose every component-property reference fails: members 302–355 on the owner's file (110 misses), 169–212 on the NB Approved MCP Testing File (90 misses, all 44 members wired in 0.8 s). Two shapes: a throw ("Could not create a new component property reference") and an accepted write that is not kept ("DISCARDED (set label#…, reads undefined)"). Every member either side wired normally. #1568's deferred retry (one `setTimeout(0)`, one re-attempt) ran ~6 s after the window and repaired 0; a few minutes later the same write on member 170 succeeded. `setReresolved: 0` — no identity moved, so this is not the #1337/#1473/#1516 stale-handle family. The refusal is per member and time-limited, and outlasts one yield.

**What changed.** `write-components.ts`: the single deferred pass is now a bounded back-off, `REF_BACKOFF_MS = [500, 2000, 5000, 10000]` (at most 4 passes, 17.5 s worst case). It stops the moment the queue empties, and a clean build never enters it. The wait is `yieldTo(ms)`: `YieldFn` gained an optional delay and `realYield` passes it to `setTimeout`. No busy-waiting. Each pass re-resolves the coordinate fresh (`liveMember` + `findOwnPart`, as #1568 did), writes, then **re-finds and reads back** before it counts a repair, because an accepted write is not a kept one. The DISCARDED shape joins the same queue: a pre-scan after the wire loop reads each wired reference back off the handle it was written to, and anything that does not hold is queued. An id divergence still goes to #866's read-back. The pre-scan reads the written handle rather than calling `findOne` on purpose: a subtree search per reference during a cold build is the ~46 s #701 removed. The read-back after it still re-finds every reference fresh and remains the check. Telemetry: `refsBackoff: [{ afterMs, retried, repaired }]` per pass, in the result, in the set's `build` report (`getSharedPluginData('prism3','build')`, additive), and as a `[prism3 #1664]` console line printed only when the back-off ran.

**Shim + arms.** `component-shim.ts` gains `refuseRefsWindow: { members, ms, shape: 'throw' | 'discard', now }`. The window opens at the first reference write on a named member and closes `ms` later on the TEST's clock, which the test's own `yieldTo(ms)` advances. So the wait the executor asked for is witnessed outside the executor, and a 10 s wait costs the suite nothing. Arms `#1664a` (a 3 s window heals fully, both shapes; independent read-back of the set's held references against a clean build), `#1664b` (a permanent refusal ends as named misses after ≤ 4 waits / ≤ 18 s, and the build returns), `#1664c` (a clean build asks for no wait).

**Mutations, each from a committed `wip:` HEAD, restored, each failing by name:** M1 `REF_BACKOFF_MS = [500]` (back to one pass) → `#1664a` ×6 (+ the `#1664b` input pin); M1b `break` after the first pass → `#1664a` ×6; M2 unbounded loop (clamp at the last delay, no pass limit) → `#1664b` ×4 (the test's clock guard throws past 20 waits); M3 wait before checking the queue → `#1664c`; M4 pre-scan disabled → `#1664a` discard ×4.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies live: keep the Figma window in the FOREGROUND.** With it in the background, the plugin's drawing calls ran 20–300× slower: a 4-member build chunk took 8 s, one took 97 s and finished the instant the window came back. That is host behavior, not ours, and it will swamp any timing you read (including the back-off's). Not fixed here and no UI copy added; whether to say anything to the designer about it is the owner's call.

**Not verified: the live window length.** 17.5 s is sized to the evidence: repaired 0 at ~6 s, repaired at "minutes". If live runs show the last pass still repairing 0, the window is longer than the schedule, and the `refsBackoff` numbers in the build report are what to read before stretching it. The back-off posts no progress while it waits, so a build that needs it pauses for up to ~18 s after the last wire chunk with no UI change; a progress phase for it would be new UI copy, so it is held.

## (2026-09-25) — the agent link, transport B: a local desktop bridge over the same protocol

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE; stacks on the mailbox PR (#1660).** Plugin + `tools/figma-bridge/` + a stamp-only regen. **ENGINE 0.155.0 → 0.156.0** (plugin behavior → MINOR); CONTRACT STANDS. Gate count **STANDS**: `apps/plugin/test-agent-bridge.ts` is an arm of the plugin `test` step.

**What it adds.** `tools/figma-bridge/server.ts` is a stdio MCP server (`figma_status`, `figma_run {cmd, args, timeoutMs}`, `figma_logs {since, limit}`) and a hand-rolled RFC 6455 WebSocket server on `ws://localhost:17331` (`node:http` + `node:crypto`, no `ws`). While the owner has the link on, the plugin's UI iframe holds the socket — the main thread has no network — and `src/agent-bridge-relay.ts` relays each command to the SAME dispatcher the mailbox uses, then streams progress and console lines back; they reach the MCP client as `notifications/progress` / `notifications/message` and stay readable through `figma_logs`. The protocol is unchanged apart from two additive fields: `transports.bridge` on the link state and a `link-off` error for a bridge command that lands after switch-off.

**Netting found a phantom-plugin defect, fixed here.** The first version had no test for a plugin reconnecting mid-command (deleting the replacement branch in `attach` left the suite green). Writing that test, modeled on the Figma Console MCP bridge's same-file reconnect (MIT, studied not copied), exposed a second, real defect: `node:http` hands over upgraded sockets HALF-OPEN, so a plugin that simply goes away — Figma quits, the iframe is killed, no close frame — never fired `'close'`, and `figma_status` kept reporting a connected plugin whose every command would wait out its timeout. The server now treats the peer's `'end'` as the end (destroy → `'close'` → detach). New `test-agent-bridge.ts` arms, each mutated from a committed HEAD and failing by name: removing the replacement → `reconnect: the older connection is closed (1000)` + `reconnect: the in-flight run fails with the reason, not a timeout`; removing the `'end'` handler → `drop: a plugin that goes away without a close frame is not left "connected"`.

**The manifest change (the owner approved it, 2026-09-25).** `networkAccess.devAllowedDomains: ["ws://localhost:17331"]`, and nothing else — `allowedDomains: ["none"]` and its offline reasoning stay as shipped. The port has one source (`BRIDGE_PORT` in the relay); the server reads it, and the manifest entry has to match it.

**Two traps worth knowing.** (1) `localhost` resolves to `::1` on some machines and `127.0.0.1` on others, so the server binds both loopback addresses (IPv6 best-effort). (2) The first test run failed `run: … unchanged` on a result carrying `é`: the TEST's stdout reader decoded each chunk separately and split a two-byte character at a chunk boundary. The server's own stdin reader already used `setEncoding('utf8')`; the test now does too.

**Mutations, each from a committed `wip:` HEAD, restored, each failing by name:** B1 the relay stops recording the ids it delivered → `e2e/routes`, `e2e/parity`; B2 bridge commands dispatched through a module-load copy of `ACTIONS` → `e2e/routes` ×2 (a copy spread per call survives — it copies the spied entries — so the mutation that means "a copy" is the load-time one); B3 the server stops unmasking → `fragmented`, `ping`; B4 the relay ignores switch-off → `e2e/switch-off` ×2.

**Not verified — the first live check.** Whether Figma's desktop app lets a development plugin's iframe open `ws://localhost:17331` under `devAllowedDomains`. First run: start the server, switch the link on, and `figma_status` should say `connected: true`.

## (2026-09-25) — the agent link, transport A: an agent drives the RUNNING plugin by command through the file (mailbox)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** Plugin + `tools/figma-mcp/` + a stamp-only regen. **ENGINE 0.154.0 → 0.155.0** (plugin behavior → MINOR); CONTRACT STANDS at 12.0.0 (`--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion`). Gate count **STANDS** at 66: the new suite `apps/plugin/test-agent-link.ts` is an arm of the existing plugin `test` step. The desktop bridge (transport B) is the stacked follow-up PR.

**What an agent can now do.** With the owner's **Agent link** switched on in the plugin (a temporary dashed chip, bottom-left — placement and name are HELD for the owner), `npx tsx tools/figma-mcp/agent-link.ts send <cmd> [args]` prints a ~750-character `use_figma` script (plus the command's args; aurora's full `BrandInput` makes it ~2 kB) that queues the command in the file's root shared plugin data (`prism3agent/inbox`); the plugin polls about once a second, runs it through the SAME handler the panel's button reaches, and writes a result envelope; `read <id>` prints the script that reads it back. Commands: `status`, `apply-theme`, `build-components`, `file-setup`, `prune`, `readback`. No `cleanup` — no panel action removes components, and the link routes only to panel handlers.

**The diagnosis that made "no parallel path" checkable rather than asserted.** Every handler in `main.ts` posted straight to `postToUi`, so a second caller could only have copied them. They now report to an `ActionSink`: the panel's sink posts exactly what was posted before (the #836 `postVerdict` reader and its `≥6` sites are unchanged — `test-build-identity.ts` still green), the dispatcher's sink captures the verdict plus the structured `data` each handler now exposes (misses by axis, orphans, the component report and telemetry, the prune plan). Both callers reach the handlers through ONE exported `ACTIONS` table.

**main.ts is importable after all.** #1106's premise was that `main.ts` cannot load outside the sandbox because it calls `figma.showUI` at module scope. It loads fine once the three globals (`figma`, `__html__`, `PRISM3_BUILD`) exist first — no restructuring needed. `test-agent-link.ts` does exactly that, spies on the `ACTIONS` entries after import, and requires BOTH the UI message and the agent command to reach the same entry; the agent side is the exact text the CLI prints, run as `use_figma` runs it. The parity arms compare the agent's `result.verdict` byte-for-byte against what the UI path posted. #1106's behavioral-coverage ask for `postVerdict` is now reachable with this pattern; not done here (one concern per PR).

**Mailbox design, and the one decision a reviewer should check.** Each key has one writer (agent: `inbox`; plugin: `claimed`, `result:<id>`, `results`, `link`), so the two sides never overwrite each other through multiplayer. The id is claimed BEFORE the handler runs; `claimed` sheds an id only once the agent has dropped it from the inbox, so retention can never cause a re-run. Results past 90 kB are chunked (UTF-8-counted by hand — `TextEncoder` is not promised in the sandbox), parts first, manifest last; the last 20 are kept. **Commands already queued at switch-on are answered `stale`, not run** — turning the link on must not replay an hour-old queue. The `link` record is written on switch on/off and after each command, NOT per poll (a write per second would be a document change and an undo step per second).

**Not verified — the first live check.** Whether a `use_figma` write reaches the owner's open plugin through multiplayer, and how fast. Designed for with a poll (not a `documentchange` listener, which would stack a second unknown and need every page loaded under `dynamic-page`).

**Mutations, each from a committed `wip:` HEAD, restored, each failing by name:** M1 dispatcher handed `{ ...ACTIONS, applyTheme: (i, s) => applyTheme(i, s) }` → `routes/*`; M2 the UI's `apply-theme` case calls `applyTheme` directly → `routes/apply-theme`; M3 `file-setup` routed to `seedFromFile` → `routes/file-setup` + `parity/file-setup`; M4 claim moved after the dispatch → `claim-before-run`; M5 `retireStale()` dropped → `stale`.

**Environment trap, for whoever re-verifies.** The container's browser cache is Chromium build 1194 and the pinned playwright wants 1234. Instead of `npx playwright install`, a scratch `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` of symlinks (`chromium_headless_shell-1234/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell` → the installed `headless_shell`) launches fine and `npm run verify` went 66/66 PASS, 0 SKIP.

**The owner's answers, after the first live run** (2026-09-25, NB Approved MCP Testing File: `status` picked up in 0.9 s, a full Button build of 432 variants in ~60 s with 0 misses, and the 96 tinted-wash variants read back at 0.1/0.2/0.3). (1) The switch stays bottom-left and stays "Agent link", drawn as a small dark box with light text. (2) The paste harness (#1659) stays: it is the only path that works with nobody at the desk (the plugin closed, Figma closed), kept for small tests. (3) Agent commands update the panel's status pills like a button does; an agent's prune PREVIEW arrives `pillOnly` and never opens the confirm dialog, because that dialog's Confirm would prune against the panel's knobs, not the input the agent previewed. **A trap for whoever re-verifies:** the panel's build progress fraction is not driven by an agent's build — `component-progress` is accepted only while the panel's own build is pending, so an agent build shows its verdict pill at the end and nothing before it.

## (2026-09-25) — the Figma test loop runs over the Figma MCP with the plugin closed: paste-in Apply Theme, run-all components, read-back, report (#111, #1553)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** Plugin + `tools/` only. **No engine change, no `out/**` change, no version bump** — `packages/engine/` is untouched. Gate count **STANDS**: the new suite is an arm of the existing plugin `test` step (`apps/plugin/test-mcp-paste.ts`, wired in `apps/plugin/package.json`), the same precedent as `test-write-preflight.ts` and `test-file-components.ts`. Files: `apps/plugin/src/apply-theme.ts` (**NEW**: Apply Theme's write sequence, lifted out of `main.ts` unchanged), `apps/plugin/src/theme-ports.ts` (**NEW**: the host → port adapters both drivers bind through), `apps/plugin/src/mcp-steps.ts` (**NEW**: the runtime bundled into each script), `apps/plugin/mcp-paste.ts` (**NEW**: the Node generator), `apps/plugin/test-mcp-paste.ts` (**NEW**: the gate), `tools/figma-mcp/{plan.ts,report.ts,README.md}` (**NEW**), `main.ts` (calls `runApplyTheme`; `SWAP_TARGET` moved to `build-deps.ts`), `write-components.ts` (`emitCoordValue` exported), `tsconfig.main.json` (includes `mcp-steps.ts`), `test-write-components.ts` (the #1280 input pin, see below). Filed from this work: #1657 (the engine's set payload writes no #1623 description), #1658 (`materialise-to-figma.ts` is a second hand-written writer that lacks the pre-flight, the stamp and the #680 cross-product).

**What an agent can now do.** `npx tsx tools/figma-mcp/plan.ts --brand <brief|example id> --apply --build all --cleanup --out <dir>` writes numbered `use_figma` scripts (≤45,000 characters each against the tool's 50,000) and a `manifest.json`; the agent runs them one per call in order, saves each return value, and `report.ts` prints one PASS/FAIL summary (pre-flight conflicts, per-step misses/refusals, the read-back compared with the plan, per-component misses and variant counts). The runbook is `tools/figma-mcp/README.md`; its first rule is that the scripts run only against a scratch file the owner has named.

**The diagnosis that made it small: bundle the executors, cut the sequence.** The plugin's apply is one call; a `use_figma` call is capped. Rather than a second writer (the path `materialise-to-figma.ts` took, and drifted on — #1658), each script is an esbuild IIFE of ONE executor step plus its plan slice as data, so the paste path and the plugin path are the same code cut at different places. The cut is invisible in the file because every executor is find-or-create by name and resolves alias targets from what the FILE holds: the color plan runs as palette → create (pass A) → alias (pass B) slices across scripts exactly as within one call. **One rule is load-bearing and non-obvious:** `applyFloatPlan` resolves aliases only among the collections in its call (`space` aliases into `core`), so every float-alias script carries every float collection with no create rows. Today's plans put all float aliases in one script, so this was unexercised until the gate forced a 29,500-character slice ceiling — the M5 mutation below survived until that arm existed.

**Bundle size, measured.** The first bundle of the color step was 84KB: `rename-map.ts` imports the one-line `figmaVarName` from `anatomy-figma.ts`, which drags the whole projector (46.5KB) and `icon-glyphs.ts` (14.6KB) in. The fix serves that import from a virtual module whose body is the real function's own source (`figmaVarName.toString()`, the engine's own ship-the-source move for `nestVariantMatch`); any other name imported from `anatomy-figma` fails the build. Second, modules are marked side-effect-free for the bundler, which dropped every non-variable step from ~17KB to 1.5–6.5KB. The variable steps stay at ~27KB because `version.ts`'s `DEPRECATIONS` table (11.7KB) is genuinely read by the rename pass. **Trap:** esbuild's `buildSync` refuses plugins, so the bundles are built once at module load with top-level `await`.

**Two host behaviors the MCP guidance does not settle, handled both ways and reported.** (1) SHARED plugin data — the guidance lists `setPluginData` as unsupported and is silent on `setSharedPluginData`, which carries the #1581 stamp and the #131 brand. Every script probes it (`probeSharedData`); if refused, it runs in LEDGER mode: the two records are kept outside the file, returned per step, merged by `report.ts --ledger-out`, and baked into the next `plan.ts --ledger` run so the pre-flight still reads provenance. The gate proves the fallback is load-bearing: without the ledger, a second run's pre-flight refuses the file the first run wrote. (2) `figma.loadAllPagesAsync` IS listed as unsupported, and the engine's component payloads call it before `figma.root.findAll*`. Instead of editing the payload text, each component script runs the payload with a `figma` parameter shadowing the global: a Proxy whose `loadAllPagesAsync` tries the native call and otherwise loads each page with `page.loadAsync()` (no page switch), and whose root searches then walk the loaded pages. **Neither has run against a live `use_figma` host yet** — the first live run's `shared` and `host.loadAllPages` fields answer both.

**`icon` needed its own arm.** The plugin writes `emitAsComponents` members as standalone `icon/<glyph>` components (#1012); the engine's chunk payload always builds a set, which would leave every button swap target missing. The paste path builds each glyph with `planToPluginJs`, then names it with the plugin's own `emitCoordValue` (now exported), sets the summary, and skips one already in the file.

**Parity proof (offline).** `test-mcp-paste.ts` runs `runApplyTheme` (the sequence `main.ts` runs) and the emitted scripts — executed as `use_figma` does, as an async function body whose one binding is `figma` — against one file model, and compares eleven named projections for nb-redesign and aurora: collections + modes, variables, literal values, aliases, scopes/hidden/descriptions, effect / paint / grid / text styles, the #1581 stamps, the #131 brand. Also: idempotent re-run (0 created, file byte-identical), re-theme (aurora over nb-redesign), the forced fine slicing, pre-flight refusal writing nothing, the ledger arms, cleanup, `summarize`, the pack round-trip on every example brand, component ordering / compilation / the page adapter, and the size check on every script for every example brand (all four `.design.md` briefs + `example-brands.json`). ## (2026-09-25) — the tinted-wash opacity takes a second assignment; 0.153.0's diagnosis was wrong (owner-found)

**STATUS: landed by the orchestrator.** On 0.153.0 the owner's NB button still built with the same 221 `container.fills.opacity -> DISCARDED (wanted 0.2, read back 1)` misses. Files: both executors (`apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts`, `packages/engine/anatomy-figma.ts`), both offline models (`apps/plugin/component-shim.ts`, the `test.ts` paste stub), `version.ts` (ENGINE 0.154.0).

**What was wrong with 0.153.0.** Its probe ran its cases in sequence on ONE rectangle. The "opacity before binding" case ran second, on a node already bound to that variable, and read back 0.2. Re-run in isolation, on FRAME, COMPONENT and RECTANGLE, it reads back 1. The rule the data actually supports: **the first time a paint bound to a color variable lands on a node, the host resets its opacity to 1; a re-assignment, once the binding is there, keeps it** (bind, assign, then assign a copy with the opacity → 0.2; assign the same bound paint twice → 0.2; every single-assignment form → 1). Verified on the owner's file for the exact new sequence: a frame 0.2, a component 0.3, and two variant members that keep 0.2 / 0.3 through `combineAsVariants`.

**Fix.** Both executors assign the bound paint, then re-assign `{ ...node.fills[0], opacity }`. 0.153's opacity-before-bind is reverted (it did nothing). Both offline models encode the measured rule. With 0.153's executors against them, `#1614 paste leg`, `#1614 plugin leg` and the NB-button arm fail by name, reading `@ 1`.

**Lesson for whoever probes the host next.** Run each case on a fresh node. A sequence of cases on one node carries state (here, an existing binding) from one case into the next, and a probe that does that can "confirm" a fix that doesn't work.

## (2026-09-25) — the tinted-wash hover keeps its opacity on the real host (owner-found)

**STATUS: landed by the orchestrator.** On 0.152.0 the owner's NB button built with 221 `container.fills.opacity -> DISCARDED (wanted 0.2, read back 1)` misses: every tinted-wash hover/pressed fill came out at full strength. Files: `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts` and `packages/engine/anatomy-figma.ts` (both executors' `paint()` take the opacity), `apps/plugin/component-shim.ts` and the `test.ts` paste stub (both model the host rule), `version.ts` (ENGINE 0.153.0).

**Measured, not guessed.** A probe on the owner's file through the Figma MCP (one temp rectangle, deleted) showed: bind, then spread `opacity: 0.2` onto the returned paint → reads back **1**; put `opacity: 0.2` on the paint, then bind → reads back **0.2**; set an opacity on a fill, clone it, bind the clone → **1**. The host keeps the opacity a paint was bound at. Both executors bound first and set opacity after, and both offline models kept whatever was assigned, so the #1614 legs passed offline and failed live.

**Fix.** `paint(var, where, opacity)` puts the opacity on the paint before `setBoundVariableForPaint`, in both executors (the paste one kept compact; it is near its byte budget). Both offline models record the bind-time opacity against the paint's `boundVariables` object (a spread carries it by reference) and normalize a bound paint back to it on assignment. With the old executors and the new models, the existing `#1614 paste leg` / `plugin leg` / NB-button assertions fail by name, reading `@ 1`; with the fix they pass.

**Same probe, #1646 answered.** A color variable CAN alias another with its own opacity from a plugin: `{ color: VARIABLE_ALIAS, opacity: 30 }` writes, a different opacity per mode writes, the opacity itself can alias a number variable, and the alias can cross collections to the real fill. The `COMPOSE_COLOR` expression shape is rejected. So a per-mode tinted wash (a hover variable aliasing the fill at each mode's own opacity step) is buildable; whether to switch is the owner's call, recorded on #1646.

## (2026-09-25) — an overridden inverse rest fill no longer aborts Apply Theme (owner-found)

**STATUS: landed by the orchestrator.** Owner rebuilt the plugin on 0.151.0 and Apply Theme failed: `write failed: emit-figma-color: nbds.color.inverse.interactive.primary.fill.hover is not a neutral step off a white / black rest fill (rest brand-neutral.025) — the Figma line cannot count its rungs`. Files: `packages/engine/modes.ts` (the per-state rung rule moves to a module-level `interactiveStateRungs`, same values), `emit-figma-color.ts` (reads it; `rungsOffRest` deleted), `test.ts` (regression arm), `version.ts` (ENGINE 0.152.0).

**Diagnosis.** #1645 built the inverse fill states' Figma line ("Primary fill on inverse, hover — 2 neutral rungs off the white / black rest") from structured data, but got the rung count by RE-DERIVING it from the light-mode aliases: rest had to be `palette.white` / `palette.black` and the state a `neutral.<n>` step, else throw. The engine's own rest is always white / black, so every committed brand passed. The owner's file overrides `inverse.interactive.primary.fill.rest` per mode to a step of their own palette (`brand-neutral.025`), which the override layer applies after derivation, and the re-derivation threw. A description is never worth aborting a write, and the number was never in doubt: the walk steps a fixed count per state.

**Fix.** The walk's `stateRungs` and the Figma line now read one exported rule. Committed `out/**` is byte-identical apart from the stamp, which proves the re-derivation always agreed with the rule where it could run. The new arm overrides the rest to `neutral.025` on the minimal brand and asserts the emission doesn't throw and that each state states 2 / 2 / 4 / 4 rungs (hand-written literals).

**Trap for whoever re-verifies.** The line still says "off the white / black rest" when an override points the rest elsewhere; the DTCG sentence says the same. The rung count is accurate (it counts from the white / black extreme the walk anchors to), but the rest named is the default, not the override. Rewording it per override is a copy call, left as is.

## (2026-09-25) — Gates that could pass vacuously now fail when their subject goes missing (#1268, #1269, #779, #1245, #1213, #1192, #1276, #1200)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** No ENGINE or CONTRACT bump: nothing emitted moves. Every change is a gate, a test, a comment, or studio markup/test code.

**#1268 — `test.ts` now fails when a section goes quiet, with no numeral.** The floor was 1800 against a live **104,698** assertions (not the 2,867 the issue measured), so the suite could lose almost all of them and still pass. Per-section floors would drift the way the floor did. So the new arm asks whether every `ok(` call site in the file executed at least once. EXPECTED is a text scan of `test.ts`. ACTUAL is V8 block coverage via `node:inspector`, which never touches `ok()`, mapped back to the file through `tsx`'s inline source map. **Traps, all measured:** (1) capturing a stack in `ok()` costs ~0.9ms a call, because V8 scans the position table of the 20,000-line top-level function (37s became 134s). Coverage costs ~13s. (2) Block coverage only instruments code compiled after it starts, and the module body is compiled first. The top-level function then reports one range, count 1, and **every site reads as executed**. So the outer instance starts coverage and imports `test.ts?cov`, then exits. (3) The transpiled script is whitespace-minified to ~25 lines, so offsets need the source map, not line numbers. (4) The arm's own messages contained the text `ok(`, and the scan flagged them. Unmapped sites are a loud failure by design. Failure-only sites (`ok(false, …)` in a catch) are exempt, and they are the negative control: on a green run at least one must read as unexecuted, or the probe cannot see a zero. **What it does not see:** a loop that still runs over fewer items.

**#1269 — paint-placement arm E is a closed set of names, not floors of 7/4** (live: 22 with an anatomy, 14 painters). A def that leaves either set fails by name, and a def that joins fails until it is listed. The failure text no longer states a corpus count.

**#1245 — the border-row smoke test asserts its family set is closed** against the rendered page's own token pills, in both directions.

**#1213 — `lint-doc-gates` parses `ci.yml` before scraping it.** `parseYamlSubset` is a strict, dependency-free parser for the block-YAML subset the workflow uses, and it refuses everything outside it. On the real file its tree is **identical to js-yaml's**. It agreed with js-yaml on 10 accept/refuse cases, including #1205's exact break. Its tree also cross-checks the regex scrape: the two must name the same steps. A step written `- run: …` then `name: …` is valid YAML the scrape cannot see, and the cross-check catches it. The #1222 comment (a missing check-run caused by an unmergeable PR) is not a property of the tree, so it is recorded in the gate header rather than gated.

**#779 §2/§3 — chrome is held to WCAG, specimens are marked at the render site.** The sweep measured 16,850 text nodes. 1,172 get their ink from an inline style, which is every specimen and no chrome. The chrome minimum is **4.53:1**, so a 4.5 / 3 (large) bar lands green with no tuning. `specimen()` in `main.ts` marks the 17 render sites. The probe records size and weight. Inline ink with no marker is a failure, which audits the marker from a second, independent reading. `.mo-playnote`'s 3.12 now fails by name. **Held for the owner:** specimens stay on the 2.0 floor, because holding each one to the contract it previews needs a specimen-to-contract map, and that is a contract decision. #779 stays open for it. **Finding filed as #1652:** Preview's pressed-state button specimens render at 2.54:1, below every specimen contract. They are either a studio role-pairing bug or the exempt inverse pressed state recorded 2026-09-24.

Mutating all six rules showed `inset` and `verticalAlign` were **already** caught by name by other arms, so the issue's "six" is really four. **#1192** — prose only: the "never demands a non-ramp" safety belongs to the window, not the anchor. It now has the plugin executor's #865 pass, in lockstep: the same properties, values and carve-outs, including the set's #1430 preserved framing, the glyph's `imported` subtree, and the #1387 declared-but-unresolvable neutralize. **The diagnosis that made it bigger than a fills fix:** the pass writes `paragraphSpacing`/`leadingTrim`, which detach an applied text style on the host (#1567, modeled in the stub), so porting it alone would have unstyled every paste label. `build` now re-applies the style after the pass, as the plugin does. **Gates for #1393, and why there are three.** (1) A node-level fills gate mirrors the plugin's #1387 one. Two footprint-drift mutation arms had to change: they deleted the paints branch's `strokesIncludedInLayout=false`, and `claimDefaults` now claims the same property on every auto-layout frame, as the plugin's always did. A **family tripwire** keeps that exemption from swallowing the one case it is contingently wrong about: an exempt axis's value that is also a live family (`appearance=text` binding `color.text.*`) fails by name instead of being counted as exempt. The reason prose dropped its false "`color.text.*` must not exist" clause. The `lint-axis-values` size reason had drifted again ("ten" beside a list of 14) and now names its exclusions instead of counting.

## (2026-09-25) — Studio previews use the inverse roles on an inverse ground (#1629); live Examples marker (#1075)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** Studio only: `apps/studio/src/outline-roles.ts` (**NEW**, pure helper), `apps/studio/src/main.ts` (the style guide's Outline row, the brand menu's Examples list), `apps/studio/test-outline-roles.ts` (**NEW**, wired into `npm test`), `apps/studio/test-smoke.mjs` (scenario 5C + section 5b), `apps/studio/package.json`. **No engine change, no `out/**`, no version bump.** Closes #1629, #1075. **#1215 held**, since it is a product call (details below).

**#1629, the diagnosis.** The Outline row took its fill, ink and edge from three separate expressions. The ink and edge had been switched to their `inverse.` twins by #461/#467. The fill never was, so the band preview painted the page's `black-alpha` wash over a near-black band. The fix pulls all three keys into one pure function, `outlineStateRoles(method, color, state, onInverseGround)`, so the ground switch now happens in one place. `outlineFillRole` is still the only method → family mapping, and the ground is a prefix in front of it, as it already was for ink and edge. Under `solid-tint` the helper reads `inverse.interactive.<c>.subtle-fill.*`, and every key it returns is asserted to resolve in the engine for every example brand, method and mode. The `opaque` guard from #575 is kept, even though no method is opaque since #1614.

**#1075, the diagnosis and the constraint kept.** The `+ New brand` half was already gone (#1199). What remained was the Examples marker, computed at render time from `brandState.id`, while the Name field deliberately skips the re-render because a re-render takes the caret. The fix is the option the issue offered: patch the class in place next to the existing `.bs-name` patch, using the same `isCurrentExample` predicate the render uses. **#1073's key question (id or origin) is deliberately left open.** The predicate is unchanged, and the smoke oracle is key-agnostic: the live markers must equal what a fresh render (close + reopen) computes, whichever key #1073 settles on.

**#1215: held, not fixed.** All four options in the issue change what the studio presents: boot a different brand, drop the corpus's only `compact` brand, surface density, or accept the gap. The issue itself calls it "a product call about what the studio should present". That is a design decision under principle 6, so the question is posted on the issue and nothing changed here.

## (2026-09-25) — `lint-us-english` catches the en-GB spellings it was blind to (#991, #1463)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** ENGINE 0.150.0 (shipped prose respelled); CONTRACT stands (no token name moves). Files: `packages/engine/prose-rules.ts` (the rule), `lint-us-english.ts` (SELF_CHECK samples + header trap 7), the respelled sources (`components/radio-row.ts`, `emit-icons.ts`, `schema/payload-manifest.json`, `README.md`, `skills/prism3-consume/SKILL.md`, `apps/studio/src/main.ts`, `styles.css`), `version.ts`, regenerated `out/**` + `icon-glyphs.ts`.

**The two holes.** (#991) `PATTERN`'s `-ise` arm listed its inflections and its `-our` arm allowed only `s`, so `coloured`, `honoured`, `favourite` and `honourable` passed. (#1463) Six classes sat outside every shape: `-ogue` (`catalogue`), `-ence` nouns (`licence`, `defence`), `-yse` (`analysed`), letter swaps (`artefact`, `aluminium`, `tyre`, `mould`, …), and the reverse single-L class (`skilful`, `fulfil`, `enrol`, `instalment`), which `DOUBLE_L` cannot see because it looks for the doubled form. The `-our` arm now takes `ed|ing|ings|ful|less|able|ably|ite|ites`. `EN_GB_WORDS` takes the letter swaps, `-ogue` and `-ence`. Two new shapes, `YSE` and `SINGLE_L`, cover the rest. Each is sampled in both directions in SELF_CHECK.

**What it found, respelled:** `catalogue` ×6 (the consume skill, radio-row's shipped `focus` doc, a studio comment that ships in both bundles), `licence` ×4 (payload manifest, the generated `icon-glyphs.ts` header), `honoured` ×2 and `colouring` ×1 (studio source that ships), `artefact` ×1 (engine README). The Remix Icon license is itself titled "License", so no proper-noun exemption was needed. The earlier `coloured` instances #991's comment listed were already gone on main.

**Deliberately not flagged.** `dialogue`, `prologue` and `monologue` are standard en-US, so flagging them would make a house-style call, not apply a spelling rule. None appear in shipped text today. The plural nouns `analyses`/`paralyses` are en-US and sit in `NOT_EN_GB`, which also hides the en-GB verb `analyses`; `analyse`/`analysed`/`analysing` stay visible.

**Mutations, by name.** Subject side: planting each of `brand-coloured`, `catalogue`, `licence`, `artefact`, `analysed`, `skilful` in the gated engine README fails the gate naming the word (exit 1); the same words give 0 hits under `origin/main`'s `enGb`. Rule side: stripping the `-our` inflections, dropping `EN_GB_WORDS`, `YSE` or `SINGLE_L` from `enGb`'s loop, or removing `contoured` or `analyses` from `NOT_EN_GB` each fails SELF_CHECK naming the sample.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** `PATTERN` needs 3+ letters before `our`, so `poured`/`toured`/`scoured` can never match. A first draft listed them in `NOT_EN_GB`. The mutation that removed `poured` stayed green, which showed the entries were dead, so they were dropped. An exemption whose removal changes nothing is not an exemption.

## (2026-09-24) — Strict interactive contrast covers destructive; `isPending` kept everywhere

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** ENGINE 0.148.0 (MINOR: emission changes when the lever is on, plus one description line); CONTRACT stands at 12.0.0 (no token name moves; the baseline's `engineVersion` stamp only). Files: `packages/engine/modes.ts` (the lever condition + the inverse fill `labelNote`), `theme.ts` / `levers.ts` (lever prose names destructive), `version.ts`, `test.ts` (new GATE B arm), regenerated `out/**` + `modes-report.md`.

**Owner decision (2026-09-24): "Setting should cover destructive."** On an inverse surface the #1456 stepped hover/pressed (and focused/selected) fills drop the `on-fill` label to about 2.5:1, exempt by default as transient. With `strictInteractiveContrast` ON, primary's brand ink was swapped to the neutral extreme so it held ≥4.5:1; destructive's danger ink (#1384) was not, so the setting silently did not protect destructive. The fix is one condition: `useBrandInk = inkPalette !== null && !strict` instead of `… && !(name === 'primary' && strict)`.

**Why it generalizes with no design choice.** The rule is by category, "a brand-ink label gives way to the neutral extreme under the lever". Only primary and destructive carry a brand ink on the inverse fill (`inkPalette !== null`); neutral and every declared interactive palette already carry `onColor`, the neutral extreme, so the uniform rule moves nothing else. Measured with the lever ON across nb / aurora / harbor / wendys and an nb variant declaring an `accent` palette: every inverse state fill, every family, all four modes (hc included), label ≥4.5:1.

**Description.** #1645 worded destructive's inverse hover/pressed fills "(exempt by default; the strict interactive contrast setting does not change the destructive label)". Now that the setting does change it, the wording reverts to the owner-approved primary sentence: "(exempt by default; the strict interactive contrast setting keeps it at 4.5:1 or more)". `labelNote` keys the claim on `inkPalette !== null` (the families the lever actually swaps), not on the name, so the claim and the mechanism share one condition. `lint-description-claims` checks the "keeps it at N:1 or more" claim.

**The trap: the PAGE column in `dark` is not covered, and the lever cannot cover it.** The task asked for page and inverse columns. On the page ground in the `dark` mode, the fill steps LIGHTER on hover/pressed under a near-white label that is *already* the neutral extreme, so primary and destructive drop to about 2.4–3.7:1 with the lever ON or OFF (nb, harbor, wendys). The lever's mechanism, swapping a brand ink for the neutral extreme, has nothing to swap there. Fixing it means re-picking the ink per state or re-stepping the page fill, a visual change the owner has not approved. It was already filed as **#1626**, so it is held there and not built here. The new test measures the page ground in base / hc-light / hc-dark and names `dark` as the one excluded mode, pointing at #1626. It does not silently skip.

**Gate.** `test.ts` GATE B (lever, every category): with the lever ON, every family's `on-fill` against every state fill, recomputed from emitted hexes, inverse in 4 modes and page in 3, plus a representation assertion over inverse/page × primary/destructive/neutral/accent. **By-name mutation:** reverting the `modes.ts` condition to primary-only fails exactly that assertion (`strict lever (every category) … fails HERE — DIPS: nb/base/inverse.destructive/hover: 3.33:1 …`, 104691 passed / 1 failed), then restored.

**Also decided (owner, 2026-09-24): KEEP `isPending` everywhere** (button, icon-button, text-field, switch-row), per the #1326 canon. Audit item C2/K-30 is withdrawn. No code change.

## (2026-09-24) — Figma gets its own short description; DTCG prose per the #1623 sign-off

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** ENGINE 0.147.0 (MINOR, emitted prose moves); CONTRACT stands at 11.3.0 (the baseline's `engineVersion` stamp only). Files: `packages/engine/figma-description.ts` (**NEW**, the Figma register), `emit-figma-{color,dims,font,styles}.ts` (every description now comes from it; the `desc` passthrough is deleted), `modes.ts` / `tree.ts` / `theme.ts` (DTCG prose), `lint-description-claims.ts` (grammar follows), `lint-figma-descriptions.ts` (**NEW** gate, wired in `verify.ts`, `ci.yml`, CONTRIBUTING §3, the PR template, CLAUDE.md), `apps/plugin/src/prune-figma.ts` + `test-prune.ts`, `test.ts`.

**The split.** The owner chose about 90 characters for Figma and the full detail in the DTCG description and `.ai.json`. So Figma is not a cut-down DTCG sentence. Each builder takes values (px, each mode's `min`, alpha, the ground role, the face) and composes its own line. Nothing in the Figma emitters reads a `$description` any more, so a DTCG wording change can't move a designer's panel.

**Decisions that were mine (technical), stated so they can be reversed:**
- A Figma contrast claim states the LOWEST `min` across modes. A floor is a floor, so it holds in every mode. The high-contrast floors live in DTCG and `.ai.json`. This drops batch A's `(7:1 in high-contrast modes)` parentheticals from Figma, which the owner's "full detail stays in DTCG" covers.
- A ground named by a palette step (`against: "neutral.050"`) is resolved to the page ground ROLE that aliases it in light. The line then names `background/secondary`, which a designer can find. The resolution throws if the match is ambiguous.
- 3:1 TEXT roles in Figma carry the large-text limit instead of their ground. The approved sentence plus a slash ground ran 107–120 characters. The ground stays in DTCG.
- The ceiling is target + 10 (100), parsed from `docs/voice-standard.md`. It is never imported from the builder, which composes and never measures.

**Traps.** (1) `modes.ts` now resolves the inverse ink BEFORE the fill-state loop, so each state can state its measured drop. It still `put`s the ink after the loop, so emission order is unchanged. Don't "tidy" the put upward: Figma creation order follows it. (2) The prune recognizer matches the current AND legacy style words. A client file applied before this still holds the old words, and a stranded one is exactly what prune exists for. The legacy regexes are frozen literals, and `test-prune.ts` holds them against frozen strings, not generated ones. (3) The claims gate's new shapes key on their own words ("The label on it drops to about", "below the … body floor"). Rewording those sentences silently turns them back into ordinary floor claims against `against`. Most would still pass, for the wrong reason.

**Open for the owner (in the PR body):** the destructive inverse label (the strict setting doesn't cover it) and focused/selected (not transient, so no exemption is claimed; this is #1626's gap). Also: two small deviations from the approved wording, `on an inverse surface` and resolving role names instead of "the page".

The transform won because `codeOnly` is load-bearing at runtime in a small way: the projector copies it onto every plan, and `figmaPropertyErrors` reads an entry's LEADING term as the admission for a dropped axis or state. So `codeOnly` entries are cut to their subject, not removed, and `notes` is removed. A second finding: esbuild keeps comments that sit inside an expression, and every def is one expression, so every def-file comment (135 "Prism 2" mentions among them) was shipping. The transform re-prints with `removeComments`, which closed that too. The bundle's one remaining "Prism2" is an engine comment in `figma-names.ts`, outside component text and outside this lane.

**Renames (display names only; ids, Figma set names and props are unchanged):** `Destructive Button` → `Button.Destructive`, `Neutral Button` → `Button.Neutral`, `Destructive IconButton` → `IconButton.Destructive`, `Neutral IconButton` → `IconButton.Neutral`, `Image placeholder` → `ImagePlaceholder`, `CheckboxGroup` → `Checkbox.Group`, `RadioGroup` → `Radio.Group`. The rule the gate holds: a name reads as its id with the separators removed, and once a family is dotted, every id under its prefix is dotted.

**Traps for whoever re-verifies.** (1) esbuild `onLoad` filters are Go regular expressions, with no lookahead, so the registry file is excluded in the callback. (2) Bundle strings are JS-escaped (`\u2014`), so the gate decodes before comparing. (3) A note can repeat a sentence a shipped prop also carries (switch-row's read-only rationale does), so arm A probes the last 40-character window no shipped field contains, and reports any string with no such window as `shared`. (4) The existing-set rule: the plugin writes the description on a set it creates, and on a set the file already had only while that set's description is empty, so a designer's own text survives a rebuild. (5) `composition.planned` holds the relocated names as they were (`form`, `card`, `emoji` among them). Whether each is real roadmap is a later call; the gate only makes sure none of them resolves.

## (2026-09-24) — the footprint check compares runtime axes and holds authoring ones (#1611)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** Files: `packages/engine/component-schema.ts` (new `ComponentDef.axisKinds`, `AXIS_KINDS`, `axisKindOf`, validator arm), `packages/engine/anatomy-figma.ts` (`AnatomyPlan.axisKinds`; `heldAxes` feeds both cohort derivations), `axisKinds` added to all 19 def files (classification only, no other def edit), `apps/plugin/component-shim.ts` (opt-in `textAdvance`), `apps/plugin/test-write-components.ts` + `packages/engine/test.ts` (#1611 arms), `version.ts` (ENGINE 0.144.0), `schema/component-surface.json` (`--accept`).

**The report.** Building NB, field-label reported four footprint misses at `size=small`: bold 46px wide against regular 45px, because NB's emphasis weight (Medium) sets wider. The owner answered the open question ("is any weight axis ever toggled live?") with *"Yes there are going to be instances where something goes bold when selected. That's fairly common."* So weight is not exempt as a kind of axis. The footprint has to hold across what a live instance switches between, and need not hold across what a designer picks once.

**The rule.** Each `variants` axis is `runtime` or `authoring`. Absent means runtime, so an unclassified axis stays compared, and the state axis is always runtime. The cohort key holds `size`, slot fill, `footprintVaries` and every authoring axis, and compares the rest. `heldAxes(plan)` is the one list both the engine's `group` and the chunked payload's `FOOTPRINT_VARIES` read, in one order, so the two keys stay byte-identical. The classification is on every plan, so an agent reading a plan knows which props change at runtime.

**Classification calls worth knowing.** `appearance` (button, icon-button) stays RUNTIME. A toggle button that fills when selected is the same shape as the owner's bold-when-selected label, so the stroke-drift guarantee (outline vs filled) is kept, along with its two mutation tests. The orchestrator's brief listed appearance as authoring; this is flagged at the top of the PR. `icon.name` and `icon.tone` are runtime (a host swaps eye/eye-off live). `field-message`, `select` and `text-field` `status` is runtime (validation arrives live); field-message stays exempt through `footprintVaries`. Everything else is authoring: size, emphasis, weight, surface, shape, width, style, offset, ratio, value, intensity. Cohort movement: field-label goes from 6 cohorts to 12, icon-button from 3 to 12 (`shape` × `surface`), and button and focus-ring now hold `surface`.

**The bold-when-selected pattern.** No shipped def has it, so the plugin test builds a fixture: field-label with `weight` classified runtime. The shim's `textAdvance` makes `body/sm/strong` 1px wider (NB's case). (a) Shipped field-label reports 0 footprint misses, and a guard confirms bold and regular really measure differently. (b) The fixture reports exactly the four small bold misses, matched by full message. (c) The fixture with the member's width reserved (a bound fixed width) reports 0 misses.

**Mutations (committed first).** Field-label `weight` set to `runtime`: plugin `✗ #1611 field-label's authoring weight is held fixed…` quotes `footprint -> emphasis=primary, weight=bold, size=small, state=rest measures 38x0 but …weight=regular… measures 36x0`, and four engine #1611 arms fail. `heldAxes` holding every axis: plugin (b) fails with `NOTHING — the runtime axis was not compared`, and the stroke-drift, chunked-drift and cohort-count arms fail.

**Traps.** `footprintVaries` on an authoring axis is now redundant (image-placeholder's `ratio`). It was left in place so the aspect-lock reason stays with the def. The engine test requires every shipped def to classify every axis, so a parallel lane that adds an axis must also classify it. `size`'s kind does not move the cohort: `size` is always held.


**Net fix (orchestrator).** The component-API alignment landed first and gave textarea a `status` axis, which this PR's every-axis-classified arm then caught as unclassified. Classified `runtime`, the same as text-field's `status`: validation changes while an instance is live. Textarea projects no Figma set, so the component surface doesn't move.

## (2026-09-24) — component API alignment: field validation, textarea model, group gap (#1623 sign-off)

**STATUS: in review (DO NOT MERGE — orchestrator nets and merges).** Four owner decisions from the #1623 sign-off, under the standing direction that APIs must be machine-readable: one name per concept across siblings.

- **C1/TF-5 — text-field validation.** The `error` message prop is gone; text-field carries select's exact `validation` (`default | error | warning | success`) + `validationMessage`. The Figma `status` axis keeps its name, so the nested field-message still follows it by name, and maps to `validation` value-for-value. Props don't project, so text-field's projected surface did not move.
- **C1/TA-4 — textarea on text-field's model.** `error` left `states` for a `status` axis with text-field's values. The paint grammar is now text-field's 3-segment one (`{status}.{slot}.{state}` first), the retired state-led `border.error` became `{error,warning,success}.border.{rest,hover,focus-visible,read-only,empty}` with text-field's roles, and the placeholder binds `color.text.secondary`. Textarea also gets `validation` + `validationMessage`. Binding warning/success borders (not only error) is part of "text-field's model": text-field binds all three since #1517, and leaving two statuses unbound would be a *different* model. Registered in `lint-paint`'s provenance exceptions (the `error → danger` cross-vocabulary keys, 5) and in `lint-axis-values`' `status` entry. Textarea has no anatomy, so nothing projects.
- **C2/K-11 + K-23 — group gap.** checkbox-group and radio-group bind a single `gap: space.0` in place of the provisional `size.{size}.gap` rung. The rows now carry 12px of block padding and self-space. The `unverified` entries are marked resolved. The group's `size` axis still reaches its label and rows through `follow`; it just no longer has a gap binding of its own. Both groups' plans moved (same member count) → surface re-accepted.
- **C2/K-30 — HELD, not implemented.** The audit's premise was "switch's `isPending` is unlike every other boolean". That's false: `button`, `icon-button` and `text-field` all carry `isPending`, per the settled #1326 decision 2 canon (`skills/prism3-build-component/SKILL.md` §6: synthetic-state booleans are `is`-prefixed, and `pending` "no longer exist[s] — do not reintroduce"). Renaming switch-row alone would split one concept across two names, which is the thing the owner's direction forbids. The choice is the owner's: (a) reverse the #1326 canon family-wide (`pending` on button, icon-button, text-field and switch-row, plus the skill), or (b) keep `isPending` everywhere and withdraw K-30.

**Gate.** `test.ts` pins the field family's validation contract with a LITERAL expected value (never read off select, per docs/34). Each of select, text-field and textarea must carry `validation` over exactly the four values with default `default`, carry `validationMessage`, carry no `error` prop and no `error` state, and have a `status` axis equal to those values. Each def is its own assertion. The groups' `space.0` gap is pinned the same way. Mutation-proven by name: renaming text-field's `validation` → `validationState`, changing textarea's values to `…danger`, and rebinding radio-group's gap to `space.100` each failed exactly one named assertion.

**Trap met: `lint-rung-names` refused the 0px group gap.** Once the groups dropped `size.{size}.gap`, their `size` axis bound no `size.*` key of their own, and arm 2 read that as "a size that resolves to nothing". Two tempting fixes are both wrong. Size-keying `space.0` per rung fails the rungless arm. Binding some other size-varying key just to satisfy the gate would be gaming it. The fix is a new admission list, `SIZE_BY_FOLLOW_ONLY` (the two groups), and it is re-checked structurally rather than trusted. An admitted def must bind no `size.*` key (else STALE). It must have at least one `nest` part that `follow`s `size`. Every followed def must admit every value of the group's enum. Mutation-proven by name: dropping radio-group from the list brings back arm 2's failures, adding a `size.small.gap` to checkbox-group fires STALE, and emptying radio-group's `follow` fires "no nest part follows 'size'".

**ENGINE 0.142.0 → 0.143.0** (component members moved). CONTRACT stands, because every bound role already ships.
