## (2026-09-24) — an outline/text hover fill binds the family the brand's `outlineInteraction` emits (#1608)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** Files: `packages/engine/anatomy-figma.ts` (**NEW** `applyOutlineInteraction`), `apps/plugin/src/brand-def.ts` (`materializeForBrand` gains the third lever), `packages/engine/lint-component-surface.ts` + `schema/component-surface.json` (16 new `<id>@outline-{solid-tint,none}` rows; **no plain row moved**), `packages/engine/test.ts` + `apps/plugin/test-write-components.ts` (the #1608 blocks), `packages/engine/components/button.ts` (the known-limitation note named the wrong role), a comment in `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts`, `version.ts` (ENGINE **0.133.0 → 0.134.0**), `schema/token-contract.json` (`engineVersion` only, informational `--accept`), the stamp-only `out/**` restamp, and this entry. **CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0.** Closes #1608. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`.

── THE DIAGNOSIS (the issue's first hypothesis was wrong) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

#1608 opened as "stale file" because the check read the committed corpus NB, which sits at the `overlay-neutral` default. The owner's configured NB carries `solid-tint` or `none`, and at those methods the engine does not EMIT `interactive.*.overlay.*` (`modes.ts`). Meanwhile `button.ts` bound that wash unconditionally, and so do `icon-button` (×3), `select` and `text-field` (neutral hover): **eight defs, not one**. Measured on NB at `solid-tint`: raw `button` misses exactly **96** paint refs (48 hover/pressed outline+text members × wash on both grounds), the owner's count. The #1387 transparent-fill neutralize in the executor was masking the symptom. At `none` that happens to look right; at `solid-tint` it silently dropped the tint.

── THE FIX ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`applyOutlineInteraction(def, method)` is the third materialize-before-projection sibling of `applyControlShape`/`applyWeightIntent`, so `figmaAnatomyPlan/Set` stay brand-agnostic. It is keyed on the REF (`color.interactive.<c>.overlay.<state>`), not the key, and routes through `modes.ts`'s existing `outlineFillRole` (not a third copy of the mapping). `overlay-neutral` returns the SAME object (identity). `solid-tint` repoints to `interactive.<c>.subtle-fill.<state>`. `none` DROPS the entry: `paintOf('overlay')` then resolves nothing, outline/text fall through to no fill, and a field falls to its rest fill. No variable is requested, so there is nothing to miss. The plugin reads the lever off the resolved theme (`brandTheme(input).outlineInteraction`, which owns the default). That is the same one `brandTheme` call the weight availability now shares (`brandLevers`), and null/throwing input falls back to the identity.

── HELD — A DESIGN QUESTION, NOT INVENTED ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The engine emits **no inverse twin of `subtle-fill`** (the `solid-tint` branch in `modes.ts` writes page-ground roles only). So a `surface=inverse` button/icon-button member at `solid-tint` still binds `color.inverse.interactive.<c>.subtle-fill.<state>` through the projector's surface rewrite, and still misses. Button drops from 96 misses to 48, all of them inverse. What an opaque tint should be on an inverse band is the owner's call. No role or fallback color was invented. Both gates carry this as ONE hand-named held pattern: any other miss, or this miss on a default-ground member, fails.

── THE GATES (docs/34) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**Engine (`test.ts`).** For each method × {nb-measured, harbor} (SYNTHETIC at `solid-tint`/`none`, since no corpus brand sets them, #1112), every def's materialized paint refs must be in the brand's Figma COLOR EMISSION (`buildFigmaColor`, namespace stripped). That is the file Apply writes, so it is an independent oracle, as #1601 did for type. Plus: hand-named bindings on the owner's member (outline/hover/default → wash / `subtle-fill/hover` / none); identity at the default for every def; the binder list named (8 defs); and an in-suite mutation (the raw def at solid-tint misses 96, by name). **Plugin (`test-write-components.ts`).** `button` is built through `materializeForBrand` against NB-redesign at `solid-tint` and at `none`, with a host holding ONLY that brand's emitted color variables. At solid-tint, the 48 default-ground members bind exactly `subtle-fill/{hover,pressed}` and no overlay miss remains. At none there are 0 `fills` misses and all 96 hover/pressed members carry no fill. An explicit `overlay-neutral` is byte-identical to the lever left unset. **Mutation-verified by name** (from a `wip:` HEAD): (M1) drop the wrap in `brand-def.ts` → three plugin #1608 lines fail showing the 96-miss shape (the "no fill" line stays green because the executor's #1387 floor clears it, so that line pins the result, not the cause). (M2) make `applyOutlineInteraction` the identity → 7 engine #1608 lines fail, and `lint-component-surface` fails on the 16 vanished rows.

## (2026-09-24) — the plugin's component build resolves weight intent per brand (#1605)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator nets + merges).** Plugin-only — the runtime half of #1602. Files: `apps/plugin/src/brand-def.ts` (**NEW** — `materializeForBrand(def, input)` + `brandWeightAvailability(input)`), `apps/plugin/src/main.ts` (`build-components` projects `materializeForBrand(def, brandInput)`), `apps/plugin/test-write-components.ts` (the #1605 block), and this entry. **No engine change, no ENGINE_VERSION bump, no `out/**` move; gate count STANDS** (the new arm lives inside the existing plugin `test`). Closes #1605. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`, `packages/engine/`.

── THE GAP, AND THE FIX ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#1602 taught the engine to resolve `field-label`'s weight axis against the brand's shipped body roles (`applyWeightIntent`), proven at the projection tier in `test.ts`. The plugin never called it: `build-components` materialized `controlShape` only, so an NB file (`body: [default, emphasis]`) still projected `body/<size>/strong` — a style NB never emits, so every bold member missed its style (the #1599 shape). The fix threads the brand's availability into the same pre-projection step, in the order the issue locked: `applyWeightIntent(applyControlShape(def, shape), weightAvailability(brandTheme(input).typography))`. The `restoreInput(figma.root)` read `controlShape` already used is now read ONCE into `brandInput` and both levers come off it. `null` (no persisted brand, or a read that throws) — and a persisted brand whose `brandTheme` throws — fall back to `rounded` + `DEFAULT_WEIGHT_AVAILABILITY`, the identity, so a themeless file builds byte-identically (asserted).

── WHY A MODULE, NOT TWO LINES IN `main.ts` ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`main.ts` calls `figma.showUI` at module scope, so no test can import it; a source-text gate on it sees that a call EXISTS, never what it DOES. Moving the materialization into `src/brand-def.ts` makes the behavior importable, so the gate runs the exact function `main.ts` calls through the real executor. The `main.ts` wiring keeps a source-text assertion (the file's existing `(5)` precedent) — the two together cover "the call is there" and "the call is right".

── THE GATE (docs/34) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

In `test-write-components.ts`, field-label is built through `materializeForBrand` against (a) NB's real input (`examples/nb-redesign.design.md`) with a host holding ONLY NB's EMITTED text styles (named by `buildFigmaTextStyles` — the emitter's side, not the projection's), and (b) aurora with `typography.weights.body = ['default']`. The styles read back off the built text nodes are compared to HAND-NAMED expectations: NB applies exactly `body/{sm,md,lg}/{default,emphasis}`, never `body/*/strong`, every text node styled, 24 members; the single-weight brand builds **12** members with no `weight` axis and only `body/*/default`. **Mutation-verified by name** (from a `wip:` HEAD): (M1) drop the `applyWeightIntent` wrap in `brand-def.ts` → five #1605 lines fail (24 unstyled nodes, `text.textStyle -> body/sm/strong` misses, 24 members instead of 12); (M2) revert `main.ts` to the bare `applyControlShape` projection → the #1605 wiring line fails. The issue suggested `test:roundtrip`/`test:verdict`; the write-adapter test is the host-truth arm that can hold a brand-specific style catalogue, so the arm lives there.

## (2026-09-23) — opt-in per-rung Desktop/Mobile type-size override (#1587)

**STATUS: PR open, labeled DO NOT MERGE (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** One arc lane — engine model + fluid emit + a new coherence gate + studio UI + docs. Files: `packages/engine/theme.ts` (`TypographyInput.sizeOverrides`; the resolution hook in `buildComposites`; the coherence throws; `mobileEndpoint` exported), `packages/engine/schema/theme-schema.json` (the `sizeOverrides` field + a `viewportSizeOverride` `$def` + sibling-prose compression for the MCP ceiling), `packages/engine/version.ts` (ENGINE **0.130.0 → 0.133.0**, changelog newest-first — the orchestrator reconciles the exact number at net time), `packages/engine/lint-size-override-coherence.ts` (**NEW gate**, #62), `verify.ts` · `.github/workflows/ci.yml` · `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 · `.github/pull_request_template.md` · `CLAUDE.md` §4 (the four-place registration `lint-doc-gates` enforces + the runner), `packages/engine/test.ts` (the by-name #1587 block + the emit↔paste-over-an-overridden-rung extension), `apps/studio/src/main.ts` + `apps/studio/src/styles.css` (the inline Desktop/Mobile control), and this entry. **`out/**` moves ONLY its `$extensions.generator.version` stamp** — no corpus brand sets an override, so every emitted value is byte-identical; `regen --check`/drift clean, `lint-emission-version` sees the stamp move under a raised ENGINE. **ENGINE bumps (behavior + public-input surface); CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0.** Closes #1587. **NOT TOUCHED:** `apps/plugin/`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`, the derive itself (`mobileEndpoint`'s numbers), `typography.sizes` (the desktop channel it already was).

── THE MODEL (write the field the pipeline already reads) ───────────────────────────────────────────────

The four owner decisions were locked on the issue before code: **override-derived storage** (store only per-rung deltas, never a second full size table), **brand-axis only** (the Desktop/Mobile axis surfaces only when a brand overrides ≥1 rung), **inline in the size table** (derived shown alongside the override, the #423 read-only-derived pattern), **Desktop / Mobile naming**. The headline the code confirmed: a composite ALREADY carries both endpoints — `sizePx` (desktop/max) and `sizeMinPx` (mobile/min) — and the whole fluid pipeline already reads them: `tree.ts` reshapes them into `$extensions.prism3.responsive.figma.modes.{mobile,desktop}` and the web `clamp()`, `emit-figma-font.ts` reads those into `type-sets.{desktop,mobile}.json`, and `materialise-to-figma.ts` reads the SAME emitted files. So the override just **AUTHORS the endpoint the derive used to own**: `TypographyInput.sizeOverrides` (keyed group → rung → `{ desktop?, mobile? }`, heading groups only) resolves in `buildComposites` — `desktop` wins over `typography.sizes` for `sizePx`; `mobile` overrides the `mobileEndpoint(...)` derive for `sizeMinPx`. Nothing downstream changed. A rung with no entry is fully clamp-derived (today's behavior). The studio writes `mobile` through `sizeOverrides` and keeps authoring `desktop` through the existing base-column `typography.sizes` (so the two viewport channels never collide from the UI); the engine accepts a `desktop` pin in `sizeOverrides` too, for the API/corpus, with a documented precedence.

── THE COHERENCE GUARD, AND WHY IT'S INDEPENDENT (docs/34) ──────────────────────────────────────────────

The DERIVED path is coherent for free — `mobileEndpoint` is `Math.min(desktop, …)` by construction, which is precisely why the only prior assertion (`sizeMinPx ≤ sizePx`, `test.ts`) held without a real guard. An AUTHORED pin escapes that clamp, so it can write `mobile > desktop` (an inverted rung — a ramp growing on the smaller viewport) or a pin that makes a smaller rung's mobile exceed a larger rung's (a backwards mobile ramp). Both are the incoherent hand-authored shapes the engine exists to replace, so both are a **build-time throw** in `buildComposites` (mirroring the #328/#1368 by-name refusals), reading the composites' OWN resolved `sizePx`/`sizeMinPx` after the loop — never re-run through `mobileEndpoint` (docs/34 shape 1: deriving the expectation from the derivation). Empirically confirmed the derived mobile ramp is non-decreasing across every corpus brand first, so the monotonicity throw cannot false-fire on the derive (display legitimately plateaus — 96/112/128px all floor to 48px mobile — so the rule is **non-decreasing, not strictly increasing**).

`lint-size-override-coherence.ts` (gate #62) is the independent record, two arms: **ARM A** reads the committed `out/figma/<brand>/type-sets.{desktop,mobile}.json` and asserts the invariant on the committed bytes (EXPECTED = the invariant transcribed as a rule, never re-derived); **ARM B/C/D** drive `brandTheme` over inputs authored IN the gate — an inverting override and a backwards-ramp override are REJECTED, a valid pin TAKES EFFECT (a `display.xl` mobile pin of 40 lands on the composite, not the derived 48), and a legal multi-rung override is not over-refused. The self-check drives the oracle both directions. **Mutation-verified by name** (from a `wip:` HEAD, restored each time): delete the invert throw → ARM B; delete the monotonicity throw → ARM B (the two ARM-B fixtures are chosen to ISOLATE each throw — the invert fixture pins the LARGEST title rung so it fails for inversion alone, the backwards fixture pins `display.sm` mobile == its own desktop so it is not inverted, only backwards); drop the `mobilePin ??` resolution hook → ARM C; corrupt a committed mobile value above its desktop → ARM A. The **emit↔paste agreement** extends to an overridden rung in `test.ts` (#1587): the theme-built and file-read font var plans stay identical when a mobile endpoint is authored, and the emitted `type-sets` mobile mode carries the pinned 40 — proving the pin flows through both write paths in lockstep, not a rung that happened to derive 40.

── VERSIONING (principle 5): ENGINE bumps, CONTRACT STANDS ───────────────────────────────────────────────

Behavior + public-input surface both move → **ENGINE 0.130.0 → 0.133.0** (restamps `out/**`'s generator version; no emitted VALUE moves since no corpus brand overrides). **CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0** — per-viewport values land in the EXISTING `type-sets`/`font-fluid` mode variables (mobile and desktop are two MODES of one variable, not two names), so no guaranteed token NAME appears; `token-contract --check` confirmed green with no CONTRACT bump, no `--accept` beyond the informational engine-stamp line. The gate count moves **61 → 62** (the new coherence gate; every other engine assertion is an arm of the existing `test`).

── THE MCP CEILING (#1368, same claw-back as #1593/#1510) ────────────────────────────────────────────────

Main's `tools/list` sits at 59,927 chars against a 60,000 ceiling (the #1593 compression left ~73 chars of headroom). The `sizeOverrides` schema had to fit by COMPRESSION, not by raising the limit: the field uses **open keys** (the `faces` #1368 pattern — `additionalProperties`, heading-only enforced by `brandTheme`'s by-name throw, not by enumerated schema properties) + a terse `viewportSizeOverride` leaf, and sibling typography/per-mode prose was trimmed (`typography.sizes`/`modeLevers.typeSizes` — the size-override family; `typefaceLibrary`; the near-duplicate per-mode `families`/`letterSpacings`/`easings` re-point descriptions, every load-bearing fact kept, the full rationale still in the `theme.ts` types). Landed at **59,757** — ~243 chars of headroom, HEALTHIER than the baseline it started from. `lint-us-english`/`lint-voice` run after the web build and cover the schema + built bundle, so the new UI labels and schema prose are in scope.

## (2026-09-23) — components resolve weight by INTENT against a brand's roles; the surface-ref gate (#1602 + #1601)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** Engine projection — `packages/engine/theme.ts` (`TYPE_WEIGHTS_DEFAULT` exported; new `weightAvailability(typography)` reads per-category roles off the emitted composites), `packages/engine/anatomy-figma.ts` (`WeightAvailability`, `DEFAULT_WEIGHT_AVAILABILITY`, `resolveWeightIntent`, `applyWeightIntent` — the sibling of `applyControlShape`), `packages/engine/component-schema.ts` (`weightIntent?: {axis, group}` field + `WEIGHT_INTENTS` vocabulary + relational validation), `packages/engine/components/field-label.ts` (`weightIntent: {axis:'weight', group:'body'}` + prose), `packages/engine/test.ts` (the #1602/#1601 net), `packages/engine/lint-component-surface.ts` (per-brand `<id>@<scenario>` rows), `packages/engine/version.ts` (ENGINE 0.130.0 → **0.132.0**, changelog), `packages/engine/schema/component-surface.json` (`--accept`: two new field-label rows), `packages/engine/schema/token-contract.json` (stamp-only re-accept), `out/**` (generator-stamp only), and this entry. Gate count **STANDS at 61** — #1601 is arms of the existing engine `test`, not a new gate (so no `ci.yml`/CONTRIBUTING/PR-template/doc-gates churn). **ENGINE bumps (behavior); CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0** — no token NAME moves (field-label binds the same `type.body.*` names; the brand resolves which role). Closes #1602 and #1601. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `apps/plugin/`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`.

── THE PROBLEM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`field-label`'s `bold` weight hard-bound `type.body.*.strong` (700). NB ships `body: [default, emphasis]` (heaviest body cut Medium/500, a deliberate brand choice — `examples/nb-redesign.design.md:73`), so `body/*/strong` is **never emitted** for NB and the projected text-style name resolved to nothing at paste time — the 252 silent discards a designer saw (#1599). And **no gate cross-checked a component's `type.*` refs against the brand's emitted composites** (#1601), so it was invisible until someone built it on that brand.

── THE DECISION (owner-locked 2026-09-23) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A weight axis carries **intents**, not role names. `regular` → the brand's `default` body role; `bold` → the brand's **heaviest** available role at/above `default` (off `WEIGHT_ROLE_ORDER`). NB → `emphasis`; a default brand → `strong`. When both intents coincide (a single-body-weight brand) the axis **collapses** — a variant axis with one value is not an axis, so field-label projects 12 members, not 24, on such a brand. Rejected: forcing `strong` as a guaranteed body role, which would fabricate a weight a brand does not want.

── THE MECHANISM (mirrors `applyControlShape`, deliberately) ─────────────────────────────────────────────

`applyWeightIntent(def, avail)` materializes the brand choice INTO the def **before** projection, exactly as `controlShape` does for a corner — so `figmaAnatomyPlan`/`figmaAnatomySet` stay pure functions of a def and their signatures do NOT change (no ripple to the seven gates + studio + plugin that call them with a def and no theme). field-label still AUTHORS concrete `type.body.*.strong`/`.default` — those are the **default-brand resolution**, which is what keeps a themeless `figmaAnatomySet(fieldLabel)` byte-identical to before (the same trick `rounded` plays). For a non-default brand `applyWeightIntent` repoints the role tail (`strong`→`emphasis` on NB) reading the intent off the token KEY's weight segment; on collapse it drops the axis from `variants`/`variantAxes` and strips `{weight}` from the type binding keys and parts. `weightAvailability` reads the roles off `typography.composites` (the emitted tree), so resolution and the gate share the independent "what does the brand ship" source, not a hard-coded role name.

── #1601, THE SAFETY NET (arms of engine `test`, docs/34) ────────────────────────────────────────────────

For each corpus brand (nb-measured, **nb-redesign**, aurora, wendys, harbor): SUBJECT = every def's projected `type.*` text-style refs (`figmaAnatomySet(applyWeightIntent(def, avail))` → `planTextStyles`); ORACLE = the brand's emitted composite set (`typography.composites` → `figmaTextStyleName`) — independent sides. All green with resolution; a `checked > 0` floor guards the vacuous pass. **Self-check:** a plan carrying a composite no brand emits (`body/md/fictional`) is flagged by the same membership test — the detector can fail. **By-name mutations, each isolated:** (a) an unknown intent → `resolveWeightIntent` THROWS by name; (b) reverting field-label to the hard `strong` binding (drop `weightIntent`) → NB dangles `body/*/strong` by name (the #1601 miss, proving resolution is what makes the gate green — they land together).

── THE SURFACE GATE (#1602 §4) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A brand-conditional projection can't be pinned by a brand-independent baseline. `lint-component-surface` now records, for each `weightIntent` def, extra `<id>@<scenario>` rows under **engine-defined** availability scenarios (`body-emphasis` = NB's bold→emphasis; `body-single` = the collapse), so a change to the resolution or collapse rule moves a row and **forces the ENGINE bump** (arm B) the default-only baseline could not. The plain `field-label` row is byte-identical (default projection unchanged), so the drift is EXACTLY the two new rows — nothing spurious. `--accept` at 0.130.0 → 0.131.0.

── A TRAP FOR WHOEVER RE-VERIFIES THIS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**`nbTheme()` (nb-fixture, from `nb-measured.json`) is NOT the [default, emphasis] NB.** It builds typography with `buildTypography()` = the vanilla defaults (`body: [default, strong]`), so `weightAvailability(nbTheme().typography).body` is `[default, strong]` and field-label resolves `bold`→`strong` there — no miss. The `body: [default, emphasis]` NB the issue names is **`examples/nb-redesign.design.md`**, compiled via `brandTheme(parseDesignMd(...).input)`. Test/gate against nb-redesign, not `nbTheme()`, or the #1601 case never fires. (Measured while wiring the test: the first cut used `nbTheme()` and reported clean under BOTH the raw and resolved defs, because there was nothing to miss.)

── DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE (guardrail: `apps/plugin/` untouched) — FILED ────────────────────────────────

The plugin's `build-components` calls `figmaAnatomySet(applyControlShape(def, controlShape), …)` but does **not** yet call `applyWeightIntent`, so at plugin RUNTIME field-label still projects the default-brand role for NB. Wiring the plugin to pass `weightAvailability(brandTheme(restoreInput(…)).typography)` into an `applyWeightIntent` at that call site is the runtime half of the fix; it is out of this lane's scope (the guardrail forbids touching `apps/plugin/`), so the engine mechanism + gates land here and the plugin wiring is **filed as a follow-up (#1605)**. Until then the fix is proven at the engine tier (test.ts across the corpus), not at paste time.

## (2026-09-23) — file-component scaffold stacks its variants instead of overlapping them (#1600)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** PLUGIN-ONLY — `apps/plugin/src/file-components.ts` (the `FNode` port gains `layoutPositioning`; a new `stackVariants` helper; called after both `combineAsVariants` sites), `apps/plugin/test-file-components.ts` (the #1600 stacking arm extends the #1563 structural gate), and this entry. **NO engine version bump, NO token-contract change, NO `out/**`** — this touches no engine surface. Gate count **STANDS at 61** — the new assertions are arms of the existing plugin `test` (`test-file-components.ts`), not a new gate. Closes #1600. **NOT TOUCHED:** `packages/engine/**`, `write-components.ts` (its `layoutPositioning='ABSOLUTE'` at :1651/:1687 is the intentional overlay-child positioning of #1503 — left alone), `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`.

── THE PROBLEM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Owner-found building NB (screenshot): in `_Section-header`, three of the four size variants (XL/Medium/Small) carried the absolute-position marker while Large was in-flow, so they piled on top of each other instead of laying out down the set; `_Headings` (`:317`) had the same shape. Root cause: after `api.combineAsVariants(...)` the scaffold **never gave the resulting set a stacking layout and never set `layoutPositioning` on the variant children**. `combineAsVariants` leaves some members at `layoutPositioning='ABSOLUTE'` (a host side-effect, the positioning half of the same #1563 class of surprise — #1563 fought the sizing half), and with no set layout to arrange them the absolute ones overlap.

── THE FIX (both-ways — no host probe needed) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`stackVariants(set, members)` does BOTH halves, so the result is correct whichever state the combine produced: (1) give the SET a VERTICAL stacking auto-layout (`itemSpacing`/`padding` for visible separation), and (2) set every variant child's `layoutPositioning='AUTO'` (in-flow), clearing any ABSOLUTE the combine left. Neither half alone suffices — (1) without (2) still overlaps the children the combine left absolute; (2) without (1) leaves the set with no layout to arrange the now-in-flow children. Applied verbatim to both `_Section-header` (`:243`) and `_Headings` (`:317`). The port extension is minimal: `FNode` gains `layoutPositioning?: unknown` (the set's `layoutMode` was already in the port). The real `figma` object still structurally satisfies the port (every `FNode` field is optional `unknown`), and the in-memory recorder in `test-file-components.ts` observes both writes with no shim change (`makeNode` records every property write).

**CAVEAT (in the PR body too):** Figma does not re-layout an already-built set on idempotent reuse — `file-setup` skips the build when the page already holds the pair — so this corrects **FRESH builds only**; an already-built file must be rebuilt to pick it up.

── THE NET (docs/34) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

New stacking block in `test-file-components.ts`, INDEPENDENT of the #1563 structural arms (it reads the SET's `layoutMode` and each member's `layoutPositioning`, which no other arm touches): for each set it asserts `layoutMode === 'VERTICAL'` and every variant child `layoutPositioning === 'AUTO'`. Expected values are the Figma Plugin-API constants for in-flow vertical stacking, hand-named — never read off the subject's `SECTION_SIZES`/`HEADINGS` tables. **By-name mutations, each from a known-good `wip:` HEAD, restored:** drop the `layoutPositioning='AUTO'` loop → the two "every variant child is in-flow" arms fail by name (set layout stays green, isolating that half); drop the `autoLayout(set, …)` call → the two "stacks variants VERTICALLY" arms fail by name (`layoutMode` reads `undefined`). Full `npm run verify` run to 61/61 PASS, 0 SKIP.

## (2026-09-23) — component writer never discards text for want of a loaded font (#1599)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** Plugin-only — `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts` (the font floor + `CompNode.fontName` port field), `apps/plugin/component-shim.ts` (the font-loaded model for `characters` writes: `DEFAULT_FONT`, a `figma.mixed` sentinel, `mixedTextFonts` opt, a throwing TEXT `characters` setter, `setTextStyleIdAsync` sets the node's font, twins carry `fontName`, `loadFontAsync` refuses a non-`FontName`), `apps/plugin/test-write-components.ts` (the by-name arms), and this entry. **NO `out/**` change, NO version bump** — this is the plugin executor, not the engine (`lint-emission-version` 0 artifacts, `regen --check`/`drift` clean). Gate count **STANDS at 61** — the new assertions are arms of the existing `plugin-test`. Closes #1599. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `packages/engine/`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`, `apps/plugin/src/write-figma.ts`/`file-components.ts`.

── THE PROBLEM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Owner-found building NB `field-label`: **252 misses**, every text node discarded, from ONE missing text style. The writer loaded a font ONLY inside the branch where the text style was found (`st.fontName`, before `setTextStyleIdAsync`). Writing `node.characters` requires the node's **current** font loaded (a hard Figma rule), so whenever the style was absent — or carried no font, or its font couldn't load — nothing loaded a font at all, `node.characters = "Label"` threw `Cannot write to node with unloaded font "Inter Regular"`, and the text was discarded. Catastrophic where it should degrade: text should land in the fallback font. (The absent-style *trigger* is a workflow-ordering matter — styles are created by Apply, not the component build — but the robustness floor holds regardless, and is the whole of this PR.)

── THE FIX ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A FLOOR, immediately before `node.characters = …`: always load the node's OWN current font, independent of the style path. When a style applied, that font IS the style's and is already loaded (no-op); when the style was missing, the node still carries its fresh-`createText` font and this is what makes the write land. `node.fontName` is `FontName | figma.mixed`; the floor guards with a SHAPE check (`typeof fn === 'object'`) rather than naming `figma.mixed` — both to narrow the union for `loadFontAsync` and to keep the executor port-driven (it never touches the global `figma`), the same "compare shape, don't name figma.mixed" the port already takes for `textStyleId`. A load that throws (a brand face not installed) is RECORDED and the write still attempted — the #680 posture: report what was skipped, write everything else. Minimal: the style still loads and applies its own font when present; this only adds a floor.

── THE SHIM (why it grew) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The defect's mechanism — `characters` write throws on an unloaded font — was NOT modelled: the shim only threw from `setTextStyleIdAsync`. Without modelling it, reverting the floor would leave every arm green (docs/34: a stub models the axis or it cannot gate it). So TEXT nodes now start on `DEFAULT_FONT` (Inter Regular, distinct from `STYLE_FONT`=Semi Bold, unloaded until named), their `characters` setter throws Figma's own message on an unloaded/`mixed` font, `setTextStyleIdAsync` re-resolves the node's font to the style's, combine/settle twins carry `fontName` through the backing field (host reconciliation, not a plugin write — same reasoning as `_exposed`), and `loadFontAsync` refuses a non-`FontName` so the mixed guard is load-bearing.

── THE NET (docs/34) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Arm runs the real `field-label` def against a file with NO text styles (`styles: []`) — the exact trigger, every text node's style absent — pinned twice first (the style misses ARE reported so the trigger is real; the plans DO carry 48 characters so "nothing discarded" is a claim about real text). **By-name mutations, each from a known-good `wip:` HEAD, restored:** (M1) delete the floor → `#1599 with the font floor, NO character is discarded …` fails naming the 48 `DISCARDED (set "Label", reads "")` misses — the field-label catastrophe in miniature; (M2) drop the floor's shape guard (`if (fn && typeof fn === 'object')` → `if (fn)`) → `figma.mixed` is handed to `loadFontAsync`, which refuses it, and `#1599 …nothing was handed to loadFontAsync — no font miss on the mixed arm` fails by name. A read-back of the built nodes is deliberately NOT a second witness: field-label's text is characters-BOUND, so a bound node reads its caption from the set-level property default whether or not the build-time write landed — the DISCARDED miss is the only arm that tells the floor apart from its absence. `npm run verify` → **61/61, 0 SKIP**.

── HOST VERIFICATION (owner's click-through, #1573/#1578 pattern) ─────────────────────────────────────────

This is shim-testable robustness; the live NB case — a brand face not installed, text falling back to Inter (#113) — is the owner's host verification. The floor makes text *appear*; the correct *font* still needs the face available in the file.

## (2026-09-23) — Figma color palette variables emit in numeric-key order (#1597)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** The #1594 fix, ported to the palette. Engine emission ORDER only — `packages/engine/emit-figma-color.ts` (a local `byNumericKey` mirror of #1594's helper + an optional `orderKeys` param on the shared `leaves()` walk, defaulting to identity; the palette emit passes `byNumericKey`), the regenerated `out/**` (three `core.palette.json` reorder — nb · aurora · wendys — + the engine-stamp bump on the DTCG trees), `packages/engine/version.ts` (ENGINE 0.130.0 → **0.131.0**, changelog newest-first), `packages/engine/schema/token-contract.json` (`engineVersion` re-stamp only, CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0), `packages/engine/test.ts` (the by-name ordering arm), and this entry. **ENGINE bump, CONTRACT stands.** Gate count **STANDS at 61** — the new assertion is an arm of the existing engine `test`. Closes #1597. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `apps/plugin/`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`, `scale.ts` — no token name, value, scope or alias moved.

**Root cause & why the fix is scoped to palette.** The palette walks the tree through the shared `leaves()` helper, which iterated child keys in `Object.keys` order — integer-like keys (`"100"`…`"950"`) first ascending, then leading-zero strings (`"025"`,`"050"`) in insertion order — so every chromatic ramp emitted `…, 900, 950, 025, 050`, dropping the two lightest tints to the BOTTOM of the Figma variables panel. `leaves()` is also the color-mode collection's walk, so rather than change its default behavior, I gave it an optional `orderKeys` (identity default, byte-identical for every other caller) and opted in only at the palette site. `byNumericKey` is a **stable no-op** for non-leading-zero groups: ramp names (`red`, `black-alpha`) and semantic keys (`background`) `parseFloat` to NaN and compare equal, and alpha steps (`5`,`10`…`90`) are already integer-like ascending — so of the whole palette only the chromatic ramps carrying `025`/`050` reorder. Verified: exactly the three `out/figma/<brand>/core.palette.json` reorder, each variable **set byte-identical** (123/163/183 vars unchanged, only sequence moved); the color-mode files and every non-palette artifact are untouched but the version stamp.

The by-name arm asserts nb's `red` palette ramp emits in an **independently hand-written literal** order (`025, 050, 100, …, 950`) — NOT derived from `Object.keys(...)`, the side under test — so it is not a `x === x` gate. **By-name mutation, restored from a `wip:` commit:** reverting the palette site to raw `leaves(...)` fails the named `#1597: palette ramp steps emit sorted by numeric key …` assertion (got `100,…,950,025,050`); restored, `test.ts` is 3884/0 green again. `npm run verify` → 61/61, 0 SKIP.

**Caveat (as #1594):** this corrects **creation** order, so **fresh** builds get numeric order; an existing file's already-created variables keep their order (idempotent find-by-name apply doesn't reorder). The benefit lands on the next fresh build.

## (2026-09-23) — gutter & margin editable per breakpoint, snapping to the spacing ladder (#1593)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** Engine + studio — `packages/engine/theme.ts` (`BrandInput['layout']` + `BrandInputAuthored` gain `gutterOverrides`/`marginOverrides`; `buildLayout` gains `resolveGap`), `packages/engine/schema/theme-schema.json` (the two new fields + sibling-prose compression for the MCP ceiling), `packages/engine/version.ts` (ENGINE 0.128.0 → **0.129.0**, changelog), `packages/engine/schema/token-contract.json` (stamp-only re-accept), `apps/studio/src/main.ts` (the per-breakpoint grid editor), `packages/engine/test.ts` (the by-name gate), and this entry. **`out/**` moves ONLY its `$extensions.generator.version` stamp** — no corpus brand sets an override, so every emitted grid VALUE is byte-identical; `lint-emission-version` sees 0 artifacts, `regen --check`/`drift` clean. Gate count **STANDS at 61** — the new assertions are arms of the existing engine `test`. **ENGINE bumps (behavior); CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0** — gutter/margin already emit as `grid/gutter`·`grid/margin` variables + grid-style values, so no guaranteed token NAME moves (`token-contract --check` level `none`, stamp-only `--accept`). Closes #1593. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `apps/plugin/`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`, `SPACE_BASE`/the spacing scale.

── THE PROBLEM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Gutter and margin were DERIVED from fixed arrays indexed by breakpoint (`GUTTER_PX`/`MARGIN_PX`), with no brand input reaching them; the studio Layout page showed them read-only. Building New Balance needs a **4px mobile gutter** — `space/050` — which the derived ladder (floor 16px) can't express.

── THE CHANGE (mirrors #1532's `columnOverrides`, with one deliberate divergence) ────────────────────────

`layout.gutterOverrides` / `layout.marginOverrides` (keyed by breakpoint name) win over the ladder for that breakpoint; an unset one keeps the ladder. **The divergence from columns:** columns CLAMP an out-of-range value, but gutter/margin **THROW off-ladder** (`resolveGap`). That is not a stylistic choice — gutter/margin emit as ALIASES to `space/*` (`emit-figma-dims.ts` + `tree.ts`'s `gridSpaceAlias`, which looks the px up in `spaceKeyOf`), so a free px would have **no space token to alias** and `gridSpaceAlias` would silently fall back to a literal, breaking the alias graph the owner chose snap-to-ladder to preserve. On-ladder is thus the invariant that keeps the emission model intact; the validator's px set is built from `spaceScale(SPACE_BASE)`, the same scale `spaceKeyOf` aliases against, so anything it admits is guaranteed to have a `space/*` token. Reaching `space/050`=4px (and `025`/`0`) is what unlocks the NB case. **No emitter change** — the Figma grid-style emitter, the layout float emitter and the DTCG grid node all already read `theme.layout.grid`, so a custom 4px gutter aliases `space/050` automatically. Studio: the per-breakpoint grid table's read-only gutter/margin cells become a select of spacing steps (Auto = the derived ladder, full ladder down to 4px); the plugin runs this UI verbatim, so no plugin change.

**Lever manifest — deliberately NOT added (technical call, flagged).** The task listed a `levers.ts` entry, but `columnOverrides` — the pattern this mirrors "exactly" — has NONE: per-breakpoint override maps live nested under the `layout` object (already a manifest root), as schema + studio, not as UI-knob levers. Adding object-typed lever entries here would diverge from the sibling it mirrors and from the `nonLeverFields` model. Kept consistent with `columnOverrides`; MCP discoverability comes via the schema, which IS inlined in `theme_brand`.

── THE NET (docs/34) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

New engine gate block (19f, `test.ts`): EXPECTED hand-authored from the documented ladders ([16,16,24,24,32]/[16,24,24,32,48]) + the snap rule + the space key for 4px read from the SCALE; ACTUAL read from the EMITTED Figma Grid Styles (px) AND the DTCG grid node's alias `$value` (the space token) — never from `buildLayout`/`resolveGap`. **By-name mutations, each from a known-good `wip:` HEAD, restored:** (M1) `buildLayout` ignores the gutter override → the APPLY arm ("wins over the 16px ladder — got 16") and the ALIAS arm ("emits as an ALIAS to space/050 — got `{prism.space.200}`") fail by name; (M2) drop `resolveGap`'s on-ladder guard → the off-ladder gutter (5px) and margin (7px) THROW arms fail by name, while APPLY/ALIAS stay green (isolating the guard). **MCP ceiling (#1368):** the two new schema fields pushed `tools/list` over 60,000; clawed back under (59,927) by compressing sibling schema prose (`surfaceMode.inverseBase`, `modeLevers`, `typography.sizes`, `modeLevers.typeSizes` — redundancy trimmed, every load-bearing fact kept), the same move #1510 made. `lint-us-english`/`lint-voice` run after the web build and cover the built bundle + schema, so the new UI labels and schema prose are in scope.

## (2026-09-23) — Figma dimension variables emit in numeric-key order (#1594)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** Engine emission ORDER only — `packages/engine/emit-figma-dims.ts` (one new pure helper `byNumericKey`, applied at the seven dimension `Object.keys` sites), the regenerated `out/**` (three `space.json` reorder + the engine-stamp bump on the DTCG trees), `packages/engine/version.ts` (ENGINE 0.128.0 → **0.129.0**, changelog newest-first), `packages/engine/schema/token-contract.json` (`engineVersion` re-stamp only, CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0), `packages/engine/test.ts` (the by-name ordering arm), and this entry. **ENGINE bump, CONTRACT stands.** Gate count **STANDS at 61** — the new assertion is an arm of the existing engine `test`. Closes #1594. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `apps/plugin/`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`, `scale.ts` — no token name, value, scope or alias moved.

── THE PROBLEM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

In the Figma variables panel the `space` sub-steps (`025`=2px, `050`=4px, `075`=6px) appeared **after `1200`**, reading as "missing" until you scroll to the bottom. Root cause is JS object-key iteration order: **integer-like** keys (`"0"`,`"100"`…`"1200"`) iterate first in ascending-numeric order, then **leading-zero string** keys (`"025"`,`"050"`,`"075"`) follow in insertion order. The emit maps over `Object.keys(brand.space)`, so the plugin *creates* the variables in that order and Figma shows creation order → sub-steps at the bottom.

── THE FIX ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

One small pure helper, `byNumericKey(keys)`, sorts by the key's numeric magnitude (`parseFloat`), and is applied at each dimension `Object.keys` emission site (`core.dimension`, `space`, `radius`, `size`, `icon`, `control`, `opacity`). It is a **stable no-op** for named collections: t-shirt/rung keys (`radius.none`, `size.md`) `parseFloat` to NaN and compare equal, so their insertion order is preserved and their output is byte-identical. Only `space` actually carries leading-zero keys among the dimension sites, so of all the regenerated figma files only the three `space.json` (nb · aurora · wendys) reorder — each verified as a pure reorder (the variable set is byte-identical as a set; new order `0, 025, 050, 075, 100, 150, …, 1200`). Applying the helper broadly (not just to `space`) is the issue-endorsed recurrence guard: a leading-zero key added to any dimension collection later sorts correctly for free.

── A PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD: `size` ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The issue named `size` (`050`, `075`) as a second mis-ordering collection. It does not, in the current corpus: the `size` Figma collection is keyed by **t-shirt rung** (`xs/sm/md/lg/xl`), not by leading-zero numeric steps, so `Object.keys(brand.size)` already iterates in the intended order and `byNumericKey` leaves it byte-identical. The helper is still applied there (no-op, recurrence guard), but `size` output does not change. Confirmed by `git diff` (only `space.json` files moved among figma output). Separately, the **color palette ramps** (`core.palette`, `emit-figma-color.ts`) mis-order the same way (`025`/`050` after each ramp's `950`) — out of scope for this dimension-only PR (guardrail: `emit-figma-dims.ts` only, one concern per PR); **filed as #1597.**

── VERSIONING (principle 5) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Reordering emission is a behavior change → **ENGINE bumps** (0.128.0 → 0.129.0); the DTCG trees restamp `$extensions.generator.version`. CONTRACT **stands** at 11.3.0 — ordering is not a token NAME or `$type` change, so `token-contract --check` reports level `none`; the `--accept` refreshes only the informational `engineVersion` field in the baseline (diff is that one line). `regen --check` and `lint-emission-version` see the reordered `space.json` + restamped trees as the expected change for this bump.

── THE NET (docs/34) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The by-name arm asserts nb's `space` variables emit in an **independently hand-written literal** order (`0, 025, 050, 075, 100, …, 1200`) — NOT derived from `Object.keys(brand.space)`, the side under test — so it is not a `x === x` gate. **By-name mutation, restored from a `wip:` commit:** reverting the `space` site to raw `Object.keys(...)` fails the named `#1594: space variables emit sorted by numeric key …` assertion (got `0,100,…,1200,025,050,075`); restored, `test.ts` is 3876/0 green again. `npm run verify` → 61/61, 0 SKIP.

── THE CAVEAT (state in PR) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

This fixes **creation** order, so **fresh** builds get numeric order. An **existing** Figma file's already-created variables keep their order — the plugin apply is idempotent find-by-name and Figma does not reorder on reuse — so the benefit lands on the next fresh build (the NB case that surfaced this).

## (2026-09-23) — the tracking UI reads in percent as well as em (#1590)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** Studio DISPLAY only — `apps/studio/src/em-percent.ts` (a new pure helper), `apps/studio/src/main.ts` (the four letter-spacing render sites), `apps/studio/test-em-percent.ts` (the by-name test) and `apps/studio/package.json` (wiring that test into `npm test`). **No engine change, no `out/**`, NO version bump** — the stored value stays em; this is a reading aid, so `lint-emission-version` sees 0 artifacts and `regen --check` stays clean. Gate count **STANDS at 61** — the new assertions are arms of the existing `@prism3/studio` `test`. Closes #1590. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `packages/engine/`, `apps/plugin/`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`.

── THE PROBLEM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The Letter Spacing / tracking UI lists values in negative em (`-0.02em`, `-0.015em`, …), but a designer — and Figma — thinks in **percent**. `-0.02em` reads as nothing until you know it is **−2%**. Letter-spacing em is percent-of-font-size, so the conversion is exact: 1em = 100%, i.e. percent = em × 100. Every site now shows both, em primary (it is the stored, authoritative value) and percent as the reading aid: `-0.02em · −2%`.

── THE CHANGE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The ×100 rule lives in ONE pure helper, `emToPercentLabel(em)`, driven by all four letter-spacing em display sites in `main.ts`: the composite tracking summary (`typeComposite`, :1642), the **ladder table** (Primitives → Leading & tracking ladders), the **rung dropdown** option labels (Semantics → Leading & tracking rungs), and the **per-mode re-point** "worth" values (`renderRepointTable`, Leading & tracking per mode). `lsOf` (:7076) is deliberately NOT touched — it feeds the actual CSS `letter-spacing`, where the number must stay a bare em, not a label. The helper strips trailing zeros (`−1.5%`, never `−1.50%`) and uses a real minus sign (−, U+2212), not a hyphen.

── THE DEVIATION, FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The lane guardrail said "touch only `main.ts` + a test". The helper is a **new module** instead of an inline function in `main.ts`, and this is the same forced move `provenance.ts` and `export-settings.ts` already made: `main.ts` touches `document` at import time (a top-level `_fontProbe`, `installStyles(STYLE)`, `build()`), so it cannot load under `tsx` — a helper inside it is unit-testable only by hand in a browser. docs/34 makes the extraction non-optional, not stylistic: the by-name mutation requires the test and the four UI sites drive the SAME function, and an inline copy the test duplicated would be a DRY-collapsed gate (shape 2) asserting `helper === helper`. Wiring the new test into `npm test` needs the one-line `package.json` edit. Both are inside `apps/studio`; nothing on the guardrail's do-not-touch list moved.

── THE NET (docs/34) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`test-em-percent.ts` asserts `emToPercentLabel` over **every** `LETTER_SPACING_LADDER` step — the exact set the UI renders — against **independently transcribed** expected labels (a `Record` typed by hand, NOT computed from the helper: deriving the oracle from the subject is shape 1/2 and cannot fail), plus a floor that every ladder step has an expected entry so a step added upstream fails loudly rather than passing unmeasured, plus the two step-independent promises (trailing-zero strip, real minus sign). **By-name mutation, restored from a known-good HEAD:** breaking the ×100 to ×10 in `em-percent.ts` fails the named `emToPercentLabel(...)` assertions (e.g. `−2%` → got `−0.2%`) across both the issue-value arm and the full-ladder sweep; restored, `npm test` for `@prism3/studio` is green again. Because the helper is display-only, the engine/version/regen gates stand untouched, which is itself the check that the change never leaked into emission.

## (2026-09-23) — the size table's base column is a base, not an appearance mode (#1586)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** Studio only — `apps/studio/src/main.ts` (the `renderSizeTable` header loop), a new pure module `apps/studio/src/size-labels.ts`, its test `apps/studio/test-size-labels.ts` wired into `@prism3/studio`'s `test` script, and this entry. **No `out/**` change, NO version bump, NO engine/emit change** — `lint-emission-version` sees 0 artifacts and `regen --check` stays clean; nothing here is emission. Gate count **STANDS at 61** — the new assertions are arms of the studio `test` gate. Closes #1586. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `packages/engine/`, `apps/plugin/`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `tools/`.

── THE PROBLEM: A VIEWPORT-INDEPENDENT BASE LABELLED AS AN APPEARANCE VALUE ───────────────────────────────

`renderSizeTable` lays out one column per THEME-axis mode (`rp.modes` = light/dark/…) and rendered the base value (`sizePx`) under the `light` column with a ` baseline` suffix → **"LIGHT baseline"**. But type sizes do NOT vary by light/dark — they vary by VIEWPORT (mobile/desktop), a separate axis the Responsive type lever derives at emit time and the studio size table does not expose. So the base value is viewport-independent, and the appearance-mode framing sent the reader looking for a desktop/mobile control that isn't there (found while setting up New Balance sizes: it was unclear whether the table edited mobile or desktop — it edits neither).

── THE FIX: REFRAME ONLY THE BASE COLUMN ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The base column now reads **"Base"** with a hover explanation — *"One base size — the Responsive type lever scales it between mobile and desktop."* (voice-standard §3: declarative, em dash carries the why). **The per-theme-mode columns stay:** `sizeByMode` is real (a brand can legitimately tweak a dark-mode size), so the dark column keeps its "Dark" label and derived modes keep " auto" (#423) — only the base column stopped implying appearance governs sizes. Out of scope, tracked as #1587: surfacing the derived desktop/mobile endpoints and per-viewport editing (needs an engine override layer).

**Why a new module.** The header text was not readily unit-testable in place: `main.ts` calls `build()` (touching `document`) at import and cannot load under `tsx` — the same constraint that put `provenance.ts` in its own module. So the column-label logic is extracted to a pure `sizeColumnHeader(isBase, isEditable, modeLabel)` helper and tested directly. This is the reason the diff touches more than `main.ts` + a test: the extraction the fix requires needs a module and a `package.json` test wiring, both inside `apps/studio/`.

── THE NET (docs/34) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**Independence:** the gate's load-bearing assertion is written against a LITERAL rule — the base column's visible text (label + suffix) must carry no appearance-mode word (`/\b(light|dark|baseline|…)\b/i`) — NOT against the module's own `SIZE_BASE_LABEL` constant, which would be `x === x` and pass whatever the label became (shape 2). A positive arm confirms it names a base and explains the mobile↔desktop scaling, so the fix is not merely deleting the word. **By-name mutation, restored to a known-good HEAD (a `wip:` commit first, `--amend`ed once green):** reverting the base branch to `{ text: modeLabel, suffix: ' baseline' }` fails the named assertion *"the base column text carries NO appearance-mode word"* (4 arms red, exit 1); after restore, 14/14 pass. `lint-us-english.ts`/`lint-voice.ts` run after the web build (verify handles ordering), so the "Base" label and tooltip in the built bundle are in scope.

## (2026-09-23) — the prune preview names the variables it would delete, not just count them (#1585)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** Plugin RUNTIME only — `apps/plugin/src/prune-figma.ts` (a new `varNote` composed beside the existing `modeNote`/`styleNote`) plus `apps/plugin/test-prune.ts` (two new arms). **No `out/**` change, NO version bump** — ENGINE STANDS, CONTRACT STANDS: nothing here is emission. Gate count **STANDS at 61** — both new assertions are arms of `plugin-test`. Closes #1585. **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `tools/`, `packages/engine/`, TokenPress, `apps/plugin/src/main.ts` (the wiring already carries `p.variables` groups with `{ collection, names }`, so no read-side change was needed).

── THE PROBLEM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`prunePreviewSummary` NAMED the two arms whose items carry the weakest provenance — modes (`modeNote`, #1570) and description-recognized styles (`styleNote`, #1577) — but the VARIABLE arm, the most numerous, showed only a count. Counting was deliberate and stays defensible: an offered variable is namespace-guarded (only in-namespace, plan-dropped vars are ever offered; `inRoot`), so a hand-added variable outside the namespace is never in the list. But a destructive action should still show its targets — a designer scanning the preview before confirming deserves to see `color → nbds/color/text/legacy`, not `1 variable`.

── THE CHANGE, AND THE ONE DISCIPLINE IT BORROWS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`varNote(p)` names the offered variables GROUPED BY COLLECTION (`color → a, b, c; space → d`), the third helper of the same shape as `modeNote`/`styleNote`, appended in `prunePreviewSummary`. Names are shown VERBATIM — the raw `<root>/…` slash paths, which are exactly what the designer reads in Figma's variable list, so the note matches the file rather than a prettified derivation. **Collections stay COUNTED** (few and coarse); no per-item selection, no UI change, the confirm stays all-or-nothing — transparency only, per the issue's scope.

Capped at `VAR_NOTE_CAP` (8) names per collection with the remainder reported as `… +K more` — the same truncate-and-say-so discipline as #1579's 60 kB report cap, and for the same reason: a preview that names its targets must not become a wall that hides the count it replaced. Held as a named constant so the test drives a fixture past it and the cap fails by name.

── THE NET (docs/34) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Two new arms, each proved by a restored mutation (tree clean at a known-good HEAD before every one, per the CLAUDE.md mutation-battery rule): **(a)** the offered variable renders BY NAME under its collection — `The variables are color → nbds/color/text/legacy` — and dropping the `varNote` append fails it by name (no other note produces `color → nbds/…`; `modeNote` is `layout → …`, `styleNote` is a kind). **(b)** a fixture with 13 in-namespace orphans in one collection caps at 8 names and reads `… +5 more`, with the beyond-cap `ghost-12` NOT named; dropping the cap (show all 13) fails it by name — the `+5 more` disappears and `ghost-12` appears. Both mutations confirmed to fail exactly their arm, then restored, then re-confirmed green.

## (2026-09-23) — the conformance scan learns to fix, for two categories only (#1553 P2)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** `tools/` only — new `tools/conformance-scan/fix.ts` and `fixtures/fix-manifest.json`, ten new arms in `mutations.sh`, the run-loop + apply snippet in the README, one binding added to the three fixtures, and the section in `tools/CLAUDE.md` that described the harness as report-only. **No `out/**` change, NO version bump** — ENGINE STANDS, CONTRACT STANDS: nothing here is emission, and `lint-emission-version` reporting a single artifact would have meant it had leaked into one. Gate count **STANDS at 61**, `ci.yml` untouched — a tool answers a question and exits 0 (`tools/CLAUDE.md`), and this one's own self-checks are the author's, like `diff.ts --selftest` before it. Refs #1553 (P2). **NOT TOUCHED:** #1367/#1385, `.claude/settings.json`, `apps/plugin/`, `apps/tokenpress/`, `packages/engine/`, the manifest's `main` (the deferred bridge, decision #4).

── THE SAFE/UNSAFE BOUNDARY IS THE DESIGN, AND THE FIXTURE IS WHERE IT IS PROVEN ──────────────────────────

P1 answered *"does this Figma file match what the engine says should be there?"* and stopped. P2 closes the loop for the two categories that are safe to automate and carries every other finding through as an exclusion with a reason. `fix.ts` is a plan EMITTER — pure, no Figma access, applies nothing; the writes are the operator's, through one `figma_execute` in the README, dry run first. Safe: **(c)** `setValueForMode` back to the engine's value (no structure moves — same variable, same mode, same bindings, one value), and **(a)** a rebind of a raw literal to the variable the engine plans, **only when that variable is in the file**.

**That last clause is the whole tool, and the fixture now carries both halves of it.** The two cases are the *same shape* in the report — a hex where a variable belongs — and only one is a fix that can run. So `widget · /caption · fills` was added as a raw literal whose planned `fix/color/text/secondary` is exactly the variable the (f) structure omission takes out: a rebind there has nothing to bind to, so it is a structure gap wearing a binding finding's clothes. Both halves in one file, one row apart in the answer key, for the same reason the `strokeWeight` lenience is proven working and failing in one file. `diff.ts --selftest` stays green (25 findings, all nine categories).

Unsafe, and each reason is a case where the obvious op is destructive or cannot run rather than a policy preference: **(f)** structure is a rebuild and the plugin's rebuild is behind a `STALE` guard — decision #5, held by the owner; **(b)** which token a node carries is a design decision, and the two candidates usually render alike, so a wrong automatic choice is invisible and permanent; **(d)** mode add/remove belongs to the reconciler (#1570) and the prune (#1521), where mode identity is tracked; **(h)** is a rebuild; **(g)** is a *consequence* — fixing the value cleared both of the fixture's light-mode contrast findings, which is precisely why contrast is never its own op; **(e)** retyping a live variable coerces every value bound through it; **(i)** would fork the plugin's four style writers.

── FOUR DECISIONS WORTH THE INK ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**1. The plan is a complete accounting, not a subset.** `ops + excluded === findings`, asserted, and the exclusions print under the ops with their reasons. A fix tool whose output is a silent subset of the diff teaches its operator that the plan IS the remaining work — the one belief that makes (f) dangerous, since those findings do not stop existing because nothing can be done about them automatically. The same property makes a tenth diff category safe to add: `EXCLUSION_REASON` is keyed by `Category`, so a new one is a compile error in `fix.ts` until somebody classifies it, and the classification it cannot get by default is `safe`.

**2. DEVIATION, flagged for the owner — the signature.** The brief said `fix(diffReport)`; it is `fix(report, expected, actual)`. With the states in hand, `resolvedType`, variable existence and library-consumed status are **read** rather than inferred from report prose: that is what lets the plan emit a correctly typed `setValueForMode` value (a canonical `12` is ambiguous between STRING and FLOAT, and a mistyped write either throws or silently coerces) and what makes *"the expected variable EXISTS in the file"* a lookup instead of a guess — the only place that fact lives. The written value comes from the expectation STATE and must **agree** with the finding's `expected` or the finding is excluded, because a report and a state that disagree are most likely a report kept from an earlier scan. A coordinate is never parsed back out of a rendered subject either (`showBindKey` is one-way); it is matched against a map of the expectation's own keys.

**3. Idempotence is absoluteness, not bookkeeping.** Every op writes a desired state (`setValueForMode(mode, <value>)`, `setBoundVariable(property, <variable>)`), never a delta — so a second apply is a no-op and a `fix.ts` run over the re-scan emits zero ops. The self-check proves both by applying the plan to the actual `State` in memory and re-diffing. That in-memory apply is a **model** of Figma and a narrow one — it claims only that a value write replaces a value and a rebind replaces a bind state — and it is not a claim that Figma behaves that way. Only the host acceptance run can say that, which is why it is a step in the README rather than a passing arm.

**4. #1569's false positives are cosmetic in a report and DESTRUCTIVE in a plan, so every plan built at a committed config carries a standing warning.** This is the sharpest thing the lane found and it is not in the brief. `expected.ts` without `--design` builds the expectation at the brand's **committed** levers; #1569 already recorded what that does to a *report* (62 `high` findings that were the lever delta and nothing else). Feed the same report to `fix.ts` and each of those becomes a `setValueForMode` that writes the **brand default over the operator's own lever setting** — a scan that merely lied now silently reverts a deliberate design decision, and it does so at every coordinate the levers moved. So the plan's `notes` say, unconditionally, which config the expectation was built at and that `--design <the brief this file was applied at>` must be re-run first; `selftest` step 8 asserts the note is present, and a by-name arm fails if the condition is defeated. The detection is a sniff on `report.brand` (`' ← '` means a supplied brief) — a weakness stated in the code, and the reason that format is itself pinned by an existing `expected.ts` arm.

── THE NET (docs/34): THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS IS INVERTED HERE ─────────────────────────────────────────

Every check in this harness before `fix.ts` can only fail by going quiet about a real defect. This one leads to a WRITE, so it can also fail by saying too much — and **an op that should not exist is the failure that hurts, because it is performed in someone's Figma file minutes later and not in this repo.** So: `fixtures/fix-manifest.json` is hand-written (a key generated from the plan's own output is `docs/34` shape 1 and cannot fail), asserted as set equality **both ways** with exact counts, with the two ops' written **values** pinned (an op that exists and writes `26` where Figma wants `26/255` passes every by-name check and lands a near-white fill), the seven never-fixable categories pinned **by name, one arm each**, and a requirement that every category be either pinned or one of the two safe shapes.

**Ten new mutation arms, 54 detected / 0 undetected, each behind its own commit (every revert reaches `HEAD`).** The two that carry the lane both remove a *guard*: drop the "is this variable in the file" check and the un-rebindable twin leaks in as an op (`EXTRA op rebind: … /caption · fills`); drop the raw-literal whitelist and `gadget · size=sm · / · fills` leaks in — a node property on a component the file does not have. **Nothing downstream of the plan could have caught either**: the in-memory apply performs a rebind to a missing variable as happily as a real one, because that write only fails in Figma. The hand-written key is the only thing that notices.

**Three things left unproven on purpose, written down rather than left to be rediscovered as oversights.** (i) *"The value comes from the state, never the report's prose"* is not falsifiable by a self-check that computes the report from the same states — it needs a report kept from an earlier scan, which an operator can have and a fixture cannot be. (ii) No mutation of this fixture produces an idempotence-only failure, because every op is absolute by construction; that arm is a net for a future op shape that is not. (iii) The `excluded: findings - ops` mutant — the `docs/34` shape-1 form of the accounting bug — is **equivalent** in this fixture (25 − 2 is 23), so the arm that stands in for it mutes the catch-all exclusion instead and seventeen findings land in no bucket, which is the failure the invariant exists to catch. The counted-from-the-arrays assertion stays in the code for the day a third bucket appears.

── WHAT IS LEFT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**HOST ACCEPTANCE IS NOT DONE, and it is BLOCKED on an input rather than on time.** What is needed on the live QA file: scan → apply the plan via `figma_execute` → re-scan; the value-mismatch and rebindable-raw-literal findings clear, the excluded categories remain, and a second apply comes back all `ALREADY`. The blocker is decision 4 — the live QA file was applied at moved levers (#1569 recovered them: density `spacious`, breakpoints `[768, 1920]`, from the file's own aliases), so a plan built without the `design.md` **that file was applied at** would write brand defaults over exactly those levers. Recovering the config by inference from the file is what `docs/34` shape 1 forbids and what makes the plan agree with the file by construction; it has to come from the operator. So the run is handed back with the brief, not performed on a guess. Until then the only claim in hand is that the plan is internally consistent with the scan's own model of the file. Two known gaps, both named in the README: a rebind binds the paint's **color** and leaves a designer's paint-level `opacity` alone (so a rebound fill can still render at 50%, and the scan does not compare opacity), and the plan is bounded by what the scan could see — a scoped read plans only inside its scope, and the report's own blind spots cannot be fixed or excluded because they were never findings.

## (2026-09-23) — provenance for the prune: a written stamp for modes, a read signature for styles (#1577, #1581)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (the orchestrator verifies + reviews + merges under the net).** Plugin RUNTIME only — `apps/plugin/src/prune-figma.ts` (the recognizer + the ∈-owned gate), `apps/plugin/src/write-figma.ts` (the stamp), `apps/plugin/src/main.ts` (five lines of wiring, isolated in its own commit — see the deviation below), plus `test-prune.ts` and `test-write-float.ts`. **No `out/**` change, NO version bump** — ENGINE STANDS, CONTRACT STANDS: nothing here is emission, and `lint-emission-version` / `lint-component-surface` firing would have meant the change had leaked into it.
