## (2026-09-18) — `image-placeholder`: `footprintVaries: ['ratio']` clears two false footprint misses (#1515)

**STATUS: LANDED. ENGINE 0.118.0 → 0.119.0; CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0. Bug fix (false-positive QA miss) found in owner QA 2026-09-18 — same class as #1474/field-message.**

**THE SYMPTOM.** `image-placeholder` projected with **two footprint misses** in owner QA: `ratio=4:3 measures 720×540 but ratio=1:1 measures 720×720 (same)` and the 16:9 twin (`720×405`). The footprint read-back (`write-components.ts`, exercised by `test-roundtrip.ts`) compares members expecting an EQUAL box — a filled button must not measure wider than its outline sibling — and flagged the two ratios as differing from 1:1.

**THE DIAGNOSIS.** The differences are correct: the `ratio` axis (1:1/4:3/16:9) is an aspect-ratio LOCK, so it is SUPPOSED to change the frame's height — that is the whole point of the component. The cohort check was comparing the right thing (the full box) in the wrong cohort. This is exactly the #1010 class field-message hit: an axis that legitimately varies the footprint needs the `footprintVaries` exemption so the cohort key partitions the members rather than comparing them.

**THE FIX — one declaration, plus the reason the schema had to learn.** `figmaProperties.footprintVaries: ['ratio']` on `image-placeholder`. This threads into `planSetLayout`'s cohort key (`anatomy-figma.ts`) so each ratio becomes its own cohort — no cross-ratio comparison, misses cleared. But `field-message`'s `status` moves the box because a `presentWhen`-gated part appears/disappears, and the schema validator (`figmaPropertyErrors`) enforced *exactly* that: `footprintVaries` was accepted only for an axis some part's `presentWhen` gates. `ratio` gates no part — it moves the box through the frame's `aspectRatio` LOCK. The validator's own comment anticipated this ("a def whose box moves for some other reason should have to **extend this check and say what the reason is**"), so the check gained a SECOND legitimate mover: an axis some box derives its `aspectRatio` from. An axis that does NEITHER is still a blanket and still refused — the exemption is not switched to always-on.

**INDEPENDENCE / BY-NAME MUTATION (docs/34).** Three arms in `test.ts`'s image-placeholder block, EXPECTED authored there, SUBJECT the real def (and its mutant): (a) the def declares the exemption; (b) it reaches the engine's cohort key (`ratio=1:1 | ratio=4:3 | ratio=16:9` — each ratio its own cohort, which is what clears the misses); (c) **MUTATION** — strip the frame's `aspectRatio` lock and `ratio` moves the box for no reason, so `footprintVaries: ['ratio']` is refused BY NAME (`'ratio' neither gates a part … nor drives a box's aspect-ratio lock`). Deleting the new `|| p.aspectRatio === axis` acceptance clause leaves (c) red — the acceptance is load-bearing on the lock, not a hole that exempts the whole def. The chunked-payload parity block (#1010) stays on `field-message` and its stale "the one def" landmark is corrected to name `image-placeholder` as the second.

**SCOPE — projected surface, no token move.** A projected-component-surface change (#1252 case) → ENGINE bump. The projected member GEOMETRY moves (the cohort/footprint changes the plan digest), so `schema/component-surface.json` regenerated and `--accept`ed (`image-placeholder` 3 members → 3 members, different plans). `schema/paint-census.json` did NOT move (the frame's paint is unchanged; `lint-paint` clean). No emitted `out/**` VALUE moves — committed trees restamp only `$extensions.generator.version` 0.118.0 → 0.119.0. `schema/token-contract.json` `--accept`ed as a stamp-only `engineVersion` sync (no guaranteed path moved; `ratio` is a component-structure property, not a token name or React prop). CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0. No lint gate enumerates `footprintVaries` defs, so there was no scope floor to extend.

**GATES.** Full `npm run verify`: 60/60 gates reached a verdict, all PASS.

**NOT TOUCHED.** #1367 and #1385 are out of this lane's scope.

**FILES.** `components/image-placeholder.ts` (the declaration), `component-schema.ts` (the validator's second legitimate mover + doc-comment), `version.ts` (bump + changelog), `test.ts` (the three by-name arms + the corrected chunk-parity landmark), the regenerated/accepted `out/**` + `schema/component-surface.json` + `schema/token-contract.json`.

## (2026-09-18) — field-message per-status captions reach the LIVE Figma projection (#1513)

**STATUS: LANDED. PLUGIN-ONLY (`apps/plugin/`) — no engine code, def, plan, baseline, or emitted `out/**` artifact changed; ENGINE and CONTRACT both STAND (this is a write-path fix, not a projection or emission change). Gate count stays 60. Follows #1474 (the Set A copy) and its scope note, which predicted exactly this.**

**THE SYMPTOM.** Owner QA saw every `field-message` status member render the `default` caption "This is a standard message." in a live Figma file — never the four distinct Set A strings #1474 shipped (default *This is a standard message.* / error *Something needs fixing.* / warning *Double-check this.* / success *All set.*). The engine + offline shim were correct (`test-write-components.ts` green), so the gap was the live host write path — exactly what #1474's scope note (progress 2026-09-18) called out.

**THE DIAGNOSIS — RESET-ON-BIND, and why the shim was blind to it.** `figmaAnatomySet` expands `byVariant.status` into each member's own `characters` (`anatomy-figma.ts` `textDefaultOf`), and `build` writes that per-coordinate copy onto the text node BEFORE combine (`write-components.ts` ~:1339 `node.characters = n.characters`). But a component set carries ONE TEXT property with ONE `defaultValue` — the canonical fallback (`planSetProperties` → `n.textDefault ?? n.characters`, #1018). When the wire loop binds each member's text node via `componentPropertyReferences.characters`, **Figma adopts that single default onto the bound node**, discarding the pre-combine per-member write. So all four members collapse to "This is a standard message." The offline `component-shim.ts` `componentPropertyReferences` setter only validated the id and stored it — it never modeled the reset — so the shim (and every gate over it) round-tripped green while the live projection shipped the fallback four times. Textbook docs/34 shape: the gate's subject was under-modeled.

**THE FIX (two halves — the host behavior, then defeating it).** (1) `component-shim.ts` now models reset-on-bind: wiring a TEXT node's `characters` reference resets the node's `characters` to the property's `defaultValue` (threaded via a `propLookup` into `guardRefs`, since `defs` lives inside `combineAsVariants`). This reproduces the bug offline. (2) `write-components.ts` re-asserts each member's own caption AFTER wiring, inside the existing ref read-back loop — reusing the node that loop already found, so it adds ZERO host subtree searches (the #701 search-count gate is exact, and a separate re-find pass tripped it; folding into the read-back keeps the count). `build`'s pre-combine write is the right value on the wrong side of the bind seam; this is its twin after the seam. Inert for any def with no `byVariant` (the re-write equals the fallback), read back like every other write here.

**THE DIAGNOSIS THAT MADE IT SMALL.** `applyControlShape` (the only difference between the live plan path and the shim/test path) rewrites radius `tokens` only and is the identity for non-pillable defs like `field-message` — so the live and shim PLANS are byte-identical. That ruled out the plan and pointed squarely at how the host APPLIES it, which is the reset the shim never had.

**SAFETY NET (docs/34, by name).** New `#1513` block in `test-roundtrip.ts` builds field-message through the shared shim + real `applyComponentPlan` and reads the four captions back off the host. The oracle is the four Set A strings authored IN THE TEST, not read off the def, so reverting a caption in `field-message.ts` diverges by name. Two non-vacuity floors: (1) the set-level TEXT property default IS the fallback, and (2) reset-on-bind is LIVE — re-binding a caption reference collapses the node to that fallback in-test — so a green positive arm is the fix defeating a REAL reset, not a shim that never resets. **Mutation confirmed:** neutralizing the `write-components.ts` re-assert collapses all four captions to the fallback, failing the new `#1513` positive assertion AND the pre-existing `#1018/#1474` caption assertion in `test-write-components.ts` by name; restored green. Full `npm run verify`: 60/60 PASS.

**Files.** `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts` (the per-member caption index + the re-assert in the ref read-back loop), `apps/plugin/component-shim.ts` (`guardRefs` `propLookup` + reset-on-bind model, three call sites), `apps/plugin/test-roundtrip.ts` (the `#1513` host-truth block).

## (2026-09-18) — OPT-IN PRUNE: a plugin button that deletes the styles/variables a config change dropped (#1521)

**STATUS: LANDED. PLUGIN + SHARED-UI, no engine code, def, gate, baseline, or emitted `out/**` artifact changed; ENGINE and CONTRACT both STAND. Gate count stays 60. Owner chose Option 1 (opt-in prune button, not the report variant).**

**THE FRICTION.** A re-emit ADDS and UPDATES but never DELETES. Lower `typography.displayCeiling` from `3xl` to `xl` and the `2xl`/`3xl` display styles + type-set variables the new plan no longer emits stay in the file — so it keeps looking like it still has six display sizes, and the designer deletes the stale rungs by hand. #479 / #1152 made that deletion deliberate: a re-emit runs after every knob change and must never blind-delete, because at that moment it cannot tell a stale engine ghost from a variable a designer hand-bound.

**THE CHANGE.** An explicit, opt-in **Prune stale** action in the plugin UI (Figma-only), beside Apply to Figma. Clicking it computes what the current plan no longer emits and opens a confirm dialog showing the count + scope; the delete runs only on the designer's confirm — so the "never blind-delete on an apply" rule holds, and the user is the one accepting the action. Covers **text styles AND variables AND stranded collections**.

**WHAT MAKES IT SAFE — DETECTION REUSED, NAMESPACE GUARD ADDED (the whole argument).** Nothing new is scanned: the detector REUSES `orphansOf` / `strandedCollections` from `write-figma.ts` — the same set subtractions the executors' drift reports are built on — and the text-style arm reuses `orphansOf` over style names (the "text-style equivalent" the brief asked for). The one addition is the engine's own emitted NAMESPACE, and it is what keeps a hand-added item from ever being swept up:
- **Variables** — an `orphansOf` orphan in a plan-owned collection, RESTRICTED to names carrying the brand root (`rootOf(name) === root`). A designer's hand-added `my-brand/x` in the `color` collection is reported by `orphansOf` too, and this spares it.
- **Stranded collections** — a `strandedCollections` result that is NON-EMPTY and whose every variable is in the brand-root namespace (the #1148 `color.surface` shape). A hand-made "My Tokens" holding foreign-root variables, or an empty collection (provenance unreadable), is left.
- **Text styles** — an `orphansOf` orphan whose TOP-LEVEL GROUP the plan still emits. Text styles carry NEITHER root NOR the `core` tier (`figma-names.ts`), so the root guard cannot apply; their namespace is the group the plan emits. Dropped `display/2xl` shares the `display` group with the surviving `display/xl` and prunes; a hand-added `Marketing/Hero` shares no group and is left. Dropping the WHOLE `display` group prunes nothing there — the conservative direction, and #1521's named case (a partial drop) is covered.

**ARCHITECTURE.** `apps/plugin/src/prune-figma.ts` is pure detection (`computePrunePlan` over plain snapshots — no `figma.*`, the whole namespace policy unit-testable) + a thin executor (`applyPrunePlan`, deleting through a minimal `.remove()` port the real Figma satisfies, recording — never throwing — any name it cannot find). The three pruned sets are disjoint by construction (variable orphans only inside plan-OWNED collections; a stranded collection is one no plan owns). The main thread (`main.ts`) builds the SAME plans `applyTheme` builds (so "stale" means exactly "not in the plan this brand emits"), reads the file once, computes on preview, and **recomputes from a fresh read on apply** rather than trusting the preview's list — so the delete acts on the file's current orphan set, not a stale preview.

**UI (shared studio surface, the one-UI-no-fork pattern).** A new `prune` / `prune-result` message pair on the typed bridge (`messages.ts`), a `postPrune(input, confirm)` seam on `HostCommit` (`write-adapter.ts`, no-op on web — CSS custom properties have no stale-item problem), and, in `apps/studio/src/main.ts`, a Figma-only **Prune stale** bar button, its own verdict pill (its own slot, like the theme write and the component build — one kind per fact), and a confirm dialog reusing the export dialog's `exdlg-*` chrome (the deliberate cross-surface reuse the #770 class-name law names). The destructive CTA names the outcome ("Delete N items", per the voice standard's Destructive tone), never a bare "Confirm".

**ACCEPTANCE — `test-prune.ts` + a by-name mutation (docs/34).** Added to `npm run -w @prism3/plugin test`. A SYNTHETIC arm states the namespace policy crisply and a REAL-PLAN arm drives the detector off the shipped NB plans (so `root` derivation and the `<root>/…` names are the engine's own, not a fixture that could drift). Each "NOT pruned" assertion names the item a dropped guard would delete; verified by mutation — removing the variable `inRoot` filter turns *"variable: a hand-added variable OUTSIDE the namespace is NOT pruned"* red BY NAME (and eight more), restored after. The executor arm proves it deletes EXACTLY the plan and leaves planned + hand-added + empty-collection items untouched.

**SCOPE — no contract, no engine, no emitted artifact.** `version.ts` untouched; `token-contract --check` stays level `none`. New: `apps/plugin/src/prune-figma.ts`, `apps/plugin/test-prune.ts`. Edited: `apps/plugin/src/{messages.ts, main.ts}`, `apps/plugin/tsconfig.main.json` (include the new module), `apps/plugin/package.json` (test script), `apps/studio/src/{write-adapter.ts, main.ts}`. Editing `apps/studio/src` is how the plugin gets UI — the iframe IS the shared studio app (one UI, no fork), the same path Apply and the component build take.

**GATES.** Full `npm run verify`: 60/60 gates reached a verdict, all PASS. No gate added or moved — a delete the designer triggers is an action, not an assertion; `test-prune.ts` rides the existing `plugin-test` gate.

## (2026-09-18) — reconcile.ts: normalize the brand ROOT before comparing — clean file was 100% false WRONG-TOKEN (#1522)

**STATUS: LANDED. TOOLS-ONLY (`tools/binding-audit/reconcile.ts`) — no engine code, def, gate, baseline, or emitted `out/**` artifact changed; ENGINE and CONTRACT both STAND. Measurement harness, NOT a gate — gate count stays 60. Follow-up of #1511.**

**THE BUG.** Run against a CLEAN, correct projection, `--reconcile` reported **5,433 WRONG-TOKEN / 0 MATCH** in the owner's 2026-09-18 QA (live NB file, 8,622 nodes / 21 sets) — a 100% false-positive rate. Every WRONG-TOKEN had the identical shape: `got ads/color/interactive/primary/fill/rest · want color/interactive/primary/fill/rest`, differing ONLY by the leading `ads/` brand root. Not drift — a uniform normalization difference.

**ROOT CAUSE (the whole diagnosis, and why the fix is small).** `reconcile.ts` did no variable-name normalization. The two sides sit on OPPOSITE sides of the #1097 rename. The expected **ledger** is built from `figmaAnatomyPlan`, which is **pre-materialization** — root-less names (`color/...`). The **live file** is **post-materialization**: `materialization-renames.ts:228` (namespace-and-core-tier, #1097) maps `name → ${root}/${name}`, *adding* the brand root, and `test.ts:120` asserts that as intended. `--reconcile` (#1511) is newer than the rename but inherited the root-less ledger, so it compared names from two sides of the same rename. The whole 5,433 differ by exactly one leading segment; strip it and the same file is 5,433 MATCH · 0 WRONG-TOKEN.

**THE FIX — derive the root, never hardcode it (it is a lever).** `reconcile()` now normalizes the brand root before comparing. `deriveRoot(ledger, export)` derives the root the SAME way #1097 defines it: **the leading segment the materialization ADDED** — present on the file's bound names but ABSENT from the ledger's own top-level groups (`color`). Keying off the ledger's groups is what tells a real brand root (`ads`) apart from a ledger group a root-less export leads with (`color`): a root-less export derives NO root and normalizes to a no-op, which is why the pre-existing root-less selftest arms still hold unchanged. It is **modal** among candidates, so a lone drifted bind under a different first segment cannot outvote the real root and its drift still surfaces. `stripRoot` removes only that derived prefix — a name NOT wearing the root is left intact, so a bind un-rooted or rooted differently still mismatches rather than being silently normalized. Brand-agnostic: works for `ads`/`hds`/`wds`/`nbds`/`prism`, no `BRAND_ROOTS` lookup and no live-brand knowledge (the reconciler is brand-invariant by construction — the plan carries names, not values).

**WHY STRIP THE FILE SIDE, NOT ADD TO THE LEDGER.** The issue offered either. Adding the materialized root to the ledger needs the SAME root the engine materialized with, i.e. knowing which brand the file is — the reconciler cannot know that and stays brand-invariant. Deriving the added segment from the export and stripping it needs no brand knowledge and no per-brand table, so it is the smaller, brand-agnostic move.

**TEETH PRESERVED (docs/34 — normalization must not mask drift).** Two new `--selftest` arms, both built from the LIVE ledger (never stale against a hand-written fixture): (1) *root-prefixed but correct → all MATCH* — the exact class that was 100% WRONG-TOKEN, now proven to reconcile clean; (2) *root-prefixed with one wrong → exactly one WRONG-TOKEN by name* — a single perturbed bind under the same root still surfaces, so the root strip does not swallow real drift. The four original arms (all-correct, one-wrong-but-valid, one-blanked, one-stray, plus one-uncovered-EXTRA) are unchanged and still pass. End-to-end over a synthesized full rooted export (5,558 rooted binds, mimicking the live file): 5,558 MATCH · 0 WRONG-TOKEN clean; corrupt one bind → exactly 1 WRONG-TOKEN by name.

**SCOPE — no contract, no engine, no emitted artifact.** `version.ts` untouched; `tools/` is scanned by no gate. One file changed: `tools/binding-audit/reconcile.ts` (`deriveRoot` + `stripRoot` helpers, the normalized comparison, two selftest arms). No gate added or moved — a live-file reconciler is a tool, not an assertion (`tools/CLAUDE.md`); gate count stays 60.

**GATES.** Full `npm run verify`: 60/60 gates reached a verdict, all PASS. `reconcile.ts --selftest`: 7/7 arms pass.

**NOT TOUCHED.** #1367 and #1385 are out of this lane's scope.

## (2026-09-18) — binding-audit: live-file RECONCILE — diff a real Figma file's actual binds vs the expected ledger (#1511)

**STATUS: LANDED. TOOLS-ONLY (`tools/binding-audit/`) — no engine code, def, gate, baseline, or emitted `out/**` artifact changed; ENGINE and CONTRACT both STAND. Measurement harness, NOT a gate — gate count stays 60. Follow-up of #1499.**

**THE GAP IT CLOSES.** #1499's `audit.ts` audits the ENGINE's emission (correct by construction) and can print the expected per-member ledger (`--ledger`). What it could not do is check a LIVE Figma file against that ledger: whether every node is bound to the EXACT correct token. The console script the owner ran during QA found nodes with NO variable bound, but never checked whether the bound ones point at the RIGHT variable. The real QA risk is a live file drifting from the engine's intent — a manual rebind, a stale projection, a wrong swap — and WRONG-TOKEN is the class that had no check.

**THE CHANGE — two halves that share one documented interface.** (1) A read-only **console export snippet** (documented in `tools/binding-audit/README.md`) the owner pastes into Figma; it walks the selected projected component sets and dumps, per node, its member-relative name-path and each bindable field's ACTUAL bound variable resolved to its NAME (or `UNBOUND`) as small, versioned JSON (`{format:'prism3-binding-export', version:1, nodes:[…]}`). (2) A **reconcile mode** — `npx tsx tools/binding-audit/audit.ts --reconcile <export.json>` (logic in the new `reconcile.ts`) — ingests that JSON and diffs it against the ledger, reporting per `(component, member, node, slot)`: **MATCH / WRONG-TOKEN** (got X, want Y — the check that did not exist) **/ UNBOUND / EXTRA / UNKNOWN-NODE**, plus a **COVERAGE** summary. Partial exports are normal, so a coordinate ABSENT from the export is reported as *not covered*, never as UNBOUND — only a node the export carries with that field `UNBOUND` is an UNBOUND finding.

**THE MATCHING KEY (the one subtle diagnosis, and why the fix is small).** `(component, member, node, field)` off the projection's deterministic name-path — set name = `def.id`, member = the variant-coordinate string, field ∈ {fills, strokes, descendantFills}. The node path is **member-relative** (member root = `/`), and this is load-bearing: the plugin converts the plan's root frame (`container`/`glyph`) IN PLACE into the member component and renames it to the coordinate (`createComponentFromNode` + `comp.name = spec.name` in `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts`), so the live member IS the plan root. The ledger stores that root name as its first path segment (`/container/icon`); the reconciler strips it (`memberRelative`) so it lines up with a live walk that starts AT the member, and the snippet emits member-relative paths directly. A node the ledger cannot place → UNKNOWN-NODE, never a crash. **This is exactly the coordinate the #1499 README's in-console diff got wrong** (it compared a member-root-relative `/icon` against the ledger's `/container/icon` and would have reported every node unbound) — that companion is replaced by the export→reconcile split, whose diff half is fixture-tested apart from any live file.

**INDEPENDENCE / DRY (docs/34).** The ledger builder is extracted to `ledger.ts` so `--ledger` (what a live file is diffed against) and `--reconcile` (the diff) share ONE builder and cannot drift — a reconciler that rebuilt the ledger its own way could silently disagree with the snippet on a coordinate, the exact defect the ledger exists to catch. `reconcile()` is pure (ledger + export → result), so the round-trip proves the diff logic with no Figma in the loop.

**ACCEPTANCE — the fixture round-trip.** `reconcile.ts --selftest` builds four scenarios from the LIVE ledger (never stale against a hand-written fixture) and asserts each verdict in isolation: all-correct → all MATCH; one wrong-but-valid → exactly one WRONG-TOKEN by name; one blanked → one UNBOUND; one stray node → one UNKNOWN-NODE (plus one uncovered field → one EXTRA). It exits non-zero on any mismatch. A committed `fixtures/example-export.json` (a partial `icon-button` export seeded to hit every verdict) backs the README's worked example (export → reconcile → report), reproducible via `--reconcile`. Both are self-checks the author runs, NOT wired into `ci.yml` — a live file is not in CI, so the tool answers and exits 0 and the gate count stays 60.

## (2026-09-18) — ADD `radio-group`, the single-select twin of `checkbox-group` (#1469)

**STATUS: LANDED. ENGINE 0.117.0 → 0.118.0 (rebased past #1474); CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0. Owner-directed during QA (2026-09-17) — `radio` had a row but "Radio Group: None available" in the QA build status; this builds the deferred #901 companion now that `radio-row` exists.**

**THE CHANGE.** A new projected component `radio-group` (`RadioGroup`): a `field-label` above a vertical stack of `radio-row`s, for choosing EXACTLY ONE from a bounded set. It is `checkbox-group`'s single-select twin — modeled on `components/checkbox-group.ts` part-for-part, composing the already-collapsed Row (`radio-row` projects a size-only 3-member set since #1348) so it inherits the Row's collapse rather than `radio-control`'s 36-member explosion. The nest chain is four deep (`focus-ring` ← `radio-control` ← `radio-row` ← `radio-group`), the same shape `checkbox-group` has one family over. Files: `components/radio-group.ts` (new), registered in `components/index.ts` after `radioRow` on composition order.

**AUTO-LAYOUT PARITY (the mechanical half — #1475 / PR #1504).** The #1475 audit measured `checkbox-group` host-truth and found Prism 2's `radio-button-group.json` is BYTE-FOR-BYTE the same auto-layout as `checkbox-group.json` (same VERTICAL root, same `label` container, same `padding {8,8,0,0}`, rows `FILL`) — Prism 2 already treats them as one shape. So `radio-group` mirrors `checkbox-group` AS IT STANDS: root `container` VERTICAL `sizing {x:fill, y:hug}`; `gap: size.{size}.gap` (the provisional [HELD] inter-row gap); block `pad-y`=`space.100` (8), inline `pad-x`=`space.0` (0); a nested `field-label` (secondary·bold·required-on) size-followed; three `nest-fixed` `radio-row`s following `size`. Verified against `reference/Prism2/component-specs/radio-button-group.json` directly (root width 320, VERTICAL, HUG, padding 8/8/0/0).

**THE ONLY DELTAS ARE WHAT SINGLE-SELECT SEMANTICS FORCE (not design — encoded, per the brief).** `value`/`defaultValue`/`onChange` are SCALAR (`string`, exactly-one) where `checkbox-group` owns an array; `role="radiogroup"` not `group`; the group is a SINGLE tab stop with roving tabindex + arrow navigation (the opposite of checkbox-group, and radio's headline keyboard difference); the shared `name` is LOAD-BEARING (enforces browser-level exclusivity, a row setting its own breaks it) rather than a submission convenience; and there is NO select-all (a multi-select affordance that does not apply to radio). The single-select a11y is encoded in `accessibility` + `anatomy.codeOnly`, the way the field defs encode theirs — Figma has no accessibility tree, so none of it is projectable.

**OPEN DECISION FOR THE OWNER (carried unchanged from `checkbox-group`, per #1475).** The audit's guidance is explicit: `checkbox-group`'s auto-layout is itself an open question on ONE row — the group hugs its width and its rows do not fill it, where Prism 2 gives a fixed-320 root with `FILL` rows, because the projection cannot emit cross-axis child FILL (`layoutAlign: STRETCH`), filed as **#1503**. `radio-group` COPIES that model deliberately so the two match by SHARING one resolution — building it to a different width model is the one outcome that guarantees they never match. If the owner decides fixed-320-and-fill (Prism 2 parity) or hug-and-stretch (STRETCH support), that lands on `checkbox-group` first and `radio-group` follows. **No NEW design/composition choice was invented here** — the single-select model is inherent to radio, the auto-layout mirrors checkbox-group, and every [HELD] fork (the size axis as a generalization, the provisional inter-row gap, the group error visual, the variable row count) is checkbox-group's, inherited rather than re-decided.

**SCOPE — ENGINE-ONLY, CONTRACT UNMOVED.** A new component-set NAME is the projected Figma surface, not a DTCG token-name path, and no component id lives in the versioned contract (docs/30, #1252/#1347). `token-contract --check` confirms level `none` (guaranteed 598 unchanged) — CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0. ENGINE bumps 0.117.0 → 0.118.0 because the projected surface grows a def (`lint-component-surface` tracks it). No emitted `out/**` VALUE moves: the group paints nothing and adds no token, so `out/**` restamps only `$extensions.generator.version` 0.117.0 → 0.118.0.

**BASELINES.** `schema/component-surface.json` `--accept`ed after the forward ENGINE bump (`radio-group`: no set → 3 members; every other def byte-identical). `schema/paint-census.json` `--accept`ed (`radio-group`: 3 members / 0 assignments in both `set` and `grid` — the empty-tree sha, mirroring `checkbox-group`, because the group paints nothing). `schema/token-contract.json` `--accept`ed as a stamp-only `engineVersion` sync (the #1470/#1476 precedent: the ENGINE bump flips the check's `informationalOnly` branch on; the inverse-overlay conditional-path churn in that diff is PRE-EXISTING and independent of this change — no guaranteed path moved, level `none`).

**REGISTERS UPDATED (docs/34 scope floors — a new size-axis/projecting/group def must join them).** `lint-axis-values` (the `size` canonical `defs` list — REQUIRED: an undeclared/unlisted axis pair fails the gate by name), `lint-hit-target` (`EXCLUDED` map, radio-group is a group container whose tap targets are the nested rows — REQUIRED: every def must be measured or excluded), `lint-rung-names` (`MUST_COVER`), `lint-standalone-floor` (`MUST_PROJECT`). Also removed the stale `radio-group` FORWARD-REFERENCE alias from `radio-row` (`aliases`) — it was a placeholder for the not-yet-built group, which #1469 built; `radio-group` now resolves to the group, not the row. Component `aliases` are source metadata only (not emitted to `out/**`), so that removal moves no artifact.

**GATES + BY-NAME MUTATION (docs/34).** Full `npm run verify`: 60/60 gates reached a verdict, all PASS. Two by-name mutations proving a gate catches a radio-group regression, each restored via `git checkout --`:
- `lint-component-surface` — mutating `radio-group`'s `variantAxes` to add an axis (member count 3 → 9) fails BY NAME: *"surface/radio-group: 3 → 9 members … the projected surface moved"*.
- `lint-paint` — giving `radio-group` a paint binding (so it stops being paint-empty) fails BY NAME: the census `radio-group` `set`/`grid` assignments move off 0, flagged *"radio-group … census mismatch"*.

## (2026-09-18) — Binding-audit tool: expected part→variable ledger + unbound / mis-bound detection (#1499)

**STATUS: PR open on branch `lane/1499-binding-audit`. Tools-only (`tools/binding-audit/`) — NO engine/token/surface change, NO version bump, NO new gate. Owner-requested (QA 2026-09-18): "an audit to find any unbound or incorrectly bound tokens … it's too much for me to be checking all token binds."**

**THE MOTIVATION.** The owner found unbound and mis-bound tokens by hand during QA — the icon-button glyph binding `interactive.<family>.text.*` instead of `.icon.*` (fixed as #1471) is the motivating case — and wanted it systematized. The load-bearing half is *bound to the WRONG token*: a console pass over a live Figma file sees bound-vs-unbound but not mis-bound, so the tool builds the EXPECTED binding map from the defs/projection and diffs the ACTUAL emission against it.

**WHAT IT IS.** `tools/binding-audit/audit.ts`, a measurement harness (reports, exits 0). Three outputs, per #1499: (1) the EXPECTED `(component, member, node, slot) → bound-variable` ledger, walked out of `figmaAnatomyPlan` over every def's Figma set — brand-invariant, because the plan carries variable NAMES not resolved values; `--ledger` emits it as JSON for a live-file diff. (2) UNBOUND — a declared color bind the projector returns at no coordinate (the baked-where-it-should-bind class; ring *nominations* excluded by shape, not by copying lint-paint's exemption list). (3) MIS-BOUND — a slot bound to a role whose family mismatches its kind, read off the plan node (`FRAME` fills = surface, strokes = border; `TEXT` fills = text ink; any `descendantFills` = glyph ink) against `ALLOWED` (slot-kind → role-family). README carries the read-only Figma-console companion that diffs a live file's `boundVariables` against the ledger.

**THE KEY DESIGN CALL — TOOL, NOT GATE — and why it is not laziness.** The mis-bind check is a HEURISTIC. `ALLOWED` encodes what a slot-kind SHOULD bind from design semantics, but the corpus carries deliberate cross-slot bindings a first-principles map would flag: the disabled outline edge binds `color.disabled.icon` not `color.disabled.border` (#1349, pinned BY NAME in `test.ts`); the switch thumb paints `on-fill`; the switch on/off glyphs are tinted with the track's `fill` role. Those are decisions, not defects, so `ALLOWED` admits them WITH a stated reason, and a run over today's corpus is clean. A gate here would either re-encode those exemptions (duplicating `test.ts`/`lint-paint.ts`) or assert a bare zero over a heuristic — so per `tools/CLAUDE.md` it stays a tool. #1499 anticipates this: "if a specific mis-binding later becomes a contract, a gate enforces it separately." No gate ⇒ `verify.ts`/`ci.yml`/CONTRIBUTING §3/PR template/CLAUDE.md §4 untouched (lint-doc-gates stays green — the gate list did not move).

**INDEPENDENCE (docs/34), even without a gate.** EXPECTED (`ALLOWED`, the reachability sentinels) is authored apart from the defs it checks; the mis-bind map is deliberately NOT built by asking the projector to resolve each key and comparing to itself. Reachability uses a per-key sentinel so a returned variable names exactly ONE key even where two keys share a real ref (the collision that let #784's own defect pass a ref-matching check — reused here).

**MUTATION-PROVEN BY NAME.** Reintroducing the #1471 defect (repointing icon-button's `outline.icon` from `interactive.<family>.icon.rest` back to `.text.rest`) makes the tool name it precisely: `icon-button | /container/icon [glyph-ink] -> color/interactive/primary/text/rest family=text ×120`, across all three icon-button components on both grounds (6 findings). Reverted in place via the editor, not `git checkout` (per CLAUDE.md's mutation-restore hazard); `git diff` on the def is empty afterward.

**WHAT IT SURFACED — nothing new to file.** 0 mis-bound. 1 unbound: `field-message default.icon → color.icon.secondary`, which is the code-only category-(b) case `lint-paint.ts` already documents (the default status projects no glyph member; the fix if it ever matters is to delete the key, not widen anything). It is intentional, so no issue is filed; the tool correctly surfaces it as "verify intended," and it is. The empirically-checked corpus vocabulary (147 distinct node-type × field × role triples over 20,644 assignments) is what grounded `ALLOWED` and `familyWord`.

**TRAP FOR THE RE-VERIFIER.** The audit's cleanliness is load-bearing on `ALLOWED`'s admissions. If a future change removes one of the pinned cross-slot bindings (say #1349's disabled-edge decision reverts), the corresponding `ALLOWED` admission becomes a stale hole — but this being a tool, nothing fails; read the admission reasons against `test.ts`'s pins when either moves. The switch/#1349 admissions are the ONLY reason the healthy corpus reports zero; they are not tolerances.

**VERIFICATION.** Full `npm run verify` — 60/60 gates reached a verdict, all PASS (tools/ is not wired into CI, so the tool itself is exercised by hand: default run, `--json`, `--ledger`, and the mutation above). See the PR body.

**WHAT.** Owner QA (#1475) flagged three auto-layout items — `field-message`, `checkbox-group`, `image-placeholder` — plus an implicit "does `checkbox-group` match Prism 2, and what should `radio-group` (#1469) copy?" The audit measures every projected component's auto-layout **host-truth** (project via `figmaAnatomySet`, apply through the real `applyComponentPlan` against `component-shim.ts`, read back off the built members) and compares to `reference/Prism2/component-specs/*.json`. Every claim quotes a number from a run. Report: `docs/superpowers/qa-2026-09-18-autolayout-audit.md` (the harness is in its appendix; it is NOT committed, per docs-only).

**THE DIAGNOSIS THAT MADE IT SMALL.** Two of the three flagged items and the whole systemic gap reduce to one engine fact: `sizingMode` maps only `'fixed' → FIXED`, so `sizing: 'fill'` and `'hug'` are the **same** projection (both `AUTO`), and there is no def field for cross-axis child FILL (`layoutAlign: 'STRETCH'` — Figma deprecated the `MIN|CENTER|MAX` form; `component-schema.ts:513`). So Prism 2's fixed-320-root + `FILL`-children shape projects as hug-both-axes + no-stretch across `checkbox-group`, `text-field`, `select`, `field-message`. Main-axis fill already matches (label `layoutGrow:1` via `wrap`, host-verified by #1424); only the cross axis — the width of a vertical stack — diverges. Filed as #1503 (capability gap + owner design call), which #1469 inherits.

**ITEM 3 WAS NOT A DEFECT IN THE COMPONENT.** `image-placeholder` binds one nominal side (`width→container.narrow`=720) and locks the ratio, so `1:1`/`4:3`/`16:9` measure 720×720 / 720×540 / 720×405 — correct, and the `targetAspectRatio` reads back 1.0000/1.3333/1.7778. The footprint check groups by `footprintVaries` (+ slot/size), which the def leaves `[]`, so all three ratios share one empty group and two get flagged `(same )` — an empty group name the QA read as "same width." Fix is one line: `footprintVaries: ['ratio']` (the #1010 mechanism `field-message` already uses). Filed as #1502.

**WHAT MATCHED.** `checkbox-group`'s block padding (`space.100`=8), inline padding (`space.0`=0) and vertical hug reproduce Prism 2 exactly; direction and icon-order match on `field-message`; main-axis fill matches on the rows. The divergences that remain are the width model (systemic) and two `field-message` choices (cross-axis `MIN` vs Prism 2 `CENTER`; gap 6 vs 4) that are the owner's design calls, flagged in the report, not filed.

**TRAP FOR THE RE-VERIFIER.** The audit is the **offline** arm — it proves what `applyComponentPlan` writes, not what Figma keeps (accept-and-discard is out of reach; `tools/component-roundtrip/` is the real-host arm, not in CI). "Hugs its width" is read off `counterAxisSizingMode`, not a measured box. The report's "what a programmatic pass cannot see" section states the limits.

**GATES.** Docs-only under `docs/` — outside the scan scope of every engine gate (`lint-us-english`/`lint-voice` measure 0 `docs/` files by design). Ran `lint-us-english` + `lint-voice` after the studio + plugin builds anyway (per #1475): PASS, and the diff touches no gate subject. No `npm run verify` version churn — nothing under `out/**`, `schema/**`, or `version.ts` moved.

**Files.** `docs/superpowers/qa-2026-09-18-autolayout-audit.md` (new), `docs/00-progress.md` (this entry). No code.

## (2026-09-18) — TextField PROJECTS into Figma: anatomy + figmaProperties, status-led validation (#1494)

**STATUS: LANDED (#1498). ENGINE 0.113.0 → 0.114.0 (rebased past #1486); CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0 (stamp-only `--accept`). Owner-confirmed projection decisions.**

**THE GAP.** TextField was a complete def (props, states, variants, paintKeys, tokens, a11y, docs, ai) with NO `anatomy` block and no `figmaProperties` — it named its parts only in `composition`, so it reached zero Figma members while every sibling field part (`field-label`, `field-message`, `select`) projected. Select is the proven template for a composed field, so this brings TextField up to select's shape verbatim, with the three field-specific differences the owner confirmed.

**THE STATUS-LED ERROR REWORK (why, and it is the load-bearing change).** Validation had been folded into the STATE axis (`error` was a state). That was the pre-projection shortcut a single unprojected axis could afford; it is wrong once the def projects, because `error` co-occurs with rest/hover/focus rather than replacing one of them — a state cannot do that. So validation became the `status` VARIANT axis `[default, error, warning, success]`, the SAME four values `field-message` carries, so the nested message follows it by name (`nest-fixed` `follow`, a same-name same-value passthrough). `error` LEFT `states`; the paint grammar became select's `['{status}.{slot}.{state}', '{slot}.{state}', '{slot}']` (status-led first so the error swap wins over the interactive progression); the state-led `border.error` became status-led `error.border.{state}` bound PER non-disabled state → `color.border.danger` (border-ONLY swap; `default`/`warning`/`success` bind no status border and fall through — the message carries them). `border.rest` became the bare `border` rest fallback (rest projects as `state=undefined`, so a `.rest`-suffixed key would be unreachable — select's exact reason).

**THE ANATOMY.** Root `container` (column) → nested `field-label` (nest-exposed, exposing size/emphasis/weight) · `control` (the bordered input box, `role:target`, `paintSlots [overlay,fill,border]`, `justify:space-between` so the trailing affix pins to the trailing edge, `height→min-height`) holding `content` (leadingVisual + text) + `trailingVisual` + `focusRing` (absolute, `when:focus-visible`, nests `focus-ring`) · nested `field-message` (nest-fixed, `follow:['status']`, optional). Mirrors select part-for-part; the `focus-ring` COLOR token was DROPPED (the nested ring owns its stroke), which also retired TextField's `NESTED_WITHOUT_ANATOMY` entry (its anatomy landed, exactly as #910/#1221 retired checkbox/radio/switch).

**READ-ONLY IS PROJECTED (the field state select lacks).** The projected `stateAxis` is `[rest, hover, focus-visible, disabled, read-only]` — read-only keeps FULL-contrast `text.primary` over `border.secondary` (read-only ≠ disabled). So the projected surface is **status(4) × state(5) = 20 members** (select is 16). `pending` and `empty` stay in `states` (the code tier carries the spinner swap and the placeholder-ink re-point) but are admitted OUT of the projected axis via `anatomy.codeOnly`, each entry LEADING with the state name (figmaPropertyErrors' `admits` rule).

**THE TRAILING SLOT.** Select's disclosure chevron has no TextField analogue; TextField's trailing part is the clear/reveal AFFIX. Modeled exactly as the leading glyph — an optional `trailingVisual` swap slot painted the `icon` ink, a `trailingIcon` presence boolean + swap, pinned to the trailing edge by the control's `space-between`. A `codeOnly` note records that the real affix is an INTERACTIVE control (own tab stop + accessible name) that Figma projects only as the glyph. New projection props added to back the Figma properties: `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `showMessage` (mirroring select).

**SIZE IS NOT A VARIANTS AXIS (a forced call, worth recording).** The task framed `size` as a non-projected variants axis admitted in `codeOnly`. That is UNREPRESENTABLE for the `size` axis specifically: `size` is `figmaAnatomyPlan`'s positional argument, and `figmaAnatomySet` passes `undefined` for an unprojected size while `figmaAnatomyPlan` (#795 guard) THROWS on a declared-but-unprojected size (`text-field: no size was given, but the def declares sizes […]`). So the single-projected-size field is expressed exactly as select expresses it: `size` is a code-API PROP + the `size.{small,medium,large}.*` geometry tokens (kept), NOT a `variants` axis; the projected control binds the bare `md` geometry keys (`min-height`→`size.md.min-height`, the 44px #1437 floor). `style` (the other non-projected axis) is NOT positional, so it stays in `variants` and is admitted in `codeOnly` normally.

**VERSIONING.** Projected-component-surface change (#1252 case) → ENGINE bump 0.113.0 → 0.114.0 (rebased past #1486's 0.113.0). No emitted `out/**` value moves (components are not committed under `out/`), so committed artifacts move only their `$extensions.generator.version` stamp. CONTRACT STANDS at 11.3.0: TextField composes existing field tokens and adds NO new guaranteed token NAME (`token-contract --check` level `none`; stamp-only `--accept` synced the baseline's `engineVersion` field). Baselines regenerated + `--accept`ed: `schema/component-surface.json` (TextField no set → 20 members) and `schema/paint-census.json` (TextField enters the census — set 20/100, grid 28/140). Registers updated in the same PR: `lint-paint` PROVENANCE_EXCEPTIONS gains five `text-field|error.border.*` keys (status `error` → `danger` role); `lint-axis-values` moves text-field off the `size` set onto the `status` set; `lint-rung-names` LADDER_STATED_ONCE and `lint-hit-target` INTERACTIVE mark text-field single-size (like select/icon); `test.ts` TextField assertions and the `#1009` CENTRE_OK register updated for the new keys.

**GATE (docs/34, mutation-proven by name).** No new gate FILE — the existing paint/surface/scope gates were extended via regen + baselines. Verified they catch a TextField regression: repointing `error.border.rest` from `color.border.danger` to the resolving non-danger `color.field.border.rest` (the "careless rebind" shape lint-paint's own header names) fires **`lint-paint` census arm 2 BY NAME** — `census/text-field.set: paint hash … — the same count of assignments, pointing somewhere else`. Arm 1 (provenance) is exempt on that key and arm 3 (reachability) stays green, so only the independent census hash separates right from wrong here; restored in place (no `git checkout`), lint-paint green.

**A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT NOTED, NOT FIXED (one concern per PR).** `packages/engine/version.ts` line ~2978 carries a stray `>>>>>>> origin/main` merge-conflict marker, committed by #1480 (c3a5ae2 — the `+>>>>>>> origin/main` line is in that commit's diff). It sits INSIDE the changelog block comment, so it compiles and every gate is green over it, but it is real conflict noise in a shipped source file. Left untouched here (unrelated to #1494); should be filed and removed in its own change.

**VERIFICATION.** Full `npm run verify` — see the PR body. Engine `test.ts` 3807/0; `regen --check` byte-identical; `lint-paint`/`lint-component-surface`/`lint-hit-target`/`lint-axis-values`/`lint-rung-names` green; `token-contract --check` level `none`.

## (2026-09-18) — studio control-shape preset picker: selected card follows the #439 inset-ring pattern, not an outset ring (#1477)

**STATUS: PR open on branch `lane/1477-studio-selected`, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). Studio-surface only — no engine/token change, no version bump.** Owner QA find (2026-09-17).

**THE DEFECT (grounded, owner QA).** On the Size & radius page, the control-shape preset picker (Boxed / Hairline / Rounded / Pill) marked the SELECTED card with `cell.style.outline = '2px solid currentColor'` set inline in `paintControlShapePreview` (`apps/studio/src/main.ts`). An `outline` is painted OUTSIDE the border box, so the 2px ink ring sat tight against — and appeared to touch — the preview silhouette and the adjacent cell, reading like a stray focus ring rather than a considered selection affordance. It is exactly the treatment #439 rejected for the mode chip.

**THE PATTERN IT NOW MATCHES (#439, `styles.css` ~:823-835).** The app already has a decided selection treatment on `.mctx-b.on`: a `--panel` (white) ground + an ink border + an **INSET** 1px ring (`box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ink)`), deliberately chosen so selection is findable "without out-shouting the page," and deliberately inset because an outset ring painted outside the box gets clipped or collides. The preset card was doing the thing that note rejects.

**THE FIX (surgical, one specimen).** Replaced the two inline `cell.style.*` lines with a class toggle: the selected cell now carries `.on`, and the list carries a `rad-shapes` modifier (kept in the `rad-` scope so the mint law / `checkScope` accepts it without a `mix()`). Two CSS rules, scoped to `.rad-shapes` so the corner-radius ramp above — which shares `.rad-*` but never has a selected state — is untouched:
- `.rad-shapes .rad-cell` reserves a 1px **transparent** border + `--r-sm` radius + `11px 13px` padding, so selecting a card shifts NO layout and the ring can never touch the silhouette.
- `.rad-shapes .rad-cell.on` fills in `--panel` ground + `--ink` border + `inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ink)` — byte-for-byte the #439 treatment (2px of contiguous ink, entirely inside the border box).

**MODE COVERAGE.** This specimen paints from the studio-CHROME tokens (`--ink`/`--panel`), which are a single fixed light palette (`:root` only — the studio UI has no dark/HC chrome; the mode bar re-resolves the *preview*, not the chrome). So the selected card renders identically in light, dark and HC — verified by a Playwright probe reading the computed style of the selected `.rad-cell.on`: `outline: none`, `box-shadow: rgb(24,24,27) 0 0 0 1px inset`, `border: 1px solid rgb(24,24,27)`, `background: rgb(255,255,255)`, one selected cell of four.

**VERIFICATION.** Studio gates green (`typecheck` · `test` · `build` · `test:smoke` · `check:ignore` · `lint:contrast`), and full `npm run verify` — **60/60 gates PASS**. No new gate: this is a visual affordance change to one specimen, verified by the existing smoke suite (which drives the built `dist`) plus the computed-style probe above; there is no falsifiable engine invariant to mutate.

**Files.** `apps/studio/src/main.ts` (`paintControlShapePreview`: inline outline → `.on` class + `rad-shapes` list modifier) and `apps/studio/src/styles.css` (the two `.rad-shapes` rules + the #1477/#439 rationale comment). No engine, token, or version change.

## (2026-09-18) — link interactive states made perceptible (perceptual-interval walk) + a `pressed` link state (#1486)

**STATUS: PR open on branch `lane/1486-link-perceptibility`, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). ENGINE 0.112.0 → 0.113.0 (rebased); CONTRACT 11.2.0 → 11.3.0 (MINOR — 4 guaranteed name ADDs). Owner-decided.**

**THE DEFECT (grounded, owner QA 2026-09-17).** `modes.ts` `LINK_STATES` was `default/hover/visited/focused` — no `pressed`. The engaged link states stepped the action ramp a FIXED **1 rung (hover) / 2 rungs (visited)** off `linkBase` (`linkStateCand`). `linkBase` is forced deep — a saturated brand red must clear **4.5:1 AS TEXT**, which pins it near the ramp end — and the ramp COMPRESSES perceptually there, so 1–2 fixed rungs are a barely-visible step (the owner's case: 950 → 900 → 850 indistinguishable). The floor is *slack* at the extreme (~8–10:1), so the fix is step SIZE vs ramp compression, NOT the floor or the direction (do not reverse the base off the extreme — that is a brand-colour change).

**THE FIX — a PERCEPTIBILITY-TARGETED adaptive walk (owner-decided; link stays a single GLOBAL link, NOT per-family).** `walk` gains an optional `percept` qualifier: a step counts only if it clears the floor AND is ≥ `LINK_STATE_DE` (CIEDE2000) from the PREVIOUS qualifying state (`prev` starts at the origin, advances to each qualifying step — an EVEN perceptual ladder). Near an extreme this consumes MORE rungs to reach a visible change; a healthy ramp is unaffected in spirit. **Byte-identical for every non-link walk** — `percept` is undefined there, the ΔE test short-circuits, and `prev` is never read; fills/outlines are untouched. `LINK_STATE_DE = 7.0`, a TUNED CONSTANT not a lever yet (the `STATE_RUNGS` precedent — no brand has asked to tune it, a lever costs a manifest entry + a studio control + a documented contract, and the derivation must be right first). Calibrated by rendering the corpus: 7.0 lands every corpus link on a clean two-rung engagement step (ΔE ≈ 7.5–9.5 ≈ ΔL* ≈ 9–11, squarely the issue's ~ΔL* 8–12).

**DEPTH LADDER default → hover → pressed → visited.** hover (1st qualifying step) and pressed (2nd) are the EVEN engagement ladder — a link's rest → hover → pressed, mirroring a button; visited (3rd) sits beyond as the deepest, most-settled state; `focused` stays a colour no-op (the ring carries focus); `visited` stays. `pressed` is APPENDED to `LINK_STATES` so the existing four keep their emission order. All four twins move together — `text.link.*`, `icon.link.*`, and the `inverse.` twins of both — because `buildContent` runs for the text and icon profiles over the page and inverse grounds, so adding `pressed` to `LINK_STATES` adds exactly 4 guaranteed names.

**GRACEFUL DEGRADATION where the ramp CANNOT afford three ΔE-7 steps** (a near-black brand's action ramp, or an HC mode pinning the base near the extreme under a 7:1 floor). Two composed fallbacks, both LINKS-ONLY so fills stay byte-identical: (1) `walk`'s perceptual last-resort is the DEEPEST floor-clearing step in the forward direction (monotonic + maximally separated) rather than the plain `50·steps` landing, which could undershoot a deeper found state and read out of order; (2) the ladder prefers the perceptual walk but, if it collides (two states on one rung), falls back to the plain floor-clearing walk for ALL THREE — the pre-#1486 counting, distinct by construction — so link states NEVER collide. The strong perceptual promise is kept wherever the ramp affords it (asserted on the shipping corpus), and relaxed to distinct + floor-clearing where it does not.

**THE GATE (`test.ts` block L-04, docs/34).** Reads the EMITTED colours back and measures their CIEDE2000 separation against its OWN authored floor `LINK_PERCEPT_FLOOR = 6.0` — deliberately BELOW the engine's 7.0 tuning and ABOVE what the old fixed 1-/2-rung walk produced (~4.5), and it must NOT import `LINK_STATE_DE` (the gate's promise and the engine's tuning are two independent numbers). `deltaE2000` is a shared PRIMITIVE (like `contrast` in every contrast gate), not a shared derivation — the two sides compared are the emitted artifact and a hand-authored floor. Coverage: the 4 shipping brands + 6 stress fixtures × modes. ALL modes: 4 distinct link states, each clears its own contrast floor. BASE modes (light/dark): consecutive depth states ≥ 6 ΔE — the strong promise. HC is excluded from the strong floor and says so (the ramp physically cannot supply three ΔE-6 steps under a 7:1 bar), not silently skipped. A self-check feeds the ΔE detector a near-identical pair (must flag) and a separated pair (must pass); a non-vacuity floor asserts the sweep actually read ≥16 base ladders. **Mutation (docs/34, by name):** removing the perceptibility qualifier (`clearsPercept → true`) fires L-04 by name on every base-mode pair across all ten brands (ΔE ~4–5 < 6), AND the NB figma divergence table fires ("divergence CHANGED"). Restored; 3799/0.

**NB REGRESSION — the sixth `NB_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` group.** NB hand-authored its engaged link states at the conservative fixed rungs, so the perceptual walk diverges from the frozen real-NB Token Press export in every mode (hover +1→+2, visited +2→+3 qualifying steps; text and icon move together because NB's `iconContrast` is 'text'). Recorded as 16 from→to divergence entries (NOT by rewriting the frozen fixture — that would make it self-referential, docs/34 shape 6), same owner stance already on record for the relaxed fills: "NB's own conservatism showing up as a regression target, not a reason to keep the bar." `link/default` is UNCHANGED (the base is not walked) and stays byte-checked; the new `pressed` leaf is an engine addition NB's export predates, so it lives in `ENGINE_ADDED_VARS` (text + icon), not the divergence table.

**VERSIONING.** ENGINE 0.109.0 → 0.110.0 (emitted link-state VALUES move in every brand + a new `pressed` token). CONTRACT 11.2.0 → 11.3.0 MINOR: `token-contract --check` reported exactly 4 ADDs (`color.{text,icon}.link.pressed` + their `inverse.` twins, guaranteed 594 → 598), level MINOR; the baseline was `--accept`ed only AFTER raising `CONTRACT_VERSION` (the guard refuses otherwise). The baseline is never a `regen.ts` artifact. The perceptibility value moves carry no contract (the existing link names are unchanged). `regen --check` byte-clean at 108 artifacts.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** A `walk` result is a `Cand` (`{path, rgb}`, NO `.num`) while `linkBase` is a `RatedNum` (has `.num`); the ladder's distinctness compares by `.path`, not `.num` (an early draft compared `.num` and silently fell back to the plain ladder everywhere, erasing the whole fix while every test still passed — caught only by re-probing the emitted values). HC modes legitimately REFLECT off the ramp end, so a degenerate near-black brand may deepen then lighten — the gate asserts distinct + floor there, NOT monotonicity.

**Files.** `packages/engine/modes.ts` (`LINK_STATES` +`pressed`, `LINK_STATE_DE`, `walk` percept qualifier + deepest-clearing fallback, the ladder in `buildContent`), `packages/engine/version.ts` (both bumps + changelogs), `packages/engine/test.ts` (L-04 gate, the extended distinctness check, the sixth `NB_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` group, `ENGINE_ADDED_VARS` +pressed), `apps/studio/src/main.ts` (link-roles UI copy), `packages/engine/schema/token-contract.json` (`--accept`), and the regen artifacts (`out/**`, `component-surface.json`, etc.). Full `npm run verify`: see the PR body.

## (2026-09-17) — emit reusable Figma GRID STYLES, one per breakpoint (#1480)

**STATUS: branch `lane/1480-grid-styles` off main, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). ENGINE 0.111.0 → 0.112.0 (rebased); CONTRACT STANDS at 11.2.0 (stamp-only `--accept`). Owner-approved (reusable Grid Styles, not specimen frames).**

**THE GAP — genuinely absent, by prior decision.** Layout emitted as FLOAT variables ONLY (`emit-figma-dims.ts` `buildFigmaLayout`, the `layout` collection: `grid/columns`, `grid/gutter`, `grid/margin`, `container/*`, `breakpoint/*` per breakpoint mode). Those numbers are the responsive source of truth, but a variable cannot BECOME a live Figma column grid — **Figma has no variable→layout-grid binding** — so a designer got the numbers and no applicable grid. Zero `createGridStyle`/`layoutGrids` code existed anywhere. The owner chose reusable **Grid Styles** (one per breakpoint) over specimen frames.

**THE CAPABILITY.** A new emitted STYLE surface, the fourth style class beside effect/paint/text. `buildFigmaGridStyles` (`emit-figma-styles.ts`) → a `grid-styles.json` artifact per brand: one `Grid / <bp>` style per breakpoint, a `COLUMNS`/`STRETCH` layout grid whose `count`/`gutterSize`/`offset` are the breakpoint's columns/gutter/margin, sourced from the SAME layout data (`theme.layout.grid`). Names follow the auto breakpoint names, so a 2-breakpoint brand yields exactly `Grid / sm` + `Grid / md` (the #1479 interlink). Plan: `buildGridStylePlan` (`write-plan.ts`, sibling of `buildStylesPlan`). Executor: `apps/plugin/src/write-grid-styles.ts` (sibling of `write-text-styles.ts`) via `figma.createGridStyle()`, idempotent find-by-name, wired into the apply path in `main.ts` (the global `figma` structurally satisfies the `GridStylesApi` port) and driven offline by the `test-write-grid-styles.ts` shim.

**THE PLATFORM CONSTRAINT (called out in the design record — docs/10 item 4).** Figma grid styles are **STATIC**: they cannot mode-switch off a variable. So N breakpoints = **N separate grid styles**, coexisting with the numeric `layout` variable collection. Two representations of one dataset — the variables stay responsive-by-mode (the source of truth), the grid styles are the fixed, apply-able form. The overlay colour is baked (Figma's default column red at 10%): a grid style carries no themeable colour, so there is no variable binding and nothing the executor can miss.

**VERSIONING.** `out/**` GROWS by one artifact per brand (3 new `grid-styles.json`, EXPECTED_ARTIFACTS 108 → 111 in BOTH `verify.ts` and `ci.yml`) → ENGINE bump 0.109.0 → 0.110.0. CONTRACT STANDS at 11.2.0: a grid style is a Figma STYLE, not a token name — `buildContract` reads DTCG token trees and never sees it (`token-contract --check` level `none`; guaranteed count unchanged at 594). The baseline's `engineVersion` field is stamp-only synced by `--accept` (it refuses a real move; a `none` accept is the sanctioned stamp sync, the #1476 precedent). The baseline is NOT a `regen.ts` artifact.

**GATE (docs/34, by name + mutation-proven).** `test.ts` block `(19d)` asserts each breakpoint emits a `Grid / <bp>` COLUMNS/STRETCH style with the right `count`/`gutterSize`/`offset(margin)`. INDEPENDENCE (shape 1): the expected columns/gutter/margin are HAND-AUTHORED from theme.ts's DOCUMENTED layout contract (NB's default floors → sm..2xl; the `cols` 4/8/…/base ladder at base 12; the `GUTTER_PX`/`MARGIN_PX` ramps), NEVER read back from `theme.layout` or `buildFigmaLayout`. ## (2026-09-17) — `foreground.*` Figma scopes drop `TEXT_FILL` — a surface is not ink (#1484)

**STATUS: PR open on branch `lane/1484-foreground-scope`, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). ENGINE 0.110.0 → 0.111.0 (rebased onto #1485); CONTRACT STANDS at 11.2.0 (a Figma scope is emitted metadata, not a guaranteed token name — `token-contract --check` level `none`).** Owner QA find (2026-09-17, variable-scope review).

**THE BUG (grounded).** The `foreground` semantic color family carried Figma variable scopes **Frame + Shape + Text**. But `foreground.*` are on-color **SURFACE/fill** colors — the ground you paint UNDER on-color content — not ink (that is `text.*`). The stray `TEXT_FILL` wrongly offered every `foreground/*` variable in Figma's text-fill picker. Scope assignment is `emit-figma-color.ts`'s `COLOR_SCOPES` table (role-family → scopes), dispatched by `colorScopes` on `seg[1]`. The correct precedent is right there in the same table: `background`/`scrim`/`veil` are all `[FRAME_FILL, SHAPE_FILL]`, no Text.

**THE FIX.** One line: `COLOR_SCOPES.foreground` → `['FRAME_FILL', 'SHAPE_FILL']` (was `[..., 'TEXT_FILL']`). `foreground` now scopes like its surface twins, and `text.*` remains the only top-level color family that scopes as `TEXT_FILL`. No token value, no name, no projected component member moves — only the emitted `scopes` array on every brand's `color/foreground/*` Figma variables (16 vars × 4 modes × 4 brands). The `inverse.foreground.*` twin moves with it for free: `colorScopes` strips the `inverse` marker before dispatch (`seg.filter(...i===1 && s==='inverse')`), so `inverse.foreground.*` → `foreground` → the same surface scopes.

**GATE (docs/34 — a NEW by-name gate, and why the existing fixture gate could not catch this).** Added `test.ts` block **(e4)**: a per-role-family scope assertion over the top-level `COLOR_SCOPES` families (background/scrim/veil/foreground/text/icon/border), with the expected scope sets **hand-written as literals, deliberately NOT imported from `COLOR_SCOPES`** — deriving the oracle from the table it checks would be shape 2 (the DRY trap, `table === table`, unfalsifiable). It sits alongside the existing #1471 slot-scope gates (e/e2/e3 for interactive/disabled/field) — extended, not duplicated. **Why a new gate at all:** the frozen NB fixture (`fixtures/figma/nb`) is the real hand-built NB export, and it carries `foreground = FRAME/SHAPE/TEXT` — the very legacy mistake QA flagged. So the `scopes match fixture` gate is structurally blind to this class: matching the fixture here means being *wrong*. The engine now intentionally **diverges** from the frozen fixture on these scopes, recorded in `NB_KNOWN_SCOPE_DIVERGENCES` (16 entries, one fixture name per line, exact `nb → engine` scope sets, staleness-checked) rather than by editing the frozen fixture (shape 6: rewriting the fixture to agree would blind it to a real future regression). A `scopeDivHit` floor + a post-loop staleness `ok()` catch a waiver that no longer applies, as loudly as a missing one.

**MUTATION (by name, restored in-session).** Reverting `COLOR_SCOPES.foreground` back to include `TEXT_FILL` fires the new gate **by name**: `color role-families carry surface/ink/stroke scopes by family (#1484 …) — WRONG SCOPE: foreground (color/foreground/primary=["FRAME_FILL","SHAPE_FILL","TEXT_FILL"])`, and the scope-divergence staleness arm names all 16 vars. The `scopes match fixture` gate stays **green** under that mutation — which is the whole point: it agrees with the wrong fixture, and only the independent by-name literal gate separates right from wrong here. Restored: 3795/0.

**VERSIONING.** ENGINE bump (rebased 0.110.0 → 0.111.0 after #1485 took 0.110.0): the emitted `scopes` metadata on `out/figma/**` is an observable surface change (principle 5 — any behavior change), so `out/**`'s `$extensions.generator.version` restamps with it. CONTRACT STANDS at 11.2.0: a Figma scope is not a guaranteed token name; no name is added, removed, or retyped (`token-contract --check` level `none`; stamp-only `--accept` syncs the baseline's informational `engineVersion` field).

**Files.** `emit-figma-color.ts` (the one-line scope fix + comment), `test.ts` (the (e4) by-name gate + `NB_KNOWN_SCOPE_DIVERGENCES` waiver + staleness check), `version.ts` (ENGINE bump + changelog), `schema/token-contract.json` (stamp-only), and the regen artifacts (`out/figma/**` scope arrays, `out/*.tokens.json` version stamps). No new gate FILE (extends `test.ts`), so no `verify.ts`/`ci.yml`/gate-count change. Full `npm run verify`: 59/59 PASS.

## (2026-09-17) — the text-style cut binds a STRING variable, so condensed/width cuts are bindable in Figma (#1485)

**STATUS: branch `lane/1485-font-cut-bind` off main, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). ENGINE 0.109.0 → 0.110.0 (emitted `out/figma/**` moves — new STRING cut variables + text styles now bind `fontStyle`, and the DTCG `figma.binds`/`baked`/`note` metadata moves). CONTRACT STANDS at 11.2.0 (rebased; `token-contract --check` level `none`): the cut lives in Figma variables + `$extensions.prism3.facePin`, not a guaranteed DTCG token NAME — `$value` is unchanged.** Unblocks the New Balance condensed binding.

**THE MODEL, AS THE OWNER RESOLVED IT.** A Figma Text Style has ONE weight/style control. The engine used to bind it via the FLOAT weight-role variable (numeric, e.g. 300) and BAKE `fontStyle` beside it — but a numeric weight can never reach a WIDTH cut like *Light Condensed*, so a facePin (#1368) could only bake a literal: unthemeable, and unreachable from Figma's binding UI. #1485 binds that single control to a **STRING cut variable** holding the Figma style name instead (exactly what the owner did in Prism2). There is no dual-bind: the STRING is authoritative; the numeric weight-role FLOAT variable is **retained as parallel data** (still emitted in `core`, DTCG `$value.fontWeight` still aliases it) but is no longer bound on the Text Style.

**WHAT CHANGED.** `emit-figma-font.ts` now emits a STRING cut variable per distinct **(category, weight-role, italic)** slot — `<root>/core/font/style/<cat>/<role>[-italic]`, scope `FONT_STYLE`, value = the facePin verbatim or the weight-role's named-instance derivation (`fontStyleName`), computed by one `cutName` helper both the variable emission and `buildFigmaTextStyles` read (single source, no drift). `buildFigmaTextStyles` binds `fontStyle` to it and drops the `fontWeight` bind (now `{ bound: false, value: numeric }` — parallel data). `write-plan.ts` gains `fontStyleVar` and resolves the row's cut STRING from that variable's value (the same seam `fontFamilyPrimary` uses), dropping `fontWeightVar`. The plugin (`write-text-styles.ts`) and CLI paste (`materialise-to-figma.ts`) bind `fontStyle`, not `fontWeight`; `materialise` gains a `FONT_STYLE` scope code (`'y'`). `tree.ts`'s composite `figma.binds`/`baked`/`note` metadata updated (`fontWeight`→`fontStyle` in binds; `fontStyle` out of baked). NB has 9 cut slots; aurora/wendys similar.

**WHY PER-CATEGORY, not per-role (the load-bearing decision).** A facePin is keyed **(category, weight-role)**: display/subtle can pin "Light Condensed" while title/subtle derives "Light". A per-role-only cut variable would collapse the two onto one value — a silent cut swap, the exact "Light Condensed"→"Light" downgrade the issue named as the danger. So the cut variable carries the category segment, and the isolation is asserted (gate assertion D + `test.ts` #1485(d), which proves title/subtle keeps its OWN "Light" while display/subtle is "Light Condensed" under a one-slot pin).

**DTCG.** The cut's home is `$extensions.prism3` (where `facePin` already lives) — DTCG's typography composite has no width field, so the extension is the honest home, and the numeric `fontWeight` stays in `$value` as before. No family-split was invented (no consumers today); this is the owner's deferred call, recorded in the issue.

**Safety net (docs/34, by name).** A new committed-artifact gate, `lint-cut-binding.ts` (the direct sibling of `lint-lineheight-bake.ts`, opposite verdict — line height must STAY unbound, the cut must BE bound), reads `out/figma/**` and asserts: (A) the cut is bound to a per-category STRING cut variable, never baked; (B) that variable exists in `core.font.json` as STRING/`FONT_STYLE` with a non-empty value; (C) `fontWeight` is unbound numeric parallel data; (D) per-category isolation (the cut's category = the style's family category). EXPECTED is #1485's contract transcribed as constants; ACTUAL is the committed export; a self-check drives the oracles both directions. The facePin VALUE (which the committed brands don't carry — none has `faces`) is pinned in `test.ts`'s #1485 block against the input pin. **Mutations, each restored from a `wip:` commit + regen:** (1) `fontStyle` `bound:true`→`false` (revert to baked) → gate assertion A fires by name ("cut is BAKED") on all 113 styles AND `test.ts` #1485(a/b/d); (2) drop the facePin override in `cutName` → `test.ts` #1485(a) fires ("value=\"Light\"" ≠ "Light Condensed"), the silent downgrade caught; (3) `fontWeight` `bound:false`→`true` → gate assertion C fires ("fontWeight is VARIABLE-BOUND"). Wired into `ci.yml`, `verify.ts`, and all three doc gate regions (`lint-doc-gates.ts` clean).

**FOLLOW-UP FILED (not in this PR — one concern per PR, TokenPress is a guest surface).** TokenPress's reverse exporter needs a matching `fontStyle`-bound-variable reader to round-trip the cut back out to DTCG. Filed as **#1489**; referenced in this PR body.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** `lint-us-english.ts` / `lint-voice.ts` FAIL standalone here — their scope includes the built web+plugin bundles, so they must run AFTER the studio + plugin builds (which `npm run verify` does in order). Run them last, or via `verify.ts`, never before the builds.

## (2026-09-17) — mint `type.label.lg` (18px / emphasis) so the large button label stops reusing the medium rung (#1260)

**STATUS: PR open on branch `lane/1260-label-lg`, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). ENGINE 0.108.0 → 0.109.0; CONTRACT 11.1.0 → 11.2.0 (MINOR — one guaranteed name ADD, rebased onto #1479/#1483/#1476/#1471).** Implements the owner's resolved target on #1260 (Owner QA input, 2026-09-17): the large button label is **18px at emphasis (600) weight**.

**THE GAP.** `type.label.*` shipped only `sm`=12 / `md`=14 (`theme.ts` `TYPE_VARIANTS.label`), so `button.ts` bound `size.large.type → type.label.md.emphasis` — the SAME rung as `medium`. A large button's label was typographically identical to a medium one while height/padding/gap all moved (40/48/56, etc.). All three siblings (`button` / `button-destructive` / `button-neutral`) come off the one `makeButton` factory, so all three collapsed identically. #1248's type-key sweep MEASURED this (2 distinct styles across 3 sizes) and recorded `2` as the authored expectation with the reason attached, precisely so the fix had to come back and raise it.

**THE THIRD PATH (owner-resolved).** The issue's two original routes were both wrong for the target: route 1 (`label.lg`=16, following the 12/14 progression) is **too small**; route 2 (move button to `type.body.lg`=18) hits the size but is **default/strong weight**, not the label tier's emphasis (600). The owner's 18px/emphasis target implies a third path — mint `type.label.lg` at the **body-lg SIZE (18) but the label tier's own WEIGHT (emphasis/600)**. Added `['lg', 18]` to `TYPE_VARIANTS.label`; `label` already ships `weights: ['emphasis']`, so `type.label.lg.emphasis` emits automatically. Re-pointed `size.large.type → type.label.lg.emphasis` across all three siblings (one factory edit).

**RESOLVED px PER DENSITY — the owner's density nuance.** `label` is reading/UI text, which is EXEMPT from the `typeScale` shift (`theme.ts` `buildComposites`: `const shifted = isHeading ? shiftPx(base) : base`). Measured after the fix, `type.label.lg` resolves to **18px at every typeScale** — compact, default, expressive alike — so it lands the owner's 18px at the comfortable (default) density they target and does NOT drift under the shift. Verified two ways: the `tBrand` probe (`compact/default/expressive` all give `lg=18px/emphasis`), and the emitted trees (both nb at default density AND aurora at compact density emit `type.label.lg.emphasis → font.size.18` = 1.125rem = 18px, `weight-role.emphasis` = 600).

**VERSIONING.** ENGINE bumps (0.104.0 → 0.105.0): two observable surfaces move — emitted `out/**` GROWS (`type.label.lg.emphasis` is a new token in every brand) AND the projected component surface moves (the large button member's text style). CONTRACT bumps MINOR (10.3.0 → 10.4.0): `token-contract --check` reports exactly one guaranteed ADD (`type.label.lg.emphasis`, guaranteed 587 → 588 — it lands in the intersection because every corpus brand incl. `minimal` binds the label face) and level `MINOR`; the baseline was `--accept`ed only AFTER raising `CONTRACT_VERSION` (the gate refuses otherwise). The baseline is never a `regen.ts` artifact. `size.large.type` is a component binding, not a token path, and `type.label.md.emphasis` is untouched and still bound at `medium`, so the single ADD is the whole guaranteed diff.

**GATE (docs/34 — the recorded collapse gets deleted, not left).** #1248's sweep authored `2` for button/label with the reason "no `lg` rung to bind". Updated to `3` (`button`, `button-destructive`, `button-neutral`) with the reason rewritten to record the fix. **By-name mutation, restored from a `wip` HEAD:** re-pointing `size.large.type` back to `md` fires the sweep BY NAME on all three siblings — `button/label's type style DISCRIMINATES across 'size' into the 3 authored style(s) — 3 values gave 2 distinct [label/sm/emphasis, label/md/emphasis, label/md/emphasis] (#1248)` — so the collapse cannot return silently. Restored: 3751/0.

**STALE-CLAIM SWEEP (claims my change falsified, updated in the same PR so none strand).** (1) `button.ts` header + the `size.large.type` comment + `notes.unverified` all said the `lg` gap "still stands" / "still open" — now record it CLOSED. (2) `lint-rung-names.ts` cited button's clamp as the LIVING example for its "monotonic not strict" rule and stated "13 of 14 tier families strictly increasing; the single non-strict one is that clamp" — the clamp is gone (every corpus tier family is now strictly increasing), so the prose now keeps the rule on its own terms (a reversal is the real bug; `switch`'s shorter ladder and any future control that outruns its tier still clamp benignly) rather than on a stale example; and its `DEFAULT_RUNG` note that "`type.label` has two rungs so 'middle' is not well defined" now uses the tier gaining its third rung as the live case for naming the constant rather than deriving it from tier length. (3) `field-label.ts` + test.ts:9440 said `type.label.*` is "12/14 with no lg" as part of field-label's rationale for using `type.body.*` — corrected to "12/14/18, emphasis-only, middle rung 14 not 16", which keeps the operative reason (wrong weight AND the 16px middle rung it still lacks) true.

**Files.** `theme.ts` (`+lg` rung), `components/button.ts` (binding + 3 prose sites), `components/field-label.ts` (rationale), `version.ts` (both bumps + changelog), `test.ts` (#1248 sweep `2→3`, the fixture name-set, and the field-label rationale comment), `fixtures/figma/nb/text-styles.json` (+`text/label/lg/emphasis`, 18px/115% LH/Semi Bold — the typography half of this fixture is an engine snapshot that moves with the engine, #328's stance), `schema/token-contract.json` (`--accept`), and the regen artifacts (`out/**`, `component-surface.json`, etc.).
