## (2026-09-17) — a dedicated interactive ICON ink role; component glyphs unbound from `text.*` (#1471)

**STATUS: branch `lane/1471-icon-ink-role` off main, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). Owner-APPROVED CONTRACT MINOR. ENGINE 0.107.0 → 0.108.0; CONTRACT 11.0.0 → 11.1.0 (rebased onto #1479/#1483/#1476).**

**THE GAP.** The interactive color column had no `icon` sub-role — its members were fill(+states) / on-fill / text / border / overlay (+ the `inverse.` twin). So a component's GLYPH inked from the interactive `text` role: `button.ts` outline/text `*.icon` → `text.{rest,hover,pressed}` and `icon-button.ts` outline/ghost `*.icon` → the same (`filled.icon` correctly on `on-fill` — a glyph on a filled ground). An icon is not text, and the owner wants glyphs bound to an ICON token.

**THE CHANGE — VALUE-IDENTICAL, so NO VISUAL CHANGE.** `modes.ts` now mints `interactive.<family>.icon.{rest,hover,pressed}` (and its `inverse.interactive.<family>.icon.*` twin) for every family — the three built-ins (primary/neutral/destructive) and every opt-in `interactivePalettes` column. Its VALUE is the very same resolved candidate the sibling `text.*` role uses (one derivation, shared by value — the exact pattern `border` already follows via `iBorder` consuming `iText`), so the emitted COLORS are byte-identical to before. Emission is folded into the `iText` loop (page) and the inverse-text loop (`invColumn`), so icon can never drift from text: same candidate, same ground, same `secondaryMin` gate. Then every glyph ink key in `button.ts` (`outline.icon.*`, `text.icon.*`) and `icon-button.ts` (`outline.icon.*`, `ghost.icon.*`) re-points from `...text.*` to `...icon.*`; `filled.icon` stays on `on-fill`. **Both button and icon-button families move together** (labels keep `text.*` — a label IS text).

**Why the inverse twin is mandatory, not optional.** Both families carry a `surface=inverse` axis, and the projector rewrites each `color.*` ref → `color.inverse.*` at inverse coordinates (`anatomy-figma.ts`). A glyph binding `color.interactive.<fam>.icon.rest` therefore resolves to `color.inverse.interactive.<fam>.icon.rest` on an inverse member — so the inverse icon column MUST exist or the rewrite dangles. It mirrors `inverse.interactive.<fam>.text.*` value-for-value.

**VERSIONING (owner-approved CONTRACT MINOR).** This ADDS 18 guaranteed emitted names (9 page + 9 inverse; `token-contract --check` classified it MINOR, exactly those 18 ADDED, nothing removed or retyped) — a pure addition cannot break an existing reference. `CONTRACT_VERSION` raised 10.3.0 → 10.4.0 FIRST (the `--accept` guard refuses until the version carries the increment the diff requires — satisfied, not worked around), then `token-contract.ts --accept`. `ENGINE_VERSION` → 0.105.0 (emitted trees move their new `icon.*` leaves + stamp; the projected component surface moves its glyph bindings — a `lint-component-surface` #1252 DRIFT with member counts UNCHANGED, re-`--accept`ed, and a `lint-paint` census DRIFT, re-`--accept`ed). The baseline is NOT in `regen.ts`. Guaranteed count 587 → 605.

**Gate representation + mutations (docs/34, each restored in-session).** The emitted-surface shape gate (`test.ts`) now enumerates `icon.{rest,hover,pressed}` alongside `text`/`border`, the Figma-scope gate asserts the icon role scopes as a GLYPH (`[FRAME,SHAPE,STROKE]`, like `icon.*`/`disabled.icon`, not TEXT — the `INTERACTIVE_SLOT_SCOPES.icon` entry already existed), the `#1282` button gate now also asserts the glyph binds `icon.<state>` (not `text`), and the `#1427` icon-button block + its ARM A moved from `text/` to `icon/`. **(A)** Removing the page icon emission → shape gate MISSING `interactive.primary.icon.{rest,hover,pressed}` + scope gate `primary/icon/*` + `token-contract --check` REMOVED × 9 / MAJOR, all by name. **(B)** Re-pinning `button` `outline.icon` back to `text.rest` → `#1282/#1471 button{,-destructive,-neutral} outline rest` fail by name. Both restored → 3751 pass.

**VERIFICATION.** `npm run verify` FOREGROUND: **57/59 PASS · 0 FAIL**, the 2 SKIP being the `drift`/`drift-coverage` pair (they compare `out/**` against HEAD and skip on an uncommitted tree — cleared once this commit lands; `regen --check` byte-matches the working tree). Contrast contracts unchanged because the values are unchanged. One-off `npx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell` was needed for the web smoke gate (writes outside `node_modules`, CLAUDE.md-sanctioned).

**Trap for re-verifiers.** `icon` mirrors `text` BY VALUE, so no contrast contract or emitted color moves — do not expect `out/**` color diffs, only new `icon.*` leaves. If a future change makes the glyph ink diverge from the label (a real design decision, owner's to make), the shared-candidate fold in `iText`/`invColumn` is where they split, and the icon gate at `secondaryMin` would need re-examining against SC 1.4.11 (a glyph is non-text, 3:1) — held identical to `text` here only because the value is identical.

## (2026-09-17) — emitted text styles now read largest → smallest within each type group (#1476)

**STATUS: PR open on branch `lane/1476-text-style-order`, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). ENGINE 0.106.0 → 0.107.0 (every brand's `out/figma` `text-styles.json` reorders); CONTRACT STANDS at 11.0.0 (rebased onto #1479/#1483) — ordering is not a token name, no guaranteed name moves (`token-contract --check` level `none`, stamp-only `--accept` to sync the baseline's `engineVersion` field — no guaranteed/brand-dependent path moved).**

**WHAT & WHY.** Owner QA (2026-09-17): the Figma styles list read smallest-first (`display/sm`, then `md`, then `lg`), because the plugin creates styles in plan order and the plan is the engine's `collectComposites` walk of the `type` tree, which is ascending by size. A designer reads a type ramp top-to-bottom (display at the top, small labels at the bottom; within a role, `lg` before `md` before `sm`), so the list was upside-down. The fix orders the emitted styles **largest → smallest within each type group**.

**THE BOTH-PANELS FINDING (owner-confirmed, and it decided the whole approach).** The earlier worry was that Figma's Assets panel sorts styles **alphabetically**, independent of the right-panel creation order — which would have forced a numeric/zero-padded **name prefix** (`01-display-lg`) to control the Assets order, dirtying every style name. The owner checked and confirmed the Assets panel **mirrors the right-panel creation order** ("whatever order I place them in inside the right panel"), NOT an independent alpha sort. So **sorting the plan fixes both panels at once and names stay CLEAN — no prefix.** This is the load-bearing fact of the issue; if a future Figma release makes the Assets panel sort independently, the prefix tradeoff is back on the table and this is where to start.

**WHERE THE SORT LIVES, and why there.** `emit-figma-font.ts` `orderComposites`, applied to the `collectComposites` result inside `buildFigmaTextStyles`. That composite array is the **single deterministic driver of Figma creation order**: the emitted `text-styles.json` artifact AND every plan consumer inherit it — `buildTextStylePlan` (write-plan.ts) flattens `buildFigmaTextStyles` directly, so the plugin's `applyTextStylePlan` (`for (const row of plan) … createTextStyle()`) and the paste path `materialise-to-figma` both get the order for free. A plugin-only sort would have missed the artifact and the paste path; sorting the engine plan covers all three.

**THE ORDERING RULE.** A `SIZE_RANK` map (`3xl`=7 … `2xs`=0, largest first) covers six-plus rungs so it generalises past three-rung families. A **stable** decorate-sort keyed by `(group-first-appearance-index, −sizeRank, walk-index)`: the group key preserves the existing tier order **exactly as the walk produced it** — we invent no new tier ordering (the issue's explicit fallback: "if the tier order is ambiguous, keep it, only flip the size axis"); the rank key flips the size axis to descending; the walk-index tiebreak keeps the weight-role variants within one size (`default` / `…-link` / `strong` / `…-link`) in their original order. A second path segment that is not a known size (e.g. `code/inline`) shares one fallback rank and, being stable, stays put. Result for nb-redesign: `display/3xl…sm`, `title/2xl…xs`, `body/lg…sm`, then `label`, `caption`, `eyebrow`, `code` — tiers unchanged, sizes descending.

**Safety net (docs/34, by name).** `test.ts` `font-plan #1476` asserts the emitted names are size-descending within each **contiguous** group (a group must not be re-entered — otherwise "descending within a group" is satisfiable by interleaving). The expected rank table is **transcribed independently in the test**, NOT imported from the emitter's `SIZE_RANK` — a deliberate second copy, so reversing the emitter's sort makes the gate fail rather than both moving together (docs/34 shape 2). Falsifiability is pinned two ways that do not depend on emitter state: a hand-authored **ascending** fixture must report a violation, and its **descending** twin must come back clean (so the detector is neither vacuous nor stuck-on). **Mutation applied:** flipped `orderComposites`'s comparator to ascending — the suite reported `❌ font-plan #1476: NB text styles are size-descending within each contiguous group — display/md/strong (rank 3) after rank 2 within 'display'…` by name, plus the multi-rung arm. Restored; full suite 3755/0.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** The changelog note in `version.ts` originally spelled a path as `out/figma/**/text-styles.json`; `**/` contains `*/`, which **closes the block comment early** and made `emit-dtcg.ts` fail to parse. Avoid `**/` (and `*/`) inside block comments — spell brand-wildcarded paths without the glob, as the entry now does.

## (2026-09-17) — component-property references wire on EVERY member; the member-level combine detach that #1337's recovery couldn't reach (#1472/#1473)

**STATUS: PR open on branch `lane/1472-1473-ref-wiring`, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). ENGINE 0.105.0 → 0.106.0 (a PLUGIN write-path behavior change — principle 5's "any behavior change"; `out/**` + `schema/*` are a STAMP-ONLY regen, the generator.version line and nothing else, `regen --check` byte-clean at 108 artifacts). CONTRACT STANDS at 11.0.0 (rebased onto #1479) — no token name or component member moves.** Closes #1472 AND #1473 (one shared root cause). #1428 and #1337 are the two prior fixes this sits directly on top of.**

**THE DEFECT (grounded, QA 2026-09-17).** `field-label` ⚠️ 27 misses, `select` ⚠️ 36, all `set_componentPropertyReferences: Could not create a new component property reference`, concentrated on single coordinates (field-label `emphasis=secondary/weight=bold`, select `status=warning/state=hover`) rather than uniform — the tell of a per-MEMBER detach, not a name collision. On the affected members the property no longer drives the node, which is the coupled #1472 symptom: a `button`/`icon-button` INSTANCE_SWAP whose `mainComponent` reference never lands cannot swap.

**THE DIAGNOSIS — one level past #1337.** The wire loop writes each reference on the #701 fast-path handle (`builtParts.get(part)`, captured BEFORE `combineAsVariants`). #1337 already handles the case where the combine detaches that handle: the recovery (`write-components.ts` wire-loop catch) re-finds the part by name and re-wires it. But it re-found the part **through the `member` handle snapshotted right after combine** (`members = [...set.children]`, kept for the layout pass). The host keeps reconciling ids AFTER combine and, for some members, reassigns the **member's own identity** too — so that snapshotted handle ends up with a DETACHED subtree while a fresh `set.children` read hands back a live, referenceable twin for the same coordinate. #1337's recovery re-found through the SAME stale handle, landed on the detached node, and Figma threw again → a **permanent** miss the read-back repairs (`#866`/`#1279`) could never reach, because a throw never lands in `wiredRefs`.

**THE FIX (`apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts`).** Re-resolve the MEMBER from a FRESH `set.children` read, taken once right before the wire loop (after combine, the layout `resize`, and `addComponentProperty` have all settled), keyed by name into `liveByName`. Every re-find by name now goes through it — the wire-loop non-built branch and its recovery, the `#866` ref read-back, the `#1279` bound read-back, and the ORPHAN scan (which reads `componentPropertyReferences` and would otherwise miss the settled members' refs on the live twin and report false ORPHANs). Geometry read-backs (coincident/footprint) deliberately KEEP reading the combine-time `members` snapshot — position/size ride that handle. **Inert without the new shim mode**: when member identity is stable (every prior run) the fresh read is the very same objects, so `liveByName.get(name)` returns the snapshot member and nothing changes — the existing #1337 `detachPartsOnCombine` test still passes unmodified. The same fix lands the #1472 swap `mainComponent` ref (it wires through the identical loop).

**THE GATE (docs/34, mutation-proven BY NAME).** The class shipped as a soft ⚠️. New shim mode `settleAfterCombine: 'all' | string[]` (`component-shim.ts`) models the host behavior `detachPartsOnCombine` stopped one level short of: on the first post-snapshot set op (`resize`, with `addComponentProperty` as fallback trigger) each named member is REPLACED in the live `set.children` by a fresh **guarded** twin (attached child-twins that CAN hold a reference) and the combine-time original's whole subtree is DETACHED (throwing ref setters). The snapshot array still references the detached original; a fresh read finds the twin — exactly the divergence the live host produces. Two gates drive it: **`test-write-components.ts` #1473** (mirrors the #1337 battery: 0 "could not create" misses, `refsRepaired === wantRefs` reachability floor proving the settle fired on every reference, plus a host read-back asserting every declared set property — the independent `planSetProperties` expectation, not the executor's `wiredRefs` — is referenced on every settled member's live node) and **`test-roundtrip.ts` #1473** (reads references back through `anatomy-readback.ts`, a reader entirely separate from the executor, and asserts 0 `propertyRef`/`visible` DISCARDED). **Mutation:** revert the `liveByName` re-resolution in the recovery and BOTH gates fail by name — 72 "could not create" misses, `refsRepaired=0`, and the read-backs name the coordinates (`emphasis=primary, weight=regular, size=small, state=rest/label` …) — while the #1337 gate stays GREEN, which is the proof the new gate catches a *distinct* defect (#1337's detach keeps member identity; this one doesn't). `field-label` is the fixture for the same reason it was #1337's: the corpus's only member with two TEXT parts, and the def the live misses were filed on.

**#1472's second half — NOT code, reported for the orchestrator.** The swap PROPERTY is created (the QA status shows `swap …:INSTANCE_SWAP` with ref counts), so the target resolves and the slot is a real instance; the per-member `mainComponent` wiring is what this PR lands. What remains is **library presence**: the file offers only the single `icon/FPO-default-icon` placeholder as a swap candidate — the 43 real `icon/*` glyph components must be built/imported into the file (and available at the scope the designer swaps in) for there to be anything to swap *to*. That is build-ordering / library-presence, not a `write-components.ts` bug; no engine change is warranted. Flagged here (and in the PR body) rather than folded in — one concern per PR (principle 3); if the owner wants the icon set guaranteed present before the control sets, that is its own lane.

**Traps for re-verifiers.** (1) The ENGINE bump is STAMP-ONLY — `out/**`'s only diff is `generator.version 0.105.0 → 0.106.0`; a grep of `out/` for any other change finds nothing, and `schema/*` is likewise stamp-only. The bump records a plugin-side behavior change (principle 5), NOT an emission move — `lint-emission-version` explicitly permits a version moving over an unchanged emission. (2) The shim's `settleAfterCombine` twins carry references but NOT geometry (x/y=0); the gate reads only references off them, and the roundtrip block filters to `propertyRef`/`visible` divergences for exactly that reason — do not add geometry assertions against the settled twins. (3) The fix is inert offline without `settleAfterCombine` (identity stable → fresh read equals snapshot), so `refsRepaired`/`boundRepaired` on every other run are unchanged. (4) CONTRACT stays 11.0.0 — a component-property reference is neither a token name nor a guaranteed-surface path.

## (2026-09-17) — breakpoint count made truly brand-flexible: gate the 2/3/4-floor path, demote the upper layout tiers to `brandDependent` (#1479)

**STATUS: branch `lane/1479-breakpoint-flex` off main, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). ENGINE 0.104.0 → 0.105.0; CONTRACT 10.3.0 → 11.0.0 (owner-approved MAJOR — 12 guaranteed paths demoted). `token-contract --check` clean at 11.0.0, `regen --check` byte-identical (out/** moves by the version stamp ONLY). Capability + gate + contract; NB's own count is unchanged (a separate follow-up, see below).**

**THE GAP — supported by construction, untested below 5.** The breakpoint count is already a per-brand lever (`layout.breakpoints`, `levers.ts:147`). `bpNames(n)` (`theme.ts:1708`) auto-names by slicing the t-shirt ladder — n≤5 anchors at `sm` (`sm,md,lg,xl,2xl`), n≥6 prepends `xs` (Bootstrap) — and emission is count-derived, not hardcoded (`buildLayout` maps over the floor list; `emit-figma-dims.ts:385` iterates `Object.keys(gridNode)`; `#65`/CR-08 already fixed the Figma emit layer for aurora's 6). So a 2/3/4-floor brand worked **by construction** — but nothing exercised it below 5, and "exercised by construction" is not a test (the it's-exercised fallacy, docs/34). The owner wants brands to be able to REMOVE breakpoints (2/3/4 all auto-named, no desktop/mobile rename), so the sub-5 path needed a real gate before it could be relied on.

**THE GATE** (`test.ts` block `(19c)`, beside the CR-08 aurora block it complements). Builds 2-, 3-, and 4-floor brands and confirms 6, each off a minimal input whose ONLY departure is the floor list, and asserts the whole `layout` collection: the auto-names (Figma modes AND the DTCG `breakpoint` node keys — coherence, not two lists that happen to agree), the per-breakpoint grid columns (`4/8/…/base` ladder), and the gutter/margin ramps. INDEPENDENCE (docs/34 shape 1): `expect` is hand-authored from the DOCUMENTED contract in `theme.ts` (the `bpNames` comment, the `cols` ladder, `GUTTER_PX`/`MARGIN_PX`), never computed by calling `bpNames`/`buildLayout` — a gate whose expected value is derived from the emitter cannot see the emitter break.

**THE MUTATION TRAP worth carrying.** The obvious mutation — `bpNames`'s `.slice(0, n)` → `.slice(0, 5)` (the "hardcoded 5") — changes NOTHING for a sub-5 brand and was discarded after it passed green: `buildLayout` maps over the FLOOR list, so a name index beyond `floors.length` is never read. The mutations that actually move what this gate sees are WITHIN the used range: **(M1)** swapping the `sm`-anchor order `md`↔`lg` → the auto-name and DTCG-coherence arms fail BY NAME for n=2/3/4; **(M2)** `cols` top rung `base` → `base - 1` → the grid-columns arm fails BY NAME for all four. Both verified against the full suite, then reverted. A distinctness/"count-blind" arm was written and then REMOVED: it was redundant with the per-case `names.length === n` checks, and the one mutation that would isolate it (making `buildLayout` ignore `input.breakpoints`) gives aurora 5 floors and crashes CR-08 before the block runs — so it could never be shown to fail cleanly, and docs/34 warns an arm that cannot be made to fail is worse than none.

**THE CONTRACT RECLASSIFICATION (owner-approved MAJOR, no consumers).** `token-contract.json` listed `breakpoint.{lg,xl,2xl}` and `grid.{lg,xl,2xl}.{columns,gutter,margin}` — 12 paths — as **guaranteed**, purely because every corpus brand happened to ship 5+ floors. But the breakpoint count is a lever, so those upper tiers were never truly promised: a 2/3/4-floor brand emits none of them. They are `brandDependent` now, mirroring `breakpoint.xs`/`grid.xs.*`, which are already brand-dependent because only aurora's 6 floors reach them. The demotion is realized the ONLY honest way — a new `minimal-bp2` corpus member (2 floors) drops the 12 paths out of the intersection — **not** by hand-editing the baseline (which `--accept` rewrites and regen must never touch; docs/30, docs/34 shape 6). A guaranteed removal is MAJOR whether or not the path is still emitted elsewhere (it reports as DEMOTED, still emitted, no migration path — so no `DEPRECATIONS` entry): 10.3.0 → 11.0.0, `--accept` after the bump (it refuses first). Owner confirmed no consumers bind these names. After this, a brand changing its breakpoint count never forces a contract move again.

**Why the ENGINE bump, and why out/** moves.** No emitted token value and no projected component member moves — a 5-floor brand emits exactly what it did before, and the only `out/**` diff is `$extensions.generator.version` `0.104.0` → `0.105.0`. The ENGINE bump accompanies the contract reclassification (owner-directed) and restamps the corpus so the producer stamp tracks the release that moved the promised surface; `lint-emission-version` is satisfied (emission moved, version moved forward).

**NB IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED.** Setting New Balance itself to 2 breakpoints is a ~1-line config (`theme.ts` NB fixture → `breakpoints: [0, 768]`) but needs a design value (NB's desktop breakpoint floor), so it is a separate follow-up pending owner confirmation — NOT in this PR. Note NB's `desktop`/`mobile` split is its **type viewport** axis (`type-sets`), distinct from this layout axis; this change does not touch it.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** The corpus count is coupled in two `test.ts` assertions (`live.corpus.length` and the `#1010` glyph-artboard `px.length`), both moved 6 → 7 for `minimal-bp2`; a future corpus member moves both again. The `485`/`234` path counts in `docs/30` and `version.ts`/`token-contract.ts` headers are already historically stale (live is 575/268 after this) and deliberately NOT tracked in prose (#1180) — left untouched.

## (2026-09-17) — `lint-us-english` gains the doubled-L and `-re` classes; 506 real en-GB spellings it had been passing are respelled (#1447)

**STATUS: branch `issue-1447-us-english-double-l-and-re` off main, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). ENGINE 0.103.0 → 0.104.0 (emitted `$description`/`meaning` prose moves in every brand's `out/**`, AND the projected component surface moves — four defs' `note`/`description` prose, a `lint-component-surface` #1252 DRIFT with member counts unchanged, re-`--accept`ed); CONTRACT STANDS at 10.3.0 (`token-contract --check` level `none`, stamp-only `--accept`).**

**THE BLIND SPOT.** `prose-rules.ts` detected en-GB with two shapes — `PATTERN` (`-ise`/`-our`) and `STEMS` (`grey`) — which are exactly CLAUDE.md's three named examples of the US-English rule, read as its extent. Two whole classes fall outside both and the gate ran, found nothing, and printed `✓ clean` over them (docs/34 shape 8, the gate written from the same mental model as its subject): **doubled L before a suffix** (`travelling`, `labelled`, `signalling`, `modelled`, `cancelled` — en-US `traveling`, `labeled`, …) and **the `-re` endings** (`centre`, `centred`, `centres`, `metre`, `litre`, `theatre`, `fibre`, `calibre`, `lustre` — en-US `-er`). `travelling` shipped green in #1425 and was caught only by the human review of #1440; `centred`/`centres` sat in `out/nb.tokens.json` on main through every scan.

**THE TWO RULES ADDED (`prose-rules.ts`, so the shape-index crossing check inherits them for free).** `DOUBLE_L` is a **stem alternation**, not a suffix scan: `\b[A-Za-z]*(travel|label|cancel|model|signal|fuel|level|channel|panel|…|wool)l(ed|ing|er|ers|or|ors|ery|ous|en|ist|ists)\b`. A bare `ll(ed|ing|er)` scan is unusable because en-US doubles too after a stressed syllable (`controlled`, `compelled`, `installed`) and in every `-ll` stem (`called`, `scrolling`, `smaller`), so the rule lists the unstressed-final stems en-GB doubles; the suffix list stops where en-GB stops, so `cancellation` (doubled in both) is unreachable, and `-y` (`totally`, `equally`, `initially`) is deliberately absent. `RE_ENDINGS` is a **substring scan like `STEMS`**: `\b[A-Za-z]*(centre|metre|litre|theatre|fibre|calibre|lustre|sabre|spectre|meagre|manoeuvre|sepulchre)[A-Za-z]*\b` — inflections and compounds come free (`centred`, `centrepiece`, `kilometres`, `fibreglass`) and it is safe where the `-ise` scan needs a list because the en-US form differs by letter ORDER, so `parameter`/`diameter`/`perimeter` (`meter`, never `metre`) and `epicenter` cannot match. **Word-boundary anchoring on BOTH ends is the whole false-positive defense**; there is no `\b\w+re\b`. Both are case-insensitive like `STEMS`, so shipped comment SHOUTING (`THE ROW MUST NOT CENTRE`) is caught too.

**`NOT_EN_GB` ADDITIONS: one, pre-emptive — `cancellous`** (anatomy; en-US doubles it). The first run over the built corpus found **506 hits, every one genuine**, so the corpus itself contributed no allowlist entry. Per-word: `signalling` ×56 per `*.ai.json` (the four status-family `meaning` strings in `ai-metadata.ts`); `centred`/`centres` ×6 per token tree and per `figma/*/control.json` (the `control.size.*` inset and line-box descriptions in `tree.ts`); `labelled` ×49, `centred` ×18, `centres` ×7, `centre` ×6, `modelled`, `unlabelled`, `mislabelled`, `LABELLED` ×3, `CENTRE` ×3 in each plugin bundle file — the component defs' `description`/`note`/`aria`/`avoidWhen`/`whenToUse` prose and the comments that ship with them (#849). All respelled at the source (33 files: `ai-metadata.ts`, `tree.ts`, `scale.ts`, `theme.ts`, `modes.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `levers.ts`, `ramp.ts`, `write-plan.ts`, `component-schema.ts`, `anatomy-figma.ts`, `anatomy-readback.ts`, every `components/*.ts` with a hit, `apps/studio/src/{main.ts,styles.css,provenance.ts}`, `apps/plugin/src/{write-components.ts,write-figma.ts}`), then regen. Meaning unchanged in every case — only letters moved; no identifier, key or token path was touched (`aria-labelledby` survives intact because the sed was word-bounded, which is the one trap in a mechanical respell: `labelled` is a substring of that attribute).

**Why this is NOT the gate-plus-allowlist PR it was scoped as.** The lane brief expected the new patterns to over-catch legitimate text and said to allowlist until green. The corpus had the opposite problem: everything caught was real. Allowlisting `centred` and `signalling` would have neutered the gate against the exact words the issue was filed on (a `NOT_EN_GB` entry is for en-US words the pattern over-catches, never for en-GB words that ship), and a red gate cannot land. So the issue's own scope note applies — "this issue owns the gate widening + the pre-existing `centred` cleanup" — and the cleanup rides here, which forces the regen and the ENGINE bump. `regen --check` is byte-identical to the committed `out/**` AFTER the respell, not to main's.

**Safety net (docs/34, by name).** `SELF_CHECK` gains seven samples driving the shared `enGb`: four positive (`travelling`, `unlabelled`/`cancelled`, `centred`, `kilometres` — the last because only a substring scan sees a compound) and three negative (`controlled`/`compelled`/`caller`, `cancellation`/`totally`/`equally`, `diameter`/`parameter`/`centered`). **Mutations, each restored from a `wip:` commit:** (A) `travelling` appended to `packages/engine/README.md`, `labelled` to the root `README.md`, `centre` to `skills/prism3-theme/SKILL.md` → gate exits 1 naming all three by file, line and word. (B) `DOUBLE_L` removed from the `enGb` loop → `❌ the gate's detection is broken` naming the two doubled-L samples, before any file is scanned. (C) `RE_ENDINGS` removed → the same, naming `centred` and `kilometres`. Neither neutering goes quiet.

**Traps for re-verifiers.** (1) A mechanical `centre → center` rewrite turns `centred` into `centerd`; the first regen on this branch shipped that into `out/**` for a few minutes before the word-diff review caught it. Respell `centred → centered` as its own rule, and read the word-level diff (`git diff --word-diff`) before trusting a sed. (2) The 506 count is the FIRST run's total across `out/**` + both bundles; `out/**` alone accounts for ~330 of it because every brand repeats the same source strings. (3) `test.ts` and the `lint-*.ts` headers still say `centred`/`labelled` in their `ok()` messages and comments — not shipped, not gated, left alone (surgical). (4) Not covered by this issue and STILL blind, measured on the same corpus after this pass: `catalogue` ×8, `licence` ×3, `artefact` ×1 (plus `-yse`: `analyse`/`paralyse`, and the reverse single-L class `skilful`/`fulfil`/`enrol`, none currently shipping). Filed as #1463 rather than folded in — one concern per PR.

## (2026-09-17) — #1451: the #1429 gate's comment said "12 per icon-button family"; the gate measures 48

**STATUS: PR open on branch `fix/1451-icon-button-wash-count`, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). Comment-only correctness fix — NO ENGINE bump (0.103.0 stands), CONTRACT 10.3.0, no emitted artifact moves, no gate behavior moves.**

**THE DRIFT.** The prose atop the #1429 overlay-wash block in `apps/plugin/test-roundtrip.ts` stated the wash was "measured here as 96 bindings per button family and **12** per icon-button family". The issue (filed off the #1448 review) said the gate reports **24**. On current main it reports **48** — and the brief's rule was "use the number the code produces, not the issue title", so 48 is what the comment now says. The 12 was measured at 0.93.0 before the icon-button def gained two axes; the gate prints per-family figures at run time, so the assertion was always right and only the comment drifted.

**WHY 48, derived independently of the gate (docs/34 — the number is checked against the def, not copied from the output).** A wash binds on `container.fills` at every outline/ghost × hover/pressed coordinate, and icon-button's axes are `appearance ×3 · size ×3 · shape ×2 · surface ×2` (216 members). So: 2 wash appearances × 2 wash states × 3 sizes × 2 shapes × 2 surfaces = **48**. The two doublings since the comment was written, in merge order on main: `#1353` (`shape`, 12 → 24, merged BEFORE the #1429 gate — so the comment was stale on arrival, which is what the review caught) and `#1427` (`surface`, 24 → 48, merged after). Button's 96 is unchanged and still matches. The `test:roundtrip` output on this branch: `button=96 ×3, icon-button=48 ×3, 432 bindings, 0 dangling`.

**Scope.** One comment edited; the new wording carries the derivation so the next axis change has a formula to re-check against rather than a bare number, and points at assertion (1) as the live figure. The dated #1429 entry below (2026-09-16) still says 12 — it is a record of what was measured at 0.93.0 and is left as history. Nothing else in `apps/plugin/` or `packages/engine/` carries the stale count (grepped for the "12 per icon-button" shape repo-wide; this comment was the sole instance). Full `npm run verify` FOREGROUND: **59/59 PASS**.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** The number in that comment will go stale AGAIN the next time an icon-button axis is added or removed (it is a product of the def's axis sizes, and nothing gates a comment). Whoever changes the axes: re-run `test:roundtrip`, read the `#1429 … every named family (… icon-button=N …)` line, and update the comment's count and formula in the same PR.

## (2026-09-17) — the `glyphScale` range refusal gets its own by-name mutation test (#1409)

**STATUS: test-only PR on branch `1409-glyphscale-refusal-test` — do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). No ENGINE bump, CONTRACT 10.3.0, `regen --check` byte-identical, no emission change.**

**The untested guard.** #1408 added `PartDef.glyphScale` (a `vector` part's drawn grid occupies this fraction of its artboard; checkbox-control's mark and dash author `0.8`) with a refusal in `anatomyErrors` (`packages/engine/component-schema.ts`, the `if (p.glyphScale !== undefined)` block): the value must be in `(0, 1]`, and the field is refused on any non-`vector` kind. Its progress note argued the guard was "exercised by construction (0.8 is in range)" — the it's-exercised fallacy docs/34 names: a passing in-range value proves the happy path, never the refusal. Hand-verified at merge, committed nowhere. Either comparison could be deleted or mis-written (`>= 0`, `< 1`) and 3,742 assertions stayed green — a guard with no test is one a future cleanup deletes silently.

**The test added** (`packages/engine/test.ts`, beside the #1340 `glyphPx` refusal battery it mirrors — same file, same vocabulary). Three arms, nine assertions, all `#1409`-prefixed so a mutation report names them:

- **(a) in range accepted** — `0.0001`, `0.5`, `1` validate with no `glyphScale`-family error. Not a truthiness check: the filter is the glyphScale message family only, so an unrelated authoring error on the patched def cannot mask a wrongly-firing refusal.
- **(b) out of range refused by name** — `0`, `-0.1`, `1.0001`, `1.5` each produce the range message with the VALUE ECHOED (`declares glyphScale 1.5 … must be in (0, 1]`), so a refusal that fires on the wrong probe cannot satisfy it.
- **(c) wrong kind refused by name** — an in-range `0.8` on the control BOX (the mark's host, the realistic one-level-up slip) produces the `only a 'vector'` message.

**Why the boundary is independent (docs/34 shape 1 / shape 2).** EXPECTED is `(0, 1]` authored as literals in the test from the schema's own doc-comment contract (`0 < glyphScale ≤ 1`), never read from the comparison the subject runs. The two just-inside / just-outside PAIRS are what pin the bound's *type* rather than its existence: `1` accepted + `1.0001` refused fails on a `< 1` rewrite, `0` refused + `0.0001` accepted fails on `>= 0`. The subject is the REAL checkbox-control mark patched per probe, with a probe-subject assertion first (it is a vector carrying a numeric `glyphScale`), so a def rename or a mark that stops authoring the field fails there rather than leaving every arm vacuous on an undefined patch.

**Mutation confirmation — four mutations, each failing BY NAME and nothing else** (wip commit between each; every restore is `git checkout -- component-schema.ts`, which reaches HEAD):

| Mutation on the subject | Suite | Named failures |
|---|---|---|
| `<= 1` → `<= 2` (admit above 1) | 3749 / 2 failed | `#1409 glyphScale 1.0001 … refused BY NAME`, `#1409 glyphScale 1.5 … refused BY NAME` |
| `> 0` → `>= 0` (admit 0) | 3750 / 1 failed | `#1409 glyphScale 0 … refused BY NAME` |
| `<= 1` → `< 1` (tighten — proves the ACCEPT arm can fail) | 3750 / 1 failed | `#1409 glyphScale 1 is IN (0, 1] and validates clean` |
| delete the wrong-kind arm | 3750 / 1 failed | `#1409 glyphScale on a NON-vector part … refused BY NAME` |

Restored: 3751 passed, 0 failed. The third row is the one worth keeping: a test that only asserts refusals is half a gate — a refusal widened to `> 0 && < 2` and one tightened to `> 0 && < 1` are both wrong, and only an acceptance arm at the inclusive edge sees the second.

**Not folded in.** #1409's optional `edge ÷ 8` comment-phrasing note in `checkbox-control.ts` / `component-schema.ts` / `version.ts` is left as filed — prose in three files is a separate concern from a test-only PR (principle 3).

## (2026-09-17) — a shipped $description bricked the plugin (Figma import-expression reject); hotfix #1460 + the gate that would have caught it (#1461)

**STATUS: hotfix #1460 MERGED (f630f8d, ENGINE 0.103.0). Gate PR open on branch `claude/gate-1461-sandbox-reject` — do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).**

**THE INCIDENT (found in owner QA, 2026-09-17).** Re-importing the plugin from its manifest failed at load: `SyntaxError: possible import expression rejected around line 11138` from Figma's plugin sandbox (`rejectImportExpressions` / `rejectDangerousSources`). Line 11138 of `dist/main.js` was the `radio-control` `checked.border` **`$description`**, which shipped the literal phrase "the Figma import (2026-09-15)". Figma's MAIN-THREAD controller sandbox scans the bundle SOURCE TEXT — **string literals included** — for `import` immediately followed by `(`, reads it as a dynamic-import expression, and rejects the WHOLE plugin. The plugin would not run at all. **Hotfix (#1460):** reworded to "the 2026-09-15 Figma import" — meaning identical, the `import (` adjacency gone; rebuilt `main.js` carries 0 occurrences. ENGINE 0.102.0 → 0.103.0, CONTRACT 10.3.0.

**WHY 58 GATES + CI STAYED GREEN.** No gate read `main.js` the way Figma does. `plugin-no-node-builtins` scans the same bundle but only for `node:` builtins; `plugin-verdict` / `plugin-start` drive the UI (`dist/ui.html`) in a browser, not the main-thread sandbox eval; `lint-us-english` / `lint-voice` read the bundle as PROSE. A whole class of shipped text — anything reaching `dist/main.js`, and component `description`/`note`/`aria` fields do (#849) — could carry a token sequence Figma refuses, invisibly to the suite.

**THE GATE (#1461), the rule that would have caught it.** `apps/plugin/lint-sandbox-reject.ts`, wired into `verify.ts` + `ci.yml` + `CLAUDE.md` §4 + `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 + the PR template (58 → 59 gates; `lint-doc-gates` clean, 59 vs 59 both directions). It reads `dist/main.js` as source text and fails on any Figma-sandbox-rejected sequence. **Independence (docs/34):** the reject patterns are AUTHORED in the gate from Figma's documented sandbox behaviour, not derived from the bundle; the list is narrow and proven (`import\s*\(` is the sequence the incident hit — add a pattern only on a real observed reject). **Not vacuous:** `selfCheck()` runs each pattern against a POSITIVE control (the exact incident phrase, must match) and a NEGATIVE (its fix, must not), and a missing/empty `dist/main.js` is a FAIL that says "run the plugin build first", never a silent pass. **Scoped to `main.js`, deliberately:** `dist/ui.html` is a browser iframe where `import(...)` is valid runtime syntax and the identical description ships harmlessly, so scanning it would fail on legitimate prose. **Mutation-proven by name:** reintroducing `import (` into the `radio-control` description and rebuilding fires the gate on `main.js:11138` (the exact incident line); restored, green.

**Traps for re-verifiers.** (1) The gate runs `after: ['build-plugin']` — it needs the built bundle; a stale/missing `dist/main.js` fails loudly. (2) Do NOT extend the pattern list to `ui.html`-context syntax or to static `import`/`export` — those false-positive on prose and on the iframe. (3) The latent "import (" occurrences in `version.ts`'s changelog comments and `anatomy-figma.ts:394` are not currently reachable into `main.js`; if a future bundling change surfaces them, this gate catches them.

## (2026-09-17) — RENAME the icon-button appearance value `text` → `ghost` (icon-button family only; Button keeps `text`) (#1432)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). Branch `claude/fix-1432-icon-button-ghost` off main (ENGINE 0.100.0 / CONTRACT 10.3.0, after #1341/#1384/#1427/#1456).** **ENGINE bump 0.100.0 → provisional 0.101.0 (the projected component surface moves — the icon-button appearance member names `appearance=text` → `appearance=ghost` and the `ghost.*` paint keys — a `lint-component-surface` #1252 trigger; a rebase relay reassigns the ENGINE integer to the true next-free above main before merge). CONTRACT STANDS at 10.3.0 — NO bump (see the load-bearing correction below).** Implements the OWNER DECISION recorded in the #1432 body (2026-09-17): rename the appearance axis VALUE `text` → `ghost` for the three icon-button families ONLY.

**WHAT CHANGED, and why each is what the owner decided.**
- **The tertiary appearance VALUE is `ghost`, not `text`, for `icon-button` / `icon-button-destructive` / `icon-button-neutral` ONLY.** A "text" appearance names nothing on an icon-only control (there is no text); `ghost` is the industry term for a borderless/fill-less icon button. Changed in `components/icon-button.ts`: `variants.appearance`, the `appearance` prop (enum type, `values`, `default: 'ghost'`, description), the `iconButtonIntentTokens` paint KEYS (`text.icon*` / `text.overlay*` → `ghost.icon*` / `ghost.overlay*`), and the shipped `docs.usage` / destructive `description` prose (`filled > outline > ghost`, `appearance=ghost`).
- **Button KEEPS `text` — the two families deliberately diverge on this one appearance-value name (owner-accepted, NOT a bug to align).** `button.ts` is untouched. This is the first intentional appearance-ladder divergence in the corpus.
- **The mechanical mapping is UNCHANGED — an axis-VALUE rename only.** The `ghost.*` paint keys bind the SAME `color.interactive.<family>.text.*` ink roles the `text.*` keys did (button's `text` appearance ink role, `iText` since #576). Only the icon-button coordinate NAME moved; the projector is generic (reads `paintKeys` + the def's own tokens), so no `anatomy-figma.ts` change was needed and there is no hardcoded appearance branch anywhere.

**⚠ THE CONTRACT MAJOR PREMISE IN THE ISSUE IS MECHANICALLY IMPOSSIBLE — CONTRACT STANDS AT 10.3.0 (read before "restoring" 11.0.0).** The #1432 body and the lane brief both state this is a "guaranteed NAME-surface change → CONTRACT MAJOR" and that `token-contract --check` will show a REMOVE (`…text…`) + ADD (`…ghost…`) for the three icon-button families. **It does not, and cannot.** `token-contract.ts` versions the emitted TOKEN-name surface only (`tokenPaths` over `buildTree(theme)`); a component appearance-axis VALUE is not a token — it never enters the tree, the baseline `schema/token-contract.json` contains **no `icon-button` path**, and after the rename `token-contract --check` reports the guaranteed surface **UNCHANGED (587, level `none`, "no guaranteed path moved — no version bump required")**. This is the exact **#1427 precedent**: adding icon-button's `surface` axis was likewise a projection change that left CONTRACT at 10.3.0, because "a component prop/variant name is not part of the token-name contract". **The gate ENFORCES the stand:** `satisfiesBump(prev, next, 'none')` accepts ONLY version equality, so setting `CONTRACT_VERSION` to 11.0.0 makes `token-contract --accept` **REFUSE** ("this change is NONE but CONTRACT_VERSION is still 11.0.0") and leaves `--check` permanently red — **deadlocking `npm run verify` (58/58 is unreachable at 11.0.0)**. Both were verified empirically this lane. Per principle 5 and the #1384/#1427/#1429 rule — the objective gate result decides the bump, not the provisional guess — CONTRACT STANDS at 10.3.0 (`--accept` is stamp-only, engineVersion 0.100.0 → 0.101.0).

**FLAGGED to the orchestrator/owner (a decision, not smuggled).** The icon-button appearance-value rename IS a breaking change to the **component API surface** — a code consumer writing `<IconButton appearance="text">` must move to `"ghost"` — but that surface is **ENGINE-tracked** (this bump + `lint-component-surface`), NOT token-contract-tracked. If the owner wants the component-API name surface under a versioned contract (so a rename like this forces a CONTRACT bump), that requires a **NEW mechanism** — a component-API section in `token-contract.ts` — which is a separate design task out of scope for this rename. This lane ships the rename verified at CONTRACT 10.3.0 and surfaces the reconciliation rather than fabricating a MAJOR bump the gate refuses.

**GATE RECONCILIATION (docs/34 — kept independent, mutate-and-confirm-by-name).** `lint-axis-values.ts` is the gate that asserts the icon-button appearance vocabulary. Its single `sole` `appearance` entry (`['filled','outline','text']`, six defs) is SPLIT into two: `canonical` (`['filled','outline','text']`, the three `button` defs) and `overlapping` (`['filled','outline','ghost']`, the three icon-button defs). `overlapping` is the correct — and expensive — relation: the two ladders agree on `filled`/`outline` and diverge on the tertiary rung alone, which is exactly the "reads as aligned while disagreeing on one value" shape the register exists to flag, and here the divergence IS the decision. ARM C recomputes the relation by set algebra (`relate(['filled','outline','ghost'], canonical)` → `overlapping`), so the declared relation is checked against the values, not trusted.

**SAFETY NET — by-name mutation (docs/34), restored from HEAD after (a `wip:` commit made first).** Reverted ONE icon-button family (`icon-button-destructive`) back to `appearance: ['filled','outline','text']` → `lint-axis-values.ts` fires BY NAME on two arms: ARM A (`icon-button-destructive · appearance: [filled, outline, text] — declared, but the entry does not name 'icon-button-destructive'`) AND ARM B (`appearance: [filled, outline, ghost] names 'icon-button-destructive', which does not declare that axis with those values`). So a stray `text` on any icon-button family cannot pass. Full `npm run verify` FOREGROUND: **58/58 PASS** (engine suite 3742/0).

**Traps for re-verifiers.** (1) CONTRACT stays 10.3.0 — do NOT bump to 11.0.0; the issue's premise that `token-contract --check` shows the rename is empirically false (component appearance values are not tokens), and 11.0.0 makes `token-contract --accept` refuse and verify go red. See the ⚠ block above. (2) Button KEEPS `text` — do NOT "align" the two families; the divergence is the owner's accepted decision. (3) The `ghost.*` paint keys bind `color.interactive.<family>.text.*` — the `text/` in the emitted ink-role paths and in `test.ts` assertions is the ink ROLE (button's `text` appearance behaviour), NOT the icon-button appearance value; do NOT "fix" it to `ghost/`. (4) `out/**` is stamp-only (component defs are not emitted to `out/`; only the `generator.version` line moved). (5) `component-surface.json` (icon-button ×3: 216 → 216 members, plans moved) and `paint-census.json` (icon-button ×3 census hashes) are re-accepted at the forward ENGINE bump; `token-contract.json` is stamp-only at 10.3.0. (6) Bump `version.ts` BEFORE regen. (7) Smoke needs `npx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell` in a fresh container before `verify`. (8) The `lint-us-english` gate covers component-def comments once they reach `apps/*/dist` — a British spelling in an icon-button.ts comment ships and fails it (caught and fixed here: "behaviour" → "behavior").

## (2026-09-16) — the inverse interactive fill STEPS per state again, 2 rungs away from the extreme (#1456, reverses #1384's flat fill)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). Branch `claude/fix-1456-inverse-fill-step` off main (ENGINE 0.99.0 / CONTRACT 10.3.0, after #1341/#1384/#1427).** **ENGINE bump 0.99.0 → provisional 0.100.0 (emitted VALUES move — the inverse fill hover/pressed/focused/selected states across the corpus — via `lint-emission-version`; MINOR increment continuing 0.94 → … → 0.99, so 0.100.0; a rebase relay reassigns to the true next-free integer above main before merge). CONTRACT STANDS at 10.3.0 — NO bump.** Implements the OWNER DECISION on #1456 (2026-09-16, refined same day), which REVERSES the flat inverse fill #1384 shipped and restores per-state feedback the same way page buttons carry it.

**WHY CONTRACT DOES NOT BUMP (read before "correcting" it to 10.4.0).** Hover/pressed rebind to EXISTING neutral ramp rungs and rest keeps the absolute #1384 established — no guaranteed token NAME is added, removed or retyped. `token-contract.ts --check` reports the guaranteed surface unchanged (guaranteed **587**, "no guaranteed path moved — no version bump required"); `--accept` prints "baseline accepted at 10.3.0 (no surface change)" and refreshes only the informational `engineVersion` stamp (0.99.0 → 0.100.0). This is the #1384/#1427/#1429 precedent: the objective gate result decides the bump, not a provisional guess.

**WHAT CHANGED, and why each is what the owner decided.**
- **The inverse fill STEPS per interactive state again — 2 NEUTRAL rungs per state, AWAY FROM THE EXTREME the resting absolute sits at.** REST is unchanged (still the crisp `core.palette.white` / `core.palette.black` literal-color sentinel #1384 made — the owner explicitly kept rest). Only hover/pressed (and their focused/selected twins) move off it, into the adjacent neutral ramp rungs:
  - **Light-family modes** (rest = white, the light extreme): step DARKER — **hover = `neutral.100`, pressed = `neutral.200`** (focused rides hover, selected rides pressed).
  - **Dark-family modes** (rest = black, the dark extreme): step LIGHTER — **hover = `neutral.900`, pressed = `neutral.800`**.
  This mirrors the page fill's own 2-rungs-per-state walk (`050 → 150 → 250`) — the same `STATE_RUNGS`/`walk` machinery, anchored at the EXTREME (white ≈ rung 0, black ≈ rung 1000) and walking `dir` rungs INWARD (`dir` is +1 in a light mode / −1 in a dark mode, so the fill always steps away from the extreme it rests at). Verified identical rungs across all 4 corpus brands (each names its neutral palette `neutral`). Uniform across primary/neutral/destructive; the per-family ink is preserved (primary → brand, destructive → danger, neutral → extreme). No new primitive — reuses #1384's `white`/`black` and the ramp rungs already in the tree.
- **The edge rule is handled by `walk`'s existing overshoot reflection (L-01).** "If a base fill is too close to one end to step the default direction, step the other direction." For the default white/black bases — which sit AT the extremes — inward is always accommodated, so they always step 100/200 (light) / 900/800 (dark). The reflection covers the general case (a user-overridden base near an end) for free; no special-casing added.
- **On-fill INK contract is REST-ONLY (the load-bearing correction, owner #1456).** The label/icon ink must clear AA on the REST fill ONLY; hover/pressed are transient states EXEMPT from the ink contract (standard a11y practice — the resting state carries the contract). The family ink stays derived to pass at REST and RIDES the stepped hover/pressed fills WITHOUT a per-state contrast gate. **This is what dissolves #1384's reason for going flat:** #1384 flattened the fill precisely to keep the dark-band HOVER ink from dropping to ~1.78:1; under the REST-ONLY exemption that drop is acceptable BY DESIGN, so the fill steps freely. Measured worst-case non-rest on-fill ink across the whole corpus (both lever positions, all modes/families): **2.54:1** (nb/light/primary/pressed) — comfortably above the studio smoke's 2.0 rendered floor, because stepping anchors at the extreme and stays NEAR it (neutral.100/200 or .900/.800), unlike #1389's fill which stepped from `neutral.850` toward a mid-gray `neutral.750`.
- **Studio Source control — NO CODE CHANGE (correct 1:1).** The inverse specimen row (`apps/studio/src/main.ts`, shared studio+plugin) already reads `inverse.interactive.<c>.fill.${s}` PER STATE and the `on-fill` ink, so it auto-reflects the stepping with no edit. The rest source picker (white/black Auto + pinnable steps) governs rest only, which is unchanged.

**SCOPE / BLAST RADIUS — one shared-role change covers BOTH buttons and icon-buttons.** The stepped fill is the shared `modes.ts` role `inverse.interactive.<family>.fill`, which BOTH `button` (via its `surface` axis + the projector's `color.* → color.inverse.*` rewrite) and `icon-button` (which inherited the `surface` axis in #1427) bind. Confirmed both inherit the stepped fill by construction (the projector rewrite is generic); icon-button needs no separate change. Diffed against `origin/main`: exactly the `inverse.interactive.{primary,neutral,destructive}.fill.{hover,pressed,focused,selected}` values + their `$description` prose, plus the rest `$description` (value unchanged). Nothing else moved.

**GATE RECONCILIATION (docs/34 — kept independent, mutate-and-confirm-by-name).**
- **GATE A (#1384 → #1456)** asserted the inverse fill was FLAT/absolute across states. RECONCILED to the stepped model: REST = the crisp absolute (white light / black dark, from the MODE NAME); hover/focused = the 2-rung step (neutral.100 / .900); pressed/selected = the 4-rung step (neutral.200 / .800). Expected rungs are derived from the mode name + the brand's neutral-palette name (brand config), NEVER from `walk`/`dir`/`stateRungs` (the producer). Four named arms: the exact-rung arm (a flattened or moved rung fails), the STEP-not-FLAT arm (any non-rest state still equal to the absolute fails), the DIRECTION arm (recomputes the emitted rung integers — a light band must ascend 100 → 200, a dark band descend 900 → 800; inverting the mode-mirror fails), and the UNIFORM arm (all three families equal at every state).
- **GATE B (#1384) stays REST-ONLY.** It recomputes the per-family on-fill ink against `fill.rest` at a hard 4.5 floor — NOT extended to hover/pressed. The per-mode contrast contract likewise never asserts on-fill ink on the stepped states: `inverse.interactive.<c>.on-fill` is a SINGLE role gated only against `fill.rest`, so the exemption is scoped by construction (no blanket removal). The `strictInteractiveContrast` lever arm is UNCHANGED and still holds: lever ON opts into all-state strictness, and the neutral-extreme ink it selects still clears 4.5 at hover/pressed under stepping (measured worst 10.75:1) — the lever survives the step.
- **The harshness carve-out** ("no pure black on the canvas in standard mode") comment was updated: only REST is now the pure absolute (the stepped states are neutral.100/200 or .900/.800, never a pure extreme), so only rest exercises the carve; the carve regex still covers all states harmlessly and the "clears its own min" honesty check is unchanged.

**SAFETY NET — by-name mutations (docs/34), each fired the named arm, restored from HEAD between mutations (a `wip:` commit each), the good state re-verified after.**
- **(a) FLATTEN** the inverse fill (`const c = ... walk(...)` → `const c = fillRestAbs`, all states = rest absolute) → GATE A's STEP-not-FLAT arm (`every hover/pressed/focused/selected state STEPS off the resting absolute`) AND the exact-rung arm fire by name.
- **(b) WRONG DIRECTION** (invert the mode-mirror: `extremeAnchor = cfg.family === 'light' ? 1000 : 0`) → GATE A's DIRECTION arm (`the step goes AWAY from the extreme … inverting the mode-mirror fails HERE`) AND the exact-rung arm fire by name.
- **(c) REST-ONLY exemption is real:** temporarily added a hover/pressed on-fill ink-contrast assertion to GATE B and confirmed it fails on the dark band (the ~1.78:1 hover the exemption blesses), proving the exemption is load-bearing and not vacuous — then REMOVED it (kept GATE B rest-only).
- Full `npm run verify` FOREGROUND: **58/58 PASS**. Engine suite 3742/0. Every mode's REST contrast contract still passes; the worst non-rest on-fill ink is 2.54:1 (above the 2.0 rendered floor) BY DESIGN.

**Traps for re-verifiers.** (1) CONTRACT stays 10.3.0 — do NOT bump to 10.4.0; hover/pressed rebind to EXISTING ramp rungs and rest keeps the absolute, so no guaranteed name moved (`token-contract --check` says "no guaranteed path moved", guaranteed 587). (2) REST is UNCHANGED — do NOT "restore" a white/black hover; #1456 keeps #1384's crisp absolute at rest and only steps hover/pressed. (3) The stepped hover/pressed on-fill ink dipping below AA is BY DESIGN (owner: hover/pressed exempt) — do NOT re-introduce a per-state ink contrast gate; that was #1384's mistake, and re-adding it would force the flat fill back. (4) The step anchors at the EXTREME (white ≈ 0, black ≈ 1000) and walks INWARD — this is why light lands 100/200 and dark lands 900/800; do NOT confuse it with #1389's fill, which anchored at `neutral.850` and stepped toward the ground (a much bigger ink drop that #1384 read as a failure). (5) Bump `version.ts` BEFORE regen (the stamp lands in every tree). (6) Smoke drives the built `dist` — needs a Chromium available before `verify`. (7) If `regen --check` disagrees, look for an untracked file under `packages/engine/out/` before assuming drift. (8) `token-contract.json` is NEVER in regen — its `engineVersion` stamp is refreshed only by `token-contract.ts --accept` (stamp-only here, contract 10.3.0 unchanged).

## (2026-09-16) — icon-button follows Button 1:1 apart from `shape`: per-state glyph ink + a new `surface` axis (#1427)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). Branch `claude/fix-1427-icon-button` off main (ENGINE 0.98.0 / CONTRACT 10.3.0, after #1341 + #1384 landed).** **ENGINE bump 0.98.0 → provisional 0.99.0 (the projected component surface moves — a new `surface` variant axis + per-state glyph ink — a `lint-component-surface` #1252 trigger; a rebase relay reassigns the ENGINE integer to the true next-free above main before merge). CONTRACT STANDS at 10.3.0 — NO bump.** Implements the two decision-free `icon-button` fixes the Figma-import QA (2026-09-15, ENGINE 0.87.0) found, across all three families (icon-button / -destructive / -neutral, the shared `makeIconButton` factory), plus the owner's 2026-09-16 instruction that the added `surface` axis inherits #1384's white-inverse model.

**WHY CONTRACT DOES NOT BUMP (read before "correcting" it to 10.4.0).** The orchestrator's provisional was CONTRACT MINOR → 10.4.0, on the assumption that adding the `surface` axis adds guaranteed inverse icon-button token/prop NAMES. It does not: a variant axis is a component-PROJECTION change, not a token EMISSION change. The inverse roles it binds — `color.inverse.interactive.<family>.*` — ALREADY ship (bound by Button since #1134), and a component prop/variant name is not part of the token-name contract (`token-contract.json` versions the guaranteed TOKEN-name surface). `token-contract.ts --check` shows guaranteed **587 unchanged** and prints *"no guaranteed path moved — no version bump required"*; `--accept` says *"baseline accepted at 10.3.0 (no surface change)"* and refreshes only the informational `engineVersion` stamp (0.98.0 → 0.99.0). This is the exact **#1353 precedent** (adding the `shape` axis to icon-button kept CONTRACT put) and the #1384/#1429 rule: the objective gate result decides the bump, not the provisional guess.

**WHAT CHANGED, and why each is what the issue/owner asked.**
- **(item 1) THE GLYPH INK NOW WALKS STATE on `outline`/`text`.** It was pinned to `.rest` while the container's edge (`outline`) and overlay wash (`outline`/`text`) moved per state — so an outline icon-button's border stepped on hover/pressed while its glyph did not, and a text icon-button's glyph sat unchanged while the overlay wash lightened the ground beneath it (the same composited-contrast collapse Button measured, #1351). This is Button's **#1282/#1351** change reaching the icon-only control: four keys per family added in `iconButtonIntentTokens` — `outline.icon.{hover,pressed}` and `text.icon.{hover,pressed}`, each binding `color.interactive.<family>.text.<state>`, the very roles `iText` has emitted since #576 and that the border already consumes by value. Nothing new in the token tier; the glyph now walks the SAME three steps the label does on Button. Neutral's ink is `walkable:false`, so its three states collapse onto rest exactly as the border does — no change to a neutral icon-button. `filled.icon` stays `on-fill` (static — the ink sits on a solid fill, not a wash), item 1 is scoped to outline/text.
- **(item 2) A NEW `surface` AXIS (default / inverse), following Button 1:1.** icon-button had appearance:3 / shape:2 / size:3 / state:6 but NO `surface` axis while Button has surface:2. Added `surface: ['default','inverse']` to `variants`, the `surface` prop, and `figmaProperties.variantAxes`, and turned the focus-ring's `nest-fixed` into `follow: ['surface']` (the one line Button carries — the def's own note literally predicted this). **APPENDED after `shape`** so the three axes Button shares (appearance/size/surface) keep their relative order and `shape` stays the one icon-button-specific axis; the existing `shape` axis is untouched at its #1353 position (minimal diff). Each set DOUBLES 108 → 216 (3 appearance × 3 size × 2 shape × 2 surface × 6 state). No projector change was needed — the inverse rewrite is already generic (keyed on the `surface` axis by NAME in `anatomy-figma.ts`) and `surface` was already in the closed `VARIANT_AXES` vocabulary.
- **(item 3) INVERSE ICON-BUTTONS INHERIT #1384's WHITE-INVERSE MODEL 1:1, with the ICON as the "ink".** No new binding: a `surface=inverse` FILLED member's container binds the SHARED `color.inverse.interactive.<family>.fill.rest` role #1384 made white (the projector's `color.* → color.inverse.*` rewrite), and its glyph binds the inverse `on-fill` — the role #1384 GATE B floors ≥4.5 on the white fill. So primary inverse icon-button = white fill + primary icon-ink, neutral = white + neutral icon-ink, destructive = white + destructive icon-ink, all AA-clean on white by the same contrast-aware mechanism Button uses. The shared `inverse.interactive.<family>.fill` role and the `white` fill-source are INHERITED, NOT re-minted — exactly the "icon-button inherits white for free once #1427 adds the axis" property #1384's blast-radius note recorded. **No STOP-AND-FLAG:** no brand's family icon-ink failed to stay itself and clear AA on white (the token-tier #1384 GATE A/B, which assert these shared roles, still pass 3740/0).
- **NO HOVER-WASH ON THE INVERSE FILL (deliberate — owner decision pending).** #1384 made the inverse fill FLAT (no per-state feedback) and deferred the hover/pressed WASH as a SEPARATE owner design decision. ## (2026-09-16) — transparent field fill + contrast-aware border + hover wash (#1341/#1342)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). Branch `claude/fix-1341-1342-transparent-field-fill`.** **ENGINE bump 0.95.0 → provisional 0.97.0 (values + projected surface both move — see below; a rebase relay reassigns to the true next-free integer above main before merge). CONTRACT 10.2.0 → 10.3.0 (one guaranteed ADDITION, `core.palette.transparent`; nothing removed or retyped).** Implements the OWNER-DECIDED spec recorded on #1341 (2026-09-14, refined 2026-09-15, reaffirmed 2026-09-16) — TRANSPARENT over the issue body's original "white default". Closes #1341 AND #1342.

**WHAT CHANGED, and why each is what the owner decided.**
- **A `transparent` alpha-0 COLOUR primitive** (`core.palette.transparent`), added beside `white`/`black` in `tree.ts` via the same `alphaLeaf` mechanism the `*-alpha` ramps use (so the sibling #1384 can add opaque white/black fill *sources* the same way — the mechanism generalizes, this PR scopes it to `transparent`). It is a colour value (`rgba(0,0,0,0)` / `#00000000`), DISTINCT from the `opacity.*` number scale (a multiplier) and from the `white-/black-alpha` ramps (which start at 5%). "No paint," expressed as a colour.
- **`color.field.fill` AND `color.inverse.field.fill` default to it** (kept themable — only the default VALUE moves; a brand may still point either at a solid surface). The inverse twin moves too, to keep #892's page/inverse mirror invariant ("every inverse rule is its page sibling's with the ground swapped") — a field is paint-less on the page AND on a dark band.
- **Contrast-aware field border (a real a11y change, #1341's finding).** With a transparent fill the BORDER is the field boundary, so `color.field.border.{rest,hover}` are re-gated to clear the non-text floor (SC 1.4.11, ≥3:1) against the DARKEST permissible ground — `background.secondary` — not the page. The old border measured ~3.3:1 on white but **~2.7:1 on the off-white secondary surface** (aurora's was literally `#8e8e92` at 2.69). Result: one step darker in LIGHT only (nb/aurora `neutral.400→450`, harbor `450→500`), **byte-identical in dark/HC** (already cleared secondary; in HC secondary===primary===base). Placeholder likewise re-points its ground off the now-transparent `field.fill` to `background.secondary` (same rgb, so the pick is byte-identical — only the recorded `against` moves). Both borders + placeholder are REPRESENTED and gated in every mode, so the per-mode contrast contract enforces this going forward.
- **Hover is an alpha WASH, not a solid fill (#1342).** `select` (the component #1342 opened on) gains an `overlay` paintSlot on its control, bound to the existing `color.interactive.neutral.overlay.hover` (a 10% neutral wash that tints relative to the CURRENT ground — the button outline/text overlay pattern #1210/#1233). Precedence `overlay > fill`: the transparent fill at rest, the wash at hover. No new role, no invented alpha. `pressed` is not a select state, so only `hover` washes. `text-field` has no anatomy (it is a code-only composition brief, not projected), so it carries no paint; its hover stays border-only in its own model and the family reuse is available to any code consumer.
- **Disabled keeps its solid fill** (WCAG-exempt), unchanged.
- **Studio Source control for `field.fill`** (the missing-control gap the issue named): a "Field fill" row in the Foreground-fills editor (shared `apps/studio/src` drives studio + plugin). "Auto" reads **Transparent (no paint)**; picking a neutral step gives a solid fill. Contrast-marked on the value ink (`text.primary` ≥4.5 on the picked step) — the field analogue of the on-fill gate.

**WHY "darkest permissible ground" is `background.secondary`, and why this is NOT a held design decision (the one place a re-verifier might expect a STOP).** The owner decided "≥3:1 on the darkest permissible ground" but not which concrete ground that is, and a secondary-gated border still fails 3:1 on the *even darker* `background.tertiary` (measured 2.79/2.78/2.92). The tie-break is the engine's OWN established policy, not a fresh pick: every contrast-gated foreground (`text.secondary`, the bold fills, …) already validates against `cfg.floor`, "the worst-case supported surface", which resolves to the `background.secondary` tier (nb `neutral.050`, harbor `neutral.100`). Tertiary is *beyond* the floor for those roles too — text is not guaranteed on it either — so gating the field border at the floor is consistent with the whole system, matches the owner's worked `#E9E9EA` example exactly, and is the strictly-worse of the two page tiers a field realistically sits on in every mode (so the pick only ever strengthens, never weakens). Choosing tertiary would be a heavier border the owner did not ask for; choosing the floor is the mechanical implementation of the decision, so it is executed, not surfaced.

**VERSIONING.** CONTRACT is a clean MINOR: `token-contract.ts --accept` shows exactly one line, `ADDED core.palette.transparent`; the field names keep their names and `color` type (only default values move), the border re-points a *ground* not a path, and the hover reuses an existing role. ENGINE moves for VALUES (every brand's field fill + the light border) via `lint-emission-version`, AND for the projected component surface (select's overlay paint) via `lint-component-surface` (#1252) — both baselines `--accept`ed forward, and `schema/paint-census.json` re-accepted for select's new hover-overlay assignments.

**SAFETY NET — by-name mutation arms in `test.ts` (docs/34), verified by mutating each subject and confirming the named arm goes red:**
- `field(#1341)` fill arm — `field.fill` AND `inverse.field.fill` alias `core.palette.transparent` in every mode; mutate either back to `cfg.bg.secondary` (a solid) → fires.
- `field(#1341)` border arm — RECOMPUTES `contrast(border, background.secondary)` from the two roles' own hexes (does NOT trust the recorded `ratio`, the lint-ratio-truth lesson) and asserts ≥ the non-text floor on the DARKEST ground; mutate the pick's ground back to the page (`baseRgb`, the old `#8E8E92`) → the recomputed contrast drops below 3 and this arm fires by name even though the mislabelled recorded ratio would have passed.
- `#1342` hover-wash arms — `select` binds `overlay.hover → color.interactive.neutral.overlay.hover`, its control paints an `overlay` slot, and that role is an `ink-on-composite` wash with `0 < alpha < 1` in every mode; mutate the binding to a solid role → the alpha/model check fires.
- Plus every mode's contrast contract still passes (788/788 harbor), and the wireframe greyscale contract and the NB Figma-palette fixture check were extended (not weakened) to admit `transparent` as a colourless primitive alongside `white`/`black`.

**Traps for re-verifiers.** (1) The light-mode border darkening is the DESIGNED a11y fix, not drift — do not "restore" `neutral.400`; it fails 3:1 on the off-white surface, which is the whole point. (2) `field.fill`'s resolved role `hex` is the transparent primitive's opaque base (`#000000`) — never read it as a display colour; the studio row shows `background.primary` when transparent, and the emitted DTCG value is the alias `{…core.palette.transparent}`, not the hex. (3) `background.secondary` is now referenced as an `against` ground by the field roles, so it enters `groundsOf`; both sides are computed, so they still agree. (4) ENGINE bump is owed on BOTH counts (values via `lint-emission-version`, surface via `lint-component-surface`) — do not drop it. (5) If `regen --check` disagrees, look for an untracked file under `packages/engine/out/` before assuming drift.

**FOLLOW-UP TO FILE (flagged for the orchestrator, not opened here).** The knowledge-base has **no POV on the default field fill** (recorded on #1341). A `from:prism3` intake issue + a `09-gaps` note in the knowledge-base is warranted now that transparent has shipped as the engine's answer — per the KB's own routing. Also latent: applying the hover wash to `text-field`/`textarea` needs those defs to gain anatomy (they are code-only today); tracked adjacent to #1342, not folded in here (surgical).
