## (2026-09-16) — the 44px interactive hit-target floor, codified as policy + a by-name gate (#1443)

**STATUS: PR #1454 open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). Branch `claude/fix-1443-hittarget-floor-gate` off main (ENGINE 0.96.0 / CONTRACT 10.2.0).** **NO ENGINE bump — docs + a new gate only; `lint-emission-version` reports 0 artifacts changed vs base, so no bump is owed (the #1396 executor/test-only precedent). CONTRACT stands at 10.2.0.** #1443 (owner-decided, from #1437): interactive controls adopt a 44px hit-target floor (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.5 Enhanced), about the TOUCH/hit area rather than the visual size.

**THE MODEL (owner-decided, 2026-09-15 + a 2026-09-16 correction).** The floor governs the **comfortable and spacious** densities. At a control's default size the `md` rung is 44px (comfortable) / 56px (spacious), so a control meets the floor there by binding that rung; `select` also binds `size.md.min-height` = `max(size.md.height, 44)` (#1426/#1437). There are exactly **two permanent, owner-decided exceptions** and nothing else: (1) **small button** — knowingly below the floor; (2) **compact density** — a deliberate dense/desktop mode, allowed below the floor. The compact exception is scoped to compact ALONE — a control below 44 on comfortable or spacious is a real failure, not a density affordance. (The first cut of this lane, following the initial unblock, modeled the sub-44 controls as a TRACKED-GAP tier keyed to a filed issue #1453; the 2026-09-16 correction blessed compact density as a permanent exception, so those are not gaps and #1453 was closed by-design.)

**WHAT SHIPPED.** (1) A policy note in `docs/28` (§4, beside the `touch-target-expansion` ceiling): the floor, its rationale, and BOTH exceptions. (2) `packages/engine/lint-hit-target.ts`, wired into `verify.ts` + `ci.yml` + `CLAUDE.md` §4 + `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 + the PR template (count 57 → 58; `lint-doc-gates` green, 58 vs 58 both directions).

**THE GATE, AND WHY IT IS INDEPENDENT (docs/34).** EXPECTED is `FLOOR_PX = 44`, a LITERAL, deliberately NOT `scale.ts`'s `AAA_TARGET_PX` — the emitter derives `select`'s `min-height` from that constant, so sharing it would assert `x >= x` (shape 2). ACTUAL is the px of the token each control ACTUALLY binds at its DEFAULT size (read through `def.tokens[bindKey]`), resolved from a fresh tree built at each density from one base brand input — so the floor is tested against the density LEVER the compact exception is scoped to. **Density scoping is asserted:** each build is asserted to be the density it claims, so a comfortable brand cannot be mislabeled compact and slip past the floor, and the compact measurement cannot be credited to a comfortable one. **Both exceptions self-justify:** small button and the compact `md` are each asserted to be actually BELOW 44, so a future lift fails by name rather than persisting. **Representation, not count:** every def in `componentDefs` is measured or EXCLUDED with a reason (nested atoms whose target is the row above, the group whose rows are the targets, the fluid multi-line textarea, the non-interactive parts). **Mutation-proven:** pointing `button`'s default (`size.medium.height`) at the smaller `size.sm.height` rung resolves 36px on the comfortable build and the floor assertion fires by name for all three button-family defs; restored, green.

**MEASUREMENT (the reason this stopped to flag twice).** At default size, every interactive control clears 44 on comfortable (44) and spacious (56); on compact the `md` rung is 36 (now a blessed exception). Deliverable #3: `switch-control` does NOT have a 44px padding hit area — it is a nested-only 24–32px atom whose tap target is the `switch` row, and the row binds `size.md.height` (36 on compact). Surfaced to the owner rather than allowlisted; resolved by the compact-density exception (the row meets 44 on comfortable/spacious, and compact is a blessed dense mode). `textarea` is excluded (fluid multi-line height, no single-line dimension). No genuine comfortable/spacious gap exists, so no gap issues are filed and #1453 is closed by-design.

**Traps for re-verifiers.** (1) The floor is a LITERAL 44, not `AAA_TARGET_PX` — do not "DRY" them together; that is the shape-2 collapse the header forbids. (2) The floor governs comfortable + spacious; compact is a PERMANENT exception, not a gap — do not file compact-density gap issues (that was the pre-correction model; #1453 is closed by-design). (3) The gate reads the token a control BINDS at its DEFAULT size, not a rendered pixel — `button`'s CSS `::before` hit overlay and the rows' consumer padding are not emitted. Non-default small variants sit at the same 36px `sm` rung as the small button on comfortable; whether to gate them too is a scope the owner has not extended (noted in `docs/28`). (4) NO engine bump: `lint-emission-version` = 0 artifacts changed is the objective test; `regen --check` byte-identical (108 artifacts).

## (2026-09-16) — emitted component SETS keep their variant-set frame (#1430)

**STATUS: PR #1449 open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). REBASED onto post-#1424/#1433/#1429/#1428 main (2026-09-16).** **ENGINE bump 0.95.0 → 0.96.0 (rebased: main took 0.94.0 for the #1424/#1433 row bundle and 0.95.0 for #1428 select ref-wiring; #1429 was gate-only and consumed no integer, so 0.96.0 is the next free above 0.95.0 — the provisional first cut was 0.98.0 off 0.93.0 main). CONTRACT stays 10.2.0.** #1430 (owner-triaged QoL: a natively-created Figma component set gets a dashed purple set outline; our emitted sets didn't, making them hard to pick out on a busy canvas). The issue posed a correctness fork first, and the answer clears it.

**THE DIAGNOSIS — case (b), with evidence; NOT case (a).** The emitted sets ARE genuine `ComponentSetNode`s, so the projection/node model is correct (variant switching, the properties panel, publishing all work). Evidence: `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts` builds the set with `figma.combineAsVariants(fresh, api.currentPage)` (a `CompSet`/`ComponentSetNode`), and the host reads it back as `type === 'COMPONENT_SET'` — now asserted directly in `test-roundtrip.ts` (`page.children[0].type`). So this is NOT (a), a projection emitting plain frames grouped some other way. It is (b), a **presentation strip**: `combineAsVariants` returns a container Figma has already dressed as a variant set (a 5px radius, a purple dashed border, an opaque fill), and #865's default-claim (`claimDefaults(wr(set), null, …)`) BLANKED all of it to a bare frame — `strokes=[]`, `dashPattern=[]`, corners 0. That neutralization is exactly why an emitted set read as an ordinary frame. The PASTE path (`anatomy-figma.ts`) never neutralized the set (its #865 claim is member-only), so only the plugin stripped it.

**THE FIX — preserve the BORDER as a #865 claim, keep the fill neutral.** For the set node — the sole `claimDefaults(n === null)` call; every member carries a plan — `strokes`/`strokeWeight`/`strokeAlign`/`dashPattern` and the four corner radii are now claimed by PRESERVING what the host dressed the set with (a `keep` helper: read the live value, write it back, so #865's "every visual property is a decision" still holds) rather than blanking them. **Preserve, not a hardcoded purple**, because the exact values are Figma's own and are recorded nowhere offline to re-assert — echoing the host keeps an emitted set's border pixel-identical to a native one, which is the whole of the ask; a guessed literal is the thing that would drift. **The opaque FILL is the one framing property NOT preserved** — it is cleared to transparent, because keeping it would put a solid box behind whatever a designer arranges around the set AND would trip #1387's no-opaque-white rule; a set's canvas identity is its dashed purple border, not a fill. Every other non-framing default on the set still neutralizes. Members are untouched (the change forks only on `isSet`).

**SAFETY NET — host-observable, so asserted BY NAME (docs/34).** The set-ness and the border are host-observable, so `test-roundtrip.ts` gets a `#1430` block over the WHOLE projected corpus (the strip affected every set): every emitted set reads back as a real `ComponentSetNode` carrying a non-empty dashed stroke and a set-shaped radius. The shared `component-shim.ts` now MODELS the border `combineAsVariants` applies (a bare `COMPONENT_SET` from `mkNode` could not tell the fix from the #865 blank — docs/34 shape 4); the oracle is authored in the gate, not derived from the executor. **Mutation-verified:** reverting `keep('strokes')` back to the #865 `set('strokes', [])` fires the positive arm by name, STRIPPED-listing every emitted set (`icon`, `focus-ring`, `button`, …); a negative arm (a set stripped of its stroke IS reported) proves the check is not vacuous. The framing VALUES themselves cannot be pinned offline (no live host); what is checkable — and what the defect was — is whether the executor DESTROYS a border the host supplied.

**Versioning.** PLUGIN-SIDE — the set frame is a live Figma object, not an emitted artifact, so the logic itself produces no `out/**` diff and `lint-emission-version` does not compel the bump. But the built set is a consumer-observable change and `ENGINE_VERSION` is the "what code produced this" answer (and the MCP `serverInfo.version`), so it moves; the only `out/**` churn is the re-stamped `generator.version` across the eight token files (regen run). CONTRACT stays 10.2.0 — no guaranteed token NAME moves (this is node-type styling, not tokens); `token-contract --check` confirms the guaranteed surface unchanged.

**Traps for re-verifiers.** (1) The fix forks ONLY on `isSet` (`n === null`, the set); the member INK branch was carefully preserved byte-for-byte (a first cut wrongly excluded TEXT members from the strokes/dashPattern claim and broke #865 — the strokes/dashPattern block runs for every created member, TEXT included). (2) The fill is deliberately NOT preserved (cleared to transparent) — do not "restore" it to match `combineAsVariants`; it would obscure content and trip #1387. (3) `component-shim.ts` seeds only the border/radius, not a fill, for the same reason. (4) Smoke needs `npx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell` in a fresh container before `verify`.

## (2026-09-16) — `select` host-truth: a nested-instance part-name collision dropped the `value` reference (#1428)

**STATUS: PR #1450 open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). REBASED onto post-#1424/#1433/#1429 main (2026-09-16).** **ENGINE bump 0.94.0 → 0.95.0 (rebased: main took 0.94.0 for the #1424/#1433 row bundle; #1429 was gate-only and consumed no integer, so 0.95.0 is the next free above 0.94.0 — the provisional first cut was 0.96.0 off 0.93.0 main). CONTRACT STANDS at 10.2.0** (a projection/binding fix adds no token NAME — `token-contract.ts --check` confirms the guaranteed surface unchanged). The QA of the Figma plugin import (2026-09-15, ENGINE 0.87.0) reported `select` dropping **40 component-property references** — `leadingVisual.mainComponent -> ↳ swap leading icon`, `leadingVisual.visible -> leading icon`, and `text.characters -> value` — with Figma's own `set_componentPropertyReferences: Could not create a new component property reference`, all cited on `status=warning, state=hover` coordinates.

**THE DIAGNOSIS — a NODE-NAME COLLISION across a nested composition, NOT a variant-matrix bug.** `select` is the only def that COMPOSES two other components as in-flow instances: it nests `field-label` AND `field-message`. **Both of those defs have a part named `text`** (field-label's label text; field-message's caption) — the SAME name as select's own value node, also `text`. Both write executors (the plugin's `applyComponentPlan` and the engine's paste payload `PAYLOAD_WIRE_REFS`) re-find each part by name to wire its Figma reference — `member.findOne(x => x.name === 'text')` — and **Figma's `findOne` descends INTO nested instances.** So the lookup returned a `text` layer that lives *inside* the field-label (or field-message) instance — a sublayer of ANOTHER component, which cannot hold *this* set's reference. Figma refuses with "Could not create a new component property reference", and the `value` binding is dropped.

**Why only `text`, and why the `(warning/hover)` framing is incidental.** `leadingVisual` has a UNIQUE name and `message` is matched on the nested-instance node ITSELF (a valid target), so neither ever collided — which is exactly why `message.visible` was never in the QA list. Only `text.characters` collides. The collision is **per-member and general** — every one of the 16 members' `text` read-back lands on the wrong node — so the warning/hover coordinates were simply where the live build's throw path happened to surface (the `leadingVisual` misses in the 0.87.0 log were the raw pre-#1337 detach with no recovery; #1337's recovery re-finds by name and so was itself defeated by this same collision for `text`). Reproduced offline: with the nested `text` modeled, **all 16 members** report the dropped `value` reference; 0 with the fix.

**THE FIX — `findOwnPart`, in BOTH executors (they share the one-plan-two-executors contract).** A scoped re-find that matches a part by name WITHOUT descending into a nested INSTANCE (`apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts` for the plugin's recovery + ref/binding read-backs; the `PAYLOAD_WIRE_REFS` string in `packages/engine/anatomy-figma.ts` for the paste path's wire + read-back). A referenced part is ALWAYS the member's own layer — Figma forbids referencing a nested instance's internals — so skipping instance subtrees loses nothing and lands the lookup on the right node. The nested-instance node itself is still matched by name (select's swap slot and `message` nest are referenced ON the instance, not inside it). Still an independent re-query of the live tree (reads `children`), so the docs/34 read-back property is preserved — the search is scoped, not short-circuited. **The plan/projection is unchanged** — the fix is in the two EXECUTORS, so `lint-component-surface`'s `planStamp` and every emitted token tree are byte-identical; committed `out/` moves ONLY on the `engineVersion` stamp (8 files).

**SAFETY NET — mutation-verified BY NAME (docs/34), one gate per executor.** The offline shims model nested instances as OPAQUE stubs, so both host-truth harnesses were blind to this by construction — the subject was under-modeled. Both now take an opt-in `nestedInstanceParts` that makes each nested instance carry a colliding `text` child whose `componentPropertyReferences` setter REFUSES the write, exactly as a sublayer of another component does. **`apps/plugin/test-roundtrip.ts`'s #1428 arm** drives select's PLUGIN executor; **`packages/engine/test.ts`'s #1428 arm** drives its PASTE payload. Each has a **reachability floor** (a naive descending `findOne` returns the flagged nested `text`, proving the collision materialized — not an empty-set silence) and then asserts select's `value` reference survives on every member. Reverting `findOwnPart` in either executor fails ITS named assertion — paste with the live host's own "Could not create a new component property reference", plugin read-back with `text.characters -> DISCARDED`. Verified by reverting each in turn: exactly the one #1428 arm goes red, by name.

**Versioning rationale (read before re-verifying the bump).** Neither emission gate FORCES this bump: `lint-emission-version` is blind to component payloads (not committed under `out/`) and `lint-component-surface` hashes the PLAN, which did not move (the fix is in the executors). The bump is owed by version.ts's surface rule — "what a consumer can OBSERVE" — because a consumer who pastes the payload or runs the plugin now gets select's `value` reference where it was silently dropped. Recorded in `version.ts` and here precisely because no red enforces it. CONTRACT holds: no guaranteed token NAME is added, removed or retyped.

**Traps for re-verifiers.** (1) The bump is policy-owed, not gate-forced — do not "correct" it to no-bump because `regen --check` is green without it; the emitted trees are identical apart from the stamp. (2) `findOwnPart` matches the nested-instance NODE by name but does not descend into it — a swap slot (an INSTANCE that IS a referenced part) is still found; only its internals are skipped. (3) The two `nestedInstanceParts` shim opts inject a THROWING ref setter on the nested child (a node inside a nested instance is not referenceable) — an accepting setter would let the read-back "repair" onto the wrong node and hide the miss. (4) Smoke needs `npx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell` in a fresh container before `verify`. (5) If `regen --check` disagrees, look for an untracked file under `packages/engine/out/` before assuming drift.

## (2026-09-16) — #1429 overlay-wash "misses" are a telemetry reading, not a dropped wash; gated in test:roundtrip against the emitted brand

**STATUS: PR #1448 open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). REBASED onto post-#1424/#1433 main (2026-09-16).** **NO ENGINE bump owed — ENGINE taken from main at 0.94.0, CONTRACT at 10.2.0.** This is a gate-only change: one assertion block added to `apps/plugin/test-roundtrip.ts` and its three engine imports. No emitted artifact moves, no projected member moves, no token/prop NAME moves — the #1396/#1387/#1332/#1377 precedent for an executor/test-only change (a host-truth/read-back gate). After regen, `lint-emission-version` reports **0 artifacts changed** between the merge base and HEAD, which is the objective test that no bump is owed; so `ENGINE_VERSION` MATCHES main's 0.94.0 rather than inventing a fresh integer for a change that emits nothing. `regen --check` byte-identical, `token-contract --check` unchanged at guaranteed 586 / 10.2.0. The lane's provisional `0.97.0` assumed an emission code change; the diagnosis is (b) and the fix is a gate, so no bump — settled by the `lint-emission-version` result, not by assertion.

**THE FINDING (QA 2026-09-15, ENGINE 0.87.0):** all button families reported **96** misses and all icon-button families **24**, of the form `container.fills -> color/interactive/<primary|destructive|neutral>/overlay/{hover,pressed}` — read as "the hover/pressed overlay wash is not being bound on the container across the corpus."

**DIAGNOSIS — (b), A TELEMETRY READING, NOT A DROPPED WASH.** Reproduced live at 0.93.0, two measurements:
- **The projection DOES apply the wash.** The `container` box declares `paintSlots: ['overlay','fill','border']` (`button.ts:348` / `icon-button.ts:216`), so on an outline/text hover/pressed coordinate `interactive.<c>.overlay.<state>` (the translucent wash) binds onto `container.fills`. Measured by building through the shim and reading the container back: **96** wash bindings per button family, **12** per icon-button family (the QA's 24 was the 0.87.0 icon-button projection; that def's member set has since changed — the overlay mechanism is unchanged). Quoted plan: `container.paints.fills = "color/interactive/primary/overlay/hover"` on a `state=hover, appearance=outline` member.
- **The emitter DOES emit it, and it resolves.** Cross-checking every button/icon-button plan paint/bound var against the engine's actually-emitted Figma variable tails (`buildFigmaColor(theme)`), across the whole corpus: **0 dangling on every `outlineInteraction: 'overlay-neutral'` brand** (nb, aurora, harbor, wendys, minimal) and **18 on `minimal-levers` (`outlineInteraction: 'none'`)** — exactly the `interactive.*.overlay.{hover,pressed}` fills (page + inverse). This reproduces #1387's measurement byte-for-byte.

So the wash binds and resolves wherever the brand uses it. The 96/24 QA misses came from a brand on `outlineInteraction: 'none'` (the `minimal-levers` corpus member), which DELIBERATELY does not emit the wash; the brand-agnostic component binds it regardless, the paste's name-resolution channel reports the miss, and **#1387 already neutralizes the visual to transparent** (never Figma's white). Counting a legitimate opt-out as a corpus-wide defect was the false positive. No projection or emission change was made — a disproven "genuinely dropped" premise is a result.

**THE GATE GAP, now closed (docs/34 shape 11).** #1387's own review named it: `test-roundtrip.ts` stocks its shim's variable catalogue FROM THE PLAN (`fullFor`), so a bound paint ALWAYS resolves — a wash the engine never emits, or emits under a drifted name, round-trips green. The only witness is an INDEPENDENT ORACLE: the token layer the engine actually emits (`emit-figma-color`/`modes.ts`), a code path separate from the projection (`anatomy-figma`). The new block reads each container's bound wash off the HOST (what the executor wrote) and checks it against `buildFigmaColor(nbTheme())`'s emitted tails. Three positive checks + two negative controls, all citing #1429:
- **(1) per-family reachability floor** — the wash is bound on `container.fills` in EVERY named family (`button{,-destructive,-neutral}`, `icon-button{,-destructive,-neutral}`). Per-family, not a corpus count, because the button factory is shared but icon-button is a separate def, so a corpus-wide `>0` would pass on a single-family drop (docs/34 representation).
- **(2) resolution** — every bound wash resolves against the independent emitted overlay-neutral brand: 0 dangling. This is the QA's "miss", proven ABSENT for a brand that uses the wash.
- **(3) right tokens** — the exact names the QA quoted (`color/interactive/primary/overlay/{hover,pressed}`) are bound (docs/34 shape 5, not a truthiness check).
- **negative (a) projection drop** and **(b) emission drop** prove neither check is vacuous.

**MUTATION-BY-NAME (docs/34), source-level, run before merge:**
- Drop `'overlay'` from BOTH defs' `container.paintSlots` → floor (1) fires alone, naming all six families `DROPPED IN`, and (3) fires for both primary names. 5 failed.
- Drop `'overlay'` from `button.ts` ONLY (icon-button keeps it) → floor (1) STILL fires, naming exactly `button, button-destructive, button-neutral` as `DROPPED IN`, while (3) passes because icon-button still binds `primary/overlay/hover`. This is the proof the per-family floor is load-bearing: a corpus-wide count would have gone green here.
- Restored: all PASS.

**TRAP FOR RE-VERIFIERS.** Do NOT "simplify" the oracle to the shim's own `fullFor` catalogue or to `planPaintVars` — that is precisely the shape-11 collapse this block exists to undo (the corpus loop above already resolves everything that way). The oracle must stay the engine's emitted layer. And the floor is per-FAMILY on purpose: reverting it to a single corpus `washBindings > 0` re-opens the single-family blind spot the mutation above exercises. `minimal-levers` (`outlineInteraction: 'none'`) legitimately has NO wash and must never be used as the resolution oracle — an overlay-neutral brand only.

## (2026-09-16) — radio/checkbox ROW QA bundle: labels WRAP, error keeps the selected fill, rows get top/bottom padding (#1424 + #1433)

**STATUS: PR #1446 open (base main), do NOT merge — orchestrator verifies + merges. REBASED onto post-#1425/#1426 main (2026-09-16).** **ENGINE 0.91.0 → 0.94.0 (the next free integer above main's 0.93.0 — #1426 select took 0.92.0, #1425 switch took 0.93.0); CONTRACT taken from main UNCHANGED at 10.2.0 (this lane adds no guaranteed token name).** Two owner-approved QA items on the radio/checkbox ROW family, bundled because they touch the same two defs — `radio` and `checkbox-row` (renamed from `checkbox` in #1347) — and the same anatomy region (the row + its label). Prism 2 is the measured target for both (`reference/Prism2/component-specs/{radio-button-row,checkbox-row}.json`).

**#1424 — LONG LABELS WRAP INSTEAD OF OVERFLOWING (decision-free).** Today a long row label grows the row horizontally off the edge; Prism 2 wraps it (its description text is `layoutSizingHorizontal: FILL`, control top-anchored). **Diagnosis:** the engine had no way to say "fill the main axis and reflow" — `sizing: 'fill'` maps to AUTO (#989), a known, deliberately-deferred limitation (`scale.ts`/`version.ts` both note that closing it needs `layoutGrow` threaded through the plan type, the projector and BOTH executors), and `field-message` already carries a latent `x: 'fill'` no-op — so I could NOT change `fill`'s global meaning without breaking it. **Fix:** a narrow, opt-in `PartDef.wrap` (text-only) → the plan carries two new fields, `layoutGrow: 1` (fill the row's main axis, fixing the WIDTH) + `textAutoResize: 'HEIGHT'` (auto height, so the fixed-width box reflows), threaded through both executors (`write-components.ts`'s neutralizer, driven off the plan and still an unconditional `set` so the #865 claim holds; the emitted payload) and classified in `anatomy-readback.ts` (so the corpus round-trip diffs them). Each row's `row` gains `minWidth: 320` (Prism 2's root width — a def-local LITERAL, the `select` #1345 precedent, NOT a token), because `layoutGrow` fills REMAINING space and a hugging row has none. The control side needs no change — `controlBox` is already `x:hug, y:fixed` and does not grow.

**#1433a — ERROR-STATE FILL (owner DECIDED, implemented as a LOCK).** Owner's decision: signal error on the control BORDER/RING (and the field-message), and KEEP the selected control's inner fill — the checkbox's filled box + check, the radio's inner dot — on the INTERACTIVE color; do NOT turn it red (color is not error's sole carrier). **The atoms already satisfied this on `b09ca0a`** (verified by projection: at `selection=checked, state=error`, checkbox-control's `control.fills` and radio-control's `dot.fills` both stay `color/interactive/primary/fill/selected` while `control.strokes` goes `color/border/danger` — there is no `checked.fill.error`/`checked.indicator.error` key, so error falls back to the interactive fill). So #1433a shipped NO atom change — the deliverable is the by-name gate that LOCKS it, which a red-fill mutation flips.

**#1433b — ROW TOP/BOTTOM PADDING. VALUE PINNED: `space.150` = 12px on nb.** Prism 2's rows sit content in `padding {top:12, bottom:12, start:0, end:0}` — a CONSTANT inset (the same 12 on the 48-tall checkbox row and the 56-tall radio row, NOT size-scaled). Both rows now bind `pad-y → space.150` (the nearest existing spacing step and an EXACT 12px match on nb — no new rung minted) and `pad-x → space.0` (inline zero), mirroring `checkbox-group`'s own padding exactly. **Decision (row padding): `space.150` (12px on nb).**

**CONTRACT taken from main at 10.2.0, no further bump.** `wrap`/`layoutGrow`/`textAutoResize`/`minWidth` are STRUCTURE (schema + plan + projection), never emitted token NAMES; the padding binds EXISTING guaranteed names (`space.150`, `space.0`, both already emitted). This lane adds no guaranteed token name, so on the rebase it inherits main's 10.2.0 (#1426 → 10.1.0, #1425 → 10.2.0) with nothing to add — `token-contract --check` confirms the guaranteed 586 unchanged. **ENGINE bumped** because the projected component surface of both rows moves (#1252): `lint-component-surface` flagged both digests and was `--accept`ed after the forward bump (member COUNT unchanged, 3→3, plans changed).

**Safety net (docs/34, by-name).** #1424: `test.ts` reads the projected plan and pins, for BOTH rows, label→(layoutGrow 1 + textAutoResize HEIGHT) and control→fixed/hug, with a mutation dropping `wrap` that flips the label assertion BY NAME; plus the two NEW refusal arms `PartDef.wrap` adds (wrap on a non-text kind; wrap under a floorless row) each with its own by-name mutation — the floorless-row arm makes the row's `minWidth` load-bearing rather than decorative. `test-roundtrip.ts` reads the same two facts back off the built shim with an oracle authored THERE, so a def that stops wrapping fails there even though the generic plan-vs-host diff would still agree (the aspect-lock independence pattern). #1433a: `test.ts` reads the projected error member and pins, for BOTH atoms, fill-stays-interactive (== the rest fill, == the interactive role) / border-goes-danger, with a mutation binding the forbidden `checked.fill.error`/`checked.indicator.error` → danger that flips it BY NAME. Engine suite 3638→3654 (16 new), 0 failed.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** (1) `layoutGrow`/`textAutoResize` are child/text-side properties the plugin NEUTRALIZER writes (not the main bind loop) — they are driven off the plan there (`n?.layoutGrow ?? 0`, `n?.textAutoResize ?? 'WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT'`) and still `set()` unconditionally so `lint-unclaimed-defaults` stays satisfied. The emitted payload writes them too (both executors), so a pasted script wraps identically. (2) The offline shim/round-trip verifies the fields READ BACK; it does NOT run layout, so real-host WRAP (a two-line label with the control on line one) is offline-unverified — the same posture as the decomposition nest-sizing notes. (3) `minWidth: 320` is a LITERAL, not a token (no CONTRACT touch); if `regen --check` disagrees look for an untracked file under `out/` before assuming drift. (4) Bump `version.ts` BEFORE `regen` (the stamp lands in every tree). (5) Smoke needs `npx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell` in a fresh container before `verify`.

## (2026-09-15) — `switch-control` scaled to Prism 2's toggle proportions (#1425)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.92.0 → 0.93.0; CONTRACT bump 10.1.0 → 10.2.0 (MINOR, additive).** (Rebased onto post-#1426 main — see the serialization trap below; the first cut was 0.88.0 / 10.1.0 off 0.87.0 main.) The #1425 lane (owner-triaged, `engine`+`a11y`, decision-free calibration against Prism 2 + the hit-target floor). QA of the Figma plugin import found `switch-control` at **~half Prism 2's scale** — a 16px track at aurora's largest switch rung, a thumb half that, a 2px border reading heavy, and no track meeting the hit-target minimum in isolation.

**THE DIAGNOSIS — the switch was BORROWING the wrong tier fields.** `switch-control` bound its track HEIGHT to `control.size.*.height` (the SQUARE box a checkbox/radio reads, 16/20 on nb, 12/16 on aurora) and its thumb to `control.size.*.dot` (half that box). So the track was one checkbox-box tall and the thumb half again — structurally incapable of Prism 2's 32px track / 24px thumb, because the shared box tier caps the thumb at 0.5× and can't reach a 32px edge without dragging checkbox/radio up with it. `scale.ts`'s own #997 header had already named the blocker: *"0.75 is not adoptable without splitting `dot` away from radio."* #1425 does that split.

**THE FIX — the switch gets its OWN two tier fields.** `control.size.*` now carries `track` (the switch's cross-axis edge, a density-windowed ladder `[16,24,32,40,48]` — multiples of 8 so the 0.75 thumb and centred inset stay integer) and `thumb` (`0.75 × track`, Prism 2's 24-in-32). `width` rebased from `2× height` to `2× track` (2:1, field-convergent) and `inset` from `(height − dot) / 2` to `(track − thumb) / 2` — both switch-only fields, so **checkbox and radio, which read only `height`/`dot`, do not move a pixel**. At the default density `md` is Prism 2 exactly: track 32, thumb 24, width 64 (its focus-variant width, 2:1 on-grid), inset 4, 2px border, pill. `switch-control` rebinds track-height←`.track`, thumb←`.thumb`, glyph follows the (larger) thumb; the `switch` Row rebinds its #1299 nested-height pin to `.track` so the instance is not squashed back to the box height. `emit-figma-dims.ts` adds `track`/`thumb` to its AUTHORED variable list (a DTCG field is not a Figma variable until put there — the exporter gate caught the omission on the first run, as designed).

**THE `core.dimension.5` TRAP — why this is MINOR, not MAJOR (worth the most words, because the first cut hit it).** Re-deriving `inset` to `(track − thumb)/2` drops aurora's **UNUSED** `control.size.lg.inset` from 5→4, and that leaf was aurora's ONLY reference to `core.dimension.5`. So the primitive would have **DEMOTED** out of aurora's grid — a guaranteed-surface removal (MAJOR) AND a **hard block at `lint-materialization-renames`**, which has no accounting path for a non-rename deletion (its whole design is to force exactly this conversation). It is **not** avoidable by picking switch numbers: the density window makes compact-`lg` the SAME rung index as comfortable-`md`, so pinning Prism 2's 32 at `md` forces compact-`lg` to 32 (inset 4, no 5); a density-INVARIANT track that could hold a 40px compact rung fails the #910 brand-density invariant instead. **The fix is not to churn the grid's small-primitive floor for an unrelated tier's arithmetic:** `buildDims` now also feeds the box mark-clearance `(height − dot) / 2` — the quantity that WAS `inset` before #1425 (aurora's compact clearances are 3/4/5) — so `core.dimension.5` stays exactly as guaranteed as it was on `main`, sourced by a real geometric value rather than a phantom. First cut wrongly accepted the demotion at CONTRACT 11.0.0; corrected to 10.1.0 MINOR (guaranteed 585: +`track`/`thumb` ×3 rungs, +`core.dimension.{3,18}`; `core.dimension.30` joins brand-dependent, comfortable/spacious only).

**SAFETY NET — mutation-verified BY NAME (docs/34).** No new refusal arm (no schema field, no `anatomyErrors` change — the switch's non-square track already binds `width` with `sizing.x: 'fixed'`, and the cross axis may hug/fix freely). BEHAVIOR mutations, each fired the named `#1425` assertion before the real run, restored via `git checkout` off a `wip:` commit: **(1)** `SWITCH_THUMB_RATIO` 0.75→0.5 → *"#1425 …: every switch `thumb` is exactly 0.75× its `track`"* + the *thumb-to-track proportion sits strictly between a radio dot and the whole track* arm, all densities; **(2)** `SWITCH_TRACK_RUNGS` → the box ladder `[12,16,20,24,28]` → *"#1425 …: every switch `track` is TALLER than the square box `height`"* (the exact undersize this fixes) + the fractional-inset floor. `EXPECTED_CONTROL` in `test.ts` is authored as px (all three densities, box + switch fields side by side), pinning comfortable-`md` at 32/24/64/4 independently of the ladder constants. Full `npm run verify`: all gates PASS. ## (2026-09-15) — a text category may PIN a VERBATIM FACE per weight-role slot; NB's condensed headings bind engine-side (#1368)

**STATUS: PR #1442 open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.90.0 → 0.91.0 (rebased onto post-#1371 main, which took 0.90.0 after #1347/#1423 took 0.89.0); CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** The engine expressed only NUMERIC weights within a family, so a WIDTH cut — NB's display/title *ITC Garamond Std Light Condensed* (`ITCGaramondStd-LtCond`) — could not be emitted from a brand input: `subtle` (300) resolves plain "Light", never "Light *Condensed*". Owner picked **Option A** (a verbatim face pin), not Option B (a first-class width axis, deferred), with the constraint "slot into an existing type set, no capability sprawl."

**THE FORK I HIT AND HELD (need_input → owner-resolved 2026-09-15).** Implementing Option A surfaced a real type-model fork the lane was told not to decide alone: does a verbatim pin REPLACE weight-role resolution for a slot, or must weight roles still resolve *within* the condensed family? I verified from the NB reference (`reference/New Balance/tokens/tokens/shared/typography.json`) that NB's `heading` role carries a condensed **sub-family with its own weight ramp** (Light Condensed 300 + Book Condensed) inside one family, and that NB models width as STRING-valued `font/weight` variables scoped `FONT_STYLE` — a different tier shape from the engine's FLOAT numeric weights. The owner's own example (`display: 'ITCGaramondStd-LtCond'`, a bare PostScript name) does not map onto the host write contract (`materialise-to-figma.ts` writes `fontName = {family, style}`). So I reported `need_input` rather than invent a general type-model. **The owner resolved all three forks:** (i) the pin is `{family, style}`, not fontStyle-only; (ii) it is a per-(category, weight-role) SLOT pin — general mechanism, populated one slot at a time; NB pins display/subtle + title/subtle only (a single Light cut each, NO multi-weight condensed map); (iii) the numeric `fontWeight` stays the slot's weight-role numeric (Light = 300 = subtle), so it stays truthful — only the STYLE drives the Figma text.

**THE MECHANISM.** `typography.faces.<category>.<weightRole> = { family, style }` (theme.ts `FacePin`). `buildComposites` attaches the pin to the matching composite(s) as `TypeComposite.facePin`; `tree.ts` hangs it on the DTCG leaf as `$extensions.prism3.facePin` and adds `fontStyle` to the baked field list; `emit-figma-font.ts` bakes `fontStyle = facePin.style` **instead of** the numeric-weight → style-name derivation (`fontStyleName`). fontFamily still BINDS `font/family/<category>` — and the write lane resolves the loaded `fontName.family` FROM that variable's value (`write-plan.ts` `fontFamilyPrimary`), which is exactly WHY `family` must equal the category's bound family: a divergent family would be silently dropped at the host. `buildComposites` refuses it (plus three more guards) rather than emit a Text Style the host ignores.

**WHY family-must-match is the load-bearing invariant, not a nicety.** The host contract (`materialise-to-figma.ts`) is `s.fontName = { family: fontFamilyPrimary, style: fontStyle }`, and `fontFamilyPrimary` comes from the bound `font/family/*` variable, never from the pin. The pin's `family` is therefore a self-contained restatement that MUST agree with the variable, or the pin's family is a no-op. The refusal makes the disagreement loud at build.

**CONTRACT holds 10.0.0 (brandDependent).** A face pin adds NO guaranteed token NAME — it changes a baked style VALUE on existing `type.*` composites and hangs a `$extensions.prism3.facePin` on them; no path is added, removed or retyped. `token-contract --check` confirms the guaranteed 577 unchanged; only the informational `engineVersion` stamp was `--accept`ed (→ 0.91.0). **ENGINE bumped** because the emitted Figma style of a pinned composite (and the emit `note` prose on every typography leaf) moves — a consumer-observable change.

**Safety net (docs/34, by-name).** `test.ts`'s new **#1368** block is the mechanism's regression, oracle = the engine's own build (the emitted Text Style + the host-truth write-plan row, not a recorded number): (a) the pinned display composite carries `facePin {family,style}` and its Text Style bakes `fontStyle='Light Condensed'`; (b) the host-truth write-plan row = `{family:'ITC Garamond Std', style:'Light Condensed'}`; (c) the slot still binds the `subtle` weight-role numeric, untouched; (d) an UNPINNED category (title, when only display is pinned) still derives `'Light'` from the weight — proving the pin is per-slot; (e) nb-redesign's display/subtle emits ITC Garamond Std / Light Condensed. **Four NEW REFUSAL arms**, each its own by-name mutation (mutate the subject, confirm the named guard fires): family mismatch, weight-role the category does not ship, unbound category (`code: null` then pinned), malformed/empty `{family, style}`. All four throw by name; deleting any guard reddens its assertion.

**nb-redesign updated to USE the mechanism.** `examples/nb-redesign.design.md` gains a `typography.faces` block binding the Light Condensed cut on display/subtle + title/subtle, and the three "#1368 can't bind Light Condensed / set condensed by hand in the plugin" limitation notes (header, families comment, finishing-checklist item 3) are removed — that gap is closed for these two slots. The seed still compiles/validates/builds clean (the `every-example-compiles` block exercises it).

**MCP schema — COMPRESSED to fit, gate ceiling UNCHANGED at 60,000 (owner directive 2026-09-15, reversing this lane's first pass).** The brand schema is inlined once into `tools/list`; the 60k gate keeps that surface lean for clients. My first pass raised the ceiling 60k→64k to fit the `faces` field; the owner directed: compress, don't raise. Determined the ceiling is a self-imposed gate (`test.ts` + `mcp-test.ts` size assertions, not an MCP-protocol hard limit), so compression is the preferred path and it fits. `faces` uses OPEN keys (`additionalProperties`, not a 7×5 enumeration) with a terse description; the pin leaf is `{family, style}` — the optional `postscript` provenance field was **dropped** (it drove nothing, and removing it both shrinks the schema and matches the owner's `{family, style}` model exactly). `tools/list` stays under 60,000; both gate copies keep the 60,000 ceiling.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** Smoke needs `npx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell` in a fresh container before `verify` (the cached browser version can lag the pinned playwright). And bump `version.ts` BEFORE `regen` — the `ENGINE_VERSION` stamp lands in every emitted tree, so a regen run before the bump leaves `out/**` one version behind and `regen --check` red.

## (2026-09-15) — `controlShape` gains two fixed off-ramps: Boxed + Hairline (#1371)

**STATUS: PR open (#1441), do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.89.0 → 0.90.0 (merged onto post-#1347 main, which took 0.89.0 — the next free integer above it, never lower); CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** The #1371 lane (owner-decided 2026-09-15): the `controlShape` lever offered `rounded` (binds `radius.md`, tracks corner softness) and `pill` (binds `radius.capsule`, height ÷ 2). It gains TWO fixed off-ramps, keeping the semantic model intact — **each value names a RELATIONSHIP to a rung, never a raw radius**: **`boxed`** → `radius.none` (fixed 0px / sharp, independent of the softness dial) and **`hairline`** → `radius.hairline` (the fixed 1px sentinel #1362). The complete four-way set is now **Boxed · Hairline · Rounded · Pill**. Explicitly NOT a raw-radius picker — the relationships (rounded tracks the ramp, pill = height ÷ 2) stay.

**MECHANISM — a generalization, not a new path.** `applyControlShape` (`anatomy-figma.ts`) went from a single `pill`-vs-rest branch to a `CONTROL_SHAPE_RUNG` map (`rounded`→`null`/identity, `pill`→`radius.capsule`, `boxed`→`radius.none`, `hairline`→`radius.hairline`). It still repoints the ROUNDED rung **BY REF** (`radius.md`) — so it reaches button's `radius` key and icon-button's `radius.square` key alike and LEAVES the intrinsic `circular`/switch/radio round rung — and `rounded` is still the IDENTITY (same object back), so the default plan stays byte-identical.

**THE HAIRLINE↔RUNG COUPLING — decided mechanically, NOT a UX fork.** `radius.hairline` is opt-in (#1362): it exists only when the brand's `radiusHairline` lever is on. So `controlShape: hairline` would otherwise repoint a control's corner to a rung the brand never provisioned and **dangle**. Resolved the way the owner's brief pre-blessed ("auto-enable radiusHairline … the option is only offered/valid when it's on"): `brandTheme` **couples them** — choosing the shape IMPLIES the rung. The `radiusHairline` local that `buildDims` already threads is OR'd with `input.controlShape === 'hairline'`, so the ladder emits `radius.hairline` and the binding always resolves. This was NOT a non-trivial design fork (it is the mechanical "resolve the rung"), so the lane did not stop. `boxed` needs no coupling — `radius.none` is the ramp's floor (`RADIUS_LADDER` `factor: 0`), always emitted. Chose implication over rejection deliberately: rejection would leave a dead-end dropdown option that throws at build; implication satisfies the designer's intent ("hairline controls") directly with no second lever to discover.

**CONTRACT holds 10.0.0.** `controlShape` is a LEVER, not a token name, so widening its enum adds no guaranteed name; `radius.none` was already emitted and `radius.hairline` is `brandDependent` (opt-in, never guaranteed) — so no guaranteed token NAME is added, removed or retyped. `token-contract --check` confirms the guaranteed 577 unchanged (only the informational `engineVersion` stamp was `--accept`ed).

**Why ENGINE MINOR.** Adding enum values + their emitted radius bindings moves the PROJECTED COMPONENT SURFACE for a brand that picks one (#1252 — observable surface is emitted trees AND projected components), even though no corpus brand sets `controlShape`, so committed `out/**` moves only on the per-tree `generator.version` stamp (0.89.0 → 0.90.0).

**Safety net (docs/34, by-name, mutation-verified).** The enum simply admits two more values (schema `enum` + `brandTheme`'s enumLevers) — no new refusal arm — so a BEHAVIOR mutation is what is owed. `test.ts`'s new **#1371** arm derives the bound radius var from the projected PLAN (`radiusBindings`, independent of the `CONTROL_SHAPE_RUNG` map it checks) and pins, by name, that `boxed`→`radius/none` and `hairline`→`radius/hairline` at every size while `circular`/switch/radio stay `radius/round`, that each off-ramp is the identity on the excluded set and moves ONLY the radius binding on the pill-able set. A coupling arm reads the EMITTED tree and pins that a brand setting only `controlShape: hairline` still emits `radius.hairline = 1px` while `boxed` provisions nothing; a two-way enum arm pins that `boxed`/`hairline` validate clean and garbage is still rejected. **Mutation-verified (committed a `wip:` snapshot first, restored via `Edit`):** (1) repointing `CONTROL_SHAPE_RUNG.boxed` to `radius.md` failed **7 NAMED assertions** including "`button@small boxed binds radius/none … (radius/md)`" and the map arm; (2) dropping the `|| input.controlShape === 'hairline'` OR failed the single named "hairline IMPLIES the hairline rung … (got undefined)" assertion — cleanly, by name, not a crash. Suite back to **3599/0**.

**Baselines refreshed:** only `schema/token-contract.json`'s informational `engineVersion` (→ 0.90.0, no surface change) and `schema/lever-manifest.json` (regen, the two new options + description). `schema/theme-schema.json` is hand-authored (not a regen artifact) — its `controlShape` enum was edited by hand to add `boxed`/`hairline`. `lint-component-surface` / `paint-census` did NOT move: they gate the DEFAULT (`rounded` = identity) projection, which is unchanged.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** The ENGINE bump IS correct (projected-surface change #1252); `out/**` DTCG trees move only their version stamp because no corpus brand sets `controlShape`. If `regen --check` disagrees, look for an untracked file under `packages/engine/out/` before assuming drift. The hairline coupling lives in `theme.ts`'s `radiusHairline` local — it feeds the radius LADDER emission, which `controlShape` otherwise never touches (the lever is a projection-time def rewrite). Smoke needs `npx playwright install chromium` in a fresh container before `verify`.

**STATUS: PR #1422 open, DO NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges). The orchestrator INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED this: `checkbox` is 0 occurrences in `schema/token-contract.json`, the diff is stamp-only, so ENGINE-only is correct and stands.**

**REBASED ONTO POST-#1423 MAIN (orchestrator directive, 2026-09-15).** After this PR opened, #1423 (radio-control outer ring rebind, its own 2026-09-15 entry below) merged to main and took ENGINE 0.88.0. ENGINE → **0.89.0** (next free above 0.88.0, never lower); CONTRACT stays **10.0.0**. So the "0.88.0" figures in the narrative below are the ORIGINAL pre-rebase stamp; the shipped stamp is 0.89.0.

**SEND-BACK FIXES (orchestrator review, 2026-09-15 — both technical, applied to the same PR):**
- **A. Padding fidelity.** The group container bound `padding.inlineLabel: 'pad-y'` (= `space.100` = 8px), which the projector applies as paddingLeft/Right for a slotless container (`anatomy-figma.ts`) — an 8px inline inset contradicting Prism 2's `{start: 0, end: 0}` AND this def's own comments. FIX: added a `pad-x → space.0` slot and bound `inlineLabel: 'pad-x'`, so the inline sides are truly 0 and the rows fill the group's width. The change moves only the two projection baselines (`component-surface.json` + `paint-census.json`, re-`--accept`ed at 0.88.0); `regen --check` stays byte-identical (a component-padding binding is not emitted to `out/`).
- **B. Gate scope-floor (docs/34 "represented, not counted").** `lint-rung-names.ts` MUST_COVER had `checkbox-row` but not `checkbox-group`, though the group carries a `size` axis binding the rung ladder (`size.*.gap`) and its peers `radio`/`switch` are covered. FIX: added `'checkbox-group'` to MUST_COVER so the floor pins it (the sibling registers `lint-axis-values`/`lint-standalone-floor` already had it).

**WHAT SHIPPED (OPTION B, owner-decided 2026-09-15).** Three things, all in one PR:
1. **RENAME** the labelled-row def `checkbox` → `checkbox-row` (id + `name: Checkbox.Row`, file `checkbox.ts` → `checkbox-row.ts`, export `checkbox` → `checkboxRow`). Behaviour is byte-identical — only identity moves — so its projected member set is unchanged (3 size members) and the baselines rename the KEY, not the digest.
2. **KEEP** `checkbox-control` (the primitive) unchanged.
3. **ADD** `checkbox-group` — a `field-label` above a stack of `checkbox-row`s, built from Prism 2's real specs (`reference/Prism2/component-specs/checkbox-group.json` / `checkbox-row.json` / `checkboxes.json`).

**WHY THE RENAME IS CHEAP NOW.** There are NO consumers yet (v1 is still being built), so retyping the guaranteed component id/prop names costs nothing today and would be expensive once apps reference `checkbox`. The owner accepted the break for exactly that reason. This is the deliberate, right-time rename, not a drive-by.

**THE GROUP COMPOSES VIA THE COLLAPSED ROW (the #1347 requirement).** The nest chain is four deep — `focus-ring` ← `checkbox-control` ← `checkbox-row` ← `checkbox-group`, the corpus's deepest. The group nests `checkbox-row` (size-only, 3 members since #1330's `nest-exposed`), NOT `checkbox-control` (the 54-member atom), and the row nests are `nest-fixed` (the group does not re-expose the rows' selection into its own matrix). So it inherits the Row's collapse, never the atom's explosion: the group projects a size-only 3-member set. `test.ts`'s `#1347` block pins all of this independently (nest targets read off the anatomy, member count a straight multiply of the `size` cardinality, chain walked by `nests`).

## (2026-09-14) — line height is a deliberate, correct UNBOUND PERCENT bake, now gated (#1356)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **NO version bump — ENGINE stays 0.87.0, CONTRACT stays 10.0.0.** No emitted bytes change (gate + comments + docs only); `regen --check` confirms byte-identity. The #1356 lane (owner-authored, `engine`, part of the #1329 host-truth audit): the audit found every TEXT node binds `fontSize`/`fontWeight`/`fontFamily` to `core/font/*` but `boundVariables.lineHeight` is empty everywhere. The issue asked, correctly, to **confirm first whether the omission was deliberate — if so, document why; if not, bind it.**

**FINDING — the omission is DELIBERATE and CORRECT; binding is *wrong*, not merely unimplemented.** Three independent facts, each verified against the tree and against Figma's own API/docs (2026-09):
1. **The role is a UNITLESS multiplier.** `theme.ts:840` types `lineHeights: { key; value }[]` as unitless multipliers (1.15, 1.5, …); the emitted DTCG primitive `core.font.line-height.*` is typed `number` in `token-contract.json`. Figma's text `lineHeight` takes PERCENT or PIXELS, never a unitless float — so a FLOAT variable holding `1.5` bound to line height renders as **1.5 PIXELS**, not 150%. Silently catastrophic (every line collapses).
2. **Figma binds line height as PIXELS ONLY.** A percentage/unitless line height cannot be variable-bound at all — a long-standing, intentional platform limitation (`setBoundVariable('lineHeight', v)` on a FLOAT is applied as pixels; percentage binding surfaces "variable of resolved type 'FLOAT' cannot be bound to this field"). Confirmed via Figma's plugin API docs + forum record.
3. **There is NO line-height Figma variable to bind to.** `buildFigmaFont` (`emit-figma-font.ts`) projects the `core` collection as family (STRING) + size/weight/weight-role (FLOAT) and emits **no `font/line-height/*` variable at all**. Verified across every emitted collection in all three brands (`lint-lineheight-bake.ts` assertion E: 0 line-height variables).

A faithful, bindable line height would have to be a **per-size PIXEL** value = fontSize × multiplier. That is **size-dependent** — a fluid composite's fontSize is bound to a `type-sets` variable whose desktop and mobile values differ (measured: all 33 fluid composites across the 3 brands have differing per-mode sizes), so no single pixel value is correct across the modes. The current PERCENT bake (`round(multiplier × 100)`) is the ONE representation that stays invariant — 115% is right at 40px and 56px alike. `emit-figma-font.ts` (the `lineHeight: { bound: false, value: { unit: 'PERCENT', … } }` bake) already said so; #1356 extends that rationale and cites the three facts.

**DECISION BOUNDARY — HELD, not crossed.** Making line height bindable would require **minting a new guaranteed variable/name surface** (per-size PIXEL line-height variables that do not exist today) AND **dropping the documented mode invariance** — a design/contract change that is the owner's, not an engine lane's. This PR mints **no new name**, changes **no contract** (`token-contract --check`: guaranteed count unchanged, 10.0.0), and does not bind. It delivers the issue's "if deliberate, document why" branch: extend the emitter rationale (`emit-figma-font.ts`), add a docs note (`docs/10` §4), and add a docs/34 by-name gate. **If the owner ever wants binding**, that is a separate contract decision (new per-size PIXEL variable, invariance tradeoff); assertion E is set so minting such a variable cannot land silently without revisiting this gate. (Flagged for the owner; not filed as a defect, because the current behavior is correct, not broken.)

**THE GATE — `lint-lineheight-bake.ts` (docs/34, independent + by-name).** Reads the committed `out/figma/<brand>/` export (aurora, nb, wendys — discovered + a MUST_COVER floor); EXPECTED is the documented contract (`bound === false`, `unit === 'PERCENT'`) transcribed as constants, never computed from the emitter (independence). Asserts: **A** line height UNBOUND, **B** unit PERCENT (not the mode-varying PIXELS), **C** the `letterSpacing` sibling (same platform case, same emitter line), **D** the **mode-invariance witness** — for every fluid composite whose bound font size differs across modes, line height is a single unbound PERCENT whose rendered pixels **diverge** across the modes (px_mobile ≠ px_desktop, the proof a fixed absolute value could serve at most one mode), with a **non-empty witness floor**; **E** no line-height variable exists to bind to. A self-check drives the oracle over synthetic inputs in both directions (a bound field flagged, a conforming field clean). Complements `test.ts`, which checks NB's PERCENT *value* against the fixture for one brand but **never asserts `bound: false`** (the #1356 claim) and covers neither the invariance nor every brand; this gate does not re-derive `round(multiplier×100)` (that would be docs/34 shape 8).

**MUTATION-VERIFIED BY NAME** (see PR body for the exact edits + named failures; targets cited by CONTENT, not line number — #1419 recorded these lines are 355/356 now, drifted from 337/338 by #1418's own rationale block): the `lineHeight` bake `bound:false`→`true` + regen fires assertion **A** across every style/brand; `unit:'PERCENT'`→`'PIXELS'` + regen fires **B**; the `letterSpacing` bake `bound:false`→`true` fires **C**. Not "the suite went red" — THIS gate names the bind. Committed a `wip:` snapshot before each mutation so the `git checkout -- emit-figma-font.ts out/` restore reaches a clean HEAD.

**Wiring (five-file gate add, `lint-doc-gates` enforced):** `ci.yml`, `verify.ts` GATES, `CLAUDE.md` §4, `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3, `.github/pull_request_template.md`.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** No version bump is correct here — this PR adds a gate + comments + docs and changes **zero** emitted bytes, so `lint-emission-version` requires no move and a bump would be wrong. `regen --check` proves byte-identity; if it disagrees, look for an untracked file under `packages/engine/out/` before assuming drift. The gate reads committed artifacts, so a mutation test must `regen` before running it (the emitter change alone does not touch `out/` until regen). Smoke needs `npx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell` in a fresh container before `verify`.

## (2026-09-14) — button family's disabled border rebinds to track the disabled ink (#1349)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.86.0 → 0.87.0; CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** The #1349 lane (owner-triaged, `engine`+`a11y`, decision-free directive): on the DISABLED state the button's border read much heavier than the disabled icon/text ink. A border is a non-text graphical object, so its whole a11y bar is SC 1.4.11's **3:1 against adjacent colors** — it does not need to be darker than the ink. The directive: rebind the disabled border to track the disabled ink.

**OLD → NEW binding (button / button-destructive / button-neutral — one `makeButton` factory, one shared line, so all three move together):**
- OLD: `disabled.border` → `color.disabled.border` — a muted neutral matched to `disabled.fill` (both resolve `neutralLow()` in `modes.ts`), gated `min: 0` with **no contrast contract**. That role resolves at **1.48–1.80:1** against the page across the example corpus (measured live in the #1349 test's reverted-mutation run) — i.e. the old edge was not a compliant graphical object at all, it was exempt.
- NEW: `disabled.border` → `color.disabled.icon` — the disabled ink's graphical-object peer (`disabled.text`/`disabled.icon` resolve identically; icon is the non-text one). `button.ts:338`.

**The measured 3:1 graphical-object ratio.** The disabled border is STRUCTURAL (`anatomy-figma.ts` `STRUCTURAL = {fill, border}`), so it paints **only on `outline`** — the one appearance with a border at rest. An outline button has no fill, so its edge sits on the **page** (`background.primary`), which is exactly the ground `disabled.icon` is gated against. So the border inherits that role's real contract: **nb 3.16:1, aurora 3.16:1, harbor 3.32:1** (reduced strategy, `disabledMin` floor 3); **HC modes ≥4.5:1**. Clears 3:1 in every mode by construction — `disabled.icon`'s own `min` is ≥3, so nothing can dip below the graphical-object bar. `filled`/`text` disabled paint no border (STRUCTURAL guard), so there is no filled-button ink-on-fill contrast to reconcile.

**The exemption interaction.** The disabled ink is NOT contrast-exempt here — `modes.ts` gates both `disabledStrategy` branches (`full` = 4.5, `reduced` = `disabledMin` 3–4.5) since #290; the old ungated WCAG-inactive path is gone. So there is no exemption to square the 3:1 bar against: the rebind swaps a `min: 0` role for a role carrying a live ≥3 contract. The `color.disabled.border` ROLE is unchanged and still bound by the other bordered controls (icon-button, text-field, select, checkbox/radio/switch-control), so no guaranteed token NAME moves — CONTRACT holds 10.0.0 (`token-contract --check` confirms guaranteed 577 unchanged; only the informational `engineVersion` stamp was `--accept`ed).

**Safety net.** No new schema field or refusal arm — a pure token rebind, so only a BEHAVIOR mutation is owed (stated explicitly). `test.ts`'s #1349 arm pins, per family, that the disabled BORDER role EQUALS the disabled ICON role and is NOT `color.disabled.border`, and re-measures the resolved ratio ≥3 via `resolveAllModes` (independent of the button def) across the example brands × every mode, with a non-empty-sweep floor. Reverting `button.ts:338` to `color.disabled.border` fails 14 NAMED `#1349` assertions (6 role-equality + 8 ratio, the ratio ones printing the sub-3 numbers above). The pre-existing paint tests at `test.ts:9460` read the binding dynamically, so they follow it and cannot notice a revert — which is why the by-name pin was added rather than relying on them.

**Baselines refreshed (bump-gated `--accept`):** `lint-component-surface` (button trio's `outline` disabled coordinate repoints, same 432 members each) and `paint-census` (same assignment count, different variable). `out/**` moved only its per-tree `generator.version` stamp (0.86.0 → 0.87.0) — component payloads are not committed under `out/`.

**Trap for re-verifiers.** `regen --check` and its drift-coverage SKIP under `npm run verify` while `out/**` is uncommitted (verify compares against HEAD) — commit first, then they pass. `token-contract --check` fails on an uncommitted informational stamp until `--accept` is run; that is not a contract move (guaranteed 577, still 10.0.0). And the smoke gate needs `npx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell` in a fresh container before `verify` runs any gate.

## (2026-09-14) — image-placeholder marker grows to a 180px literal glyph size (#1340)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.85.0 → 0.86.0; CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** The #1340 lane (owner-triaged, `engine`, decision-free direction, nice-to-have): the empty-state "no image" marker was `icon.size.lg` (32px) — tiny against the 720px frame — and the owner asked to make it larger and, ideally, scale it with the frame.

**WHAT SHIPPED — a larger FIXED size (the floor), grounded in Prism 2, not a size that tracks the frame on resize.** The marker is now a def-local literal `glyphPx: 180` on the `marker` vector. Two decisions behind that:
- **The SIZE (180px) is grounded in Prism 2, not aesthetic.** `reference/Prism2/component-specs/image-placeholder.json` has NO empty-state marker glyph (its nested elements are `scrim` and `playCircleLine`, both `visible:false` by default — the overlays prism3 defers, #1316). Its ONE centered in-frame glyph is `playCircleLine`, **160px on the 480px-tall 4:3 frame = 1/3 of the shorter side**, held FIXED across ratios (it has no per-ratio size variant). 1/3 of prism3's 4:3 nominal shorter side (720 × 3/4 = 540) is **180px**. Held FIXED across the three ratios, as Prism 2 holds its centered glyph fixed. At the 720px nominal frame that is 25% of the width, 1/3 of the 4:3 shorter side, 44% of the 16:9 shorter side (matching Prism 2's play-circle-to-16:9-shorter proportion there). The `playCircleLine` is a CTA, not the empty-state marker, so it is the frame-family proportion ANCHOR rather than the same element — stated transparently, not a like-for-like reference.
- **True "scale with the frame" was NOT projectable and is a follow-up.** A marker that tracks the frame's ACTUAL flexing extent on resize is a responsive/proportional size — a Figma scale-constraint / percentage projection the engine does NOT have. The fluid `100%` container is skipped in `emit-figma-dims.ts` for exactly this reason ("Figma has no percentage FLOAT primitive"), and a per-ratio glyph would still be three FIXED sizes, not resize-tracking. So the FLOOR (a larger fixed size) shipped and the proportional stretch is surfaced as a separate mechanism question (recorded in `image-placeholder.notes.unverified`). This is the select-width pattern: ship the achievable, hold the fork.

**MECHANISM — a new projection field `PartDef.glyphPx`, a def-local LITERAL, NOT a token.** No icon rung reaches a marker-of-the-frame proportion (`icon.size.xl` tops out at 40px) and no other semantic dimension names near 180; minting a token would move CONTRACT and hand a brand a knob nobody should re-theme. So the size is a literal in the `minWidth`/`glyphScale` family: carried on `FigmaNodePlan.glyphPx` only when set (every existing glyph's plan byte-identical), and BOTH executors resize the imported SVG frame to it after the read-back and before the bind loop (the outline's SCALE constraints scale the drawn grid to fill). Twin executors, both now resize.

## (2026-09-14) — field-label cluster: Required BOOLEAN (#1338) + disabled DIM as one mechanism (#1339)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.84.0 → 0.85.0; CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** The field-label lane the #1338/#1339 owner decisions (2026-09-13) authorized, built on the #1412 node-visibility mechanism (#1331) that just merged. The old `indicator` [none/required/optional] variant axis is GONE — a boolean is two states, the marker's presence IS the choice, and Prism 2 models it exactly this way (`reference/Prism2/component-specs/form-label.json`: a `required` element, content `*`, `required` boolean default `true`). Mechanism specifics:
- The `indicator` PART stays (a text node, `paintSlot: 'indicator'`) and gains `optional: true` — now BUILDABLE, since #1412 made `present()` keep a boolean-driven optional part (the old header's "unbuildable in both directions" contradiction is resolved).
- `booleans: { required: { part: 'indicator', default: true } }` — built VISIBLE (`default: true` is both the built visibility and the boolean's own default, "as built"). This is the FIRST corpus consumer to default the toggled part VISIBLE; select's leading glyph defaults it hidden. Direct mapping (required=true → visible), so NO inverted-boolean mechanism was needed.
- The marker's TEXT (`*`) is a `texts` entry keyed on the SAME `required` prop, Figma name `required marker` — one consumer prop backing TWO Figma properties on one node (`characters` + `visible`), exactly as select's `leadingIcon` backs a swap + a boolean. `characters` is required for the node to render at all (#798).
- **Interpretation note (surfaced to orchestrator):** the owner's prose said "reveals/hides the *Optional* affordance," but every precise signal — "as in Prism 2," the cited Prism 2 spec (marker `*`, default shown), the issue body ("turning it off *hid* the portion" → default shows it), and the named mechanism (#1412 does DIRECT visibility only) — converges on ONE implementable reading: a `Required` boolean, default true, showing a `*` required marker, hidden when off. A "(optional)"-shown-when-not-required model would need an INVERTED boolean the mechanism does not have, i.e. a fork; the decision as written forces the direct model. Marker text stays editable in Figma, so a brand can carry `(required)` or another glyph.

**#1339 — disabled DIM as ONE mechanism (the STATE), fit via EXISTING projection.** The fit determination the orchestrator asked for: the owner's literal suggestion ("a Figma boolean/visibility driving the dim") is UNBUILDABLE — the #1412 boolean toggles VISIBILITY, and a disabled label must DIM (an ink change), not vanish. But #1339 did NOT need a new appearance-boolean mechanism, so no fork/STOP: the `disabled` STATE already dims via existing paint projection (`disabled.label` / `disabled.indicator` → `color.disabled.text`, projected as the disabled variant coordinate). The collapse is therefore: KEEP the `disabled` state (the single mechanism), REMOVE the redundant code-side `disabled` prop that duplicated it. In code the dim is driven by the disabled FIELD's context, not a prop on the label — the field's native disabled is the source of truth (matching select's own nested-label codeOnly). "One mechanism, not a state axis + a prop," using existing projection.

A committed test asserts, on a resolved brand across all four modes, that the disabled ink clears ≥3:1 AND is genuinely dimmer than the rest ink (a real dim, not a same-ink no-op) — dimmed but legible.

Components consume token roles; they emit no token names. `token-contract.ts --check`: "no guaranteed path moved — no version bump required." Removing the indicator axis and collapsing disabled dropped no *projected variant* that is a token name (the projected member count is UNCHANGED at 24 — the boolean toggles in place and the disabled state stays), and even a dropped component variant is not a token-contract subject.
