## (2026-09-14) — the NODE-VISIBILITY BOOLEAN projection, proven by select's leading glyph (#1331)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.83.0 → 0.84.0, CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** The FOUNDATIONAL lane the #1331 owner decision (2026-09-14) authorized: build a reusable node-visibility boolean projection and ship it proven by its first consumer, select's leading glyph. `field-label` #1338 (Required boolean) / #1339 (disabled dim) are the NEXT lane and are NOT built here.

**THE MECHANISM — a Figma BOOLEAN component property drives a part's `visible`, in place.** A `figmaProperties.booleans` entry (now the object form `{ part, default?, figmaName? }`, mirroring `swaps`/`texts`) declares that a part is EMITTED at every projected member and its `visible` flipped by a boolean — rather than the two mechanisms it sits beside: a **variant/slot axis** (`slotAxes`) emits the node in the true members and DROPS it in the false ones, MULTIPLYING the set (and is what #326's asymmetric padding forces on button's leading/trailing); **`presentWhen`** DROPS the node at the gated-out coordinates of a variant it multiplies over. The boolean keeps ONE member and toggles visibility, so the set does not grow. New plan fields `FigmaNodePlan.visible` (the built visibility, carried only when `false` so every existing plan is byte-identical) and `visibleProp` (the Figma property name); `present()` keeps a boolean-driven part in the tree; `planSetProperties` derives the BOOLEAN whose default is the node's BUILT visibility ("as built"); both executors build the node hidden and wire `componentPropertyReferences.visible` through the existing per-member ref machinery.

**WHY THE `booleans` HOOK WAS DECLARED BUT UNBUILDABLE, and the two things that fixed it.** `booleans` has existed (validated, wired to `drivenBy`→`propertyRef{field:'visible'}`) but no def used it, because it was contradictory: the validator REQUIRES the target `optional`, and `present()` then returned `!optional` = false and DROPPED the node the boolean would toggle (recorded verbatim in `field-label.ts`'s indicator note). Fix 1: `present()` now keeps a boolean-driven part in the tree. Fix 2 (the load-bearing one): **select's leading glyph must be BOTH a swap (`mainComponent`, which icon) AND a boolean (`visible`, present?) on ONE node** — the #1380 `leading icon` switch with `↳ swap leading icon` beneath it — but `propertyRef` is singular, so the boolean rides its own `visible`/`visibleProp` fields instead of colliding with the swap, and the one-property-per-node validator rule is now keyed on the Figma FIELD (a swap's `mainComponent` and a boolean's `visible` coexist; two SAME-field claims still collide). The ref machinery (engine `refs`, `refByMember`, both wire loops) is keyed by `part+field` so both refs on `leadingVisual` survive.

**FIRST CONSUMER — select's leading glyph, 32 → 16.** Was a `leading` slot ×2 variant axis; now the boolean `leading icon` (hidden by default, matching the prop's "Hidden by default"). status(4) × state(4) × leading(2) = **32** → status(4) × state(4) = **16** — the exact halving. Recomputed against CURRENT main (the #1331 body's "40→20" predates #1344's `empty` removal; the owner comment's "32→20" was itself stale — the boolean removes the whole ×2, not a partial cut). Clean for select precisely because the glyph sits INSIDE `content`, taking NO #326 padding asymmetry a boolean cannot drive — the #1331/#1379 split. **#1379 button is OUT of scope and untouched** (its edge-hugging leading/trailing stay variant axes).

**CONTRACT reasoning.** A variant axis becoming a boolean property is component-API surface, not a token NAME — no guaranteed token NAME is added, removed or retyped, so CONTRACT holds **10.0.0**; `token-contract --check` confirms the guaranteed **577 unchanged** and `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp. `ENGINE` is a MINOR (0.83.0 → 0.84.0): the projected surface moved. `regen --check` in sync at **108 artifacts** (component defs emit into no committed file; only the `$extensions.generator.version` stamp moved, one line each in the 8 `*.tokens.json`). Baselines re-`--accept`ed at the forward bump: `component-surface` (select 32 → 16, digest moves), `paint-census` (select `set` 32 → 16 members / 144 → 80 assignments — the removed leading=false column; the DECLARED `grid` census holds at 20/100, since the leading glyph was always painted and still is, now at every member). paint-census `grid` unchanged is the tell that no paint role moved.

**docs/34 — the mechanism pinned INDEPENDENTLY of the projector, mutations confirmed BY NAME.** `test.ts`'s `#1331` block (EXPECTED authored / ACTUAL read off the emitted plan): the leading glyph node is emitted at EVERY member with `visible:false` + `visibleProp:'leading icon'` AND its swap on the SAME node; the set is 16; `planSetProperties` declares `leading icon` BOOLEAN default false, ordered ABOVE its swap. Two BEHAVIOR mutations flip by name: dropping the boolean re-DROPS the (optional) node at every member (`present()` → `!optional`), and reverting `leading` to a slot axis re-DOUBLES the set to 32 and re-drops the node in the false members — the multiplication the boolean replaced. **NEW REFUSAL ARM (principle 6 / docs/34):** a boolean on a `presentWhen`/`when`-gated part is refused (two conflicting presence mechanisms) — reverting the arm fails *"#1331 a boolean on a presentWhen-gated part is refused BY NAME"*. The widened field-based collision keeps a by-name arm proving two SAME-field claims (two booleans on one node) still fail, and the LOOSENING is pinned positively (select's swap+boolean on one node validates clean). **test-roundtrip (host truth, #874):** the `leading icon` BOOLEAN property, the built node's `visible=false`, and its `componentPropertyReferences.visible` wiring are all read back off the built node; `anatomy-readback.ts` classifies the two new plan fields so the round-trip diff also covers them corpus-wide.

**Trap for whoever re-verifies (recorded in `select.notes.unverified`).** In Figma auto-layout, a child with `visible:false` is EXCLUDED from layout — it takes no space or gap — so a hidden leading glyph adds no gap to `content`, exactly as the absent slot did. The offline shims model the boolean property, the built `visible=false` and the ref wiring (all gated), but NOT auto-layout's exclusion of invisible children from the flow: whether a real Figma host reflows `content` when the switch toggles is a host question no Node gate answers. Symptom on a real host: a persistent gap where the hidden glyph sits, or the field not tightening when leading is off.

**`npm run verify` → 54 PASS · 0 FAIL · 2 SKIP before the `out/` commit (the two drift gates SKIP until `out/` is committed, then PASS → 56/56; `regen --check` standalone is already in sync at 108).**

## (2026-09-14) — select gains a 320 min-width floor + rides its declared responsive fill; the HELD half of the select cluster (#1343a + #1345)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.82.0 → 0.83.0, CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** The held half of the select cluster, on the #1343 owner decision (2026-09-13). The icon-ink half (#1343b) and #1342/#1344 shipped in #1407; this ships the default width (#1343a) and the responsive auto-layout (#1345).

**MECHANISM — a MIN-WIDTH on the control, NOT a token and NOT a bound `width`.** The owner's steer was explicit: 320 is a comfortable projection default (8px increments), not a semantic `field.width` role. Expressed it as a new projection primitive `PartDef.minWidth` — a **literal px** the def states (the #1346 glyph-inset precedent: a def-local literal, never a token) — carried onto `FigmaNodePlan.minWidth` and written by both executors inside their `layoutMode` branch (Figma accepts a minimum width only on an auto-layout frame). `select.ts`'s `control` carries `minWidth: 320`.

**WHY THE FLOOR SITS ON THE CONTROL, and this is the load-bearing diagnosis.** Prism 2's select (`reference/Prism2/component-specs/select.json`) is `root width 320 · HUG` with its inner containers (`input`/`content`/`text`) `FILL`ing that width. The engine **cannot project a child that FILLs** — `sizing: 'fill'` maps to AUTO (#989/#990) — so a floor on the *container* would leave a hugging (narrow) control inside a 320 frame, which reads as broken. Flooring the *visible control* reproduces Prism 2's rendered geometry the one way projection allows: the control renders at ≥320, the hugging column inherits that width, and — because the control's sizing stays `'fill'` (→ AUTO, not FIXED) — the field **FLEXES above the floor** rather than being pinned. That flex IS #1345, riding on #1343a exactly as the owner framed it.

**NO WIDTH-REFUSAL CHANGE, so no refusal mutation owed.** A min-width on the control avoids the row-oriented `width`-requires-`sizing.x`-fixed rule entirely (no `width` binding, no sizing change). The `PartDef.minWidth` validator refuses it on a non-box and on a layout-less box (Figma would silently drop it otherwise) — a wrong-kind rule modeled on `clipsContent`.

**CONTRACT reasoning.** No guaranteed token NAME is added, removed or retyped (320 is a component geometry literal, not a token), so CONTRACT holds **10.0.0**; `token-contract --check` confirms the guaranteed **577 unchanged** and `--accept` refreshed only the baseline's informational `engineVersion` stamp. `ENGINE` is a MINOR (0.82.0 → 0.83.0): a new projected property moved the surface, so `lint-component-surface.ts` needed a bump-gated `--accept` (`select`'s `planStamp` moved; member count holds at **32**). `regen --check` in sync at **108 artifacts** (only the `$extensions.generator.version` stamp moved, one line each in the 8 `*.tokens.json`). paint-census unchanged — `minWidth` is geometry, not paint.

**docs/34 mutation-by-name (in `test.ts`, EXPECTED authored / ACTUAL read off the emitted plan, independent of the projector):**
- **#1343a** — removing `control.minWidth` drops it from the plan, flipping *"#1343a select control carries the 320 min-width floor"* by name.
- **#1345** — flipping the control's `layout.sizing.x` `'fill'` → `'fixed'` turns its `primaryAxisSizingMode` AUTO → FIXED, flipping *"#1345 select control FLEXES (not hard-fixed)"* by name.
- The roundtrip (`test:roundtrip`) independently reads `minWidth` back off all **32** built control nodes and diffs against the plan (the executor writes it, the host echoes it, the reader compares it); `lint-component-surface` arm A is a second, coarser by-name guard (the `planStamp` moves on removal).

**Trap for re-verifiers.** `sizing.x`/`sizing.y` are MAIN/CROSS, not horizontal/vertical — the projector maps `sizing.x` → `primaryAxisSizingMode`. For select's COLUMN container this means `sizing.x` is *vertical*; the container's `{x:'fill', y:'hug'}` is therefore a latent axis inconsistency (it reads as "vertical fill" where the field wants "horizontal fill, vertical hug"), invisible only because BOTH `fill` and `hug` project to AUTO at the top level. Filed separately (principle 3 — file, don't fix); not touched here because it is a no-op in projection and the owner considers the fill correctly declared. The width floor is direction-agnostic (Figma `minWidth` is always horizontal), so it sidesteps the whole question.

**`npm run verify` → 54 PASS · 0 FAIL · 2 SKIP before the `out/` commit (the two drift gates SKIP until `out/` is committed, then PASS → 56/56).**

## (2026-09-14) — checkbox-control inner glyph inset to Prism 2's 0.80 mark-to-box ratio (padded artboard, no token); pressed border confirmed reusing rest, documented (#1346)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.81.0 → 0.82.0, CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** Both #1346 items shipped in one PR. The projected component surface moves (checkbox-control's mark/dash glyph documents are padded, so their `glyphSvg` and `glyphViewBox` change from a 24 to a 30 artboard — the #1252 ENGINE trigger, same 54 members); no emitted TOKEN NAME moves (the inset is a def-local literal baked into the glyph DOCUMENT, never a token), so `token-contract --check` reports the guaranteed **577 unchanged** and `--accept` refreshed only the baseline's informational `engineVersion` stamp at contract 10.0.0. `regen --check` in sync at **108 artifacts** (components emit no per-component file; only the `$extensions.generator.version` stamp moved, one line each in the 8 `*.tokens.json`). **`npm run verify` → 56/56 PASS (0 FAIL · 0 SKIP) once `out/` is committed.**

**Item 1 — the inner-glyph size, MEASURED against Prism 2, not nudged.** QA read the check/dash as slightly too large. **How it was derived before:** `mark`/`dash` bind `size.{size}.control` (the FULL control box) and draw the `check` artwork's own ~71% grid inset, so the check ink spanned **70.7%** of the box width (measured: the `check` path is 16.97×12.02 in the 24×24 grid; the dash 14.00×2.00 = 58.3% wide). **Prism 2's ratio:** `reference/Prism2/component-specs/checkboxes.json` pins `checkFill` (and `subtractFill`) at 16×16, and its control SQUARE is **20×20** — derived from the focus frame, which is 28×28 at offset −4, so box = 28 − 2×4 = 20 (the 28 is the ring frame, the 20 is the box). Cross-checked two ways: Prism 2's `cornerRadius` 2 on a 20px box is exactly the engine's own control corner (`edge ÷ 8`), which lands on 20 and not 16; and the engine's own checkbox-control focus ring sites at the same −4. So Prism 2's mark-to-box ratio is **16/20 = 0.80**. **The reconciliation (the "inset twice" trap):** Prism 2's `checkFill` and the engine's `check` are the same Remix-lineage glyph, so BOTH carry the ~71% artwork inset inside the mark frame — that inset is common and cancels. What differs is the FRAME: Prism 2's is 0.80 of the box, the engine's was 1.0. Applying 0.80 as a *second* inset on top of the ~71% would inset twice; the correct NET move is the FRAME 1.0 → 0.80. **Rendered result:** check ink 70.7% → 0.80×70.7% = **56.6%** of box width, dash 58.3% → 46.6% — Prism 2's proportion. This is a measured calibration, not an arbitrary value.

**Item 1 — the mechanism, and why it mints no token.** The plan is brand-agnostic (a frame binds a *variable*, never a per-brand literal), so shrinking the FRAME to 0.80 would need the mark to bind a variable worth 0.80×box at every rung/density — and the only sub-box control token, `control.size.*.dot`, is 0.5 (the radio dot). A new `control.size.*.mark` token would track correctly but is a GUARANTEED name (every corpus brand emits `control.size.*`, so it sits in the contract's 577) → a CONTRACT MINOR bump, the exact class #910's `dot` and #997's `inset` each bumped for. Since the orchestrator's constraint is CONTRACT-holds-ENGINE-only, the inset is instead baked into the emitted glyph DOCUMENT: a new schema field **`glyphScale`** (on `mark`/`dash`, value 0.8) makes the projector pad the artboard to `grid ÷ 0.8` = 30, centred with a **negative viewBox origin** (`-3 -3 30 30`) so the path `d` and the shared vocabulary are byte-untouched. The host's existing box binding then resizes the 30 frame to the box and the SCALE-constrained vector renders the grid at 0.80. A def-local literal, not a token — `token-contract --check` stays at 577.

**Item 2 — pressed border: CONFIRMED reusing rest, DOCUMENTED, mints nothing (owner 2026-09-13).** Verified: only `color.field.border.rest` and `color.field.border.hover` exist (no `.pressed` role), so the empty box's pressed border falls through to `unchecked.border` (rest); the *checked* box does carry `checked.fill.pressed`. The owner declined to mint `field/border/pressed`, consistent with #1342's no-new-`field/fill/hover` call — the field family stays lean, pressed is transient, and the check-fill already signals activation. Recorded in the def header + the `unchecked.border` token comment. No binding or token moved.

**Version + baselines.** ENGINE 0.81.0 → 0.82.0 (projected glyph geometry moved). `schema/component-surface.json`: `checkbox-control` re-`--accept`ed at the forward bump (54 members → 54 members, new plan digest — the only def that drifted). `schema/token-contract.json`: informational `engineVersion` only (guaranteed 577 and brand-dependent 256 byte-identical). `lint-paint` census UNCHANGED (glyph geometry is not part of the paint census; member counts and slots are unmoved). `out/**`: only the generator stamp, 8 files, one line each.

  1. **No ~320px token exists.** The nominal-width idiom (`image-placeholder`/`veil`: `width: 'nominal-side' → container.narrow`) resolves to **720px** and is brand-responsive (480–960); the dimension grid maxes at 128px (`theme.dims.grid`). 320 is a NEW value with no home — a new `field.width` role (or a raw dimension primitive) is a token-tier addition, which is the owner's call under §6, not the mechanical fallout of a fix.
  2. **The container is a COLUMN, and the engine's `width` binding + its validator are ROW-oriented.** `select`'s root `container` is `direction: column`, so its width is the COUNTER axis; but the `width`-requires-`sizing.x==='fixed'` refusal (`component-schema.ts`, anatomyErrors) checks the MAIN axis. Probed: `sizing:{x:'fixed',y:'hug'}`+width validates but projects `primaryAxisSizingMode: FIXED` (a fixed HEIGHT) with a hugging width — wrong; the projection I actually want (`sizing:{x:'hug',y:'fixed'}` → `primary AUTO`/`counter FIXED`, hug height + fixed 320 width, exactly Prism2's root) is REFUSED by the row-oriented rule. A faithful fixed column width needs a direction-aware fix to that refusal (a schema-refusal change owing its own by-name mutation).
  3. **`fill` does not stretch in the projection** (`#989`/`#990`: both `hug` and `fill` map to `AUTO`), so even with a fixed 320 container the inner `control`/`content` project as `hug`, not filling the 320 — a 320 frame with a left-hugging control. `select.notes.unverified` already records this as a code-side concern.

  Prism2's model (`reference/Prism2/component-specs/select.json`) is: `root` **width 320**, HUG vertical; every inner container (`inputWithLabel`, `input`, `content`, `text`) `layoutSizingHorizontal: FILL`. Prism3 ALREADY declares that fill throughout (`container`/`control`/`content` all `x:'fill'`), so #1345's responsive intent is present in the def; the only Prism2 divergence is the fixed 320 root width — i.e. #1345 rides entirely on #1343a. **RECOMMENDATION:** introduce a `field.width` semantic role (or agree a raw dimension) at 320 and make the `width` refusal direction-aware (for a `column`, require `sizing.y==='fixed'`) so the container becomes `{x:'hug', y:'fixed'}`+`width` — hug height, fixed 320, filling children — with a by-name mutation for the widened refusal; OR, the lighter option, treat 320 as a code-side default width (documented in `codeOnly`, no projected surface change). Both are one more ENGINE bump and one more `component-surface`/`paint-census` `--accept`, so batching them here would have churned the surface a second time regardless — the fork, not the batch, is why they are held.

## (2026-09-11) — the inverse FILLED fill STEPS per state; the primary label's AA is a lever (#1389 / F3)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.76.0 → 0.77.0, CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** Emitted inverse-fill VALUES move in every corpus tree; no token NAME moves, and the new `strictInteractiveContrast` lever RE-SELECTS an existing role's value rather than adding a path — so `token-contract --check` reports the guaranteed **577 unchanged** and `--accept` refreshed only the baseline's informational `engineVersion` stamp (0.76.0 → 0.77.0) at contract 10.0.0; `lint-emission-version` requires the bump (the emission moved); `regen --check` in sync at 108 artifacts. **`npm run verify` → 56/56 PASS (0 FAIL · 0 SKIP · 0 ADVISORY).**

**The defect (owner decision B4a, built not re-decided), from the 2026-09-09 host-truth audit (#1389).** On the inverse band a *filled* button's fill was identical across every interaction state, so it gave no hover/pressed feedback. Page-ground filled buttons signal by STEPPING the fill; the overlay wash is an outline/text mechanism (no fill to change) and is the wrong tool for a filled button. The owner ran a design fork (B1/B2/B3, posted to #1389 with the measured data) and decided **B4a**: step the inverse filled fill per state, toward the ground, uniform across families — light `050→150(hover)→250(pressed)`, dark `850→750→650`, `focused`=hover, `selected`=pressed — and keep the vivid #1244 brand label as the DEFAULT, treating hover/pressed as transient states that may dip below AA (rest must still clear it), with a LEVER to tighten.

**Premise re-check (the F1 rule, #1387).** Reading the emitted `out/*.tokens.json` on 0.76.0 BEFORE any code moved: `inverse.interactive.primary.fill.{rest…selected}` was byte-identical (`neutral.050` light / `neutral.850` dark) in all four corpus brands — genuinely flat. Crucially, `neutral`/`destructive` ALREADY stepped (their `on-fill` is the neutral extreme, which survives the darkening); only `primary` was held, by `holdInverseFill` — the #1351-part-2 decision this reverses. Reproduced, not an audit misread.

**Why it was flat, and the wall B4a had to clear.** Stepping the fill darker lowers the contrast of any ink on it. Primary's `on-fill` is a single VIVID brand step (#1244) gated only against `fill.rest`; on the stepped fill it dips below AA on hover/pressed — measured across all four brands and both standard modes, `4.69→3.62→2.75` (light) / `4.79→3.49→2.43` (dark), so **even one rung fails**. #1351-pt-2 held primary flat for exactly this reason. There is no fill step that both moves and keeps a fixed vivid rest-gated ink at AA — the only directions from a near-white/near-black rest are toward mid, which always lowers ink contrast. The owner's B4a resolves it by ACCEPTING the transient dip on the default (rest still AA) and providing the lever for brands that need AA everywhere.

**The change — the fill step + the direction fix.** `modes.ts` `invColumn`: dropped `holdInverseFill` (all three families step) and flipped the walk from `-dir` to `dir`. `-dir` walked toward MORE contrast with the band (like the outline/text ink); in light it overshot the white extreme and reflected inward onto `050→150→250` by luck, but in dark it walked toward the black extreme and only reflected on `pressed`, emitting a NON-MONOTONE `850→950→650`. `dir` steps toward the inverse SURFACE (the ground) — +1 light, −1 dark — giving the owner's exact monotone rungs in both modes with no reliance on the reflection guard. This is also why the dark `neutral`/`destructive` step, previously `850→950→650`, is now the intended `850→750→650`.

**The lever — `strictInteractiveContrast` (the customization B4a conditioned acceptance on).** A new optional boolean BrandInput field (off by default), wired through `theme.ts` (BrandInput + Theme), `schema/theme-schema.json`, and `levers.ts` (color group, advanced). OFF: primary inverse `on-fill` keeps the vivid brand ink (`brandOnFill`, #1244). ON: it swaps to the neutral extreme (`onColor` — the near-black/near-white ink the other families already use), which clears 4.5 on the stepped fill at 7.6–16:1. Only the inverse primary `on-fill` moves; `neutral`/`destructive` were already the neutral extreme and are unchanged. `destructive` needs NO change here — its "red is lighter ink" note (#1367/#1352 class) is about the OUTLINE/TEXT ink's page contrast, not this filled surface. Documented via the skill `omits:` list (an advanced studio-tuning knob, alongside `neutralEmphasis`/`outlineInteraction`).

**#1239 still holds, and this is the crux.** That invariant is REST-ONLY, CROSS-FAMILY: the three families' `fill.rest` are one value on the neutral ramp. Per-state stepping leaves rest uniform — all three still resolve `neutral.050`/`850` at rest, by construction (one shared `fillRest`) — confirmed empirically across all four brands × both modes (UNIFORM everywhere). The stronger "one value at EVERY state" also holds with the lever OFF (all three families walk the same neutral ramp identically).

**The gate gap I flagged, now closed (docs/34).** The `on-fill` contract only gated the ink against `fill.rest`, so a later-state dip was a SILENT fail. `test.ts` block **d3** adds two named gates, each derived independently of the producer: **GATE A** reads the emitted neutral rung and asserts the fill STEPS toward the ground — rungs INCREASE per state on a light-mode (near-black) inverse surface and DECREASE on a dark-mode (near-white) one (direction derived from the mode, NOT the engine's `dir` — docs/34 shape 2), non-degenerate (hover≠rest, pressed≠hover) and mirrored (focused=hover, selected=pressed), REPRESENTED across all 3 families × 4 brands with a non-empty floor. **GATE B** is the per-state on-fill contract + lever: `rest` is a HARD 4.5 floor in every mode (never exempt); hover/pressed/focused/selected are exempt by default and ENFORCED when the lever is ON; the lever is proven real — OFF keeps primary on the BRAND ramp, ON swaps it to the NEUTRAL extreme AND that extreme clears 4.5 at every state. All ratios recomputed from emitted hexes, never read off the role's own `ratio`.

**Mutation-by-name (docs/34), run by commit-between-mutations (the `git checkout --` restore trap).** (a) Re-adding `holdInverseFill = name === 'primary'` fails the named `#1389 GATE A … STEPS per state` (primary hover==rest), alone. (b) Flipping the walk back to `-dir` fails the named `#1389 GATE A … MONOTONE toward the ground` via the dark `850→950→650`. (c) Reverting the lever wiring (`&& !theme.strictInteractiveContrast`) fails the named `#1389 GATE B … swaps primary on-fill to the NEUTRAL extreme` (ON stays on the brand ramp). Each restored, suite green again.

## (2026-09-10) — the focus ring is CONCENTRIC with its host, and sheds a stale nominal-side binding (#1388 / F2)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **ENGINE bump 0.75.0 → 0.76.0, CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0.** The change is entirely in the two host executors; the projected plan is byte-identical, so the only committed movement is each emitted tree's `$extensions.generator.version` stamp plus the contract baseline's informational `engineVersion` stamp (`regen --check` moves nothing else, `lint-emission-version` requires the bump, `token-contract --check` reports the guaranteed 577 unchanged and `--accept` refreshed only the informational field at contract 10.0.0). **`npm run verify` → 56/56 PASS (0 FAIL · 0 SKIP · 0 ADVISORY).**

**The defect (owner-approved design, implemented not re-decided), from the 2026-09-09 host-truth audit (#1388).** `focus-ring`'s `topLeftRadius` was `0` with NO radius binding, on the main component and every nested instance — a hard square around a rounded button, and a SQUARE ring around a circular radio. The owner approved CONCENTRIC (host radius + the ring's offset), not match: the ring sits OUTSIDE the host, so it must run parallel to the host edge at the constant gap, which means a larger radius. Worked example: a radius-8 button at +4 inset → a radius-12 ring.

**Premise re-check (the F1 rule, #1387 — the audit's paint/geometry reads can misread a derived value).** Both symptoms were confirmed against the current engine by reading the projected plan and the emitted tokens, not by trusting the issue text. (1) `figmaAnatomySet(focusRing)` binds `{width, height → size/md/height, strokeWeight → focus/ring/width}` and no radius; the button's `focusRing` NESTED_INSTANCE carries `absoluteInset`/`absoluteStrokeInset` and `bound: {}`; and neither executor's absolute loop wrote a corner radius. So the ring is a radius-0 square, confirmed. (2) The ring's `nominal-side` binds width AND height to `size.md.height`; an instance inherits that. On aurora `size.sm.height`=28, `size.md.height`=36, `focus.ring.offset`=2, `focus.ring.width`=2 → a small button's ring resizes to 28 + 2×(2+2) = 36 = `size.md.height`. The coincidence #1388 names, reproduced exactly. Neither premise was an F1-style misread.

**The concentric formula.** The ring is positioned at `-inset` and sized `host + 2×inset`, where `inset = gap + strokeWidth` (the #801 sum). For the corner to stay parallel at the constant gap the ring's radius must be `hostRadius + inset` — the ring grows uniformly on every axis including its radius, so it is concentric by construction. Read per-corner off the host node (a bound corner reads back its resolved number; the host binds all four to `radius/md`) and written to the ring's four corners. One derivation covers three cases without a table: a **radius-0 host** → `inset` (a rounded-rect ring around a square control, not a hard square); a **full-round host** (radio, radius ≥ half its side) → `host + inset ≥ ringSide/2`, which Figma clamps to the ring's own half-side, so a circle stays a circle; an **ordinary rounded host** stays at the gap. Frozen at paste like `x`/`y` and the inset (Figma's radius write takes a number, and the host radius read here is already resolved), so it shares their `codeOnly` ceiling — an already-pasted ring does not re-flow when a brand changes its corner radius.

**The latent sibling, cleared — and #1290 predicted it verbatim.** `focus-ring.ts`'s #1290 note said, of the inherited nominal side: *"If a nested ring is ever found sitting at the md control height instead of its host's box, that is this binding surviving the resize, and the fix is in the host executor (clear the instance's inherited width/height before resizing), not here."* That is exactly F2's second symptom, and exactly this fix: the absolute loop now calls `setBoundVariable('width', null)`/`('height', null)` on the ring instance before the resize. Same binding surface as the radius work (the one host-executor loop that writes the nested ring's geometry), which is why #1388 scoped them together and this PR does not split them. `strokeWeight` — the ring's own brand stroke — is left bound; only the two dimensions the host overwrites are cleared.

**The gate gap the audit flagged, now closed (docs/34).** No gate checked a resolved radius on a built node — `diffAnatomy` compares plan-to-host STRUCTURE and iterates the plan's fields, and the ring's radius is neither a plan field nor structure, so shape-4/shape-11 blindness applied. Fixed in all THREE offline shims (`test.ts`'s `makeFigmaStub`, `apps/plugin/component-shim.ts`, and `lint-unclaimed-defaults.ts`'s own stub — the last two surfaced only when the full `verify` ran, each needing `setBoundVariable(field, null)` to unbind): a per-corner radius (a bound corner reads back resolved, an unbound one reads what was written, default 0) and the ring instance's INHERITED nominal-side binding are now modeled. `test.ts`'s absolute-part execution block carries the gate, and its EXPECTED is INDEPENDENT of the concentric code — the host's own radius (set by the bind loop, read off the built host) plus the DECLARED inset, never read back from the ring-radius producer. A parity assertion pins the PLUGIN executor's radius to the paste path's (itself pinned to that oracle), so both executors are covered. Circle and radius-0 are REPRESENTED, not counted (a full-round host asserted to yield radius ≥ side/2; a radius-0 host asserted to yield exactly the inset), and the clear has a POSITIVE CONTROL (a fresh un-hosted ring instance must carry the inherited binding the host then removes).

**Mutation-by-name (docs/34), run by commit-between-mutations (the checkout-restore trap, `git checkout --` reaches back to HEAD).** (a) Reverting the concentric four-corner write (ring stays radius 0) fails the named `anatomy/ring #1388: the ring's radius is CONCENTRIC` assertion AND both edge-case assertions, in both executors via the parity gate. (b) Dropping the `setBoundVariable(…, null)` clear fails the named `anatomy/ring #1388/#1290: the host CLEARS the ring instance's inherited width/height bindings` assertion, while its positive control stays green. Each restored, suite green again.

## (2026-09-10) — outline/text hover/pressed no longer paint a white box on the host: the DECLARED-but-UNRESOLVABLE fill neutralizes to transparent (#1387 / F1)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **No ENGINE bump, no CONTRACT bump** — a pure plugin-executor + shim + test change. Nothing under `out/**`, no schema baseline, and no `version.ts` moved (`regen --check` byte-identical, `lint-emission-version` agrees, `token-contract --check` unchanged) — the #1386/#1390 precedent. **`npm run verify` → 56/56 PASS (0 FAIL · 0 SKIP · 0 ADVISORY).**

**THE PREMISE WAS MISDIAGNOSED TWICE, and the log is worth keeping because the fix depended on getting past it.** The brief said outline/text buttons paint a "raw opaque `#ffffff` UNBOUND literal" and asked to bind the existing-but-unused `interactive.<palette>.subtle-fill.{hover,pressed}` role. Both halves were wrong against the code: (1) the emitter does NOT emit a literal — since #1219 the `container` box's `paintSlots: ['overlay','fill','border']` binds `interactive.<family>.overlay.{hover,pressed}` (the translucent wash, `outlineInteraction: 'overlay-neutral'` default) on outline/text hover/pressed, and that binding RENDERS correctly on every overlay-neutral brand; (2) `subtle-fill` is emitted ONLY under `outlineInteraction: 'solid-tint'`, which no corpus brand sets (`modes.ts`, #1112), so binding to it would be an unresolvable reference AND would smuggle the owner-held overlay↔solid-tint design choice into a "decision-free bug". Stopped and flagged rather than implementing; the owner corrected the brief to "bind the wash properly / fall back to no-fill, never white".

**THE REAL CAUSE (host-truth, evidence below).** The component set is BRAND-AGNOSTIC — one set, root-relative variable names, built in-plugin to bind against whatever brand is loaded (the only place brand-awareness can live is the executor, which reads `getLocalVariablesAsync`). So the projection binds `overlay.{hover,pressed}` UNCONDITIONALLY, while the token engine emits that wash only under `overlay-neutral`. On a brand built with `outlineInteraction: 'none'` or `'solid-tint'` the wash variable is genuinely absent from the file, the plugin executor's `paint()` returns null (miss reported), and the `container` FRAME keeps Figma's default **opaque white** fill — the audit's "SOLID `#ffffff`, opacity 1, unbound" on 324 members. Measured live (`figmaAnatomySet` paint refs vs `figmaArtifacts(brandTheme(...))` emitted variable tails): **0/213 dangling on every overlay-neutral brand** (nb, aurora, harbor, wendys, minimal) and **18/213 on `minimal-levers` (`outlineInteraction: none`)** — exactly the `interactive.*.overlay.{hover,pressed}` fills (default + inverse) across the six button/icon-button families. Alpha/translucent washes CAN be bound Figma variables (they render on overlay-neutral), so this is NOT a host limitation — option-3 fallback is not triggered.

**THE FIX (plugin executor, the brand-aware layer).** `write-components.ts`: a plan fill that is DECLARED but does not resolve against the loaded brand's catalogue now neutralizes to `[]` (transparent) instead of leaving the frame's white default, and still reports the miss. This EXTENDS `claimDefaults`' own rule ("nobody asked for a fill means no fill, not a white one") from UNCLAIMED to CLAIMED-BUT-UNRESOLVABLE; TEXT is exempt (`[]` is invisible text). Result: overlay-neutral → wash binds & renders (unchanged); `none`/`solid-tint` → the lever's intended clean no-change hover instead of a white box. The overlay-wash design, the `outlineInteraction` default, and the token names are all untouched — no switch to `subtle-fill`.

**THE GATE GAP THE AUDIT FLAGGED, now closed (docs/34).** Nothing checked that a fill RESOLVES to a bound variable rather than a literal on the host: `test-roundtrip.ts` derives its shim variable catalogue FROM the plan (so every paint always resolves — docs/34 shape 11), and both offline shims started frames at `fills: []`, so neither could witness Figma's white default (shape 4 — a stub models the axis or it cannot gate it). Fixed in `component-shim.ts` (the plugin shim now models the opaque white frame default) and gated in `test-write-components.ts` with three guards: a POSITIVE CONTROL (a freshly created frame carries the white default, so "no white after build" is a real check), a REACHABILITY floor (the 4 outline/text × hover/pressed members declare the overlay wash the audit flagged, so the neutralize path runs on exactly those containers — shape 9), and the INVARIANT (no built node keeps an opaque `#ffffff` literal where its plan declared an unresolvable paint). **Mutation-by-name:** reverting the executor neutralize fails exactly the named `#1387 no built node keeps an opaque #ffffff literal` assertion, alone (11 white containers — the 7 `filled` + 4 overlay coordinates), while the positive control and reachability floor stay green.

**SCOPE HELD — the PAYLOAD executor is a separate, broader defect, filed as #1393.** The fix lands on the plugin path (`applyComponentPlan`). The payload / MCP-console executor (`PAYLOAD_BUILD` in `anatomy-figma.ts`) has NO `claimDefaults`-equivalent pass at all, so it leaves Figma's defaults (incl. white) on UNCLAIMED coordinates (e.g. outline/text `rest`) as well as declared-but-unresolvable ones. A one-line copy of this fix there would be partial (still white at `rest`) and ungatable node-level today (`runPayload` returns only a summary; the payload stub doesn't model white). Ported properly with its own gate under **#1393**, not smuggled in here.

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **No ENGINE bump, no CONTRACT bump** — this is a gate/test-only change (`packages/engine/test.ts` and the payload stub it carries). Nothing under `out/**` or in `version.ts` moved.

**THE GAP, from #1386's independent review** (this file's #1386 entry, "THE PAYLOAD HALF IS STILL UNGATED in the sense #1377 meant"). `nest-exposed` (#1330) has TWO production executors that write `isExposedInstance = true` after `createComponentFromNode`: the plugin's `applyComponentPlan` (`write-components.ts`), gated host-truth by `test-roundtrip.ts` — and the PAYLOAD / MCP-build executor, the `PAYLOAD_BUILD` string's `__expose[]` queue (filled by `__expose.push(node)` near `anatomy-figma.ts:2347`, drained by `__exposeNow(member)` at each `createComponentFromNode` site). On `main`, deleting `__expose.push(node)` from the payload path left `test.ts`, `regen --check` and `mcp-test` all GREEN: `test:roundtrip` drives only the plugin executor, and every other payload assertion in `test.ts` reads the emitted string as TEXT — a substring probe over a string that documents itself (docs/34 shape 12).

It is the payload string's OWN read-back, not a second copy of the plugin's round-trip.

**WHY THE STUB HAD TO GROW A MODEL (docs/34).** `test.ts`'s payload stub modeled no `isExposedInstance` at all and `createComponentFromNode` was `(n) => n` — so the payload's exposure write landed on nothing and the read-back would have been vacuous. Both are now modeled in lockstep with `component-shim.ts` (the parity gate drives both executors against this one host): `isExposedInstance` starts a definite `false` (Figma's default) with a setter that REFUSES out of containment (Figma's message verbatim), and `createComponentFromNode` converts the root's type to `COMPONENT` in place — the two halves that make the deferred write meaningful. `=== true`, not truthiness (docs/34 shape 5): the default is a definite `false` and the payload's write is the only thing that moves it.


## (2026-09-09) — the read-back stops calling a per-side-bound `strokeWeight` DISCARDED (#1332)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** **No ENGINE bump, no CONTRACT bump** — this is a diagnostic/read-back fix, not an emission change. `regen --check` is clean (108 artifacts byte-match, no stamp movement), `lint-emission-version` agrees, and no guaranteed token name moved — the same shape as #1386. Every emitted artifact is identical; only the READ-BACK's acceptance criterion changed.

**THE DIAGNOSIS, from the 2026-09-09 host-truth Figma-console audit.** The build telemetry / read-back reported `strokeWeight → DISCARDED` for bordered components even though the weight WAS bound. On the real host, `setBoundVariable('strokeWeight', v)` does not bind the scalar `strokeWeight` key — it splits the binding across the **four per-side keys** `strokeTopWeight` / `strokeRightWeight` / `strokeBottomWeight` / `strokeLeftWeight` and leaves the scalar unbound. Confirmed bound on every bordered set: focus-ring (→`focus/ring/width`); checkbox-control / radio / switch / select / button (→`border-width/*`). The read-back asked `boundVariables.strokeWeight`, found nothing, and reported a false miss on a weight that is in fact bound.

**THE FIX — accept EITHER the scalar OR the COMPLETE per-side binding, in all four read-backs.** A weight now counts as held when `strokeWeight` is present OR all four per-side keys are. It is **not** weakened into always-passing: a partial per-side binding (three of four) or nothing at all is still a genuine miss the read-back reports. The four sites, one per surface:
- `anatomy-readback.ts` `boundIdOf` (the #874 round-trip reader) — resolves through any one per-side key (all four name one variable).
- `write-components.ts` — the per-node build read-back (#1266) and the post-combine set read-back (#1279), via a shared `weightHeld(bv, field)`.
- `anatomy-figma.ts` — the paste executor's per-node read-back (the code-read twin), inline in the payload string.

**WHY THE SHIMS HAD TO MODEL THE PER-SIDE SPLIT, which is the durable part (docs/34).** The offline shims recorded the SCALAR — so they agreed with the very assumption that produced the false `DISCARDED`, and the whole bordered corpus round-tripped green either way: a harness modelling the wrong host truth cannot witness the fix. Both shims (`component-shim.ts` and `test.ts`'s payload stub, kept in lockstep for the parity gate) now split `strokeWeight` into the four per-side keys on `setBoundVariable`, exactly as the audit found Figma does. With that, the whole bordered corpus exercises the per-side path, and the read reads it back off a side (measurement getters and the `#1266`/`#1228`/`#1278` weight assertions updated to match). `lint-unclaimed-defaults`'s shim stays scalar deliberately — it reads the prop NAME passed to `setBoundVariable`, not the split, and the read-back accepts a scalar too.

**MUTATION (docs/34), two ways.** (a) A new focused block in `test-roundtrip.ts` pins host truth and both directions BY NAME: the built ring binds the four per-side keys with the scalar unbound; a per-side-bound weight reads BOUND (no false `DISCARDED`); a GENUINELY unbound weight (a raw number, no keys) is reported `strokeWeight→UNBOUND`; and an INCOMPLETE per-side binding (three of four) is still reported, not accepted. (b) The corpus-wide check: reverting `boundIdOf`'s per-side branch fails **`every def round-trips` BY NAME** on all eleven bordered defs (`focus-ring, button×3, icon-button×3, checkbox-control, radio, switch, select — host: strokeWeight→UNBOUND`) AND the new positive assertion, then green again on restore.

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → **56/56 gates PASS** (0 FAIL · 0 SKIP · 0 ADVISORY). The per-gate table is in the PR body.

## (2026-09-09) — the `nest-exposed` marking moves past `createComponentFromNode` (#1378, closes #1377)

**STATUS: PR open, owner merges.** **No ENGINE bump, no CONTRACT bump** — and that is a claim worth defending rather than assuming. Every emitted artifact is byte-identical (`regen --check` clean, no stamp movement), `component-surface.json` and `paint-census.json` are unchanged, and the projected `checkbox` plan is the same plan it was before. The defect was never in what the engine PLANNED; it was that a correct plan could not be BUILT. `lint-emission-version` agrees without argument.

**FOUND IN THE FIELD, on a live apply into a QA file**, not by a gate:

```
component build failed: in set_isExposedInstance: Instance must be contained
within a component or component set to be exposed. — 2 nodes had already
reached the file; they are parked in the frame '⚠ Prism3 partial build —
checkbox (2 nodes; undo to remove)'
```

**THE DIAGNOSIS, AND THE CODE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN IT DOWN.** Both executors carried the same comment above the same write:

> ``isExposedInstance` is writeable on a primary instance inside a component/set, which a member's nested instance becomes **after combine**.`

Correct, and then contradicted one line later: the write sat inside `build`, which assembles a member's whole subtree DETACHED and hands the root to `createComponentFromNode` only afterwards. At write time the chain above the nested instance terminates in a parentless FRAME. Figma refuses, and because the refusal lands mid-build the whole 3-member set dies with 2 nodes already in the file — `checkbox-control` (which nests nothing, so it is never marked) built fine, which is what made this read as "one component is broken" rather than "the ordering is wrong". #1330's author had already filed the doubt as **#1378** ("Verify on real Figma: `isExposedInstance` is settable at nest-exposed write time"). It is not. The answer is now in the title.

**THE FIX** — collect during the build, write after the conversion, in both executors. The plugin threads a per-member `expose: Wr[]` alongside the existing `parts` map (same reason, same shape: one array shared across a set would carry members' handles into each other's marking pass). The payload executor has no per-member collector to thread, so it uses a module-level queue drained by `__exposeNow(member)` at each of its three `createComponentFromNode` sites, cleared on the way out. Both write per node and read back, so a refusal costs one exposure instead of the set — the failure mode that stranded 2 nodes in a live file.

**WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT, WHICH IS THE DURABLE PART.** `test-roundtrip` drives the real executor against `component-shim.ts` and went green on a write the real host rejects outright, for two compounding reasons — and the pair is the lesson, because each one hid the other:

1. `isExposedInstance` was a plain settable field. The shim's own header states the rule it needed here — *"a shim that cannot refuse cannot witness a refusal"* — 15 lines above, about `textAlignVertical`. This field got 7 lines of comment asserting the containment precondition and modeled none of it.
2. `createComponentFromNode` was `(n) => n` — the identity function. Returning the same object is right (Figma converts in place, which the executor's own trail bookkeeping depends on), but leaving the TYPE alone made the shim model a host where a converted frame never becomes a component. So even a correctly-modeled precondition could only ever have refused, and the fix would have looked like the bug.

Both are now modeled. **The `nestExpose` predicate had been reporting `compared NOTHING` — a predicate with no subject** — because the build threw before reaching those nodes; it now walks 3. That counter is the only reason the hole was visible at all, and it earned its keep here exactly as its own comment predicted.

**A THIRD FINDING FELL OUT OF THE TYPE FLIP, and it is not collateral.** With the shim converting, 1,694 members diverged on `type`: plan `FRAME`, host `COMPONENT`. The host is right — a member root IS a component after conversion, on every member of every set, in every real file. `HOST_TYPE.FRAME = ['FRAME']` had been agreeing with the shim's failure to convert, so the readback would have been wrong the first time anyone pointed it at a live member root. Fixed with an `isRoot` flag threaded through `diffNode`, set `true` at exactly one call site, rather than by widening `FRAME` to accept `COMPONENT` everywhere — a stray component inside a member is a real defect shape and this predicate must keep noticing it.

**VERIFICATION — three mutations, and the middle one is the informative failure:**

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| exposure collection disabled (`if (false && …)`) | `nestExpose 3× :: row/controlBox/control` — **fails by name** |
| shim precondition disabled | still PASSES — correct, and not a hole: with the write now in a legal place the precondition has nothing to refuse. Its witness is the run below. |
| write moved back into `build` (the pre-fix ordering, new shim) | fails with Figma's message **verbatim** — the shim now guards the ordering permanently |

The gate was built and confirmed failing *before* the fix, which is the strongest available order: the shim reproduced the live error message exactly, off a file it has never seen. 56/56 gates pass.

**TRAP FOR WHOEVER RE-VERIFIES THIS.** Whether the marking survives `combineAsVariants` is **still unmeasured**. It is written after `createComponentFromNode` and before the combine, and #1279 has the combine dropping bindings, while the shim's detach-mode twin explicitly copies `isExposedInstance` across — i.e. combine-loses-it is a modeled possibility, not an idle worry. The per-node read-back would report a `DISCARDED` miss if the host dropped it at that point, so the failure is instrumented rather than silent, but nobody has watched it happen on a live host. **Do not read this PR's green suite as proof of that step.** Filed as **#1385**.

**THE PAYLOAD HALF IS STILL UNGATED** in the sense #1377 meant: the fix is a code-read twin of the plugin's, and no harness drives the generated payload against a host. #1377 is closed because the shim gap it named is closed and the defect it would have caught is fixed; the standing asymmetry between the two executors is #1265's territory.

## (2026-09-09) — icon-property canon + the #1309 Figma display-name mechanism (#1380, closes #1309)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges, and folds in the `prism3-build-component` skill doc at merge time).** ENGINE bump 0.74.0 → **0.75.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — a Figma display name is neither a token name nor a React prop, so the guaranteed 577 are unchanged (`token-contract.ts --check` confirms; `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp).

**The canon (owner-decided, from a live Prism2 reference; implemented not re-decided).** Every component with leading/trailing icon slots projects its Figma properties panel as: `label` (text) at the TOP, then `leading icon` (a true/false variant **switch**) immediately followed by `↳ swap leading icon` (instance swap), then `trailing icon` → `↳ swap trailing icon`. All lowercase; the `↳ ` prefix (U+21B3 + space) on the swaps only, which is what makes Figma render the swap nested beneath its switch. Applied to **button** (leading + trailing) and **select** (leading only — its glyph sits inside `content`, no #326 asymmetry). **icon-button** (owner-decided 2026-09-09): its icon is REQUIRED — no presence switch — so its swap gets `swap icon`, lowercase, **NO `↳`** (nothing to nest under); identity unchanged.

**The core — the #1309 mechanism.** The Figma property NAME was the code prop/axis name verbatim: `planSetProperties` used the `texts`/`swaps` KEY, and the presence-axis panel name was the slot-axis `name`. So `↳ swap leading icon` could not be a property name without being a React prop. #1309 adds an OPTIONAL `figmaName` decoupling, extended beyond `texts` to **`swaps`** (now a `string | {part, figmaName}` union) **and the presence axes** (`slotAxes[].figmaName`). The code prop/axis stays idiomatic (`leadingVisual`, `label`, `leading`/`trailing`); only the projected name changes — which is why CONTRACT holds. `figmaPropertyErrors` validates the KEY against `props` as before and NEVER requires `figmaName` to be a prop; it adds two rules on the display name itself — it must RENDER, and panel names must be UNIQUE (a name colliding with a variant/state axis or another property fails).

**How the presence-axis name flows (the load-bearing part).** A presence axis is a variant axis, so its Figma property name IS the member-name segment Figma derives the variant property from. `planComponentName` therefore writes the `figmaName` (`leading icon=true`) into the coordinate, and everything that parses that coordinate follows in step: `figmaAxisNames` (so the axis-parity gate compares like with like), `planSetLayout`'s footprint-cohort `group`, and the chunked payload's `cellOf` (via a new injected `SLOT_KEYS`). `AnatomyPlan.slotFigmaNames` carries the decoupled names — present ONLY when a def decouples, and OMITTED otherwise so `planStamp` does not move for any untouched def. `planSetProperties` now orders text → swap → boolean, the "label at the top" half of the canon (the panel INTERLEAVE of variant switches with component properties is host-RENDERED, the repo's standing "owner's Figma check, not ours" position — what the engine controls and gates is that `label` is created first).

**Baselines re-accepted (touched defs only).** `schema/component-surface.json` moved for button×3 + icon-button×3 + select (7 digests — the member NAMES carry the switch labels, and icon-button's swap propertyRef carries `swap icon`). `schema/paint-census.json` moved for button×3 + select ONLY (the census hashes a coordinate that carries the slot-axis name; icon-button's coordinate has no slot axis, so its swap rename is invisible to the census — correctly unchanged). Every other def byte-identical; `regen --check` moves only each `out/**` artifact's generator stamp (0.74.0 → 0.75.0).

**Mutation (docs/34), by manual edit-and-restore over the committed tree (a `wip:` commit was made first — the `git checkout --` trap).** (a) Changing button's leading swap `figmaName` (`↳ swap leading icon` → `↳ swap LEADING GLYPH`) fails **`lint-component-surface` BY NAME** (`surface/button … DRIFTED`, ×3) AND the roundtrip **`panel order (#1380): button`** host-truth (host holds the mutated label). (b) Removing `planSetProperties`'s text→swap sort fails the roundtrip **`panel order (#1380): button`** AND **`select`** by name (host holds `↳ swap leading icon` before `label`). Both restored; suites green after. The display-name validator's two rules (renders, uniqueness) are exercised by direct negative probes.

**Skill doc (folded in by the orchestrator at merge, in this PR).** `skills/prism3-build-component/SKILL.md` §6 ("Naming canon") now documents the `figmaName` display-name field and the icon-property canon — `label` first, `leading icon`/`trailing icon` true/false switches with `↳ swap leading icon`/`↳ swap trailing icon` nested beneath, and the required-single-icon `swap icon` case — so a future component author follows it. `lint-skills` gates that prose against the shipped mechanism. It also leaves §3's stale `nest-exposed` "REFUSED (#761)" line untouched (that predates #1330 and is filed separately — one concern per PR).

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → every gate PASS. The per-gate table is in the PR body. Scope note: `#1331` (select 40→20 count) and `#1379` (button count) stay OPEN — this renames and reorders, it does not cut counts.

## (2026-09-09) — `nest-exposed` is BUILT; the checkbox Row collapses 54 → 3 (#1330, reverses #761)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.73.0 → **0.74.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — a Figma variant/axis collapse is component-API surface, not a token name (the #1327/#1333 reading); `token-contract.ts --check` confirms the guaranteed 577 unchanged, `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp.

**The problem (owner-APPROVED, #1330; implement not re-decide).** A composed component NESTED its child and then RE-ENUMERATED the child's variant axes into its own variant set instead of EXPOSING the nested instance's properties. Measured in QA: the checkbox Row declared `variantAxes: ['selection','size']` + a 6-value `stateAxis` and nested `checkbox-control` `nest-fixed` with `follow: ['selection','size','state']` — **54 members (3 selections × 3 sizes × 6 states) that merely mirrored the atom it nests**. The owner approved reversing #761 (which had deferred `nest-exposed` "pending the property-count measurement"). The MECHANISM was mine to design.

**The schema shape I chose, and why (`NestingRelation`).** `nest-exposed` carries the SAME `variant` + `follow` as `nest-fixed` PLUS a new `expose: readonly string[]` naming the CHILD axes the consumer drives from the parent. Per-property opt-in, NOT a bare flag: `tools/nest-exposed-cost/measure.ts` had already measured the two candidate shapes (a bare `nestExposed:true` vs a named list) and found they cost the same (≈35 B at the one cliff), so the choice is SEMANTIC. Naming the axes is what lets the Row expose `selection` + `state` while `follow`ing its OWN `size` (size scales the label ramp, the gap and the row height — the control does not touch those, so it stays the Row's axis). `variant` is the DEFAULT member the instance starts at (an instance is always of ONE member) — `{selection:'unchecked', state:'rest'}`, with `follow:['size']` filling size per Row member. Validator enforces: non-empty `variant`, non-empty `expose`, `expose ∩ follow = ∅`, and the same `follow`-reachability rule `nest-fixed` has.

**The projection + both executors.** `FigmaNodePlan` gains `nestExpose` (emitted only for `nest-exposed`; `nestVariant` is now emitted for BOTH relations — the default coordinate). Both executors (the pasted payload in `anatomy-figma.ts` and `apps/plugin/src/write-components.ts`) mark the nested instance `isExposedInstance = true` (Figma's real, all-or-nothing primitive, confirmed writable in `@figma/plugin-typings`). `anatomy-readback.ts` classifies `nestExpose` as a CHECKED field (host-truth: the built instance must read back `isExposedInstance === true`), and `component-shim.ts` models `isExposedInstance` (default `false`, carried across `combineAsVariants`). The all-or-nothing Figma reality vs the named-axis intent is documented (the axes drive React/`.ai.json`/Storybook; Figma exposes wholesale with `size` pre-pinned by `follow`).

**The checkbox Row (checkbox.ts).** The `control` nest becomes `nest-exposed` (`expose: ['selection','state']`, `follow: ['size']`, `variant: {selection:'unchecked', state:'rest'}`). `selection` drops from `variants` and `variantAxes`; the `stateAxis` is removed; `figmaProperties.variantAxes` is `['size']` → **3 members**. `checkbox-control` (the atom) is UNCHANGED and still carries the full 54-member selection×size×state set. The Row's React props (`checked`, `indeterminate`, `size`, …) are the code API and STAY — only the Figma VARIANT matrix collapses. The Row keeps its `states` list so `lint-paint` arm 2 (which reads `def.states`, not the stateAxis) keeps `disabled.label` reachable; the label's per-state Figma treatment is now `codeOnly` (a disabled Row in Figma shows the exposed disabled CONTROL beside a full-ink label — the documented cost of the collapse). `lint-axis-values`' `selection` register entry drops `checkbox`, leaving `checkbox-control`.

**The two baselines re-accepted (checkbox ROW only).** `schema/component-surface.json` (checkbox 54 → 3 members) and `schema/paint-census.json` (checkbox set 54 → 3, grid 63 → 21) — every other def byte-identical. `regen --check` moves only each `out/**` artifact's generator stamp (0.73.0 → 0.74.0); no token byte moved, which is why CONTRACT holds.

**Mutation (docs/34), by manual edit-and-restore over the committed tree (a `wip:` commit was made first — the `git checkout --` trap):** (a) reverting the control nest to `nest-fixed` (same 3-member count, `nestExpose` dropped) fails **`lint-component-surface` BY NAME**: `surface/checkbox: plan digest e93f84cd…, baseline 8289636c… — the same member COUNT, projecting different plans`. (b) dropping the executor's `node.isExposedInstance = true` write fails **`test-roundtrip` (host-truth, #1371) BY NAME**: the `nestExpose` predicate reports `isExposedInstance=false — the nested instance was not marked exposed` on all 3 Row members, `❌ 1 FAILED`. Both restored; suite green after. The schema shape's four negative rules (empty variant, empty expose, expose∩follow, follow-reachability) are mutation-proven as `ibBroke` assertions in `test.ts`'s nesting gate.

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → **56/56 gates PASS** (0 FAIL · 0 SKIP · 0 ADVISORY). The per-gate table is in the PR body.

## (2026-09-09) — split the overloaded `tone` variant axis → `status` (validation) and `emphasis` (label prominence) (#1334)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.72.0 → **0.73.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — an axis rename is component-API surface, not a token name (the #1327/#1333 reading); `token-contract.ts --check` confirms the guaranteed 577 unchanged, `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp.

**The problem (owner-approved 2026-09-08, part of #1329; implement not re-decide).** `tone` was carrying three concepts across the corpus: `icon`'s semantic INK role (`inherit`/`primary`/…/`info`), `field-message` + `select`'s validation OUTCOME (`[default, error, warning, success]`), and `field-label`'s label EMPHASIS (`[primary, secondary]`). `lint-axis-values.ts`'s register recorded the strain directly — the validation set stood `overlapping` with icon's ink set (shares `success`/`warning`, diverges `error`↔`danger`) and the emphasis set a `subset` of it. Two axes reading as one is the #756 failure mode arriving from the inside. The owner's split: the validation axis → **`status`** (which the plugin studio UI already calls those palettes), field-label's emphasis axis → **`emphasis`**.

**Scope call, flagged for the owner.** The issue says "retire `tone` entirely" but enumerates only the two overloaded uses (field-message/select, field-label) — it never mentions **`icon`**, which also declares a `tone` axis (the nine-value semantic-ink vocabulary). That is a *distinct third concept*, not part of the overload the issue describes, and renaming it would be an unapproved design decision with its own naming question. So this PR renames the three named defs and **leaves `icon.tone` untouched**; `VARIANT_AXES` keeps `tone` (icon) and gains `status` + `emphasis` (16th and 17th names). "Retire `tone` entirely" is therefore scoped to the overloaded uses — `tone` now has exactly one honest, non-overlapping use (icon's ink). If the owner wants icon's axis renamed too, that is a separate change.

**The change (mirrors #1327/#1333 rename machinery).** In each def: the `variants` key, the paint-key placeholder (`{tone}` → `{status}`/`{emphasis}`), `presentWhen` coords (field-message's three glyphs), `variantAxes`, `footprintVaries` and `byVariant` (field-message), `select`'s message-nest `follow: ['status']` + fallback `variant`, and `select`'s field-label-nest `emphasis: 'secondary'` coord. The mirrored consumer props renamed too (`field-message.tone` → `status`, `field-label.tone` → `emphasis`); `select`'s prop stays `validation` (it was already decoupled, and the follow drives the nested message by axis name). Gates carrying the axis name updated: `lint-axis-values` register (3 entries — field-label→`emphasis`/`sole`, field-message+select→`status`/`sole`, icon `tone` `canonical`→`sole`), `lint-glyph-geometry` `at` coords (functional), and prose in `lint-paint`/`lint-rung-names`/`lint-component-surface`/`anatomy-figma`/`component-schema`.

**Token keys do NOT move, which is why CONTRACT holds.** Paint keys resolve the placeholder to the axis VALUE (`{status}` → `error`), so a def's `tokens` keys (`error.label`, `error.border.rest`, …) are value+slot and are byte-identical. `lint-paint`'s `PROVENANCE_EXCEPTIONS` keys (`field-message|error.label`, `select|error.border.rest`) are resolved keys — unchanged; only their prose was updated. No `DEPRECATIONS`/`MATERIALIZATION_RENAMES` entry owed (an axis rename is neither a token-PATH move nor a Figma-collection rename — the #1327 reading); both gates pass with 0 claims.

**What DID move, and the two baselines re-accepted.** `out/**` moved only each artifact's generator stamp (0.72.0 → 0.73.0) — `regen --check` confirms no token-layer byte moved. The projected COMPONENT SURFACE moves because member names carry the axis (`status=error` replacing `tone=error`; `emphasis=…`): `schema/component-surface.json` re-`--accept`ed for field-label (24), field-message (4), select (40) at unchanged member COUNTS. And **`schema/paint-census.json` DOES move for all three** — unlike #1333's TEXT-property rename — because the census hashes a `(coordinate, node path, slot, variable)` row and the coordinate carries the axis NAME; re-`--accept`ed (assignment counts unchanged, every other def byte-identical).

**No studio/plugin UI text changed.** The axis name is the projection (the Figma variant property name); `apps/studio/src/main.ts` and the plugin do not display the component axis name to the user (the word `tone` does not appear in either), and the studio's own "emphasis"/"status" strings are unrelated concepts (button/neutral emphasis, weight roles, the `status.*` colour levers — the task's "do not rename unrelated uses" case). Select's consumer-facing "Validation" label is unchanged.

**Mutation (docs/34), by manual edit-and-restore over the committed tree** (a `wip:` commit was made first — the CLAUDE.md `git checkout --` trap). Cleanly reverting `select`'s axis `status`→`tone` in the def (internally consistent) at the unchanged 40-member count fails **`lint-component-surface.ts` BY NAME**: `surface/select: plan digest 5be66c441bab…, baseline d442f622330e… — the same member COUNT, projecting different plans`. It is also caught by **`lint-axis-values.ts`** (ARM A: `select · tone: [default, error, warning, success]` undeclared; ARM B: `status: […] names 'select', which does not declare that axis`). Hand-written `test.ts` literals (not derived) also pin the rename: `fieldMessage.variants.status`, the projected member names `status=default | …`, `field-label.variants.emphasis` (new assertion added), and the plugin `test-write-components.ts` member-name join. Restored; both gates green after.

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → **56/56 gates PASS** (0 FAIL · 0 SKIP · 0 ADVISORY). The per-gate table is in the PR body.

The exact reconstructed line: **`lineHeights: { tight: 1.2, snug: 1.2, compact: 1.2 }`**. Flagged inline in the brief and in the PR body.

## (2026-09-09) — two opt-in caption fine-print rungs: `caption.sm` = 10px (#1360) and an 8px escape hatch (#1363)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.71.0 → **0.72.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — both rungs are emitted ONLY for a brand that opts in, so no corpus brand emits them and the guaranteed token-name surface is unchanged (`token-contract.ts --check` confirms 577 guaranteed unchanged; `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp).

**The problem (owner decision, settled 2026-09-09; implement both as OPT-IN levers, off by default).** Two fine-print sizes measured on the New Balance redesign have no engine representation. `caption` ships `md` (11px) and `lg` (12px); there is no 10px rung, even though 10 is the ladder floor — and 10px is NB's single highest-volume text size (1,073 nodes) (#1360). And 8px (`Body Copy/8`, 144 nodes at a literal 1:1 scale) is below the ladder floor entirely: `fontSizeLadder()` was a brand-invariant `[10, 11, 12, …]`, so 8px was unreachable by any brand input (#1363). Both were filed rather than fixed because adding a rung is a public-contract change; the owner has now decided to ship both, off by default so no corpus brand moves.

**The change — two enumerated opt-in levers modeled on `titleFloor`** (set membership on one group, touching nothing else):
- **`typography.captionFloor: 11 | 10`** (default 11). `10` adds `caption.sm` = 10px. 10 is already a ladder step, so this is pure set membership — the rung is pushed in `buildComposites` ahead of `caption.md`, through the same strictly-increasing ramp guard.
- **`typography.sizeFloor: 10 | 8`** (default 10). `8` PREPENDS an 8px step to `fontSizeLadder` (which gains a `floor` arg; the rest of the ladder is byte-identical) and adds `caption.xs` = 8px. Threaded through both `fontSizeLadder` call sites in `buildTypography` (`sizesPx` and `buildComposites`), so the `modeLevers.typeSizes` ladder check and the fluid `mobileEndpoint` — both of which read `typography.sizesPx` — stay consistent for free. Caption is reading text (static, never fluid), so the "8px has nowhere to shrink on mobile" concern is moot.

The two levers are **orthogonal** — either, both, or neither. Both registered in `levers.ts` (regenerating `schema/lever-manifest.json`, 39 → 41 levers) and `schema/theme-schema.json` (so the input is accepted and the manifest→schema parity gate passes), and enforced by `validateBrandInput` (enum `[10,11]` / `[8,10]`).

**8px is an escape hatch, and the engine says so.** 8px sits below every practical legibility floor and below the size range this system's contrast ratios were reasoned about. So `sizeFloor:8` pushes a FLAGGED note into the decisions log (`$extensions.prism3.decisions`) the way `actionPalette` flags a decoupled action colour — a deliberate, recorded exception, never a rung reached by accident. `captionFloor:10` (ordinary fine print, already on the default ladder) is not flagged.

**Default-off, so the corpus is byte-identical.** No corpus brand (aurora/harbor/wendys/nb/minimal/minimal-levers) sets either lever, so every emitted `out/**` byte is unchanged except each artifact's generator stamp (0.71.0 → 0.72.0). Both note additions — the caption clause in the main typography note AND the escape-hatch note — are gated on the opt-in, so a default brand's decisions log does not move (the first draft appended the caption clause unconditionally and moved all 8 artifacts; caught by `test.ts`'s byte-identical arm and made conditional). `regen --check` confirms it.

**The docs/34 gate, extended here rather than filed.** Nothing gated the type SIZE ladder for these opt-in rungs before this: `lint-ramp-*` gate the studio radius/space ramp previews and `lint-axis-values` gates component `VARIANT_AXES` — neither the type-size ladder, which is gated in `test.ts`. A new `test.ts` **C1d** block REPRESENTS both rungs and the flag: the default caption tier is md/lg only; `captionFloor:10` adds caption.sm=10; `sizeFloor:8` adds caption.xs=8 AND floors the ladder at 8; opting in APPENDS caption rungs only (every non-caption composite byte-identical); and `sizeFloor:8` is FLAGGED as an escape hatch in notes. The oracle is the fixed ladder step (10/8) and the flag string, independent of the composite arithmetic. Both opt-ins also run through the full `typeCases` composite-invariant battery.

**Mutation (docs/34), by manual edit-and-restore over the committed tree** (never `git checkout --` on uncommitted work — the CLAUDE.md trap; a `wip:` commit was made first). Removing the `caption.sm` push fails **C1d `[#1360] captionFloor:10 adds caption.sm=10px` BY NAME**; removing the `caption.xs` push fails **`[#1363] sizeFloor:8 adds caption.xs=8px` BY NAME**; removing the 8px `fontSizeLadder` prepend fails **`[#1363] sizeFloor:8 pushes the size-ladder floor to 8px` BY NAME**; removing the escape-hatch `notes.push` fails **`[#1363] sizeFloor:8 is FLAGGED as an escape hatch in notes` BY NAME**. All restored.

**Studio + plugin exposure is automatic.** Both are proper levers in `levers.ts`, so the studio and plugin auto-expose them via the lever manifest — no separate UI work, which is the required UI path. `skills/prism3-theme/SKILL.md` documents both (lint-skills gates it).

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → full suite, all-PASS (0 FAIL). The per-gate table is in the PR body.

## (2026-09-09) — an opt-in 1px `radius.hairline` sentinel (#1362)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.70.0 → **0.71.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — `radius.hairline` is emitted ONLY for a brand that opts in, so no corpus brand emits it and the guaranteed token-name surface is unchanged (`token-contract.ts --check` confirms 577 guaranteed unchanged; `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp).

**The problem (owner Option A, settled 2026-09-08; implemented not re-decided).** The radius ramp rides an even 2px sub-grid — `radiusScale()` snaps every non-`none` rung with `snap2 = (v) => Math.round(v / 2) * 2` — so 1px / 3px / 5px are unreachable from ANY `radiusScale` (∈[0,2]) / `baseMd` (∈[2,12]) input. New Balance's redesign uses **1px** as its dominant corner (68 nodes, a deliberate near-sharp look), which the closest faithful input (`radiusScale: 1`) renders at 2px and `radiusScale: 0` flattens to sharp. The constraint is the sub-grid itself.

**The change.** Rather than change the `snap2` math (which would move the scaled ramp for every brand), a FIXED, UNSCALED `hairline` = 1px rung is added the **same way the `round`/`capsule` pills are** — pushed onto the ramp AFTER the scaled-ladder computation and its monotonicity guard, so it perturbs neither — but gated on a new opt-in `radiusHairline` brand-input lever (a `form` toggle, **off by default**). Unlike the pills it is not a pill (no clamp semantics, no `pill` flag) and it is ON the 4px dimension grid (`dimensionGrid` seeds 0/1/2), so `tree.ts` aliases it (`radius.hairline → {…dimension.1}`) rather than minting a literal. Threaded `scale.ts` (`radiusScale` gains a `hairline` param) → `theme.ts` (`buildDims`, plus both the baseline and per-mode `radiusScale` calls so a `modeLevers.radius` ramp carries the sentinel too and still no-diffs on it — 1px is mode-invariant), registered in `levers.ts` (regenerating `schema/lever-manifest.json`) and `schema/theme-schema.json` (so `validateBrandInput` accepts it and the manifest→schema parity gate in `test.ts` passes).

**Default-off, so the corpus is byte-identical.** No corpus brand (aurora/harbor/wendys/nb) sets `radiusHairline`, so every emitted radius is unchanged to the byte — the only `out/**` diff is each artifact's own generator stamp (0.70.0 → 0.71.0). This is an opt-in ADD, not a default change. **NB is deliberately NOT switched on in this PR** — that is a separate brand-input change; this PR only makes 1px reachable.

**The docs/34 finding, fixed here rather than filed.** The radius SENTINELS were not gated for presence at all before this: the `round`/`capsule` pills are pushed unconditionally and nothing asserted they exist — `test.ts` L-03 filters `!r.pill` and never looks at the pills themselves, so a deleted `ramp.push(...)` would have gone silently green. A new `test.ts` **L-03b** block now asserts each sentinel is PRESENT and UNSCALED across scales (round=128/capsule=999 pill, hairline=1 non-pill, all fixed at scale 0…2), that hairline is ABSENT unless opted in, that opting in leaves the scaled ladder byte-identical (the sentinel only appends), that the scaled ladder stays EVEN at every scale (1px reachable ONLY via the sentinel), and that an opted-in brand EMITS `radius.hairline` aliasing `{…dimension.1}` while a plain brand emits none. Independent of the scaled-rung arithmetic — the oracle is the FIXED contract of a sentinel (px does not move with scale; 1px is unreachable from the even ladder), not a recomputation of the ramp.

**Mutation (docs/34), by manual edit-and-restore over the committed tree (never `git checkout --` on uncommitted work — the CLAUDE.md trap; a `wip:` commit was made first).** (a) Removing the `hairline` push in `scale.ts` fails **6 L-03b assertions BY NAME** (`radius.hairline = 1px, unscaled and non-pill (scale=…)` and the emitted-tree arm). (b) Altering the `round` push (px 128 → 129) fails **4 L-03b assertions BY NAME** (`radius.round sentinel present, pill, fixed at 128px`), proving the pill-presence arm bites too. Both restored.

**Studio exposure.** The toggle is added to the "Corner radius" section beside `baseMd` and `radiusScale` (`renderSizeRadiusPage`), rendered by the studio's generic `toggle` control — the same explicit-key pattern `baseMd` uses. So it is usable end-to-end (studio + `BrandInput`/`design.md`), not just plumbed.

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → full suite, all-PASS (0 FAIL). The per-gate table is in the PR body.
