## (2026-09-08) — the text-bearing button family sizes its icon one rung smaller than its control (#1350)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.69.0 → **0.70.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — a component binding is a reference to a token name, never a token name; every rung it now points at already ships (`token-contract.ts --check` confirms 577 guaranteed paths unchanged; `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp).

**The change (owner Option A, settled 2026-09-08; implemented not re-decided).** The audit in #1350 found the button family's icon slots bound to `icon.size.{sm,md,lg}` = 20/24/32 (small/medium/large), and the owner judged `large` = 32 too big, fixing `large` = 24 and shifting the whole family down one rung. So `button` / `button-destructive` / `button-neutral` rebind their leading/trailing icon slots to `icon.size.{xs,sm,md}` = **16 / 20 / 24**. `icon-button` is **UNCHANGED** (icon-only, so its larger glyph is intended). One binding edit per size, in the shared `makeButton` factory, so all three text-button defs move together.

**This intentionally reverses #756's composition-identity position — for buttons only, and the owner sanctioned it.** #324/#756 built a three-way identity: a standalone `<Icon>`, a Button's leading visual, and an icon-button's glyph all render the same size at a given control size (medium → 24 everywhere), so control size → icon size is the identity rather than a reconciliation. The owner has now sanctioned a labelled button carrying a glyph **one rung smaller** than a standalone icon: the label already carries the button, so the flanking glyph reads better small. `icon-button` has no label to lean on, so it keeps the 1:1 ladder and still matches a standalone icon. **The composition identity now holds for icon-button and is deliberately offset for buttons.** Recorded here, in `lint-rung-names.ts`'s arm 3 header, and in `button.ts`'s `size.*.icon` block.

**The #756 gates are RE-POINTED, not deleted (docs/34 — the invariant changed shape, it did not disappear).**
- `lint-rung-names.ts` arm 3 (#756's default-`md` rule) now checks the default rung **per tier family** and expects the button family's `icon.size.*` family at `OFFSET_DEFAULT_RUNG` — exactly one rung below `md`, i.e. `sm` — while every other family (geometry, label type) still resolves to `md`. The expected rung is derived from the RULE (`RUNG_ORDER` minus one from `md`), never from the button's own binding, so the two sides of the comparison stay independent. A new `ICON_OFFSET_DEFS` records the sanctioned pair and is checked BOTH directions (a listed def that does not exist, or that stops binding the named family at its default, fails as stale).
- `test.ts`'s icon-button↔button parity assertion now asserts the button's leading visual is **exactly one `ICON_SIZES` rung below** the icon-button's glyph (and that they diverge — equality would mean the offset was reverted), with the ladder order as the independent oracle. The offset is asserted on the bound-variable NAME (`icon/size/sm` vs `icon/size/md`), not resolved pixels, for the same reason lint-rung-names does: the defect class is a wrong-NAME-that-resolves.

Both still FAIL BY NAME if the button icon drifts to any rung other than the sanctioned offset.

**Versioning (#1252 decision).** ENGINE and not CONTRACT. Every rung the button now points at (`icon.size.{xs,sm,md}`) already ships in all four brands, so no token path is added, removed or retyped and `CONTRACT_VERSION` stands at 10.0.0. What moves is the PROJECTED COMPONENT SURFACE: the three button defs' leading/trailing icon members bind a different `icon.size.*` variable and measure a different artboard, so each member's `planStamp` moves and `schema/component-surface.json` was re-`--accept`ed for the three defs (member COUNT holds at 432 each). `lint-emission-version` is blind to it — component payloads are not committed under `out/` — the exact gap `lint-component-surface` covers. `regen --check` moves only each committed artifact's own generator stamp (0.69.0 → 0.70.0).

**Mutation (docs/34), both run by manual edit-and-restore over the committed tree (never `git checkout --` on uncommitted work — the CLAUDE.md trap).** (a) Reverting a button icon rung in the def (e.g. `size.medium.icon` back to `icon.size.md`) moves the three button members' `planStamp` and fails **`lint-component-surface` BY NAME** (`surface/button` / `-destructive` / `-neutral`, same member count, different plan). (b) Mutating the button icon to a NON-sanctioned size — back to `md`(24), or a two-rung slip to `xs`(16) at medium — fails the re-pointed **`lint-rung-names` arm 3 BY NAME** (`its OWNER-SANCTIONED icon family 'icon.size.*' reaches tier rung(s) '…' — the #1350 offset is that the button family's icon resolves to 'sm'…`) AND the **`test.ts` parity assertion BY NAME** (`the button's leading visual is EXACTLY ONE ICON RUNG BELOW the icon-button's glyph`). Both restored.

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → full suite, all-PASS (0 FAIL). The per-gate table is in the PR body.

## (2026-09-08) — the destructive button ink clears the floor on darker surfaces, not just white (#1352)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.68.0 → **0.69.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — this moves token VALUES, not names (`token-contract.ts --check` confirms 577 guaranteed paths unchanged; `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp).

**The defect (owner-settled decision, implemented not re-decided; issue comment 2026-09-08).** The Destructive Button's `text`/`outline` appearance binds its label + icon to `interactive.destructive.text.*`, which was gated only against `background.primary`. On a white page that landed the light interactive red (~danger 500, e.g. aurora `#c94c44` at 4.56:1) — but the moment the button sat on a slightly-darker card (`background.secondary`/`tertiary`) the ink dropped to ~3.3:1, an AA failure. The inverse variant had the mirror-image hole: `inverse.interactive.destructive.text.*` gated only against the darkest inverse band (`#d9554c` at 4.95:1) and fell to ~4.1:1 on the lighter inverse tiers. The owner reframed the original "should inverse be red?" question into a decision-free contrast fix: destructive text/icon must pass ≥4.5:1 on white AND on the darker surfaces it can sit on, pulling from a status-negative dark enough to clear the floor — the destructive ink "should rarely be the brand red".

**The diagnosis — one wrong ground, two contexts.** The interactive ink helpers (`iText`, `invColumn`) gated the destructive ink against the *primary* surface of their context, not the WORST-CASE one. A destructive outline/text button can sit on any page tier, whose darkest emitted surface is `background.tertiary` (and, on the inverse band, whose LIGHTEST — least-contrast-for-a-light-ink — is `inverse.background.tertiary`). Gating on the primary surface alone left the ink one rung too light for the tiers it actually sits on. The floor family (`floorRgb` = neutral 50) does NOT cover this: it is *lighter* than the surface ladder, so it is not the worst case for these page-placed inks — the tertiary tier is.

**The fix — gate the destructive ink (and the border that follows it) against the worst-case tier of its context.** `iText`/`invColumn` gained an optional `ground`/`against` pair (default `background.primary` / `inverse.background.primary`, so every OTHER column is byte-identical). The destructive column passes `background.tertiary` on the page and `inverse.background.tertiary` on the inverse band. Deriving "the darkest negative that clears the floor" is mechanical — the least danger step clearing `secondaryMin` on the worst surface — so it is done here rather than flagged as a hue choice. It lands the page ink on the danger-600 neighbourhood (`#a13731` for a neutral-white page — the same status-negative `text.danger` already uses, exactly the value the owner named) and the inverse ink a rung lighter (danger-400, `#e0695e`), each clearing 4.5:1 on every tier of its context. The FILL and `on-fill` are untouched; only the outline/text ink and the border that follows it move. Once the ink passes on white the earlier "red-on-white" tension on the inverse white-fill destructive button (#1361) dissolves for free.

**Scope — DESTRUCTIVE ONLY.** `primary`/`neutral`/`accent` interactive text inks share the same on-darker-surface structure (gated against the primary surface only), but they are out of scope for #1352 and, for `primary`, the brand action colour is deliberately the identity even where that costs a tier — filed as a follow-up issue rather than smuggled in (principle 3). The destructive column is special precisely because a destructive control must read as destructive on every surface.

**Versioning (#1252 decision).** ENGINE and not CONTRACT: `interactive.destructive.text.{rest,hover,pressed}`, `.border.*`, and the `inverse.` twins move VALUES only — no token path is added, removed, or retyped, and the button/icon-button bindings (`color.interactive.destructive.text.*`) are untouched — so `CONTRACT_VERSION` stands at 10.0.0. No projected surface moves: `lint-component-surface`/`lint-paint` bind NAMES and PLACEMENTS, and this touches neither (verified green, not re-`--accept`ed). `regen --check` moves each corpus brand's committed `out/` destructive-ink values (in `harbor` the darker light-mode ink converges with the hc-light ink, shrinking that overlay — a legitimate consequence, not a bug), and `lint-emission-version` requires the bump. `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp.

**Mutation (docs/34).** The docs/34 finding is that on-darker-surface contrast was NOT gated: the ink's declared `against` named the *easier* primary surface, so the gate could not see the failure on the tier where it lived. The fix moves the declared `against` to the strict surface, and the `against` STRING is declared INDEPENDENTLY of the ground the value derives against (two expressions, not one — docs/34 shape 2). So reverting `dTextGround` to `baseRgb` (the light red) leaves `against` at `background.tertiary` and drops the recomputed ratio below the floor: **`lint-ratio-truth` fails BY NAME** on `interactive.destructive.text.rest` — both arm A (*"records ratio 5.62 against 'background.tertiary', but the emitted colors measure 4.08"*) and arm B (*"measures 4.08 against 'background.tertiary', below its 4.5:1 minimum, and NO warning names it"*). The inverse arm was mutation-proven identically on `inverse.interactive.destructive.text.rest` against `inverse.background.tertiary`. Both mutations run by manual edit-and-restore over a committed tree, never `git checkout --` on uncommitted work (the CLAUDE.md trap). `test.ts`'s inverse-ground assertions assert the `inverse.background.` prefix + the ratio floor rather than pinning the primary band, so a regression to a page ground still fails there by name.

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → full suite, all-PASS (0 FAIL). The per-gate table is in the PR body.

## (2026-09-08) — the focus ring adapts per mode to sit on its own ground (#1336)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.67.0 → **0.68.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — this moves token VALUES, not names (`token-contract.ts --check` confirms 577 guaranteed paths unchanged; `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp).

**The defect (owner-settled decision, implemented not re-decided), from the 2026-09-08 host-truth audit.** The default focus ring (`border.focus`) responded to the HIGH-CONTRAST modes but not to plain dark: `#007CBB` on aurora's light AND dark page alike, adapting only in HC. The inverse ring (`inverse.border.focus`) was worse — pinned to `#007CBB` in ALL FOUR modes, including on a light inverse band in dark mode where a *dark* ring is what sits on it. The owner settled it: both rings must adapt per mode to keep visible contrast against their respective grounds — the default lightening in dark mode, the inverse darkening in dark mode (the inverse band is light there).

**The diagnosis — one bar, two sites.** Both rings stopped adapting for the same reason once you see it: the contrast bar they were held to was low enough that a single brand action step satisfied it on grounds of *opposite* lightness. The default ring was `rated(actionRest, baseRgb)` — `actionRest` is gated against the mode FLOOR, not the ring's own ground, and in standard modes that floor is the 3:1 fill minimum the anchor cleared on both the light and the dark page. The inverse ring already resolved through `chromatic` against the band, but at `nonTextMin` (3:1) — the same low bar, so the anchor cleared in every mode and it froze. HC was the tell that the mechanism was sound: the default HC ring already adapts and reproduces real-NB's hand-authored HC focus exactly, precisely because HC gates the fill at the escalated `actionMin` (7:1) bar the anchor CANNOT clear on both extremes.

**The fix — raise the bar to `actionMin` and pick against the actual ground.** `focusRing(ground)` resolves the action ramp against the ground it is painted on at `actionMin`, anchored on the brand action step: `chromatic`/`pickBrand` keeps the anchor where it clears (so the light-mode page ring is UNCHANGED) and otherwise takes the nearest step that does — a lighter step on a dark ground, a darker one on a light ground. The default ring takes `focusRing` in the standard modes and keeps `actionRest` in HC (already correct, max-contrast, NB-faithful — scoping the change to exactly what was inert). The inverse ring takes `focusRing` in EVERY mode: it has no NB-authored HC value to preserve and its HC non-response was explicitly in scope. Aurora now reads default `#007CBB → #0088BE` (dark) and inverse `#007CBB → #006E99` (dark, dark-on-the-light-band), each clearing ≥4.5:1 on its real surface.

**A fidelity win falls out.** nb's standard dark default ring now lands on `red/450` — real-NB's OWN hand-authored dark focus — where the old `actionRest` derivation diverged to `red/550`. The adaptive rule REPRODUCES the lighter-in-dark ring NB shipped by hand, so the `dark border/focus` row in `test.ts`'s `NB_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` is now stale and removed (a stale waiver fails the fixture gate as loudly as a missing one). The HC rows never existed and still don't — HC default is untouched.

**Also reviewed (the audit's broader finding): 6 inverse roles equal to their default counterparts.** Two dispositions. (1) `inverse/interactive/neutral/on-fill` is INTENTIONALLY equal — it is ink chosen for the neutral interactive fill, and that fill is the same uniform neutral extreme on both grounds (#1231), so the ink is legitimately identical; not a ground-adaptation defect. (2) The five semantic borders `inverse/border/{brand,success,warning,danger,info}` all already clear the 3:1 non-text floor on the inverse band at palette step 500 (measured 4.19–4.58:1 across modes), so unlike the focus ring they are not *failing* to sit on their ground — whether they should nonetheless DIVERGE (step lighter on the dark band for more presence) is a visual-design decision, not a mechanical fix, and applying the focus ring's `actionMin` rule to a decorative 1.4.11 border would be the wrong mechanism. Per the owner's "fix the focus ring, file the rest" instruction and principle 3 (one concern per PR; file don't smuggle), these five are filed as a follow-up issue with the audit evidence rather than changed here.

**Versioning (#1252 decision).** ENGINE and not CONTRACT: `border.focus` and `inverse.border.focus` move VALUES only — no token path is added, removed, or retyped, and the `focus-ring` def's bindings (`color.border.focus`, `color.inverse.border.focus` via the `surface=inverse` rewrite, docs/20 §9.11) are untouched — so `CONTRACT_VERSION` stands at 10.0.0. No projected surface moves: `lint-component-surface` and `lint-paint`'s census hash binding NAMES and PLACEMENTS, and this touches neither (verified green, not re-`--accept`ed). `regen --check` moves each corpus brand's committed `out/` focus-ring values across the affected modes, and `lint-emission-version` requires the bump — the emission changed, so the version must.

**Mutation (docs/34).** Reverting the derivation (either ring back to its pre-#1336 pick) without regenerating re-emits the frozen values and **`regen --check` reports it BY NAME** as drift against the committed artifacts (`border.focus` / `inverse.border.focus`, every brand's `out/`). `lint-ratio-truth` recomputes every affected ratio from the FINAL emitted colours against each ring's declared `against` ground and stays green — the fix raises contrast, never lowers a floor — which is the correct behaviour for a value change: the floor-vs-ground contract IS gated (a ring dropping below `nonTextMin` on its ground would fail arm A/B by name), the per-mode ADAPTATION is not independently gated. Filing that adaptation gate was weighed and left out to avoid ballooning (owner's "do not balloon; filing is acceptable"): it belongs with the semantic-border follow-up, since a "focus ring visibly differs from its light-mode value in dark mode" assertion is the same shape of check for both. Restored, then re-`--accept`ed at the forward bump; the mutation was run by manual edit-and-restore, not `git checkout --` (the CLAUDE.md trap).

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → full suite, all-PASS (0 FAIL). The per-gate table is in the PR body.

## (2026-09-08) — every Figma TEXT component-property name is lowercase (#1333)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.66.0 → **0.67.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — a component-property name is component-API surface, not a token name (`token-contract.ts --check` confirms 577 guaranteed paths unchanged; `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp).

**The defect (owner-settled decision, implemented not re-decided).** The TEXT-property namer in `anatomy-figma.ts` uses the `figmaProperties.texts` KEY verbatim as the Figma property name. Four defs capitalized it — `button`'s `Label`, `field-label`'s `Label`, `field-message`'s `Message`, `select`'s `Value` — while every INSTANCE_SWAP and VARIANT name was already lowercase, and three defs (`checkbox`/`radio`/`switch`) already spelled their TEXT prop `label`. The owner settled #1333 on: make ALL Figma TEXT property names lowercase. So `Label`→`label`, `Message`→`message`, `Value`→`value`; already-lowercase ones untouched. This makes #1309's display-name split (decouple Figma display name from code prop) unnecessary for now — deliberately NOT built.

**Where the single source is, and why the rename touches `props` too.** The casing is not in the namer — it reads the def key verbatim. `component-schema.ts`'s `figmaPropertyErrors` validates each `texts` key against a `props[].name` (line 1314/1321: `propNames.has(prop)`), so the two are COUPLED. Lowercasing only the `texts` key would fail validation ("is not a declared prop"); decoupling them is #1309. So the correct single source is the def, and the rename lands on BOTH the `props[].name` and the `texts` key in each of the four defs — code-side prop and Figma panel name move together, both lowercase.

**Versioning (#1252 decision).** ENGINE and not CONTRACT: the property name reaches the plan (`FigmaNodePlan.propertyRef.prop` and the set-level `FigmaPropertyPlan.name`), so `planStamp` — which hashes the whole plan — moves for every def whose TEXT name was capitalized: `button` / `button-destructive` / `button-neutral` / `field-label` / `field-message` / `select`, **six surfaces at the SAME member count, different digest**, re-`--accept`ed into `schema/component-surface.json`. `checkbox`/`radio`/`switch` were already lowercase, so their digests are byte-identical and were NOT re-accepted. `lint-paint.ts`'s census is UNCHANGED and NOT re-accepted — it hashes paint binding NAMES and PLACEMENTS, and a TEXT-property rename touches neither (verified: `✓ paint is where the defs say it is`). `regen --check` moves each committed token artifact only by this file's own generator stamp (0.66.0 → 0.67.0); `lint-emission-version` is green (version moved with no emission-value change). No rename registry entry is owed: a component-property rename is neither a token-PATH move (`DEPRECATIONS`) nor a Figma-COLLECTION rename (`MATERIALIZATION_RENAMES`).

**Mutation (docs/34).** Reverting one name back to capitalized in its def — coherently (prop + `texts` key together, so the def stays valid and the projector does not throw) — moves that def's `planStamp` and fails `lint-component-surface.ts` arm A **BY NAME**, verbatim: `surface/field-message: plan digest 83eb047aa7a1…, baseline 641de7d7a6d3… — the same member COUNT, projecting different plans`, while the member count holds at 4. `test.ts`'s hand-written property-name assertions — FieldLabel `label`, FieldMessage `message`, Button `label:TEXT` — also fail by name on such a revert; they are literals compared against the projected name, never derived from the def (docs/34 shape 8). Restored, then re-`--accept`ed at the forward bump. (The mutation was run by manual edit-and-restore, not `git checkout --`, so no uncommitted work was at risk — the CLAUDE.md trap.)

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → full suite, all-PASS (0 FAIL). The per-gate table is in the PR body.

## (2026-09-08) — the inverse PRIMARY filled fill holds constant so the brand ink stops losing contrast per state (#1351 part 2)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.65.0 → **0.66.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — this moves token VALUES, not names (`token-contract.ts --check` confirms 577 guaranteed paths unchanged).

**The defect — the second real WCAG AA failure #1351 recorded, and the `filled` half part 1 deliberately left.** On `surface=inverse` the primary filled button is a near-white surface carrying a BRAND `on-fill` ink (`#006E99`-class, from #1244/#1255's auto-selected safe brand step). That ink is a single value, gated only against `fill.rest`. But the inverse fill WALKED darker per state — rest `neutral.050` (#E9E9EA) → hover `.150` (#CECED0) → pressed `.250` (#B4B4B6) — so the constant brand ink lost contrast as the ground darkened beneath it: measured over the corpus on the real inverse backdrop, **4.69 → 3.62 FAIL → 2.75 FAIL**. Destructive/neutral survived only because their `on-fill` is near-black `#0D0D0E`; this was the primary ramp alone.

**The owner's settled decision (implemented, not re-decided).** #1351 defect 2 offered two fixes and said *flag, don't pick*: (a) cap the fill darkening on inverse, or (b) step `on-fill` per state. The owner picked **(a), all the way to constant** — hold the inverse primary fill white across all six states, so the per-state feedback lives ENTIRELY in the outline/text ink (which steps, part 1 #1358) and never in the filled fill. Holding the fill removes the failure outright: the brand ink now sits on the SAME near-white ground in every state, so its rest contrast (≥4.5) holds through hover/pressed/focused/selected. No contrast handling was added, and hover/pressed stay contrast-exempt (#1281/#1282) — the fix simply stops the ground from moving out from under a fixed ink.

**Where the fix lives, and why it is the token tier and not `button.ts`.** The button's `filled.fill.{rest,hover,pressed}` bindings are SHARED across surfaces — the projector only swaps the `color.* → color.inverse.*` namespace on a `surface=inverse` coordinate, never the state — so a binding edit cannot make the fill behave differently on inverse than on the (correctly-stepping) default surface. The only place that can hold the inverse fill constant WITHOUT touching the default is the token derivation: `modes.ts`'s `invColumn` fill-state loop, guarded `holdInverseFill = name === 'primary'`, now emits `fillRest` for every `FILL_STATES` step instead of walking the neutral ramp. So the filled button binds the exact same roles as before, and those roles simply resolve to one value across states on the inverse band.

**Scope — PRIMARY ONLY, destructive/neutral untouched.** The guard is `name === 'primary'`; destructive keeps its neutral walk (050 → 150 → 250, its near-black ink survives it) and neutral is unchanged, pending their own decisions (#1253/#1254 — genuinely different questions, and #1352's destructive rest-contrast tension is still the owner's). Extra `interactivePalettes` columns keep walking too. The `outline`/`text` appearances (part 1) are not touched.

**Versioning (#1252 decision).** ENGINE and not CONTRACT: `inverse.interactive.primary.fill.{hover,pressed,focused,selected}` now alias neutral.050 (light) / .850 (dark) in place of the walked steps, across all four modes and every corpus brand — a pure VALUE move, no path added/removed/retyped, so `CONTRACT_VERSION` stands and `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp to 0.66.0. Unlike part 1 this is an EMISSION change, not a projected-surface change: no button binding moves, so `lint-component-surface` and `lint-paint`'s census are byte-identical and were NOT re-`--accept`ed (the census hashes binding NAMES, not resolved values). `regen --check` moved each brand's committed `out/` token + figma + overlay artifacts (the fill values and their recomputed ratios), and `lint-emission-version` requires the bump — the emission changed, so the version must.

**Mutation (docs/34).** Reverting the `holdInverseFill` guard so the primary inverse fill walks again re-emits the darker hover/pressed/focused/selected values, which **`regen --check` reports BY NAME** as drift against the committed artifacts (`inverse.interactive.primary.fill.*`, every brand's `out/`). `lint-ratio-truth` recomputes every affected ratio from the final colours and stays green — near-white on the dark band clears `nonTextMin` more easily held than walked — which is exactly the point: the fix cannot lower a floor. Restored, then re-`--accept`ed at the forward bump. This is the correct gate for a value-only change; the projected-surface gates (`lint-component-surface`/`lint-paint`) legitimately do not move, because no binding did.

**The #1357 blind spot still stands (filed by part 1, not closed here).** The token contract gates `on-fill` against `fill.rest` only — the rest pairing, which always passed — so no token-tier gate ever composited the constant ink over the WALKED hover/pressed fill, the rendered pairing that failed. Holding the fill constant makes fill.hover/pressed EQUAL fill.rest, so the rest gate now covers every state by construction; but the component-level gate that composites an appearance's own ink over its own per-state fill is still what would have caught this class, and it remains #1357's PR (folding it in here would be half-doing it, docs/34).

## (2026-09-08) — `field-label` dropped its `Label`/`indicator` text references on some variants: a refused property reference is now recovered, not lost (#1337)

**The symptom, off a live aurora build.** Building the `field-label` set reported, on a subset of
variants (the QA saw `tone=secondary, weight=bold`), `set_componentPropertyReferences: Could not create
a new component property reference` for BOTH `text.characters -> Label` and `indicator.characters ->
indicator`. The two text fields then had no property to override and the text disappeared from those
members. `field-label` is the corpus's only member with TWO TEXT parts, which is why it is the def that
surfaced this.

**The diagnosis, and why it is not a def defect.** The projection is provably correct: `figmaAnatomySet`
emits 24 well-formed members, `planSetProperties` derives exactly `Label:TEXT` + `indicator:TEXT`, and
every one of the 48 references wires cleanly through `applyComponentPlan` against the default #874 shim —
0 misses. Nothing in the plan is unique to the failing coordinate (both `textStyle=body/*/strong` and
`fills=color/text/secondary` are shared with other members), so the cause is not plan content; it is the
live combine.

The wire loop writes each reference on the #701 FAST-PATH handle (`builtFor.get(part)`), captured BEFORE
`combineAsVariants`. The combine can leave that handle a DETACHED pre-combine node while the live member
holds an id-rewritten twin — the exact divergence #866 (`refsRepaired`) and #1279 (`boundRepaired`) built
their READ-BACK repairs against, and which both entries recorded as UNCONFIRMED live because the default
shim keeps one node object across combine, so no handle ever detaches offline. #1337 is that divergence
confirmed, in its harsher form: a `componentPropertyReferences` write to a detached node does not merely
discard (which the read-back repairs), it THROWS — a detached node is not a component sublayer. A throw
never lands in `wiredRefs`, so the read-back repairs cannot reach it, and the reference stayed a permanent
miss. This is the "reference targeting a node that doesn't exist at that variant" shape.

**The fix — the THROW sibling of #866, in the executor.** In the wire loop's catch, re-find the live node
by name and wire the reference there before reporting a miss — exactly as the read-back re-wires on an id
divergence. On success it lands in `wiredRefs` (so the read-back re-verifies it) and `refsRepaired` counts
it. Cause-independent and inert when it cannot help: it fires only after a throw, only re-tries a node that
is NOT the one that threw, and if the live node refuses it too the ORIGINAL cause is still reported. The
projection (`field-label.ts`, `anatomy-figma.ts`) is untouched, so the emitted surface, `component-surface`
and `paint-census` are byte-identical and neither ENGINE nor CONTRACT moves. The single-shot payload path
(`PAYLOAD_WIRE_REFS`) already writes on the live `findOne` node, so it never had this failure and needs no
change — which is itself evidence the fast-path handle is the culprit.

**The gate that was missing, and the mutation that proves it (docs/34).** No offline gate caught this
class: the shims only ever threw "Could not FIND a component property" (unknown name), never modeled
Figma REFUSING a valid reference, and `test-roundtrip`/`test-write-components` were green on `field-label`
throughout. So `component-shim.ts` gains an opt-in `detachPartsOnCombine` mode that models the one host
behaviour the shim otherwise cannot reach — the combine detaching the pre-combine handles and handing the
live members fresh twins — which also makes #866/#1279's own repairs reproducible for the first time. The
new `#1337` block in `test-write-components.ts` drives `field-label` through it and asserts (a) 0 "could
not create" misses, (b) every reference still reaches every member, and (c) `refsRepaired === 48` as the
reachability floor, so the arms cannot pass vacuously on an un-detached run. Mutation-by-name: deleting the
wire-loop recovery turns all three arms red and reproduces the issue's miss lines byte-for-byte
(`... /text.characters -> Label (in set_componentPropertyReferences: Could not create a new component
property reference)`).

**Standing caveat, flagged for the owner.** The offline model reproduces the executor mechanics but not a
real Figma file; the exact live divergence is inferred from #866/#1279's lineage and the issue's miss
format, not observed here. If a real-host build shows the LIVE node ALSO refuses the reference (a
fundamental Figma limit on the two-TEXT-property structure at those coordinates rather than a stale
handle), then the residual is a `field-label` design-structure question — that is the owner's call, not a
mechanical fix, and this change still stands as correct hardening (a refused reference that CAN be placed
on the live node now is, and one that genuinely cannot is still reported rather than silently dropped).

## (2026-09-08) — `text`-appearance button ink steps with state on the inverse band (#1351 part 1)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.64.0 → **0.65.0**. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — the fix binds token names that already ship, so no guaranteed path moves (`token-contract.ts --check` confirms 577 unchanged).

**The defect — a real WCAG AA failure, decision-free.** On `surface=inverse`, the `text` appearance held its label/icon ink at `interactive.<family>.text.rest` across all six states while the translucent-white overlay wash lightened the ground beneath it, so the composited contrast collapsed. `outline` already did this correctly (#1282 made its ink step `text.rest → hover → pressed`); `text` was the half that treatment left behind. The prior code comment argued `text` needed no per-state ink because — unlike `outline` — it draws no border for the ink to fall out of step with, and that reasoning missed the ground the ink actually sits on: the overlay is a lightening layer, and a pinned ink over a lightening ground loses contrast whether or not a border is present.

**Measured over the emitted corpus, composited over each band's own per-state overlay** (`composite(inverse.background.primary, overlay, alpha)`, then `contrast(ink, composite)`): the shipped rest-ink fell to **2.62:1** at worst (`minimal` light `text` pressed — the issue's `#0D0D0E`-backdrop case reproduced), failing across every non-HC brand for both `button` and `button-destructive` at hover and pressed. The per-state ink recovers it to **5.07:1** at worst — matching the issue's ">5:1" claim for `outline`, whose identical treatment proves it.

**The fix.** `button.ts`'s `intentTokens` gains four keys — `text.{label,icon}.{hover,pressed}` → `color.interactive.<family>.text.{hover,pressed}` — mirroring the `outline` block already above it. The roles are the same ones `iText` has emitted since #576 and `outline` already binds, so nothing is added to the token tier; the projector's `color.* → color.inverse.*` rewrite gives the inverse band its own stepped ink, which is where the failure lived. Neutral is `walkable: false`, so its states collapse onto rest and a neutral text button is byte-identical. **The three button components share the fix through the factory**, so `test.ts`'s "differ only in the `interactive.<family>` bindings" invariant is preserved.

**Strict scope — part 2 NOT touched.** #1351 part 2 (the `filled` inverse-PRIMARY `on-fill` holding constant while the fill darkens: 4.69 → 3.62 → 2.75) carries a design choice the owner is still making (cap the fill darkening, or step `on-fill` per state) and is deliberately left alone. No `filled` binding moved.

**Versioning (#1252 decision).** No committed `out/` VALUE moves — component payloads are not committed under `out/`, and the fix binds existing tokens — so `regen --check` moved only each artifact's generator stamp (0.64.0 → 0.65.0, 8 files × 1 line). The bump is demanded from the projected-surface side: the three button components' `text`-appearance hover/pressed members now paint a stepped ink at the SAME 432 member count, so `lint-component-surface.ts` and `lint-paint.ts`'s census were re-`--accept`ed (authored baselines, never regen). `CONTRACT_VERSION` stands — a component binding is a reference to a token name, never a token name — and `token-contract.ts --accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp.

**Mutation (docs/34).** Reverting any of the four new keys back to `.text.rest` moves the affected button components' `planStamp` and fails `lint-component-surface.ts` arm A **BY NAME** at the same member count (*"surface/button: plan digest … — the same member COUNT, projecting different plans"*, all three defs) and moves `lint-paint.ts`'s census hash. Restored, then re-`--accept`ed at the forward bump.

**The gate blind spot that let this ship is FILED, not closed here (#1357).** The token contrast contract gates `inverse.interactive.<c>.text.rest` against the RAW `inverse.background.primary` (≈4.87, passes) and gates the overlay wash's legibility for `inverse.text.primary` (the strong page ink, passes) — NEITHER composites the outline/text appearance's own per-state ink over its own per-state overlay, the rendered pairing that failed. The overlay's `legibleFor` cannot simply be repointed at the interactive family's text ink, because the same wash is reused for neutral row/menu/card hover where the ink genuinely is `text.primary` (docs/20 §6). A gate that catches THIS class must be COMPONENT-level: it must resolve which ink the appearance binds per coordinate, apply the projector's inverse rewrite, pair it with the overlay on the same coordinate, composite, and assert AA — a token-tier check cannot see that the button bound `text.rest`. `lint-paint.ts` arm 4 already demonstrates the whole pipeline (plan a def → read painted variables per coordinate → resolve values per mode → contrast), so #1357 is tractable as its own mutation-proven arm; folding a new cross-tier contrast gate into this focused, decision-free WCAG fix would be half-doing it (docs/34), so it gets its own PR. This is the one thing worth carrying forward: **the fix is real and verified, but the reason the failure shipped undetected is still open in #1357.**

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → full suite, all-PASS (0 FAIL, 0 SKIP). The per-gate table is in the PR body.

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.63.0 → **0.64.0** (0.61/0.62/0.63 spent by select / image-placeholder / icon-count building alongside; forward-only, next free integer above main). **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — no token name moved; a component-property name and an anatomy part-key name are component-API surface, which `docs/30` keeps outside the guaranteed token-NAME surface.

**What, and why it is decision-free.** Every change is either mechanical or was DECIDED by the owner in #1326 (the 2026-09-07 component-consistency audit, verdict "one coherent system"). Two groups.

**Group A — `select` was the one def out of step with its siblings.** (1) A STALE `text`-part `//` comment described a `label.filled` binding at a `filled` state the def never had; the `tokens` block re-points the value ink at the `empty` state (`label` bare = the full-contrast value, `label.empty` = the muted placeholder) and the part's own `note` already said so. Reconciled the comment to the `empty`-model reality. (2) The root part key `root` → `container`. Every other def names its root part semantically (button/icon-button `container`; checkbox/radio/switch `row`; field-label `label`; focus-ring `ring`; icon `glyph`; image-placeholder `frame`; veil `wash`); `select` alone carried the bare `root`. `container` is the existing key that fits a column stack — not `row`, which would misdescribe a column — following button/icon-button rather than inventing a name. (3) `composition.supersededBy: []` added, for shape parity with the current defs that pair `supersedes` with an explicit `supersededBy` (checkbox / checkbox-control / image-placeholder / veil). None of the three encoded a design choice — each is a mechanical alignment to the prevailing convention derived by inspecting all of `components/*.ts`.

**Group B — the boolean-prop naming canon (#1326 decision 2).** DOM-backed booleans are BARE, synthetic-state booleans are `is`-prefixed. Exactly the concrete renames the decision names, no others: `switch` `isReadOnly` → `readOnly` and `pending` → `isPending`; `button` / `icon-button` / `field-label` `isDisabled` → `disabled` (their `isPending` / `isInactive` stay `is`-prefixed — synthetic). Prose references to each renamed prop within its own def were updated with it (a `disabled` prop with prose still saying `isDisabled` is the same stale-reference class as A1). The switch header's `pending` references are the STATE, which is not renamed, so they stand.

**Only `select`'s Figma surface moved, and only from the part-key rename.** The part key reaches the plan as a node name, so `root` → `container` moved `select`'s `planStamp` digest (same 40 members, different digest) and its paint-census node paths — `lint-component-surface.json` and `paint-census.json` both re-`--accept`ed, authored baselines never regen. The boolean-prop renames are code-side React prop names that `figmaAnatomySet` does not project (`lint-component-surface`'s stated limit 3), and both switch booleans map to `codeOnly` states rather than the projected state axis — so Group B moves NO Figma surface, which both surface gates confirm (only `select` drifted). The A1 comment fix edits a `//` comment, not a plan field, so it moves nothing.

**No rename registry entry is owed.** `DEPRECATIONS` is token-PATH only; `MATERIALIZATION_RENAMES` is Figma-COLLECTION only. A component-property rename is neither, and both gates pass with 0 claims — so nothing is registered (the task's "let the gates dictate" rule, and they demanded nothing).

**Versioning.** `token-contract.ts --check` confirms 10.0.0 stands (577 guaranteed paths byte-identical); `--accept` refreshed only the baseline's informational `engineVersion` stamp 0.63.0 → 0.64.0 — the one-line refresh every ENGINE bump requires, and the reason `token-contract --check` flips to a fail on any bump until it is run. `lint-emission-version` is green (the version moved with no emission change — component payloads are not committed under `out/`). `regen` restamped only each `out/` artifact's generator version.

Reverting `select`'s root part key `container` → `root` in the def made `lint-component-surface.ts` arm A **fail BY NAME**: `surface/select: plan digest …, baseline … — the same member COUNT, projecting different plans` (member count held at 40, so the count arm stayed silent and the digest arm carried it — the intended assertion). `lint-paint`'s `census/select.set` and `census/select.grid` failed the same way. ## (2026-09-07) — stale icon-count prose corrected and gated: `version.ts`'s "set of 39 members" claim, and a `lint-icon-count.ts` drift gate (#1293)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.60.0 → **0.63.0** (0.61/0.62 spent by the select + image-placeholder components building alongside; orchestrator re-stamps at merge). **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — no token name moved.

It is load-bearing where it sits — the justification a reader consults for PR-C's `COMPONENT_SET` diagnosis row — and nothing gated a changelog line against the def, so a one-line grep disproved it. **The true count is derived, never restated.** `ICON_NAMES.length` in `icon-glyphs.ts` (generated from `icons/*.svg` through `icon-set.ts`) = **43**. Per #1290/#1110's lesson, the fixes name that source rather than bake a numeral: the 0.49.0 entry now names `emitAsComponents` + the standalone shape + the surviving reason for the `COMPONENT_SET` row (a designer's own icon library is very often a set — the reason #1292's test states in code), with no number; `icon.ts`'s `codeOnly` "verified across all 40 sources" → "across every source in the set"; `test.ts`'s two glyph-shape messages drop their fragile "39 glyphs"/"20 curved" corpus counts.

**The drift gate — `lint-icon-count.ts` (docs/34).** Scans the icon def's shipping metadata prose (`description`, prop descriptions, part notes, `codeOnly` entries — pulled by explicit path off the imported `icon` def, a DECLARED scope) and fails if any integer bound to a glyph-set noun disagrees with `ICON_NAMES.length`. EXPECTED is derived from the set, never a second hardcoded numeral — the #1110 trap the task named. It caught a REAL drift on the tree it landed on: `icon.ts`'s "40 sources", stale since #1316 grew the set to 43. **Scope is the icon def only**: the changelog genre (`version.ts`, `docs/00-progress.md`) is append-only history that legitimately records the count of its moment — the same reason `lint-layout-claims.ts` exempts this log — and so is a dated attributed fact in another def (`field-message.ts`'s "#920 landed 39 glyphs"), which a whole-corpus scan would false-flag. **Why this bumps ENGINE with no `out/` value change.** `icon.ts`'s `codeOnly` is part of the projected component plan, and `planStamp` hashes the whole plan — so editing that one prose string moved the icon SURFACE digest (`lint-component-surface`), the #1252 case, even though `regen --check` is byte-identical and `lint-emission-version` reports nothing (the veil entry below hit the same `planStamp`-hashes-`codeOnly` trap). Baselines re-`--accept`ed, both authored never regen: `component-surface.json` (icon 43 members, digest moved, version → 0.63.0) and `token-contract.json` (informational `engineVersion` stamp → 0.63.0, "no surface change", contract 10.0.0 — every ENGINE bump requires this refresh). `regen` restamped the 8 top-level tokens files' generator version and nothing else.

**Two deliberate scope calls, flagged rather than smuggled.** (1) `version.ts` is repaired in place (the load-bearing, ungated reference the issue names) — both the 0.49.0 claim and the 0.50.0 note that quoted it, reconciled together so the internal reference stays coherent. `docs/00-progress.md`'s own historical PR-C entry (and the two later entries that quote its wording, at the #1288 and #1280-PR-D entries) are left as **append-only history**: a later entry there already recorded the correction, and editing the PR-C entry would falsify the later one that quotes "set of 39 members" by content. The record is completed by this entry, not by rewriting the old one. ## (2026-09-07) — an aspect-ratio LOCK + a clipsContent opt-in, and the `image-placeholder` component that uses them (#1316)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump → **0.62.0** — `select` (the entry below) merged to main at 0.61.0 while this was in review, so this takes 0.62.0, the next free integer above main; merged `origin/main` in and kept both changelog entries, both defs in `componentDefs`, and CONTRACT at 10.0.0. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — the def binds only existing roles.

**What.** Two engine capabilities plus the component that consumes them. (1) An aspect-ratio LOCK: a `box` can declare `aspectRatio: '<axis>'`, and each member's frame is locked to the proportion its own `ratio` coordinate names, deriving one dimension from the other. (2) A `clipsContent` opt-in on the box (default false, unchanged for every existing component). (3) `image-placeholder` (`packages/engine/components/image-placeholder.ts`, registered in `components/index.ts`) — an empty-state media frame: a neutral fill, a centered `image` glyph as the "no image" marker, `clipsContent: true`, and a `ratio` axis of `1:1 | 4:3 | 16:9` driving the lock.

**Option A held — the lock is a component-STRUCTURE property, not a token.** The owner-approved approach (Option A, 2026-09-07) is an aspect-ratio LOCK, not two dimension bindings. The engine has always STRIPPED the lock because it bound two dimensions (the second `setBoundVariable` evicts the first — the `unlockAspectRatio` sites). A ratio-locked box binds ONE nominal dimension (`width` → `container.narrow`, the veil idiom) and lets `lockAspectRatio()` derive the other. Because the ratio is structure and not a token, ecosystem impact is nil — no DTCG, no TokenPress, and `CONTRACT_VERSION` stays 10.0.0 (verified: `token-contract.ts --check` reports the guaranteed set byte-identical, and `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp to 0.62.0).

**How it is expressed — the axis VALUE is the ratio.** `aspectRatio` on the box names a variant axis (`'ratio'`); the projector parses that member's value (`16:9` → 16/9) with `parseRatio` and carries the number onto `FigmaNodePlan.aspectRatio`. No per-variant literal map that could drift from the axis it mirrors. Both executors (payload in `anatomy-figma.ts`, port in `write-components.ts`) resize the frame to the proportion, `lockAspectRatio()`, then bind the single dimension — ordered so the lock is captured from the resized box and there is no second binding for it to evict. `parseRatio` lives in `component-schema.ts` (one parser, read by the validator and the projector); the read-back gate authors its OWN contract so its expectation stays independent (docs/34).

**`ratio` reopens the closed `VARIANT_AXES` list — the fifteenth name, owner-decided, mechanical fallout.** A width-to-height PROPORTION no existing name expresses; distinct from `size` (a scale rung) and `width` (a single main-axis length). Argued in the `VARIANT_AXES` header; carried in `lint-axis-values.ts` as a `sole` set. `anatomyErrors` refuses a `ratio` value that is not a positive `W:H` (the lock would capture NaN) — the one thing this axis's values are checked for beyond the register. **Flagging this** as the structurally-notable consequence, the same shape veil's `value`/`intensity` had: honouring the owner's axis name reopened a deliberately-closed vocabulary.

**THE PASTE-TIME-DERIVE RISK — resolved to A, not fallen back to C.** The brief asked to PROVE that binding a variable on the SINGLE axis of a LOCKED node makes Figma derive the other, or fall back to Option C. This cannot be proven offline: Figma documents the derive on RESIZE (and `targetAspectRatio` is read-only), and a variable binding IS a resize, but that a `setBoundVariable` triggers the derive at paste time is a LIVE-file fact no offline host can witness — the same accept-and-discard class the round-trip gate names as real-Figma-only. **Nothing falsified A**, so there was no fallback: what the offline gates prove is that the lock is captured with the RIGHT ratio (read back as `targetAspectRatio`), and Figma's documented lock contract supplies the derive. The derive-on-paste itself is filed for the real-host arm (`tools/component-roundtrip/`, not in CI) and recorded in the def's `codeOnly`/`notes.unverified`. **If a pasted placeholder is ever found NOT deriving its height, the fallback is Option C** (a nominal square + the ratio in code/AI metadata only, the veil "layout fact Figma can't hold" posture).

**The read-back gate (docs/34), and where it lives.** Per the verify checklist, the aspect-lock read-back lives in `test:roundtrip`. `anatomy-readback.ts` classifies the two new plan fields — `aspectRatio` (built `targetAspectRatio` vs the PLAN's ratio) and `clipsContent` — so the corpus round-trip covers both per member (plan-as-oracle). On top of that, `test-roundtrip.ts` carries an INDEPENDENT block: it builds `image-placeholder` through the shared shim and checks each member's built frame against an owner-decided ratio CONTRACT authored in the gate (`{1:1→1, 4:3→4/3, 16:9→16/9}`), so a ratio flipped/added/dropped in the def fails BY NAME — which plan-as-oracle cannot catch, because a coherent def flip moves the plan too. The shim (`component-shim.ts`) and the `test.ts` payload stub both model `lockAspectRatio()`/`targetAspectRatio`, capturing from the live width/height a resize just set — never from a plan input, so the read-back is an independent witness. `test.ts`'s payload resize assertion was re-pointed from "node is never resized" to "node is never resized AFTER its bind loop" (resize-then-bind is safe; the aspect-lock resize runs before it), the same widening the absolute-part kind forced once before.

**Neutral roles (chosen + why).** `fill` → `color.background.secondary` (a neutral surface one step off the page, so the empty frame reads as filled rather than a hole; a designer wanting a more recessed well rebinds to `background.tertiary`). `icon` → `color.icon.tertiary` (the most muted ink, for a de-emphasized "no image" marker). Both existing semantic roles → no new token. The glyph is decorative (aria-hidden), so `icon.tertiary` is not held to a text-contrast floor.

**clipsContent — threaded, not hardcoded.** `FigmaNodePlan.clipsContent` (carried only when true, so every existing box's plan is byte-identical) is threaded to the sites both executors hardcoded to `false`: `anatomy-figma.ts`'s payload frame branch, `write-components.ts`'s box branch and its `claimDefaults` pass. `lint-unclaimed-defaults` already carries a `clipsContent` row (a #865 visually-significant property); the thread keeps it satisfied — the executor still WRITES the value, now from the plan.

**DEFERRED (#1316 residue, owner-held).** The optional scrim/veil overlay (a wash for text over the image) and the play-circle video overlay both nest other components (`veil`, the `play-circle` glyph) and are NOT built here — this PR is the core empty-state aspect-locked frame. Named in the def's `codeOnly` and `notes.unverified`. The raster swap itself is a native Figma action (an image fill), not a modeled slot.

**Mutation tests (docs/34; a `wip:` commit preceded each so the `git checkout --` restore reached HEAD, per the CLAUDE.md pathspec trap):**
- **(a) — flip a ratio in the def.** Changing `image-placeholder`'s `variants.ratio` `16:9` → `2:1` made `test-roundtrip.ts`'s aspect-lock block **fail by name** (`member ratio=2:1 is not an owner-decided ratio`), and `lint-axis-values` fail (the register set no longer matches). The generic plan-vs-built round-trip did NOT catch it (the plan followed the def) — which is exactly why the independent contract block exists. Restored.
- **(b) — break the clipsContent thread.** Reverting `write-components.ts`'s `claimDefaults` `set('clipsContent', n?.clipsContent ?? false)` to a hardcoded `false` made the round-trip `clipsContent` check **fail by name** on `image-placeholder`'s frame (plan says true, host reads false). Restored.
- **(c) — mutate a fill binding.** Pointing `image-placeholder`'s `fill` at a wrong role moved the paint census (`lint-paint.ts` arm 2) **by name**; `test.ts`'s binding-resolution arms also fail. Restored.

**Baselines re-`--accept`ed (all authored, never regen):** `paint-census.json` (image-placeholder grid 3 coords / 6 assignments, set 3 members / 6), `component-surface.json` (image-placeholder no-set → 3 members, at ENGINE 0.62.0), `token-contract.json` (engineVersion stamp → 0.62.0, contract 10.0.0 "no surface change"). Registers touched: `VARIANT_AXES` (+`ratio`), `lint-axis-values` (`ratio` sole set), `lint-standalone-floor` `MUST_PROJECT` (+`image-placeholder`), `lint-rung-names` `NO_SIZE_AXIS` (+`image-placeholder`), `lint-glyph-geometry` `FIXED_GLYPH` (+`image-placeholder.marker`).

**One trap for the next reader — a ratio box's `width` is NOT a #990 track.** `test.ts`'s #990 `width` arms assume `width` means a 2:1 track that binds BOTH axes to different variables. A ratio box binds `width` alone (the lock derives height), so it is excluded from that cohort by `!p.aspectRatio`; adding a ratio box without that exclusion asks it for a height it deliberately omits and builds with a `state: 'rest'` it does not declare.

**Verify:** engine `npm run verify` gates all pass (see the CLAUDE.md §4 list); web + plugin (typecheck/test/build/test:verdict/test:start/test:roundtrip + `lint-unclaimed-defaults`) + tokenpress + exporter + tokens, with `lint-us-english`/`lint-voice` LAST (their scope includes the built `apps/plugin/dist` bundle, which carries the `image-placeholder` `description`/`note`/`aria`/`codeOnly` prose).

## (2026-09-07) — `select` is a COMPONENT: the composed, native-first field, first def to NEST the two shared field parts (#761 mechanism resolved)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.60.0 → 0.61.0. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — no new token.

**What.** A new component `select` (`packages/engine/components/select.ts`, registered in `components/index.ts`). It is ONE unified component (owner-decided Option A) — NOT a checkbox-style decomposition: a `box` column holding a nested `field-label`, a bordered control box, and a nested `field-message`. The control box carries the fill, the stateful border, radius, a fixed single-line height, an optional leading-glyph swap slot, the value/placeholder text, and a trailing `chevron-down` vector; an absolute `focus-ring` rings it. Native-first: it models the CLOSED control only — the open menu is the platform's (native `<select>` popup, or a separate listbox), so there is no `expanded` state and no option-list anatomy. tone(4) × state(5) × leading(2) = **40 members**.

**FIRST def to NEST the shared field parts.** `text-field` names `field-label`/`field-message` only in `composition`; `select` actually nests them as in-flow `kind: 'nest'` instances (#1226's mechanism, whose first real consumer was `checkbox`→`checkbox-control`). `nest-exposed` is refused in this engine (#761), so both are `nest-fixed`. `lint-nesting` edges go 8 → 11 (select nests field-label, field-message and focus-ring).

**The validation axis is spelled `tone`, aligned to field-message's own `tone` — the point of the whole shape.** `follow` passes an axis through a `nest-fixed` BY NAME (`component-schema.ts` `NestingRelation`), so to drive the nested message's tone from select's validation, select's driving axis MUST be named `tone` and carry field-message's exact values `[default, error, warning, success]`. The `message` nest declares `nesting: { kind: 'nest-fixed', variant: { tone: 'default' }, follow: ['tone'] }` — a same-name, same-value passthrough (a `tone=error` select nests the `tone=error` message), not a value mapping. The consumer prop / UI still reads "Validation"; only the Figma variant axis is `tone`. `lint-axis-values`'s overlapping `tone` entry gains `select` and records that the alignment is BY DESIGN. The `field-label` nest is fixed (small / secondary / regular / rest) with NO follow — its size/tone/weight/state vocabulary is not select's, so there is nothing to pass through; its four projected axes are all named in the coordinate because `nestVariantMatch` requires the coordinate to account for every axis the member name carries (verified: all three nest coordinates resolve to exactly one real member of each nested set).

**Validation → border follows text-field EXACTLY: error is a border-ONLY swap, warning/success are message-only.** `error` swaps the control border to `color.border.danger`; `warning`/`success` leave the border neutral and let the nested message carry the tone; `default` is neutral. No `border.warning`/`border.success` roles are invented — the tier does not emit them and text-field deliberately does not color the border for those tones. The neutral progression is state-driven (`border.hover` → `field.border.hover`, `border.focus-visible` → `border.focus`, bare `border` → `field.border.rest`); the error swap is tone-driven and PERSISTS through hover and focus (the focus ring, a separate part, carries the focus signal on top), so `disabled` > `error` > the interactive states.

**The paint-grammar trap worth flagging — two 2-placeholder templates cannot coexist.** `paintKeyErrors` checks every 2-segment key against BOTH 2-placeholder templates, so a state-led `label.empty` fails the `{tone}.{slot}` reading and a tone-led `error.border` fails the `{slot}.{state}` reading. The fix was to make the tone template 3-SEGMENT (`{tone}.{slot}.{state}`), keeping the two vocabularies at different lengths — so `error` binds its danger border once per non-disabled state (`error.border.{rest,hover,focus-visible,empty}` → `color.border.danger`, four keys), which is also what makes the swap persist. Each is a `lint-paint` provenance exception (tone `error` → the `danger` role — the same mapping `field-message|error.*` already carries). The placeholder-vs-value ink uses the existing `empty` state (bare `label` → `text.primary` the value, `label.empty` → `field.placeholder`), text-field's exact polarity — `filled` is NOT in the engine's closed `states` vocabulary, so reusing `empty` avoids a new mechanism.

**Roles reused, no new token, no contract bump.** Every binding is an existing semantic role (`field.border.*`, `border.focus`, `border.danger`, `field.fill`, `field.placeholder`, `text.primary`, `icon.secondary`, `focus.ring.*`, cross-cutting `disabled.*`). A component binding is a reference, so no guaranteed path moves: `token-contract.ts --check` reports 577 → 577 and stays at 10.0.0; `--accept` refreshed only the informational `engineVersion` stamp to 0.61.0. `border-width.hairline` (1px, the field/button edge weight) not `border-width.thick` (2px, the selection-control weight) — a select is a field. Focus ring uses the FIELD offset (0) because an input's own border supplies the separation.

**Mutation tests (docs/34; a `wip:` commit preceded each so the `git checkout --` restore reached HEAD, per the CLAUDE.md pathspec trap):**
- **(a) — break a nest-fixed relation on the nested field-message.** Repointing the `message` nest's `nests` from `field-message` to `field-messag` made `lint-nesting.ts` **fail BY NAME**: `nest-resolves: select.message nests 'field-messag', which is not a component in componentDefs … a designer building select would find its nested target never appears`. Restored.
- **(b) — mutate a border binding.** Repointing `error.border.rest` from `color.border.danger` to `color.field.border.rest` (a neutral border that resolves) made `lint-paint.ts` arm 2 (census) **fail BY NAME** — `census/select.grid … paint hash …, the same count of assignments pointing somewhere else` and `census/select.set …` — since the danger boundary silently became neutral. Restored.

**Baselines re-`--accept`ed (all authored, never regen):** `paint-census.json` (select grid + set), `component-surface.json` (select no-set → 40 members), `token-contract.json` (engineVersion stamp → 0.61.0, contract 10.0.0 "no surface change"). `lint-standalone-floor`'s `MUST_PROJECT` gains `select` (its root is a column with children — a real extent).

**Verify:** `npm run verify` + web/plugin/tokenpress/exporter/tokens per CLAUDE.md principle 4; `lint-us-english`/`lint-voice` last (their scope includes the built `apps/plugin/dist` bundle, which carries select's `description`/`note`/`aria`/`avoidWhen`/`codeOnly` prose).

## (2026-09-07) — the media veil is a COMPONENT: `veil` binds the six existing `veil.*` roles into a standalone full-bleed overlay (#1030)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.59.0 → 0.60.0. **CONTRACT stands at 10.0.0** — no new token.

**What.** A new standalone component `veil` (`packages/engine/components/veil.ts`, registered in `components/index.ts`). It is the designer-selectable wash placed over a photograph so text on top stays legible — NOT the modal backdrop, which stays `scrim.default`, referenced directly by dialogs and out of scope. A `box` root, full-bleed, one `fill` paint slot, two variant axes `value` (dark | light) × `intensity` (subtle | medium | strong) = 6 members. The fill for each (value, intensity) coordinate binds the matching semantic role: `veil.dark.subtle` … `veil.light.strong`.

**Binds EXISTING roles — no new token, no contract bump (the load-bearing decision).** The six `veil.*` roles already ship (renamed by #1317, the entry below). A component binding is a *reference* to a token name, never a token name, so no guaranteed path moves: `token-contract.ts --check` reports the guaranteed set byte-identical (577 → 577) and stays at **10.0.0**; `--accept` refreshed only the baseline's informational `engineVersion` stamp to 0.60.0 (the same refresh #1012/0.47.0 and 0.57.0 describe), contract unchanged. A prior build tried to bind the raw alpha **primitives** (`black-alpha.*`/`white-alpha.*`) and hit the semantic-layer wall; binding the semantic `veil.*` roles is the accepted path — the shape `button` uses to bind `color.field.*`. Verified explicitly.

**Two axis names reopen the closed `VARIANT_AXES` list — owner-decided names, mechanical fallout.** `value` and `intensity` are not in the list #756 deliberately closed (only #1248 had reopened it, once, for `weight`). The names are the owner's decision (a component's variant API is a design call); reopening the list to honour them is the mechanical consequence, and each is held to that list's own bar — a distinct kind of distinction no existing name expresses. `intensity` is a wash's MAGNITUDE (nearest `weight`/`appearance`, and neither); `value` is a dark-vs-light lightness polarity in the colour-theory sense (nearest `tone`/`surface`, and neither). Both are argued in the `VARIANT_AXES` header and carried in `lint-axis-values.ts` as `sole` sets. **Flagging this** as the one structurally notable consequence: honouring the brief's axis names required reopening a deliberately-closed vocabulary twice in one change.

**Axis VALUES are lower-case (`dark`/`light`), and that is enforced not stylistic.** `lint-paint.ts` arm 1 checks a paint key's lead segment against the veil role it binds, and the roles are `veil.dark.*`/`veil.light.*`. Lower-case values (matching the corpus convention — `unchecked`, `off`, `regular`) are what let arm 1 cover every veil fill **with no exemption**; capitalized `Dark`/`Light` would have needed six `PROVENANCE_EXCEPTIONS` entries — fixing a false positive by narrowing a scan, which the repo forbids. A UI may still label the value "Dark".

**Gradient washes DEFERRED (#1318, owner-held).** Prism 2's veil carries `Gradient from top/bottom/left/right` variants beside the solid washes. Not built here: the engine has no gradient-paint capability — a paint slot resolves to one flat colour variable — so a gradient axis would bind no paint. Documented in the def's `anatomy.codeOnly` and `notes.unverified`, and filed as #1318. Only the three solid intensities per polarity ship.

**Shape: a normal standalone build — neither `notStandalone` nor `emitAsComponents`.** A veil is full-bleed and has no intrinsic size, but a standalone Figma component has no parent to fill, and a fill-sized root acquires no extent (`lint-standalone-floor.ts`, #869's white-box defect). So the root binds a NOMINAL square side — `size: 'nominal-side'` → `container.narrow` (720px, a semantic role, so it does not trip `test.ts`'s primitive-leak warning) — exactly `focus-ring`'s #1280 idiom: present only so the library artifact is a wash-shaped rectangle a designer resizes over their image. Real full-bleed geometry is a code/layout concern, admitted in `codeOnly`. `lint-standalone-floor.ts`'s `MUST_PROJECT` gains `veil`; `lint-rung-names.ts`'s `NO_SIZE_AXIS` admits it (no size rung to compare).

**Mutation test (docs/34; a `wip:` commit preceded the mutation so the `git checkout --` restore reached HEAD, per the CLAUDE.md pathspec trap).** Pointing `veil`'s `dark.strong` fill at `color.veil.light.strong` — a wrong polarity that resolves — made `lint-paint.ts` arm 1 **fail BY NAME**: `provenance: veil|dark.strong — value='dark' is absent from 'color.veil.light.strong' — a dark coordinate would paint another value's colour`. Restored. (A wrong-RUNG mutation within the same polarity, `dark.strong` → `color.veil.dark.subtle`, resolves and satisfies provenance but moves the paint hash, caught by the census arm 2 — the two arms cover different mutations.)

**Baselines re-`--accept`ed (all authored, never regen):** `paint-census.json` (veil grid 6 coords / 6 assignments, set 6 members), `component-surface.json` (veil no-set → 6 members; re-accepted a second time after the `codeOnly` prose was finalized, since `planStamp` hashes `codeOnly`), `token-contract.json` (engineVersion stamp → 0.60.0, contract 10.0.0 "no surface change").

**One trap for the next reader — `planStamp` hashes `codeOnly`.** The component-surface baseline moved a second time purely because a `codeOnly` string changed (a colour→color spelling fix, and a `node:`-substring fix in a comment that the plugin build's builtin scanner flags). `planStamp` hashes the whole plan including `codeOnly`, so editing that prose after `--accept` drifts the surface baseline — re-accept after the prose is final, not before. (The `node:` one is worth knowing: a code comment reading "one node: a rectangle" tripped `plugin-no-node-builtins` because the scanner greps for the `node:` substring; reworded to "one box".)

**Verify:** `npm run verify` → 53 PASS · 0 FAIL · 2 SKIP (the `drift`/`drift-coverage` pair, skipped only because `out/` carries uncommitted version-stamp changes locally — `regen --check` passes directly, 108 artifacts byte-match, and CI runs it against the committed tree). Covers engine gates + web + plugin + tokenpress + exporter + tokens, with `lint-us-english`/`lint-voice` last (their scope includes the built `apps/plugin/dist` bundle, which carries the veil `description`/`note`/`aria`/`codeOnly` prose).

## (2026-09-07) — the media veil's rungs rename from WCAG-floor names to intensity: `large`/`body`/`enhanced` → `subtle`/`medium`/`strong` (#1317)

**STATUS: PR open, do NOT merge (orchestrator verifies + merges).** ENGINE bump 0.58.0 → 0.59.0, CONTRACT bump 9.4.0 → **10.0.0 (MAJOR)**.

**The decision (owner-settled).** The three veil rungs were named for the WCAG contrast floor each clears — `large` (3:1) / `body` (4.5:1) / `enhanced` (7:1). The owner found this over-claims: a real photo's combined contrast under the wash depends on the specific image, so a name like `body` implies a per-image "clears 4.5:1" guarantee the engine cannot keep — the floor is measured against the **worst pixel of an unknown image**, not the designer's actual photo. Renamed to **intensity** — `subtle` (weakest wash) / `medium` / `strong` (darkest) — which claims only magnitude the designer can see, leaving the contrast judgment with them. Order preserved (weakest→darkest): `large`→`subtle`, `body`→`medium`, `enhanced`→`strong`, both polarities.

**Values are unchanged — proven, not asserted.** `VEIL_RUNGS` keeps the three WCAG floors as the **default-picker** (each rung still derives to the least emitted alpha step clearing its floor), so only the names move. `regen --check` byte-matches; the emitted veil alphas are identical before and after — aurora dark `subtle`/`medium`/`strong` = black-alpha `50`/`60`/`70` (was `large`/`body`/`enhanced` = `50`/`60`/`70`), light = white-alpha `40`/`50`/`60`. The only value-carrying bytes that moved under `out/**` are the veil path segments themselves plus each tree's generator stamp. **Do NOT switch to raw fixed opacities** — the derivation is retained as the picker.

**CONTRACT bump class — the tooling decided it, not the task.** The task said "let `--check` tell you the class." It reported **MAJOR** (six guaranteed paths removed, six added), so 9.4.0 → 10.0.0; `token-contract.ts --accept` refuses unless `CONTRACT_VERSION` is already raised by exactly that, which it was. The six removals ship `DEPRECATIONS` entries pointing at their intensity twins, so a consumer/codemod can follow the rename. Guaranteed count unchanged (577 → 577 — a rename, not a net add/remove).

**Registry: `DEPRECATIONS` in `version.ts`, NOT `MATERIALIZATION_RENAMES` — a deliberate deviation from the task's file list.** The task named `materialization-renames.ts` as the registry to add the six mappings to. Reading that file's header (as it instructed) shows why that would be wrong: a MATERIALIZATION rename is one the contract *cannot* see (Figma namespace/tier/collection/spelling). A veil rung rename **is** contract-visible — it moves a guaranteed token PATH — so it belongs in `DEPRECATIONS`, and the Figma variable rename derives from it automatically via `rename-map.ts`'s `projectionsOf` (a rung rename moves the ROLE `veil/dark/body`→`veil/dark/medium`, which projects to a real variable rename). Adding a materialization rule too would put **two** records in front of one Figma operation — exactly the `multiplyClaimed` refusal `lint-materialization-renames.ts` exists to raise. Confirmed empirically: `lint-materialization-renames` passes with **0 materialization rules** for the veil rename (18 keys removed/added, all claimed by the 18 contract records `deriveVariableRenames()` produced from `DEPRECATIONS`). The gate's own remedy line names `version.ts`/`DEPRECATIONS` as the fix, not a rule.

**The `DEPRECATIONS` follow-forward, the trap worth flagging.** #1148's six value-tier veil entries (`color.appearance.veil.<pol>.<old>` → `color.veil.<pol>.<old>`, since 9.0.0) pointed `replacedBy` at names this change retires. `classify` would flag those as dangling. Per the file's own "renamed out from under them" rule (the 3.0.0 border entries do the same), `path` stays history and `replacedBy` follows the LIVE name — so those six now point at the intensity twins. They were broken out of the shared-leaf `flatMap` loop because path-leaf (old rung) and replacement-leaf (new rung) now differ. Both the 9.0.0 (tiered) and 10.0.0 (short) entries collapse onto the same six Figma rows by spelling (`deriveVariableRenames` keeps the greatest `since`), the identical shape #1013+#1140 already exercise.

**Files.** `modes.ts` (`VEIL_RUNGS` + the long veil design note rewritten — it argued the OLD "name the contract, not the magnitude" philosophy, which now contradicts the decision — + the emit-loop `$description` prose, now intensity language that verifies-against-your-photo); `ai-metadata.ts` (veil descriptions reworded to intensity, dropped the now-unused `VEIL_RUNGS` import); `test.ts` §9c (`WCAG_FLOOR` keys + messages; arm-D path `veil.dark.body`→`veil.dark.medium`; and **five rename-map projection counts** the change legitimately moved — projecting 266→278, tier-only-dropping 243→237, project-nothing 410→404, doubly-claimed 113→119, shipped 153→159, plus two new `ERAS` rows 9.0.0/10.0.0); `inverse-coverage.ts` (`INVERSE_GAPS` veil paths); `version.ts` (both version consts + changelogs + `DEPRECATIONS` + new `VEIL_RUNG_RENAMES` literal const); `schema/token-contract.json` (`--accept`ed); `docs/20` §8.2 (superseding decision note + two stale inline naming claims corrected); `docs/42` + `schema/decisions-index.json` (indexed).

**Mutation tests (docs/34; a `wip:` commit preceded each so the `git checkout --` restore reached HEAD, per the CLAUDE.md pathspec trap):**
- **(a) — leave one old rung name un-renamed.** Reverting `inverse-coverage.ts`'s `color.veil.dark.subtle` back to `color.veil.dark.large` made `test.ts`'s INVERSE_GAPS both-directions arm **fail by name** (a gap path that resolves to no live role). Separately, reverting one `DEPRECATIONS` new-entry `replacedBy` to the old rung made `token-contract.ts --check` fail with a dangling deprecation, by name. Restored.
